signals.title: [Bug]: DeepSeek thinking-mode warnings scale with replayed history and obscure useful logs
signals.text: ### Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. ### What happened? When using the LiteLLM Python SDK with DeepSeek thinking mode and multi-turn tool calling, DeepSeek may return a successful assistant tool-call response containing: ```json { "role": "assistant", "content": "", "reasoning_content": "", "tool_calls": [...] } ``` This can be a real provider response rather than a client-side loss of reasoning content. In one recorded mini-swe-agent run, the preserved raw response objects contained `reasoning_content: ""`, while DeepSeek reported: ```json { "completion_tokens_details": { "reasoning_tokens": 0 } } ``` All six affected responses completed normally with `finish_reason: "tool_calls"` and valid tool calls. The DeepSeek Chat Completions API is stateless, so clients resend the conversation history on subsequent requests: [https://api-docs.deepseek.com/guides/multi_round_chat/](https://api-docs.deepseek.com/guides/multi_round_chat/) When LiteLLM receives an empty historical `reasoning_content`, it replaces `""` with a single-space placeholder so that DeepSeek accepts the request. It also emits this warning for every affected assistant message: ```text DeepSeek thinking mode: assistant message is missing `reasoning_content` and none was saved in `provider_specific_fields`. A single-space placeholder is being injected to satisfy API validation, but the model will receive a blank reasoning chain for this turn, which may silently degrade multi-turn response quality. Preserve `reasoning_content` from the original assistant response when building multi-turn conversation history. ``` The compatibility handling works, and warning that LiteLLM modified the request can be useful. The problem is the warning cardinality. LiteLLM transforms a request copy without modifying the caller-owned conversation history. The client therefore continues to store the original `reasoning_content: ""`. Every time the complete history is submitted again, the same historical message emits the same warning again. If multiple empty-reasoning assistant messages accumulate, LiteLLM emits one identical warning for each affected historical message on every subsequent request. During a long agent run, these warnings can dominate the console and make actual errors, tool output, evaluation results, and other actionable diagnostic information difficult to locate. In one successful mini-swe-agent run: ```text LiteLLM: 1.97.0 mini-swe-agent: 2.4.6 Model: deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash Logical model calls: 41 Final agent status: Submitted ``` Six provider responses contained an explicitly present empty `reasoning_content`. They occurred at assistant responses 3, 4, 10, 11, 16, and 22. Because every later request replayed the complete history, these six affected messages appeared: ```text (41 - 3) + (41 - 4) + (41 - 10) + (41 - 11) + (41 - 16) + (41 - 22) = 180 ``` times in aggregate across subsequent request histories. This is a count of affected-message replays derived from the trajectory, not a count extracted from the console. It demonstrates how a small number of provider-returned empty values can repeatedly enter the same warning path during one successful agent run. Expected behavior: 1. Continue replacing empty historical `reasoning_content` values with a DeepSeek-compatible placeholder. 2. Continue avoiding mutation of caller-owned history. 3. Emit at most one aggregated warning per request, including the number of affected messages, for example: ```text DeepSeek thinking mode: injected single-space reasoning_content placeholders into 6 assistant messages in this request. ``` No cross-request state or permanent suppression is required. Emitting one aggregated warning again on a later request would still be reasonable. A possible implementation direction would be to count affected messages during request transformation and emit one summary warning after processing the message list. Individual message indices could optionally be logged at debug level. This is related to, but distinct from, #28045 and #31439. Those issues concern missing `reasoning_content` causing request failures. Here, the compatibility handling succeeds; the reported problem is the amplification of identical warnings during normal history replay. #### Related issues This issue is a follow-up to #28045, not a duplicate of it. #28045 reported that missing reasoning_content in DeepSeek thinking-mode history caused HTTP 400 responses. The completed fix added the current compatibility behavior for the Chat Completions path: recover saved reasoning when possible, or inject a single-space placeholder and emit a warning. That compatibility behavior is working in this report—the provider requests succeed. This issue concerns a downstream logging consequence of the fix: the warning is emitted separately for every affected historical assistant message whenever a stateless client resubmits the full conversation history. #31439 reports the corresponding missing-reasoning failure on the separate DeepSeek Anthropic-compatible /v1/messages path. This report does not cover that endpoint; it concerns repeated warnings on the LiteLLM SDK Chat Completions path. ### User Flow #### Before a hypothetical fix The SDK requests succeed, but identical per-message warnings accumulate and obscure the developer's useful terminal output. 1. The developer stores `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` in `.env` and runs `LITELLM_LOG=INFO uv run --env-file .env python -u repro.py`; the script submits a real `POST https://api.deepseek.com/beta/chat/completions` request containing two historical assistant tool-call messages whose `reasoning_content` values are `""`. 2. The developer observes that the first SDK call returns normally and prints `call 1 succeeded`, but the terminal prints the same placeholder-injection warning twice—once for each affected historical assistant message. 3. The script submits a second real `POST https://api.deepseek.com/beta/chat/completions` request with the same history, and the developer observes that it prints `call 2 succeeded`. 4. The developer observes that the same two warnings are printed again before the second result; in a longer agent conversation, these repeated warnings increasingly obscure later tool and diagnostic output. #### After a hypothetical fix The same SDK requests succeed while the developer receives one concise summary warning per request. 1. The developer stores `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` in `.env` and runs `LITELLM_LOG=INFO uv run --env-file .env python -u repro.py`; the script submits a real `POST https://api.deepseek.com/beta/chat/completions` request containing two historical assistant tool-call messages whose `reasoning_content` values are `""`. 2. The developer observes that the first SDK call returns normally and prints `call 1 succeeded`, while the terminal prints one warning stating that two assistant messages required placeholders. 3. The script submits a second real `POST https://api.deepseek.com/beta/chat/completions` request with the same history, and the developer observes that it prints `call 2 succeeded`. 4. The developer observes one summary warning before the second result; other tool and diagnostic output remains easy to locate. ### Proof the bug occurs The following reproduction uses the LiteLLM Python SDK and sends real requests to the official DeepSeek API. It does not use mocks. #### SDK setup ```text OS: Ubuntu 22.04 under WSL2 Python: 3.11 LiteLLM: 1.97.0 Provider: DeepSeek official API Model: deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash Endpoint used by LiteLLM 1.97.0: POST https://api.deepseek.com/beta/chat/completions ``` A valid DeepSeek API key was provided through the following environment variable: ```text DEEPSEEK_API_KEY=<REDACTED> ``` The actual credential is intentionally omitted. Create `repro.py`: ```python from importlib.metadata import version from litellm import completion TOOLS = [ { "type": "function", "function": { "name": "bash", "description": "Execute a bash command", "parameters": { "type": "object", "properties": { "command": {"type": "string"}, }, "required": ["command"], }, }, } ] MESSAGES = [ { "role": "user", "content": "Use bash to inspect the working directory.", }, { "role": "assistant", "content": "", "reasoning_content": "", "tool_calls": [ { "id": "call_repro_1", "type": "function", "function": { "name": "bash", "arguments": "{\"command\":\"pwd\"}", }, } ], }, { "role": "tool", "tool_call_id": "call_repro_1", "content": "/tmp", }, { "role": "assistant", "content": "", "reasoning_content": "", "tool_calls": [ { "id": "call_repro_2", "type": "function", "function": { "name": "bash", "arguments": "{\"command\":\"printf done\"}", }, } ], }, { "role": "tool", "tool_call_id": "call_repro_2", "content": "done", }, { "role": "user", "content": "Reply only with OK.", }, ] def main() -> None: print("litellm:", version("litellm")) for call_number in range(1, 3): response = completion( model="deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash", messages=MESSAGES, tools=TOOLS, reasoning_effort="medium", max_tokens=32, ) reasoning_values = [ message["reasoning_content"] for message in MESSAGES if message.get("role") == "assistant" ] print( f"call {call_number} succeeded; " f"response={response.choices[0].message.content!r}; " f"caller reasoning values={reasoning_values!r}" ) if __name__ == "__main__": main() ``` Run: ```bash LITELLM_LOG=INFO uv run --env-file .env python -u repro.py 2>&1 | tee repro.log ``` Full output: ```text litellm: 1.97.0 19:35:06 - LiteLLM:WARNING: transformation.py:87 - DeepSeek thinking mode: assistant message is missing `reasoning_content` and none was saved in `provider_specific_fields`. A single-space placeholder is being injected to satisfy API validation, but the model will receive a blank reasoning chain for this turn, which may silently degrade multi-turn response quality. Preserve `reasoning_content` from the original assistant response when building multi-turn conversation history. 19:35:06 - LiteLLM:WARNING: transformation.py:87 - DeepSeek thinking mode: assistant message is missing `reasoning_content` and none was saved in `provider_specific_fields`. A single-space placeholder is being injected to satisfy API validation, but the model will receive a blank reasoning chain for this turn, which may silently degrade multi-turn response quality. Preserve `reasoning_content` from the original assistant response when building multi-turn conversation history. call 1 succeeded; response=''; caller reasoning values=['', ''] 19:35:08 - LiteLLM:WARNING: transformation.py:87 - DeepSeek thinking mode: assistant message is missing `reasoning_content` and none was saved in `provider_specific_fields`. A single-space placeholder is being injected to satisfy API validation, but the model will receive a blank reasoning chain for this turn, which may silently degrade multi-turn response quality. Preserve `reasoning_content` from the original assistant response when building multi-turn conversation history. 19:35:08 - LiteLLM:WARNING: transformation.py:87 - DeepSeek thinking mode: assistant message is missing `reasoning_content` and none was saved in `provider_specific_fields`. A single-space placeholder is being injected to satisfy API validation, but the model will receive a blank reasoning chain for this turn, which may silently degrade multi-turn response quality. Preserve `reasoning_content` from the original assistant response when building multi-turn conversation history. call 2 succeeded; response=''; caller reasoning values=['', ''] ``` This output demonstrates that: - both real provider calls complete successfully; - each request emits two identical warnings for the two affected historical messages; - replaying the same history emits the same warnings again; - LiteLLM correctly leaves the caller-owned values unchanged as `["", ""]`. This report is limited to the LiteLLM SDK Chat Completions path. I have not verified the behavior against `/v1/responses` or `/v1/messages`. ### What part of LiteLLM is this about? SDK (litellm Python package) ### What LiteLLM version are you on ? v1.97.0 ### Twitter / LinkedIn details _No response_

signals.title: [Bug]: azure/gpt-5.6* entries missing cache_creation_input_token_cost — cache writes billed at zero since v1.97.0
signals.text: ### Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. ### What happened? Every `azure/gpt-5.6*` entry in the price map lacks `cache_creation_input_token_cost`, while its non-Azure counterpart has it. Since v1.97.0 correctly classifies Azure's `cache_write_tokens` as cache-creation tokens, those tokens now resolve to no rate and are billed at **zero**. This is a regression in effect, though not in code. Before v1.97.0 the same tokens were folded into plain input and under-reported by ~20%; now they are dropped entirely and under-report by ~98%. The fix for #33772 corrected the code path and the OpenAI entries, but the Azure entries were not updated to match. All eight Azure entries are missing the key; all four non-Azure counterparts have it: | Model | input_cost_per_token | cache_creation_input_token_cost | |---|---|---| | `gpt-5.6` | 5e-06 | 6.25e-06 | | `azure/gpt-5.6` | 5e-06 | **missing** | | `azure/us/gpt-5.6` | 5.5e-06 | **missing** | | `gpt-5.6-sol` | 5e-06 | 6.25e-06 | | `azure/gpt-5.6-sol` | 5e-06 | **missing** | | `azure/us/gpt-5.6-sol` | 5.5e-06 | **missing** | | `gpt-5.6-luna` | 2e-07 | 2.5e-07 | | `azure/gpt-5.6-luna` | 2e-07 | **missing** | | `azure/us/gpt-5.6-luna` | 2.2e-07 | **missing** | | `gpt-5.6-terra` | 2e-06 | 2.5e-06 | | `azure/gpt-5.6-terra` | 2e-06 | **missing** | | `azure/us/gpt-5.6-terra` | 2.2e-06 | **missing** | Azure prices cache writes at 1.25× input, same as OpenAI, so the values should mirror the non-Azure entries (with the 10% uplift already present on `azure/us/*`). **Expected:** a request whose prompt tokens are mostly cache writes is billed at the cache-creation rate. **Actual:** those tokens cost nothing, so spend is under-reported by ~98%. Not a duplicate of #36094 — that one is about the per-token input/output prices for Luna being wrong by 5×. This one is about a missing key across the whole gpt-5.6 Azure family causing cache-write tokens to price at zero. Fixing either leaves the other in place. ### User Flow Before a (hypothetical) fix: a platform team charging back Azure OpenAI spend per team sees almost nothing billed for their RAG service, whose requests carry a large cached system prompt 1. Their RAG service sends POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with "model": "azure-gpt-5.6-sol" and a ~2,200-token system prompt 2. The response comes back 200 with "usage": {"prompt_tokens": 2219, "prompt_tokens_details": {"cache_write_tokens": 2217}} 3. They open https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs and the request shows $0.000225 spend 4. Their monthly Azure invoice for the same traffic is roughly 60× higher than the total the gateway reports, so per-team chargeback is unusable After a (hypothetical) fix: the same request is billed at the cache-write rate, and the gateway total lines up with the invoice 1. Their RAG service sends the same POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with "model": "azure-gpt-5.6-sol" and the same ~2,200-token system prompt 2. The response comes back 200 with the same usage object 3. https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs shows that request at $0.014015 spend 4. The monthly total tracks the Azure invoice, so chargeback per team is accurate ### Proof the bug occurs **Config / setup the proxy ran with:** ```yaml model_list: - model_name: azure-gpt-5.6-sol litellm_params: model: azure/gpt-5.6-sol api_base: os.environ/AZURE_OPENAI_ENDPOINT api_version: "2025-04-01-preview" general_settings: master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY database_url: os.environ/DATABASE_URL ``` Live Azure OpenAI deployment, `gpt-5.6-sol`, GlobalStandard. Authentication is a workload identity, so no key appears in the config. **Version or commit:** v1.97.0 (the same request on v1.97.0 is compared against v1.94.2 below) **Commands and their full output:** Send a request whose prompt is large enough to trigger a cache write: ```bash python - <<'EOF' import json prefix = 'You are a documentation assistant. ' + ( 'The following is reference material about cloud architecture patterns. ' * 220) json.dump({"model": "azure-gpt-5.6-sol", "messages": [{"role": "system", "content": prefix}, {"role": "user", "content": "say ok"}], "max_tokens": 10}, open("req.json", "w")) EOF curl -s http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $LITELLM_MASTER_KEY" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" --data @req.json | jq .usage ``` Output — the provider reports 2217 cache-write tokens: ```json { "completion_tokens": 5, "prompt_tokens": 2219, "total_tokens": 2224, "prompt_tokens_details": { "audio_tokens": 0, "cached_tokens": 0, "cache_write_tokens": 2217, "cache_creation_tokens": 2217 } } ``` What the gateway recorded for that request: ```bash curl -s "http://localhost:4000/spend/logs" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $LITELLM_MASTER_KEY" | jq '.[-1] | {model, spend, prompt_tokens}' ``` ```json { "model": "azure/gpt-5.6-sol", "spend": 0.000225, "prompt_tokens": 2220 } ``` Correct value is `3 × 5e-6 + 2216 × 6.25e-6 + 5 × 3e-5 = 0.014015`, so this is 98% short. **Same request, three setups:** | Setup | recorded spend | vs correct | |---|---|---| | v1.94.2, price map | 0.011245 | −20% | | v1.97.0, price map | **0.000225** | **−98%** | | v1.97.0, prices declared in config | 0.001470 | correct | The third row is the workaround, and it confirms the price map entry is the only thing missing — nothing else changed: ```yaml - model_name: azure-gpt-5.6-sol litellm_params: model: azure/gpt-5.6-sol input_cost_per_token: 0.000005 output_cost_per_token: 0.00003 cache_creation_input_token_cost: 0.00000625 cache_read_input_token_cost: 0.0000005 ``` (That run's request was mostly cache *reads* rather than writes, since the prefix was already cached: 2213 read + 8 write + 10 output = 2213×5e-7 + 8×6.25e-6 + 10×3e-5 = 0.0014565, matching the recorded 0.001470.) **Isolating it to the price map** — same code path, same usage object, the two entries differ only in whether the key exists: ```python import litellm from litellm.types.utils import Usage, PromptTokensDetailsWrapper details = PromptTokensDetailsWrapper(cached_tokens=0) details.cache_write_tokens = 2216 usage = Usage(prompt_tokens=2219, completion_tokens=5, total_tokens=2224, prompt_tokens_details=details) for model, provider in [("gpt-5.6-sol", "openai"), ("azure/gpt-5.6-sol", "azure")]: p, c = litellm.cost_calculator.generic_cost_per_token( model=model, usage=usage, custom_llm_provider=provider) print(f"{model}: {p + c:.8f}") ``` ``` gpt-5.6-sol: 0.01401500 azure/gpt-5.6-sol: 0.00016500 ``` ### What part of LiteLLM is this about? Proxy ### What LiteLLM version are you on ? v1.97.0 ### Twitter / LinkedIn details _No response_

signals.title: [Bug]: DeepSeek thinking-by-default models + tools: _fill_reasoning_content guard never fires without explicit reasoning params, upstream 400
signals.text: ## What happened? DeepSeek V4 models (`deepseek-v4-pro`, `deepseek-v4-flash`) run **thinking mode by default server-side**. In a multi-turn tool-calling loop, DeepSeek's API requires `reasoning_content` to be passed back on assistant messages, otherwise it returns: ``` 400 {"error":{"message":"The `reasoning_content` in the thinking mode must be passed back to the API.", "type":"invalid_request_error"}} ``` LiteLLM already handles this: `DeepSeekChatConfig._fill_reasoning_content` (added for #28045) promotes `provider_specific_fields.reasoning_content` or injects a minimal placeholder. However, the gate that decides whether to run it assumes thinking is **opt-in**: ```python # litellm/llms/deepseek/chat/transformation.py def _thinking_mode_active(self, model: str, optional_params: dict) -> bool: return ( supports_reasoning(model=model, custom_llm_provider="deepseek") and (optional_params.get("thinking") or {}).get("type") == "enabled" ) ``` When the request carries **no** `thinking`/`reasoning_effort` at all — the common case for a router/proxy deployment that doesn't inject reasoning params — the guard is `False`, `_fill_reasoning_content` never runs, and the DeepSeek API rejects every second call of a tool loop with the 400 above. The model was in thinking mode the whole time; the request just never said so. The guard's opt-in assumption is documented in its own comment ("preventing spurious injection on models like deepseek-v3.2 that support thinking as opt-in but not always-on") — correct for opt-in models, wrong for thinking-by-default models. ## Reproduction (litellm proxy v1.96.2 or SDK) ```python import litellm TOOLS = [{"type": "function", "function": {"name": "get_time", "description": "Get current time", "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {}}}}] MSGS = [ {"role": "user", "content": "What time is it? Use the tool."}, {"role": "assistant", "content": "", "tool_calls": [{"id": "call_1", "type": "function", "function": {"name": "get_time", "arguments": "{}"}}]}, {"role": "tool", "tool_call_id": "call_1", "content": "14:32 UTC"}, ] # FAILS with the 400 above — no reasoning params, guard never fires: litellm.completion(model="deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro", messages=MSGS, tools=TOOLS) # WORKS — reasoning_effort maps to thinking:{"type":"enabled"}, guard fires, # _fill_reasoning_content runs: litellm.completion(model="deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro", messages=MSGS, tools=TOOLS, reasoning_effort="high") ``` Both verified against the live DeepSeek API through a litellm proxy v1.96.2. ## Expected behavior For models whose thinking mode is on by default, `_fill_reasoning_content` should run unless the request **explicitly disables** thinking (`thinking: {"type": "disabled"}` / `reasoning_effort: "none"` — explicit disable works today and needs no fill: verified that a disabled-thinking tool loop passes). ## Proposed fix Make the default-on property data-driven and extend the guard: 1. Add a capability flag in the model cost map for thinking-by-default models (e.g. `"thinking_by_default": true` on `deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro`, `deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash`, and other always-on reasoning models). 2. Change the guard to: ```python def _thinking_mode_active(self, model: str, optional_params: dict) -> bool: if not supports_reasoning(model=model, custom_llm_provider="deepseek"): return False thinking = (optional_params.get("thinking") or {}).get("type") if thinking == "enabled": return True if thinking == "disabled": return False return thinking_by_default(model) # <- new: no explicit choice on the wire ``` This keeps the #28045 behavior intact for opt-in models (deepseek-v3.2) and closes the hole for default-on models. ## Workaround we're using today Pin `reasoning_effort` on the proxy deployment so the guard fires (wire-neutral: every non-`"none"` value maps to plain `thinking: {"type": "enabled"}`, which is already the server default): ```yaml - model_name: deepseek-v4-pro litellm_params: model: deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro api_key: os.environ/DEEPSEEK_API_KEY reasoning_effort: "high" ``` ## Environment - litellm v1.96.2 (proxy, `ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.96.2`) - Models: `deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro`, `deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash` - Surfaced at scale behind a router where client requests carry no reasoning params (the deployment decides) — every tool-using turn 400s on its second call.
signals.author: marcelinobadin

signals.title: [Bug]: Serving a request permanently clears that model's pricing from /v2/model/info (Model Management Costs column goes blank)
signals.text: ### What happened? Serving a single completion for a model permanently clears that model's `input_cost_per_token` / `output_cost_per_token` from `/v2/model/info`, so the **Costs** column on the Model Management page goes blank for that model. The price never comes back on its own. The net effect is that the models you actually use show no pricing in the UI, while the models you have never called still show theirs — which is a confusing signal, because it looks like the *used* models are the misconfigured ones. The pricing data itself is fine the whole time: `litellm.model_cost` still holds the correct entry, and cost tracking keeps working (the `x-litellm-response-cost` header stays exact). This is a reporting bug in `/v2/model/info` only. ### Config (nothing custom — no pricing overrides anywhere) ```yaml model_list: - model_name: claude-fable-5 # control: never called litellm_params: model: anthropic/claude-fable-5 api_key: os.environ/ANTHROPIC_API_KEY - model_name: claude-haiku-4-5 # the one we call litellm_params: model: anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 api_key: os.environ/ANTHROPIC_API_KEY general_settings: master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY store_model_in_db: true ``` ### Steps to reproduce 1. `POST /reload/model_cost_map` (to start from a known-good state — every model reports its price) 2. `GET /v2/model/info` — both models report prices 3. `POST /chat/completions` with `{"model": "claude-haiku-4-5", ...}` — one request, succeeds normally 4. `GET /v2/model/info` again ``` reload Price data reloaded successfully! 3054 models updated. BEFORE claude-fable-5 input_cost_per_token=1e-05 output_cost_per_token=5e-05 BEFORE claude-haiku-4-5 input_cost_per_token=1e-06 output_cost_per_token=5e-06 BEFORE cost map claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 input=1e-06 output=5e-06 --- one request to claude-haiku-4-5; response cost header = 3.3e-05 --- AFTER claude-fable-5 input_cost_per_token=1e-05 output_cost_per_token=5e-05 AFTER claude-haiku-4-5 input_cost_per_token=None output_cost_per_token=None AFTER cost map claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 input=1e-06 output=5e-06 ``` Only the model that was called loses its pricing. The untouched control model keeps its. `litellm.model_cost` (via `/public/litellm_model_cost_map`) is unchanged and still correct, and the request billed correctly (`3.3e-05` = 8 in × $1/M + 5 out × $5/M). Leaving the proxy idle does **not** cause the drop — only traffic to that specific model does. I verified this by reloading, waiting 20s with no traffic (prices stayed), then calling one model (only that one dropped). ### What I think is going on Two things combine: 1. After a request, that deployment's `model_info` contains the cost keys as explicit `None` rather than being absent. `Deployment.__init__` (`litellm/types/router.py`, ~L442-457) normalises a `model_info` dict through the `ModelInfo` pydantic model, which materialises every unset cost field as `None`; the router passes the deployment's `model_info` into per-request kwargs at `litellm/router.py:3170`. 2. `_enrich_model_info_with_litellm_data` (`litellm/proxy/proxy_server.py`, ~L11761) then backfills from the cost map with: ```python for k, v in litellm_model_info.items(): if k not in model_info: model_info[k] = v ``` That fills keys that are **absent**, but never keys that are present-and-`None`. So once step 1 has written a `None`, the cost map can no longer heal it, and the value stays blank for the life of the process. A merge that treated `None` as "not set" (`if model_info.get(k) is None`) would fix the symptom; not clobbering the deployment's `model_info` with a null-filled dump in the first place would fix the cause. ### Workaround `POST /reload/model_cost_map` (or the reload button in the UI) rebuilds the deployments and restores every price — but only until each model is called again. ### Relevant log output No errors are logged; requests succeed normally and are billed correctly. ### Are you a ML Ops Team? Yes ### What LiteLLM version are you on? litellm 1.97.0 (`ghcr.io/berriai/litellm-database:main-stable`), litellm-proxy-extras 0.4.84, litellm-enterprise 0.1.54, Python 3.13.15, Postgres-backed with `store_model_in_db: true`.
signals.author: aliasaria

signals.title: [Bug]: Guardrail mode=block silently behaves as redact on provider-native passthrough routes (e.g. Gemini generateContent) — only bedrock is wired up
signals.text: ### Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. (Related but distinct: #32201, #34411 — both are passthrough+guardrail issues but cover response-side tool-call enforcement and spend-log accuracy, not this request-side mode config being dropped.) ### What happened? A guardrail using the Generic Guardrail API (`guardrail: generic_guardrail_api`) configured with `additional_provider_specific_params.secrets.config.mode: "block"` correctly blocks on `/chat/completions`, `/completions`, `/v1/responses`, and the Anthropic-native `/v1/messages` route — but on the Gemini-native `generateContent` passthrough route, the same config silently behaves as `mode: "redact"` instead. No error, no warning — the guardrail runs, correctly detects the sensitive content, but never blocks. **Expected:** a request containing a detectable secret, sent through `POST /v1beta/models/{model}:generateContent` with the guardrail enabled and `secrets.config.mode: "block"`, is rejected. **Actual:** the request succeeds (200), and the guardrail span reports a redact-style outcome instead of a block. We ruled out the guardrail provider itself: calling our guardrail's HTTP endpoint directly (bypassing LiteLLM entirely) with the identical secret and the identical `mode: "block"` config correctly returns: ```json {"action": "BLOCKED", "blocked_reason": "Secret detected: Anthropic API Key (1 total)"} ``` So the guardrail's own scoring logic honors `mode: block` correctly when given the config — the config just isn't reaching it that way on this route. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Configure a `generic_guardrail_api` guardrail (or any other guardrail backend that supports `additional_provider_specific_params`): ```yaml guardrails: - guardrail_name: "my-secrets-block" litellm_params: guardrail: generic_guardrail_api mode: pre_call api_base: os.environ/GUARDRAIL_API_BASE default_on: false additional_provider_specific_params: secrets: enabled: true config: mode: block ``` 2. Register a Gemini model and call it via the native passthrough shape: ```bash curl -X POST "http://localhost:4000/v1beta/models/gemini-2.5-flash:generateContent" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $LITELLM_MASTER_KEY" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "contents": [{"role": "user", "parts": [{"text": "My API key is sk-ant-api03-abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789."}]}], "guardrails": ["my-secrets-block"] }' ``` 3. Compare against the same guardrail/model/secret sent via `/chat/completions` instead — that one correctly blocks with an HTTP 400. ### Suspected root cause (pending maintainer confirmation — not independently verified by patching LiteLLM's source) Per a source-level read of `litellm/llms/pass_through/guardrail_translation/handler.py`: `LlmPassthroughRouteHandler` (used for `CallTypes.allm_passthrough_route`, i.e. native-provider passthrough calls including Gemini's `generateContent`) dispatches by `custom_llm_provider` through a handler map that only contains an entry for `bedrock`. For any other provider — `vertex_ai`/`gemini` included — there's no matching handler class, and the observed behavior (guardrail runs, detects correctly, but resolves to the default mode) is consistent with `additional_provider_specific_params` — specifically the nested `secrets.config.mode` field — not being forwarded through to the guardrail hook the same way `OpenAIChatCompletionsHandler` does for the standard `/chat/completions` path. `resolve_check_mode()` (guardrail-side) falls back to a default of `'redact'` for `secrets`/`pii` whenever the `mode` field is absent or unparseable, which matches exactly what we observed. ### Suggested fix direction Either: - Extend the provider-passthrough handler map so `additional_provider_specific_params` is forwarded uniformly regardless of `custom_llm_provider`, or - If there's an architectural reason non-bedrock native passthrough can't carry the full guardrail params, fail loudly (log a warning, or refuse to silently downgrade `block` to `redact`) rather than silently applying the default mode — a security-relevant guardrail decision silently reverting to a *less restrictive* mode is the concerning part here, independent of which routes are supported. ### Relevant log output Guardrail span from our LiteLLM v1 OTel export, from the failing call: ```json { "guardrail_mode": "pre_call", "guardrail_name": "fiddler-secrets-block", "guardrail_response": "\"Secret detected: Anthropic API Key (1 total)\"", "guardrail_status": "guardrail_intervened" } ``` Note `guardrail_status` reports the redact-path outcome despite the guardrail being configured for `mode: block`. ### Twitter / LinkedIn details _No response_ ### Are you a ML Ops Team? Yes ### What LiteLLM version are you on? v1.94.0 ### Additional context Prior related fix from our team: #27617 (`GuardrailRaisedException` missing `status_code`, fixed in 1.88.0) — happy to help verify a fix here the same way.
signals.author: robin-fiddler

signals.title: [Bug]: native CLI login consent page lists teams in database order and preselects the first one
signals.text: ### Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. ### What happened? The consent page that `lite login --pkce` opens in the browser (added by #37626) asks a user who belongs to several teams which team their CLI requests should be attributed to. The dropdown lists the teams in whatever order the database returns them and the first entry is what the form submits when the user clicks Approve without touching it. On the same proxy, with the same user, that first entry was `forge-team-b-35551` while the alphabetical first is `forge-team-a-35551`, and during an earlier QA run the order changed between two logins. A user who takes the default can end up bound to a team they did not mean to pick, and their first chat call then fails with `403 team not allowed to access model` if that team's allowlist does not cover the model they asked for Expected: the teams come back in a stable, predictable order (alias, case-insensitively, then id as a tiebreaker), or the form does not preselect anything when there is more than one team and makes the user choose. The same team lookup backs the classic `lite login` flow's team choice, so sorting it there fixes both ### User Flow Before a (hypothetical) fix: a developer on several teams clicks Approve on the consent page, gets bound to whichever team the database listed first, and their first chat call is refused 1. The developer runs `lite login --pkce` against `https://litellm-domain`; the CLI opens `GET https://litellm-domain/authorize?response_type=code&client_id=...&code_challenge=...&resource=https://litellm-domain` in their browser 2. After signing in, the consent page shows an "Attribute requests to team" dropdown whose first entry is `forge-team-b-35551`, with `lit5874-cli-team` second and `forge-team-a-35551` sixth, in no recognizable order 3. They click Approve without touching the dropdown; the browser posts `POST https://litellm-domain/authorize/complete`, lands back on the CLI's loopback page, and the terminal prints `Login successful!` 4. They send `POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions` with `"model": "gpt-5.4-mini"` and get `403 {"error": {"message": "team not allowed to access model. This team can only access models=['gpt-4o-mini']. Tried to access gpt-5.4-mini", "type": "team_model_access_denied"}}` 5. They open `https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs` and see the failed request attributed to `forge-team-b-35551`, a team they never meant to use from the CLI After a (hypothetical) fix: the dropdown is sorted and the developer sees the team they expect before approving 1. The developer runs `lite login --pkce` against `https://litellm-domain`; the CLI opens the same `GET https://litellm-domain/authorize?...` URL in their browser 2. After signing in, the consent page lists the teams alphabetically (`forge-team-a-35551`, `forge-team-b-35551`, `lit5874-cli-team`, ...), so the entry at the top is the same on every login and on every replica 3. They pick `lit5874-cli-team`, click Approve, the browser posts `POST https://litellm-domain/authorize/complete`, and the terminal prints `Login successful!` 4. They send `POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions` with `"model": "gpt-5.4-mini"` and get `200` with a normal completion 5. `https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs` shows the request attributed to `lit5874-cli-team` ### Proof the bug occurs Config the proxy ran with (`litellm --config config.yaml --port 53218`, Postgres-backed so teams and memberships live in the DB; the env vars named are `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY`, and `DATABASE_URL`, values redacted): ```yaml model_list: - model_name: gpt-5.4-mini litellm_params: model: openai/gpt-5.4-mini api_key: os.environ/OPENAI_API_KEY - model_name: claude-haiku-4-5 litellm_params: model: anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5 api_key: os.environ/ANTHROPIC_API_KEY general_settings: master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY database_url: os.environ/DATABASE_URL store_model_in_db: true coordination_redis: host: 127.0.0.1 port: 53217 ``` Commit: `64e7ab1beb`, the tip of #37626 (branch `litellm_lit5874_native_cli_oauth_pkce`, based on `litellm_internal_staging` at `6fcdea03b0`) The signed-in user is `default_user_id`, a member of nine teams. The "browser" below is a script standing in for the system browser: it signs in at `POST /login`, fetches the consent page the CLI sent it to, prints the dropdown's `<option>` entries in page order, and then submits the form. Two logins in a row: ``` $ lite --base-url http://127.0.0.1:53218 login --pkce (run 1) Login successful! browser side: POST /login -> 303 GET /authorize -> 200 team <select> options, in page order: forge-team-b-35551 (f7f1356b...) lit5874-cli-team (e34bc8db...) qa-team-a-35551 (4c2befa8...) qa-team-b-35551 (dd13137d...) qa-team-a-35551 (57d853bc...) forge-team-a-35551 (94554a34...) qa-team-b-35551 (57f324f9...) risk37518-team-1787186008 (a0a759e9...) testteam (ae98be70...) same labels sorted, for comparison: forge-team-a-35551 (94554a34...) forge-team-b-35551 (f7f1356b...) lit5874-cli-team (e34bc8db...) qa-team-a-35551 (4c2befa8...) qa-team-a-35551 (57d853bc...) qa-team-b-35551 (57f324f9...) qa-team-b-35551 (dd13137d...) risk37518-team-1787186008 (a0a759e9...) testteam (ae98be70...) preselected (first option, what Approve submits untouched): forge-team-b-35551 POST /authorize/complete (team_id=lit5874-cli-team) -> 200 $ lite --base-url http://127.0.0.1:53218 logout Logged out successfully. Authentication token cleared. $ lite --base-url http://127.0.0.1:53218 login --pkce (run 2) Login successful! browser side: POST /login -> 303 GET /authorize -> 200 team <select> options, in page order: forge-team-b-35551 (f7f1356b...) lit5874-cli-team (e34bc8db...) qa-team-a-35551 (4c2befa8...) qa-team-b-35551 (dd13137d...) qa-team-a-35551 (57d853bc...) forge-team-a-35551 (94554a34...) qa-team-b-35551 (57f324f9...) risk37518-team-1787186008 (a0a759e9...) testteam (ae98be70...) preselected (first option, what Approve submits untouched): forge-team-b-35551 POST /authorize/complete (team_id=lit5874-cli-team) -> 200 ``` The order is neither alphabetical nor the order the user joined the teams in (`lit5874-cli-team` was the most recent membership). What happens to a user who clicks Approve without touching the dropdown, same proxy, same user: ``` $ lite --base-url http://127.0.0.1:53218 login --pkce (browser clicks Approve without touching the team dropdown) Login successful! browser side: GET /authorize -> 200 preselected (first option, what Approve submits untouched): forge-team-b-35551 POST /authorize/complete (team_id left at the preselected first option) -> 200 stored team_id: f7f1356b-a734-41f0-9120-6f01756f9853 $ curl http://127.0.0.1:53218/v1/chat/completions -H 'Authorization: Bearer <stored key>' -d '{"model":"gpt-5.4-mini","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]}' {"error":{"message":"team not allowed to access model. This team can only access models=['gpt-4o-mini']. Tried to access gpt-5.4-mini","type":"team_model_access_denied","param":"model","code":"403"}} HTTP 403 $ lite --base-url http://127.0.0.1:53218 logout Logged out successfully. Authentication token cleared. ``` ### Fix sketch The order comes from `fetch_cli_sso_team_details` in `litellm/proxy/management_endpoints/ui_sso.py`, which runs `find_many(where={"team_id": {"in": teams}})` with no `order`, and `lookup_consent_teams` in `litellm/proxy/_experimental/mcp_server/proxy_api_credentials.py` hands those rows to `_team_field` in `litellm/proxy/common_utils/html_forms/native_client_consent.py` as is. Sort once at the source: have `fetch_cli_sso_team_details` return the details ordered by `(team_alias or team_id).casefold()` and then `team_id`, so the consent page, the classic `lite login` team choice, and anything else reading that helper agree. If the product call is that a multi-team user must choose explicitly, `_team_field` can additionally render a disabled, selected placeholder option (`Choose a team`) and mark the select `required` when there is more than one team, so Approve without a choice is refused by the browser Tests: extend `tests/test_litellm/proxy/management_endpoints/test_ui_sso.py` with a `find_many` stub that returns rows out of order and assert the helper's output is sorted by alias then id (including two teams that share an alias), extend `tests/test_litellm/proxy/_experimental/mcp_server/test_proxy_api_credentials.py` so `lookup_consent_teams` keeps that order, and, if the placeholder is added, extend `tests/test_litellm/proxy/common_utils/html_forms/test_native_client_consent.py` to assert the first option is the disabled placeholder whenever two or more teams are passed QA: on a Postgres-backed proxy, add one user to three teams whose aliases sort differently from their creation order, run `lite login --pkce`, and check that the consent page at `/authorize` lists them alphabetically on two consecutive logins (and on each replica when running more than one); then click Approve untouched and confirm the stored `team_id` in `~/.litellm/token.json` is the alphabetical first, or that the browser refuses to submit without a choice if the placeholder route is taken ### What part of LiteLLM is this about? Proxy ### What LiteLLM version are you on ? commit 64e7ab1beb (PR #37626 branch, based on litellm_internal_staging at 6fcdea03b0) ### Twitter / LinkedIn details _No response_

signals.title: Gemini/Vertex AI cost calc doesn't recognize ON_DEMAND_FLEX traffic type — flex requests billed as standard
signals.text: ### What happened For Gemini/Vertex AI models, LiteLLM extracts the provider's traffic type from the response body (`usageMetadata.trafficType`) and maps it to a billing `service_tier` via `_GEMINI_TRAFFIC_TYPE_TO_SERVICE_TIER` in `litellm/cost_calculator.py`: ```python _GEMINI_TRAFFIC_TYPE_TO_SERVICE_TIER: Final[dict] = { "ON_DEMAND_PRIORITY": "priority", "FLEX": "flex", "BATCH": "flex", "ON_DEMAND": None, } ``` This mapping is missing the `"ON_DEMAND_FLEX"` value. When a Vertex AI request actually opts into flex/shared capacity (via Vertex's request-level opt-in mechanism, forwarded through LiteLLM's `extra_headers` passthrough — confirmed unmodified in `litellm/llms/vertex_ai/gemini/vertex_and_google_ai_studio_gemini.py`, e.g. lines 2744/2846/3033), the response's `usageMetadata.trafficType` comes back as `"ON_DEMAND_FLEX"`, not `"FLEX"` or `"BATCH"`. Since `"ON_DEMAND_FLEX"` isn't in the dict, `_map_traffic_type_to_service_tier()` returns `None`, and `generic_cost_per_token()` falls back to standard `input_cost_per_token`/`output_cost_per_token` pricing instead of the flex-tier price — even though the request was genuinely served at flex tier by the provider. Net effect: flex-tier Gemini/Vertex requests are silently billed at standard rate, with no visibility that flex was actually applied. ### Reproduction 1. Call Vertex AI's `generateContent` directly (`https://aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/{project}/locations/{location}/publishers/google/models/{model}:generateContent`) with headers that opt the request into shared/flex capacity scheduling. The response's `usageMetadata.trafficType` is `"ON_DEMAND_FLEX"`. 2. Route the same request through LiteLLM as `vertex_ai/<model>`, forwarding the same headers via `extra_headers` (LiteLLM passes them straight through to the upstream `httpx` call). 3. Compare `x-litellm-response-cost` between a flex-headers call and a baseline call with equal token counts — cost is identical. Flex is not reflected in cost tracking. 4. Confirmed against current `origin/main` (`litellm/cost_calculator.py`): `_GEMINI_TRAFFIC_TYPE_TO_SERVICE_TIER` still only has `ON_DEMAND_PRIORITY`, `FLEX`, `BATCH`, `ON_DEMAND` — `ON_DEMAND_FLEX` is absent. Note this is distinct from a separate, already-partially-addressed gap: as of this writing, `gemini-3.5-flash` has `input_cost_per_token_priority`/`output_cost_per_token_priority` in `model_prices_and_context_window.json` but no `_flex` price fields yet (unlike `gemini-3.5-flash-lite`, which has both `_flex` and `_priority`). Both the mapping fix below and flex pricing data are needed for flex-tier Gemini/Vertex requests to cost correctly. ### Expected behavior `_GEMINI_TRAFFIC_TYPE_TO_SERVICE_TIER` should map `"ON_DEMAND_FLEX"` → `"flex"` (same target as `"FLEX"`/`"BATCH"`), so `generic_cost_per_token()` correctly selects `input_cost_per_token_flex`/`output_cost_per_token_flex` when those are configured for the model (either in the shipped price map or via per-deployment `litellm_params` overrides). ### Suggested fix Add `"ON_DEMAND_FLEX": "flex"` to `_GEMINI_TRAFFIC_TYPE_TO_SERVICE_TIER` in `litellm/cost_calculator.py`. ### Relevant code - `litellm/cost_calculator.py` — `_GEMINI_TRAFFIC_TYPE_TO_SERVICE_TIER`, `_map_traffic_type_to_service_tier()` - `litellm/llms/vertex_ai/gemini/vertex_and_google_ai_studio_gemini.py` — `## ADD TRAFFIC TYPE ##` block that reads `usageMetadata.trafficType` into `model_response._hidden_params["provider_specific_fields"]["traffic_type"]` ### Version Confirmed present on `origin/main` at `pyproject.toml` version `1.99.0`.

signals.title: [Bug]: Orphaned fallback references not cleaned up on model deletion — no warning, cascades on primary failure
signals.text: ## Environment - LiteLLM version: v1.97.0 (image: litellm/litellm:v1.97.0) - Deploy type: Plain Kubernetes manifest (kubectl apply), no Helm/Terraform - Database: PostgreSQL — models and fallbacks managed via UI/DB (not config.yaml; config.yaml only has general_settings.master_key) ## What happened? When a model referenced in a fallback configuration is deleted via the LiteLLM Admin UI (or /model/delete API), the fallback mapping is not removed and no warning is shown. This creates an orphaned fallback reference that causes a cascade failure when the primary model goes down — instead of a clean "no fallback available" response, the proxy retries against the nonexistent fallback and returns a verbose, confusing 500 error. ## Reproduction steps 1. Create two test models via API: ``` POST /model/new {"model_name": "test-primary-tmp", "litellm_params": {"model": "openai/nonexistent-model", "api_base": "https://httpstat.us/500", "api_key": "fake-key"}, "model_info": {}} POST /model/new {"model_name": "test-fallback-tmp", "litellm_params": {"model": "openai/nonexistent-model", "api_base": "https://httpstat.us/500", "api_key": "fake-key"}, "model_info": {}} ``` 2. Configure fallback `test-primary-tmp -> test-fallback-tmp`: ``` POST /fallback {"model": "test-primary-tmp", "fallback_models": ["test-fallback-tmp"]} ``` 3. Delete the fallback target model via /model/delete (no warning shown in UI or API response). 4. Confirm the fallback still references the deleted model: ``` GET /fallback/test-primary-tmp → {"model": "test-primary-tmp", "fallback_models": ["test-fallback-tmp"], "fallback_type": "general"} ``` Orphaned reference confirmed — `test-fallback-tmp` no longer exists but the mapping persists. 5. Trigger a request to the primary model (which fails): ``` POST /v1/chat/completions {"model": "test-primary-tmp", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "test"}], "max_tokens": 5} ``` ## Error response (HTTP 500) ```json { "error": { "message": "litellm.InternalServerError: InternalServerError: OpenAIException - Connection error.. Received Model Group=test-primary-tmp Available Model Group Fallbacks=['test-fallback-tmp'] Error doing the fallback: litellm.BadRequestError: You passed in model=test-fallback-tmp. There are no healthy deployments for this model No fallback model group found for original model_group=test-fallback-tmp. Fallbacks=[<other production fallback mappings omitted>, {'test-primary-tmp': ['test-fallback-tmp']}]. Received Model Group=test-fallback-tmp Available Model Group Fallbacks=None Error doing the fallback: litellm.BadRequestError: You passed in model=test-fallback-tmp. There are no healthy deployments for this model LiteLLM Retried: 2 times, LiteLLM Max Retries: 2", "type": null, "param": null, "code": 500 } } ``` ## Relevant pod log ``` 19:09:41 - LiteLLM Proxy:DEBUG: common_request_processing.py:2686 - An error occurred: litellm.InternalServerError: InternalServerError: OpenAIException - Connection error.. Received Model Group=test-primary-tmp Available Model Group Fallbacks=['test-fallback-tmp'] Error doing the fallback: litellm.BadRequestError: You passed in model=test-fallback-tmp. There are no healthy deployments for this model No fallback model group found for original model_group=test-fallback-tmp. Fallbacks=[<other production fallback mappings omitted>, {'test-primary-tmp': ['test-fallback-tmp']}]. Received Model Group=test-fallback-tmp Available Model Group Fallbacks=None Error doing the fallback: litellm.BadRequestError: You passed in model=test-fallback-tmp. There are no healthy deployments for this model LiteLLM Retried: 2 times, LiteLLM Max Retries: 2 model_group: `test-primary-tmp` INFO: 127.0.0.1:59670 - "POST /v1/chat/completions HTTP/1.1" 500 Internal Server Error ``` ## Expected behavior 1. UI warning: when deleting a model referenced in a fallback, show a warning naming which model group(s) depend on it. 2. Cascade cleanup: if deleted anyway, automatically remove all fallback references pointing to it (or clearly flag them as broken). 3. Graceful degradation: when the fallback target no longer exists, return a clear "fallback model not available" error instead of a cascading retry loop with a generic 500. ## Actual behavior 1. No warning is shown in the UI when deleting a model referenced in fallbacks 2. The fallback mapping persists as an orphaned reference in the DB 3. When the primary model fails, the proxy attempts to fall back to the deleted model, which also fails, causing a cascade error with retries and a generic HTTP 500 ## Impact - Silent configuration corruption (orphaned DB reference) - Cascade failures when primary models go down, in place of clean failover - Hard to debug — verbose error doesn't clearly point at the root cause - No self-service fix short of manually discovering and calling DELETE /fallback/{model} ## Cleanup performed All test models and the fallback mapping were removed after reproduction; no production models or configurations were affected. --- Check for existing issues: I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. Related but not duplicates: #8331/#8332 (error deleting a fallback rule itself, different flow), #17729 (cascading failure from unhealthy deployments, different root cause), #29742 (proposes disable/enable to sidestep this, doesn't fix the validation gap).

signals.title: `split_concatenated_json_objects` raises `JSONDecodeError` on a malformed remainder, aborting the whole multi-tool-call turn
signals.text: ### What happened? `split_concatenated_json_objects` (litellm/litellm_core_utils/prompt_templates/common_utils.py) parses a raw string containing concatenated JSON objects (tool-call `arguments` from parallel tool calls). When one object in the sequence is truncated or otherwise malformed, `decoder.raw_decode(raw, idx)` raises `json.JSONDecodeError` uncaught, propagating out of the function and aborting the caller's (`parse_tool_call_arguments`) entire multi-tool-call turn — not just the one malformed call. ### Steps to Reproduce ```python from litellm.litellm_core_utils.prompt_templates.common_utils import ( split_concatenated_json_objects, ) split_concatenated_json_objects('{"a": 1}{"b": ') ``` Expected: returns `[{"a": 1}]` — the complete objects already decoded — so the caller can fall back to `{}` for the one unparseable tool call. Actual: raises `json.JSONDecodeError`. ### What part of LiteLLM is this about? Completions ### What LiteLLM version are you on? v1.94.3
signals.author: jimmychen-p72

signals.title: [Bug]: `content: null` is stripped from assistant messages with `tool_calls` before the provider call
signals.text: ### Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. ### What happened? # What happened For an assistant message carrying `tool_calls` and `content: null` — the shape the OpenAI spec prescribes for a tool-call-only turn — litellm removes the `content` key entirely before handing the request to the provider SDK. Providers that require the key to be present then reject the request. This is in the library, not the proxy: it reproduces with a plain `litellm.completion()` call. # Reproduction (no proxy, no provider, no API key) ```python import json, litellm from openai.resources.chat.completions import Completions captured = {} def spy(self, *a, **kw): captured["messages"] = kw.get("messages") raise RuntimeError("stop") Completions.create = spy # intercept at the litellm -> openai-SDK boundary msgs = [ {"role": "user", "content": "hi"}, {"role": "assistant", "content": None, "tool_calls": [{"id": "call_1", "type": "function", "function": {"name": "f", "arguments": "{}"}}]}, {"role": "tool", "tool_call_id": "call_1", "content": "ok"}, ] try: litellm.completion(model="openai/some-model", messages=msgs, max_tokens=1, api_base="http://127.0.0.1:1/v1", api_key="x", timeout=3) except Exception: pass print(json.dumps(captured["messages"][1])) print("content key present:", "content" in captured["messages"][1]) ``` Actual output: ``` {"role": "assistant", "tool_calls": [{"id": "call_1", "type": "function", "function": {"name": "f", "arguments": "{}"}}]} content key present: False ``` Expected: the message reaches the SDK as `{"role": "assistant", "content": null, "tool_calls": [...]}`. # Where it is *not* happening Called in isolation, these both preserve `content: null`: - `OpenAIGPTConfig.transform_request(...)` - `openai` SDK 2.33.0 — `maybe_transform(...)` and `client._build_request(...)` (inspected the final httpx body) `grep -rn "exclude_none=True"` over the installed package only matches under `llms/openai/responses/`. So the key is dropped earlier in the pre-processing path. # Real-world impact Against a provider whose deserialiser requires the key: ``` litellm.BadRequestError: OpenAIException - Failed to deserialize the JSON body into the target type: messages[1]: missing field `content` at line 1 column 165. ``` The identical body sent **directly** to the same provider returns `200`, as does one with `content: ""`. Only the key-absent form fails — which is what litellm produces. Confirmed against the proxy's own `POST Request Sent from LiteLLM` debug line: `content: null` goes in, no `content` key goes out. Any agent framework on the OpenAI SDK emits `content: null` for tool-call-only turns, so every multi-turn tool-calling conversation breaks against such providers. In our deployment this caused 28 failed agent runs over 8 days and looked like a provider fault, since the error text names the upstream. # Expected Forward `content: null` verbatim. If normalisation is intended, `""` is a safe substitute — dropping the key is not, since the two are not equivalent for strict deserialisers. # Ruled out - `drop_params: true` vs. removed — identical - 1.95.0 → 1.97.0 — no change - `modify_params` / message sanitization — only runs in the Anthropic transformation path - `custom_llm_provider: hosted_vllm` instead of `openai` — identical - `custom_llm_provider: openai_like` — not routable via the proxy (`Unmapped LLM provider for this endpoint`) # Environment - litellm `v1.97.0` (Docker `ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.97.0`), Python 3.13, `openai` SDK 2.33.0 - `custom_llm_provider: openai`, `drop_params: true` - Client in production: Cline 3.0.55 ### User Flow The application is an unattended documentation agent: a scheduled job wakes a Cline agent (v3.0.55) in a container, hands it a ticket, and the agent reads the repository, writes a wiki page or an ADR, and opens a PR. All of its model traffic goes to our self-hosted LiteLLM gateway at `https://ai-gateway.int.ai-in-action.de/v1`, model group `inceptron/GLM-5.2`. Multi-turn tool calling is the whole job — the agent reads files, runs commands, and writes files, one tool call at a time. ### Before a (hypothetical) fix The run dies on the second round trip, the moment the agent sends back a turn in which it only called a tool and wrote no prose. 1. The job starts the agent on ticket `CICD-338`. The agent sends `POST https://ai-gateway.int.ai-in-action.de/v1/chat/completions` with a system prompt, the ticket text, and its four tools (`read_files`, `run_commands`, `editor`, `submit_and_exit`). Returns `200`, body carries an id like `chatcmpl-948cc3d44e4d5cf95cf2dca81de44e8d` and an assistant message with `"content": null` and one `tool_calls` entry for `read_files`. 2. The agent reads the requested file locally and appends two messages to its history: the assistant turn it just received, verbatim (so `"content": null` plus `tool_calls`), and the tool result. 3. The agent sends the grown history to `POST https://ai-gateway.int.ai-in-action.de/v1/chat/completions`. Returns **`422`**: `litellm.BadRequestError: OpenAIException - Failed to deserialize the JSON body into the target type: messages[3]: missing field 'content' at line 1 column 20417. Received Model Group=inceptron/GLM-5.2`. No id, no assistant turn, nothing to continue from. 4. The agent retries the same history twice more. Same `422` each time, only the index in the message differs — observed at `messages[3]`, `[5]`, `[34]`, `[44]`, depending on where in the conversation the first prose-less turn sits. 5. The run ends after ~90 seconds with no wiki page, no ADR, no PR, and no output file. The operator sees only a failed run whose error text names the model provider, so the provider looks at fault. 6. After three such rounds the job stops picking up that ticket at all. It stays parked until someone clears the state by hand. Over 8 days this happened 28 times. 7. Sanity check the operator runs by hand: the exact same conversation sent directly to the provider at `POST https://api.inceptron.io/v1/chat/completions` returns `200` with an id like `chatcmpl-948cc3d4…`. The same conversation through the gateway returns `422`. No security or authorization consequence: no data is exposed, and no user gains access they shouldn't have. The damage is availability — long tool-calling runs cannot complete. ### After a (hypothetical) fix The same run continues past the second round trip and finishes the documentation task. 1. The job starts the agent on ticket `CICD-338`. The agent sends `POST https://ai-gateway.int.ai-in-action.de/v1/chat/completions` with a system prompt, the ticket text, and its four tools. Returns `200`, body carries an id like `chatcmpl-948cc3d44e4d5cf95cf2dca81de44e8d` and an assistant message with `"content": null` and one `tool_calls` entry for `read_files`. 2. The agent reads the requested file locally and appends two messages to its history: the assistant turn it just received, verbatim (so `"content": null` plus `tool_calls`), and the tool result. 3. The agent sends the grown history to `POST https://ai-gateway.int.ai-in-action.de/v1/chat/completions`. Returns **`200`**, with a fresh `chatcmpl-…` id and the next assistant turn — again `"content": null` plus a `tool_calls` entry, this time for `editor`. 4. Steps 2 and 3 repeat for roughly 40 further round trips, each returning `200`. The agent reads, edits, and commits. 5. The run ends after ~10 minutes with a wiki page written, a PR opened on branch `docs/CICD-338-doku`, and a result file the job can read. 6. The ticket moves on by itself. Nothing is parked, and nothing has to be cleared by hand. 7. Sanity check: the same conversation returns `200` both directly at `POST https://api.inceptron.io/v1/chat/completions` and through the gateway — the two agree. ### Proof the bug occurs See "what happened" ### What part of LiteLLM is this about? Proxy ### What LiteLLM version are you on ? v1.97.0 ### Twitter / LinkedIn details _No response_

signals.title: is_thinking_enabled crashes with AttributeError when thinking is passed as a bare bool (follow-up to #25792)
signals.text: ### What happened? `BaseConfig.is_thinking_enabled` (litellm/llms/base_llm/chat/transformation.py) does `(non_default_params.get("thinking") or {}).get("type") == "enabled"`. When `thinking` is a bare bool (`true`/`false`, per Claude Code's shorthand for the enabled flag, as opposed to the dict shape `{"type": "enabled"}`), `True or {}` evaluates to `True`, and `.get("type")` is then called on a bool — raising `AttributeError: 'bool' object has no attribute 'get'`. This is the same root-cause class as #25792 (a `None` thinking value from `_map_reasoning_effort("none", ...)` hits the same `.get()` chain) — any non-dict truthy `thinking` value breaks it, not just `None`. ### Steps to Reproduce ```python from litellm.llms.base_llm.chat.transformation import BaseConfig BaseConfig().is_thinking_enabled({"thinking": True}) ``` Expected: returns `True`. Actual: `AttributeError: 'bool' object has no attribute 'get'`. ### What part of LiteLLM is this about? Completions ### What LiteLLM version are you on? v1.94.3

signals.title: Completing a batch with output_file_id=None sets batch_processed=True unconditionally, permanently losing spend recovery
signals.text: ### What happened? In litellm/proxy/openai_files_endpoints/common_utils.py, when a batch's `db_status` transitions to `"complete"`, `update_data["batch_processed"] = True` is set unconditionally. `batch_processed=True` is the sole re-pickup gate for CheckBatchCost's cost-recovery poller (`_find_jobs` selects on `batch_processed=False`). A batch can legitimately reach `status="completed"` with `output_file_id` still `None` — either the provider response is briefly lagging before the output id populates, or every request line errored. Setting the flag unconditionally in the lagging case permanently retires the batch from any future cost-recovery pass, silently losing the spend record with no retry. ### Steps to Reproduce 1. Create a batch whose provider marks it `completed` before `output_file_id` is populated in the same response (a real, observed timing window). 2. The retrieve-success path sets `batch_processed=True` on that response. 3. Expected: the batch is only retired once the provider proves there were no successful lines (or its output file has actually arrived); otherwise it stays eligible for the next `CheckBatchCost` pass. 4. Actual: `batch_processed=True` is set immediately regardless, and the batch is never revisited even after its output file id later populates. ### What part of LiteLLM is this about? Proxy ### What LiteLLM version are you on? v1.94.3
signals.author: jimmychen-p72

signals.title: GET /v1/files has no way to list all files a caller owns without pinning a model
signals.text: ### What happened? Once an unscoped `GET /v1/files` (the shape `client.files.list()` produces, no `target_model_names`) is routed to the managed-files path instead of guessing a provider (see #35362), it still can't return anything: the only DB helper for listing managed files, `get_user_created_file_ids` (litellm_enterprise/proxy/hooks/managed_files.py), requires `model_object_ids` and filters with `"flat_model_file_ids": {"hasSome": model_object_ids}`. There is no model-agnostic query that returns "every file this caller owns." Ownership does not depend on a model — the existing owner filter used elsewhere in this file scopes by caller identity alone — so an unscoped listing is well defined and should return the caller's managed files, not an empty page or an error. A correct fix also needs real pagination: an admin key can own every file on the proxy, and OpenAI's Files API defaults/caps `limit` at 10000, so the result set needs `limit`/`after` handled at the DB layer (keyset pagination on `unified_file_id`), not loaded and filtered wholesale. ### Steps to Reproduce 1. Run a DB-backed proxy with managed files enabled and enough files that a caller owns more than one page. 2. Upload several files as the same caller with `target_model_names` pinned, so `LiteLLM_ManagedFileTable` accumulates owned rows. 3. Call `client.files.list()` (no `target_model_names`). 4. Expected: the caller's owned files, paginated with a stable cursor and an accurate `has_more`. 5. Observed: no code path returns owned files without a pinned model — `get_user_created_file_ids` requires `model_object_ids` it never has here. ### What part of LiteLLM is this about? Proxy ### What LiteLLM version are you on? v1.94.3
signals.author: jimmychen-p72

signals.title: [Bug]: /v1/messages drops the vendor half of `perplexity/perplexity/*` model ids — Agent API models 400, `sonar` silently answers off the chat endpoint
signals.text: ### Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. ### What happened? Perplexity's Agent API names its third-party models `<vendor>/<model>`, so a litellm deployment for one of them reads `model: perplexity/perplexity/kimi-k3`. That deployment answers on `/v1/responses` but returns 400 on `/v1/messages`, with Perplexity rejecting `Invalid model 'kimi-k3'`. The vendor half of the id is dropped somewhere on the Anthropic Messages path, so what reaches Perplexity is a name it has never heard of The same drop happens quietly for `perplexity/perplexity/sonar`, which is already in the shipped cost map. There the shortened name `sonar` happens to be a real Perplexity chat model, so `/v1/messages` returns 200, but it answers off the chat endpoint rather than the Agent API the deployment asked for, and the spend recorded is litellm's own per-token math instead of the amount Perplexity metered I expected `/v1/messages` to reach the same model `/v1/responses` reaches, since both point at one deployment ### User Flow Before a (hypothetical) fix: a developer running an Anthropic-SDK app against a Perplexity Agent API model gets a 400 naming a model they never asked for 1. Their proxy admin adds a deployment named `kimi-k3` pointing at `perplexity/perplexity/kimi-k3` and restarts the proxy 2. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/responses with `"model": "kimi-k3"` and get a 200 whose output text reads `pong` 3. They point their Anthropic SDK at the proxy and send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages with the same `"model": "kimi-k3"` 4. They get a 400 reading `Invalid model 'kimi-k3'. Permitted models can be found in the documentation at https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/getting-started/models.`, naming a model id neither they nor their admin ever wrote 5. Swapping in the shipped `perplexity/perplexity/sonar` deployment hides the failure instead of fixing it: POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages returns 200, but the answer comes back without the Agent API's search results, and https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs records a different dollar amount than Perplexity's own dashboard bills for that call After a (hypothetical) fix: the same request answers on `/v1/messages` exactly as it does on `/v1/responses` 1. Their proxy admin adds the same deployment and restarts the proxy 2. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/responses with `"model": "kimi-k3"` and get a 200 whose output text reads `pong` 3. They point their Anthropic SDK at the proxy and send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages with the same `"model": "kimi-k3"` 4. They get a 200 whose content text reads `pong` 5. The shipped `perplexity/perplexity/sonar` deployment answers off the Agent API on `/v1/messages` too, and https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs shows the amount Perplexity metered for the call ### Proof the bug occurs Config the proxy ran with (`pplx_config.yaml`): ```yaml model_list: - model_name: kimi-k3 litellm_params: model: perplexity/perplexity/kimi-k3 api_key: os.environ/PERPLEXITY_API_KEY general_settings: master_key: sk-1234 ``` Env vars: `PERPLEXITY_API_KEY=<redacted>`, nothing else set Commit: `edbb3429a3` on `litellm_internal_staging` (v1.99.0), started with `python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config pplx_config.yaml --port 43821 --detailed_debug` Commands and their full output: 1. The model answers on `/v1/responses` ``` $ curl -s -D - http://localhost:43821/v1/responses \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model":"kimi-k3","input":"Reply with exactly: pong","max_output_tokens":2048}' HTTP/1.1 200 OK {"model": "kimi-k3", "status": "completed", "output": [{"type": "message", "content": [{"type": "output_text", "text": "pong"}]}]} ``` 2. The same model, same proxy, on `/v1/messages` ``` $ curl -s -D - http://localhost:43821/v1/messages \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model":"kimi-k3","max_tokens":2048,"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Reply with exactly: pong"}]}' HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request {"error":{"message":"litellm.BadRequestError: PerplexityException - Invalid model 'kimi-k3'. Permitted models can be found in the documentation at https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/getting-started/models.. Received Model Group=kimi-k3\nAvailable Model Group Fallbacks=None","type":null,"param":null,"code":"400"}} ``` 3. The shipped `perplexity/perplexity/sonar` deployment (`model_name: agent-sonar`) on the same proxy returns 200 on `/v1/messages`, but off the chat endpoint ``` $ curl -s -D - http://localhost:43821/v1/messages \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model":"agent-sonar","max_tokens":256,"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Reply with exactly: pong"}]}' HTTP/1.1 200 OK x-litellm-response-cost: 5.999999999999999e-06 {"id":"0122f771-c977-4952-b4e3-e217031c637a","type":"message","role":"assistant","model":"agent-sonar","stop_sequence":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":5,"output_tokens":1},"content":[{"type":"text","text":"pong"}],"stop_reason":"end_turn"} ``` The 5 input and 1 output tokens priced at 6e-06 are litellm's own per-token math for Perplexity's `sonar` chat model, not what the Agent API metered ### What part of LiteLLM is this about? Proxy ### What LiteLLM version are you on ? v1.99.0 ### Twitter / LinkedIn details _No response_
