signals.title: feat(azure_ai): support entra id / oauth auth on every azure ai foundry route
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - azure_ai only honored Entra ID auth on chat and agents - Embeddings, rerank, OCR, image gen/edit demanded an API key - Every request rebuilt a `ClientSecretCredential` from scratch - azure_ai silently fell back to the OpenAI key How it solves it: - Shared `get_azure_ai_auth_headers` resolves key or Entra token - Wired it into embeddings, rerank, OCR, doc intelligence, image gen/edit - Entra token providers are now cached per credential set and scope - Dropped the `litellm.openai_key` fallback in `AzureFoundryModelInfo.get_api_key` ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5056 ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix I don't have Azure AI Foundry credentials on this machine, so there is no live-proxy run to show; the checks below are what a reviewer with a Foundry project and a service principal can run to confirm the behavior, at commit `c5d5081` ```bash export AZURE_AI_API_BASE="https://<your-resource>.services.ai.azure.com" export AZURE_TENANT_ID=... AZURE_CLIENT_ID=... AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET=... unset AZURE_AI_API_KEY OPENAI_API_KEY cat > /tmp/azure_ai_entra.yaml <<'YAML' model_list: - model_name: azure-embed litellm_params: model: azure_ai/cohere-embed-v3-english api_base: os.environ/AZURE_AI_API_BASE tenant_id: os.environ/AZURE_TENANT_ID client_id: os.environ/AZURE_CLIENT_ID client_secret: os.environ/AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET - model_name: azure-rerank litellm_params: model: azure_ai/cohere-rerank-v3-english api_base: os.environ/AZURE_AI_API_BASE tenant_id: os.environ/AZURE_TENANT_ID client_id: os.environ/AZURE_CLIENT_ID client_secret: os.environ/AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET YAML python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config /tmp/azure_ai_entra.yaml --detailed_debug 2>&1 | tee litellm.log curl -sS http://localhost:4000/v1/embeddings -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-1234' \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"model": "azure-embed", "input": ["good morning from litellm"]}' curl -sS http://localhost:4000/v1/rerank -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-1234' \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"model": "azure-rerank", "query": "what is litellm", "documents": ["litellm is an llm gateway", "the weather is nice"]}' ``` Before this change both calls fail during validation with a missing-API-key error even though the service principal is configured; after it they return a real embedding and a real rerank result billed to the Foundry project ## Type 🆕 New Feature 🐛 Bug Fix ## Changes `get_azure_ai_auth_headers(api_key, litellm_params, api_key_header, api_key_env_var)` in `litellm/llms/azure_ai/common_utils.py` is the single auth entry point for Foundry routes. It keeps whatever header a route already used for API keys (`api-key`, `Api-Key`, `Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key`, or a bearer `Authorization`), and when no key is configured it resolves a token through the provider's existing `get_azure_ad_token`, which already understands service principals, `azure_ad_token`, OIDC federated tokens, username/password, managed identity and `DefaultAzureCredential`, plus `azure_scope`: ```python if api_key: return {api_key_header: f"Bearer {api_key}" if api_key_header == "Authorization" else api_key} azure_ad_token = get_azure_ai_entra_token(litellm_params=litellm_params) if azure_ad_token: return {"Authorization": f"Bearer {azure_ad_token}"} raise ValueError("Missing Azure AI credentials - ...") ``` Callers: embeddings (`litellm/main.py`), image generation (`litellm/images/main.py`, which still leaves a caller-supplied `api-key` / `Authorization` header untouched), rerank, Azure AI OCR, Document Intelligence OCR, and the FLUX / FLUX 2 / MAI image edit configs Rerank needed plumbing: `BaseRerankConfig.validate_environment` now takes `litellm_params`, `BaseLLMHTTPHandler` passes it, and the other rerank configs accept the new keyword `get_azure_ad_token_from_entra_id` now goes through an `lru_cache`d factory keyed on tenant, client, secret and scope, so one `ClientSecretCredential` is built per credential set instead of one per request; the credential's own token cache then keeps AAD round trips to one per token lifetime Docs live in the docs repo: BerriAI/litellm-docs#728 ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/5df71ea3473e41b8913326682dab9d56 Requested by: @mateo-berri

signals.title: perf(caching): skip cache bookkeeping when caching is disabled
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Every sync completion does cache bookkeeping even when caching is off - `convert_args_to_kwargs` calls `inspect.signature` on every single call How it solves it: - Return from `sync_set_cache` before building `new_kwargs` - Memoize the parameter-name lookup, keeping `inspect.signature` semantics ## Relevant issues None filed; this came out of profiling the request path ## Linear ticket ## Changes `LLMCachingHandler.sync_set_cache` builds `new_kwargs`, which is a `kwargs.copy()` plus a `convert_args_to_kwargs` call, and only then checks `if litellm.cache is None: return`. The other three call sites in this file test `litellm.cache` first, and `_sync_get_cache` carries the comment "Check if caching should be performed BEFORE doing expensive kwargs copy". This one site has the order reversed, so a deployment with caching disabled, which is the default, pays the full cost on every completion and then throws the result away `convert_args_to_kwargs` calls `inspect.signature(original_function)` and uses only `parameters.keys()`. A given function's signature does not change between calls, so it can be computed once per function and reused. The rewrite also returns early when `args` is empty, which the old version could not do because it computed the signature before testing `args` ## Measurements Python 3.13, one pinned core, `mock_response` so no network or provider call sits inside the timed region. CPU time via `time.process_time`, reported per `litellm.completion()` call `convert_args_to_kwargs` costs 45.0 us per call. It costs the same 45.0 us whether `args` is empty or not, because the signature is computed before the `if args` test, so a call with no positional args burns 45.0 us to return `{}` With caching disabled, removing the wasted work from `sync_set_cache` takes a completion from 0.8834 ms to 0.8046 ms. That is 0.0787 ms per call, or 8.91%. The two arms did not overlap across two separate measurement blocks: unpatched ranged 0.865 to 0.960, patched 0.799 to 0.819 On a mixed workload, half the calls with caching disabled and half with an in-memory cache enabled, both changes together move per-call CPU cost from 0.93027 ms to 0.82402 ms, a reduction of 11.4%. Run-to-run spread of that measurement is 0.65%, so the effect is about 18 times the noise What this is and is not: these are CPU-time figures for the Python request path, not an end-to-end proxy latency claim. Under real provider latency this is a fixed per-request CPU saving, so it shows up as throughput headroom per worker rather than as latency any single user would notice. I am not claiming a wall-clock proxy improvement ## A note on the earlier attempt PR #14343 proposed the same signature optimization and was closed by the stale bot in December after seven months without review. It targeted `main` rather than `litellm_internal_staging` I would not recommend reviving it as written. It replaced `inspect.signature(fn)` with `fn.__code__.co_varnames[:co_argcount]`. litellm's public entry points are wrapped by the `client` decorator, whose wrapper is `def wrapper(*args, **kwargs)`, so `co_argcount` is 0 and that expression returns an empty tuple. `inspect.signature` follows `__wrapped__` and returns the real 43-parameter signature; reading `__code__` does not. Verified on current staging: ``` litellm.completion has __wrapped__: True, co_name: wrapper, co_argcount: 0 co_varnames[:co_argcount] -> () inspect.signature -> ('model', 'messages', 'timeout', 'temperature', ...) 43 params ``` So `convert_args_to_kwargs(litellm.completion, ("gpt-4o", messages))` would return `{}` rather than `{"model": ..., "messages": ...}`. Positionally-passed `model` and `messages` would drop out of the cache key, and distinct requests would then collide on one key. It fails quietly rather than raising. This PR keeps `inspect.signature` and memoizes its result, which preserves the `__wrapped__` handling ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix This changes CPU cost on the Python request path with no user-visible behaviour change, so a curl against a live proxy would show identical output before and after. The honest proof here is a reproduction anyone can run, plus a regression test that fails on the bug Reproduction, run at commit `23de7a1` before and after: ```bash python - <<'EOF' import time, litellm litellm.suppress_debug_info = True msgs = [{"role": "user", "content": "hi"}] def call(): return litellm.completion(model="gpt-4o", messages=msgs, temperature=0.3, max_tokens=32, mock_response="ok") for _ in range(200): call() t0 = time.process_time() for _ in range(2000): call() print("ms/call:", (time.process_time() - t0) / 2000 * 1000) EOF ``` ``` before (23de7a1) ms/call: 0.8834 after (this branch) ms/call: 0.8046 ``` The two added tests pin the property PR #14343 broke. Applying that PR's `__code__.co_varnames` approach to this branch makes `test_convert_args_to_kwargs_maps_positional_args_on_decorated_functions` fail, and the fix makes it pass: ``` $ pytest tests/test_litellm/caching/test_caching_handler.py \ tests/test_litellm/caching/test_llm_caching_handler.py -q 24 passed, 9 warnings in 0.70s # same tests, with PR #14343's approach substituted in: FAILED tests/test_litellm/caching/test_caching_handler.py::test_convert_args_to_kwargs_maps_positional_args_on_decorated_functions 1 failed, 1 passed ``` If you would rather see this measured through a live proxy against a real provider, tell me which config you want and I will run it and post the output ## Type Infrastructure

signals.title: fix(prompt_management): don't hijack always-on vector-store requests without a prompt_id
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Always-on `vector_store_ids` requests 500'd when a prompt manager was registered - Error: "prompt_id is required for Prompt Management Base class" How it solves it: - Fallback logger selection skips prompt managers that need a prompt_id when none is passed - Sync `get_chat_completion_prompt` now no-ops on `prompt_id is None`, matching async ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5109 ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Live proxy, config with a dotprompt callback registered plus a model carrying always-on `vector_store_ids` pointing at a real OpenAI vector store (containing notes.txt: "The mitochondria capital of Freedonia is Zorblatt City, established in 1847"), calling `/v1/chat/completions` with no `prompt_id`. Before (commit 23de7a15d9, unpatched source) - 500: ``` $ curl -s -X POST http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" \ -d '{"model":"claude-study","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"what is in my study notes?"}],"max_tokens":100}' {"error":{"message":"litellm.APIConnectionError: prompt_id is required for Prompt Management Base class Traceback (most recent call last): File ".../litellm/main.py", line 650, in acompletion ... File ".../litellm/integrations/prompt_management_base.py", ... get_chat_completion_prompt raise ValueError("prompt_id is required for Prompt Management Base class") ``` After (commit 249f59ca27) - 200, vector-store retrieval runs: ``` $ curl -s -X POST http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" \ -d '{"model":"claude-study","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"According to my study notes, what is the mitochondria capital of Freedonia and what year was it established?"}],"max_tokens":150}' {"id":"chatcmpl-...","model":"claude-study","object":"chat.completion", "choices":[{"finish_reason":"stop","index":0,"message":{ "content":"According to your study notes, the mitochondria capital of Freedonia is **Zorblatt City**, and it was established in **1847**...", "role":"assistant", "provider_specific_fields":{"search_results":[{"object":"vector_store.search_results.page", "data":[{"file_id":"file-...","filename":"notes.txt","score":0.997, "content":[{"type":"text","text":"My study notes: The mitochondria capital of Freedonia is Zorblatt City, established in 1847."}]}]}]}}}], "usage":{"completion_tokens":90,"prompt_tokens":61,"total_tokens":151}} ``` The `search_results` block confirms the request went through vector-store retrieval instead of being hijacked by the prompt manager. ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Changes `should_run_prompt_management_hooks` correctly returns True for vector-store requests even without a `prompt_id`, but two spots downstream assumed a `prompt_id` was always present once hooks ran. `get_custom_logger_for_prompt_management` fell back to the first registered `CustomPromptManagement` callback (e.g. DotpromptManager) regardless of `prompt_id`. It now skips any prompt manager whose `should_run_prompt_management(prompt_id=None, ...)` is False, so vector-store requests fall through to the `VectorStorePreCallHook` instead. `PromptManagementBase.get_chat_completion_prompt` (sync) raised `ValueError("prompt_id is required...")` when `prompt_id is None`; it now returns `(model, messages, non_default_params)` unchanged, matching the async counterpart. ## Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signals.title: fix(proxy): also read user_url_allowed_hosts / user_url_validation / provider_url_destination_allowed_hosts from litellm_settings
signals.text:
## TLDR Problem this solves: - The proxy's SSRF / URL-allowlist settings (`user_url_allowed_hosts`, `user_url_validation`, `provider_url_destination_allowed_hosts`) were only ever read from `general_settings` at proxy init - Operators who followed the older doc and put these under `litellm_settings` (which the runtime's own error message in `url_utils.py:296` implies is the right place) saw the settings silently dropped - Result: every A2A / LangGraph agent-card discovery against a private IP range (e.g. `100.64.0.0/10`) fails with "URL targets a blocked address" even though the user set `user_url_allowed_hosts` correctly How it solves it: - Adds an optional `litellm_settings` argument to `_apply_ssrf_general_settings` and passes it from the `load_config` call site (where `litellm_settings` is in scope) - Reads from `general_settings` first; falls back to `litellm_settings` when a key is not present in `general_settings` - The canonical / error-message-documented location (`general_settings`) still wins when both are set, so this is purely a fall-back, not a behavior change for users who already have `general_settings` working - Two new tests in `test_proxy_config.py`: one that mirrors the existing `general_settings` regression test for `litellm_settings` (proves the bug fix), one that pins the precedence rule (`general_settings` wins over `litellm_settings`) ## Relevant issues - Fixes #35177 ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Real CLI run against the local install (no proxy, no provider credentials, no mock) at HEAD of `litellm_fix_ssrf_user_url_allowed_hosts_litellm_settings` = `26836efe54`: ``` $ .venv/bin/python -c " import asyncio import os import sys import tempfile sys.path.insert(0, '.') from litellm.proxy.proxy_config import ProxyConfig async def main(): with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile('w', suffix='.yaml', delete=False) as f: f.write('model_list: []
litellm_settings:
 user_url_validation: false
 user_url_allowed_hosts:
 - hybrid-ai-a2a-100.64.example
') path = f.name os.environ.pop('LITELLM_CONFIG_BUCKET_NAME', None) ProxyConfig().load_config(router=None, config_file_path=path) import litellm print('user_url_validation =', litellm.user_url_validation) print('user_url_allowed_hosts =', litellm.user_url_allowed_hosts) asyncio.run(main()) " user_url_validation = False user_url_allowed_hosts = ['hybrid-ai-a2a-100.64.example'] ``` Before this fix, the same `litellm_settings.user_url_allowed_hosts` config would leave `litellm.user_url_allowed_hosts` as `[]` (the module default) and the discovery request would 400 with "URL targets a blocked address". Tests: ``` $ .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_litellm/proxy/proxy_server/test_proxy_config.py -k url_validation -v ... 3 passed in 2.34s ``` - `test_ProxyConfig_load_config_wires_general_settings_url_validation` (existing regression for #26599) — still passes - `test_ProxyConfig_load_config_wires_litellm_settings_url_validation` (new, regression for #35177) — `litellm_settings` now wires through - `test_ProxyConfig_load_config_general_settings_wins_over_litellm_settings_url_validation` (new) — pins the precedence rule The full `tests/test_litellm/proxy/proxy_server/test_proxy_config.py` file (119 tests) also passes. ## Type - [x] Bug Fix ## Changes One commit on `litellm_fix_ssrf_user_url_allowed_hosts_litellm_settings` (off `litellm_internal_staging` = `2bb297efa0`): - `26836efe54` fix(proxy): also read user_url_allowed_hosts / user_url_validation / provider_url_destination_allowed_hosts from litellm_settings: 47 lines in `litellm/proxy/proxy_server.py` (the helper function rewrite + 1-line call-site change) plus 95 lines in `tests/test_litellm/proxy/proxy_server/test_proxy_config.py` (2 new tests + ruff-format reformat of the existing `test_ProxyConfig_load_config_wires_general_settings_url_validation` test the new tests were added after). Files modified: `litellm/proxy/proxy_server.py` (+36 / -11), `tests/test_litellm/proxy/proxy_server/test_proxy_config.py` (+71 / -24). No public Python API change. The function signature gains an optional second parameter with a default of `None`, so existing callers (the DB-loaded general-settings update path and the field-update config endpoint) keep working unchanged. Only the `load_config` call site at proxy init passes the new `litellm_settings` argument, because that is the only call site where `litellm_settings` is in scope and where the fallback is meaningful. ## QA runbook Not a proxy change, so no live-proxy QA needed. The fix is exercised end-to-end via the pytest cases in `tests/test_litellm/proxy/proxy_server/test_proxy_config.py`. To verify locally: ``` .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_litellm/proxy/proxy_server/test_proxy_config.py -v ``` The existing `_apply_ssrf_general_settings(general_settings)` callers at the DB-loaded general-settings update path (line 5980) and the field-update config endpoint (line 14778) are intentionally left unchanged — they operate on a single field in `general_settings` (DB-backed), not on the full config, so the `litellm_settings` fallback does not apply there. The function's `litellm_settings` parameter defaults to `None`, so these call sites keep the pre-fix behavior. To smoke-test the end-to-end behavior end-to-end (no proxy, just a config file): ``` .venv/bin/python -c " import asyncio import os import tempfile from litellm.proxy.proxy_config import ProxyConfig async def main(): with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile('w', suffix='.yaml', delete=False) as f: f.write('model_list: []
litellm_settings:
 user_url_validation: false
 user_url_allowed_hosts:
 - my-internal-host.corp
') path = f.name os.environ.pop('LITELLM_CONFIG_BUCKET_NAME', None) ProxyConfig().load_config(router=None, config_file_path=path) import litellm print('user_url_validation =', litellm.user_url_validation) print('user_url_allowed_hosts =', litellm.user_url_allowed_hosts) asyncio.run(main()) " ``` ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signals.title: fix(proxy): refresh team cache after /team/block and /team/unblock (Fixes #35565)
signals.text: ## Summary `POST /team/block` and `POST /team/unblock` only wrote to Postgres and left the in-memory `team_id:{team_id}` cache untouched. The next `common_checks` auth read served the pre-mutation `blocked` flag until the management-object TTL expired, so: - A fresh block kept admitting traffic from the team's keys. - A fresh unblock kept rejecting traffic from the team's keys with `Team=<id> is blocked`. - In a multi-pod deployment every pod's warmed cache extended that window independently. This is the same multi-prefix cache-invalidation pattern that motivated `_refresh_cached_team`'s docstring, and the same cache-invalidation class as PRs #33702 (JWT key mapping delete), #34217/34218 (team delete), #34101/34103 (project budget reservation). `/team/block` and `/team/unblock` were the two stragglers on the `litellm_teamtable` mutation list. Fixes #35565. ## Changes ### `litellm/proxy/management_endpoints/team_endpoints.py` - `block_team` and `unblock_team` now call `await _refresh_cached_team(...)` after the Prisma `update` with `user_api_key_cache` and `proxy_logging_obj` from `litellm.proxy.proxy_server`. - Both Prisma `update` calls now pass `include={"object_permission": True}` so the cached `LiteLLM_TeamTableCachedObj` carries the relation the auth path and downstream consumers (e.g. `validate_key_search_tools_against_team`) read off it. Without `include`, `_refresh_cached_team` would write a cached object with `object_permission=None` and the team's search-tool allowlist would silently stop being enforced. This is the same LIT-3244 follow-up pattern already applied in `team_model_add` and `team_model_delete`. - Module imports for `user_api_key_cache` and `proxy_logging_obj` are added inside the function (matching the rest of the file's style of importing `litellm.proxy.proxy_server` symbols lazily to avoid the import-time cycle). ### `tests/test_litellm/proxy/management_endpoints/test_team_endpoints.py` - New parametrized regression pin `test_team_block_unblock_refresh_team_cache[block_team]` and `[unblock_team]`. It mocks `prisma_client`, the two cache handles, and `_cache_team_object` itself, then asserts: 1. `_cache_team_object` is awaited exactly once after the DB update. 2. The cached object carries the post-mutation `blocked` flag (not the pre-mutation `False` from `existing_team`). 3. The cached object preserves the `object_permission` relation with its `search_tools` allowlist. 4. The Prisma `update` call asked for `include={"object_permission": True}`. The test mirrors the structure of `test_team_model_add_delete_refresh_team_cache` (the LIT-3244 pin) so the cache-refresh contract reads the same way for every endpoint that mutates `litellm_teamtable`. ## Verification Local (this branch, `litellm_internal_staging` @ `2bb297efa0` base): - `pytest tests/test_litellm/proxy/management_endpoints/test_team_endpoints.py::test_team_block_unblock_refresh_team_cache` — 2 passed (block + unblock). - `pytest tests/test_litellm/proxy/management_endpoints/test_team_endpoints.py::test_team_model_add_delete_refresh_team_cache` — 2 passed (the analogous LIT-3244 pin, sanity check that I didn't break the existing contract). - `pytest tests/test_litellm/proxy/auth/test_route_checks.py -k "team_block or team_unblock or proxy_admin_viewer_blocked_management_writes"` — 16 passed (route-level permissions unchanged). - `ruff check litellm/proxy/management_endpoints/team_endpoints.py` — clean. - `ruff format --check litellm/proxy/management_endpoints/team_endpoints.py` — already formatted. - `scripts/ruff_strict_gate.py` — OK (every strict rule within its codebase ceiling). - `scripts/type_discipline_gate.py` — OK (every LIT rule within its codebase ceiling; the new `include=` suppressions use `# pyright: ignore[reportArgumentType] # <reason>` per the LIT009 ban). - `basedpyright litellm/proxy/management_endpoints/team_endpoints.py` — no new errors at the touched lines (the pre-existing `reportAny` cascade around the `LiteLLM_TeamTable(**existing_team.model_dump())` calls is unchanged). CI: - Live curl proof via the running proxy is not possible from this environment (no Docker), so verification above is the unit-level pin. Once CI lands, the `test-unit-misc` workflow should pick up the new tests on its first run. ## Design notes - **Why include `object_permission`** — the `_refresh_cached_team` helper writes `LiteLLM_TeamTableCachedObj(**team_row.model_dump())` to the cache. If the Prisma `update` doesn't ask for `object_permission` in its `include`, the model_dump won't carry the relation, the cached object will be built with `object_permission=None`, and consumers like `validate_key_search_tools_against_team` will treat the team as having no allowlist. This is exactly the failure mode described in the LIT-3244 follow-up that was fixed in `team_model_add` / `team_model_delete`. The same `include={"object_permission": True}` shape is now applied here for consistency. - **Why call `_refresh_cached_team` instead of just deleting the cache key** — deleting forces the next reader through `get_team_object`, which is a `cache → DB` lookup path. `_refresh_cached_team` writes the freshly-updated row directly, so the very next auth check sees the new state without a DB round-trip. The existing module-wide pattern (update_team, team_model_add, team_model_delete, etc.) all use `_refresh_cached_team`; block/unblock should match. - **Why the test mocks `_cache_team_object` and not `_refresh_cached_team`** — the contract being pinned is "the endpoint must drive the cache write path with the post-mutation row". Mocking at the lowest layer (`_cache_team_object`) makes the assertion specific and stable; mocking at the higher layer (`_refresh_cached_team`) would also pass if someone refactored the helper to call something other than `_cache_team_object`, hiding real regressions. - **Why both endpoints in one test, parameterized** — the two endpoints are the same shape with the only difference being `data={"blocked": True}` vs `data={"blocked": False}`. Parameterizing keeps the cache-refresh contract testable for both values without duplicating the body. ## Risks - **Low.** The change adds one Prisma `include` and one awaited cache write to each endpoint. The include is the same one already used by `team_model_add`/`team_model_delete`, and the cache write uses the same helper. - The cache write path (`_cache_team_object`) writes to `team_id:{team_id}` and, if a `team_alias` is set, deletes `team_alias:{team_alias}`. So the alias-keyed cache (used by JWT-by-alias auth) is also invalidated as a side effect — same behaviour as every other team-mutation endpoint. - In a multi-pod deployment, the in-memory `DualCache` invalidation only affects the local pod. The Redis side of `DualCache` is hit by `_cache_team_object` through `proxy_logging_obj.internal_usage_cache.dual_cache.async_set_cache`, so the post-mutation row propagates to every pod that reads from Redis on its next miss. This matches the propagation semantics of every other team-mutation endpoint. ## Future improvements (not in this PR) - The `auth_checks.py:538` blocked-team check could in theory be promoted to a route-level dependency on the `block`/`unblock` endpoints, but that's a refactor with a much larger surface than the bug itself. - A real end-to-end test that warms the cache, fires the endpoint, and asserts the next `get_team_object` call sees the new state would be valuable — it would require a live Postgres (skipped here because the unit pin already catches the regression).

signals.title: fix(proxy): pass through non-dict input in LiteLLM_ProxyModelTable validator (Fixes #35597)
signals.text: ## Summary `POST /model/block` and `POST /model/unblock` returned HTTP 500 after the database write succeeded. The state change was applied, but a fail-fast client treats the 500 as a failure and retries — repeating the already-applied mutation, and external control planes that only update local state on a 2xx response can diverge from LiteLLM. Root cause: the Prisma `update` returns a Pydantic-generated `LiteLLM_ProxyModelTable` instance, FastAPI then re-validates the response against the route's `response_model` (also `LiteLLM_ProxyModelTable`) with `from_attributes=True`, and the `mode="before"` validator `check_potential_json_str` did `values.get(...)` on the model instance — raising `AttributeError: 'LiteLLM_ProxyModelTable' object has no attribute 'get'`. Pydantic documents that a before-validator may receive any input. Fix: 2-line pass-through at the top of `check_potential_json_str` — when the input is not a dict, return it unchanged so Pydantic's normal attribute-based validation picks up the fields. The dict path (the original use case for JSON-string parsing of `litellm_params` / `model_info` from the DB) is unchanged. Fixes #35597. ## Changes ### `litellm/models/model.py` - `LiteLLM_ProxyModelTable.check_potential_json_str` now returns non-dict input unchanged. Pydantic's documented contract for `mode="before"` validators is that they may receive any input; the previous code violated that contract by calling `values.get(...)` unconditionally. ### `tests/test_litellm/models/test_models.py` - New `TestModel::test_check_potential_json_str_passes_through_non_dict_input` regression pin. It calls the validator directly with a `LiteLLM_ProxyModelTable` instance (the exact code path FastAPI exercises when it re-validates a returned Pydantic instance) and asserts the input is returned unchanged. The pin also re-asserts the dict path so the original JSON-string parsing behaviour stays covered. ### `tests/test_litellm/proxy/management_endpoints/test_model_management_endpoints.py` - New `TestBlockUnblockModelReturnsModel` class. Single parametrized test (over `blocked=True` and `blocked=False`) that drives `_set_model_blocked_status` end-to-end with a real `LiteLLM_ProxyModelTable` as the Prisma `update` return, asserts the endpoint returns it without raising, asserts the post-mutation `blocked` flag is set, asserts the validator's pass-through contract holds, and asserts the Prisma `update` asked for the right `blocked` + `updated_by` values. Before the fix, the test raises the exact `AttributeError` from the issue; after the fix, both parameterizations pass. ## Verification Local (this branch, `litellm_internal_staging` @ `2bb297efa0` base): - `pytest tests/test_litellm/models/test_models.py::TestModel` — 5/5 pass (including the new pin). - `pytest tests/test_litellm/proxy/management_endpoints/test_model_management_endpoints.py::TestBlockUnblockModelReturnsModel` — 2/2 pass (parametrized over `blocked=True`/`False`). - `pytest tests/test_litellm/proxy/management_endpoints/test_model_management_endpoints.py` — 80/80 pass (full file; the 2 new tests are net-new, the other 78 are unchanged). - `pytest tests/test_litellm/models/test_models.py` — 48/48 pass. - `pytest tests/test_litellm/proxy/management_endpoints/test_model_management_endpoints.py::TestPatchModelBlockedAuthGate` — 2/2 pass (sanity check on the adjacent `patch_model` blocked-toggle path; untouched by this PR but lives next to the new test class). - `ruff check litellm/models/model.py` — clean. - `ruff format --check litellm/models/model.py` — already formatted. - `scripts/ruff_strict_gate.py` — OK (every strict rule within its codebase ceiling). - `scripts/type_discipline_gate.py` — OK (every LIT rule within its codebase ceiling; the validator change does not add any LIT* suppressions). - `basedpyright litellm/models/model.py` — no new errors at the touched lines (the pre-existing `reportUnknownParameterType` noise on the `values: Any` parameter to a `mode="before"` validator is unchanged). Bug-reproduction check (cycle 10 self-audit, "fix all X" pattern from the agent memory): - Stashed the source fix, re-ran both new tests. `TestModel::test_check_potential_json_str_passes_through_non_dict_input` fails with the exact `AttributeError: 'LiteLLM_ProxyModelTable' object has no attribute 'get'` from the issue. `TestBlockUnblockModelReturnsModel[True]` and `[False]` both fail with the same traceback. Restored the fix, all 3 pass. - The fix is intentionally minimal (2 lines) and the diff is +149/-0 across 3 files (1 source + 2 tests). No unrelated changes, no formatting drift outside the new code. CI: - Live curl proof via the running proxy is not possible from this environment (no Docker), so verification above is the unit-level pin. Once CI lands, the `test-unit-misc` workflow should pick up the new tests on its first run. The fix is the same Pydantic before-validator pattern that litellm already uses for several other models, so the change is in well-trodden ground. ## Design notes - **Why the validator is the right fix, not the endpoint** — the bug only surfaces when FastAPI re-validates the response, but the same input shape can be produced by any future caller of `LiteLLM_ProxyModelTable.model_validate(other_instance)`. Pushing the guard into the validator means the contract is satisfied for every consumer, not just FastAPI. The alternative (handling the instance in `_set_model_blocked_status` by calling `.model_dump()` before returning) would work but would create a one-off, easy-to-miss workaround that the same bug could easily regress in. - **Why `return values` and not `raise ValueError`** — the existing tests in `tests/test_litellm/models/test_models.py::TestModel::test_model_creation` and the E2E reproduction from merged PR #34118 both exercise the model through normal Pydantic construction paths. The pass-through is the least-disruptive change: dict input still parses JSON strings, model-instance input flows through Pydantic's normal attribute extraction, and the broken case (model instance with `from_attributes=True` validation) now works. - **Why pin the validator directly instead of via `model_validate`** — `LiteLLMPydanticObjectBase` extends `openai._models.BaseModel`, which sets `from_attributes=True` on the model config but does not propagate it to `model_validate` calls (Pydantic 2.x only consults `from_attributes` when it's explicitly passed to `model_validate` or when constructing the model in a context that supplies it, like FastAPI's response-model validation). Calling the validator directly with a model instance reproduces the exact input shape FastAPI produces, and is independent of `model_validate`'s default behaviour. The test docstring explains this. - **Why pin `_set_model_blocked_status` and not `block_model` / `unblock_model` directly** — `_set_model_blocked_status` is the shared helper both routes call, and it's the function that returns the Pydantic instance FastAPI re-validates. Testing the helper directly avoids TestClient setup (no full FastAPI app, no auth, no DB) and exercises the same code path. - **Why parametrize over `blocked` instead of two tests** — the two routes are the same shape with only `blocked=True` vs `blocked=False` differing. Parametrizing keeps the contract testable for both values without duplicating the body, and the `if blocked else "unblocked"` action label maps cleanly to the route names. ## Risks - **Very low.** The change is a 2-line guard at the top of an existing validator. The dict path is unchanged (the JSON-string parsing of `litellm_params` / `model_info` is the original purpose of the validator and is re-asserted in the new unit pin). The non-dict path now returns the input unchanged, which is the Pydantic-documented behaviour for a `mode="before"` validator receiving a non-dict. - The pre-existing `test_parses_json_string_fields` test still passes, confirming the JSON-string parsing path is intact. ## Future improvements (not in this PR) - A real E2E test that wires the FastAPI app, hits `POST /model/block` via TestClient, and asserts a 2xx response would be valuable — it would require a full app + DB setup (skipped here because the unit pin already catches the regression at the validator layer). The E2E test added in merged PR #34118 already documents the post-write non-2xx behaviour, so the maintainer has a clear acceptance test for the fix. - The same `mode="before"` validator pattern is used in other Pydantic models across the litellm proxy. If the same class of bug is lurking elsewhere, the same 1-line guard (`if not isinstance(values, dict): return values`) would fix it. A repo-wide audit would be a follow-up cycle.

signals.title: feat: add FlexAI as an OpenAI-compatible provider
signals.text: ## Relevant issues New provider registration (no linked issue). Follows [Adding OpenAI-Compatible Providers](https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/contributing/adding_openai_compatible_providers) and `litellm/llms/openai_like/README.md`. ## What this adds [FlexAI](https://flex.ai)'s Token Service is an OpenAI-compatible inference endpoint (`https://api.flex.ai/v1`) serving open-weight models — Qwen3.x, DeepSeek-V4, GLM-5.2, gpt-oss, Llama 3.x, Gemma 4, Mistral — plus embedding, image, and speech models. | File | Change | | --- | --- | | `litellm/llms/openai_like/providers.json` | `flexai` entry: `base_url=https://api.flex.ai/v1`, `FLEXAI_API_KEY`, `FLEXAI_API_BASE` override, `base_class=openai_gpt`, `/v1/chat/completions` + `/v1/responses` | | `litellm/constants.py` | `flexai` in `openai_compatible_providers`; `https://api.flex.ai/v1` in `openai_compatible_endpoints`, so `JSONProviderRegistry.get_by_base_url` resolves an `api_base` override | | `litellm/types/utils.py` | `FLEXAI` in the `LlmProviders` enum | | `model_prices_and_context_window.json` | 21 entries for the served roster | | `litellm/model_prices_and_context_window_backup.json` | same 21 entries (asserted byte-identical by a test — see note below) | | `provider_endpoints_support.json` | endpoint-support block | | `tests/test_litellm/llms/openai_like/test_flexai_provider.py` | 18 tests | No provider-specific branch in `get_llm_provider_logic.py`: the generic JSON-provider lookup from #37658 resolves `flexai` from `providers.json` by base URL and already prefers an explicit `api_key` over the environment. Rebasing onto that let me delete the branch I had written by hand; the tests now cover the generic path. No `param_mappings` needed — verified `max_completion_tokens` is accepted natively. ```python import litellm response = litellm.completion( model="flexai/gpt-oss-120b", messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}], ) ``` ## How the pricing entries were produced Taken from FlexAI's authenticated `GET https://api.flex.ai/v1/models` and verified live against prod. Every entry carries a `source` pointing at the public catalog page, [platform.flex.ai/models](https://platform.flex.ai/models). (An earlier revision cited a public JSON feed at `tokens.flex.ai/api/models`; FlexAI has since withdrawn that endpoint, so the `source` links were repointed.) Roster and price agreement, verified **2026-08-20** (FlexAI's served set changes as models are pinned/unpinned, so treat the feed above as the source of truth rather than this snapshot): ``` prod /v1/models : 24 models committed flexai/* : 21 entries (the served set at the time of writing; FlexAI has since added 3 more) committed, NOT in prod : none price spot-check (prod pricing vs committed entry): every committed entry matches prod /v1/models on input/output per-token cost, cache-read cost and context length ``` Both cost-map files were edited by **text splice** rather than a `json.dump` rewrite, so every other entry is byte-identical — the diff is 255 pure insertions per file, zero deletions. Validated against `model_prices_and_context_window.schema.json` (0 errors). ## Live verification from this branch Against prod `https://api.flex.ai/v1`: ``` completion() flexai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 HTTP 200 tokens=6/2 cost=$0.0000008400 completion() flexai/gpt-oss-120b HTTP 200 tokens=69/8 cost=$0.0000013726 of which 64 prompt tokens were cache reads; FlexAI's own usage.cost for the same call reports 1.37e-06 -> agrees responses() flexai/gpt-oss-120b HTTP 200 max_completion_tokens accepted -> yes (no param_mappings needed) ``` ## Checks run - `pytest tests/test_litellm/llms/openai_like/test_flexai_provider.py -q` → **18 passed** - `pytest tests/test_litellm/llms/openai_like/ tests/litellm/llms/openai_like/ -q` → **161 passed, 5 skipped** - `python tests/code_coverage_tests/check_provider_folders_documented.py` → passes (`All 27 openai_like providers are documented`) - `python tests/code_coverage_tests/check_get_model_cost_key_performance.py` → passes - `jsonschema` validation of the new entries against `model_prices_and_context_window.schema.json` → 0 errors ## Cache-read pricing 15 of the 21 models expose `input_cache_read` pricing, so each carries `cache_read_input_token_cost`. Without it litellm silently under-reports spend whenever prompt caching hits — the call above bills 64 of its 69 prompt tokens as cache reads. ## Two notes for the reviewer **1. The packaged backup copy.** `litellm/model_prices_and_context_window_backup.json` is what `GetModelCostMap.load_local_model_cost_map()` reads, so a provider whose entries land only in the root file gets `"This model isn't mapped yet"` whenever the remote map is unavailable or `LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True`. I hit exactly that, so both files are updated, and `test_flexai_entries_match_packaged_backup` asserts they stay in sync. Happy to drop that test if the backup is meant to be regenerated by tooling instead. **2. Non-chat models are priced but not yet routable.** 5 of the 21 entries are `embedding` / `image_generation` / `audio_transcription` / `audio_speech` for models FlexAI serves. JSON-configured providers currently route only chat completions (`JSONProviderRegistry.exists()` is consulted in `completion()`) and the Responses API, so `provider_endpoints_support.json` honestly declares those endpoints `false`. Their *pricing* is nonetheless correct and calculator-verified — per Greptile's catch, they use the fields the generic calculators actually read (`input_cost_per_image`, `input_cost_per_character`), with tests exercising both calculators. Glad to trim them to chat-only if you'd rather the cost map track routable endpoints exactly. ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests — 18 unit tests, all passing - [x] My PR passes all unit tests on the touched paths (`161 passed, 5 skipped` across both `openai_like` test dirs) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] Bot reviews addressed — Greptile's P2 (non-chat pricing fields) and veria-ai's credential-precedence finding are both fixed, each with regression tests 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) https://claude.ai/code/session_013jmFw7fcJTtdTgmkKJa5yr

signals.title: fix(mlflow): include cache token counts in mlflow.chat.tokenUsage attribute
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - MLflow traces lose cache token counts for cached prompts - Cost computed from stored usage over-stated up to 6.7x How it solves it: - Lift cache fields from raw response usage into `mlflow.chat.tokenUsage` - Covers Anthropic-style top-level fields and OpenAI-style `prompt_tokens_details` ## Relevant issues Fixes mlflow/mlflow#24869 ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix The `MlflowLogger` builds `mlflow.chat.tokenUsage` from the flattened `StandardLoggingPayload`, which carries no cache token fields, so MLflow prices every input token at the full rate for cached workloads. The cache-rich usage is available in the raw response the logger already stores. Repro with `mlflow.litellm.autolog()` on a completion whose usage carries `cache_read_input_tokens=10000, cache_creation_input_tokens=300` (mock replaces only the HTTP transport, the entire callback and logging path is real): Before this change the MLflow span stores ``` {'input_tokens': 10500, 'output_tokens': 200, 'total_tokens': 10700} ``` With this change ``` {'input_tokens': 10500, 'output_tokens': 200, 'total_tokens': 10700, 'cache_read_input_tokens': 10000, 'cache_creation_input_tokens': 300} ``` Cost impact using litellm's own `cost_per_token` for `claude-haiku-4-5` with the numbers above: input cost 0.0105 from the cache-blind usage vs 0.001575 with the cache breakdown, a 6.7x over-statement that this PR fixes for MLflow users. `pytest tests/test_litellm/integrations/test_mlflow.py` passes (5 tests, including the 2 added here).

signals.title: fix(pricing): correct four Vertex AI MaaS per-token rates
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Four Vertex AI MaaS models overstate spend vs what Google charges - deepseek-v3.1 had copy-pasted deepseek-r1-0528 rates How it solves it: - Correct input/output per-token rates in both cost maps - Verified each rate against Google docs and independent trackers ## Relevant issues Fixes #35904 ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [ ] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix `spend` is derived from these entries, so the fix is verifiable through the cost calculator that the proxy uses to write SpendLogs. Captured at commit 138798ea49 with `LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True` so it reads the edited map, replaying the reporter's 33-in / 78-out qwen3-coder request: ``` $ LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True uv run --no-sync python -c " import litellm from litellm import completion_cost from litellm.utils import ModelResponse, Usage, Choices, Message m='vertex_ai/qwen/qwen3-coder-480b-a35b-instruct-maas' resp=ModelResponse(choices=[Choices(message=Message(content='x'))], usage=Usage(prompt_tokens=33, completion_tokens=78, total_tokens=111), model=m) resp._hidden_params['custom_llm_provider']='vertex_ai' print('cost', completion_cost(completion_response=resp, model=m, custom_llm_provider='vertex_ai')) info=litellm.get_model_info(m) print('rates', info['input_cost_per_token'], info['output_cost_per_token'])" cost 0.00014766 rates 2.2e-07 1.8e-06 ``` Before the fix the same request recorded 0.000345 (rates 1e-06 / 4e-06), roughly 2.3x the real 0.00014766. A pure Vertex e2e curl would need live Vertex MaaS credentials, which are not available in this environment, so the proof runs through the exact same `completion_cost` path the proxy uses to populate SpendLogs. Corrected rates (per 1M tokens), all cross-checked against Google's model docs and independent trackers (portkey, llmreference, cloudprice, getmaxim, modelavailability): | Key | Was in/out | Corrected in/out | | --- | --- | --- | | vertex_ai/qwen/qwen3-coder-480b-a35b-instruct-maas | 1.00 / 4.00 | 0.22 / 1.80 | | vertex_ai/deepseek-ai/deepseek-v3.1-maas | 1.35 / 5.40 | 0.60 / 1.70 | | vertex_ai/openai/gpt-oss-120b-maas | 0.15 / 0.60 | 0.09 / 0.36 | | vertex_ai/qwen/qwen3-235b-a22b-instruct-2507-maas | 0.25 / 1.00 | 0.22 / 0.88 | The corrected qwen3-coder rate also matches the existing Bedrock entry qwen.qwen3-coder-480b-a35b-v1:0 (0.22 / 1.80) in the same file ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Changes Corrected input_cost_per_token / output_cost_per_token for the four Vertex MaaS entries in model_prices_and_context_window.json and the bundled litellm/model_prices_and_context_window_backup.json

signals.title: fix(router): apply model_info nested under litellm_params instead of dropping it
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Custom pricing nested one level deeper is silently dropped - Those deployments then log $0.00 spend forever - A common config mistake fails without any warning - Budgets keyed on that spend never fire How it solves it: - Detect model info nested under the params block - Promote it to where it is read, and warn once - Correctly-placed config keeps working unchanged ## User Flow Before: an admin puts a deployment's pricing one level deeper than expected, the proxy starts cleanly, and every request on that deployment records $0.00. 1. The admin adds a deployment to `config.yaml` where `model_info` (carrying `input_cost_per_token` / `output_cost_per_token`) is nested **inside** the params block rather than beside it, then starts the proxy 2. The proxy starts with no error or warning about the placement 3. A developer sends POST `https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions` against that deployment and gets a normal completion 4. `https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs` shows the request at **$0.00**, and the custom rates the admin set are nowhere in effect 5. A monthly budget on that key never triggers, because recorded spend stays at zero After: the misplacement is tolerated and announced. 1. The admin adds the same deployment with the same nesting, and starts the proxy 2. The proxy logs a warning naming that deployment and saying its model info was found in the wrong place 3. The developer sends the same POST `https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions` and gets the same completion 4. `https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs` shows the request priced at the admin's configured rates 5. The budget enforces correctly, and the admin can move the block to silence the warning ## Relevant issues Fixes #35691 ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Captured at commit `09889e1986` (`litellm_internal_staging`). Deployment registration and cost lookup both run before any provider call, so the proof drives the real Router startup path directly. Worth recording how this diagnosis was reached: my first explanation of #35691 was wrong, and three independent verification passes refuted it. Reading the reporter's actual config showed the real cause — the pricing was nested a level deeper than the code reads it, so it was never seen at all. The wrong fix was discarded rather than shipped. **Before:** a deployment whose `model_info` sits inside the params block registers with no custom pricing, and cost for its requests resolves to `0.0` with no warning emitted. **After:** the same config emits a warning naming the deployment, the pricing is promoted to where it is read, and cost resolves at the configured rates. A correctly-placed `model_info` takes exactly the same path as before — 6/6 tests cover both placements plus the warning. ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats - Warns rather than erroring, so existing misconfigured deployments keep serving ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signals.title: fix(cost-map): bedrock_mantle gpt-5.6 sol/terra/luna now support 1M context
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - AWS raised gpt-5.6 sol/terra/luna on Bedrock to 1M context - our cost map still caps them at 272k input tokens - router pre-call checks reject long-context requests as too big How it solves it: - bump `max_input_tokens` to 1000000 for the three bedrock_mantle entries - same bump in the bundled backup cost map ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [ ] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) Data-only change to the cost map, so there is no code path to unit test beyond what the existing model info tests already cover ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Proxy config used for both runs (a 900,001 token o200k_base prompt in `body.json`, `enable_pre_call_checks: true`, which is what surfaces the stale ceiling), hitting real Bedrock Mantle in us-east-1 with SigV4 credentials: ```yaml model_list: - model_name: gpt-5.6-luna litellm_params: model: bedrock_mantle/openai.gpt-5.6-luna aws_region_name: us-east-1 router_settings: enable_pre_call_checks: true ``` Before, at 24dbd2b2db (the cost map with 272000): ``` $ curl -s -X POST http://localhost:4000/v1/responses -H 'content-type: application/json' \ -H 'authorization: Bearer sk-1234' --data-binary @body.json {"error":{"message":"litellm.ContextWindowExceededError: litellm.BadRequestError: litellm._pre_call_checks: Context Window exceeded for given call. No models have context window large enough for this call. Model=bedrock_mantle/openai.gpt-5.6-luna, Max Input Tokens=272000, Got=900008 model=gpt-5.6-luna. context_window_fallbacks=None. fallbacks=None. ...","code":"400"}} ``` After, with this change, same request, real Bedrock: ``` $ curl -s -D - -X POST http://localhost:4000/v1/responses -H 'content-type: application/json' \ -H 'authorization: Bearer sk-1234' --data-binary @body.json HTTP/1.1 200 OK x-litellm-response-cost: 0.24752293500000003 "model": "gpt-5.6-luna", "usage": {"input_tokens": 900007, "cache_write_tokens": 900005, "output_tokens": 16, "total_tokens": 900023} ``` (the response comes back `status: "incomplete"` only because that body pins `max_output_tokens: 16`) Same 900,001 token prompt through the SDK, asking a question that requires reading the tail of the prompt, on both variants my credentials can reach: ``` $ python big_live.py bedrock_mantle/openai.gpt-5.6-luna prompt tokens (o200k_base): 900001 usage: input_tokens=900024 output_tokens=333 total_tokens=900357 output: ['1000'] $ python big_live.py bedrock_mantle/openai.gpt-5.6-sol prompt tokens (o200k_base): 900001 usage: input_tokens=900024 output_tokens=747 total_tokens=900771 output: ['5000'] ``` Terra is not verified live, my account cannot subscribe to it (`Your subscription to the model could not be established`), and it ships the same 1M window as Sol and Luna per the AWS announcement ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Changes `max_input_tokens` for `bedrock_mantle/openai.gpt-5.6-sol`, `bedrock_mantle/openai.gpt-5.6-terra`, and `bedrock_mantle/openai.gpt-5.6-luna` goes from 272000 to 1000000 in both `model_prices_and_context_window.json` and `litellm/model_prices_and_context_window_backup.json`, matching AWS's announcement that all three now serve 1 million token context windows. Output limits, pricing, and the first-party `gpt-5.6-*` entries (already at 1050000) are untouched ### Final Attestation - [ ] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signals.title: fix(model registry): add the provider deprecation_date metadata still missing after #36403
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - 65 live models still carry no `deprecation_date` - Azure retirement dates were missing almost entirely - `text-embedding-004` carried the Gemini API date, not Vertex's How it solves it: - Adds the dates from Azure, Vertex, Gemini and xAI retirement schedules - Corrects `text-embedding-004` to Vertex's own retirement date - Data only, `deprecation_date` and nothing else ## User Flow Before: a proxy admin planning migrations off retiring Azure and Vertex deployments has no retirement date for any of them, so nothing tells them when their traffic breaks 1. They run a proxy serving `azure/gpt-5.1`, `azure/o4-mini`, `xai/grok-code-fast-1`, `vertex_ai/veo-2.0-generate-001` and `vertex_ai/text-embedding-004` 2. They look for the retirement date of each model in the registry the proxy ships with, and get nothing back for any of the five 3. `text-embedding-004` is the one entry that does carry a date, 2026-01-14, which is the day the Gemini API dropped it, not the day Vertex retires it, so a Vertex deployment reads as already dead while it keeps serving traffic until 2027 4. They call `xai/grok-code-fast-1` and nothing in the gateway signals that xAI already retired that slug on 2026-05-15 and silently routes it to `grok-build-0.1`, which is priced differently 5. Deprecation alerting from #26900 has no dates to alert on for these deployments, so the first signal is a 410 from the provider After: every one of those deployments carries the retirement date its provider publishes 1. They run the same proxy with the same five deployments 2. The shipped registry now reports 2027-05-15 for `azure/gpt-5.1`, 2026-10-16 for `azure/o4-mini`, 2026-05-15 for `xai/grok-code-fast-1` and 2026-06-30 for `vertex_ai/veo-2.0-generate-001` 3. `vertex_ai/text-embedding-004` reports 2027-04-01, the date Vertex publishes, so the deployment is no longer treated as retired 4. The already-passed date on `xai/grok-code-fast-1` marks it as retired, which is what xAI documents, so the pricing surprise from the silent redirect is visible before the invoice 5. Deprecation alerting from #26900 has a real date for each of these deployments, so migrations get planned ahead of the shutdown ## Relevant issues Supports #26900 (`/model/deprecations` and deprecation alerts), which reads `deprecation_date` Rebased after #36403 landed the OpenAI, Anthropic and Gemini side of this audit, so this PR now carries only what is still missing on `litellm_internal_staging` ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review No new tests: this is a data-only change, and `tests/test_litellm/test_model_prices_schema.py` already enforces the `YYYY-MM-DD` shape of every `deprecation_date`, which is the only property this change can violate ## Changes 66 entries, 65 additions and 1 correction. Every value comes from the provider's own retirement schedule | retirement date | entries | source | | --- | --- | --- | | 2026-05-15 | `xai/grok-code-fast-1`, `xai/grok-code-fast-1-0825` | [xAI](https://docs.x.ai/developers/migration/may-15-retirement) | | 2026-06-30 | `vertex_ai/veo-2.0-generate-001`, `vertex_ai/veo-3.0-generate-001`, `vertex_ai/veo-3.0-fast-generate-001` | [Vertex](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/models/model-versions) | | 2026-10-01 | `azure/o3-mini` | [Azure](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/openai/concepts/model-retirement-schedule) | | 2026-10-02 | `gemini-2.5-flash-image`, `vertex_ai/gemini-2.5-flash-image` | Vertex | | 2026-10-16 | `azure/o4-mini` | Azure | | 2026-10-20 | `gemini-2.5-pro`, `gemini-2.5-flash`, `gemini-2.5-flash-lite` | Vertex | | 2026-10-21 | `azure/o1`, `azure/o3` | Azure | | 2026-10-23 | the nine `azure/{low,medium,high}/*/gpt-image-1` size variants | Azure | | 2026-12-17 | `azure/o3-pro` | Azure | | 2027-02-09 | `azure/gpt-5`, `azure/gpt-5-mini`, `azure/gpt-5-nano` | Azure | | 2027-04-01 | `text-embedding-004` (correction, was 2026-01-14), `text-embedding-005`, `text-multilingual-embedding-002`, `multimodalembedding@001` | Vertex | | 2027-04-07 | the nine `azure/{low,medium,high}/*/gpt-image-1-mini` size variants | Azure | | 2027-04-14 | `azure/gpt-4o-mini`, `azure/global-standard/gpt-4o-mini` | Azure | | 2027-05-15 | `azure/gpt-5.1{,-codex,-codex-mini}` and their `us`, `eu`, `global` variants | Azure | | 2027-06-08 | `azure/gpt-5.2` | Azure | | 2027-06-16 | `azure/gpt-image-1.5` | Azure | | 2027-09-02 | `azure/gpt-5.4` and its `us`, `eu` variants | Azure | | 2027-09-07 | `azure/gpt-5.4-pro` | Azure | | 2027-09-21 | `azure/gpt-5.4-mini`, `azure/gpt-5.4-nano` | Azure | | 2027-10-21 | `azure/gpt-image-2` | Azure | | 2027-10-26 | `azure/gpt-5.5` and its `us`, `eu` variants | Azure | Deliberately not changed: the `gemini/gemini-2.5-{pro,flash,flash-lite}` entries, since the Gemini API deprecation page still says "No shutdown date announced" for them while Vertex publishes 2026-10-20 for the unprefixed entries, and `gemini/gemini-embedding-001`, where staging's 2028-05-14 already matches Google ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix `deprecation_date` is inert in the library today, `grep -rn deprecation_date litellm/**/*.py` returns nothing, and the proxy strips it out of the `model_info` it serves, so there is no live route that reflects this data yet. #26900 is the consumer that will read it. Both facts, and the registry values themselves, are shown against a live proxy on localhost:4000 at `2f571b71ef`, booted with `LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True` so it reads the registry this PR edits ``` $ LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True litellm --config deprecation_config.yaml --port 4000 $ curl -s -X GET 'http://localhost:4000/model/info' -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-1234' | \ python3 -c "import json,sys; [print(m['litellm_params']['model'],'| deprecation_date:',m['model_info'].get('deprecation_date','<absent from response>')) for m in json.load(sys.stdin)['data']]" azure/gpt-5.1 | deprecation_date: <absent from response> azure/o4-mini | deprecation_date: <absent from response> vertex_ai/text-embedding-004 | deprecation_date: <absent from response> xai/grok-code-fast-1 | deprecation_date: <absent from response> vertex_ai/veo-2.0-generate-001 | deprecation_date: <absent from response> ``` The registry the proxy loaded does carry them. Before, at `76ad1c319d` (the base commit), and after, at `2f571b71ef` ``` $ git show 76ad1c319d:model_prices_and_context_window.json | jq -r '["azure/gpt-5.1","azure/o4-mini","xai/grok-code-fast-1","vertex_ai/veo-2.0-generate-001","text-embedding-004"][] as $m | "\($m)\t\(.[$m].deprecation_date)"' azure/gpt-5.1 null azure/o4-mini null xai/grok-code-fast-1 null vertex_ai/veo-2.0-generate-001 null text-embedding-004 2026-01-14 $ jq -r '["azure/gpt-5.1","azure/o4-mini","xai/grok-code-fast-1","vertex_ai/veo-2.0-generate-001","text-embedding-004"][] as $m | "\($m)\t\(.[$m].deprecation_date)"' model_prices_and_context_window.json azure/gpt-5.1 2027-05-15 azure/o4-mini 2026-10-16 xai/grok-code-fast-1 2026-05-15 vertex_ai/veo-2.0-generate-001 2026-06-30 text-embedding-004 2027-04-01 $ jq '[to_entries[] | select(.value.deprecation_date)] | length' model_prices_and_context_window.json 324 # 259 on the base commit $ git diff -U0 HEAD~1 -- model_prices_and_context_window.json | grep -c '^+ ' 66 # every added line is a deprecation_date line $ python3 ci_cd/check_files_match.py Passed! Files model_prices_and_context_window.json and litellm/model_prices_and_context_window_backup.json match. ``` ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats - Nothing surfaces `deprecation_date` yet, #26900 is the consumer - Azure regional variants inherit their base model's date - Providers move these dates, so the data needs periodic refreshes Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/680cda1b74c34159899de6c6ae064ef6 Requested by: @mateo-berri

signals.title: fix(anthropic): map Responses API cached input tokens to cache_read_input_tokens on /v1/messages
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - `/v1/messages` on Responses-API models never returned `cache_read_input_tokens` - Anthropic-shape clients saw an uncached prompt on every call - Streaming read cache counts from fields a Responses usage never has How it solves it: - Map `input_tokens_details.cached_tokens` to `cache_read_input_tokens` - Subtract it from Anthropic `input_tokens`, as Anthropic clients expect - Share one mapper between the streaming and non-streaming bridge ## Relevant issues Fixes #36091 ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Live proxy on localhost:4000, one model routed to a Responses-API upstream that reports a cache hit on the second identical prompt (`input_tokens: 25616`, `input_tokens_details.cached_tokens: 25613`, `output_tokens: 5`). The upstream here is a local stand-in rather than api.openai.com, which this environment cannot reach, so a reviewer should re-run the same two calls against a real `openai/gpt-5.x` deployment: the numbers below come straight from whatever the upstream reports, so any cached prompt reproduces it Before, at 24dbd2b2db ``` $ for i in 1 2; do curl -s -X POST localhost:4000/v1/messages -H 'x-api-key: sk-1234' -H 'content-type: application/json' \ -d '{"model":"gpt-5.6-luna","max_tokens":16,"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]}' | jq -c .usage; done {"input_tokens":25616,"output_tokens":5} {"input_tokens":25616,"output_tokens":5} ``` The same prompt through `/v1/chat/completions` showed the upstream cache working the whole time (`prompt_tokens=25616 cached_tokens=25613`), so only the Anthropic shape lost it After, at e0300384cd ``` $ for i in 1 2; do curl -s -X POST localhost:4000/v1/messages -H 'x-api-key: sk-1234' -H 'content-type: application/json' \ -d '{"model":"gpt-5.6-luna","max_tokens":16,"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]}' | jq -c .usage; done {"input_tokens": 25616, "output_tokens": 5} {"input_tokens": 3, "output_tokens": 5, "cache_read_input_tokens": 25613} $ curl -s -N -X POST localhost:4000/v1/messages -H 'x-api-key: sk-1234' -H 'content-type: application/json' \ -d '{"model":"gpt-5.6-luna","max_tokens":16,"stream":true,"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]}' | grep message_delta data: {"type": "message_delta", "delta": {"stop_reason": "end_turn", "stop_sequence": null}, "usage": {"input_tokens": 3, "output_tokens": 5, "cache_read_input_tokens": 25613}} ``` Call 1 is the cold prompt and call 2 is the cache hit, so `input_tokens` drops to the 3 uncached tokens and the 25613 cached ones show up where an Anthropic client reads them. `/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/responses` are unaffected by this change: it only touches the Anthropic bridge's Responses adapters ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Changes `responses_adapters/transformation.py` built `AnthropicUsage` from `input_tokens` and `output_tokens` only, and `responses_adapters/streaming_iterator.py` fetched the two details objects into the cache variables and then overwrote both with `cache_creation_input_tokens` / `cache_read_input_tokens` off the usage object, names that only exist on Anthropic usage and never on a Responses one, so both counts were pinned to 0 on every call Both now go through `responses_adapters/usage.py::anthropic_usage_from_responses_usage`, which reads `input_tokens_details.cached_tokens` (object or dict shaped) and returns ```python AnthropicUsage( input_tokens=input_tokens - cache_read_input_tokens, output_tokens=output_tokens, cache_read_input_tokens=cache_read_input_tokens, ) ``` omitting the cache field entirely when there is no hit, which matches how the chat-completions bridge already reports it. The subtraction is the part that is easy to miss: the Responses API counts cached tokens inside `input_tokens`, while Anthropic reports them alongside it, so passing the total through unchanged would double-count the prompt for anything summing the fields. The cached count is clamped to `input_tokens` so an upstream reporting more cached than total can't yield a negative Regression tests cover both paths in the existing adapter test files: the mapped fields and the subtraction, the no-cache-hit case still omitting the fields, and a usage object missing the counts falling back to zeroes instead of raising mid-stream ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signals.title: feat(gemini): add gemini-3.1-flash-lite-image pricing and fix its capability fields
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - `gemini-3.1-flash-lite-image` is missing from the cost map - Image generation calls on it log spend of $0 - Capability fields copied from the non-lite model were wrong How it solves it: - Adds bare, `gemini/` and `vertex_ai/` entries to both cost maps - Sets output limit 4096, no structured outputs, per-route caching and function calling - Adds AI Studio batch rates on the `gemini/` entry ## Relevant issues Fixes #31945, fixes #32650. Supersedes #31946 (original commit kept, that fork is not pushable from here) ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5286 ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Live Google AI Studio image generation through a local proxy, real spend, config with one deployment `nano-banana-2-lite -> gemini/gemini-3.1-flash-lite-image` Request, identical in both runs: ```bash curl -s http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-1234' \ -d '{"model":"nano-banana-2-lite","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Generate a picture of a banana wearing sunglasses"}],"modalities":["image","text"]}' curl -s -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-1234' http://localhost:4000/spend/logs ``` Before, at `0c3017e1de` (base). The call succeeds and returns an image, but the model is unmapped so spend is zero: ``` usage: {"prompt_tokens": 9, "completion_tokens": 1502, "completion_tokens_details": {"text_tokens": 382, "image_tokens": 1120}} 2026-08-06T19:38:34.245000Z gemini/gemini-3.1-flash-lite-image spend= 0.0 ``` After, at `c8941f671f` (this branch). Same call, now billed: ``` usage: {"prompt_tokens": 9, "completion_tokens": 1490, "completion_tokens_details": {"text_tokens": 370, "image_tokens": 1120}} 2026-08-06T19:37:11.263000Z gemini/gemini-3.1-flash-lite-image spend= 0.03415725 ``` That matches Google's published rates token for token: `1120 * $30/1M + 370 * $1.50/1M + 9 * $0.25/1M = $0.03415725`, and it confirms the 1120 output image tokens per 1K image the Vertex model card documents Capabilities as served at `c8941f671f`, `curl -s -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-1234' http://localhost:4000/model/info`: ```json { "max_output_tokens": 4096, "supports_function_calling": true, "supports_prompt_caching": false, "supports_response_schema": false, "input_cost_per_token": 2.5e-07, "output_cost_per_image_token": 3e-05 } ``` Function calling on the `gemini/` route really is supported, which is why the flag flipped to true. Live tool call at `c8941f671f`: ```bash curl -s http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-1234' \ -d '{"model":"nano-banana-2-lite","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"What is the weather in Paris? Use the tool."}],"tools":[{"type":"function","function":{"name":"get_weather","description":"Get weather","parameters":{"type":"object","properties":{"city":{"type":"string"}},"required":["city"]}}}]}' ``` ```json [{"function": {"name": "get_weather", "arguments": "{\"city\": \"Paris\"}"}, "type": "function"}] ``` ## Type 🆕 New Feature ## Changes Adds `gemini-3.1-flash-lite-image` (Nano Banana 2 Lite, GA on Vertex June 30 2026) plus the `gemini/` and `vertex_ai/` variants to `model_prices_and_context_window.json` and the bundled backup. Prices are $0.25/1M input, $1.50/1M text and thinking output, $30/1M image output, so $0.0336 per 1K image at 1120 tokens The capability fields do not just mirror the non-lite `gemini-3.1-flash-image`, since the model cards differ. Output limit is 4096 rather than 32768, structured outputs are unsupported on both routes, and caching and function calling split per route: AI Studio supports function calling and no caching, Vertex is the reverse with implicit context caching. Grounding with Google Search is unsupported on Lite, so the `supports_web_search` and search context pricing fields are deliberately absent. The `gemini/` entry also carries the batch rates, half of standard, matching its sibling Sources: https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/models/gemini-3.1-flash-lite-image and https://cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/models/gemini/3-1-flash-lite-image `tests/test_litellm/test_gemini_3_1_flash_lite_image_pricing.py` pins the prices, the per-route capabilities, and the absence of the grounding fields in both maps, and asserts `completion_cost` for a 1K image ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/3c40df3edf324054b7fa9f297cb83098 Requested by: @mateo-berri <!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY --> --- > [!NOTE] > **Low Risk** > Metadata and pricing JSON only, with regression tests; no runtime routing or auth changes, though incorrect rates would affect reported spend. > > **Overview** > Adds **`gemini-3.1-flash-lite-image`** to `model_prices_and_context_window.json` and the bundled backup so LiteLLM can price and advertise the Lite image model (bare, `gemini/`, and `vertex_ai/` keys). > > Entries use **`image_generation`** mode with Google’s published token and per-image costs (including **`output_cost_per_image_token`** for ~1K images), **4096** max output tokens, no structured outputs, and **no** web-search / grounding pricing fields. **`gemini/`** gets AI Studio batch rates and function-calling enabled with prompt caching off; Vertex-style keys keep caching on and function calling off. > > New tests lock the JSON values in both maps and assert **`get_model_info`** / **`completion_cost`** bill image output tokens correctly instead of $0 or “unmapped” errors. > > <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 246dd796471570e53e8f929a515228a98881fed4. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup> <!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

signals.title: fix(model_prices): refresh `deprecation_date` metadata from OpenAI/Anthropic/Gemini docs
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - `deprecation_date` is missing on ~80 live models - A few existing dates are flat-out wrong - #26900 alerts are only as good as this data How it solves it: - Backfills dates from OpenAI/Anthropic/Gemini deprecation pages - Corrects 5 stale dates against those same pages - No pricing/capability edits; `deprecation_date` only ## Relevant issues Supports #26900 (`/model/deprecations` endpoint + Slack deprecation alerts), which reads `deprecation_date` from this file. ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests — data-only change; covered by the existing schema/pricing tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Data-only change to `model_prices_and_context_window.json` (no code paths touched), verified by the repo's own checks at commit on this branch: ``` LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True uv run --no-sync pytest tests/test_litellm/test_model_prices_schema.py -q 18 passed LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True uv run --no-sync pytest tests/test_litellm/test_cost_calculator.py tests/test_litellm/litellm_core_utils -q 1571 passed, 1 skipped ``` ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Changes Only the `deprecation_date` key is touched — 86 entries (81 added, 5 corrected). Every value comes from the provider's own deprecation page; nothing was inferred. ### Corrections (existing values that disagree with the provider) | model | was | now | source | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `claude-3-opus-20240229` | 2026-05-01 | 2026-01-05 | [Anthropic](https://docs.claude.com/en/docs/about-claude/model-deprecations) | | `claude-opus-4-20250514` | 2026-05-14 | 2026-06-15 | Anthropic | | `claude-sonnet-4-20250514` | 2026-05-14 | 2026-06-15 | Anthropic | | `gpt-4-0613` | 2025-06-06 | 2026-10-23 | [OpenAI](https://platform.openai.com/docs/deprecations) | | `gpt-4-1106-preview` | 2026-03-26 | 2026-10-23 | OpenAI | ### Backfills Anthropic ([docs.claude.com](https://docs.claude.com/en/docs/about-claude/model-deprecations)) — retired models that had no date: -
