signals.title: feat(ui): per-model reasoning effort in complexity tier editor
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - tier editor can only write bare model names - reasoning effort per tier is yaml-only - editing a yaml router would strip tier params How it solves it: - reasoning effort control per selected tier model - control only shows for reasoning-capable models - unset stays a plain string, set becomes an object ## User Flow Before: an admin who wants the reasoning tier to run their reasoning model at xhigh has to leave the dashboard and hand-edit config yaml 1. They go to https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=add_model, open the Auto Router tab and pick the complexity router 2. They pick a model for each tier and save, which is the only choice the form offers 3. The reasoning tier now runs that model at its default effort, with no way to raise it from the UI 4. Worse, if the router was written in yaml with a tier carrying `litellm_params`, opening it in the edit modal and saving silently drops those params After: the effort sits next to the model that uses it, and hand-written tier params survive an edit 1. They go to https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=add_model, open the Auto Router tab and pick the complexity router 2. They select a model for the reasoning tier as before, and a "Reasoning effort" picker appears under it for any model the proxy reports as reasoning-capable 3. They pick xhigh, which is offered only for models whose metadata advertises it, then save 4. Requests classified into that tier now run at xhigh, while tiers they left alone are saved exactly as before, as plain model names 5. Opening an existing router from https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=llm-model-hub shows the stored effort preselected, and any other tier params the operator wrote in yaml are still there after saving ## Relevant issues Dashboard half of the tier `litellm_params` feature whose backend landed in #37064 (already merged, no dependency remains). ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix This PR is dashboard-only, so the proof is a click-through. The backend half and its live curl proof against a running proxy, with an Anthropic tier at xhigh and an OpenAI tier at high each overriding a caller-sent lower effort, are in #37064, which is merged Captured at commit `3e197afed9`, which rebased onto current `litellm_internal_staging` and ported the effort picker off antd onto the shared Base UI `Select` to match staging's dashboard migration Start the proxy and the dashboard dev server: ```bash python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config litellm/proxy/dev_config.yaml --detailed_debug --port 4000 cd ui/litellm-dashboard && npm run dev ``` Then: 1. Go to http://localhost:3000/ui/?page=add_model, open the Auto Router tab, pick Complexity Router 2. In the Reasoning tier's model select, pick a reasoning model such as an o-series or Claude Opus deployment, and confirm a "Reasoning effort" picker appears under it. Pick a non-reasoning model such as gpt-4o-mini and confirm no picker appears for it 3. Set the reasoning tier's effort to xhigh (offered only where the model advertises it), leave the other tiers untouched, and save 4. Go to http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=llm-model-hub, open the router you just created, and confirm the reasoning tier reads back with xhigh preselected while the other tiers are still plain model names 5. Send a request that classifies as reasoning and check http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=logs shows it routed to that model with the effort applied ## Type 🆕 New Feature ## Caveats (if any) - effort options come from model metadata, not a live provider check - the UI surfaces reasoning effort only, not arbitrary tier params - other tier params written in yaml are preserved, not editable - leaving the effort on "Model default" keeps the tier entry a plain model name, so existing configs are byte-identical after a save Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/cdf8ee24d7f7481092e012da8495cfef Requested by: @krrish-berri-2

signals.title: fix(guardrails): take caller identity on /guardrails/apply_guardrail from auth, not the body
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Caller metadata decides identity on `/guardrails/apply_guardrail` - A caller can claim any alias or team id - Guardrails keyed on that metadata can be steered How it solves it: - Authenticated identity is layered over caller metadata - Uses the same sanitizer the in-line request path uses - Non-identity metadata still passes through untouched ## User Flow Before: a guardrail configured to treat one team differently can be talked into it by anyone 1. An admin runs a guardrail that behaves differently for a known key alias or team id, reading it from request metadata 2. A caller sends POST https://litellm-domain/guardrails/apply_guardrail with `"metadata": {"user_api_key_alias": "<the privileged alias>"}` and their own text 3. The response comes back as if the request came from that alias, so text the guardrail would otherwise act on is returned untouched After: the same request is judged on who the caller actually is 1. The caller sends the same POST with the same forged `metadata` 2. The proxy overwrites the identity fields with the ones authentication established for that key 3. The guardrail runs against the real identity, so the forged alias buys nothing, while any other metadata the caller sent still reaches the guardrail ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Live proxy on `localhost:4000` at commit `9ce19120fc`, postgres-backed, with a guardrail that skips work for one key alias and a guardrail endpoint that records every payload it receives. The route is admin-only, so the master key is used; its authenticated alias is empty, which is exactly what has to win over the alias the body claims. ``` $ # 1) forged identity in the body $ curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4000/guardrails/apply_guardrail \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"guardrail_name":"gg-skip-alias","text":"scan me","metadata":{"user_api_key_alias":"e2e-batch-worker"}}' 200 $ curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8787/_count # payloads the guardrail received {"records":1} $ # 2) the same call without the forged alias, for contrast 200 {"records":1} ``` Before this change the first call returned `{"records":0}`: the forged alias matched the exemption and the guardrail never ran. ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - `request_data` now always carries authenticated metadata - Callers relying on it being absent will see it ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR <!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY --> --- > [!NOTE] > <sup>[Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) is generating a summary for commit 2a7f02826f811a2bfa4e88201bea5de60d62431a. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup> <!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

signals.title: feat(helm): compose DATABASE_URL_READ_REPLICA from a reader host secret key
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - No way to compose DATABASE_URL_READ_REPLICA from separate secret keys - envFrom vars don't resolve in $(VAR) env interpolation - Secret stores often hold a bare reader hostname, not a full URL How it solves it: - New db.secret.readReplicaEndpointKey injects DATABASE_READER_HOST into the env array - db.readReplicaUrl can then reference $(DATABASE_READER_HOST), same pattern as the writer URL ## User Flow Before: an operator whose secret store holds the reader hostname as its own secret key cannot enable read-replica routing 1. They store username, password, writer host, and reader host as separate keys in one Kubernetes secret synced from their secret store 2. They set db.readReplicaUrl to `postgresql://$(DATABASE_USERNAME):$(DATABASE_PASSWORD)@$(DATABASE_READER_HOST):5432/$(DATABASE_NAME)?sslmode=require` and mount the secret via environmentSecrets 3. The pod starts with DATABASE_URL_READ_REPLICA containing the literal text `$(DATABASE_READER_HOST)` because Kubernetes only interpolates vars defined in the env array, not envFrom 4. The proxy fails to reach the reader and read-replica routing never activates After: the same operator enables read-replica routing with the same secret layout 1. They store the same keys in the same Kubernetes secret 2. They set db.secret.readReplicaEndpointKey to the reader host key and keep the same db.readReplicaUrl 3. The pod starts with DATABASE_READER_HOST sourced from the secret and placed before DATABASE_URL_READ_REPLICA, so the URL interpolates fully 4. The proxy connects to the reader and routes read-only queries there ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5653 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Shared setup: values file used for both renders ```yaml db: deployStandalone: false useExisting: true database: litellm url: postgresql://$(DATABASE_USERNAME):$(DATABASE_PASSWORD)@$(DATABASE_HOST):5432/$(DATABASE_NAME)?sslmode=require secret: name: pg-creds usernameKey: username passwordKey: password endpointKey: writer-host readReplicaEndpointKey: reader-host readReplicaUrl: postgresql://$(DATABASE_USERNAME):$(DATABASE_PASSWORD)@$(DATABASE_READER_HOST):5432/$(DATABASE_NAME)?sslmode=require ``` ### Before (973329e986) 1. `helm template litellm helm/litellm-helm -f reader-values.yaml -s templates/deployment.yaml` 2. Rendered env has DATABASE_URL_READ_REPLICA referencing `$(DATABASE_READER_HOST)` but no DATABASE_READER_HOST entry anywhere in the env array, so Kubernetes leaves the reference as literal text at runtime ```yaml - name: DATABASE_URL value: "postgresql://$(DATABASE_USERNAME):$(DATABASE_PASSWORD)@$(DATABASE_HOST):5432/$(DATABASE_NAME)?sslmode=require" - name: DATABASE_URL_READ_REPLICA value: "postgresql://$(DATABASE_USERNAME):$(DATABASE_PASSWORD)@$(DATABASE_READER_HOST):5432/$(DATABASE_NAME)?sslmode=require" ``` ### After (0dd9870fe4) 1. Same `helm template` command 2. DATABASE_READER_HOST is now sourced from the secret and rendered immediately before DATABASE_URL_READ_REPLICA, so the $(VAR) reference resolves ```yaml - name: DATABASE_URL value: "postgresql://$(DATABASE_USERNAME):$(DATABASE_PASSWORD)@$(DATABASE_HOST):5432/$(DATABASE_NAME)?sslmode=require" - name: DATABASE_READER_HOST valueFrom: secretKeyRef: name: pg-creds key: reader-host - name: DATABASE_URL_READ_REPLICA value: "postgresql://$(DATABASE_USERNAME):$(DATABASE_PASSWORD)@$(DATABASE_READER_HOST):5432/$(DATABASE_NAME)?sslmode=require" ``` 3. Adding `readReplicaUrlKey: reader-url` to the same values file suppresses the reader-host secret ref entirely and sources DATABASE_URL_READ_REPLICA from that key; likewise no reader-host ref is emitted when readReplicaUrl is unset, so an unused key can't block pod creation 4. `helm unittest -f 'tests/*.yaml' helm/litellm-helm` passes: 14 suites, 97 tests ## Type 🆕 New Feature ## Caveats (if any) - readReplicaUrlKey wins when both keys are set; the reader-host ref is then omitted Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/4977773ef12040748630173bf865083a

signals.title: feat(mistral): add zai-glm-5-2 and glm-5-2 model pricing
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Mistral hosts Z.ai's GLM 5.2, litellm has no cost map entry - Every call to it is logged at $0, so budgets never apply - Mistral also serves it as `glm-5-2`, unmapped as well How it solves it: - Adds `mistral/zai-glm-5-2` and `mistral/glm-5-2` with Mistral's prices - Prices cached input at $0.14 per million, a tenth of input - Takes limits and reasoning from Mistral's live model API - Adds a test pinning every number to the in-repo map ## User Flow Before: a developer pointing their app at Mistral's GLM 5.2 gets every request logged at zero spend, so their cost dashboard and their budgets are blind to the model 1. They add a deployment for `mistral/zai-glm-5-2` and send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with a roughly 11k token prompt 2. The completion comes back fine, but the response carries `x-litellm-response-cost-original: 0.0` 3. They send the identical request again to reuse Mistral's prompt cache. The reply reports `"cached_tokens": 11072` and still costs `0.0` 4. They call GET https://litellm-domain/model/info?model=zai-glm-5-2 and every field they need is empty: `max_input_tokens` null, `input_cost_per_token` 0, `cache_read_input_token_cost` null, `supports_reasoning` null 5. They try the short name Mistral also serves, `mistral/glm-5-2`, and get the same empty metadata and the same $0 6. They call GET https://litellm-domain/model_group/info and the entry reports `supports_reasoning` false and `supports_function_calling` false, even though the same prompt with a tool attached does come back with a `tool_calls` reply 7. They open https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs and see both requests at $0 spend, so a key or team budget scoped to this model can never be exceeded After: the same requests are priced correctly, and a cache hit visibly costs a tenth of a cold call 1. They add the same deployment and send the same POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with the roughly 11k token prompt 2. The response now carries `x-litellm-response-cost: 0.0155698`, which is $1.40 per million input tokens 3. They send the identical request again. The reply reports `"cached_tokens": 11072` and the cost drops to `0.00161908`, with `x-litellm-response-cost-cache-read: 0.00155008` showing the reused tokens billed at $0.14 per million 4. GET https://litellm-domain/model/info?model=zai-glm-5-2 returns `max_input_tokens` 1048576, `max_output_tokens` 131072, `input_cost_per_token` 0.0000014, `cache_read_input_token_cost` 1.4e-07, and `supports_reasoning` true 5. The short name `mistral/glm-5-2` returns the same metadata and prices identically 6. GET https://litellm-domain/model_group/info now reports `supports_reasoning` true and `supports_function_calling` true, matching what the model actually does 7. https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs shows real spend on both requests, so key and team budgets now apply to this model ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Both sides run a local proxy against Mistral's live API with a real key, and every completion below is a real billed Mistral call. Shared setup: ```yaml # glm_config.yaml model_list: - model_name: zai-glm-5-2 litellm_params: model: mistral/zai-glm-5-2 api_key: os.environ/MISTRAL_API_KEY - model_name: glm-5-2 litellm_params: model: mistral/glm-5-2 api_key: os.environ/MISTRAL_API_KEY general_settings: master_key: sk-glm52qa ``` `payload.json` is a roughly 11k token prompt (a repeated paragraph) plus `"Reply with the single word OK."`, `max_tokens: 8`, `temperature: 0`. `LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True` makes the proxy read the in-repo cost map instead of the published one, which is how an unmerged cost map change is exercised. Mistral's own API is the source of the numbers: ``` $ curl -s https://api.mistral.ai/v1/models/zai-glm-5-2 -H "Authorization: Bearer $MISTRAL_API_KEY" | jq -c '{id, name, max_context_length, aliases, capabilities}' {"id":"zai-glm-5-2","name":"glm-5-2","max_context_length":1048576,"aliases":["glm-5-2"],"capabilities":{"completion_chat":true,"function_calling":true,"reasoning":true,"vision":false,...}} ``` and https://docs.mistral.ai/models/zai-glm-5-2 prices it at $1.4 per million input, $0.14 per million cached input, $4.4 per million output, with a 1M context and 128k max output. ### Before (3357ec8d34) Base branch `litellm_internal_staging`, where neither model id exists in the cost map. #### Model metadata the gateway reports 1. `curl -s "http://localhost:27411/model/info?model=zai-glm-5-2" -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-glm52qa"` ```json { "max_input_tokens": null, "max_output_tokens": null, "input_cost_per_token": 0, "cache_read_input_token_cost": null, "output_cost_per_token": 0, "supports_reasoning": null, "supports_prompt_caching": null, "supports_function_calling": null, "supports_response_schema": null, "supports_tool_choice": null, "supports_assistant_prefill": null } ``` 2. `curl -s "http://localhost:27411/model/info?model=glm-5-2" -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-glm52qa"` returns the identical all-null block 3. `curl -s http://localhost:27411/model_group/info -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-glm52qa"` ``` {"model_group":"zai-glm-5-2","max_input_tokens":null,"max_output_tokens":null,"input_cost_per_token":0.0,"supports_reasoning":false,"supports_function_calling":false} {"model_group":"glm-5-2","max_input_tokens":null,"max_output_tokens":null,"input_cost_per_token":0.0,"supports_reasoning":false,"supports_function_calling":false} ``` #### Cost of a real request, cold then cached 1. `curl -s -D - -X POST http://localhost:27411/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-glm52qa" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d @payload.json` ``` x-litellm-response-cost-original: 0.0 x-litellm-response-cost-input: 0.0 x-litellm-response-cost-output: 0 {"prompt_tokens":11115,"cached_tokens":0,"completion_tokens":2} ``` 2. The same command again, so Mistral serves it from its prompt cache ``` x-litellm-response-cost-original: 0.0 x-litellm-response-cost-input: 0.0 x-litellm-response-cost-output: 0 {"prompt_tokens":11115,"cached_tokens":11072,"completion_tokens":2} ``` Two real billed Mistral calls, 22230 prompt tokens between them, both recorded at $0 #### The capabilities the entry claims, driven for real 1. `curl -s -X POST http://localhost:27411/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-glm52qa" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"zai-glm-5-2","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"What is the weather in Paris? Use the tool."}],"tools":[{"type":"function","function":{"name":"get_weather","parameters":{"type":"object","properties":{"city":{"type":"string"}},"required":["city"]}}}],"tool_choice":"auto","max_tokens":100,"temperature":0}'` ``` {"finish":"tool_calls","tool":"get_weather"} ``` The model really does call tools, while the metadata above reports `supports_function_calling` null 2. `curl -s "http://localhost:27411/health?model=zai-glm-5-2" -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-glm52qa"` returns `{"healthy_endpoints":1,"unhealthy_endpoints":0}` ### After (10829fff04) #### Model metadata the gateway reports 1. `curl -s "http://localhost:29337/model/info?model=zai-glm-5-2" -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-glm52qa"` ```json { "max_input_tokens": 1048576, "max_output_tokens": 131072, "input_cost_per_token": 0.0000014, "cache_read_input_token_cost": 1.4E-7, "output_cost_per_token": 0.0000044, "supports_reasoning": true, "supports_prompt_caching": true, "supports_function_calling": true, "supports_response_schema": true, "supports_tool_choice": true, "supports_assistant_prefill": true } ``` 2. `curl -s "http://localhost:29337/model/info?model=glm-5-2" -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-glm52qa"` returns the identical block, so the alias Mistral serves is priced the same 3. `curl -s http://localhost:29337/model_group/info -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-glm52qa"` ``` {"model_group":"zai-glm-5-2","max_input_tokens":1048576.0,"max_output_tokens":131072.0,"input_cost_per_token":0.0000014,"supports_reasoning":true,"supports_function_calling":true} {"model_group":"glm-5-2","max_input_tokens":1048576.0,"max_output_tokens":131072.0,"input_cost_per_token":0.0000014,"supports_reasoning":true,"supports_function_calling":true} ``` #### Cost of a real request, cold then cached 1. `curl -s -D - -X POST http://localhost:29337/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-glm52qa" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d @payload.json` ``` x-litellm-response-cost: 0.015569799999999998 x-litellm-response-cost-input: 0.015560999999999998 x-litellm-response-cost-output: 8.8e-06 {"prompt_tokens":11115,"cached_tokens":0,"completion_tokens":2} ``` 11115 x $1.4/M is $0.015561 of input, 2 x $4.4/M is $0.0000088 of output 2. The same command again, so Mistral serves it from its prompt cache ``` x-litellm-response-cost: 0.0016190800000000002 x-litellm-response-cost-input: 6.0200000000000054e-05 x-litellm-response-cost-cache-read: 0.0015500800000000001 x-litellm-response-cost-output: 8.8e-06 {"prompt_tokens":11115,"cached_tokens":11072,"completion_tokens":2} ``` 11072 reused tokens x $0.14/M is $0.00155008, the remaining 43 x $1.4/M is $0.0000602, and the cache hit costs a tenth of the cold call instead of nothing #### The capabilities the entry claims, driven for real 1. The same tool call as before still returns `{"finish":"tool_calls","tool":"get_weather"}`, and the metadata now says `supports_function_calling` true 2. `curl -s -X POST http://localhost:29337/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-glm52qa" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"zai-glm-5-2","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Give me the capital of France."}],"response_format":{"type":"json_schema","json_schema":{"name":"capital","strict":true,"schema":{"type":"object","properties":{"capital":{"type":"string"}},"required":["capital"],"additionalProperties":false}}},"max_tokens":50,"temperature":0}'` returns `{ "capital": "Paris" }`, backing `supports_response_schema` true 3. `curl -s "http://localhost:29337/health?model=zai-glm-5-2" -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-glm52qa"` returns `{"healthy_endpoints":1,"unhealthy_endpoints":0}`, unchanged from Before ## Type 🆕 New Feature ## Caveats (if any) - Prices and limits read from Mistral's docs and live model API on 2026-08-20 - Public Preview at Mistral, so limits and pricing may still move - Mistral caches implicitly here; `prompt_cache_key` needs `allowed_openai_params` - `reasoning_effort` still 400s: mistral's config only passes it for magistral ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR - [x] 10829fff04 passes /live-pr-risk --- > [!NOTE] > [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) is generating a summary for commit 10829fff048539f6ee7ca1b903c5e3d5350b47dd. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).

signals.title: feat(perplexity): add Agent API third-party models
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Perplexity's Agent API serves four third-party models litellm can't price - Calls to them on `/v1/responses` record no spend at all - The shipped `perplexity/perplexity/sonar` entry is priced off chat rates - `/v1/chat/completions` rejects the same models with a 400 - Perplexity's metered cost arrives as a float, which litellm dropped How it solves it: - Adds DeepSeek V4 Flash 0731, GLM 5.2, Kimi K3, Kimi K2.7 Code - Keys keep both prefixes, matching the shipped `perplexity/perplexity/sonar` entry - Records Perplexity's published Agent API rates and per-model `supports_reasoning` - Resolves ids that repeat the provider prefix, as a last resort - Keeps that prefix through the chat-to-responses bridge - Accepts a float `usage.cost` in the cost calculator, not just a dict - Syncs the same four entries into the bundled backup cost map ## User Flow Before: a developer calling Perplexity's Agent API models through litellm gets no spend recorded on `/v1/responses` and a flat 400 on `/v1/chat/completions` 1. Their proxy admin adds a deployment named `kimi-k3` pointing at `perplexity/perplexity/kimi-k3` and restarts the proxy 2. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/responses with `"model": "kimi-k3"` and get a 200 reading `pong`, but the reply carries no `x-litellm-response-cost` header 3. https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs shows that call at $0, even though the response body says Perplexity metered $0.00052 for it 4. They point the same app at POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with the same `"model": "kimi-k3"` and get a 400 reading `Invalid model 'perplexity/kimi-k3'` 5. Their admin's older `perplexity/perplexity/sonar` deployment does return a cost on `/v1/responses`, but it reads $0.000036 where the same response body says Perplexity metered $0.00002 After: the same calls come back priced at exactly what Perplexity metered, and `/v1/chat/completions` answers instead of failing 1. Their proxy admin adds the same deployment and restarts the proxy 2. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/responses with `"model": "kimi-k3"` and get a 200 reading `pong` with `x-litellm-response-cost: 0.00086`, the same figure the response body reports as metered 3. https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs shows that call at that dollar figure instead of $0 4. They point the same app at POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with the same `"model": "kimi-k3"` and get a 200 reading `pong` with `x-litellm-response-cost: 0.00082` 5. The `perplexity/perplexity/sonar` deployment now reads $0.00002 on `/v1/responses`, matching what Perplexity metered ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/.py -v` - [x] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Shared setup, identical on both sides. `pplx_config.yaml`: ```yaml model_list: - model_name: kimi-k3 litellm_params: model: perplexity/perplexity/kimi-k3 api_key: os.environ/PERPLEXITY_API_KEY - model_name: glm-5.2 litellm_params: model: perplexity/perplexity/glm-5.2 api_key: os.environ/PERPLEXITY_API_KEY - model_name: deepseek-v4-flash litellm_params: model: perplexity/perplexity/deepseek-v4-flash-0731 api_key: os.environ/PERPLEXITY_API_KEY - model_name: kimi-k2.7-code litellm_params: model: perplexity/perplexity/kimi-k2.7-code api_key: os.environ/PERPLEXITY_API_KEY - model_name: agent-sonar litellm_params: model: perplexity/perplexity/sonar api_key: os.environ/PERPLEXITY_API_KEY general_settings: master_key: sk-1234 ``` Both proxies were started the same way, against a real `PERPLEXITY_API_KEY`, and every call below hit `https://api.perplexity.ai` for real money: ``` python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config pplx_config.yaml --port --detailed_debug ``` ### Before (edbb3429a3) #### /v1/responses, the four new Agent API models 1. Ask each of the four models to answer ``` $ for m in kimi-k3 glm-5.2 deepseek-v4-flash kimi-k2.7-code; do curl -s -D - -o /tmp/$m.json http://localhost:43821/v1/responses \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d "{"model":"$m","input":"Reply with exactly: pong","max_output_tokens":2048}" \ | grep -Ei '^HTTP/|^x-litellm-response-cost' done HTTP/1.1 200 OK HTTP/1.1 200 OK HTTP/1.1 200 OK HTTP/1.1 200 OK ``` All four answer, and not one reply carries an `x-litellm-response-cost` header. The full header block for `kimi-k3` shows the cost headers are simply absent: ``` x-litellm-call-id: 50a55adf-ea5b-4492-a23f-1718b3d948e8 x-litellm-model-name: perplexity/perplexity/kimi-k3 x-litellm-model-api-base: https://api.perplexity.ai x-litellm-version: 1.99.0 x-litellm-key-spend: 0.0 x-litellm-model-group: kimi-k3 ``` 2. Read what Perplexity actually charged, straight out of the same response bodies ``` $ for m in kimi-k3 glm-5.2 deepseek-v4-flash kimi-k2.7-code; do echo -n "$m "; jq -c '.usage.cost.total_cost' /tmp/$m.json done kimi-k3 0.00052 glm-5.2 0.00022 deepseek-v4-flash 1e-05 kimi-k2.7-code 0.00083 ``` Perplexity billed for all four calls; litellm recorded nothing #### /v1/responses, the shipped `perplexity/perplexity/sonar` entry 1. Call the deployment and compare the recorded cost against the metered one ``` $ curl -s -D - -o /tmp/sonar.json http://localhost:43821/v1/responses \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model":"agent-sonar","input":"Reply with exactly: pong","max_output_tokens":2048}' \ | grep -Ei '^HTTP/|^x-litellm-response-cost:' HTTP/1.1 200 OK x-litellm-response-cost: 3.6e-05 $ jq -c '{metered: .usage.cost.total_cost, tokens: [.usage.input_tokens, .usage.output_tokens]}' /tmp/sonar.json {"metered":2e-05,"tokens":[31,5]} ``` $0.000036 recorded against $0.00002 metered: 31 + 5 tokens run through the `perplexity/sonar` chat rates instead of the Agent API's own bill #### /v1/chat/completions, an Agent API model 1. Send the same model through chat completions ``` $ curl -s -D - http://localhost:43821/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model":"kimi-k3","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Reply with exactly: pong"}],"max_tokens":2048}' HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request x-litellm-response-cost: 0 {"error":{"message":"litellm.BadRequestError: PerplexityException - Invalid model 'perplexity/kimi-k3'. Permitted models can be found in the documentation at https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/getting-started/models.. Received Model Group=kimi-k3 Available Model Group Fallbacks=None","type":null,"param":null,"code":"400"}} ``` #### /v1/messages, an Agent API model 1. Send the same model through the Anthropic Messages route ``` $ curl -s -D - http://localhost:43821/v1/messages \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model":"kimi-k3","max_tokens":2048,"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Reply with exactly: pong"}]}' HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request {"error":{"message":"litellm.BadRequestError: PerplexityException - Invalid model 'kimi-k3'. Permitted models can be found in the documentation at https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/getting-started/models.. Received Model Group=kimi-k3 Available Model Group Fallbacks=None","type":null,"param":null,"code":"400"}} ``` ### After (a369cb0da) #### /v1/responses, the four new Agent API models 1. Ask each of the four models the same thing ``` $ for m in kimi-k3 glm-5.2 deepseek-v4-flash kimi-k2.7-code; do echo -n "$m " curl -s -D - -o /tmp/a_$m.json http://localhost:41773/v1/responses \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d "{"model":"$m","input":"Reply with exactly: pong","max_output_tokens":2048}" \ | grep -Ei '^x-litellm-response-cost:' done kimi-k3 x-litellm-response-cost: 0.00086 glm-5.2 x-litellm-response-cost: 0.00072 deepseek-v4-flash x-litellm-response-cost: 1e-05 kimi-k2.7-code x-litellm-response-cost: 0.00023 ``` 2. Check each recorded cost against what Perplexity metered on that same call ``` $ for m in kimi-k3 glm-5.2 deepseek-v4-flash kimi-k2.7-code; do echo -n "$m "; jq -c '{status, metered: .usage.cost.total_cost, text: [.output[] | select(.type=="message") | .content[].text]}' /tmp/a_$m.json done kimi-k3 {"status":"completed","metered":0.00086,"text":["pong"]} glm-5.2 {"status":"completed","metered":0.00072,"text":["pong"]} deepseek-v4-flash {"status":"completed","metered":1e-05,"text":["pong"]} kimi-k2.7-code {"status":"completed","metered":0.00023,"text":[" pong "]} ``` Every recorded cost equals the metered one, to the cent Perplexity reports #### /v1/responses, the shipped `perplexity/perplexity/sonar` entry 1. Call the same deployment and compare again ``` $ curl -s -D - -o /tmp/a_sonar.json http://localhost:41773/v1/responses \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model":"agent-sonar","input":"Reply with exactly: pong","max_output_tokens":2048}' \ | grep -Ei '^HTTP/|^x-litellm-response-cost:' HTTP/1.1 200 OK x-litellm-response-cost: 2e-05 $ jq -c '{metered: .usage.cost.total_cost, tokens: [.usage.input_tokens, .usage.output_tokens]}' /tmp/a_sonar.json {"metered":2e-05,"tokens":[31,5]} ``` Same 31 + 5 tokens as the Before run, now recorded at the $0.00002 Perplexity metered instead of $0.000036 #### /v1/chat/completions, an Agent API model 1. Send the same model through chat completions ``` $ curl -s -D - http://localhost:41773/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model":"kimi-k3","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Reply with exactly: pong"}],"max_tokens":2048}' HTTP/1.1 200 OK x-litellm-response-cost: 0.00082 {"id":"chatcmpl-a5932875-eaaf-443d-a3eb-f9e854605c0c","created":1787259030,"model":"kimi-k3","object":"chat.completion","choices":[{"finish_reason":"stop","index":0,"message":{"content":"pong","role":"assistant"}}],"usage":{"completion_tokens":49,"prompt_tokens":110,"total_tokens":159,"completion_tokens_details":{"reasoning_tokens":0},"prompt_tokens_details":{"cached_tokens":92},"cost":0.00082}} ``` The 400 is gone, the model answers `pong`, and the recorded $0.00082 matches the `cost` Perplexity returned #### /v1/messages, an Agent API model 1. Send the same model through the Anthropic Messages route ``` $ curl -s -D - http://localhost:41773/v1/messages \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model":"kimi-k3","max_tokens":2048,"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Reply with exactly: pong"}]}' HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request {"error":{"message":"litellm.BadRequestError: PerplexityException - Invalid model 'kimi-k3'. Permitted models can be found in the documentation at https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/getting-started/models.. Received Model Group=kimi-k3 Available Model Group Fallbacks=None","type":null,"param":null,"code":"400"}} ``` Byte for byte the same failure as Before: this route drops both prefixes before the call goes out, which is a separate bug filed as #37716 and deliberately left alone here ## Type 🆕 New Feature 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - `/v1/messages` still rejects these models, unchanged, tracked in #37716 - `supports_reasoning` for DeepSeek and GLM comes from upstream docs - Perplexity's Router page lists a different GLM 5.2 cache-read rate - `perplexity/perplexity/sonar` still carries no per-token rates - Cost breakdown headers can read negative on cached prompts; the total is right - The two Nemotron Agent API models are out of scope here ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR --- > [!NOTE] > **Medium Risk** > Touches global `get_model_info` name resolution and Perplexity spend calculation. The new lookup is last in the ladder, but a mistake there could mis-price or mis-route models. > > **Overview** > Adds four Perplexity Agent API models (`deepseek-v4-flash-0731`, `glm-5.2`, `kimi-k3`, `kimi-k2.7-code`) as double-prefixed cost-map keys (`perplexity/perplexity/...`) with published rates and per-model `supports_reasoning`. > > **Model lookup** now keeps a last-resort `provider_prefixed_model_name` candidate so IDs that already start with the provider name (e.g. `perplexity/glm-5.2`) can hit those keys. Existing shorter keys such as `perplexity/sonar` still win. > > The completion→responses bridge re-prefixes the model before calling `responses()` / `aresponses()`, so a second `get_llm_provider()` pass does not strip the native id. > > Perplexity cost tracking accepts `usage.cost` as a float (Responses API already flattens the dict), so metered spend is used instead of silently falling back to $0 / unmapped rates. > > Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit a369cb0da7b6581066bd15fd91e169633ede17e8. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot). - [x] a369cb0da7b6581066bd15fd91e169633ede17e8 passes /live-pr-risk

signals.title: fix(auth): return 403 for admin-only route denials
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Admin-only route denials return 401 instead of 403 - Prometheus records them as `exception_status="None"` - Those denials look identical to infrastructure failures How it solves it: - Raise `HTTPException` 403 instead of a bare `Exception` - The status code then reaches both the client and the metric ## User Flow Before: a developer holding a valid non-admin key is told their credentials are invalid, so they re-authenticate and nothing changes 1. An admin issues them a key with the `internal_user` role 2. They send `GET https://litellm-domain/policies/list` with that key 3. It comes back `401 Unauthorized`, and the message opens with "Authentication Error, Only proxy admin can be used to generate, delete, update info for new keys/users/teams" 4. Reading 401 as a credential problem, their client drops the key, signs in again, retries, and gets the same 401 5. Their operator opens the proxy metrics and finds the refusal recorded with `exception_class="Exception"` and `exception_status="None"` on `route="/policies/list"`, the same label pair an unreachable database produces, so it cannot be alerted on separately 6. A non-admin still cannot reach the route, and an admin still can After: the same request is refused as forbidden, so the client keeps its key and the metric names the status 1. An admin issues them a key with the `internal_user` role 2. They send `GET https://litellm-domain/policies/list` with that key 3. It comes back `403 Forbidden` with the same explanation and no "Authentication Error" prefix 4. Their client keeps the key and stops re-authenticating, because 403 says the credential is fine and the permission is not 5. Their operator finds the refusal recorded with `exception_class="HTTPException"` and `exception_status="403"`, now distinguishable from an infrastructure failure 6. A non-admin still cannot reach the route, and an admin still can. Who may call what is unchanged, only how the refusal is reported ## Relevant issues Fixes #37108 ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Shared setup, run once against a local proxy on `localhost:4000` backed by a scratch Postgres, with `callbacks: ["prometheus"]` enabled: ```bash export MASTER=sk-1234 USERKEY=$(curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4000/user/new \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $MASTER" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"user_email":"nonadmin@example.com","user_role":"internal_user"}' \ | python -c "import sys,json; print(json.load(sys.stdin)['key'])") ``` ### Before (973329e9864154d429a7d739fb6a552fe03a9b3e) 1. Call two admin-only routes with the valid non-admin key ```bash for r in /policies/list /prompts/list; do printf "GET %-16s -> " "$r" curl -s -o /tmp/b.json -w "%{http_code}" "http://127.0.0.1:4000$r" -H "Authorization: Bearer $USERKEY" echo " $(head -c 120 /tmp/b.json)" done ``` ``` GET /policies/list -> 401 {"error":{"message":"Authentication Error, Only proxy admin can be used to generate, delete, update GET /prompts/list -> 401 {"error":{"message":"Authentication Error, Only proxy admin can be used to generate, delete, update ``` 2. Read the failure metric for those two routes ```bash curl -sL http://127.0.0.1:4000/metrics -H "Authorization: Bearer $MASTER" \ | grep -oE 'exception_class="[^"]*",exception_status="[^"]*"[^}]*route="/(policies|prompts)/list"' ``` ``` exception_class="Exception",exception_status="None",...,route="/policies/list" exception_class="Exception",exception_status="None",...,route="/prompts/list" ``` ### After (2a0f2b6171) 1. Same two calls, same key ```bash for r in /policies/list /prompts/list; do printf "GET %-16s -> " "$r" curl -s -o /tmp/b.json -w "%{http_code}" "http://127.0.0.1:4000$r" -H "Authorization: Bearer $USERKEY" echo " $(head -c 120 /tmp/b.json)" done ``` ``` GET /policies/list -> 403 {"error":{"message":"Only proxy admin can be used to generate, delete, update info for new keys/us GET /prompts/list -> 403 {"error":{"message":"Only proxy admin can be used to generate, delete, update info for new keys/us ``` 2. Same metric read ```bash curl -sL http://127.0.0.1:4000/metrics -H "Authorization: Bearer $MASTER" \ | grep -oE 'exception_class="[^"]*",exception_status="[^"]*"[^}]*route="/(policies|prompts)/list"' ``` ``` exception_class="HTTPException",exception_status="403",...,route="/policies/list" exception_class="HTTPException",exception_status="403",...,route="/prompts/list" ``` ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - Clients treating 401 as "retry auth" see a status change - Master-key-only routes still raise a bare `Exception`, left out of scope - `/organization/list` and `/team/list` from the issue are already allowed for `internal_user` ## Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signals.title: fix(proxy): read config files as utf-8 instead of the locale encoding
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - A UTF-8 `config.yaml` is decoded with the locale encoding, not utf-8 - On Windows that is cp1252, so `café-gpt` is served as `cafÃ©-gpt` - Some UTF-8 bytes are undefined in cp1252 and raise instead - Two of the five call sites run at `import litellm` How it solves it: - Passes `encoding="utf-8"` at the five config read sites - Adds three regression tests, one of which fails on Linux too ## User Flow Before: an operator who names a model with any non-ASCII character gets a different name back from the gateway than the one they configured 1. They write `model_name: café-gpt` into `config.yaml` and save it as UTF-8 2. They start the proxy and send `GET http://localhost:4000/v1/models` with their master key 3. The response comes back `200` listing `"id": "cafÃ©-gpt"`, a name they never configured 4. Any request they send to `café-gpt` gets `400` for an unknown model, because the routing table holds the mangled name After: the name that comes back is the name they wrote 1. They write the same `model_name: café-gpt` into `config.yaml` 2. They start the proxy and send the same `GET http://localhost:4000/v1/models` 3. The response comes back `200` listing `"id": "café-gpt"` 4. Requests to `café-gpt` route normally ## Relevant issues None filed; found by running the proxy on Windows ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [ ] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Shared setup, both runs, Windows 11, `PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8`: ``` model_list: - model_name: café-gpt litellm_params: model: openai/gpt-4o api_key: sk-not-used general_settings: master_key: sk-1234 ``` ``` python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config config.yaml --port 4000 ``` ### Before (973329e98) 1. `curl -s http://127.0.0.1:4000/v1/models -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234"` 2. ``` http_code=200 {"data":[{"id":"cafÃ©-gpt","object":"model","created":1677610602,"owned_by":"openai"}],"object":"list"} ``` ### After (cd5d414c1) 1. `curl -s http://127.0.0.1:4000/v1/models -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234"` 2. ``` http_code=200 {"data":[{"id":"café-gpt","object":"model","created":1677610602,"owned_by":"openai"}],"object":"list"} ``` ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) `PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8` is set in both runs above, and without it neither revision starts. That is a **separate** Windows defect, not this one: the proxy writes the model name to a cp1252 stdout during startup and dies with `UnicodeEncodeError: 'charmap' codec can't encode characters` followed by `Application startup failed. Exiting.` I confirmed it reproduces identically at the merge base, so it is not introduced here, and I have left it alone to keep this PR to one problem. Happy to file it separately. Two of the five sites (`containers/endpoint_factory.py`, `proxy/container_endpoints/handler_factory.py`) run at import time rather than on the config path, so they are not limited to proxy users. `containers/endpoints.json` is ASCII today, which keeps that half latent rather than live. I also changed the config **write** path at first, on the theory that a config saved on Windows would be cp1252 and unreadable elsewhere. That was wrong and I reverted it: `yaml.dump` defaults to `allow_unicode=False` and emits pure ASCII escapes, so the write never produced non-ASCII bytes and the encoding never mattered there. A repository sweep finds roughly forty further `open()` calls that read JSON or YAML without an encoding, in credential files, guardrail pattern files, and the CLI's own config commands. Same defect, deliberately out of scope here per the isolated-scope requirement. I will file them separately. CI note: `tests/test_litellm/proxy/test_proxy_server.py` has 4 failures on my machine at the merge base, unrelated to this change. My branch has the same 4 and adds 3 passes, so nothing here introduces a failure.

signals.title: fix(proxy): update VerificationToken.spend when SpendLogs record key spend
signals.text: ## Relevant issues Fixes #37144 ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have Added testing in the [`tests/test_litellm/`](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/tree/main/tests/test_litellm) directory, **Adding at least 1 test is a hard requirement** - [ ] My PR passes all unit tests on [`make test-unit`](https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/extras/contributing_code) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible, it only solves 1 specific problem ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Changes SpendLogs can persist `api_key` from `standard_logging_object.metadata.user_api_key_hash` even when the cost-callback `token` / `metadata.user_api_key` is missing (user/team ids still trigger spend tracking). Key spend previously used only the `token` argument, so `LiteLLM_VerificationToken.spend` stayed 0 while SpendLogs accumulated. - Resolve the hashed key for `_update_key_db` from the SpendLogs payload `api_key` when `token` is missing. - In the cost callback, fall back to `standard_logging_object.metadata.user_api_key_hash` so `update_database` and spend counters receive the same key. ## Tests - Successful logged spend increments `LiteLLM_VerificationToken.spend` when `token` is provided. - Successful logged spend increments `LiteLLM_VerificationToken.spend` for the SpendLogs `api_key` when `token` is None and the standard logging payload has `user_api_key_hash`. - Cost callback passes that hash as `token` when `metadata.user_api_key` is missing.

signals.title: fix(responses): accept null created_at on in-progress Azure responses (Fixes #37159)
signals.text: ## Problem Azure OpenAI's `GET /v1/responses/{id}` returns `created_at: null` (along with `id: null` and `output: null`) while a response is still `in_progress` or `queued`. The Responses API spec lets the caller poll for completion, so the proxy must accept the in-progress payload rather than 500'ing on a pydantic ValidationError. `ResponsesAPIResponse.created_at` is currently `int` (required). The Azure in-progress payload reaches the proxy, the model rejects `created_at: null`, the transform wraps the pydantic error as `OpenAIError` / `APIConnectionError`, and the proxy returns HTTP 500 to the caller. That defeats Azure's intended polling semantics and reads as a transient 500 to the user. `id` and `output` are already nullable at a downstream layer (the transform/normalization step) so they are not changed here. Only `created_at` was still required at the model level. ## Implementation summary - One line: `created_at: int` → `created_at: Optional[int] = None` in `litellm/types/llms/openai.py:1247`. - Four regression tests in `tests/test_litellm/types/llms/test_types_llms_openai.py` in a new `TestResponsesAPICreatedAtOptional` class: - `test_accepts_null_created_at_when_in_progress` — model with `created_at=None` parses cleanly. - `test_accepts_int_created_at_when_completed` — model with `created_at=<int>` still parses (the baseline; not affected by the fix). - `test_omits_created_at_payload` — model without `created_at` defaults to None and serializes as null. - `test_transform_get_response_api_response_accepts_null_created_at` — drives `OpenAIResponsesAPIConfig.transform_get_response_api_response` with an Azure in-progress `httpx.Response` and asserts the transform returns a valid `ResponsesAPIResponse` instead of raising `pydantic.ValidationError`. ## Design decisions - Made `created_at` nullable, not unconditional. Existing completed-response payloads still set the int and the model still validates them (the int-path baseline test passes with or without the fix). No breaking change to any working config. - Did not normalize the value in `transform_get_response_api_response` instead. The issue reporter's first sentence ("or `transform_get_response_api_response` should normalize null values before constructing the model") is a valid alternative, but the model-level fix is one line vs. an extra branch in the transform and the other Azure-null field handling is already at the model level for `error`, `incomplete_details`, `instructions`, `metadata`, `model`, `object`, etc. Keeping the pattern consistent. - Did not touch `id` and `output` even though the issue body says they are nullable at Azure. Those are already nullable at a downstream layer; making them Optional on the model would be a wider behavior change (every non-Azure payload that omits them would suddenly accept null too) and is out of scope for this fix. ## Testing performed - `pytest tests/test_litellm/types/llms/test_types_llms_openai.py` — 23/23 pass (19 pre-existing + 4 new). - Self-audit (per the cycle-9-prep "fix all X" pattern): stashed the source diff, re-ran the 4 new tests, observed the exact issue-body `pydantic_core._pydantic_core.ValidationError: 1 validation error for ResponsesAPIResponse / created_at / Input should be a valid integer [type=int_type, input_value=None, input_type=NoneType]` on 3 of them. The 4th is the int-path baseline and correctly passes either way. Restored the fix, re-ran, all 4 pass. - `scripts/type_discipline_gate.py` — OK. - `scripts/ruff_strict_gate.py` — OK. - `ruff format --check` — 2 files already formatted. ## Files changed - `litellm/types/llms/openai.py` (+1 / -1) - `tests/test_litellm/types/llms/test_types_llms_openai.py` (+112 / -38) ## Risks - Minimal. The change is purely permissive — it allows a previously-rejected value (null) while still accepting the previous value (int). No working config changes behavior. - The OpenAI backend still returns an int for completed responses, so the existing `test_openai_responses_api_field_types` assertion that `isinstance(response.created_at, int)` is unaffected. ## Future improvement opportunities - Make `id` and `output` Optional on the same model if a future Azure / OpenAI change ever sends them null for completed responses too. Out of scope for this PR. - A follow-up could log a warning when the transform sees `created_at=None` so operators know a downstream caller is polling an in-progress response. Fixes #37159.
signals.author: Harsh23Kashyap

signals.title: fix: let s3_bucket_name reach litellm_params
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - `s3_bucket_name` in a model's `litellm_params` is silently dropped - Bedrock batch output cannot be downloaded without an env var - `gcs_bucket_name` works, so Vertex users never hit this How it solves it: - Adds `s3_bucket_name` to `OPTIONAL_KWARGS_KEYS` - One-line change, plus a regression test ## User Flow Before: someone running Claude batch jobs on Bedrock configures the bucket on the model, submits a job that completes, and then cannot fetch the results 1. They set `s3_bucket_name` on their Bedrock deployment in `config.yaml` and start the proxy with no `AWS_S3_BUCKET_NAME` in the environment 2. They `POST /v1/files` with `purpose=batch` and a JSONL of requests, and get a file ID back 3. They `POST /v1/batches` with that file ID, and get a batch ID back 4. They poll `GET /v1/batches/{id}` until it reports `completed`, with an empty failure message and no error file 5. They `GET /v1/files/{output_file_id}/content` and get `500 {"error":{"message":"S3 bucket_name is required. Set 's3_bucket_name' in proxy config or AWS_S3_BUCKET_NAME for Bedrock file content retrieval."}}` 6. The results are unreachable through the gateway even though the job succeeded and was billed, and the only way out is to restart the proxy with the environment variable set After: the same configuration works, and the results come back 1. They set `s3_bucket_name` on their Bedrock deployment in `config.yaml` and start the proxy with no `AWS_S3_BUCKET_NAME` in the environment 2. They `POST /v1/files` with `purpose=batch` and a JSONL of requests, and get a file ID back 3. They `POST /v1/batches` with that file ID, and get a batch ID back 4. They poll `GET /v1/batches/{id}` until it reports `completed`, with an empty failure message and no error file 5. They `GET /v1/files/{output_file_id}/content` and get `200` with one JSONL line per record 6. They read the results, matching each line back to their input by ID ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [ ] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Captured against a deployed proxy on `v1.91.3`, which carries the same allowlist as the merge base, rather than against the two commit hashes. The reproduction is a real Bedrock batch job in `eu-west-1` billed to a real account, and the download is the exact call an end user makes. A run at the merge base and at the PR tip is still worth doing before merge; I could not stand up managed files locally because that path needs a database and the migration step did not complete under emulation on my machine. Shared setup: one Bedrock deployment whose `litellm_params` carry `model`, `aws_access_key_id`, `aws_secret_access_key`, `aws_region_name` and `s3_bucket_name`, with `AWS_S3_BUCKET_NAME` absent from the process environment. Input is a 100 record JSONL, which is Bedrock's minimum. ### Before (allowlist without `s3_bucket_name`) 1. Upload the input ``` POST /v1/files purpose=batch, target_model_names=bedrock/global.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0 200 status=uploaded ``` 2. Create the batch ``` POST /v1/batches 200 status=validating ``` 3. Poll until terminal ``` GET /v1/batches/{id} 200 status=completed failure_message '' error_file_id null job: arn:aws:bedrock:eu-west-1:...:model-invocation-job/kpiid5uv6b9l ``` 4. Download the output, which is where it breaks ``` GET /v1/files/{output_file_id}/content 500 {"error":{"message":"S3 bucket_name is required. Set 's3_bucket_name' in proxy config or AWS_S3_BUCKET_NAME for Bedrock file content retrieval.","code":"500"}} ``` 5. Repeat step 4 passing the model explicitly, since a caller would try that next, and get the same result ``` GET /v1/files/{output_file_id}/content?model=bedrock/global.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0 500 same error GET /v1/files/{output_file_id}/content with header x-litellm-model 500 same error ``` ### After (`070320e94c`, and equivalently with the env var set) 1. Upload the input ``` POST /v1/files 200 status=uploaded ``` 2. Create the batch ``` POST /v1/batches 200 status=validating ``` 3. Poll until terminal ``` GET /v1/batches/{id} 200 status=completed failure_message '' error_file_id null ``` 4. Download the output ``` GET /v1/files/{output_file_id}/content 200 59400 bytes, 100 JSONL records ``` 5. Confirm every submitted record came back, keyed by ID ``` matched 100/100 ticket-0000 -> DELIVERY ticket-0001 -> BILLING ticket-0002 -> PROMO ``` ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - `s3_region_name` is likely dropped the same way, untested - Proof captured on `v1.91.3`, not at the two hashes
