signals.title: feat(proxy): add POST /auto_router/validate_complexity_router_config to dry-run the complexity-router write gate
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - The only way to check a complexity-router config is a real save - A bad config fails as a raw 400 on the write - Forms and scripts cannot show the validator's verdict beforehand How it solves it: - POST /auto_router/validate_complexity_router_config dry-runs the exact write-gate validator - Returns valid plus the verdict text, saves and routes nothing - Gated exactly like the /model/new save it rehearses, sharing test_routing's gate: a proxy admin, or a team admin naming their own team via team_id (team path is enterprise, matching team model writes) - Also registers both dry-run routes in self_managed_routes: they enforce the write's gate themselves, but the route layer used to 403 every non-proxy-admin key first, which left test_routing's team-admin support unreachable over HTTP - test_routing's routed_model_configured is now computed from get_available_models_for_user (scoped to the caller and the named team) instead of the router's full model list, so a team admin cannot use it as an existence oracle for model names their team was never granted ## User Flow Before: an operator drafting a custom-tier router config can only test it by attempting a save 1. They POST https://litellm-domain/model/new with their drafted complexity router config 2. The save fails 400 with the validator's message buried in an error wrapper 3. They fix one field and repeat, each attempt being a real write that could half-succeed After: the same operator checks the draft without writing anything 1. They POST https://litellm-domain/auto_router/validate_complexity_router_config with the same drafted config (a team admin includes the team_id they would save under) 2. A 200 comes back with valid true, or valid false plus the exact message the save would give 3. They iterate until valid true, then POST https://litellm-domain/model/new once and it succeeds ## Relevant issues Extracted from #37246 so the validation contract lands before its UI consumers ## Linear ticket Part of LIT-5214 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Run from this branch against a live proxy on port 4471 ### Valid config as proxy admin ``` curl -s http://127.0.0.1:4471/auto_router/validate_complexity_router_config -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"complexity_router_config": {"tiers": {"CASUAL": "tier-simple", "AUDIT": "tier-security"}, "tier_definitions": [{"name": "CASUAL", "description": "casual chat"}, {"name": "AUDIT", "description": "security audits"}], "fallback_tier": "AUDIT", "classifier_type": "llm", "classifier_llm_config": {"model": "classifier-model"}}}' ``` ``` {"valid":true,"error":null} ``` ### Config the write gate rejects ``` curl -s http://127.0.0.1:4471/auto_router/validate_complexity_router_config -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"complexity_router_config": {"tiers": {"CASUAL": "tier-simple", "AUDIT": "tier-security"}, "tier_definitions": [{"name": "CASUAL", "description": "casual chat"}, {"name": "AUDIT", "description": "security audits"}], "fallback_tier": "AUDIT", "session_affinity": true, "classifier_type": "llm", "classifier_llm_config": {"model": "classifier-model"}}}' ``` ``` {"valid":false,"error":"complexity_router_config is invalid at complexity_router_config: Value error, session_affinity cannot be combined with tier_definitions: these features rely on the built-in tier severity order, which a custom tier set does not define. The router would drop this deployment at load time, so the write is rejected instead."} ``` ### Team admin validating for their own team Setup: create the user, a team they administer, and a key for them ``` curl -s http://127.0.0.1:4471/user/new -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"user_id": "proof-team-admin", "user_role": "internal_user"}' curl -s http://127.0.0.1:4471/team/new -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"team_id": "proof-team-1", "team_alias": "proof-team", "members_with_roles": [{"role": "admin", "user_id": "proof-team-admin"}]}' curl -s http://127.0.0.1:4471/key/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"user_id": "proof-team-admin"}' ``` Then validate with that key, naming the team ``` curl -s http://127.0.0.1:4471/auto_router/validate_complexity_router_config -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEAM_ADMIN_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"complexity_router_config": {"tiers": {"CASUAL": "m1"}, "classifier_type": "heuristic"}, "team_id": "proof-team-1"}' ``` ``` {"valid":true,"error":null} ``` The same key can also reach test_routing for its team now that the routes are registered in self_managed_routes; before this change the route layer 403'd it as an admin-only route before the endpoint's own gate ran ``` curl -s http://127.0.0.1:4471/auto_router/test_routing -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEAM_ADMIN_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"prompt": "what is 2+2", "complexity_router_config": {"tiers": {"SIMPLE": ["gpt-4o-mini"], "COMPLEX": ["gpt-5.5"]}, "classifier_type": "heuristic"}, "team_id": "proof-team-1"}' ``` ``` {"routed_model":"gpt-4o-mini","routed_model_configured":true,"routing_decision":{"router_model_name":"auto_router_routing_test","router_type":"complexity","routed_model":"gpt-4o-mini","cause":"heuristic_scorer","tier":"SIMPLE", ...} ``` ### routed_model_configured is scoped to what the caller can use With the team above granted only gpt-4o-mini, the team admin routes a prompt to gpt-5.5, which this proxy serves but the team was never granted. The field reads false, so it cannot confirm the name exists ``` curl -s http://127.0.0.1:4471/auto_router/test_routing -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEAM_ADMIN_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"prompt": "compare and contrast three architectures for a multi-region database and justify a recommendation", "complexity_router_config": {"tiers": {"SIMPLE": ["gpt-4o-mini"], "MEDIUM": ["gpt-5.5"], "COMPLEX": ["gpt-5.5"], "REASONING": ["gpt-5.5"]}, "classifier_type": "heuristic"}, "team_id": "proof-team-1"}' ``` ``` {"routed_model":"gpt-5.5","routed_model_configured":false, ...} ``` The same probe as a proxy admin still reads true ``` {"routed_model":"gpt-5.5","routed_model_configured":true, ...} ``` ### Caller who could not save the router A plain internal_user key without a team_id gets the gate's verdict, not the route layer's generic 403 ``` curl -s http://127.0.0.1:4471/auto_router/validate_complexity_router_config -H "Authorization: Bearer $PLAIN_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"complexity_router_config": {"tiers": {"CASUAL": "m1"}, "classifier_type": "heuristic"}}' ``` ``` {"detail":{"error":"User does not have permission to dry-run an auto router. Your role=internal_user. Call as a PROXY_ADMIN, or as a team admin by specifying a team_id."}} ``` ### Unauthenticated ``` curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" http://127.0.0.1:4471/auto_router/validate_complexity_router_config -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"complexity_router_config": {}}' ``` ``` 401 ``` ## Type 🆕 New Feature ## Caveats (if any) - The endpoint validates config shape only; it does not check that tier model names resolve to deployments, matching the write gate it mirrors - The name is scoped to the complexity router on purpose: other router config families added later get their own validation routes instead of overloading this one - Registering /auto_router/test_routing in self_managed_routes also fixes a pre-existing gap where its team-admin branch was unreachable over HTTP, since both dry runs share one gate this belongs in the same change <!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY --> --- > [!NOTE] > **Medium Risk** > Touches proxy route-auth (self_managed_routes) and what model names a team admin can confirm exist. Auth is aligned with /model/new and the new endpoint does not persist or bill. > > **Overview** > Adds `POST /auto_router/validate_complexity_router_config` so operators can get the **same write-gate verdict** as `/model/new` without saving. It returns `{valid, error}` via `validate_complexity_router_config_write` and does not create, route, or bill. > > Both this route and `/auto_router/test_routing` are registered on `self_managed_routes` and share `_authorize_router_dry_run` (proxy admin, or team admin naming their own `team_id`). That also makes `test_routing`’s team-admin path reachable over HTTP instead of 403ing at the route layer. > > `test_routing` now sets `routed_model_configured` from `get_available_models_for_user` (caller/team-scoped) rather than the proxy’s full model list, so it is not an existence oracle for ungranted models. > > <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit bdb831183c20fbca9ac3c217e5aa84bad42fe937. signals.title: fix(ui): keep keyword tier rules that target operator-defined tiers when hydrating the edit modal
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - The backend accepts keyword rules targeting operator-defined tiers - The edit modal's hydration only keeps built-in tier names - Opening and saving a router silently deletes those rules How it solves it: - Hydration keeps any rule with a non-empty string tier - The rule type widens from the built-in union to string - A round-trip unit test pins hydrate then serialize losslessly ## User Flow Before: an operator whose custom-tier router routes pentest prompts by keyword loses that rule by touching the edit form 1. They run a router whose config defines a SECURITY_REVIEW tier and a keyword rule sending "pentest" prompts to it 2. They open http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=models-and-endpoints and open that router's Edit Auto Router modal 3. The keyword rules section shows their MEDIUM rule but not the SECURITY_REVIEW one 4. They press Save without changing anything, and the stored config now has the SECURITY_REVIEW rule deleted 5. "pentest" prompts quietly stop routing to the security tier, with nothing telling them why After: the same modal shows and preserves every rule 1. They run the same router and open the same Edit Auto Router modal 2. The keyword rules section lists both rules, the SECURITY_REVIEW one included 3. They press Save without changing anything, and the stored config still carries both rules 4. "pentest" prompts keep routing to the security tier ## Relevant issues Extracted from #37246; the data loss is reachable on staging today because #37226 (merged) already accepts these configs ## Linear ticket Part of LIT-5214 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix UI change; screenshots to be posted from the steps below 1. Create a router whose complexity_router_config defines a custom tier and a keyword rule targeting it, via POST http://localhost:4000/model/new with tier_definitions including SECURITY_REVIEW and keyword_tier_rules [{"keywords": ["pentest"], "tier": "SECURITY_REVIEW"}] 2. Open http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=models-and-endpoints, find the router, open Edit Auto Router 3. Before this change the SECURITY_REVIEW rule is missing from the keyword rules list and a no-op Save deletes it from the stored config; after, it is listed and survives the save 4. Confirm via GET http://localhost:4000/v1/model/info that keyword_tier_rules still contains the SECURITY_REVIEW rule after saving ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - The rule editor's tier dropdown still offers only built-in tiers; offering defined tier names is part of the tier editor UI in #37246 <!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY --> --- > [!NOTE] > **Low Risk** > Small UI hydration/type change that prevents data loss on save; routing logic and auth are untouched. The dropdown still cannot pick custom tiers, so operators can preserve but not newly select them here. > > **Overview** > Stops the Auto Router edit modal from silently dropping keyword-tier rules that target operator-defined tiers. > > `hydrateKeywordTierRules` no longer filters against the built-in `SIMPLE`/`MEDIUM`/`COMPLEX`/`REASONING` set. Any rule with keywords and a non-empty string `tier` is kept, so a no-op save no longer deletes custom-tier routing. The `KeywordTierRule` type is widened to `string` to match. > > Tests pin hydrate/serialize round-trip for names like `SECURITY_REVIEW`. The dropdown still only lists built-in tiers. > > <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 5a4ebb7e9baba7583d7a1367fc3d846c086df1f9. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup> <!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

signals.title: fix(zai): add provider and current model catalog
signals.text: ## TLDR Fixes the Z.AI dashboard onboarding path and brings the bundled Z.AI catalog up to the current documented models. - Adds Z.AI to the Add Model provider catalog. - Lets provider search match the LiteLLM slug `zai` as well as the display name. - Adds the six current Z.AI models missing from the model cost map: `glm-5.3`, `glm-5.2`, `glm-5-turbo`, `glm-5v-turbo`, `glm-4.7-flashx`, and `glm-4.6v`. - Keeps `model_prices_and_context_window.json` and the bundled backup map in sync. The Z.AI provider uses the OpenAI-compatible base URL `https://api.z.ai/api/paas/v4`. ## User Flow Before: 1. A proxy admin opens Add Model and searches for `zai` or `z.ai`. 2. The provider dropdown returns no result, so no Z.AI credentials or model choices can be configured. After: 1. The same admin searches for `zai` or `z.ai` and selects Z.AI. 2. The form shows the API key field and default Z.AI API base. 3. The model selector includes the current Z.AI models, including GLM-5.3, GLM-5.2, GLM-5-Turbo, GLM-5V-Turbo, GLM-4.7-FlashX, and GLM-4.6V. ## Root Cause LiteLLM supported the `zai` provider in the SDK and had existing Z.AI metadata, but the dashboard provider-creation catalog omitted it. The catalog also lagged the current Z.AI model list. ## Relevant Issues Fixes #25482 Supersedes the stale unmerged implementation in #25485. The existing provider-name mapping from #26419 is retained. ## Validation - `python3 -m json.tool model_prices_and_context_window.json` - Verified the canonical and bundled backup maps are byte-identical. - Added `tests/test_litellm/test_zai_model_metadata.py`, which asserts the documented 15-model Z.AI subset and exact metadata for the six newly catalogued models. - `npm run test -- --run src/components/add_model/AddModelForm.test.tsx` passes: 13 tests. - In a local Admin UI running against the proposed bundled catalog, `GET /public/litellm_model_cost_map` exposes all six new model IDs and the Add Model selector shows all six, including search results for `zai/glm-4.7-flashx` and `zai/glm-4.6v`. ## CI Note The earlier `misc` failure in run 32214763016 is unrelated to this PR's original changes. It failed `tests/test_litellm/batches/test_batch_utils.py::test_handle_completed_vertex_batch_computes_cost_usage_and_models`, where a Vertex batch cost expectation was double the observed value. This PR did not change batch code, Vertex code, or the model cost map in that run. The new push should receive a fresh CI result. ## Pre-Submission Checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests. - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks. - [x] My PR's scope is isolated to Z.AI dashboard onboarding and catalog metadata. - [x] I have received a Greptile Confidence Score of at least 4/5 before requesting maintainer review. ## Type Bug Fix ## Caveats - The focused Python test requires the full LiteLLM Python dependency set, which is unavailable in this local worktree. The JSON, bundled-map consistency, runtime API, and UI flows were verified locally; GitHub CI will run the Python test. - A full local Docker image build requires the Docker buildx plugin. ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including edge cases and real-world customer regressions.

signals.title: fix(proxy/mcp): pass through client-native tool_use turns in auto-execute loop (#37031)
signals.text: Fixes #37031 ## Problem When `require_approval: "never"` is configured for server-side MCP tools, the proxy auto-executes tools emitted by models during `/v1/messages` calls. When an agentic client (e.g. Claude Code) sends its own client-side tools (`Read`, `Bash`, `Edit`) in the same turn, the auto-execute loop attempts to look up every requested tool in `tool_server_map`. Missing client tools cause a `KeyError` that is caught and converted into `Error executing tool: '<tool>'`, breaking all client-native tools. ## Fix Updated `anthropic_messages_with_mcp` in `mcp_handler.py` to check whether any emitted `tool_use` block is missing from `tool_server_map`. If client-native tools are detected in the turn, server-side auto-execution breaks and returns the response directly to the client. This allows agentic clients to handle their local tools while preserving valid Anthropic tool/result message ordering. ## Checklist - [x] Verified fix via unit test (`pytest tests/test_mcp_client_tool_passthrough.py` passes). - [x] Handled mixed client/server tool turns without invalidating message sequence.

signals.title: fix(logging): only hand a call to a prompt manager that claims it
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - `cache_control_injection_points` returns HTTP 500 when a prompt manager is registered - Dotprompt claims prompt-less calls, then rejects them for having no `prompt_id` How it solves it: - Ask each prompt manager whether it owns the call before handing it over - Managers that decline no longer block the cache-control hook ## User Flow Before: an admin who turns on prompt caching for a model gets a 500 on every request to it, once any prompt manager is configured 1. The admin configures `claude-opus-4-5` with `cache_control_injection_points: [{role: system, location: message}]` and sets `callbacks: ["dotprompt"]` 2. A developer sends POST http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions with that model, a system message, a user message, and no `prompt_id` 3. The response is HTTP 500 and no assistant message comes back 4. They remove `cache_control_injection_points` and resend the same request, which now returns HTTP 200, so the caching setting is what breaks it After: the same request returns an answer, and the system message reaches the provider marked for caching 1. The admin keeps the same config 2. The developer sends the same POST http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions 3. The response is HTTP 200 with an assistant message 4. The provider receives the system block carrying `"cache_control": {"type": "ephemeral"}`, so the cached prefix is billed as a cache read on the next call ## Relevant issues Fixes #37469 ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix `cache_control_injection_points` is in `DynamicPromptManagementParamLiteral`, so `should_run_prompt_management_hooks` returns True with `prompt_id=None`, and `get_custom_logger_for_prompt_management` then returned `prompt_management_loggers[0]` without asking whether that logger could handle the call. `DotpromptManager.get_chat_completion_prompt` delegates to `PromptManagementBase`, which raises on `prompt_id=None` The failure happens in local preprocessing before any provider request is built, so the run below drives real HTTP through the full SDK path with an upstream that records what it receives. I do not have provider credentials on this machine, so the upstream is a stub on 127.0.0.1 rather than Anthropic. The "After" case proves the fix by showing the system block on the wire with `cache_control` attached, which is exactly what the provider would have been sent Shared setup, both cases: ```bash cat > /tmp/upstream.py <<'PY' import json from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, HTTPServer CANNED = {"id": "msg_stub", "type": "message", "role": "assistant", "model": "claude-opus-4-5", "content": [{"type": "text", "text": "Hi from the stub upstream."}], "stop_reason": "end_turn", "usage": {"input_tokens": 12, "output_tokens": 6}} class Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler): def do_POST(self): open("/tmp/last_request.json", "wb").write(self.rfile.read(int(self.headers["content-length"]))) payload = json.dumps(CANNED).encode() self.send_response(200) self.send_header("content-type", "application/json") self.send_header("content-length", str(len(payload))) self.end_headers() self.wfile.write(payload) def log_message(self, *a): pass HTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 8899), Handler).serve_forever() PY cat > /tmp/call.py <<'PY' import json, sys, litellm litellm.callbacks = ["dotprompt"] try: r = litellm.completion( model="anthropic/claude-opus-4-5", api_key="sk-ant-stub", api_base="http://127.0.0.1:8899", messages=[{"role": "system", "content": "You are helpful."}, {"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}], cache_control_injection_points=[{"role": "system", "location": "message"}]) print("HTTP 200:", r.choices[0].message.content) print("system sent upstream:", json.dumps(json.load(open("/tmp/last_request.json"))["system"])) except Exception as e: print(f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}") sys.exit(1) PY python /tmp/upstream.py & ``` ### Before (c696fdfb05) 1. `python /tmp/call.py` 2. Output: ``` ValueError: prompt_id is required for Prompt Management Base class ``` ### After (54754e48bc) 1. `python /tmp/call.py` 2. Output: ``` HTTP 200: Hi from the stub upstream. system sent upstream: [{"type": "text", "text": "You are helpful.", "cache_control": {"type": "ephemeral"}}] ``` ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - Empty `prompt_id` was also affected; now covered by a test - A named prompt plus cache control still selects only the manager - Every in-tree manager already gates on `should_run_prompt_management` - Prompt-less `CustomPromptManagement` subclasses keep being selected, tested ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signals.title: fix: omit thinking.type=disabled for always-on thinking Claude models
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - `thinking: {"type": "disabled"}` forwarded verbatim to Fable/Mythos models - those models 400: "thinking.type.disabled is not supported for this model" - routers retargeting requests across model generations hit this constantly How it solves it: - new cost map flag `thinking_always_on` on Fable/Mythos entries - Anthropic, /v1/messages, and Bedrock Converse transforms omit the param when flagged - omission is the API documented remedy; model thinks adaptively by default ## User Flow Before: a caller whose request was valid on Claude Sonnet 4.5 gets a 400 when a router sends the same request to Claude Fable 5 1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages with `"model": "claude-fable-5"`, `"thinking": {"type": "disabled"}` 2. The response is a 400 with `"thinking.type.disabled" is not supported for this model. Thinking defaults to adaptive mode when not specified` 3. The same body against a router model group fails the whole request whenever the router picks a Fable 5 deployment, even though the request was valid on the model the caller originally targeted After: the same request succeeds; the model thinks adaptively as the API prescribes 1. They send the same POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages with `"model": "claude-fable-5"`, `"thinking": {"type": "disabled"}` 2. The response is a 200 with the model's normal content; the gateway omitted the unsupported param and logged a warning 3. Requests carrying `thinking: {"type": "disabled"}` to models that accept it (Sonnet 4.5, Opus 4.8, Opus 5, Sonnet 5) are forwarded byte for byte, unchanged ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Setup: local proxy on :4620 from this branch, `LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True`, real Postgres, models `claude-fable-5` and `claude-sonnet-4-5` served through a live Anthropic-compatible upstream (real provider account for this repo is out of credit; the upstream is the team's live gateway hitting the real Anthropic API, so requests, money, and the 400 are real). Config: ```yaml model_list: - model_name: claude-fable-5 litellm_params: model: anthropic/claude-fable-5 api_base: https://<gateway-host> api_key: os.environ/ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN - model_name: claude-sonnet-4-5 litellm_params: model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5 api_base: https://<gateway-host> api_key: os.environ/ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN general_settings: master_key: sk-1234 ``` ### Before (4bb3152cc5) #### /v1/messages, claude-fable-5, thinking disabled 1. `curl -s -w "HTTP %{http_code}" -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4620/v1/messages -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"claude-fable-5","max_tokens":64,"thinking":{"type":"disabled"},"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"say hi repro leg 1"}]}'` 2. `HTTP 400` with `"\"thinking.type.disabled\" is not supported for this model. Thinking defaults to adaptive mode when not specified; use \"thinking.type.enabled\" with \"budget_tokens\" for extended thinking"` #### /v1/chat/completions, claude-fable-5, thinking disabled 1. Same body against http://127.0.0.1:4620/v1/chat/completions 2. `HTTP 400`, `litellm.BadRequestError: AnthropicException` wrapping the same provider error #### /v1/messages, claude-sonnet-4-5, thinking disabled (negative control) 1. Same body with `"model": "claude-sonnet-4-5"` 2. `HTTP 200`, normal text content (this model accepts disabled) ### After (1eb90f3d0a) #### /v1/messages, claude-fable-5, thinking disabled 1. Same curl as Before 2. `HTTP 200`, content starts with an adaptive thinking block then text; proxy log shows `Dropping thinking={'type': 'disabled'} for model=claude-fable-5: thinking is always on for this model and cannot be disabled. The model thinks adaptively when the param is omitted.` #### /v1/chat/completions, claude-fable-5, thinking disabled 1. Same curl as Before (max_tokens 2048 so text survives the thinking budget) 2. `HTTP 200`, `content: "Hi! ..."`, `model: claude-fable-5` #### /v1/messages, claude-sonnet-4-5, thinking disabled (negative control) 1. Same curl as Before 2. `HTTP 200`, normal text content, request body forwarded unchanged (no warning logged) ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - Bedrock Converse arm covered by unit tests only; no AWS credentials in this rig - /v1/responses already converts `thinking` to `reasoning`, never forwards disabled - Opus 5 `disabled` plus `output_config.effort xhigh/max` is a caller contradiction, untouched - unmapped future Fable/Mythos ids covered by a `fallback_generalizations` rule ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR <!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY --> --- > [!NOTE] > **Medium Risk** > Changes Anthropic/Bedrock request transforms and model capability metadata. Scope is narrow (only drops `thinking.type=disabled` for flagged models) but incorrect flagging would silently change thinking behavior. > > **Overview** > Stops Fable/Mythos (and unmapped family ids) from 400ing when a caller or router forwards `thinking={"type": "disabled"}`. Those models reject disabled thinking; omitting the param is the documented fallback to adaptive thinking. > > Adds a cost-map flag `thinking_always_on` on Fable/Mythos entries plus a `claude-always-on-thinking` fallback rule. Chat, `/v1/messages`, and Bedrock Converse transforms drop only that disabled shape for flagged models and leave it unchanged for models that accept it (e.g. Opus/Sonnet 5). Also hoists the duplicated `local_model_cost_map` pytest fixture into shared conftest. > > <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 1eb90f3d0aed662f88d8138b4a317b0e599a5abb. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup> <!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

signals.title: fix(fireworks_ai): add missing serverless models to cost map
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Fireworks serverless models like kimi-k3 report $0 cost - Cost map lags behind the Fireworks serverless pricing page How it solves it: - Adds 10 missing serverless models to the cost map - Prices and context windows taken from Fireworks pricing docs ## User Flow Before: a platform team exposing Fireworks through a `fireworks_ai/*` wildcard route sees zero cost reported for kimi-k3 and deepseek-v4-flash-0731, so spend tracking undercounts 1. The proxy admin lists `fireworks_ai/*` once in the proxy config and has cost map auto-sync enabled 2. A developer sends POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with `"model": "fireworks_ai/accounts/fireworks/models/kimi-k3"` and gets a 200 completion back 3. The response header `x-litellm-response-cost` reports zero cost, and the same request through POST https://litellm-domain/v1/responses and POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages reports zero as well 4. The same three calls with `"model": "fireworks_ai/accounts/fireworks/models/deepseek-v4-flash-0731"` also report zero cost, so every downstream spend report shows $0 for both models After: the same wildcard traffic is billed at the published Fireworks serverless rates, with no proxy upgrade needed 1. The proxy admin lists `fireworks_ai/*` once in the proxy config and cost map auto-sync pulls the updated prices 2. A developer sends POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with `"model": "fireworks_ai/accounts/fireworks/models/kimi-k3"` and gets a 200 completion back 3. The response header `x-litellm-response-cost` now carries a non-zero amount at $3/1M input and $15/1M output, on /v1/chat/completions, /v1/responses, and /v1/messages alike 4. The same three calls with `"model": "fireworks_ai/accounts/fireworks/models/deepseek-v4-flash-0731"` bill at $0.14/1M input and $0.28/1M output, so downstream spend reports carry the real numbers ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5852 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [ ] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Live A/B through a real proxy against the real Fireworks API, no mocks. Both legs run the same wildcard config and the same venv, and the tree under test is asserted from `litellm.__file__`, so the runs differ only in the commit the proxy serves: ```yaml model_list: - model_name: "fireworks_ai/*" litellm_params: model: "fireworks_ai/*" api_key: os.environ/FIREWORKS_AI_API_KEY general_settings: master_key: sk-1234 ``` ```bash LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True .venv/bin/litellm --config fw_wildcard.yaml --port <free port> ``` ### Before (merge base f6eaca9069) ```bash curl -sS -D - http://localhost:46910/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model": "fireworks_ai/accounts/fireworks/models/kimi-k3", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Say hi"}], "max_tokens": 16}' ``` ``` HTTP/1.1 200 OK x-litellm-response-cost-original: 0.0 x-litellm-response-cost-input: 0.0 x-litellm-response-cost-output: 0.0 x-litellm-key-spend: 0.0 ``` The bare `x-litellm-response-cost` header is absent on every 200, and the sub-headers all read 0.0 ### After (PR tip c15e4602e8) Same curl, same prompt, same port-free proxy on the PR commit: ``` HTTP/1.1 200 OK x-litellm-response-cost: 0.00051 x-litellm-response-cost-original: 0.00051 x-litellm-response-cost-input: 0.00027 x-litellm-response-cost-output: 0.00024 x-litellm-key-spend: 0.00051 ``` That lines up with the published rates exactly. Usage came back as 90 prompt and 16 completion tokens, so 90 at $3/M is $0.00027 in and 16 at $15/M is $0.00024 out ### Both legs, every call | Call | Endpoint | Model | Before | After | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 1 | /v1/chat/completions | kimi-k3 | 200, cost 0.0 | 200, cost 0.00051 | | 2 | /v1/responses | kimi-k3 | 200, cost 0.0 | 200, cost 0.00051 | | 3 | /v1/messages | kimi-k3 | 200, cost 0.0 | 200, cost 0.00051 | | 4 | /v1/chat/completions | deepseek-v4-flash | 200, cost 0.0 | 200, cost 5.32e-06 | | 5 | /v1/responses | deepseek-v4-flash | 200, cost 0.0 | 200, cost 5.32e-06 | | 6 | /v1/messages | deepseek-v4-flash | 200, cost 0.0 | 200, cost 5.32e-06 | | 7 | /v1/chat/completions | kimi-k3 short slug | 200, cost 0.0 | 200, cost 0.00051 | | 8 | GET /v1/models | both | absent, 294 ids | present, 314 ids | | 9 | chat + tool_choice required | kimi-k3 | 400 | 200, tool_calls | Call 8: the twenty added keys are exactly the twenty new ids in the wildcard expansion, 294 to 314 Call 9 before, the capability gate rejected the request before it ever reached Fireworks: ``` litellm.UnsupportedParamsError: fireworks_ai does not support parameters: ['tool_choice'], for model=accounts/fireworks/models/kimi-k3 ``` Call 9 after, the same request is forwarded and comes back with a real tool call: ```json {"finish_reason": "tool_calls", "tool_calls": [{"index": 0, "function": {"arguments": "{}", "name": "say_hi"}, "id": "say_hi_0", "type": "function"}]} ``` So the entry does not just fix billing, it also unblocks tool calling that the gate was refusing. That one call runs with `max_tokens` 400 rather than 16, because kimi-k3 spends its budget on reasoning before emitting a tool call and 16 truncates first. The before-leg rejection comes from the param gate ahead of the provider, so the token budget has no bearing on it ### Pricing sources Every cost value comes from the [Fireworks serverless pricing table](https://docs.fireworks.ai/serverless/pricing), re-checked row by row for all ten models. Context windows were verified against the live models API rather than the docs page: kimi-k3, kimi-k3-fast and deepseek-v4-flash-0731 each report `context_length` 1048576, which is what this PR sets ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - Data-only change; no test file maps to the cost map JSON - `qwen3p8-max` carries `max_output_tokens: 65536` from the upstream Qwen spec, but Fireworks enforces no output cap of its own, `max_tokens` of 65537 and 999999 both come back 200. It only has an effect under `modify_params: true`, which is off by default, where a larger `max_tokens` gets clamped down to 65536 - fast/us variants keyed under accounts/fireworks/routers/, matching the existing glm-5p1-fast pattern - deepseek-v4-flash-0731 kept alongside the older deepseek-v4-flash slug ### Final Attestation - [ ] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR <!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY --> --- > [!NOTE] > **Low Risk** > Data-only cost-map updates; incorrect prices could mis-bill spend reports but there is no runtime or auth logic change. > > **Overview** > Stops Fireworks serverless models from reporting **$0 cost** by adding them to the cost map (and backup) with published rates, context windows, and capability flags. > > New aliases cover `kimi-k3` (plus fast/us), `deepseek-v4-flash-0731`, `glm-5p2-fast` (plus us), `qwen3p8-max`, `muse-glimmer-30b`, and Nemotron variants, under both short `fireworks_ai/` names and full `accounts/fireworks/models` or `routers` paths. > > <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit c15e4602e83d047dade394097f5247929d49f09e. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup> <!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY --> - [x] c15e4602e8 passes /live-pr-risk

signals.text:
## TLDR Problem this solves: - Bedrock launched Grok 4.6 but LiteLLM cannot route or price it - The bare `bedrock/global.xai.grok-4.6` slug hits Invoke, which the model rejects - The `bedrock/converse/` workaround answers but logs $0 spend How it solves it: - Adds `bedrock_mantle/xai.grok-4.6`, `us.xai.grok-4.6`, `global.xai.grok-4.6` to the cost map - The `bedrock_converse` provider routes the bare CRIS slugs to Converse - In-Region and Geo CRIS: $2.20/$6.60 per 1M tokens, $0.55 cache read - Global CRIS: $2.00/$6.00 per 1M tokens, $0.50 cache read - 500K context, reasoning, tool calling, vision, prompt caching per the model card ## User Flow Before: a developer calling Grok 4.6 on Bedrock through the proxy gets a 404 on the natural slug, and the workaround slug logs no spend 1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with `"model": "bedrock/global.xai.grok-4.6"` and a short user message 2. The call fails with 404 `BedrockException - Bedrock Invoke HTTPX: Unknown provider=None, model=global.xai.grok-4.6. Try calling via converse route - bedrock/converse/<model>` 3. They retry with `"model": "bedrock/converse/global.xai.grok-4.6"` and get 200 with the model's reply 4. https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs shows that request at $0 spend After: the same request on the natural slug succeeds and is priced 1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with `"model": "bedrock/global.xai.grok-4.6"` and a short user message 2. The call returns 200 with the model's reply 3. https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs shows the request priced at $2.00 per 1M input and $6.00 per 1M output tokens, and `bedrock/us.xai.grok-4.6` prices at $2.20/$6.60 ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5877 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [ ] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? signals.title: fix(proxy): run pre-call guardrails on batch input file uploads
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Guardrails never ran on batch input file uploads - Batch records reached providers completely unscanned - The gap was silent, nothing said a guardrail was skipped How it solves it: - Scan each JSONL record through the existing guardrail dispatch - Reject the upload when any record trips a guardrail - Skipped entirely when no pre-call guardrail is configured ## User Flow Before: a platform team with a PII guardrail turned on for every request finds that batch jobs bypass it entirely 1. They upload a batch file with POST https://litellm-domain/v1/files, `purpose=batch`, where one row's prompt contains a customer email address 2. The upload returns 200 with an id like `file-9sR7kQopg8iZ6bGpp3Yk9G` 3. They fetch https://litellm-domain/v1/files/file-9sR7kQopg8iZ6bGpp3Yk9G/content and see the email address stored verbatim at the provider 4. Nothing in the response, the headers, or the logs says a guardrail was skipped 5. Any team member with a key on that proxy can move data past the guardrail simply by putting it in a batch file instead of a chat request After: the same upload is refused, and the response names the row that tripped 1. They upload the same file with POST https://litellm-domain/v1/files, `purpose=batch` 2. The upload returns 400 saying `A guardrail changed batch input line 2 (custom_id row-2)` 3. Nothing is stored at the provider, so there is no file id to fetch 4. They remove or clean row 2, re-upload, and get a normal 200 with a file id 5. A team member can no longer move data past the guardrail by putting it in a batch file ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-2026 ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/<your_test_file>.py -v` - [x] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Shared setup. `config.yaml`: ```yaml model_list: - model_name: gpt-4o-mini litellm_params: model: openai/gpt-4o-mini api_key: os.environ/OPENAI_API_KEY guardrails: - guardrail_name: "custom-pre-guard" litellm_params: guardrail: custom_guardrail.myCustomGuardrail mode: "pre_call" default_on: true files_settings: - custom_llm_provider: openai api_key: os.environ/OPENAI_API_KEY ``` `custom_guardrail.myCustomGuardrail` is the example guardrail shipped in `litellm/proxy/example_config_yaml/custom_guardrail.py`, which masks the literal `litellm` in any message. Uploads go to the real OpenAI files API. `batch_input.jsonl` has three records, and line 2 trips the guardrail: ``` {"custom_id": "row-1", ... "content": "hello clean row"} {"custom_id": "row-2", ... "content": "this row mentions litellm and should be redacted"} {"custom_id": "row-3", ... "content": "another clean row"} ``` `clean.jsonl` holds two records the guardrail does not touch. `unreadable.jsonl` holds one record whose `url` is `/v1/rerank` and whose body carries only `model` and `documents`, so there is no message, prompt or input to scan. `risk_input.jsonl` holds one record naming its route in full, `https://api.openai.com/v1/responses`, with a Responses body carrying `input`, and one ordinary chat record. It is uploaded with `-H "x-noma-application-id: app-1"`, the header noma reads to pick its application. A probe guardrail logs the call type and the headers it was handed for each record, which is what cases 4 and 5 read. ### Before (a0f367fcd1) #### 1. clean batch file 1. `curl -sS http://localhost:4000/v1/files -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-..." -F purpose=batch -F file=@clean.jsonl` 2. `{"id":"file-8ZKvsc1GV4w62AqvHVf2dD","bytes":372,"object":"file","purpose":"batch","status":"processed"}` #### 2. batch file whose line 2 trips the guardrail 1. `curl -sS http://localhost:4000/v1/files -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-..." -F purpose=batch -F file=@batch_input.jsonl` 2. `HTTP 200` and `{"id":"file-9sR7kQopg8iZ6bGpp3Yk9G","bytes":590,"object":"file","purpose":"batch","status":"processed"}` 3. `curl -sS http://localhost:4000/v1/files/file-9sR7kQopg8iZ6bGpp3Yk9G/content -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-..."` 4. Line 2 comes back verbatim, unscanned: `{"custom_id": "row-2", ... "content": "this row mentions litellm and should be redacted"}` #### 3. record whose body has nothing a guardrail can read 1. `curl -sS http://localhost:4000/v1/files -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-..." -F purpose=batch -F file=@unreadable.jsonl` 2. `HTTP 200` and `{"id":"file-4QZuAkQgkPP465TWiHUHtP","bytes":117,"object":"file","purpose":"batch","status":"processed"}` #### 4. record naming its route in full 1. Upload `risk_input.jsonl` as above 2. No guardrail runs on the batch path at all, so neither record is scanned and no call type is resolved #### 5. guardrail that picks its policy from a request header 1. Upload `risk_input.jsonl` as above, with `-H "x-noma-application-id: app-1"` 2. No guardrail runs, so no headers reach one ### After (8b2f6d6dd0) #### 1. clean batch file 1. `curl -sS http://localhost:4000/v1/files -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-..." -F purpose=batch -F file=@clean.jsonl` 2. `{"id":"file-PGmbVim7grkmM24vYia2nr","bytes":372,"object":"file","purpose":"batch","status":"processed"}` #### 2. batch file whose line 2 trips the guardrail 1. `curl -sS http://localhost:4000/v1/files -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-..." -F purpose=batch -F file=@batch_input.jsonl` 2. `HTTP 400` and `{"error":{"message":"{'error': 'A guardrail changed batch input line 2 (custom_id row-2). Per-record redaction is not enabled, so the file was rejected rather than modified'}","code":"400"}}` 3. No file id is returned, so nothing was stored at the provider #### 3. record whose body has nothing a guardrail can read 1. `curl -sS http://localhost:4000/v1/files -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-..." -F purpose=batch -F file=@unreadable.jsonl` 2. `HTTP 400` and `{"error":{"message":"{'error': 'Batch input line 1 (custom_id u-1) targets /v1/rerank and its body has no messages, prompt or input, so guardrails cannot read it. Give the record a chat, completion, embedding, responses or messages body'}","code":"400"}}` #### 4. record naming its route in full 1. Upload `risk_input.jsonl` as above 2. `HTTP 200`, and the probe records each call type: ``` RISKPROBE call_type=aresponses headers={'host': ...} RISKPROBE call_type=acompletion headers={'host': ...} ``` 3. The Responses record scans as `aresponses`. Run against the same file at `abfb3d7ddc`, before the url was reduced to its path, it read as `aembedding`, so a guardrail scoped to chat or Responses would have skipped it while the upload was accepted #### 5. guardrail that picks its policy from a request header 1. Upload `risk_input.jsonl` as above, with `-H "x-noma-application-id: app-1"` 2. The probe is handed the sanitized headers, so a header-selected policy applies to batch records the same way it does online. At `abfb3d7ddc` the same run logged `headers=None` ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - Records are rejected, not redacted; redaction is #37561 - A guardrail that only runs post_call does not trigger scanning - Model-level guardrails still run post-routing, so batch misses them - A record whose body has no readable content is refused - Large files scan serially in windows of 32; no cap yet - One oversized JSONL line is parsed whole, as staging's validation already does Sits on top of the batch upload validation already on staging, which rejects a line that does not parse, a line that is not an object, and a line missing `custom_id`, `method`, `url` or `body`. The guardrail scan relies on all four rather than re-checking them, so case 3 above is the remaining gap it covers: validation checks that `body` is present, not that its value is an object with readable content. Only `purpose=batch` uploads are scanned, and `purpose` comes from the caller. Against OpenAI this cannot be used to skip the scan, since the provider rejects a `.jsonl` upload under `purpose=assistants` with `Invalid extension jsonl`, verified live. It is unverified for the managed files, Bedrock and Vertex paths, where LiteLLM stores the file itself and nothing revalidates `purpose` at batch creation. Worth closing on those paths as follow-up work. ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR <!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY --> --- > [!NOTE] > **Medium Risk** > Touches proxy guardrail dispatch and `/v1/files` batch uploads, so a scan bug could reject valid jobs or still miss content. Behavior is reject-only and skipped when no pre-call guardrails are configured. > > **Overview** > Closes a silent bypass where `purpose=batch` file uploads skipped pre-call guardrails entirely. > > When pre-call guardrails (or pipelines) are configured, each JSONL record is scanned through `pre_call_hook` with a new `guardrails_only` path so rate limits, budgets, prompt templates, and hanging-request alerts do not fire per row. Records are scanned in windows of 32; the file is rewound and never rewritten. A blocking guardrail exception is re-raised as-is; redaction or an unreadable body (no messages/prompt/input) returns 400 naming the line/`custom_id`. Call type comes from the record URL (including absolute URLs) with body-shape fallback. > > Request metadata is narrowed to what guardrails actually read (headers, tags, guardrail config) so OTel spans and secrets are not copied per record. Scanning is skipped when no pre-call guardrail would run. > > <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit d2d124e71cac0f2b7ea7dc1fd2ebcc00f5e58ff2. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup> <!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

signals.title: feat(complexity_router): add business classification rubric preset
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Built-in rubrics only cover chat and agentic coding traffic - Business/sales prompts over-route with engineering-flavored tier criteria How it solves it: - Adds a `business` classification rubric preset to the dropdown - The preset swaps in business tier definitions and business calibration examples - Keeps the same four tiers, so escalation and tier renames still work ## User Flow Before: an admin routing sales and support traffic has no business preset, so routine drafting over-routes to expensive tiers 1. They open http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=llm-playground, Add Model, Auto Router tab, and expand Complexity Router settings 2. The Classification Rubric dropdown offers only Legacy, Chat, and Agentic 3. They pick Chat, save, and send POST http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions with "draft a cold outreach email for a VP of Engineering at a fintech" 4. The classifier routes it to the COMPLEX tier model, and http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=logs shows the expensive deployment served it After: the same admin picks the Business preset and routine business drafting stays on the mid tier 1. They open the same Auto Router form and expand Complexity Router settings 2. The Classification Rubric dropdown now also offers Business, described as suited to sales, support, and go-to-market traffic 3. They pick Business, save, and send the same POST http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions with the same outreach-email prompt 4. The classifier routes it to the MEDIUM tier model, and http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=logs shows the cheaper deployment served it ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [ ] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix QA steps against a live proxy (`python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config litellm/proxy/dev_config.yaml --detailed_debug --reload --use_v2_migration_resolver` plus `npm run dev` in `ui/litellm-dashboard`): 1. Open http://localhost:3000, Add Model, Auto Router tab, pick Complexity Router and the LLM classifier 2. Confirm the Classification Rubric dropdown shows Business with the business/sales description, and that the info tooltip says Business also rewrites the tier definitions 3. Select Business and save; confirm the stored router shows `classification_rubric: "business"` in its config 4. POST http://localhost:4000/auto_router/test_routing with "draft a cold outreach email for a VP of Engineering at a fintech" and expect the MEDIUM tier; repeat with "do we discount to close this quarter or hold price and risk slipping? commit to a recommendation" and expect REASONING Offline evidence: on a 136-case hand-labeled business corpus (2 runs, claude-haiku-4-5 classifier, anchor-lookalike cases excluded), this preset scores 87.3% accuracy with 9.4% over-routing versus 81.6% and 13.1% for legacy, and 77.0%/73.4% accuracy for chat/agentic on the same corpus ## Type 🆕 New Feature ## Caveats (if any) - Corpus labels are hand-authored; shadow eval recommended before defaulting anyone to it - Business is the only preset that swaps tier criteria; legacy, chat, and agentic prompts are byte-identical to before ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/c9cfad97660c420a8f7090a7685fac0f <!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY --> --- > [!NOTE] > <sup>[Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) is generating a summary for commit 7c6dc20021e7806796d89de6c1410639eba9dba6. signals.title: fix(proxy): guarantee max_parallel_requests slot release when stream logging fails and make slot TTL configurable
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Streaming logging failures leaked max_parallel_requests slots for 1 hour - Keys hit false 429s at 1-5 actual in-flight requests - Leaked slots could not self-heal faster than the fixed 3600s TTL How it solves it: - Cost calc, payload build, and logging hooks no longer abort success callbacks - The slot-releasing limiter callback now always runs after a stream ends - New env var LITELLM_PARALLEL_REQUEST_SLOT_TTL_SECONDS tunes stale-slot pruning ## User Flow Before: during a provider incident, a user's key locks out with false 429s for an hour 1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with `"stream": true` on a key with `max_parallel_requests: 50` 2. The provider errors mid-stream or a logging callback raises while the stream is finalized; the response ends but the concurrency slot stays occupied 3. After a burst of such failures, new requests on that key return 429 `ProxyRateLimitError: max_parallel_requests ... Remaining: 0` even though only 1-5 requests are actually in flight 4. The key stays locked for about 60 minutes until the 3600 second slot TTL prunes the leaked slots After: the same failures release their slots immediately, and the TTL safety net is tunable 1. They send the same POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with `"stream": true` 2. The provider errors mid-stream or a logging callback raises; the slot is still released when the stream ends 3. Follow-up requests on the key succeed; `Remaining` reflects real in-flight concurrency 4. As defense in depth, the admin can set `LITELLM_PARALLEL_REQUEST_SLOT_TTL_SECONDS=300` so any slot leaked by a crashed worker self-heals in minutes instead of an hour ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [ ] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Live proxy QA run is in progress; this section will be updated with the before/after curl runs against a local proxy hitting a real provider ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - TTL constant is read once at import time, not hot-reloadable ### Final Attestation - [ ] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/3077f9f9416344eab7b8e3964f6c505d

signals.title: fix(pricing): add Bedrock batch rates for Qwen and Claude 4.5
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Bedrock batch rates are missing for three supported models - Cross-region Claude 4.5 profiles also lack explicit rates How it solves it: - Adds AWS's 50% batch rates to both pricing maps - Covers Qwen 3 235B, Haiku 4.5, and Sonnet 4.5 - Tests base and commercial cross-region model entries ## User Flow Before: Bedrock batch pricing for these models relies on a generic fallback 1. A developer submits a Bedrock batch using one of these model IDs 2. LiteLLM resolves the matching model pricing metadata 3. signals.title: fix(vertex_ai): only fall back to a placeholder thought signature on the first parallel function call
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Gemini signs only the first parallel function call - LiteLLM fabricates a skip-validation placeholder on every sibling call - Replayed history no longer matches what Gemini emitted Google [documents both halves of this](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/models/thinking/thought-signatures#parallel_function_calling_example). On the expected shape: "In cases of parallel function calls in a single response, only the first functionCall part will contain the thought_signature." On the placeholder: "You can set thought_signature to skip_thought_signature_validator, but, this should be a last resort as it will negatively impact model performance." Fabricating one per sibling call is the opposite of a last resort, and it costs quality on every parallel tool-calling turn That cost is measurable, not theoretical. Internal testing at Google found that setting `skip_thought_signature_validator` on parallel function calls causes gemini-3.5 to return empty text responses. Following the documented shape, one real signature on the first call and nothing on the siblings, reduced the error rate How it solves it: - Placeholder fallback now applies to the first function call only - Unsigned sibling calls are replayed with no signature - Real signatures on any call are still preserved ## User Flow Before: a developer using parallel tool calling against a Gemini 3 model gets their conversation replayed with signatures the model never produced 1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with a `get_weather` tool and ask for Paris, London and Tokyo in parallel 2. Three tool calls come back; only the first id carries a `__thought__` suffix, the other two are bare 3. They append the assistant turn plus three tool results and send the same POST again 4. The turn is replayed upstream with the real signature on Paris and a `skip_thought_signature_validator` placeholder attached to London and Tokyo, so two of the three calls claim a signature the model never returned After: the same replay carries exactly the signatures the model produced 1. They send the same POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with the same tool and prompt 2. Three tool calls come back; only the first id carries a `__thought__` suffix, the other two are bare 3. They append the assistant turn plus three tool results and send the same POST again 4. The turn is replayed upstream with the real signature on Paris and nothing on London or Tokyo, matching the original response, and the answer comes back covering all three cities ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5888 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix E2e against real Vertex AI (`gemini-3.7-flash`, `vertex_location: global`). The observable that matters here is the exact payload Vertex receives on the replay turn, so the deployment's `api_base` points at a local recording relay that logs every request body and forwards it unchanged to the real `https://aiplatform.googleapis.com`. Proxy config: ```yaml model_list: - model_name: vertex_ai/gemini-3.7-flash litellm_params: model: vertex_ai/gemini-3.7-flash vertex_project: <project> vertex_location: global api_base: http://127.0.0.1:<relay port> general_settings: master_key: sk-1234 ``` Both legs run the same two turns against their own proxy, booted from the commit under test: ``` # Turn 1: three cities, one get_weather tool, parallel calls requested curl -sS "http://127.0.0.1:<proxy port>/v1/chat/completions" \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-1234' \ -d '{"model":"vertex_ai/gemini-3.7-flash","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"What is the weather in Paris, London and Tokyo? Call the get_weather tool once per city, all three in parallel."}],"tools":[{"type":"function","function":{"name":"get_weather","description":"get weather for a city","parameters":{"type":"object","properties":{"city":{"type":"string"}},"required":["city"]}}}]}' # Turn 2: turn 1's user message + the assistant tool_calls message + three {"role":"tool","tool_call_id":...,"content":"20C"} results curl -sS "http://127.0.0.1:<proxy port>/v1/chat/completions" \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-1234' \ -d @turn2_payload.json ``` ### Before (da7a10ebbdb16b34413566b0c980dac27af1de5b, the merge base) Turn 1 returns three parallel tool calls, a signature only on the first id: ``` {"city": "Paris"} id=call_2117163__thought__AY89a18pdiowbEw4FF1FoNDFGqoXixvwugvVO... {"city": "London"} id=call_2117164 {"city": "Tokyo"} id=call_2117165 ``` Turn 2 answers normally (200, `finish_reason: stop`): "The current weather in Paris, London, and Tokyo is: Paris 20°C, London 20°C, Tokyo 20°C". The model parts of that request as the relay recorded them on their way to Vertex: ``` get_weather({"city":"Paris"}) thoughtSignature=AY89a18pdiowbEw4FF1FoNDFGqoXixvwugvVOvu4gYXn... (the model's real signature, 468 chars) get_weather({"city":"London"}) thoughtSignature=c2tpcF90aG91Z2h0X3NpZ25hdHVyZV92YWxpZGF0b3I= (fabricated placeholder) get_weather({"city":"Tokyo"}) thoughtSignature=c2tpcF90aG91Z2h0X3NpZ25hdHVyZV92YWxpZGF0b3I= (fabricated placeholder) ``` `c2tpcF90aG91Z2h0X3NpZ25hdHVyZV92YWxpZGF0b3I=` is base64 for `skip_thought_signature_validator`: London and Tokyo were sent claiming a signature the model never produced ### After (a5ad22b8a3f734b09ce5e05a68dab5c5205907a4, the PR tip) Turn 1 returns three parallel tool calls, same shape as before, a signature only on the first id: ``` {"city": "Paris"} id=call_2351596__thought__AY89a1/YoawiNHzbcgAo4j41xnvh25ItNyHlm... {"city": "London"} id=call_2351597 {"city": "Tokyo"} id=call_2351598 ``` Turn 2 answers normally (200, `finish_reason: stop`): ``` The weather in Paris, London, and Tokyo is currently: * **Paris:** 20°C * **London:** 20°C * **Tokyo:** 20°C ``` The model parts of that request as the relay recorded them on their way to Vertex: ``` get_weather({"city":"Paris"}) thoughtSignature=AY89a1/YoawiNHzbcgAo4j41xnvh25ItNyHlmafAJ8Ln... (the model's real signature, 452 chars) get_weather({"city":"London"}) no thoughtSignature field get_weather({"city":"Tokyo"}) no thoughtSignature field ``` Paris keeps its real signature and the two unsigned siblings are replayed bare, matching what Gemini returned. No placeholder anywhere in the request Notes from the runs, both pre-existing behavior this PR leaves alone: - Real signature also rides inside the first tool_call id - Model parts serialize snake_case (`function_call`); Vertex accepts them ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - Placeholder still applies when the whole turn is unsigned, since Vertex returns a 400 on a turn with no signature anywhere. That keeps history migrated off pre-gemini-3 models working - The gemini-3 gate on the placeholder is pre-existing behavior from #16812 and is unchanged here, only narrowed to the first call - Through the proxy, a signature replayed inside a tool call id does not reach this code, so `provider_specific_fields.thought_signature` is the carrier that works there. Pre-existing and unchanged by this PR: the first call still gets a placeholder and the siblings go bare, which Vertex accepts ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR - [x] a5ad22b8a3f734b09ce5e05a68dab5c5205907a4 passes /live-pr-risk

signals.title: feat(shadow_eval)!: gate the per-key budget on dollar spend instead of turns
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Shadow eval budgets are turn counts, but the thing operators care about is dollars - A turn's cost varies wildly by model and prompt, so max_turns bounds spend only loosely - The job's own judge_spend read $0.00 whenever name-based pricing missed How it solves it: - start_shadow_eval takes `max_budget` (USD per key) instead of `max_turns` - Each attempt records the shadow arm's and judge's billed cost on its row - Sampler, sweep, stop guard, and derived status all gate on recorded spend - Costs come from the billed `response_cost` figure, so deployment pricing is respected - Billed cost is recorded on every exit, even empty replies and pipeline errors - Admission re-checks the proxy's cross-pod spend counter, the same owner key budgets use - A request still sending max_turns gets a 422 naming the replacement - A 10,000-sample internal valve terminates zero-cost error loops - Pre-migration jobs keep their configured turn budget (max_budget stays NULL) ## User Flow Before: an operator wants to cap a shadow eval's own overhead at a dollar amount, and there is no way to say that 1. They send POST http://localhost:4000/auto_router/shadow_eval/start with `{"router_name": "my-router", "api_key_ids": ["<hash>"], "judge_model": "judge", "shadow_percentage": 100, "max_budget": 0.01}` 2. The job is created anyway: the `max_budget` field is silently ignored and the response shows only `"max_turns": 200` 3. Their key's traffic gets sampled until 200 turns are judged, whatever that costs; the detail response shows `"judge_spend": 0.0` even though the spend logs bill real dollars for every judge call After: the same request caps the eval at one cent per key 1. They send the same POST http://localhost:4000/auto_router/shadow_eval/start with `"max_budget": 0.01` 2. The response shows `"max_budget": 0.01` on their key, and sampling stops as soon as the key's recorded shadow plus judge spend reaches it, checked against a cross-pod counter 3. The detail response shows real dollar figures per key, `"spend": 0.012327, "status": "completed"`, matching what was billed ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more - [x] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Rig: local proxy from this branch on :4321 with real Postgres (all migrations plus this PR's). Every deployment (`cheap`/`strong`/`judge`, plus auto-router `my-router`) points at claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 through the litellm sandbox gateway, so every shadow and judge call is a real provider call priced by the real cost map and costing real money. No stubs and no mock responses anywhere in this run ### Before (3f2e0badb4) #### A dollar budget cannot be expressed and judge_spend lies 1. `curl -s http://127.0.0.1:4321/auto_router/shadow_eval/start -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -d '{"router_name": "my-router", "api_key_ids": ["<hash>"], "judge_model": "judge", "shadow_percentage": 100, "max_turns": 2, "max_budget": 0.001}'` creates the job; `max_budget` is silently ignored, the response carries only `"max_turns": 2` 2. 3 real chat turns through the shadowed key (`{"model": "cheap", "max_tokens": 30, "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "real before turn N: name one prime number"}]}`) 3. Detail reads `"attempt_count": 2, "judge_spend": 0.0, "status": "completed"`: the turn count gated it, and judge_spend reads zero because name-based pricing missed for the `openai/`-prefixed deployment 4. Meanwhile `LiteLLM_SpendLogs` shows the judge legs billing real money: 2 rows tagged `shadow_eval_judge` totaling $0.001160, uncappable by any knob ### After (f5d959a849; behavior captured at c0334292aa, since unchanged on these paths) #### The dollar budget bounds the job with real per-attempt costs 1. `curl -s http://127.0.0.1:4321/auto_router/shadow_eval/start -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -d '{"router_name": "my-router", "api_key_ids": ["<hash>"], "judge_model": "judge", "shadow_percentage": 100, "max_budget": 0.01}'` returns `"max_budget": 0.01, "max_turns": 10000, "status": "running"` 2. 8 real chat turns through the shadowed key (`{"model": "cheap", "max_tokens": 500, "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "real after turn N: write a 250 word overview of a different chemical element"}]}`) 3. Exactly 4 are sampled and the detail reads `"attempt_count": 4, "spend": 0.012327, "judge_spend": 0.005002, "status": "completed"`: sampling stopped the moment recorded spend crossed the cap, with the 10,000 turn valve untouched 4. `SELECT outcome, shadow_cost, judge_cost FROM "LiteLLM_ShadowEvalAttempt" ...` shows every row carrying real billed costs: shadow $0.001785 to $0.001870, judge $0.001232 to $0.001266 5. `curl -s -X POST .../auto_router/shadow_eval/<job>/stop` answers 400 `"Job <job> is already completed"` #### A caller still sending the retired max_turns is told, not silently defaulted 1. `curl -s http://127.0.0.1:4321/auto_router/shadow_eval/start ... -d '{"router_name": "my-router", "api_key_ids": ["<hash>"], "judge_model": "judge", "shadow_percentage": 100, "max_turns": 200}'` 2. Answers 422 with `"max_turns was replaced by max_budget, the per-key USD cap on the eval's own spend"` #### A pre-migration job keeps its turn budget 1. Create a job, then reshape its row into the legacy form with psql: `UPDATE "LiteLLM_ShadowEvalJob" SET max_budget = NULL, max_turns = 2 WHERE group_id = '<job>'` 2. 3 real chat turns through the shadowed key 3. Detail reads `"attempt_count": 2, "max_budget": null, "spend": 0.00114, "status": "completed"`: the turn budget gated it, the recorded spend is display only ## Type 🆕 New Feature ## Caveats (if any) - Breaking: start_shadow_eval replaces `max_turns` with `max_budget` - Overshoot is bounded by samples already in flight when the cap is crossed - During a rolling deploy old pods gate new jobs by the valve only - Attempt rows written by old pods mid-deploy price as judge-only - Rebased over merged #37389; its per-key Budget used column now shows dollars ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR <!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY --> --- > [!NOTE] > **Medium Risk** > Breaking API change plus new spend-budget gating that writes Redis spend counters and attempt costs. Mispricing or counter failure can overshoot or skip samples, but it reuses existing budget primitives and fail-closed reads. > > **Overview** > **Breaking:** starting a shadow eval now takes per-key `max_budget` (USD, default $10) instead of `max_turns`. Callers still sending `max_turns` get a 422. New jobs write a 10k-turn valve only to stop zero-cost error loops; pre-migration jobs keep `max_budget` null and stay turn-gated. > > Each attempt now stores `shadow_cost` plus `judge_cost`, priced from the billed `response_cost` stamp (price-map fallback). Sampling, sweep, stop, and derived status all complete a key when recorded spend hits the cap. Admission re-checks the shared `spend:shadow_eval:{job_id}` counter so pods stop before the next provider call; unverifiable spend skips the sample. > > The dashboard start form and per-key “budget used” column show dollars (`$spend / $max_budget`), with a turns fallback for legacy jobs. > > <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit f5d959a849753c1b132e63268de1684ceda025f3. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup> <!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
