signals.title: fix(ptu): hand the prune a plain delete filter the query builder can serialise
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - The nightly PTU job raises once a config deployment is priced - Its delete predicate is a read-only mapping the query builder rejects - Charges land first, so the run looks like it produced rows How it solves it: - The predicate is built as a plain dict - A test asserts that, since the in-memory fake accepts any mapping - The catch-up pass gains a config-declared reservation case ## User Flow Before: an admin who turns on PTU attribution with a deployment in `config.yaml` sees the day's costs appear and everything after it stop 1. The admin runs a proxy with `LITELLM_ENABLE_PTU_COST_ATTRIBUTION=True` and a provisioned-throughput deployment declared in `config.yaml` 2. The nightly job runs at 00:15 UTC and writes the team's reserved-capacity cost 3. It then raises, so the run never finishes 4. https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=usage shows the day's cost, which makes the run look successful 5. The lapsed-window alert never fires and the catch-up pass never runs, so a reservation whose window closed goes unannounced and earlier unpriced days are never filled in After: the same job finishes 1. The admin runs the same proxy 2. The nightly job runs and writes the same cost 3. It completes, sweeping the rows it can account for 4. https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=usage shows the same figure 5. The lapsed-window alert and the catch-up pass both run ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Refs LIT-5809 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Real Postgres, the real scheduled entry point, one config-declared PTU deployment at 100 units and $0.02 an hour. Both sides run the same three lines against the same database, and the exit code is checked rather than the output skimmed, which is how the defect reached staging in the first place. ```python proxy_server.llm_router = Router(model_list=yaml.safe_load(open("ptu.yaml"))["model_list"]) await run_scheduled_ptu_rollup(prisma, pod_lock_manager=, target_date=date(2026, 8, 18)) await prisma.db.litellm_dailyteamspend.find_many(where={"api_key": "__ptu_flat_cost__"}) ``` ### Before (c2b3c4b1e4) 1. Run it ``` exit=1 TypeError: Type not serializable ``` 2. Read the table back ``` 1 sentinel row(s) written before it died ``` The charge is there, which is what makes the failure easy to miss: the upserts precede the sweep, so the usage view fills in and the run dies afterwards ### After (db015e9c8b) 1. Run it ``` exit=0 rollup: RollupResult(day=2026-08-18, models_processed=1, rows_written=1, rows_failed=0, lapsed=()) flat-cost rows: [('ptu-team-0001', 'gpt-4o-ptu', 48.0)] ``` 2. Read the table back ``` tracebacks: 0 ``` The run completes, so the lapsed-window alert and the catch-up pass that follow it both get to run ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Changes `_prune_unrefreshed_sentinel_rows` built its bounded predicate with `MappingProxyType`, and `prisma/builder.py` refuses to serialise a `mappingproxy`. A predicate builder now returns a plain dict for both the bounded and unbounded sweeps. The unit suite could not catch this: its in-memory table accepts any mapping, so the delete looked fine. The new test asserts the predicate's concrete type, and a second one drives the catch-up pass over a config-declared reservation, which is the path the crash was blocking. ## QA runbook ## Caveats (if any) - The annotation says Mapping; the test is what pins the concrete dict ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR --- --- > [!NOTE] > [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) is generating a summary for commit db015e9c8bf2942d9455fda5e83100a83e97ba76. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).

signals.title: fix(batches): decode model-encoded output file id so completed batches book spend
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Completed batches retrieved by encoded id never wrote spend rows - Batches e2e skipped terminal state, failure paths, content downloads - Two-proxy batch routing (LIT-5347) had no e2e coverage How it solves it: - Decode the encoded output file id before fetching results - Cross-run marker baton e2e proves completion + cost write-back - New e2e: failure paths, foreign ids, second hop, content downloads ## User Flow Before: a developer runs a nightly OpenAI batch through the gateway; it completes and the results download fine, but the gateway never bills it, so their spend dashboard undercounts 1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/files?model=my-batch-model with a one-line JSONL file and get back a long scrambled id starting `file-` 2. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/batches with `{"input_file_id": "<that id>"}` and get a 200 with a scrambled batch id starting `batch_` in status `validating` 3. A minute later they send GET https://litellm-domain/v1/batches/{batch_id} and see `"status": "completed"` with an `output_file_id` 4. GET https://litellm-domain/v1/files/{output_file_id}/content returns 200 with their model responses 5. They check GET https://litellm-domain/spend/logs?request_id={batch_id}_batch_cost (or https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs) and get `[]`: the completed batch never shows up as spend After: the same nightly batch now books its real cost right after the status check 1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/files?model=my-batch-model with a one-line JSONL file and get back a long scrambled id starting `file-` 2. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/batches with `{"input_file_id": "<that id>"}` and get a 200 with a scrambled batch id starting `batch_` in status `validating` 3. A minute later they send GET https://litellm-domain/v1/batches/{batch_id} and see `"status": "completed"` with an `output_file_id` 4. GET https://litellm-domain/v1/files/{output_file_id}/content returns 200 with their model responses 5. The same GET https://litellm-domain/spend/logs?request_id={batch_id}_batch_cost now returns one row with positive spend and the batch's real token counts ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5730 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/<your_test_file>.py -v`. signals.title: chore(ui): drop the antd dependency and its leftovers
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Nothing renders antd, yet it still ships to users - A global antd StyleProvider wraps every page - A z-index hack lifts popups over antd modals - 15 test files mock a module nothing imports How it solves it: - Drops `antd` and `@ant-design/cssinjs` from package.json - Deletes the StyleProvider, cascade layer and z-index hack - Removes the inert `vi.mock("antd")` factories - Renames the shims that outlived the library ## User Flow Before: an admin loading the dashboard downloads and parses a UI library that no longer draws a single control 1. They open https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=api-keys with a cold cache 2. The page pulls the antd style engine alongside the shadcn bundle, though no component uses it since #37569 3. Every dialog they open runs through a global style provider that has nothing left to style 4. Nothing on screen comes from that library, so the download bought them nothing After: the same page ships only the kit it actually renders 1. They open https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=api-keys with a cold cache 2. Only the shadcn bundle loads 3. Every page, dialog and dropdown looks and behaves exactly as before 4. The stacking hack that lifted dropdowns over antd modals is gone, and dropdowns still open above their dialogs ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [ ] I have added meaningful tests (dependency removal only; the existing dashboard unit tests cover the touched components) - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Shared setup: one worktree per side, `cd ui/litellm-dashboard && npm ci && npm run build`, the build copied into `litellm/proxy/_experimental/out`, and a live proxy per side (`python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config litellm/proxy/dev_config.yaml --port <port> --use_v2_migration_resolver`, fresh Postgres DB each) so the browser loads the UI exactly as an admin would at http://localhost:PORT/ui/. Browser steps executed in a real Chromium driven by Playwright against those live proxies, logged in as admin ### Before (0b374541bb) #### antd presence in node_modules and the served bundle 1. `npm ls antd @ant-design/cssinjs` ``` ├── @ant-design/cssinjs@1.24.0 └─┬ antd@5.29.3 ├─┬ @ant-design/cssinjs-utils@1.1.3 │ └── @ant-design/cssinjs@1.24.0 deduped └── @ant-design/cssinjs@1.24.0 deduped ``` 2. `npm run build` completes, then `find out/_next/static -name '*.js' | xargs cat | wc -c` gives 10522409 bytes and `grep -rl cssinjs out/_next/static` hits one served chunk, `_next/static/chunks/0i9exd9dj3-75.js`: the style engine still ships to every visitor #### Dashboard pages and the create-key dialog still render 1. `GET http://localhost:53817/ui/` returns 200; after logging in, `?page=api-keys`, `?page=teams`, `?page=new_model`, `?page=mcp-servers`, and `?page=guardrails` all render the full dashboard with zero browser console errors and zero page errors 2. On `?page=api-keys`, Create New Key opens, and clicking the Models field pops a 10-option dropdown; `document.elementFromPoint` at the first option's center hits that option (`hitInsideOption: true`, `hitInsideDialogOverlay: false`), so the dropdown paints above the dialog, and clicking it selects the model ### After (552884d03c) #### antd presence in node_modules and the served bundle 1. `npm ls antd @ant-design/cssinjs` ``` litellm-dashboard@0.1.0 └── (empty) ``` 2. `npm run build` completes, then the same byte count gives 10510152 bytes and `grep -rl cssinjs out/_next/static` (plus `ant-design`, `data-ant`, and bare `antd`) hits zero files: nothing antd-flavored ships anymore #### Dashboard pages and the create-key dialog still render 1. `GET http://localhost:54293/ui/` returns 200; the same five pages render identically with zero browser console errors and zero page errors 2. The same Create New Key flow gives the same 10-option Models dropdown with the identical stacking probe result (`hitInsideOption: true`, `hitInsideDialogOverlay: false`) and the same successful selection, with the z-index override gone QA observations: - antd component code already left the bundle in #37569 - Only the cssinjs style engine still shipped; this PR removes it - node_modules sheds antd's 58M of install weight - Fresh empty DBs needed prisma db push despite --use_v2_migration_resolver; both legs, PR leaves it alone ## Type 🧹 Refactoring ## Caveats (if any) - Comments still name antd where it explains a contract - `tests/proxy_admin_ui_tests/ui_unit_tests` still declares antd - That directory is dead: no CI job runs it ### Final Attestation - [ ] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR - [x] 552884d03c passes /live-pr-risk

signals.title: refactor(ui): map hardcoded Tailwind palette classes onto semantic tokens
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Dashboard colors are hardcoded palette classes, not tokens - The `.dark` block exists but can never take effect - Sidebar reads as a card floating on near-black How it solves it: - Codemod rewrites 3,232 palette utilities onto semantic tokens - Neutrals, red, green, amber, blue collapse into token families - Retunes the dark ramp neutral, with the sidebar recessed ## User Flow Before: a proxy admin who prefers dark interfaces has no way to get one, and would see a broken page even if they forced it 1. They open https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=api-keys and get the light dashboard 2. There is no theme control anywhere on the page 3. If they force the page into dark from browser devtools, most of the screen stays light: key names, table borders, filter chips and status badges keep their fixed light-mode colors After: the same forced-dark page renders as a coherent dark interface, so a theme control can be added on top of it 1. They open https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=api-keys and get the same light dashboard, pixel for pixel 2. There is still no theme control, so nothing changes for anyone who does not go looking 3. If they force the page into dark from devtools, the whole page follows: canvas, sidebar, table rows, dividers, badges and muted text all shift together ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [ ] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally - [x] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix ### Before (7b574b9df6) #### Light mode, unchanged baseline 1. Open http://localhost:3000/?page=api-keys and screenshot the Virtual Keys table #### Dark mode forced from devtools 1. In devtools, select the `<html>` element and add `class="dark"` 2. Screenshot: the sidebar goes dark but the table body, key names, filter chips and status badges stay light ### After (922f0654b5) #### Light mode, unchanged baseline 1. Open http://localhost:3000/?page=api-keys and screenshot the same table 2. It should be indistinguishable from the Before shot #### Dark mode forced from devtools 1. In devtools, select the `<html>` element and add `class="dark"` 2. Screenshot: canvas `#212121`, sidebar `#131313`, row dividers `#303030`, all text and badges legible ## Type 🧹 Refactoring ## Caveats (if any) - No new tests: mechanical rewrite, 12 touched suites pass - An eslint rule banning new palette classes is worth adding - No theme toggle yet; dark mode stays inert until one lands - 210 palette utilities left by hand: purple, indigo, gradients - ~250 hardcoded hex values in inline styles untouched - Playground code blocks still use a light-only Prism theme - `@tailwindcss/forms` still paints bare inputs white - Semantic colors keep shadcn's saturation, brighter than the neutrals ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

They open http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=mcp-servers and click the Connect tab 2. They point at the "OpenAI platform" link; the text visibly lightens, so the link reads as clickable 3. They point at the date range control on http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=usage; its border deepens 4. They switch the browser to dark mode; the "OpenAI Responses API Integration" banner is now a dark blue tint that sits on the page instead of glaring off it 5. They open the policies page and start a new policy; the selected mode card picks up the dark theme's accent instead of the pale indigo fill ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more - [x] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Setup: run the dashboard dev server against a local proxy so the screens below render live ``` python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config litellm/proxy/dev_config.yaml --detailed_debug --reload --use_v2_migration_resolver 2>&1 | tee litellm.log ``` ``` cd ui/litellm-dashboard && npm run dev ``` Dark mode has no in-app toggle yet, so switch it on from the browser console on each page: ``` document.documentElement.classList.add('dark') ``` ### Before (47a7e1742e88ff9dcd213518ddbca208ed8bbaee) #### Hover feedback 1. Open http://localhost:3000/mcp-servers/ and click the Connect tab, OpenAI API sub-tab 2. Hover the "OpenAI platform" link under API Key Setup; capture the link, which does not change 3. Open http://localhost:3000/usage/ and hover the date range button at the top right; capture the button, whose border does not change #### Dark mode 1. Open http://localhost:3000/mcp-servers/, click the Connect tab, turn dark mode on with the console line above 2. Open http://localhost:3000/policies/, click Add New Policy, turn dark mode on, and capture the mode picker: the selected card is pale indigo ### After (e96074f93c4538ebba80353302be3a03d47b597b) #### Hover feedback 1. signals.title: fix(ui): keep semantic button colours on hover after the no-op hover cleanup
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Three buttons lose their colour when you point at them - The ghost and outline variants override them with plain foreground - Nothing caught it, so the affordance reads as broken How it solves it: - Each button pins its own hover colour again - The value is an alpha step, so it stays visible - Three tests fail if the class disappears again ## User Flow Before: an admin pointing at a red, amber, or tinted button watches it turn plain grey, so the colour that told them what the button does is gone exactly when they are about to click it 1. They open http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=teams, open a team, and go to the Logging tab 2. signals.title: perf(ui): run the vitest tiers on the threads pool
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - UI unit tests burn 86s of CI wall clock per run - The forks pool spawns a child process per test file How it solves it: - Run the vitest tiers on worker threads instead - Roughly 20% faster on identical hardware and test set - Pool lives in config, so local runs match CI ## User Flow This PR changes no runtime behaviour, so there is no end user flow to walk through. It only changes which vitest pool the dashboard's test tiers run in. No application code, no API surface, no UI, and no shipped artifact is touched. The two changed files are the vitest config and the workflow that invokes it. ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [ ] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more - [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Both sides run the whole dashboard suite on the same machine (18 cores, node 24.19.0) from `ui/litellm-dashboard`, each twice, timed end to end. The only difference is the pool, which is exactly what the workflow line changes. ### Before (5290150a05) 1. `time CI=true npx vitest run --pool forks --poolOptions.forks.maxForks=14` ``` run 1: wall=86s Test Files 743 passed (743) Tests 8591 passed (8591) run 2: wall=86s Test Files 743 passed (743) Tests 8591 passed (8591) ``` ### After (1d010d5f54) Timed at 1d55ef8684. `git diff --name-only 1d55ef8684 1d010d5f54 -- ui/ .github/workflows/` is empty, so the vitest config and the workflow command are identical at this tip; the later commit only retargets a Python test's expected argv. 1. `time CI=true npx vitest run --poolOptions.threads.maxThreads=14` ``` run 1: wall=64s Test Files 743 passed (743) Tests 8591 passed (8591) run 2: wall=68s Test Files 743 passed (743) Tests 8591 passed (8591) ``` Same 743 files and 8,591 tests pass on both pools, so the suite covers the same ground either way. To confirm the config setting is what takes effect, and is still overridable, a scratch test in each tier reported `require("node:worker_threads").isMainThread`: ``` npx vitest run src/__pooltmp__ POOLCHECK unit isMainThread=false POOLCHECK component isMainThread=false npx vitest run src/__pooltmp__ --pool forks POOLCHECK unit isMainThread=true POOLCHECK component isMainThread=true ``` ## Type 🚄 Infrastructure ## Caveats (if any) - Retargets the UI scope canary's pinned argv - Threads share one process, so a native crash takes the run down - Worker count stays pinned at 14 for the 16-core runner ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signals.title: chore(ci): close the test-census blind spots and move scripts out of workflows/
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Two test files ran nowhere and the census could not see it - A `grep -v` hid them from `assert_ci_coverage.py` - `tests/scim_tests/` held a fixture and no tests - Two plain scripts were sitting in `.github/workflows/` - The agent-shin rollout heads-up one-shot is long spent How it solves it: - CircleCI glob excludes the local-only dir structurally - Those files get an allowlist entry with a dated rationale - Scripts move to `.github/scripts/`, callers updated - Spent heads-up workflow, script and tests deleted ## User Flow Before: a maintainer auditing which tests actually run gets a clean bill of health that is wrong 1. They run `python .github/scripts/assert_ci_coverage.py` and read `OK: 2422 test files ... are each invoked by at least one job` 2. They believe every test file has a runner 3. In fact `tests/agent_tests/local_only_agent_tests/test_a2a.py` and `test_a2a_completion_bridge.py` execute in no job at all, because the CircleCI agent job pipes its glob through `grep -v "^tests/agent_tests/local_only_agent_tests/"` and the census reads only the glob 4. Nothing anywhere records that those two files are deliberately out of scope After: the same audit reports the same clean bill of health, and this time it is true 1. They run `python .github/scripts/assert_ci_coverage.py` and read `OK: 2421 test files ... are each invoked by at least one job or carry an explicit allowlist entry` 2. They open `.github/ci-coverage-allowlist.yml` and find `tests/agent_tests/local_only_agent_tests` listed with the reason it cannot run in a pull request job, the date the hidden filter was removed, and the condition for revisiting 3. If someone later drops a third test file into that directory, the census still passes, because the entry is the directory 4. If someone instead deletes the allowlist entry, the census fails and names both files ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/<your_test_file>.py -v` - [x] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix The change this PR makes to the census is mechanical, so the proof is the guard itself going from a false pass, to a true failure, to a true pass. All three runs are the same command on the same machine. ### Before (5290150a05) #### The census passes while two files run nowhere 1. Command: ``` python .github/scripts/assert_ci_coverage.py ``` 2. Output: ``` OK: 2422 test files and 10 Dockerfiles are each invoked by at least one job or carry an explicit allowlist entry. ``` 3. The two files it silently counted as covered: ``` $ sed -n '1028p' .circleci/config.yml TEST_FILES=$(circleci tests glob "tests/agent_tests/**/test_*.py" | grep -v "^tests/agent_tests/local_only_agent_tests/") ``` The glob matches them, the `grep -v` drops them before pytest ever sees them, and the census parses only the glob. ### After (03b74381b3) #### The census fails once the filter is structural, and names the files 1. With the glob narrowed to `tests/agent_tests/test_*.py` and no allowlist entry yet: ``` python .github/scripts/assert_ci_coverage.py ``` 2. Output: ``` ERROR: test files that no CI job invokes - tests/agent_tests/local_only_agent_tests: 2 test file(s) invoked by no job: test_a2a.py, test_a2a_completion_bridge.py Add each to a job's test path, or list it in .github/ci-coverage-allowlist.yml with a reason. ``` #### The census passes for the right reason once the entry lands 1. Command: ``` python .github/scripts/assert_ci_coverage.py ``` 2. Output: ``` OK: 2421 test files and 10 Dockerfiles are each invoked by at least one job or carry an explicit allowlist entry. ``` #### The sibling triage invariants still hold after the heads-up removal 1. Command: ``` uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/test_github_triage_workflows.py -q ``` 2. Output: ``` ........... [100%] 11 passed, 1 warning in 0.36s ``` #### Both moved scripts still resolve from their callers 1. Command: ``` python -m py_compile .github/scripts/run_llm_translation_tests.py .github/scripts/auto_update_price_and_context_window_file.py && echo "both compile OK" make -n test-llm-translation | tail -1 ``` 2. Output: ``` both compile OK python .github/scripts/run_llm_translation_tests.py ``` ## Type 🧹 Refactoring 🚄 Infrastructure ## Caveats - Collected agent test set is unchanged: one top-level file - The audit called the translation runner orphaned; Makefile still runs it - Heads-up removal also drops its two workflow-invariant tests - `.github/workflows/test-model-map.yaml` still uses `.yaml`, left alone ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signals.title: feat(ci): ratchet the test suite's zero-assert, mock-echo and global-state debt
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - 749 tests assert nothing at all - 742 more only assert that a mock was called - Nothing mechanical stops the sixth one landing tomorrow How it solves it: - An AST checker for the five shapes the audit named - A budget seeded at today's count, so new debt fails - Blames a change only for what it adds, never base drift - `--update` lowers a limit; nothing can raise one - Runs in the existing required lint job ## User Flow Before: a contributor adds a test that cannot fail, and CI is happy 1. They write `def test_router_falls_back():` that patches `router.function_with_fallbacks` and asserts only `mock_fallback.called` 2. They push, and every required check goes green 3. A reviewer would have to notice by eye that the fallback logic is mocked out of its own test 4. The test lands, and the suite grows one more test that survives any refactor which keeps the call and breaks the behavior After: the same push fails a required check that names the file, the line and the reason 1. They write the same test and push 2. `LiteLLM Linting / lint` fails with `TQ002: total 743 over limit 742 (this change added 1)` followed by `tests/test_litellm/test_router.py:412` 3. The message tells them to assert what the caller observes, or to record the exception as `# test-quality-ok: <reason>` 4. If instead they delete two older mock-echo tests, the total drops below the limit and the check passes, because the ceiling is what is enforced, not the individual test 5. Running `make lint-budget-update` afterwards lowers the limit by what they cleared, so the headroom they just created cannot be spent by someone else ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/<your_test_file>.py -v` - [x] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix A new gate is only worth having if it fails on a planted violation, so the proof is the gate red on one plant per rule, then green once the plant is gone. Shared setup: the planted file below, written to `tests/test_litellm/test_planted_tq_violations.py`, carries exactly one violation of each of the five rules. ```python import os import sys from unittest.mock import patch import litellm sys.path.insert(0, "..") def test_asserts_nothing(): litellm.completion def test_only_echoes_the_mock(): with patch("litellm.completion") as mock_completion: litellm.completion(model="gpt-4o", messages=[]) mock_completion.assert_called_once() def test_writes_process_globals(): os.environ["PLANTED_KEY"] = "x" litellm.drop_params = True ``` ### Before (5290150a05) #### The suite's existing debt is grandfathered, so a clean tree passes 1. Command: ``` python scripts/test_quality_gate.py ``` 2. Output: ``` OK: every TQ rule is within its test-suite ceiling (base origin/litellm_internal_staging) ``` ### After (dc0f15968c) #### Every planted rule trips, and the gate names the exact line 1. Command: ``` python scripts/test_quality_gate.py ``` 2. Output: ``` FAIL: TQ-rule totals exceed their limit (base origin/litellm_internal_staging): TQ001: total 751 over limit 749 (this change added 2) tests/test_litellm/test_planted_tq_violations.py:10 tests/test_litellm/test_planted_tq_violations.py:20 TQ002: total 743 over limit 742 (this change added 1) tests/test_litellm/test_planted_tq_violations.py:14 TQ003: total 1079 over limit 1078 (this change added 1) tests/test_litellm/test_planted_tq_violations.py:7 TQ004: total 771 over limit 770 (this change added 1) tests/test_litellm/test_planted_tq_violations.py:21 TQ005: total 2836 over limit 2835 (this change added 1) tests/test_litellm/test_planted_tq_violations.py:22 Fix the new violations, or give each one a reason (`# test-quality-ok: <reason>`), or remove an equal number elsewhere; the ceiling is the limit in test-quality-budget.json. Run `python scripts/check_test_quality.py tests/` to see every finding. ``` TQ001 reports two lines because `test_writes_process_globals` also asserts nothing, which is correct. #### A suppression carrying a reason clears it, a bare one does not 1. Command, against a file whose `sys.path.insert` carries `# test-quality-ok: vendored path is required here` and whose second test carries a bare `# test-quality-ok:` ``` python scripts/check_test_quality.py tests/test_litellm/test_planted_tq_violations.py ``` 2. Output, showing only the reasonless case survives: ``` tests/test_litellm/test_planted_tq_violations.py:14: TQ001 test `test_reasonless_suppression_does_not_suppress` asserts nothing, so it can only fail by raising; assert the observable output (suppress: `# test-quality-ok: <reason>`) 1 violation(s). ``` #### The plant removed, the gate is green again 1. Command: ``` rm tests/test_litellm/test_planted_tq_violations.py && python scripts/test_quality_gate.py ``` 2. Output: ``` OK: every TQ rule is within its test-suite ceiling (base origin/litellm_internal_staging) ``` #### The checker and gate are themselves covered 1. Command: ``` uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/test_check_test_quality.py tests/test_litellm/test_test_quality_gate.py -q ``` 2. Output: ``` ................................................ [100%] 48 passed, 1 warning in 1.37s ``` #### Cost of the check 1. Command: ``` time python scripts/test_quality_gate.py ``` 2. Output: 13s wall clock over the whole `tests/` tree on the green path. The base-tree scan only runs when a rule is already over its ceiling, so a passing PR never pays for it. ## Type 🚄 Infrastructure ✅ Test ## Caveats - Seeded counts are the shipped checker's, not the audit's scanner - TQ001 does not follow helpers across a module boundary - 25 such cases in tests/e2e are grandfathered, not suppressed - Gate rides the existing lint job, so no ruleset change - Burning the grandfathered debt down is separate, reviewed work ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signals.title: perf(ci): measure unit-shard coverage with the sys.monitoring core
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Coverage costs more than the tests on most shards - Shards run Python 3.12, where sysmon is not the default - So they pay for the slow tracer on every run How it solves it: - Ask for the sys.monitoring core explicitly on the shared base - One env var, same lines measured, same tests passing - Cuts the pytest step 47% to 89%, measured on four shards - Records why this and `branch = true` cannot both be on ## User Flow Before: a contributor waits on a required check that is spending much of its time in coverage bookkeeping 1. They push a backend change and watch the checks on their pull request 2. The slowest unit shard, `proxy-infra / Run tests`, takes about 15 minutes 3. The same directory under the legacy no-coverage workflow finished in roughly 5, so a large share of that wall clock is the tracer, not the tests 4. Nothing about the coverage number they get back is different for the wait After: the same check measures the same lines through the cheapest core coverage.py ships 1. They push the same change 2. The shards run with `COVERAGE_CORE=sysmon`, so coverage.py drives PEP 669 `sys.monitoring` instead of the settrace tracer 3. Codecov receives the same line coverage from the same `--cov=./litellm` invocation 4. This pull request's own run against #37586, which is the same code on the same day without the change, is the measurement; the numbers are in Proof of Fix below ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/<your_test_file>.py -v` - [x] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Two things need proving: that asking for sysmon is not a no-op at this Python, and that it cannot be combined with branch coverage. Both are shown against the exact versions CI pins, Python 3.12 and coverage 7.14.0. The wall-clock effect is measured by this pull request's own shard run, since a laptop under other load cannot produce a number worth quoting. Shared setup: ``` uv venv --python 3.12 .venv312 uv pip install --python .venv312/bin/python coverage==7.14.0 .venv312/bin/python -V ``` ``` Python 3.12.13 ``` ### Before (5290150a05) #### coverage does not choose sysmon on its own at 3.12 1. Command: ``` .venv312/bin/python -c "from coverage import env; print('SYSMON_DEFAULT =', env.SYSMON_DEFAULT)" ``` 2. Output, so without the env var the shards get the slow core: ``` SYSMON_DEFAULT = False ``` ### After (e4ffd6535c) #### Asking for sysmon works, and is silent 1. Command: ``` COVERAGE_CORE=sysmon .venv312/bin/python -m coverage run --source=. run.py ``` 2. Output, no warning, so the core was accepted: ``` pos nonpos ``` #### Asking for sysmon together with branch coverage is refused 1. Command: ``` COVERAGE_CORE=sysmon .venv312/bin/python -m coverage run --branch --source=. run.py ``` 2. Output: ``` coverage/core.py:94: CoverageWarning: Can't use core=sysmon: sys.monitoring can't measure branches in this version, using default core (no-sysmon); see https://coverage.readthedocs.io/en/7.14.0/messages.html#warning-no-sysmon warn(f"Can't use core=sysmon: {reason_no_sysmon}, using default core", slug="no-sysmon") pos nonpos ``` This is the open question answered: the two are mutually exclusive until the runners move to Python 3.14. Nothing in this change turns branch coverage on. #### Wall clock, this run against #37586 #37586 is the same tree on the same day with no coverage-core change, so its shards are the baseline. Comparing whole-job durations would be misleading, since a job also pays for checkout, dependency install and Prisma generation, so the numbers below are pytest's own reported wall time from each job's log, and each row states the test counts on both sides to show the same work was done. 1. Command, per shard and per pull request: ``` jobid=$(gh pr checks <pr> | grep -F "<shard> / Run tests" | awk -F'\t' '{print $4}' | sed 's#.*/job/##') gh api "repos/BerriAI/litellm/actions/jobs/$jobid/logs" | grep -E "=+ .*(passed|failed).* =+" | tail -1 ``` 2. Output: ``` budgets before 38 passed, 8 warnings in 432.37s (0:07:12) after 38 passed, 8 warnings in 47.68s proxy-utils before 200 passed, 6 warnings in 429.17s (0:07:09) after 200 passed, 6 warnings in 48.73s core-utils before 1692 passed, 1 skipped, 35 warnings in 209.43s (0:03:29) after 1692 passed, 1 skipped, 35 warnings in 88.58s (0:01:28) All Other Providers before 7742 passed, 80 skipped, 162 warnings in 464.28s (0:07:44) after 7742 passed, 80 skipped, 163 warnings in 245.20s (0:04:05) ``` Same counts on both sides of every row, so this is the same work measured twice. 3. Step-level confirmation that the gain is in the tests and not in setup, for the `budgets` shard: ``` gh api "repos/BerriAI/litellm/actions/jobs/$jobid" --jq '.steps[] | "\(.name)\t\(.started_at)\t\(.completed_at)"' ``` ``` before after 150s Install dependencies 168s Install dependencies 27s Generate Prisma client 11s Generate Prisma client 659s Run tests 74s Run tests 860s TOTAL 281s TOTAL ``` Setup did not get faster, it got slightly slower. The whole difference is the test step. The size of the gain tracks how much work each test does rather than how many tests there are: `budgets` runs 38 tests in what was seven minutes, and it drops about 89%, while `All Other Providers` runs 7,742 fast tests and drops about 47%. Shards dominated by heavy execution under the tracer are the ones that were paying most for it. ## Type 🚄 Infrastructure ## Caveats - Measured 47% to 89% off the pytest step, four shards - Blocks `branch = true` on 3.12; that trade is now documented - Same lines measured, so the coverage number should not move - Test counts identical on both sides, so it is like for like ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signals.title: refactor(ci): fold the nine thin unit-shard callers into one matrix
signals.text:
## TLDR Problem this solves: - Nine workflow files each made one call to the same base - Adding a shard meant adding a file - Changing anything shared meant editing nine files How it solves it: - One `test-unit.yml` matrix caller replaces all nine - Shard names preserved, so every required check keeps its name - No ruleset edit needed, and none should be made - 382 lines of workflow deleted, 219 added ## User Flow Before: adding a unit shard means adding a workflow file, and the reviewer has to check it against eight siblings 1. A contributor splits a slow directory and needs a new shard 2. They copy one of the nine `test-unit-*.yml` files, edit `test-path` and `artifact-name`, and commit the new file 3. They ask an admin to add the new `<shard> / Run tests` context to the branch ruleset 4. Anyone later changing something shared, a Python version or a permission block, edits nine files and hopes they are consistent After: adding a shard is one matrix entry, and the reviewer sees the whole set on one screen 1. The contributor adds an entry to the `include:` list in `.github/workflows/test-unit.yml` with its `shard`, `test-path`, `artifact-name`, workers, reruns and timeouts 2. The shard reports as `<shard> / Run tests`, the same shape as the existing eleven 3. They still ask an admin to add that one new context to the ruleset, because it is genuinely a new check 4. Anyone changing something shared edits one file, and the eleven shards cannot drift apart Nothing changes for the existing eleven shards: same names, same paths, same workers, same reruns, same timeouts. ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/<your_test_file>.py -v` - [x] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix A consolidation is only safe if it is a rename-free identity: the same eleven shards, the same inputs, and the same required-check names. All three are checked mechanically rather than by eye, and the check names are compared against the live ruleset rather than against the audit doc. ### Before (5290150a05) #### Nine files, eleven jobs, one call each 1. Command: ``` grep -l "_test-unit-base.yml" .github/workflows/test-unit-*.yml | grep -v proxy-db | wc -l ``` 2. Output: ``` 9 ``` ### After (2cd6b25a3d) #### Every shard's resolved inputs are identical, field by field The script below resolves each old caller's `with:` block against the base workflow's declared defaults, resolves the new matrix the same way, and diffs them per shard and per field. 1. Command, run with the nine old callers still present so both sides are readable at once: ``` python - <<'EOF' import yaml, pathlib, re, sys BASE_DEFAULTS = {"workers": 2, "reruns": 2, "timeout-minutes": 20, "job-timeout-minutes": 55, "max-failures": 10, "dist": "loadscope"} norm = lambda v: re.sub(r"\s+", " ", v).strip() if isinstance(v, str) else v old = {} for p in sorted(pathlib.Path(".github/workflows").glob("test-unit-*.yml")): if p.name in ("test-unit-proxy-db.yml", "test-unit.yml"): continue for jid, job in yaml.safe_load(p.read_text())["jobs"].items(): if job.get("uses") != "./.github/workflows/_test-unit-base.yml": continue old[job.get("name") or jid] = {**BASE_DEFAULTS, **{k: norm(v) for k, v in (job.get("with") or {}).items()}} wf = yaml.safe_load(pathlib.Path(".github/workflows/test-unit.yml").read_text()) new = {e["shard"]: {**BASE_DEFAULTS, **{k: norm(v) for k, v in e.items() if k != "shard"}} for e in wf["jobs"]["unit"]["strategy"]["matrix"]["include"]} print(f"old shards: {len(old)} new shards: {len(new)}") print("missing from new:", sorted(set(old) - set(new)) or "none") print("extra in new:", sorted(set(new) - set(old)) or "none") bad = 0 for shard in sorted(old): for key in sorted(set(old[shard]) | set(new.get(shard, {}))): o, n = old[shard].get(key), new.get(shard, {}).get(key) if o != n: bad += 1 print(f" DIFF {shard!r} {key}:
 old={o!r}
 new={n!r}") print("
RESULT:", "IDENTICAL" if not bad and set(old) == set(new) else f"{bad} differences") EOF ``` 2. Output: ``` old shards: 11 new shards: 11 missing from new: none extra in new: none RESULT: IDENTICAL ``` #### Every produced check name is a context the ruleset already requires 1. Command: ``` gh api repos/BerriAI/litellm/rules/branches/litellm_internal_staging \ --jq '[.[] | select(.type=="required_status_checks") | .parameters.required_status_checks[].context] | sort | .[]' ``` 2. Output, intersected with the eleven names the new matrix reports: ``` shards this workflow will report: 11 required '/ Run tests' contexts the ruleset asks for: 23 covered by the new matrix: OK All Other Providers / Run tests OK Vertex AI / Run tests OK core-utils / Run tests OK enterprise-routing / Run tests OK integrations / Run tests OK misc / Run tests OK proxy-auth / Run tests OK proxy-endpoints / Run tests OK proxy-infra / Run tests OK proxy-server / Run tests OK responses-caching-types / Run tests required but NOT produced by the new matrix (must be proxy-db or another workflow): -- auth-checks / Run tests -- budgets / Run tests -- custom-logging / Run tests -- db-and-spend / Run tests -- endpoints-and-responses / Run tests -- guardrails-hooks / Run tests -- jwt-and-keys / Run tests -- key-generation / Run tests -- logging-misc / Run tests -- proxy-runtime / Run tests -- proxy-server-core / Run tests -- proxy-utils / Run tests ``` Eleven here plus twelve from `test-unit-proxy-db.yml` accounts for all twenty-three. Nothing is orphaned and nothing is renamed. #### No test file lost its runner 1. Command: ``` python .github/scripts/assert_ci_coverage.py ``` 2. Output: ``` OK: 2422 test files and 10 Dockerfiles are each invoked by at least one job or carry an explicit allowlist entry. ``` #### The real proof is this pull request's own check list The eleven shard checks appear on this PR under their existing names. If any name had drifted, the ruleset would report a missing required check instead. ## Type 🧹 Refactoring 🚄 Infrastructure ## Caveats - `test-unit-proxy-db.yml` deliberately not folded in yet - Its shard guard reads that filename, so it moves with the guard - `test-unit-documentation.yml` stays; it calls no base workflow - All shards now share one concurrency group, same net behaviour - Setup-tax work on the base workflow is separate and untouched ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signals.title: test: remove the five test functions a later definition shadows
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Five test functions are shadowed by a later definition - Python never binds them, so pytest never collects them - August's sweep took the count 22 to 13; later work reached 5 - `conftest copy.py` is a duplicate pytest never loads How it solves it: - Deletes the five unreachable definitions and the stray conftest - Keeps the surviving twin in every case, which is the better one - Collected count is 416 before and after ## User Flow Before: someone reads a test, believes it runs, and it does not 1. A maintainer opens `tests/logging_callback_tests/test_sqs_logger.py` looking for what covers the SQS success path 2. They find `test_async_log_success_event_adds_to_queue` at line 154 and read its assertions 3. That definition is dead: an identical name at line 278 rebinds it, so the one they read has never executed 4. Any conclusion they draw about what is covered, or any edit they make to line 154, has no effect on CI After: the file contains only definitions that run 1. The maintainer opens the same file and finds one `test_async_log_success_event_adds_to_queue` 2. It is the surviving version, which additionally stubs `asyncio.create_task` 3. Editing it changes what CI does 4. `pytest --collect-only` reports the same 416 tests it did before, because the deleted definitions were never among them ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/<your_test_file>.py -v` - [x] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix The claim is that these definitions never ran, so the proof is that removing them changes nothing pytest collects. The detector below walks every scope in the test tree and reports each name a later definition rebinds. Shared setup, the four files touched: ``` FILES=(tests/llm_translation/test_bedrock_completion.py tests/llm_translation/test_openai.py tests/local_testing/test_completion_cost.py tests/logging_callback_tests/test_sqs_logger.py) ``` ### Before (5290150a05) #### The shadowed definitions exist and are unreachable 1. Command, `scripts/find_shadowed.py` being the AST detector described above: ``` python scripts/find_shadowed.py ``` 2. Output: ``` tests/llm_translation/test_bedrock_completion.py scope=module test_bedrock_cross_region_inference dead at line(s) 1205 tests/llm_translation/test_openai.py scope=TestOpenAIChatCompletion test_prompt_caching dead at line(s) 288 tests/local_testing/test_completion_cost.py scope=module test_cost_calculator_with_base_model_with_router dead at line(s) 2766 tests/logging_callback_tests/test_sqs_logger.py scope=module test_async_log_success_event_adds_to_queue dead at line(s) 154 tests/logging_callback_tests/test_sqs_logger.py scope=module test_async_log_failure_event_adds_to_queue dead at line(s) 166 shadowed test functions: 5 ``` 3. Command: ``` uv run pytest "${FILES[@]}" --collect-only -q | tail -1 ``` 4. Output: ``` 416 tests collected in 0.20s ``` ### After (c3545eee04) #### Nothing is shadowed any more 1. Command, the same detector: ``` python scripts/find_shadowed.py ``` 2. Output: ``` shadowed test functions: 0 ``` #### The collected set is unchanged 1. Command: ``` uv run pytest "${FILES[@]}" --collect-only -q | tail -1 ``` 2. Output: ``` 416 tests collected in 0.27s ``` Same number, so no test was removed from the run. That is the whole safety argument. #### The one keyless file still passes 1. Command: ``` uv run pytest tests/logging_callback_tests/test_sqs_logger.py -q ``` 2. Output: ``` 18 passed, 1 warning in 4.08s ``` #### Every test file still has a runner 1. Command: ``` python .github/scripts/assert_ci_coverage.py ``` 2. Output: ``` OK: 2422 test files and 10 Dockerfiles are each invoked by at least one job or carry an explicit allowlist entry. ``` ## Type 🧹 Refactoring ✅ Test ## Caveats - Five reappeared after a sweep, so a rule beats another sweep - That rule belongs in the checker #37588 adds, as a follow-up - Independent of #37588; this one only deletes dead definitions - The three non-SQS files need provider keys, so CI covers them - The detector is a throwaway, not added to the repo here ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signals.title: feat(ci): guard shard assignment across every sharded test tree
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - `tests/test_litellm/` is sharded with no catch-all bucket - A new directory under it is therefore collected by nothing - Nothing catches that: the coverage census cannot see it - `tests/proxy_unit_tests/` had a guard, inlined in its workflow How it solves it: - Lifts that guard into the script that already parses `test-path` - Points it at all three sharded trees instead of one - Adds the matcher that separates "does it run" from "who owns it" ## User Flow Before: a new test directory runs nowhere and every check is green 1. Someone adds `tests/test_litellm/webhooks/test_webhooks.py`, a new area with its own directory 2. `assert-ci-coverage` passes, because the token `tests/test_litellm/test_*.py` already answers "yes, that tree is run by a job" 3. `assert-shard-coverage` passes, because it only ever looked at `tests/proxy_unit_tests/` 4. No shard names `webhooks`, so pytest never collects it. The tests are green on the author's laptop and absent from CI forever After: the same PR fails, and says which directory and which tree 1. The author adds the same directory 2. `assert-shard-coverage` fails with `tests/test_litellm/webhooks: holds tests but no shard of tests/test_litellm names it` 3. They add `tests/test_litellm/webhooks` to the shard it belongs to, and the check goes green 4. A directory that is genuinely split across several shards goes in `SHARDED_ROOTS` instead, which makes the guard check its children one level deeper ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/<your_test_file>.py -v` - [x] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix A guard is only worth having if it fails on the thing it claims to catch, so each case below is planted, measured, then removed. ### Before, on `litellm_internal_staging` #### The gap: a new directory under `tests/test_litellm/` passes every check 1. Command: ``` mkdir -p tests/test_litellm/brand_new_area echo "def test_x(): assert True" > tests/test_litellm/brand_new_area/test_x.py python3 .github/scripts/assert_ci_coverage.py ``` 2. Output, the census is satisfied and the directory still runs nowhere: ``` OK: 2422 test files and 10 Dockerfiles are each invoked by at least one job or carry an explicit allowlist entry. ``` ### After #### The same planted directory now fails 1. Command: ``` python3 .github/scripts/assert_ci_coverage.py --shards ``` 2. Output: ``` ERROR: test directories and files that no shard claims - tests/test_litellm/brand_new_area: holds tests but no shard of tests/test_litellm names it Add each to the shard it belongs to. A directory that is itself split across several shards belongs in SHARDED_ROOTS instead, so its own children get checked. ``` #### It fails the same way one level deeper 1. Command: ``` mkdir -p tests/test_litellm/proxy/brand_new_endpoints echo "def test_x(): assert True" > tests/test_litellm/proxy/brand_new_endpoints/test_x.py python3 .github/scripts/assert_ci_coverage.py --shards ``` 2. Output: ``` ERROR: test directories and files that no shard claims - tests/test_litellm/proxy/brand_new_endpoints: holds tests but no shard of tests/test_litellm/proxy names it ``` #### It still catches what the old inlined guard caught 1. Command: ``` echo "def test_x(): assert True" > tests/proxy_unit_tests/test_brand_new.py python3 .github/scripts/assert_ci_coverage.py --shards ``` 2. Output: ``` ERROR: test directories and files that no shard claims - tests/proxy_unit_tests/test_brand_new.py: holds tests but no shard of tests/proxy_unit_tests names it ``` #### A fixture directory is not mistaken for a test directory The old guard kept `test_configs` out by name. This one keeps every fixture directory out by asking whether it holds a test file, so `expected_fine_tuning_api/`, `expected_responses_api_request/` and both `test_configs/` need no exception. 1. Command: ``` mkdir -p tests/test_litellm/expected_new_fixtures echo '{}' > tests/test_litellm/expected_new_fixtures/payload.json python3 .github/scripts/assert_ci_coverage.py --shards ``` 2. Output: ``` OK: all 327 test children across 3 sharded trees are assigned to a shard. ``` #### The tree as it stands is fully assigned, and the census is unchanged 1. Command: ``` python3 .github/scripts/assert_ci_coverage.py --shards python3 .github/scripts/assert_ci_coverage.py ``` 2. Output: ``` OK: all 327 test children across 3 sharded trees are assigned to a shard. OK: 2423 test files and 10 Dockerfiles are each invoked by at least one job or carry an explicit allowlist entry. ``` #### Unit tests 1. Command: ``` uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/test_assert_ci_coverage.py -q ``` 2. Output: ``` 11 passed, 1 warning in 0.30s ``` ## Type 🆕 New Feature ✅ Test ## Caveats - The required check `assert-shard-coverage` keeps its exact name and workflow - Renaming or moving it would strand a required context, so neither happens here - The script had no tests at all before this, so the new file covers both matchers - A tree sharded by subdirectory must be declared, which is the point, not a limitation ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signals.title: chore(typing): tighten annotations added in the last day and ratchet budgets
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Yesterday's commits added untyped returns and a coarse `dict` - One new `getattr` string lookup replaced a typed attribute read - Budget ceilings kept stale headroom for those violations How it solves it: - Annotate the new signatures, no runtime change - Read `existing_key_row.metadata` directly instead of `getattr` - Ratchet the three budget files down ## User Flow No user-visible change: this is annotations plus one typed attribute read, so both flows are identical Before: a developer calls the proxy and everything behaves exactly as it does today 1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/key/update with a `batch_enqueued_token_limit` in metadata as a non-admin key 2. They get back 403 naming the admin-only restriction 3. Admin keys get 200 and the limit applied After: the same steps produce the same responses 1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/key/update with a `batch_enqueued_token_limit` in metadata as a non-admin key 2. They get back 403 naming the admin-only restriction 3. Admin keys get 200 and the limit applied ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [ ] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more - [x] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) Note on tests: no new tests, since nothing here changes behavior. The existing files covering the touched code pass unchanged ## Findings fixed, each with the commit that introduced it `5c6391d7d2` refactor(batches): parameterize the batch output Mapping annotations. `_get_anthropic_result_from_batch_results_line` returned bare `dict` and `_get_response_from_batch_job_output_file` returned `Any`, both now `Mapping[str, Any]` matching what they already return `6ca48efc8b` feat(cli): add `lite login --config-claude`. The new `login` command had no return annotation, now `-> None` `6b17b8a8f2` fix(proxy): restrict batch_enqueued_token_limit metadata writes to proxy admins. The new call site went through `getattr(existing_key_row, "metadata", None)` plus an isinstance narrowing, replaced with the typed `existing_key_row.metadata` read since the row is a `LiteLLM_VerificationToken` at that point `11552dbafc` chore(typing): drop 1.3k basedpyright errors across 42 Any hotspot files. Two functions added in that pass still had no return annotation: `PrometheusLogger._set_key_list_budget_metrics` and `ModelRepository.__init__`, both now `-> None` `make lint-budget-update` ratcheted `ruff-strict-budget.json`, `type-discipline-budget.json`, and `basedpyright-code-budget.json` down for exactly these fixes. No ceiling was raised and no suppression was added ## Left alone on purpose `litellm/proxy/utils.py:531` keeps `getattr(_logging_obj, "model_call_details", {})`. Narrowing it to the `Logging` class breaks the duck-typed logging objects the failure path is exercised with, so removing the `getattr` there would be a behavior change, not cleanup `litellm/proxy/spend_tracking/ptu_flat_cost_rollup.py` keeps its `# mutable-ok` comments. Prisma query serialization needs concrete mutable mappings, so those look genuinely unavoidable `litellm/integrations/prometheus.py` is a monster file and `_set_org_list_budget_metrics` next door takes a bare `list`. Both are older than this window, so out of scope here, but the file is worth splitting ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Typing-only change with no runtime path to exercise, so the proof is the repo's own gates on the branch tip: `make check` reports PASS, with the strict, LIT, and basedpyright gates all inside their newly lowered ceilings ## Type 🧹 Refactoring ## Caveats (if any) - Budget files move, so rebases may conflict there Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/f12b1f63eb5940a89e5579d0d9877e38

signals.title: test: run the 30 test files stranded in the second mirror
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - `tests/litellm/` sat beside `tests/test_litellm/` and ran nowhere - The allowlist assumed a duplicate mirror and left it unresolved - 30 of its 34 files have no counterpart, so they are simply unrun - Not running is why three of their assertions had drifted off the code How it solves it: - Moves 29 into the real mirror and 1 beside the repo-wide checks - Corrects the three assertions the code had moved past - Leaves four files whose twins hold disjoint tests, and says so ## User Flow Before: a test is written, reviewed, merged, and never runs again 1. Someone adds a Vertex text-to-speech test under `tests/litellm/llms/vertex_ai/text_to_speech/`, matching what they see in that tree 2. It passes locally and is merged. No CI job collects `tests/litellm/`, so it never runs again 3. The handler later moves from `data=` to `json=`. Nothing fails, because nothing runs 4. The next reader sees a test asserting the old wire shape and cannot tell whether it is a stale test or a real regression After: the same test runs on every PR 1. The file now lives at `tests/test_litellm/llms/vertex_ai/text_to_speech/test_transformation.py`, inside the `llms` shard 2. It is claimed by a shard's `test-path`, not by an allowlist entry, so `assert-ci-coverage` counts it as run 3. Its assertion reads the body off the `json` kwarg, which is what the handler sends today 4. The next handler change that alters the request shape fails this test in CI ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/<your_test_file>.py -v` - [x] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix The claim is "these files were not running, and now they are." The first two commands establish it, the rest show the moved tests actually pass. ### Before (`litellm_internal_staging`) #### 30 of the 34 files have no counterpart, so nothing else covers them 1. Command: ``` find tests/litellm -name "test_*.py" | while read f; do rel=${f#tests/litellm/}; [ -f "tests/test_litellm/$rel" ] && echo "TWIN $rel" || echo "ORPHAN $rel"; done | cut -d' ' -f1 | sort | uniq -c ``` 2. Output: ``` 4 TWIN 30 ORPHAN ``` #### No job collects them 1. Command, asking the census which job token claims each file: ``` python3 .github/scripts/assert_ci_coverage.py ``` 2. Output, they pass only because the allowlist exempts the directory: ``` OK: 2422 test files and 10 Dockerfiles are each invoked by at least one job or carry an explicit allowlist entry. ``` ### After (b7d3746d59) #### Every moved file is now claimed by a real job, not by the allowlist 1. Command: ``` python3 - <<'PY' import importlib.util, sys spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("acc", ".github/scripts/assert_ci_coverage.py") m = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec); sys.modules["acc"] = m; spec.loader.exec_module(m) tokens = m._invoked_test_tokens(m._all_scalars()) paths = [l.strip() for l in open("moved.txt") if l.strip()] unrun = [p for p in paths if not any(m._token_covers(t, p) for t in tokens)] print(f"moved files: {len(paths)}; covered by a real job token: {len(paths)-len(unrun)}") PY ``` 2. Output: ``` moved files: 30; covered by a real job token: 30 ``` #### And they pass 1. Command: ``` uv run pytest $(cat moved.txt | tr '\n' ' ') -q -n 2 ``` 2. Output: ``` 216 passed, 147 warnings in 103.24s (0:01:43) ``` Before the three drift fixes the same command reported `29 failed, 241 passed, 2 errors`, with 25 of those failures inside one of the four files that stay behind. #### The shards they joined still collect Several of the moved files are named `test_transformation.py`, which pytest cannot import twice from non-package directories in one session, so this is the check that matters. 1. Command: ``` uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/llms --collect-only -q | tail -1 uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/integrations --collect-only -q | tail -1 uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/proxy/management_endpoints --collect-only -q | tail -1 uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/test_*.py --collect-only -q | tail -1 ``` 2. Output: ``` 9240 tests collected in 1.49s 2683 tests collected in 65.10s (0:01:05) 2797 tests collected in 3.53s 2654 tests collected in 65.04s (0:01:05) ``` Without the added `__init__.py`, the first of those reports `9229 tests collected, 1 error`. #### The secret scan still runs, from its new path `test_no_hardcoded_secrets.py` is the one file that did not go to the mirror. Its job runs pytest under `uv run --no-project`, an environment holding pytest and nothing else, and the mirror's conftest imports litellm on collection. It went to `tests/code_coverage_tests/` with the other repo-wide checks, which has no conftest. Verified with the job's exact command: 1. Command: ``` uv run --no-project --with 'pytest==9.0.2' pytest tests/code_coverage_tests/test_no_hardcoded_secrets.py -q ``` 2. Output: ``` 1 passed in 0.47s ``` #### The census is still green 1. Command: ``` python3 .github/scripts/assert_ci_coverage.py ``` 2. Output: ``` OK: 2422 test files and 10 Dockerfiles are each invoked by at least one job or carry an explicit allowlist entry. ``` ## Type 🧹 Refactoring ✅ Test ## Caveats - Moves are byte-identical, so `git diff --find-renames` shows every one at R100 - The three edited assertions are the only test semantics touched - The four files left behind need their bodies merged into their twins, not moved - The secret scan went to `tests/code_coverage_tests/`, not the mirror, since its job has no litellm deps - The allowlist now names those four and the test counts each would bring ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signals.title: fix(mcp): map only OpenAPI servers when a registry reload registers their tools
signals.text: ## Title fix(mcp): map only OpenAPI servers when a registry reload registers their tools ## Relevant issues None filed; found on a v1.97.0 deployment. ## Problem `MCPServerManager.reload_servers_from_database()` re-registers OpenAPI tools on every pass and then calls `initialize_tool_name_to_mcp_server_name_mapping()` for the **whole** registry, which calls `list_tools` upstream on every remote MCP server. That reload runs on a timer (`proxy_config_reload_interval_seconds`, 30s by default, via the `add_deployment` job when `store_model_in_db=True`, or the `reload_mcp_servers_job` otherwise). So a deployment with at least one OpenAPI server (`spec_path`) polls **every other MCP server every 30 seconds**, with no incoming request behind it. Servers that take a per-user credential at call time (the `x-mcp-<alias>-authorization` forwarding convention, `auth_type: none`) get called with no credential at all on that path, so they answer 401. On our proxy the log fills up twice a minute: ``` LiteLLM:WARNING: mcp_server_manager.py:4214 - Error listing tools from salesforce: Client error '401 Unauthorized' for url 'https://api.salesforce.com/...' LiteLLM:WARNING: mcp_server_manager.py:4214 - Error listing tools from pedidos_demo_auth: Client error '401 Unauthorized' for url 'https://...lambda-url.eu-west-1.on.aws/' ``` and the upstreams see a constant stream of unauthenticated requests. The existing skip in the mapping loop only covers `needs_user_oauth_token` (`auth_type == oauth2` without client credentials), which does not describe these servers. ## Fix OpenAPI tools are served from the local tool registry (`_get_tools_from_server` reads `global_mcp_tool_registry` for `spec_path` servers, no network call), so the mapping refresh those registrations need only has to cover the OpenAPI servers themselves. `initialize_tool_name_to_mcp_server_name_mapping()` takes an optional `servers` argument; the reload path passes the OpenAPI servers it registered in that pass, and `_maybe_register_openapi_tools` passes the single server it just registered. Startup (`load_servers_from_config`) still maps the full registry, unchanged. ## Testing New test: `tests/test_litellm/proxy/_experimental/mcp_server/test_mcp_server_manager.py::TestMCPServerManager::test_database_reload_maps_only_openapi_servers` — reloads a registry holding one OpenAPI server and one remote server, and asserts the mapping refresh covers only the OpenAPI one. It fails without the change and passes with it. ``` uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/proxy/_experimental/mcp_server/ -q -p no:randomly 2 failed, 2965 passed ``` The two failures are `test_mcp_env_vars.py::test_resolve_static_headers_empty_global_does_not_cover_user_var` and `::test_resolve_static_headers_raises_when_user_vars_missing`. They are pre-existing: the same two fail on an unmodified tree in the same full-directory run (`2 failed, 2964 passed`), and both pass when that file runs on its own, so it is cross-test state, unrelated to this change. `ruff format --check` and `ruff check` are clean on the changed lines (the pre-existing `UP006`/`UP045`/`I001` findings in the test file are untouched), and `scripts/type_discipline_gate.py` reports every LIT rule within its ceiling.

signals.title: test: settle three allowlist entries that were open questions
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Three allowlist entries recorded a question, not a decision - One said the files "need moving", so nobody moved them - One called a benchmark script an unexplained gap - One gave no reason a reader could act on How it solves it: - Moves the two that needed moving, so 23 tests start running - Says what the benchmark script is and why it stays out - Measures the third and names what actually blocks it ## User Flow Before: the exemption list reads as a backlog nobody can act on 1. A maintainer opens `.github/ci-coverage-allowlist.yml` to see what is not covered 2. They read "they need moving rather than a shard entry" and cannot tell whether that is a plan, a warning, or a thing already done 3. They read "referenced by no job" for a third file and cannot tell whether wiring it up is a five-minute job or a bad idea 4. Nothing moves, and the entries survive another quarter After: every remaining entry states a decision and what would change it 1. The two prompt-factory files are gone from the list, because they now live in the mirror and run 2. The benchmark script's entry says it fetches live URLs and asserts nothing, so a reader knows not to wire it up 3. The proxy-extras entry names the exact blocker: 13 migrations use unguarded DDL, and Prisma checksums forbid editing them after the fact 4. A maintainer can act on, or disagree with, each one without re-deriving it ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/<your_test_file>.py -v` - [x] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix ### The two that moved #### They pass, and did all along 1. Command: ``` uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/litellm_core_utils/test_anthropic_dedup_factory.py tests/test_litellm/litellm_core_utils/test_bedrock_converse_dedup_factory.py -q ``` 2. Output: ``` 23 passed, 1 warning in 0.30s ``` #### A job claims them now, rather than the allowlist exempting them 1. Command: ``` python3 - <<'PY' import importlib.util, sys spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("acc", ".github/scripts/assert_ci_coverage.py") m = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec); sys.modules["acc"] = m; spec.loader.exec_module(m) tokens = m._invoked_test_tokens(m._all_scalars()) for p in ("tests/test_litellm/litellm_core_utils/test_anthropic_dedup_factory.py", "tests/test_litellm/litellm_core_utils/test_bedrock_converse_dedup_factory.py"): print(p, "->", [t for t in tokens if m._token_covers(t, p)]) PY ``` 2. Output: ``` tests/test_litellm/litellm_core_utils/test_anthropic_dedup_factory.py -> ['tests/test_litellm/litellm_core_utils'] tests/test_litellm/litellm_core_utils/test_bedrock_converse_dedup_factory.py -> ['tests/test_litellm/litellm_core_utils'] ``` #### The shard they joined still collects 1. Command: ``` uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/litellm_core_utils --collect-only -q | tail -1 ``` 2. Output: ``` 1716 tests collected in 0.81s ``` ### The one that stays, measured #### 24 of 28 pass; the 4 that fail are the migration guard 1. Command: ``` uv run pytest tests/litellm-proxy-extras -q ``` 2. Output: ``` 4 failed, 24 passed, 1 warning in 64.48s (0:01:04) ``` 3. Command, on one of the four: ``` uv run pytest "tests/litellm-proxy-extras/test_litellm_proxy_extras_utils.py::TestMigrationSQLIdempotency::test_create_table_uses_if_not_exists" -q ``` 4. Output: ``` AssertionError: CREATE TABLE without IF NOT EXISTS found in migrations: 20260418000000_add_adaptive_router_tables:2: CREATE TABLE "LiteLLM_AdaptiveRouterState" ( 20260418000000_add_adaptive_router_tables:14: CREATE TABLE "LiteLLM_AdaptiveRouterSession" ( 20260429161855_workflow_runs_tables:2: CREATE TABLE "LiteLLM_WorkflowRun" ( 20260429161855_workflow_runs_tables:18: CREATE TABLE "LiteLLM_WorkflowEvent" ( 20260429161855_workflow_runs_tables:31: CREATE TABLE "LiteLLM_WorkflowMessage" ( 20260811172448_add_shadow_eval:2: CREATE TABLE "LiteLLM_ShadowEvalJob" ( 20260811172448_add_shadow_eval:18: CREATE TABLE "LiteLLM_ShadowEvalAttempt" ( 20260814000000_add_proxy_worker_heartbeat:2: CREATE TABLE "LiteLLM_ProxyWorkerHeartbeat" ( 20260817143646_add_daily_guardrail_usage_units:2: CREATE TABLE "LiteLLM_DailyGuardrailUsageUnits" ( ``` This PR changes none of those migrations. It records the finding on the entry so the next person starts from it. ### The list itself 1. Command: ``` python3 -c "import yaml; d=yaml.safe_load(open('.github/ci-coverage-allowlist.yml')); print('entries:', len(d['test_paths']), '| paths:', sum(len(e['paths']) for e in d['test_paths']))" python3 .github/scripts/assert_ci_coverage.py ``` 2. Output: ``` entries: 9 | paths: 86 OK: 2422 test files and 10 Dockerfiles are each invoked by at least one job or carry an explicit allowlist entry. ``` ## Type 🧹 Refactoring ✅ Test ## Caveats - The two moves are byte-identical; only their path changed - No migration SQL is touched here, and none should be touched in place - The benchmark script stays exempt rather than being deleted, since that is a separate call - Entries went 10 to 9 and paths 88 to 86 ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR
