signals.title: fix(vertex_ai): assemble agent engine responses from every event
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - A tool call ends the stream before the answer - Only one step's text survives a multi-step run - Reported token counts are replaced by a wrong estimate - Internal agent state can be returned as the answer How it solves it: - Only a text-bearing event may finish the stream - Keep every text part of every finalised event - Sum the counts Agent Engine actually returns - Drop the model's own reasoning parts from the answer ## User Flow Before: a developer calling a Vertex AI Agent Engine deployment that uses any tool gets an empty answer back 1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with `model: vertex_ai/agent_engine/<id>`, `"stream": true`, and one question 2. The agent calls one of its own tools, which arrives as an event carrying no text 3. The stream closes on that event, so the response is an empty message with `finish_reason: stop` 4. They repeat the request without `"stream": true` and get text back, but the `usage` block reports a few hundred tokens where the deployment charged several thousand 5. They open https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs and see that request logged at a fraction of its real spend After: the same requests return the answer and the spend the deployment reported 1. They send the same POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with `"stream": true` 2. The tool call arrives and the stream stays open 3. The answer streams in when the agent produces it, and `finish_reason: stop` arrives with it 4. The non-streaming repeat returns the same text with a `usage` block matching what the deployment charged 5. https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs shows that request at its real spend ## Relevant issues #19121 reported the stream ending early on Agent Engine deployments with MCP tools and proposed a fix in the thread. It was closed as stale without review, and the behaviour is unchanged on current main. This PR shares that diagnosis but deliberately does not surface the agent's `function_call` parts as OpenAI `tool_calls`. Agent Engine executes those server side, so a client that received them would be told to run functions it cannot run, and to reply with results the deployment is not waiting for ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally - [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix A note on the setup, so it is not overstated. The provider needs a real reasoning engine on Vertex AI, which I have access to, and a proxy instance a reviewer could reach, which I do not. So the live half is a real unmocked `:streamQuery` call against a deployed Agent Engine agent in `europe-west1`, and the two commits are then exercised by feeding that captured response through the provider on each one. The event shapes below are the API's, not mine. The same capture is committed, redacted, as the test fixture. Shared setup, one question to a deployment whose agent calls a single tool before answering: ``` $ curl -sN -X POST \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ "https://europe-west1-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/<project>/locations/europe-west1/reasoningEngines/<id>:streamQuery?alt=sse" \ -d '{"class_method":"stream_query","input":{"user_id":"pf-user","message":"What is my internal project called?"}}' [0] partial=None finish_reason=None parts=[] [1] partial=False finish_reason=STOP parts=[function_call, thought_signature] usage: p=907 c=129 t=1036 [2] partial=None finish_reason=None parts=[function_response] [3] partial=False finish_reason=STOP parts=[text(1162 chars)] usage: p=1120 c=225 t=1345 [4] partial=None finish_reason=None parts=[] ``` Event 1 is the tool call. It reports `finish_reason: STOP` and carries no text. The answer is in event 3, and the run was billed for two model calls totalling 2381 tokens ### Before (5290150a05) 1. Feed the captured response to the streaming iterator and the non-streaming transform on the merge base: ``` STREAMING stopped at event: 1 of 4 STREAMING client received : '' NON-STREAMING usage : prompt=8 completion=226 total=234 ``` 2. The stream closes on the tool call, so a streaming caller receives an empty message. The non-streaming path discards the 2381 tokens the deployment reported and substitutes a 234 token estimate produced by a gpt-3.5 tokenizer ### After (1969770c4b) 1. Feed the same captured response through the same two paths at the PR tip: ``` STREAMING stopped at event: 3 of 4 STREAMING client received : 'Here is a proposed research plan to identify your internal p' NON-STREAMING usage : prompt=2027 completion=354 total=2381 ``` 2. The tool call passes through, the answer reaches the caller, and usage is the sum of what both model calls reported ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - This capture had one text event; concatenation is covered by tests - Partial events are skipped so finalised text and counts are not doubled - The capture emitted `partial: false` only; incremental deltas are unverified - Streaming still forwards partials as deltas, which streaming callers want - Usage summing is non-streaming only; the wrapper aggregates streaming itself ### Final Attestation - [ ] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signals.title: fix(vertex_ai): stop dropping conversation history on agent engine
signals.text:
## TLDR Problem this solves: - Only the last message ever reaches the agent - Every turn starts with no conversation context How it solves it: - Flatten the whole message list when there is no session - Send only the new message when the caller supplies one ## User Flow Before: a developer chatting with a Vertex AI Agent Engine deployment finds the agent remembers nothing they said 1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with `model: vertex_ai/agent_engine/<id>` and one user message naming their internal project, and get an acknowledgement back 2. They send the same POST again with all three messages, the two above plus "What is my internal project called?" 3. The reply does not name the project, because the two earlier messages were dropped and only the last question was forwarded After: the same conversation carries its own context 1. They send the same first POST and get the same acknowledgement 2. They send the same three-message POST 3. The reply names the project, because the earlier turns now travel with the request ## Relevant issues None open for this specific behaviour. Related report against the same provider: #19121 ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally - [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix A note on the setup, so it is not overstated. The provider needs a real reasoning engine on Vertex AI, which I have access to, and a proxy instance a reviewer could reach, which I do not. So each commit builds the request body it would send, and both bodies then go to a deployed Agent Engine agent in `europe-west1` as real unmocked calls. What differs between the two runs is only the body the provider produced. Shared setup, the same three-message conversation on both sides: ```python messages = [ {"role": "user", "content": "My internal project is called QUARTZ-BADGER-7731."}, {"role": "assistant", "content": "Understood."}, {"role": "user", "content": "What is my internal project called?"}, ] ``` The token is deliberately one the model cannot produce on its own, so an answer naming it can only have come from the conversation ### Before (5290150a05) 1. The merge base builds this body: ```json {"class_method": "stream_query", "input": {"message": "What is my internal project called?", "user_id": "pf-user"}} ``` 2. Send it to the deployment: ``` $ curl -sN -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ ".../reasoningEngines/<id>:streamQuery?alt=sse" -d @before.json HTTP 200 Here is a proposed research plan to identify your internal project name: * [RESEARCH] Investigate contextual workspace metadata, configuration files, and repository manifests to detect explicit internal project identifiers or codenames. * [RESEARCH] Analyze version control history, branch names, and commit messages for references to project aliases or development tags. ... ``` 3. The agent cannot name the project. The first two messages never left the gateway ### After (4b8c94a0eb) 1. The PR tip builds this body: ```json {"class_method": "stream_query", "input": {"message": "user: My internal project is called QUARTZ-BADGER-7731.

assistant: Understood.

user: What is my internal project called?", "user_id": "pf-user"}} ``` 2. Send it to the same deployment: ``` $ curl -sN -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ ".../reasoningEngines/<id>:streamQuery?alt=sse" -d @after.json HTTP 200 Your internal project is called **QUARTZ-BADGER-7731**. Would you like to initiate a new research plan or explore a specific topic related to this project? ``` 3. A caller who passes an explicit `session_id` still gets one message per turn, since the deployment holds that history itself ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - Flattening uses a plain `role: content` layout - Tool calls and image parts flatten to their text, as before - The proxy's own session id is deliberately not reused here - A per-request user id would make such a session unfindable anyway ### Final Attestation - [ ] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signals.title: fix(pricing): add Azure GPT-5.6 cache write rates
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Azure GPT-5.6 cache writes are billed at zero How it solves it: - Adds cache-write rates for every Azure GPT-5.6 price entry ## User Flow Before: a platform team sees cached Azure prompt spend missing from proxy logs 1. The response returns HTTP 200 with `cache_write_tokens` in `prompt_tokens_details` 3. They open https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs and see the cache-write portion recorded at $0 After: the same request records cache writes at Azure's documented 1.25x input rate 1. They send the same POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions request to the same Azure GPT-5.6 deployment 2. The response returns HTTP 200 with the same `cache_write_tokens` usage details 3. They open https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs and see non-zero cache-write spend ## Relevant issues Fixes #37631 ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally - [x] My PR passes required local formatting checks - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile Confidence Score of at least 4/5 before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix A live Azure deployment is required for end-to-end proxy proof and was not available in this environment. signals.title: fix(responses bridge): map incomplete responses to finish_reason length instead of 500
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Reasoning models can spend every output token on reasoning - The Responses bridge then returned 500 on /v1/chat/completions - A user token-limit condition was counted as a system error How it solves it: - Map `incomplete_details.reason` to a chat `finish_reason` - `max_output_tokens` becomes `length`, `content_filter` becomes `content_filter` - Return an empty assistant message instead of raising - Streaming handles `response.incomplete` the same way ## User Flow Before: a developer with a small `max_completion_tokens` gets a 500 when the model spends all tokens on reasoning 1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with `"max_completion_tokens": 16` and `"reasoning_effort": "high"` to a model served through the Responses bridge 2. The model uses all 16 tokens on reasoning and produces no message 3. The gateway returns HTTP 500 with `"gpt-5.6-sol unable to complete request: max_output_tokens"`, which their monitoring counts as a gateway outage After: the same request comes back as a normal truncated completion 1. They send the same POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with `"max_completion_tokens": 16` and `"reasoning_effort": "high"` 2. The model uses all 16 tokens on reasoning and produces no message 3. The gateway returns HTTP 200 with an empty assistant message, `"finish_reason": "length"`, and real usage, matching what POST https://litellm-domain/v1/responses already reported for the same call ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more - [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Shared setup: proxy running with a config that routes `bridge/gpt-5.6-sol` to `openai/responses/gpt-5.6-sol` against the real OpenAI API, and this payload ```json { "model": "bridge/gpt-5.6-sol", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Determine the last ten decimal digits of 7 raised to the power 123456789. Think through modular arithmetic carefully, then return only those ten digits."}], "reasoning_effort": "high", "max_completion_tokens": 16 } ``` ### Before (6d47468dae) #### Non-streaming request 1. `curl -sS -i http://localhost:4010/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d "$REQ"` 2. Observed output ```text HTTP/1.1 500 Internal Server Error {"error":{"message":"litellm.APIConnectionError: APIConnectionError: OpenAIException - gpt-5.6-sol unable to complete request: max_output_tokens. Received Model Group=bridge/gpt-5.6-sol\nAvailable Model Group Fallbacks=None","type":null,"param":null,"code":"500"}} ``` #### Streaming request 1. Same curl with `"stream": true` added to the payload 2. Observed final chunks, `finish_reason` claims a normal stop even though output was truncated ```text data: {"id":"chatcmpl-12f2a2c4-fabc-423f-a478-d68bb6e683db","object":"chat.completion.chunk","created":1787240134,"model":"bridge/gpt-5.6-sol","choices":[{"index":0,"delta":{},"finish_reason":"stop"}]} data: [DONE] ``` ### After (0cf91d0a9c) #### Non-streaming request 1. `curl -sS -i http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d "$REQ"` 2. Observed output, now 200 with `finish_reason` length and real usage ```text HTTP/1.1 200 OK {"id":"chatcmpl-6454e7fa-a649-46e2-a1e6-8b83151af674","created":1787240123,"model":"bridge/gpt-5.6-sol","object":"chat.completion","choices":[{"finish_reason":"length","index":0,"message":{"content":"","role":"assistant"}}],"usage":{"completion_tokens":16,"prompt_tokens":37,"total_tokens":53,"completion_tokens_details":{"reasoning_tokens":16},"prompt_tokens_details":{"cached_tokens":0,"cache_write_tokens":0,"cache_creation_tokens":0}}} ``` #### Streaming request 1. Same curl with `"stream": true` added to the payload 2. Observed final chunks, terminal `finish_reason` is now length ```text data: {"id":"chatcmpl-9acbe013-0f4a-4c9c-9c0b-cb6ce1f72062","object":"chat.completion.chunk","created":1787240125,"model":"bridge/gpt-5.6-sol","choices":[{"index":0,"delta":{},"finish_reason":"length"}]} data: [DONE] ``` ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - A response with no output and no incomplete reason still raises, as before ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/c9ae02a8c3a34f549b33b7ac51887b5c

signals.title: fix(ui): draw one Per Day savings bar per date on Cost Optimization
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Per Day savings chart split each day into per-page partial bars - Daily bars read near zero while Cumulative showed real savings - Wide ranges loaded page by page for minutes with shifting numbers How it solves it: - Cost Optimization now calls the single-shot aggregated endpoint first - Paginated fallback merges pages by date, so days never fragment - Aggregated endpoint gained include_current_utc_day, keeping today's spend visible ## User Flow Before: a user checking daily savings sees near-zero bars on every day while the running total shows real money 1. They open http://localhost:4000/ui/cost-optimization and pick a month-wide range 2. The page fires GET /user/daily/activity once per 1,000 raw rows, hundreds of requests on a busy deployment, and every card keeps shifting while pages stream in 3. They click Per day on the Savings chart 4. A day holding $5.00 of savings renders as three thin bars of $2.00, $2.00, and $1.00, all labeled with the same date, and no bar reaches the real total 5. They switch to Cumulative and watch the line jump by the full $5.83, contradicting the Per day view they just saw After: the same view loads in one request and draws one truthful bar per day 1. They open http://localhost:4000/ui/cost-optimization and pick the same range 2. The page fires one GET /user/daily/activity/aggregated request that returns each day already summed, and the cards land on their final values immediately 3. They click Per day on the Savings chart 4. The $5.00 day renders as a single $5.00 bar, and the daily bars visibly add up to the Cumulative total 5. Spend recorded today keeps appearing through the evening for callers west of UTC, matching what the paginated path already guaranteed ## Relevant issues - Fixes the Cost Optimization Per Day chart drawing one partial bar per API page instead of one bar per day (Pylon #7383) - Switches the page to the aggregated endpoint, one request instead of hundreds, and merges the paginated fallback by date - Adds include_current_utc_day to /user/daily/activity/aggregated so the switch cannot regress the stale-evening fix from #36051 ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5818 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more - [x] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Setup: seeded LiteLLM_DailyUserSpend with 2,500 rows on 2026-08-16 at $0.002 compression savings each ($5.00 total), 500 rows on 2026-08-15 at $0.001 each ($0.50), and one row in today's UTC bucket 2026-08-20 at $0.333, then ran a live proxy on localhost:4000 backed by real Postgres ### Before (fad8116cdc) #### Per Day chart splits a day into per-page partial bars 1. Page the endpoint the way the UI does: `for p in 1 2 3; do curl -s "http://localhost:4000/user/daily/activity?start_date=2026-08-10&end_date=2026-08-17&page=$p&page_size=1000&timezone=420&include_current_utc_day=true" -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234"; done` 2. Observed: page 1 returns date 2026-08-16 with compression_savings_spend 2.0, page 2 returns 2026-08-16 again with 2.0, page 3 returns 2026-08-16 with 1.0 plus 2026-08-15 with 0.5, so the same date arrives three times with partial sums 3. Open http://localhost:4000/ui/cost-optimization, click Per day on the Savings chart: the x axis reads Aug 15, Aug 15, Aug 16, Aug 16, Aug 16, Aug 20, the y axis caps at $2.20, no bar reaches the day's real $5.00, while Total saved reads $5.83 #### Aggregated endpoint ignores include_current_utc_day 1. `curl -s "http://localhost:4000/user/daily/activity/aggregated?start_date=2026-08-15&end_date=2026-08-19&timezone=1020&include_current_utc_day=true" -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234"` (capture ran after 12:00 UTC, so a synthetic offset larger than any real timezone forces the caller-local date behind UTC; real offsets are pinned by the unit tests) 2. Observed dates: 2026-08-16 and 2026-08-15 only, today's UTC bucket is missing even though the flag was sent ### After (27d6b0ddc0) #### Per Day chart splits a day into per-page partial bars 1. `curl -s "http://localhost:4000/user/daily/activity/aggregated?start_date=2026-08-10&end_date=2026-08-17&timezone=420&include_current_utc_day=true" -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234"` 2. Observed: one row per date in a single request, 2026-08-16 with compression_savings_spend 5.0 and 2026-08-15 with 0.5, the numbers the paginated path only reached after all pages 3. Open http://localhost:4000/ui/cost-optimization: the network tab shows exactly one request, GET /user/daily/activity/aggregated?start_date=...&timezone=420&include_current_utc_day=true returning 200, and zero page-by-page calls 4. Click Per day: one bar per day, Aug 15 at $0.50, Aug 16 at $5.00, Aug 20 at $0.33, and the bars sum to the Cumulative $5.83 #### Aggregated endpoint ignores include_current_utc_day 1. Same curl with the flag now returns 2026-08-20, 2026-08-16, and 2026-08-15 2. Dropping the flag from the same command returns 2026-08-16 and 2026-08-15, so historical ranges stay untouched ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - Overlaps open PR #36022, which also merges pages by date inside the same hook - userDailyActivityAggregatedCall takes its two optional trailing args as a named rest tuple: the pagination hook spreads one positional args array into both fetch functions, and this keeps the declared parameter count at four without touching the eslint suppression baseline ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR <!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY --> --- > [!NOTE] > **Medium Risk** > Changes spend-analytics date bounds and how daily metrics are merged for charts. Wrong date extension or merge logic could under- or over-count spend, but auth and write paths are untouched. > > **Overview** > Cost Optimization now loads daily activity from the single-shot aggregated endpoint so Per Day savings charts show one bar per date instead of one partial bar per API page. > > `useDailyActivityRange` prefers `userDailyActivityAggregatedCall`. If pagination still runs, `mergeDailyResults` collapses the same date across pages (metrics and nested breakdowns) so days never fragment. > > `/user/daily/activity/aggregated` now honors `include_current_utc_day` (same live-end UTC-bucket extension as the paginated path) so today’s spend stays visible west of UTC. Historical ranges are unchanged. > > <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit bfe9a693ead9e2a979557e18a65106c7559b8b05. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup> <!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

signals.title: fix(mcp): allow oauth token to target a custom upstream header
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Minted MCP OAuth token always lands on `Authorization` - Upstreams needing a second static credential lose one of them - Tools list comes back empty because upstream rejects the call How it solves it: - New per-server `oauth_token_header` (defaults to `Authorization`) - Minted token owns that header, static `Authorization` rides alongside - Applies to the legacy client and to every v2 resolver grant that mints an upstream token (client credentials, authorization code, token exchange, ID-JAG) ## User Flow Before: an admin whose MCP gateway wants a long-lived platform token on `Authorization` plus an hourly OAuth token on `esb-oauth` cannot get both onto one request, so every tool call fails 1. They add an MCP server with `auth_type: oauth2`, client id/secret, and `static_headers` carrying `Authorization: Bearer <platform token>` and `envlbl: eng` 2. They POST http://litellm-domain/v1/Test_MCP/MCP with `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"tools/list","id":1}` 3. The gateway sees the minted OAuth token on `Authorization` and no platform token, so it answers 401 and the response carries no tools 4. Flipping it around, putting a placeholder on `esb-oauth` instead, the placeholder is sent verbatim because nothing ever writes the minted token there 5. The same failure shows up through POST http://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions and http://litellm-domain/v1/responses when the model tries to call one of that server's tools After: the admin points the minted token at `esb-oauth` and both credentials arrive on the same request 1. They add the same MCP server, this time also setting `oauth_token_header: esb-oauth` 2. They POST http://litellm-domain/v1/Test_MCP/MCP with `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"tools/list","id":1}` 3. The gateway receives `Authorization: Bearer <platform token>`, `esb-oauth: Bearer <minted token>`, and `envlbl: eng`, and answers 200 with the real tool list 4. An hour later the minted token expires, the gateway 401s once, and LiteLLM refetches and retries on `esb-oauth` while `Authorization` stays untouched 5. POST http://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions and http://litellm-domain/v1/responses now execute that server's tools normally ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-3735 ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/<your_test_file>.py -v` - [x] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Shared setup: a live proxy on port 4000 with master key `sk-1234`, plus two stubs standing in for the customer's estate, since no reachable gateway here demands two credentials. One is a fake OAuth token endpoint on :8901 that mints a fresh incrementing `minted-token-N` on every call, so a refetch is objectively visible. The other is a real streamable-HTTP MCP upstream on :8902 (`mcp.server.fastmcp`, tools `echo` and `ping`) wrapped in middleware that records inbound headers and can be armed to answer one 401. Every case drives a real JSON-RPC `initialize` plus `tools/list` through `POST /{alias}/mcp`. ```yaml mcp_servers: esb_custom: # after case url: http://localhost:8902/mcp transport: http auth_type: oauth2 oauth2_flow: client_credentials client_id: litellm-cid client_secret: litellm-secret token_url: http://localhost:8901/token oauth_token_header: esb-oauth static_headers: Authorization: Bearer static-platform-token envlbl: eng esb_baseline: # same thing without oauth_token_header ... # identical, oauth_token_header omitted ``` ```bash litellm --config config.yaml --detailed_debug --port 4000 curl -sX POST http://localhost:4000/esb_custom/mcp \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -H 'Accept: application/json, text/event-stream' \ -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"tools/list","id":1}' ``` ### Before (d2d158f271) #### Two credentials on one request 1. Point the same curl at `esb_baseline`, which is the merge base's only option since `oauth_token_header` does not exist there 2. Headers recorded by the upstream, platform credential gone and nothing on the custom header: ```json {"envlbl": "eng", "authorization": "Bearer minted-token-14"} ``` #### Refetch after a 401 1. Not reachable at the merge base: the minted token can only occupy `Authorization`, so there is no static credential left for a refetch to preserve ### After (9cd4a7bb99) #### Two credentials on one request 1. Run the curl above against `esb_custom` 2. `tools/list` answers with `esb_custom-echo` and `esb_custom-ping`, and the upstream records both credentials: ```json {"authorization": "Bearer static-platform-token", "envlbl": "eng", "esb-oauth": "Bearer minted-token-2"} ``` 3. Same config with `oauth_token_header` omitted still sends the minted token on `authorization` (`Bearer minted-token-3`) and nothing on `esb-oauth`, so the default is unchanged 4. `oauth_token_header: ESB-OAuth` with `static_headers` also claiming `esb-oauth: Bearer static-should-lose` yields `esb-oauth: Bearer minted-token-5`, so the minted token wins its own header with no duplicate 5. `oauth_token_header: " "` falls back to `authorization: Bearer minted-token-6` #### Refetch after a 401 1. Arm the upstream to answer one 401, then run the same curl against `esb_custom` 2. Requests recorded in order, refreshed token staying on the custom header while the platform credential is untouched: ``` 0 {"authorization": "Bearer static-platform-token", "envlbl": "eng", "esb-oauth": "Bearer minted-token-2"} <- 401 1 {"authorization": "Bearer static-platform-token", "envlbl": "eng", "esb-oauth": "Bearer minted-token-7"} 2 {"authorization": "Bearer static-platform-token", "envlbl": "eng", "esb-oauth": "Bearer minted-token-7"} 3 {"authorization": "Bearer static-platform-token", "envlbl": "eng", "esb-oauth": "Bearer minted-token-7"} ``` 3. `tools/list` still returns both tools ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - Not yet exposed as a field in the Admin UI form - Custom header keeps `Bearer` prefix, no prefix knob - Config path verified live, DB-stored value only unit-tested Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/da674df654414dabbc98754a496487d2

signals.title: fix(cost): stop double-billing the Azure AI Model Router flat fee
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Azure AI Foundry Model Router requests are billed the flat routing fee twice - logged spend for those requests is ~2x the real cost How it solves it: - when the token-cost path already folded the flat fee into prompt cost, skip adding it again via additional_costs ## User Flow Before: a developer routing through Azure AI Foundry Model Router sees double the expected spend 1. They send a completion whose model resolves to the Azure Model Router (e.g. `azure-model-router`) 2. `cost_per_token` folds the flat $0.14 per million input-token fee into prompt cost, and `completion_cost` then adds the same fee again through its additional_costs hook 3. Their logged spend is twice the flat fee After: the same request is billed the flat fee once 1. They send the same completion 2. The flat fee is billed a single time through the token-cost path 3. Logged spend matches the real charge ## Relevant issues ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Changes `completion_cost` computes token cost via `azure_ai` `cost_per_token`, which already folds the Model Router flat fee into prompt cost whenever it detects the router from the response `model` or the `request_model` (`is_router_request`). Right after, for `custom_llm_provider == "azure_ai"`, `completion_cost` separately computed the same flat fee through `_get_additional_costs` and summed it into the total, so any request where the token path detected the router was charged the fee twice. This guards the additional_costs branch: when `_is_azure_model_router(model)` or `_is_azure_model_router(request_model_for_cost)` is true, the token path already billed the fee, so additional_costs is left unset. The hidden-params-only path (response carries the underlying model, router known only from `_hidden_params`) is unchanged and still bills the fee once through additional_costs. ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix For a pure `azure-model-router` response with 5000 prompt tokens, `completion_cost` now returns a single flat fee (5000 * rate / 1e6) instead of twice that. Regression test `tests/test_litellm/llms/azure_ai/test_azure_ai_cost_calculator.py::TestAzureModelRouterCostBreakdown::test_additional_costs_in_cost_breakdown` asserts the single-fee total; it fails on the pre-fix code (double) and passes after. All 32 tests in that file pass. ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signals.title: fix(streaming): keep reasoning_items when reassembling a streamed response
signals.text: ## Title fix(streaming): keep reasoning_items when reassembling a streamed response ## Relevant issues None open. Searched issues and PRs (open and closed) for `reasoning_items`, `stream_chunk_builder reasoning` and `encrypted_content`: the only `reasoning_items` PRs are #24690 (merged, the feature that added the field) and its closed predecessor #24557, plus #29761, #33931, #35289, #24803, #30216, #21322, #21313, none of which adds a `reasoning_items` branch to `stream_chunk_builder`. #27765 and #28052 are about a raw `reasoning` delta key from Scaleway, a different field. ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added testing in the `tests/` directory: `tests/test_litellm/test_stream_chunk_builder_reasoning_items.py` - [x] I have added a screenshot of my new test passing locally (output pasted below) - [x] My PR passes all unit tests - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Changes `stream_chunk_builder` dropped `delta.reasoning_items` on both of its paths, so the encrypted reasoning state a provider streams back never reached the assembled assistant message. Two independent reasons, both of which had to be fixed: 1. The simple-text fast path (`litellm/main.py`, the `is_simple_text_stream` scan) checks for `tool_calls`, `function_call`, `reasoning_content`, `thinking_blocks`, `annotations`, `audio`, `images` and `provider_specific_fields`, but not `reasoning_items`. A stream carrying only text plus reasoning items is therefore classified as simple text and returns before any aggregation runs. 2. The full path has an aggregation block for each of those fields but none for `reasoning_items`. The assembled message is not throwaway. `_assemble_complete_response_from_streaming_chunks` caches exactly this response (`litellm/caching/caching_handler.py`), and the Responses API bridge reads `msg["reasoning_items"]` off assistant messages through `_get_reasoning_items` to rebuild its input. A streamed reasoning turn therefore lost its reasoning state and could not be round-tripped, and a cached one replayed without it. The fix adds `reasoning_items` to the fast-path bail-out condition and adds a merge block that concatenates the items from every chunk, matching the existing `annotations` and `images` blocks (a provider may spread items across chunks). ## Reproduction, before the fix ```python import litellm from litellm.completion_extras.litellm_responses_transformation.transformation import ( OpenAiResponsesToChatCompletionStreamIterator as It, ) text_chunk = It.translate_responses_chunk_to_openai_stream( {"type": "response.output_text.delta", "delta": "Hello"} ) done_chunk = It.translate_responses_chunk_to_openai_stream( {"type": "response.completed", "response": {"output": [{"type": "reasoning", "id": "rs_abc123", "encrypted_content": "ENCRYPTED-REASONING-BLOB", "summary": [{"type": "summary_text", "text": "Thinking"}]}], "usage": {"input_tokens": 10, "output_tokens": 5, "total_tokens": 15}}} ) rebuilt = litellm.stream_chunk_builder([text_chunk, done_chunk], messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "hi"}]) print(done_chunk.choices[0].delta.reasoning_items) # the item is streamed print(getattr(rebuilt.choices[0].message, "reasoning_items", None)) # ... and then lost ``` Before: ``` [{'id': 'rs_abc123', 'type': 'reasoning', 'encrypted_content': 'ENCRYPTED-REASONING-BLOB', 'summary': [...]}] None ``` After: both lines print the item. ## Testing New test file, run against the branch: ``` $ pytest tests/test_litellm/test_stream_chunk_builder_reasoning_items.py -q ... [100%] 3 passed in 0.53s ``` Same file run against unpatched `litellm/main.py`, to show it actually catches the bug: ``` FAILED tests/test_litellm/test_stream_chunk_builder_reasoning_items.py::test_reasoning_items_are_merged_across_chunks FAILED tests/test_litellm/test_stream_chunk_builder_reasoning_items.py::test_reasoning_items_survive_a_text_only_stream 2 failed, 1 passed in 0.54s ``` The one test that passes both ways is deliberate: it asserts a stream with no reasoning items does not grow a `reasoning_items` field. Regression control, the surrounding suites, run on the branch and on a pristine tree: ``` $ pytest tests/test_litellm/litellm_core_utils/ tests/test_litellm/test_stream_chunk_builder_annotations.py -q branch: 3 failed, 1641 passed, 1 skipped in 44.05s pristine: 3 failed, 1641 passed, 1 skipped in 37.00s ``` Identical, and the 3 failures are pre-existing on the base branch (`test_bedrock_converse_messages_pt_document_various_formats`, `TestIsBlockedIp::test_blocks_ietf_protocol_assignments_old_oracle_metadata`, `test_logfire_logger_accepts_env_vars_for_base_url`), unrelated to this change. `ruff check litellm/main.py` reports the same 76 pre-existing findings before and after, none of them in the changed lines; `ruff format --check` reports both files already formatted. To be explicit about what I did not do: I validated this at the chunk-reassembly level and with the test suite, not against a live proxy making paid reasoning-model calls, so the end-to-end provider path is not something I can claim to have exercised.

signals.title: feat(ui): serve a dark-mode variant of the LiteLLM logo
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Dark mode shows the sidebar logo inside a white slab - The bundled logo is a JPEG, so it carries no transparency - Its near-black wordmark would vanish if simply made transparent How it solves it: - Ships a transparent dark logo with a light wordmark - `/get_image?theme=dark` serves it, default response untouched - The sidebar renders both and swaps on the `dark` class ## User Flow Before: someone viewing the Admin UI with dark styling on sees the logo boxed in bright white, so the sidebar header looks broken 1. They open http://localhost:4000/ui/ with dark styling applied 2. The sidebar header shows the LiteLLM logo sitting inside a bright white rectangle against the dark sidebar 3. They ask the proxy for a dark logo at http://localhost:4000/get_image?theme=dark and get the same white-background JPEG back After: the logo sits directly on the dark sidebar with no box, and light mode is untouched 1. They open http://localhost:4000/ui/ with dark styling applied 2. The sidebar header shows the mark and a light "LiteLLM" wordmark straight on the dark sidebar, no white rectangle 3. http://localhost:4000/get_image?theme=dark now returns a transparent PNG 4. They turn dark styling off and the original logo comes back exactly as it was 5. An admin who set their own logo through `UI_LOGO_PATH` keeps seeing that logo in both modes ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more - [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Shared setup: a proxy booted from the checkout at each commit, no config changes, listening on `http://localhost:4001` ### Before (d2d158f271) #### Asking the proxy for a dark logo 1. `curl -s -D - -o /tmp/dark.out "http://localhost:4001/get_image?theme=dark"` ``` HTTP/1.1 200 OK content-type: image/jpeg content-length: 24694 ``` 2. `file /tmp/dark.out` ``` /tmp/dark.out: JPEG image data, JFIF standard 1.01, ... 1000x257, components 3 ``` Three components means R, G and B with no alpha, so the white background is baked into every pixel and there is nothing a dark sidebar can show through #### Admin UI sidebar 1. Screenshot pending ### After (f3885f6296) #### Asking the proxy for a dark logo 1. `curl -s -D - -o /tmp/dark.out "http://localhost:4001/get_image?theme=dark"` ``` HTTP/1.1 200 OK content-type: image/png content-length: 35771 ``` 2. `file /tmp/dark.out` ``` /tmp/dark.out: PNG image data, 1000 x 257, 8-bit/color RGBA, non-interlaced ``` RGBA, and the same 1000x257 as the light logo, so swapping between them cannot shift the sidebar header 3. The default response is unchanged: `curl -s -D - -o /tmp/light.out "http://localhost:4001/get_image"` ``` HTTP/1.1 200 OK content-type: image/jpeg content-length: 24694 ``` 4. `cmp /tmp/dark_before.out /tmp/light.out` exits silently, so what this build serves by default is byte for byte what the base served #### Admin UI sidebar 1. Screenshot pending ## Type 🆕 New Feature ## Caveats (if any) - No dark mode toggle ships yet, so this lands ahead of it - A custom `UI_LOGO_PATH` has no dark variant, follow-up PR - Dark asset derived from the JPEG, no vector source available - `?theme=` rejects anything but `light` and `dark` with 422 ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR
signals.author: yuneng-berri

signals.title: fix(agentic loop): return a real stream when code-interpreter interception converts the request
signals.text: ## Title fix(agentic loop): return a real stream when code-interpreter interception converts the request ## Relevant issues Fixes #37652 ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added testing in the `tests/` directory: two cases in `tests/test_litellm/litellm_core_utils/test_chat_completion_agentic_loop.py` - [x] I have added a screenshot of my new test passing locally (output pasted below) - [x] My PR passes all unit tests - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Root cause `code_interpreter_interception` converts a `stream: true` chat request into a non-streaming call, marks it with `_code_interpreter_interception_converted_stream`, and then asks the agentic-loop dispatcher to hand the result back in streamed form. `_wrap_response_as_fake_stream` (`litellm/litellm_core_utils/chat_completion_agentic_loop.py`) did that with `convert_model_response_to_streaming`, which returns a single `ModelResponseStream` object. That is one chunk, not a stream: it has no `__aiter__`. The caller iterates it, so: ``` TypeError: 'async for' requires an object with __aiter__ method, got ModelResponseStream ``` Two consequences, both of which the issue reports: 1. `litellm/main.py` guards the result with `if isinstance(response, CustomStreamWrapper)`, and a `ModelResponseStream` fails that check, so the object is returned to the proxy untouched and blows up on iteration. This fires on both call sites, which is why a plain assistant reply with no tool call is enough: the no-follow-up path at the end of `maybe_run_chat_completion_agentic_loop` converts the original response the same way. 2. The chunk-shaped object is what reaches the response cache. A later request that reads that entry has `delta` where `message` is expected, hence the reported `KeyError: 'message'` inside `convert_to_model_response_object`. The existing `cast("ModelResponse | CustomStreamWrapper", ...)` on the return value was simply not true. ## Fix Wrap the response in a `CustomStreamWrapper` over `MockResponseIterator`, which is the pattern already used elsewhere in the repo for exactly this (replaying an assembled response as a stream): see `bedrock_guardrails.py`, `tool_permission.py`, `model_armor.py` and six other guardrail hooks. `MockResponseIterator` calls the same `convert_model_response_to_streaming` internally, so the chunk content is unchanged; it is now delivered through an object that is actually iterable, and `main.py`'s `isinstance` branch recognises it. `_wrap_response_as_fake_stream` needs `model`, `custom_llm_provider` and `logging_obj` to build the wrapper. All three are already in scope at both call sites. If `logging_obj` is not a real logging object the helper returns the response unchanged, so this can never turn a working call into a new exception. Not folded in: the interception path still cannot deliver token-by-token output, since the underlying call really is non-streaming. This makes the response a well-formed single-chunk SSE stream rather than a 500, which is option (a) in the issue at the granularity the current design allows. ## Testing Two new tests in the existing `tests/test_litellm/litellm_core_utils/test_chat_completion_agentic_loop.py`, one per affected path (after a tool-call follow-up, and with no tool call at all). Both assert the result is a `CustomStreamWrapper` and then actually `async for` over it and check the reassembled text. ``` $ pytest tests/test_litellm/litellm_core_utils/test_chat_completion_agentic_loop.py -q ....... [100%] 7 passed in 0.77s ``` The same file against unpatched `chat_completion_agentic_loop.py`: ``` E AssertionError: assert False E + where False = isinstance(ModelResponseStream(id='chatcmpl-9d7f8aff-...', object='chat.completion.chunk', ...), CustomStreamWrapper) FAILED ... ::test_converted_stream_result_is_async_iterable_after_the_loop_runs FAILED ... ::test_converted_stream_result_is_async_iterable_without_a_tool_call 2 failed, 5 passed in 0.64s ``` Removing the `isinstance` assertion and going straight to the iteration reproduces the reported error verbatim on unpatched source: ``` returned type: ModelResponseStream has __aiter__: False async for RAISED TypeError: 'async for' requires an object with __aiter__ method, got ModelResponseStream ``` Regression control, the whole surrounding area, branch versus a pristine tree: ``` $ pytest tests/test_litellm/integrations/code_interpreter_interception tests/test_litellm/litellm_core_utils/ -q branch: 3 failed, 1694 passed, 1 skipped in 45.44s pristine: 3 failed, 1692 passed, 1 skipped in 37.98s ``` Exactly the two new tests, no other movement. The 3 failures are pre-existing on the base branch (`test_bedrock_converse_messages_pt_document_various_formats`, `TestIsBlockedIp::test_blocks_ietf_protocol_assignments_old_oracle_metadata`, `test_logfire_logger_accepts_env_vars_for_base_url`) and unrelated. `ruff check` reports the identical 31 pre-existing findings on both files before and after, none in the changed lines; `ruff format --check` reports both files already formatted. To be explicit about what I did not do: I validated this through the dispatcher and the test suite, not against a live proxy with a real sandboxed code-interpreter run, so the end-to-end SSE delivery to a client is not something I can claim to have exercised. I also could not reproduce the cache half of the issue directly; the fix addresses it by never producing the chunk-shaped object in the first place, which is the object the reporter traced the `KeyError: 'message'` to.

signals.title: fix(model_prices): consolidate eleven open registry audits into one changeset
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Eleven open PRs all edit the same cost map - Each one conflicts with the others on merge - Older branches revert fields the base gained since - Two of them carry deprecation dates the docs contradict How it solves it: - One branch carrying all eleven PRs' registry data - Merged per model entry, per field, onto current staging - Contradicted Gemini / text-embedding-004 dates dropped - Fresh 2026-08-20 audit adds Gemini, Voyage, Perplexity entries - Same tests as the source PRs, all passing This replaces #35911, #36017, #36080, #36113, #36188, #36444, #37029, #37252, #37632, #37512 and #37536. Those can be closed once this lands; nothing in this branch is new registry research beyond re-verifying what they claimed, plus the audit findings below ### What was merged, per source PR | Source PR | Entries carried in | Notes | | --- | --- | --- | | #35911 | 4 | Vertex AI MaaS per-token rates | | #36017 | 3 | `bedrock_mantle/openai.gpt-5.6-{sol,terra,luna}` 1M context | | #36080 | 66 | provider `deprecation_date` backfill (minus `text-embedding-004`, see below) | | #36113 | 3 | `gemini-3.1-flash-lite-image` pricing + capability fields, plus its test | | #36188 | 86 | OpenAI/Anthropic `deprecation_date` refresh (minus 4 Gemini rows, see below) | | #36444 | 3 | `gpt-5.6-cyber`, `daybreak-red-latest`, `daybreak-blue-latest`, plus its test | | #37029 | 16 | missing OpenAI models, stale limits | | #37252 | 3 | `openrouter/claude-opus-5`, `deepseek-v4-pro` | | #37632 | 17 | Mistral `*-latest` refresh, Z.ai GLM 5.2, Mistral OCR 4.1, xAI + Cohere deprecation dates | | #37512 | 20 | Fireworks serverless models, re-verified row by row (see below) | | #37536 | 15 | Bedrock batch rates for Claude 4.5 and Qwen, plus its test | Five conflicts arose where two PRs edited the same field; in every case the newer PR's value is a strict superset and won: ``` gpt-5.6-cyber / daybreak-red-latest / daybreak-blue-latest #36444: mode=responses, supported_endpoints=[/v1/responses] #37029: mode=chat, supported_endpoints=[/v1/chat/completions, /v1/responses] + supports_computer_use (cyber and red only), supports_parallel_function_calling, source <-- kept xai/grok-code-fast-1, xai/grok-code-fast-1-0825 #36080 and #37632 set deprecation_date=2026-05-15 identically ``` The merge is field-level, not entry-level, on purpose. #36017 was opened before staging gained tiered `*_above_272k_tokens` pricing for the same three `bedrock_mantle` models; replacing its entries wholesale would have silently deleted those four fields per model. Only the fields each PR actually changed relative to its own merge base are applied After merging current `litellm_internal_staging` back in, `mistral/zai-glm-5-2` (which landed on staging via #37110 with `max_input_tokens` 1048576 and `supports_reasoning: true`, plus a `mistral/glm-5-2` alias) was dropped from this branch so staging's version and its pinning test stand, which also removes the duplicate JSON key the merge produced. A field-level audit of the final delta then caught the one place the consolidation itself deleted a field: refreshing `mistral/mistral-small-latest` to Small 4.0 copied the `mistral/mistral-small-2603` entry shape and dropped `supports_vision: true`, even though the Small 4 model card states "Accepts both text and image input". Restored on `-latest`, added on `-2603` which had the same gap, and pinned by `tests/test_litellm/test_mistral_small_4_0_model_metadata.py`. Test-quality gate fixes on the two carried-in test files: dropped the `sys.path.insert` no-op in the Gemini image pricing test, and switched the GPT-5.6 Cyber cost test to `monkeypatch.setenv` / `monkeypatch.setattr` so it no longer leaks `LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP` and `litellm.model_cost` into later tests A second capability gap turned up in the same sweep, this time carried in from the source PR rather than created by the merge: #37029 sets `supports_computer_use` on `gpt-5.6-cyber` and `daybreak-red-latest` but not on `daybreak-blue-latest`, even though OpenAI lists `computer_use` among the supported tools for Daybreak Blue and for `gpt-5.6-sol`, the snapshot the blue alias resolves to. Both entries now carry the flag, which stops `/model/info` and the capability gates from reporting blue as unable to use computer tools while its siblings can. `gpt-5.6-sol` was already in the registry and untouched by any of the eleven PRs, so fixing only the alias would have left the alias and its own snapshot disagreeing. `tests/test_litellm/test_daybreak_model_metadata.py` pins the family's capability contract and that agreement ### New registry research (2026-08-20 audit run) #### Gemini / Vertex (https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/pricing, https://cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/pricing) - Added `gemini/gemini-3.5-live-translate-preview` (`gemini-3.5-live-translate-preview` on the AI Studio pricing page and in the Gemini 3 model list): audio in $3.50/1M, audio out $21.00/1M, `/v1/realtime`, audio-only in and out. Google publishes no input/output token limits for this model, so `max_input_tokens` / `max_output_tokens` are deliberately omitted rather than guessed. - Fixed a wrong audio rate on Gemini 3.5 Flash (`gemini/gemini-3.5-flash`, `gemini-3.5-flash`, `vertex_ai/gemini-3.5-flash`): the registry had `input_cost_per_audio_token` $1.00/1M and `input_cost_per_audio_token_priority` $1.80/1M. Both pages price 3.5 Flash audio at the *same* rate as text (AI Studio shows a single "Input price $1.50", Vertex shows "Input (text, image, video, audio) Global $1.50" and Priority "$2.70"), so these become $1.50/1M and $2.70/1M. - Added the batch and flex tiers for the same three entries, which were missing entirely: batch input $0.75/1M, batch output $4.50/1M, flex input $0.75/1M, flex output $4.50/1M. Flex context caching is $0.08/1M on the AI Studio page and $0.075/1M on the Vertex page, so `cache_read_input_token_cost_flex` follows whichever page the entry's `source` points at. #### Voyage (https://docs.voyageai.com/docs/pricing, plus the model tables on the embeddings / contextualized-chunk / multimodal doc pages for context length) Six missing models, all `mode: embedding`: | Entry | input $/1M | context | dim | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `voyage/voyage-4-large` | 0.12 | 32,000 | 1024 | | `voyage/voyage-4` | 0.06 | 32,000 | 1024 | | `voyage/voyage-4-lite` | 0.02 | 32,000 | 1024 | | `voyage/voyage-code-4` | 0.12 | 32,000 | 1024 | | `voyage/voyage-context-4` | 0.12 | 120,000 | 1024 | | `voyage/voyage-multimodal-3.5` | 0.12 | 32,000 | 1024 | `voyage-4-nano` is listed in the docs as an open-weight Hugging Face model with no row on the pricing page, so it is not added. `voyage-multimodal-3.5` also has a per-pixel price ($0.60/1B pixels) with no registry field for it, so only the per-token rate is recorded #### Perplexity (https://docs.perplexity.ai/getting-started/pricing, https://docs.perplexity.ai/api-reference/contextualized-embeddings-post) Two missing contextualized-embedding models, which have their own `/v1/contextualizedembeddings` endpoint and their own prices: - `perplexity/pplx-embed-context-v1-0.6b`: $0.008/1M, 32K tokens per document, 1024 dims - `perplexity/pplx-embed-context-v1-4b`: $0.05/1M, 32K tokens per document, 2560 dims #### Absorbed: #37512 (Fireworks serverless models) Registry-data-only PR. All 20 entries carried in. Prices re-verified row by row against https://docs.fireworks.ai/serverless/pricing (input / cache-read / output per 1M): Kimi K3 3.00/0.30/15.00, Kimi K3 Fast 4.50/0.45/22.50, Kimi K3 US 3.30/0.33/16.50, DeepSeek V4 Flash (0731) 0.14/0.028/0.28, GLM 5.2 Fast and GLM 5.2 Fast US 2.10/0.21/6.60, Qwen 3.8 Max 2.00/0.25/6.00, Muse Glimmer 30B 0.35/0.04/1.50, Nemotron 3.5 Lightning 30B A3B 0.05/0.01/0.20, Nemotron 3 Ultra 0.60/0.12/2.40. All match Context lengths and the vision / tool flags were re-checked against each model's own page on https://app.fireworks.ai/models/fireworks/<model>, which publishes `contextLength`, `supportsImageInput` and `supportsTools`: kimi-k3 1,048,576 + image true, deepseek-v4-flash-0731 1,048,576 + image false, glm-5p2 1,048,576 + image false, muse-glimmer-30b 131,072 + image true, nemotron-lightning-3p5-30b-a3b and nemotron-3-ultra-nvfp4 262,144 + image false. The `-fast` / `-us` SKUs are routers with no model page; they inherit the base model's verified context length One deviation from #37512: its 65,536 output cap for `qwen3p8-max` is confirmed by no official Fireworks source (the models API reports `contextLength: 0`, and a live completion accepts an arbitrary `max_tokens` with no validation error), so `max_output_tokens` / `max_tokens` stay off that entry. The input side is published: the model page (fireworks.ai/models/fireworks/qwen3p8-max) states a 262k context length, so both `qwen3p8-max` entries carry `max_input_tokens: 262144`. Its price and its vision / tool flags are confirmed and are carried in. `max_output_tokens` is not published anywhere by Fireworks for any of these models; the values carried in match what the registry already uses for the same base models #### Absorbed: #37536 (Bedrock batch rates for Claude 4.5 and Qwen) Registry-data-only PR, plus its `tests/test_litellm/test_bedrock_batch_pricing.py`. 15 entries gain `input_cost_per_token_batches` / `output_cost_per_token_batches`. Every added value is exactly 50% of that same entry's on-demand rate, which is what AWS documents: https://aws.amazon.com/bedrock/pricing/ states batch inference for select FMs is "at a 50% lower price compared to on-demand inference pricing", and https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/batch-inference-supported.html lists `anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0`, `anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929-v1:0` and `qwen.qwen3-235b-a22b-2507-v1:0` as batch-supported ### Deprecation dates that were dropped as unverifiable Cross-checking every `deprecation_date` in this branch against the raw provider tables found five values that the official docs contradict, all of them from the two deprecation-focused PRs: | Entry | PR claimed | https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/deprecations says | This PR | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `gemini/gemini-embedding-001` | 2026-07-14 (#36188) | shutdown May 14, 2028 | keeps 2028-05-14 | | `gemini/gemini-2.5-pro` | 2026-10-16 (#36188) | "No shutdown date announced" | no date | | `gemini/gemini-2.5-flash` | 2026-10-16 (#36188) | "No shutdown date announced" | no date | | `gemini/gemini-2.5-flash-lite` | 2026-10-16 (#36188) | "No shutdown date announced" | no date | | `text-embedding-004` | 2027-04-01 (#36080) | shutdown January 14, 2026 | keeps 2026-01-14 | The 2026-07-14 and 2026-10-16 values look like the *deprecation announcement* column, not the shutdown column, so #36188 should not be merged as-is even if this consolidation is rejected `gpt-audio-mini-2025-12-15` and `gpt-realtime-mini-2025-12-15` keep the 2027-01-20 date from #36188 on the strength of the family-level statement on https://platform.openai.com/docs/deprecations ("legacy audio, realtime, and transcription model families and snapshots ... removal from the API on January 20, 2027"); the individual snapshots are not listed as rows there, only the `gpt-audio-mini` / `gpt-realtime-mini` families and the `-2025-10-06` snapshots. Say the word and I'll drop those two too ### Checked, nothing changed - **Cohere**: https://docs.cohere.com/docs/models lists `command-a-plus-05-2026`, `command-a-reasoning-08-2025`, `command-a-translate-08-2025`, `command-a-vision-07-2025`, `rerank-v4.0-fast` and `rerank-v4.0-pro`, none of which are in the registry, but https://cohere.com/pricing renders its price table client-side and the per-model doc pages carry no per-token rates, so nothing could be added without guessing. Left out on purpose. - **Anthropic** (https://docs.claude.com/en/docs/about-claude/pricing), **OpenAI** (https://platform.openai.com/docs/pricing), **DeepSeek** (https://api-docs.deepseek.com/quick_start/pricing), **Groq** (https://console.groq.com/docs/models): current model lists and the newest entries' rates and limits match the registry already. - Open registry PRs left alone as not registry-data changes or not Devin-owned rolling scope: #28170 (Telnyx provider, new provider code), #36233 (Vertex Chirp 3 gRPC/WebSocket transport), #29898 (bedrock-invoke output_format behavior), #30383 (router cost backfill logic). ### Sources Every value in this branch comes from a source PR that cited it; the pages re-checked while consolidating and auditing are: - https://platform.openai.com/docs/deprecations - https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/deprecations - https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/pricing - https://cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/pricing - https://docs.claude.com/en/docs/about-claude/model-deprecations - https://docs.x.ai/developers/migration/may-15-retirement - https://docs.cohere.com/docs/deprecations - https://docs.mistral.ai/getting-started/models/models_overview/ - https://docs.voyageai.com/docs/pricing - https://docs.perplexity.ai/getting-started/pricing - https://docs.fireworks.ai/serverless/pricing - https://aws.amazon.com/bedrock/pricing/ ## User Flow Before: a proxy admin cannot tell which of eleven open cost-map PRs to merge, and merging more than one of them by hand conflicts 1. They open https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pulls and see eleven open PRs all editing `model_prices_and_context_window.json`. 2. They merge one; the next one now conflicts on the same JSON and has to be rebased by hand. 3. If they merge #36017 after staging gained tiered `bedrock_mantle` pricing, `GET https://litellm-domain/model/info` stops reporting the above-272k rates for `bedrock_mantle/openai.gpt-5.6-sol` and long-context spend is undercharged. 4. If they merge #36188, `GET https://litellm-domain/model/info` reports `gemini-2.5-pro` as retiring on 2026-10-16 and `gemini-embedding-001` on 2026-07-14, and neither matches Google's docs. 5. If they merge #37029, `GET https://litellm-domain/model/info` comes back with `supports_computer_use: true` on `gpt-5.6-cyber` and `daybreak-red-latest` but no such field on `daybreak-blue-latest`, so a client that picks models off that field sends computer-use work to red and skips blue even though OpenAI ships the tool on both. 6. They send a 200k-token prompt to `mistral/codestral-2508`, it goes out over the wire, and Mistral answers with a context-length error. After: one PR carries all of it, and the numbers match the provider docs 1. They merge this PR alone and close the other eleven. 2. `GET https://litellm-domain/model/info` reports the refreshed entries, including `bedrock_mantle/openai.gpt-5.6-sol` with both its 1M context window and its above-272k rates. 3. `gemini-2.5-pro` and `gemini-2.5-flash` come back with no deprecation date, `gemini-embedding-001` with 2028-05-14, matching https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/deprecations. 4. `daybreak-blue-latest` comes back with `supports_computer_use: true` alongside `gpt-5.6-cyber` and `daybreak-red-latest`, and so does `gpt-5.6-sol`, the snapshot the blue alias resolves to, so the same client now sends computer-use work to blue as well. 5. That same 200k-token prompt to `mistral/codestral-2508` is turned away by the gateway before it leaves, once `enable_pre_call_checks` is on, rather than travelling to Mistral to be refused there. 6. `xai/grok-4`, `command-r`, `rerank-english-v2.0` and the other newly annotated entries carry the `deprecation_date` that `GET https://litellm-domain/model/deprecations` (#26900) surfaces. 7. Requests to `voyage/voyage-4`, the new Fireworks serverless models, and Bedrock batch jobs on Claude 4.5 are priced from the new entries instead of logging $0 spend at https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs. ## Relevant issues Supports #26900. Supersedes #35911, #36017, #36080, #36113, #36188, #36444, #37029, #37252, #37632, #37512, #37536 ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5896 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more - [x] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (5/5 on this PR) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix A proxy booted at the tip `5c9ed89301` from a clean worktree, with `LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True` and a config-only model list, no database attached. Provider calls below are real billed requests against real provider APIs, not fixtures. Merge-base values come from `git show 2f23cf5701:model_prices_and_context_window.json`, and where behavior is at stake the diff itself is cited rather than a second run. ### Registry integrity at the tip 1. `git diff --name-only 2f23cf5701..5c9ed89301` lists the two registry JSON files and five test files, and nothing else. No production code is touched, so every behavior change below is driven by the data alone. 2. `python3 ci_cd/check_files_match.py` prints `Passed! Files model_prices_and_context_window.json and litellm/model_prices_and_context_window_backup.json match.` 3. `uv run --no-sync python ci_cd/generate_model_prices_schema.py` regenerates the schema and `git status` reports no change to it, so the merged data introduces no new field shape. 4. Entry-level delta against the merge base: 40 added, 0 removed, 45 changed, and no field is dropped from any changed entry. ### Prices reach the API surface `GET /v1/model/info` against the tip proxy, with the merge-base value from `git show 2f23cf5701:model_prices_and_context_window.json` alongside: | Entry and field | Base `2f23cf5701` | Tip `5c9ed89301`, served live | |---|---|---| | `fireworks_ai/deepseek-v4-flash-0731` input | not in registry | 1.4e-07 | | `fireworks_ai/deepseek-v4-flash-0731` output | not in registry | 2.8e-07 | | `voyage/voyage-4` input | not in registry | 6e-08 | | `fireworks_ai/qwen3p8-max` max_input_tokens | not in registry | 262144 | | `gemini-3.5-flash` audio input | 1e-06 | 1.5e-06 | | `mistral/mistral-small-latest` input | 6e-08 | 1.5e-07 | ### Billing matches the merged rates, on real calls **Fireworks `deepseek-v4-flash-0731`,** an entry this PR adds. Usage came back 11 prompt / 5 completion. Expected `11 x 1.4e-07 + 5 x 2.8e-07 = 2.94e-06`, and `x-litellm-response-cost` read `2.94e-06`, with the input and output breakdown headers at `1.54e-06` and `1.4e-06`. **Gemini audio.** Usage came back 13 audio + 8 text prompt, 7 completion, response body `service_tier: "default"`. Expected input `13 x 1.5e-06 + 8 x 1.5e-06 = 3.15e-05` and output `7 x 9e-06 = 6.3e-05`, total `9.45e-05`, and the cost header matched exactly. ### Deprecation reporting picks up the new dates `GET /model/deprecations` at the tip: ```json {"deprecated":[{"model_name":"grok-4","litellm_model":"xai/grok-4","deprecation_date":"2026-05-15","days_until_deprecation":-98,"status":"deprecated","litellm_provider":"xai"}],"imminent":[],"upcoming":[{"model_name":"gemini-3.5-flash","litellm_model":"gemini-3.5-flash","deprecation_date":"2027-05-19","days_until_deprecation":271,"status":"upcoming","litellm_provider":"vertex_ai-language-models"}],"warn_within_days":30,"checked_at":"2026-08-21T00:17:24.114313Z"} ``` Routing is unaffected either way, since `deprecation_date` only feeds this report and its optional alert. ### Priority audio pricing behaves identically before and after Worth showing explicitly, because the priority audio rate moves in this PR and does not take effect. A live call with `"service_tier":"priority"` at the tip, with the body confirming `service_tier: "priority"` came back honored, billed 13 audio + 8 text prompt tokens at `4.11e-05`. That equals `13 x 1.5e-06 + 8 x 2.7e-06`, so text billed at the priority rate while audio fell back to the standard rate rather than the `2.7e-06` priority audio rate this PR sets. That fallback is unchanged by this PR, and the diff proves it rather than merely suggesting it: 1. `git diff 2f23cf5701..5c9ed89301 -- litellm/types/utils.py litellm/litellm_core_utils/llm_cost_calc/utils.py` is empty. Both files are byte-identical across the range, so neither the `ModelInfo` field list nor `_get_cost_per_unit` moves. 2. `git show 2f23cf5701:model_prices_and_context_window.json | grep -c input_cost_per_audio_token_priority` prints `6`. The merge base already carried the key on all six gemini entries, at `1.8e-06`. 3. `input_cost_per_audio_token_priority` is declared in neither commit's `litellm/types/utils.py`, while twelve sibling `_priority` keys are, so it never reaches `ModelInfo` on either side. The path is therefore data-only and the same fallback runs before and after: the rate was unread at `1.8e-06` and is unread at `2.7e-06`, and no bill changes. Wiring the field through the type is a real fix, but it moves money on that path and belongs in its own PR, so it is recorded under Caveats instead. ### Gemini dates re-read from the raw docs table 1. `curl -s https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/deprecations | python3 -c "<parse every <tr>>"` 2. Output rows: ``` gemini-2.5-pro | June 17, 2025 | No shutdown date announced | gemini-2.5-flash | June 17, 2025 | No shutdown date announced | gemini-2.5-flash-lite | July 22, 2025 | No shutdown date announced | gemini-embedding-001 | July 14, 2025 | May 14, 2028 | gemini-embedding-2 text-embedding-004 | April 9, 2024 | January 14, 2026 | gemini-embedding-2 ``` ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ✅ Test ## Caveats (if any) - `gpt-audio-mini-2025-12-15` / `gpt-realtime-mini-2025-12-15` dates rest on OpenAI's family-level statement - `qwen3p8-max` output caps omitted, so `max_output_tokens` and `max_tokens` stay unset on both `fireworks_ai/qwen3p8-max` and `fireworks_ai/accounts/fireworks/models/qwen3p8-max`. Fireworks publishes no output cap for it, and a live check confirmed it enforces none: `max_tokens` of 65537 and of 999999 both came back 200. `max_input_tokens` 262144 is kept per the model page - `voyage-multimodal-3.5` per-pixel rate has no registry field, only per-token recorded - Newest Cohere models left out; no official per-token rates published - `gemini-3.5-live-translate-preview` token limits unpublished, so omitted - Several existing entries gain a `deprecation_date` that is already in the past: the Cohere `command*` and `rerank-*-v2.0` families, and the xAI slugs caught by the May 15 retirement. Routing does not change, since `deprecation_date` only feeds the deprecation report and its optional alert, so the visible effect is those models moving into the `deprecated` bucket and one alert firing on the next check for anyone who has that alerting turned on - The xAI dates land on alias slugs (`xai/grok-4`, `xai/grok-4-latest`, `xai/grok-3-latest`, `xai/grok-code-fast`, `xai/grok-code-fast-1-0825`) whose retirement is inferred from the snapshot each resolves to. xAI's retirement page lists the snapshots themselves, `grok-4-0709`, `grok-3` and `grok-code-fast-1`, and the registry already carried 2026-05-15 on those before this PR - `mistral/mistral-small-latest` bills at Small 4.0 rates now, 6e-08 to 1.5e-07 in and 1.8e-07 to 6e-07 out, because the alias moved upstream rather than because a rate was repriced. Recorded spend on that alias rises to match, and `mistral/codestral-latest` falls about 70% for the same reason - `mistral/codestral-2508` is the only entry whose limits move down, 256000 to 128000 across `max_input_tokens` / `max_output_tokens` / `max_tokens`, matching the model card. With `enable_pre_call_checks` on, the router now filters that deployment for prompts above 128k instead of forwarding them; Mistral rejects those prompts today anyway, so nothing that works now stops working. Some third-party listings still say 256k, so the vendor page is the tiebreaker here - The `input_cost_per_audio_token_priority` bump on the `gemini-3.5-flash` entries, 1.8e-06 to 2.7e-06, has no effect on billing today, and that is worth knowing before anyone relies on it. The key is not declared in `ModelInfoBase`, so `get_model_info` never copies it into `ModelInfo`, and `_get_cost_per_unit` then strips the `_priority` suffix and quietly bills audio at the standard rate. Twelve other `_priority` variants are declared, this one is not. The gap is not new here: the merge base already carried the key on all six gemini entries at 1.8e-06, so it was equally unread before this PR, which only updates the number to match Google's page. A live priority call confirmed the fallback in both directions, and wiring the field through the type belongs in its own change since it moves real money on that path ### Final Attestation - [ ] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/a711a2830ea0445ca2220c2338634354
