signals.title: fix(logging): bound the shared logging executor backlog
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Proxy memory on ECS climbs for days until the task restarts - Sync logging callbacks queue on an unbounded shared executor - Each queued task pins its request/response payload in memory How it solves it: - Caps the shared logging executor at 10,000 queued-plus-running tasks - Past the cap, new logging tasks are dropped with a rate-limited warning - Cap is tunable via `LOGGING_EXECUTOR_MAX_PENDING_TASKS` ## User Flow Before: an operator running the proxy on ECS watches per-task memory climb until the task restarts 1. They deploy the proxy with logging callbacks enabled and see task memory start at 30-40% 2. Under steady traffic, CloudWatch memory utilization climbs over days to 55-60% and never plateaus 3. At about 60% the task restarts on its own, memory drops back to baseline, and the sawtooth repeats After: the same deployment levels off instead of climbing without bound 1. They deploy the proxy with logging callbacks enabled and see task memory start at 30-40% 2. Under steady traffic, memory utilization levels off at a stable ceiling 3. If log delivery ever falls so far behind that entries must be skipped, the task log shows a warning naming `LOGGING_EXECUTOR_MAX_PENDING_TASKS` so they can raise the cap ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5386 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more - [x] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Shared setup: `flood.py` floods the shared logging executor the same way request logging does, with one slow sync callback and 200k submissions, then prints the backlog size and peak RSS ```python import resource import sys import time from litellm.litellm_core_utils.thread_pool_executor import executor def slow_callback(payload: str) -> None: time.sleep(120) for _ in range(200_000): executor.submit(slow_callback, "x" * 10_000) peak_rss_mb = resource.getrusage(resource.RUSAGE_SELF).ru_maxrss / (1024 * 1024 if sys.platform == "darwin" else 1024) print("queued tasks:", executor._work_queue.qsize()) print("peak rss mb:", round(peak_rss_mb)) ``` ### Before (cde134488c) 1. `LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True python flood.py` 2. Observed output: the backlog holds every submission and memory grows with it ``` queued tasks: 199900 peak rss mb: 2720 ``` ### After (29c77e81f8) 1. `LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True python flood.py` 2. Observed output: the backlog stops at the cap, memory stays flat, and a warning names the knob ``` 15:01:37 - LiteLLM:WARNING: thread_pool_executor.py:71 - litellm logging executor backlog is full (max_pending_tasks=10000); dropped 1 logging task(s) since the last warning. Set LOGGING_EXECUTOR_MAX_PENDING_TASKS to raise the cap. queued tasks: 9900 peak rss mb: 329 ``` ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - Past the cap, sync logging callbacks are shed, not backpressured - Proxy spend tracking is async and never rides this executor - The sync SDK passthrough flush shares the same cap - A shed submission logs a count, not a per-call-site failure line - Async callbacks already have their own bounded queue and are unaffected ## Review notes Shedding is only safe if nothing waits on what the executor hands back, so every caller of the shared executor was audited: `litellm/utils.py`, `litellm/litellm_core_utils/litellm_logging.py` (both dispatch paths and the async success hook), `litellm/litellm_core_utils/streaming_handler.py`, `litellm/interactions/streaming_iterator.py`, `litellm/responses/streaming_iterator.py`, `litellm/passthrough/main.py`, `litellm/proxy/guardrails/guardrail_endpoints.py`, and the AssemblyAI passthrough handler. All of them submit and move on. The call sites that do read a future (`batch_completion`, `asyncify`, `dual_cache`, presidio, the batches handlers, and the guardrail test-run endpoint) each build their own private `ThreadPoolExecutor` and never touch this one, so the cap cannot strand a caller The drop warning is emitted through a logger injected into the executor rather than an in-function import of `verbose_logger`, which also lets the rate-limiting test capture real log records instead of patching the module What rides this executor is worth being precise about, since shedding cost data would be a very different tradeoff from shedding log lines. On the proxy, passthrough streaming always takes the async route (`common_request_processing.py` passes `route_type="allm_passthrough_route"`, and `passthrough/main.py:191` gates on that flag), so its spend flush goes through `asyncio.create_task` at `passthrough/main.py:454` and never touches this executor. Spend rows reach the database through `_ProxyDBLogger`, which implements `async_log_success_event` and no sync counterpart, so the shed path cannot drop a billing record. The one spend-adjacent submission that does ride it is `passthrough/main.py:405`, reachable only from the sync SDK, and even there `success_handler` already skips `CustomLogger` callbacks when the call type is pass-through and defers them to the async handler The pre-fix behavior was not "this work always ran" either. An unbounded queue only runs its backlog if the process lives long enough, and the repro above shows 199,900 tasks pinning 2.7 GB right before the ECS task hits its memory limit and restarts, discarding all of them. Shedding a bounded few is strictly less loss than losing the whole backlog to a restart Every test here was mutation checked. Removing admission control, dropping the slot release, disabling the interval check, forgetting to reset the drop counter, returning an uncancelled future, and defaulting to the wrong logger each turn at least one test red ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/5e39dc1f0a084d5ead9ef6fe376e843b Requested by: @yassin-berriai

signals.title: fix(auth): cache team member default budget as a typed model (LIT-5311)
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Team member default budget never lands in Redis - Redis write fails on raw datetime columns - Error line repeats in logs, every pod re-queries DB How it solves it: - Cache a validated `LiteLLM_BudgetTable`, not the raw row - Pass `model_type` on both read and write ## User Flow Before: a team admin with Redis-backed auth caching sees a recurring cache error, and every pod keeps hitting the database for the team's per-member budget 1. The admin runs the proxy with `enable_redis_auth_cache: true` and a Redis cache backend 2. They send POST http://localhost:4000/team/new with `"team_member_budget": 25`, which comes back with a team id 3. They mint a key for a member of that team via POST http://localhost:4000/key/generate and send a POST http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions with it 4. The call succeeds, but the proxy logs `LiteLLM Redis Caching: async set() - Got exception from REDIS Object of type datetime is not JSON serializable` 5. Nothing is stored in Redis for that budget, so each pod repeats the database lookup once per cache window and logs the error again After: the same flow is quiet, and the budget is shared across pods through Redis 1. Same setup, same team, same key 2. They send the same POST http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions 3. The call succeeds and no Redis serialization error appears in the logs 4. Redis now holds the budget as JSON, so other pods read it from the shared cache instead of the database ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5311 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/<your_test_file>.py -v`. If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Shared setup, identical on both sides: local Redis on 6379, `litellm/proxy/dev_config.yaml` plus ```yaml litellm_settings: enable_redis_auth_cache: true cache: true cache_params: type: redis host: 127.0.0.1 port: 6379 ``` Team and key created once against the same database, with a real Anthropic call: ```bash curl -s -X POST http://localhost:4000/team/new -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"team_alias":"lit5311-team","team_member_budget":25,"models":["anthropic-haiku-4-5"]}' # -> team_id 0e225030-..., metadata {"team_member_budget_id": "team-lit5311-team-budget-0cfdc66a..."} ``` ### Before (3a31331435) 1. Mint a key for a team member and make a live call ```bash K=$(curl -s -X POST http://localhost:4000/key/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"team_id":"0e225030-ccf2-4701-bbf1-db05763bc2e1","user_id":"lit5311-user2"}' | jq -r .key) curl -s -X POST http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer $K" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model":"anthropic-haiku-4-5","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"say hi in 3 words"}]}' ``` ``` {"id":"chatcmpl-08d600fc-90da-4a41-b7fe-7b6678c15287","model":"anthropic-haiku-4-5",...} ``` 2. The proxy log carries the reported failure ``` 20:16:02 - LiteLLM:ERROR: redis_cache.py:762 - LiteLLM Redis Caching: async set() - Got exception from REDIS Object of type datetime is not JSON serializable, Writing value={'budget_id': 'team-lit5311-team-budget-0cfdc66ac73c44dd80df22ea170a65c0', 'max_budget': 25.0, ..., 'created_at': datetime.datetime(2026, 8, 20, 20, 15, 37, 289000, tzinfo=TzInfo(0)), ...} ``` 3. Redis holds nothing for that budget ```bash redis-cli keys 'team_member_default_budget*' ``` ``` (empty) ``` ### After (b85546fdf3) 1. Same key mint and live call ```bash K=$(curl -s -X POST http://localhost:4000/key/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"team_id":"0e225030-ccf2-4701-bbf1-db05763bc2e1","user_id":"lit5311-user3"}' | jq -r .key) curl -s -X POST http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer $K" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model":"anthropic-haiku-4-5","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"say hi in 3 words"}]}' ``` ``` Hey there friend. ``` 2. No serialization error in the log ```bash grep -c "Object of type datetime is not JSON serializable" litellm.log ``` ``` 0 ``` 3. Redis now carries the budget as JSON ```bash redis-cli keys 'team_member_default_budget*' redis-cli get team_member_default_budget:team-lit5311-team-budget-0cfdc66ac73c44dd80df22ea170a65c0 ``` ``` team_member_default_budget:team-lit5311-team-budget-0cfdc66ac73c44dd80df22ea170a65c0 {"budget_id": "team-lit5311-team-budget-0cfdc66ac73c44dd80df22ea170a65c0", "soft_budget": null, "max_budget": 25.0, "max_parallel_requests": null, "tpm_limit": null, "rpm_limit": null, "model_max_budget": null, "budget_duration": null, "allowed_models": []} ``` ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - Redis entries now carry only user-facing budget fields ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/225c12d857dd4668b01f73235a1705c1 Requested by: @yassin-berriai

signals.title: feat(sso): source generic OIDC user claims from ID/access token when UserInfo is incomplete
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - ADFS UserInfo returns only `sub`, so SSO profiles are empty - No username, email or display name for those users - Team claims carried only in the tokens were unreachable How it solves it: - New opt-in `GENERIC_INCLUDE_TOKEN_CLAIMS` merges token claims into UserInfo - Precedence: UserInfo, then id_token, then access token - All `GENERIC_USER_*_ATTRIBUTE` mappings apply to token claims - Works in both the PKCE and non-PKCE login flows ## User Flow Before: an admin whose IdP only returns `sub` from UserInfo signs in successfully but lands in the Admin UI as a nameless, team-less account 1. They open https://litellm-domain/ui/ and click through the SSO login at their IdP 2. Login succeeds and they are redirected back to https://litellm-domain/ui/ 3. The user badge shows no email and no display name 4. https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=users lists the account with an empty user id and an empty email, so admins cannot tell who it is 5. https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=teams shows no team membership, because the team claim their IdP puts in the tokens was never read After: the same login produces a full profile, with the user id, email, display name and teams their tokens carry 1. The proxy admin sets `GENERIC_INCLUDE_TOKEN_CLAIMS=true`, points `GENERIC_USER_ID_ATTRIBUTE` / `GENERIC_USER_EMAIL_ATTRIBUTE` at the claim names their tokens carry (for example `upn` and `email`), and restarts the proxy 2. The user opens https://litellm-domain/ui/ and clicks through the same SSO login 3. Login succeeds and they are redirected back to https://litellm-domain/ui/ 4. The user badge now shows their real display name and email 5. https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=users lists the account with a real user id and email 6. https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=teams shows the teams their token claim names Their role is unchanged by this PR in both directions, and the Screenshots section shows why: it already resolved from the access token before this change With the toggle unset, every one of these steps behaves exactly as it does today, which the Before and default-configuration runs below demonstrate byte for byte ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-4825 ## Review notes Greptile's one finding was that the new PKCE test replaced two `SSOAuthenticationHandler` methods with `patch.object`, which the repo CLAUDE.md calls out as an anti-pattern. That test now injects dependencies instead: the PKCE verifier cache and the httpx transport are the only doubles, and the request is a real Starlette `Request`, so `prepare_token_exchange_parameters`, `_pkce_token_exchange`, the userinfo fetch and the claim merge all run for real. The rework also makes the test stronger rather than merely tidier. It now asserts that the cached verifier reaches the token endpoint, that `sub` still comes from UserInfo, and that `email`, which exists only inside the access token, reaches the resulting `CustomOpenID`. Four mutations of `ui_sso.py` were checked against it: disabling the opt-in branch, dropping the bearer-credential filter on `received_response`, inverting the merge precedence, and ignoring the exchange-response access token. All four fail the reworked test, and two of them (disabling the opt-in branch, ignoring the exchange-response access token) passed the old one On trusting token claims: `_decode_sso_token_claims` decodes without verifying the signature, and that is deliberate rather than an oversight. Both tokens come from the authorization-code exchange, a direct TLS back-channel POST to the operator-configured token endpoint authenticated with the client secret or PKCE, never from anything the browser hands us. OIDC Core section 3.1.3.7 clause 6 explicitly permits skipping ID token signature validation on that path. It is also not a new trust surface, and the runs below make that concrete rather than theoretical: `user_role` comes back as `proxy_admin` in all three, including at the merge base where this feature does not exist, because `process_sso_jwt_access_token` already decodes the same access token the same way and already derives the role from `GENERIC_ROLE_MAPPINGS_GROUP_CLAIM`. The merge changes which claims the existing attribute mappings can see, not who is trusted to assert them Two claims in an earlier revision of this description were wrong and the runs below corrected them. It said the role was missing before the fix and arrives with it; the role was never missing. It also implied the group claim was unreachable; the group claim already reached the role mapping, and what was actually unreachable was the identity attributes and the team claim ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/<your_test_file>.py -v` - [x] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (5/5 at `b5c5f178`) `code-quality` and `documentation` were red until https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm-docs/pull/969 documented `GENERIC_INCLUDE_TOKEN_CLAIMS`, because `tests/documentation_tests/test_env_keys.py` checks env vars against litellm-docs **main**. That PR has merged and both jobs are green on `b5c5f178` ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix The condition this PR fixes is an IdP whose UserInfo response is thin while its tokens carry the real claims. That does not require ADFS specifically, so these runs use a local OIDC provider configured to behave that way: `/userinfo` returns `{"sub": "adfs-subject-0001"}` and nothing else, while `/token` returns signed JWTs carrying `upn`, `email`, `display_name`, `groups` and `team_ids`. All three runs drive the real login with curl, against a real proxy on port 4000 backed by Postgres, and read the result out of the user table, which is what `/ui/?page=users` and `/ui/?page=teams` render. Shared setup, exported before each run: ``` DATABASE_URL=postgresql://postgres:pw@127.0.0.1:6396/litellm PROXY_BASE_URL=http://localhost:4000 GENERIC_CLIENT_ID=litellm-proxy GENERIC_CLIENT_SECRET=stub-client-secret GENERIC_AUTHORIZATION_ENDPOINT=http://localhost:9700/authorize GENERIC_TOKEN_ENDPOINT=http://localhost:9700/token GENERIC_USERINFO_ENDPOINT=http://localhost:9700/userinfo GENERIC_SCOPE="openid profile email" GENERIC_USER_ID_ATTRIBUTE=upn GENERIC_USER_EMAIL_ATTRIBUTE=email GENERIC_USER_DISPLAY_NAME_ATTRIBUTE=display_name GENERIC_ROLE_MAPPINGS_GROUP_CLAIM=groups GENERIC_ROLE_MAPPINGS_ROLES="{'proxy_admin': ['litellm-admins']}" ``` The team mapping lives in the database rather than the environment, seeded once as `{"team_mappings": {"team_ids_jwt_field": "team_ids"}}` in `LiteLLM_SSOConfig`, with a `platform-eng` team created so membership has somewhere to land. Every run was launched from a directory outside the repo, so litellm's import-time `load_dotenv()` could not hand any run the checkout's `.env`. Each run prints that check, the exact tree it loaded, a UTC start and end stamp, and a liveliness probe at both ends, so a run that silently straddled two proxies, or that overlapped someone else's cleanup on a shared machine, would be visible rather than averaged in. All three runs below come from one uninterrupted pass between 22:20:38 and 22:21:04 UTC. A note on the hashes, since the branch was rebased after these runs. The capture was taken with the base at `cde134488c` and the PR at `4311b55704`. Both have since moved: the merge base is now `d8a57a1a2b` and the head is `b5c5f178`. The runs still hold, and it is checkable rather than a matter of trust. `git diff cde134488c d8a57a1a2b -- litellm/proxy/management_endpoints/ui_sso.py` is empty, so the file under test is byte-identical across the two bases and the Before run still describes the current base. `git diff 4311b55704 b5c5f178` restricted to the two changed files is likewise empty, so the After runs describe the current head. Re-running would cost a full IdP rig cycle to reproduce the same numbers. The IdP condition, identical for all three runs: ``` $ curl -s http://localhost:9700/userinfo {"sub": "adfs-subject-0001"} ``` ### Before (cde134488c) 1. Confirm the environment is clean and the proxy is the one under test ``` $ python -c "import litellm, os; print(os.environ.get('OPENAI_API_KEY') is not None, os.environ.get('ANTHROPIC_API_KEY') is not None, os.path.exists('.env'))" False False False code under test: .../scratchpad/rig/base/litellm/__init__.py times this tree mentions GENERIC_INCLUDE_TOKEN_CLAIMS: 0 Uvicorn running on http://0.0.0.0:4000 leg START (UTC): 22:20:38 liveliness: "I'm alive!" ``` 2. Drive the real SSO login ``` $ curl -s -c jar.txt -b jar.txt -L -o /dev/null -w 'final_url=%{url_effective} http_code=%{http_code}\n' \ http://localhost:4000/sso/key/generate final_url=http://localhost:4000/ui/?login=success http_code=200 ``` 3. Read the account the login created, which is what `/ui/?page=users` lists ``` $ psql -c "SELECT user_id, user_email, user_role FROM \"LiteLLM_UserTable\" ..." user_id|user_email|user_role <empty>|<null>|proxy_admin ``` 4. Read the team membership, which is what `/ui/?page=teams` shows ``` user_id|teams: <empty>| ``` 5. The identity the proxy actually resolved ``` generic result: id=None email=None first_name=None last_name=None display_name=None picture=None provider=None team_ids=[] user_role=<LitellmUserRoles.PROXY_ADMIN: 'proxy_admin'> extra_fields=None liveliness at end of run: "I'm alive!" leg END (UTC): 22:20:40 ``` The account is unusable: no user id, no email, no display name, no team. Note `proxy_admin` is already present here, at the merge base, with this feature absent. ### After (b5c5f178) First run, default configuration, `GENERIC_INCLUDE_TOKEN_CLAIMS` unset. This is the regression check. 1. Confirm the tree under test now contains the feature ``` code under test: .../worktrees/c9-pr37696/litellm/__init__.py times this tree mentions GENERIC_INCLUDE_TOKEN_CLAIMS: 1 GENERIC_INCLUDE_TOKEN_CLAIMS=false Uvicorn running on http://0.0.0.0:4000 leg START (UTC): 22:20:50 liveliness: "I'm alive!" ``` 2. Drive the same login ``` final_url=http://localhost:4000/ui/?login=success http_code=200 ``` 3. Account, team membership, and resolved identity ``` user_id|user_email|user_role <empty>|<null>|proxy_admin user_id|teams: <empty>| generic result: id=None email=None first_name=None last_name=None display_name=None picture=None provider=None team_ids=[] user_role=<LitellmUserRoles.PROXY_ADMIN: 'proxy_admin'> extra_fields=None liveliness at end of run: "I'm alive!" leg END (UTC): 22:20:52 ``` Identical to Before in every field, which is the evidence for the opt-in claim. Second run, same code, `GENERIC_INCLUDE_TOKEN_CLAIMS=true`. The flag is the only thing that changed. 4. Confirm the flag is the only difference ``` code under test: .../worktrees/c9-pr37696/litellm/__init__.py times this tree mentions GENERIC_INCLUDE_TOKEN_CLAIMS: 1 GENERIC_INCLUDE_TOKEN_CLAIMS=true Uvicorn running on http://0.0.0.0:4000 leg START (UTC): 22:21:02 liveliness: "I'm alive!" ``` 5. Drive the same login ``` final_url=http://localhost:4000/ui/?login=success http_code=200 ``` 6. The account now carries the token-sourced identity ``` user_id|user_email|user_role dana.reyes@corp.example.com|dana.reyes@corp.example.com|proxy_admin ``` 7. Team membership now resolves from the token claim ``` user_id|teams: dana.reyes@corp.example.com|platform-eng ``` 8. The resolved identity ``` generic result: id='dana.reyes@corp.example.com' email='dana.reyes@corp.example.com' first_name=None last_name=None display_name='Dana Reyes' picture=None provider=None team_ids=['platform-eng'] user_role=<LitellmUserRoles.PROXY_ADMIN: 'proxy_admin'> extra_fields=None liveliness at end of run: "I'm alive!" leg END (UTC): 22:21:04 ``` `id`, `email`, `display_name` and `team_ids` all went from empty to the values carried only in the tokens, and the user table now has a real user id, a real email and `platform-eng` membership. `user_role` is `proxy_admin` in all three runs, unchanged, which is the point made in Review notes about this PR not widening what the proxy trusts. ## Type 🆕 New Feature ## Caveats (if any) - Opt-in: default configuration matches the merge base exactly - Token claims merge shallowly, per top-level claim name - Signatures are not re-verified; see Review notes for why - Role already resolved from the access token, so it is unaffected - Documented in litellm-docs #969, now merged ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/51be51a556c74eb3aac303c1ae76f668 Requested by: @yassin-berriai

signals.title: fix(token_counter): stop large token counts from blocking the proxy event loop
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Low-entropy text stalls token counting for tens of seconds - The count runs on the proxy event loop, blocking everything - Liveness and readiness probes time out, replicas drop How it solves it: - Encode long text in bounded chunks, not one call - Caps tiktoken's quadratic merge cost, keeps counting linear - Async paths now count in a worker thread, off the loop - Chunk-size setting is bounded, so misconfiguration cannot break counting - Solves two of the ticket's three call sites, mitigates the third ## User Flow Before: a developer sending a large multimodal agent request gets it served, but the gateway stops answering anything else for the better part of a minute, and the replica gets pulled out of rotation 1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages with a Claude model and a large body whose text contains long runs of a single repeated character (dot leaders and padding from extracted form text) 2. The request sits there with no response for tens of seconds 3. Every other request against the same replica, including a plain GET https://litellm-domain/health/liveliness, hangs for that whole window instead of returning in milliseconds, and some are refused outright once the connection backlog fills 4. The platform team sees the pod fail its liveness and readiness probes with `context deadline exceeded`, CPU pinned at exactly 1.0 vCPU, no OOM and no restart, and unrelated in-flight calls surface bogus `litellm.Timeout: Connection timed out. Timeout passed=30.0, time taken=0.001 seconds` errors 5. POST https://litellm-domain/utils/token_counter on a body of the same shape stalls the replica the same way 6. Their only workaround is `litellm_settings: disable_token_counter: true`, which gives up token-based context-window pre-filtering and makes POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages/count_tokens return 503 whenever the provider's own count API fails After: the same request is served promptly and the replica keeps answering everything else while it is in flight 1. They send the same POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages with the same body 2. The request comes back in seconds, with the same token totals as before 3. GET https://litellm-domain/health/liveliness answers in about a millisecond throughout, so probes pass and the replica stays in rotation 4. POST https://litellm-domain/utils/token_counter on the same body returns in under a tenth of a second and never stalls concurrent traffic 5. No spurious 30s timeout errors appear on concurrent requests, and no `disable_token_counter` workaround is needed ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5426 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more - [x] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Shared setup: a live proxy on port 4010 with `router_settings: {enable_pre_call_checks: true}` and one direct Anthropic deployment, so the router's context-window pre-call check runs on the request path: ```yaml model_list: - model_name: anthropic-sonnet-4-6 litellm_params: model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6 api_key: os.environ/ANTHROPIC_API_KEY router_settings: enable_pre_call_checks: true general_settings: master_key: sk-1234 ``` ```bash PYTHONPATH=. python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config lit5426_config.yaml --port 4010 python -c "import json; print(json.dumps({'model':'anthropic-sonnet-4-6','max_tokens':4,'messages':[{'role':'user','content':'A'*400000}]}))" > payload2.json python -c "import json; print(json.dumps({'model':'gpt-3.5-turbo','prompt':'A'*400000}))" > payload3.json ``` Cases 2 and 3 each send one request in the background and fire 150 liveness probes at 0.2s intervals while it is in flight: ```bash curl -s -o resp.json -w 'request: %{http_code} in %{time_total}s\n' --max-time 180 -X POST "$URL" -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-1234' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data @"$PAYLOAD" & req=$! for i in $(seq 1 150); do (curl -s -o /dev/null -w "liveliness[$i]: %{http_code} in %{time_total}s\n" --max-time 45 http://localhost:4010/health/liveliness > "probes/$i" 2>&1) & sleep 0.2; done wait $req ``` ### Before (cde134488c) #### Case 1: SDK token counting (the ticket's own repro) 1. Ran: ```bash LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True python -c " import time, litellm t0 = time.perf_counter() n = litellm.token_counter(model='us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6', messages=[{'role': 'user', 'content': 'A' * 262144}]) print(f'{n} tokens in {time.perf_counter() - t0:.1f}s')" ``` 2. Output: ```text 32775 tokens in 18.8s ``` #### Case 2: liveness probes while one large POST /v1/messages is in flight 1. Ran the shared case commands against `http://localhost:4010/v1/messages` with `payload2.json` 2. Output: ```text case2: 200 in 46.104470s liveliness[1]: 200 in 41.384411s liveliness[2]: 200 in 41.184932s liveliness[3]: 200 in 40.963598s ... liveliness[150]: 000 in 7.787908s ``` 3. 129 of 150 probes eventually answered 200 with a median of 25.27s and a max of 41.38s; the other 21 were refused outright once the accept backlog filled behind the blocked loop 4. The request itself hit real Anthropic and was billed: ```text {"model":"anthropic-sonnet-4-6","id":"msg_011CeEndVd8gwwGSFEHK7Had","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"A."}],"stop_reason":"max_tokens","usage":{"input_tokens":133343,"output_tokens":4}} ``` #### Case 3: liveness probes while one large POST /utils/token_counter is in flight 1. Ran the shared case commands against `http://localhost:4010/utils/token_counter` with `payload3.json` 2. Output: ```text case3: 200 in 38.921233s liveliness[1]: 200 in 38.915943s liveliness[2]: 200 in 38.703705s liveliness[3]: 200 in 38.486415s ... liveliness[150]: 000 in 7.782811s ``` 3. 128 of 150 probes answered 200 with a median of 22.93s and a max of 38.92s, and 22 were refused 4. Response: ```text {"total_tokens":50000,"request_model":"gpt-3.5-turbo","model_used":"gpt-3.5-turbo","tokenizer_type":"openai_tokenizer","error":false} ``` ### After (db6887794c) #### Case 1: SDK token counting (the ticket's own repro) 1. Ran the same command as above 2. Output: ```text 32775 tokens in 0.1s ``` #### Case 2: liveness probes while one large POST /v1/messages is in flight 1. Ran the shared case commands against `http://localhost:4010/v1/messages` with `payload2.json` 2. Output: ```text case2: 200 in 4.823487s liveliness[1]: 200 in 0.102209s liveliness[2]: 200 in 0.001002s liveliness[3]: 200 in 0.001014s ... liveliness[150]: 200 in 0.001108s ``` 3. All 150 probes answered 200, median 0.0010s, max 0.1022s 4. The request hit real Anthropic again and reported the same input token total as Before, so nothing about the count changed: ```text {"model":"anthropic-sonnet-4-6","id":"msg_011CeEpLgWjZiiYFmwsU3V7M","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"A."}],"stop_reason":"max_tokens","usage":{"input_tokens":133343,"output_tokens":4}} ``` #### Case 3: liveness probes while one large POST /utils/token_counter is in flight 1. Ran the shared case commands against `http://localhost:4010/utils/token_counter` with `payload3.json` 2. Output: ```text case3: 200 in 0.098131s liveliness[1]: 200 in 0.002550s liveliness[2]: 200 in 0.000841s liveliness[3]: 200 in 0.000957s ... liveliness[150]: 200 in 0.000993s ``` 3. All 150 probes answered 200, median 0.0010s, max 0.0042s 4. Response reports the same 50000 tokens as Before: ```text {"total_tokens":50000,"request_model":"gpt-3.5-turbo","model_used":"gpt-3.5-turbo","tokenizer_type":"openai_tokenizer","error":false} ``` ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Review notes ### What this covers, and what it does not LIT-5426 names three call sites. Two are now genuinely off the event loop and this PR solves them: the router context-window pre-call check, and the local fallback behind `/utils/token_counter` and `/v1/messages/count_tokens`. The proof above measures exactly those: 150 of 150 liveness probes answering at a 1.0ms median where the merge base managed 129 of 150 at a 25.27s median with 21 refused outright. The third, the cost-calculator fallback that runs when a response carries no usage, is mitigated rather than solved. `_async_success_handler_body` calls `_success_handler_helper_fn` directly, with no executor and no thread hop, so that count still runs on the loop. Chunking takes it from over five minutes (killed) to 0.49s on a 2.4MB single-character payload, which is bounded and linear but not zero. That 0.49s is a bench number for the encode itself, not a proxy measurement: unlike the two cases above, I did not instrument that path against a live proxy. I did not take the third because moving it off-loop means making the async logging path async through `completion_cost`, which reaches well beyond token counting and belongs in its own change ### Why the encode moved off the loop Chunking on its own only shortens the stall. The whole chunk loop still ran on the event loop thread, so a big enough payload kept monopolizing it, which is the ticket's actual premise. Measured on this machine, a single `encode` of `"A" * 200000` blocks the loop for 8.26s: a competing coroutine's largest scheduling gap is 8263ms. Running the same encode through a worker thread leaves the max gap at 2.66ms and lets the competitor run 587k times, which confirms tiktoken releases the GIL for its Rust encode and that a thread offload genuinely helps here So the async paths now count off-loop, through the repo's existing `asyncify` helper. `/utils/token_counter` awaits `asyncify(litellm.token_counter)`, resolved at call time so the public seam callers and tests already patch keeps working, and the router's `async_get_healthy_deployments` counts off-loop and passes the result into `_pre_call_checks` rather than letting it count inline. `_pre_call_checks` keeps its own lazy inline count for the sync entry points, but the async caller sets `skip_inline_token_count`, so a count that fails off-loop is never retried on the loop; it just leaves the deployments unfiltered, which is what a failed count already did. For the same reason the pre-count resolves each deployment's context window exactly the way `_pre_call_checks` does, skipping ones it cannot map rather than letting the first unmappable deployment hide a limit declared by a later one. Sync callers such as `completion_cost` are unchanged: there is no loop to protect there, and chunking already bounds their cost ### Why the chunk size is bounded on both ends The lower bound closes more than a wrong number. A configured `-1` produced no chunks at all and silently reported **zero tokens**, and a zero count is not cosmetic: every downstream consumer of it, the context-window pre-call filter and the budget and rate-limit accounting, then sees a free request, so a single mistyped environment variable quietly stopped the proxy enforcing its limits. The clamp closes that as well as the performance hole The chunk size still needs a ceiling even with the offload, because the cost is linear in the chunk size: on a 2.4MB single-character payload it is 0.28s at 512, 0.49s at 1024, 1.8s at 4096 and 13.3s at 16384. `TIKTOKEN_ENCODE_CHUNK_SIZE_CHARS` is therefore clamped to [1, 4096]. Zero used to raise `ValueError` from `range()` and a negative value produced no chunks at all, silently reporting zero tokens and quietly disabling every context-window, trimming and accounting decision downstream. Out-of-range and unparseable values now warn and fall back to 1024 ## Caveats (if any) - Chunking drifts ~0.06% on natural text over 1KB - Cost-calculator fallback still counts on the loop, bounded to ~0.5s - Sync callers still count on the calling thread - Chunk sizes above 4096 are clamped, with a warning - Anthropic-native `image` blocks still break counting, ticketed separately ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/e1ccb43093544b83b0bebcf711acd91b Requested by: @yassin-berriai

signals.title: fix(scim): keep the matched user_id on POST /Users email match
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - SCIM POST /Users renamed a matched user's user_id - Keys, rosters, memberships and spend kept the old id - Later SCIM calls for that user failed with 409 How it solves it: - Keep the matched row's user_id, only update its fields - Team roster sync now runs against that stable id - SCIM response returns the stable id to the IdP ## User Flow Before: an admin whose users signed in through OIDC SSO first, then turned on SCIM user provisioning, loses those users along with their keys and team history as soon as the IdP sends a userName that differs from the OIDC sub 1. The admin creates a team with POST http://localhost:4000/team/new for `team_id: team-x` 2. A user already exists from SSO: POST http://localhost:4000/user/new with `user_id: oidc-sub-x` and `user_email: user@example.com`, added to `team-x`, holding a virtual key from POST http://localhost:4000/key/generate 3. The IdP starts provisioning: POST http://localhost:4000/scim/v2/Users with that same email but `userName: scim-username-x`, which comes back `200` with `"id": "scim-username-x"` 4. GET http://localhost:4000/user/info?user_id=oidc-sub-x now returns `404 User oidc-sub-x not found`, so the admin cannot find the user they had 5. GET http://localhost:4000/key/list?user_id=oidc-sub-x still lists the virtual key under the id that no longer exists, and GET http://localhost:4000/team/info?team_id=team-x still shows `oidc-sub-x` on the roster 6. When the IdP sends the next update for that user, POST http://localhost:4000/scim/v2/Users returns `409 User already exists with username: scim-username-x`, so group changes from the IdP stop landing and the stale roster entry stays After: the same flow links the SSO user to SCIM without moving them, so their keys, roster entry and spend stay attached and later IdP updates apply 1. Same team creation with POST http://localhost:4000/team/new for `team_id: team-x` 2. Same pre-existing SSO user `oidc-sub-x` with `user@example.com`, on `team-x`, holding a virtual key 3. The IdP starts provisioning: POST http://localhost:4000/scim/v2/Users with that same email and `userName: scim-username-x`, which comes back `200` with `"id": "oidc-sub-x"`, the id the admin already knows 4. GET http://localhost:4000/user/info?user_id=oidc-sub-x returns `200` with the user, their team and their key 5. GET http://localhost:4000/key/list?user_id=oidc-sub-x lists the key under a user that still exists, and the key keeps working on POST http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions 6. When the IdP later drops the user from the group, POST http://localhost:4000/scim/v2/Users with `"groups": []` returns `200` and GET http://localhost:4000/team/info?team_id=team-x no longer lists them ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5382 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more - [x] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Live proxy on localhost:4000 with `litellm/proxy/dev_config.yaml`, real Anthropic calls through `anthropic-haiku-4-5`. Shared setup for both sides, with `SUF` set to `before2` or `after2`: ```bash M="Authorization: Bearer sk-1234"; J="Content-Type: application/json" curl -s -X POST localhost:4000/team/new -H "$M" -H "$J" -d "{\"team_id\":\"team-$SUF\",\"team_alias\":\"team-$SUF\"}" curl -s -X POST localhost:4000/user/new -H "$M" -H "$J" -d "{\"user_id\":\"oidc-sub-$SUF\",\"user_email\":\"lit5382-$SUF@example.com\",\"user_role\":\"internal_user\",\"teams\":[\"team-$SUF\"],\"auto_create_key\":false}" curl -s -X POST localhost:4000/team/member_add -H "$M" -H "$J" -d "{\"team_id\":\"team-$SUF\",\"member\":{\"user_id\":\"oidc-sub-$SUF\",\"role\":\"user\"}}" KEY=$(curl -s -X POST localhost:4000/key/generate -H "$M" -H "$J" -d "{\"user_id\":\"oidc-sub-$SUF\",\"models\":[\"anthropic-haiku-4-5\"]}" | jq -r .key) ``` ### Before (3a31331435) #### SCIM provisioning by email drops the pre-existing SSO user 1. The existing key works before SCIM runs ```bash curl -s -X POST localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "$J" \ -d '{"model":"anthropic-haiku-4-5","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"say hi in 3 words"}]}' | jq -c '{model, content: .choices[0].message.content}' ``` ``` {"model":"anthropic-haiku-4-5","content":"Hi there, friend."} ``` 2. The IdP provisions the same email with a different userName ```bash curl -s -X POST localhost:4000/scim/v2/Users -H "$M" -H "$J" \ -d '{"schemas":["urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:core:2.0:User"],"userName":"scim-username-before2","name":{"givenName":"Lit","familyName":"Test"},"emails":[{"value":"lit5382-before2@example.com","primary":true}],"groups":[{"value":"team-before2"}]}' | jq -c '{id, userName, groups}' ``` ``` {"id":"scim-username-before2","userName":"lit5382-before2@example.com","groups":[{"value":"team-before2","display":"team-before2","type":"direct"}]} ``` 3. The pre-existing user is gone ```bash curl -s -o /tmp/b1 -w 'HTTP %{http_code}\n' "localhost:4000/user/info?user_id=oidc-sub-before2" -H "$M"; cat /tmp/b1 ``` ``` HTTP 404 {"error":{"message":"User oidc-sub-before2 not found","type":"internal_server_error","param":"None","code":"404"}} ``` 4. Their key and roster entry still point at the id that no longer exists ```bash curl -s "localhost:4000/key/list?user_id=oidc-sub-before2&return_full_object=true" -H "$M" | jq -c '[.keys[] | {user_id, team_id}]' curl -s "localhost:4000/team/info?team_id=team-before2" -H "$M" | jq -c '.team_info.members_with_roles' ``` ``` [{"user_id":"oidc-sub-before2","team_id":null}] [{"user_id":"default_user_id","user_email":null,"role":"admin"},{"user_id":"oidc-sub-before2","user_email":"lit5382-before2@example.com","role":"user"}] ``` #### Follow-up group change from the IdP fails and the roster stays stale 1. The IdP drops the user from the group ```bash curl -s -o /tmp/b2 -w 'HTTP %{http_code}\n' -X POST localhost:4000/scim/v2/Users -H "$M" -H "$J" \ -d '{"schemas":["urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:core:2.0:User"],"userName":"scim-username-before2","name":{"givenName":"Lit","familyName":"Test"},"emails":[{"value":"lit5382-before2@example.com","primary":true}],"groups":[]}'; cat /tmp/b2 ``` ``` HTTP 409 {"detail":{"error":"User already exists with username: scim-username-before2"}} ``` 2. The stale roster entry survives ```bash curl -s "localhost:4000/team/info?team_id=team-before2" -H "$M" | jq -c '.team_info.members_with_roles' ``` ``` [{"user_id":"default_user_id","user_email":null,"role":"admin"},{"user_id":"oidc-sub-before2","user_email":"lit5382-before2@example.com","role":"user"}] ``` ### After (294ba31562) #### SCIM provisioning by email keeps the pre-existing SSO user 1. The existing key works before SCIM runs ```bash curl -s -X POST localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "$J" \ -d '{"model":"anthropic-haiku-4-5","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"say hi in 3 words"}]}' | jq -c '{model, content: .choices[0].message.content}' ``` ``` {"model":"anthropic-haiku-4-5","content":"Hi there friend"} ``` 2. The IdP provisions the same email with a different userName, and the response carries the stable id ```bash curl -s -X POST localhost:4000/scim/v2/Users -H "$M" -H "$J" \ -d '{"schemas":["urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:core:2.0:User"],"userName":"scim-username-after2","name":{"givenName":"Lit","familyName":"Test"},"emails":[{"value":"lit5382-after2@example.com","primary":true}],"groups":[{"value":"team-after2"}]}' | jq -c '{id, userName, groups}' ``` ``` {"id":"oidc-sub-after2","userName":"lit5382-after2@example.com","groups":[{"value":"team-after2","display":"team-after2","type":"direct"}]} ``` 3. The user, their key and their roster entry are all intact ```bash curl -s "localhost:4000/user/info?user_id=oidc-sub-after2" -H "$M" | jq -c '{user_id: .user_info.user_id, email: .user_info.user_email, teams: .user_info.teams, keys: [.keys[].token][0:3]}' curl -s "localhost:4000/team/info?team_id=team-after2" -H "$M" | jq -c '.team_info.members_with_roles' curl -s "localhost:4000/key/list?user_id=oidc-sub-after2&return_full_object=true" -H "$M" | jq -c '[.keys[] | {user_id, team_id}]' ``` ``` {"user_id":"oidc-sub-after2","email":"lit5382-after2@example.com","teams":["team-after2"],"keys":["2f2bcb3f147fcc8b23674df8bbb895657a42ead943df848684661312fcf8976e"]} [{"user_id":"default_user_id","user_email":null,"role":"admin"},{"user_id":"oidc-sub-after2","user_email":"lit5382-after2@example.com","role":"user"}] [{"user_id":"oidc-sub-after2","team_id":null}] ``` 4. The original key still serves traffic ```bash curl -s -X POST localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "$J" \ -d '{"model":"anthropic-haiku-4-5","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"say hi in 3 words"}]}' | jq -c '{content: .choices[0].message.content, error: .error.message}' ``` ``` {"content":"Hello, how are you?","error":null} ``` #### Follow-up group change from the IdP applies 1. The IdP drops the user from the group ```bash curl -s -X POST localhost:4000/scim/v2/Users -H "$M" -H "$J" \ -d '{"schemas":["urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:core:2.0:User"],"userName":"scim-username-after2","name":{"givenName":"Lit","familyName":"Test"},"emails":[{"value":"lit5382-after2@example.com","primary":true}],"groups":[]}' | jq -c '{id, groups}' ``` ``` {"id":"oidc-sub-after2","groups":[]} ``` 2. The roster reflects the removal ```bash curl -s "localhost:4000/team/info?team_id=team-after2" -H "$M" | jq -c '.team_info.members_with_roles' ``` ``` [{"user_id":"default_user_id","user_email":null,"role":"admin"}] ``` ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - SCIM id for a matched email is the pre-existing id, not userName - GET /scim/v2/Users?filter=userName eq ... still resolves that user - Fix is forward looking; already re-keyed rows need manual repair Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/6f215c427423479bb5e0552db889d12e Requested by: @yassin-berriai

signals.title: perf(prometheus): render /metrics off the event loop and coalesce concurrent scrapes
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - `/metrics` rendered the registry on the event loop - Big registries stalled every other in-flight request - Concurrent scrapes each re-rendered the whole registry - `?name[]=` was silently ignored, returning everything How it solves it: - Render and gzip in a worker thread - Share one render across scrapes wanting the same output - Stream the payload in 64 KiB chunks - Apply the `name[]` filter that was being dropped ## User Flow Before: an operator running Prometheus against a busy proxy sees unrelated requests stall every scrape interval 1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions traffic across many models, plus requests with misspelled model names, growing the exposition payload 2. Their scraper sends GET https://litellm-domain/metrics every 15s, several scrapers at once 3. During each scrape, GET https://litellm-domain/health/liveliness that normally answers in under 1 ms takes up to 252 ms, and chat completions in flight slow down by the same amount 4. Overlapping scrapes make it worse, because each one pays the full serialization cost again 5. They narrow a scrape with GET https://litellm-domain/metrics?name[]=litellm_proxy_total_requests_metric_total to cut the payload, and get the entire registry back anyway After: the same scrapes return the same payload while the rest of the proxy keeps answering at normal speed 1. They send the same traffic mix to POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions 2. The same scrapers send GET https://litellm-domain/metrics every 15s 3. GET https://litellm-domain/health/liveliness stays in the low milliseconds through the scrape, 15 ms at worst, and chat completions are unaffected 4. Overlapping scrapes finish in half the wall time, since scrapers asking for the same payload share one render instead of repeating it, and each still gets a complete, fresh payload 5. GET https://litellm-domain/metrics?name[]=litellm_proxy_total_requests_metric_total now returns only that metric 6. `Accept-Encoding: gzip` behaves exactly as before, so existing scrape configs need no change ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5357 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more - [x] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Shared setup, run identically for both sides against a proxy started with `python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config <config> --port 4099` and `callbacks: ["prometheus"]`: ```bash # real Anthropic call (costs real $) curl -s -X POST http://localhost:4099/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model":"anthropic-haiku-4-5","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"say hi in 3 words"}]}' # grow cardinality the way misspelled model names do in production for b in $(seq 0 99); do ( for i in $(seq $((b*4+1)) $((b*4+4))); do curl -s -o /dev/null -m 5 -X POST http://localhost:4099/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d "{\"model\":\"typo-model-$i\",\"messages\":[{\"role\":\"user\",\"content\":\"x\"}]}" & done; wait ) done # load: 20 concurrent scrapes split across two spellings of the same Accept-Encoding, # which is what two different scrapers (Prometheus sends "gzip", curl sends "gzip, deflate") look like start=$(python3 -c 'import time;print(time.time())') for i in $(seq 1 10); do curl -sL -o /dev/null -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Accept-Encoding: gzip" http://localhost:4099/metrics & done for i in $(seq 1 10); do curl -sL -o /dev/null -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Accept-Encoding: gzip, deflate" http://localhost:4099/metrics & done sleep 0.05 for i in $(seq 1 10); do curl -s -o /dev/null -w "liveliness during scrape: %{time_total}s\n" http://localhost:4099/health/liveliness; done | sort -t: -k2 -n wait echo "20 mixed-spelling concurrent scrapes wall time: $(python3 -c "import time;print(f'{time.time()-$start:.3f}s')")" ``` Both sides were health-gated at the open and close of the measurement, and both served a 1.4 MB payload ### Before (cb4eb82249) #### Unrelated requests during 20 concurrent scrapes 1. `curl -sL -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" http://localhost:4099/metrics | wc -c` ``` 1446872 ``` 2. Load script output (sorted by latency) ``` liveliness during scrape: 0.000936s liveliness during scrape: 0.000972s liveliness during scrape: 0.000984s liveliness during scrape: 0.001031s liveliness during scrape: 0.001061s liveliness during scrape: 0.001065s liveliness during scrape: 0.012704s liveliness during scrape: 0.061474s liveliness during scrape: 0.063679s liveliness during scrape: 0.252407s 20 mixed-spelling concurrent scrapes wall time: 0.637s ``` A 1.4 MB payload already stalls the loop for 252 ms. The reported 50 MB payloads scale that into multi-second stalls #### gzip negotiation 1. `curl -sL -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Accept-Encoding: gzip" -o /tmp/m.gz -D- http://localhost:4099/metrics | grep -i content-encoding; wc -c < /tmp/m.gz` ``` Content-Encoding: gzip 33926 ``` #### name[] restriction 1. `curl -sL -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-1234' 'http://localhost:4099/metrics?name%5B%5D=litellm_proxy_total_requests_metric_total' | grep -c litellm_proxy_total_requests_metric_total` ``` 403 ``` 2. Same request, counting a metric that was not requested: `... | grep -c litellm_request_total_latency` ``` 25 ``` The filter is ignored: metrics nobody asked for come back anyway ### After (57e5273023) #### Unrelated requests during 20 concurrent scrapes 1. `curl -sL -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" http://localhost:4099/metrics | wc -c` ``` 1446852 ``` 2. Load script output (sorted by latency) ``` liveliness during scrape: 0.000994s liveliness during scrape: 0.001000s liveliness during scrape: 0.001033s liveliness during scrape: 0.001086s liveliness during scrape: 0.001105s liveliness during scrape: 0.001195s liveliness during scrape: 0.001252s liveliness during scrape: 0.001276s liveliness during scrape: 0.012803s liveliness during scrape: 0.015302s 20 mixed-spelling concurrent scrapes wall time: 0.316s ``` Worst case drops from 252 ms to 15 ms, and the same 20 scrapes finish in half the wall time #### gzip negotiation 1. `curl -sL -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Accept-Encoding: gzip" -o /tmp/m.gz -D- http://localhost:4099/metrics | grep -i content-encoding; wc -c < /tmp/m.gz` ``` content-encoding: gzip 33881 ``` #### name[] restriction 1. `curl -sL -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-1234' 'http://localhost:4099/metrics?name%5B%5D=litellm_proxy_total_requests_metric_total' | grep -c litellm_proxy_total_requests_metric_total` ``` 403 ``` 2. Same request, counting a metric that was not requested: `... | grep -c litellm_request_total_latency` ``` 0 ``` ## Review notes Answers to the two review threads on `litellm/integrations/prometheus_metrics_endpoint.py`, here rather than in the threads because neither fits a review comment. Treat this section as load-bearing rather than commentary: it is the standing record of why the library's own app is not used here, and anyone simplifying this module back to `make_asgi_app` would silently reintroduce the `?name[]=` defect below. **Single-slot scrape coalescing: correct, and fixed.** The slot was keyed on the raw `Accept` and `Accept-Encoding` strings, so two scrapers asking for identical bytes in different words never shared a render. Prometheus sends `Accept-Encoding: gzip` while curl and the Grafana agent send `gzip, deflate`. A single slot on top of that meant each arrival displaced the other's entry, so under exactly the load this PR targets nothing coalesced and every overlapping scrape paid a full render. The key is now what the scrape actually asks for: the encoder and content type `choose_encoder` selected, whether gzip was accepted, and the `name[]` filter. In-flight renders live in a map keyed on that rather than in one slot, and each render drops its own entry from its own done callback, so one finishing cannot evict another still running. The Before and After above are that exact scenario, 20 concurrent scrapes split across two spellings of the same encoding. **Custom metrics HTTP handler: keeping it, because the parts that look hand-rolled are imported, and the library's app cannot do the job.** Content negotiation is `prometheus_client`'s own `choose_encoder` and `gzip_accepted`, and `?name[]=` is its `restricted_registry`. Header and query parsing is Starlette's `Request`; the response is Starlette's `StreamingResponse`. The only rewritten code is the four-line body of `prometheus_client.exposition._bake_output`, which is private and cannot be called. By contrast the library's own `make_asgi_app` hand-decodes raw ASGI header bytes and hand-emits `http.response.start` and `http.response.body`, so this module is less hand-rolled than the thing it replaces. Delegating to `make_asgi_app` also is not possible without losing two capabilities. It takes `registry` and `disable_compression`, calls `_bake_output` inline in the coroutine, and exposes no seam to move that work off the loop. Measured on a registry the size LIT-5357 reports, 600k samples and a 72.8 MB exposition, rendering inline froze the loop for 1691 ms and let a 5 ms ticker fire once, while rendering through `asyncio.to_thread` let it fire 73 times at a 12 ms median. Separately, `make_asgi_app` passes `parse_qs(scope['query_string'])` to `_bake_output`, which yields bytes keys, and `_bake_output` then tests `if 'name[]' in params` against a str key that can never match, so the library's ASGI app silently ignores `?name[]=` and returns the whole registry. That is the 25 leaked lines in the Before section, and it is why `make_wsgi_app` is unaffected: it parses a str query string. Adopting the library app would ship that bug. This looks like an upstream defect rather than a misuse, reproduced on prometheus-client 0.20.0, which is what this repo pins, and worth reporting to that project separately. Auth is not duplicated either. `/metrics` already sits behind `PrometheusAuthMiddleware`, and mounted ASGI sub-apps are an existing pattern here. ## Type 🚄 Infrastructure ## Caveats (if any) - Bounds scrape cost, does not shrink the payload - 50 MB exposition still costs 50 MB of transient memory - Render is pure Python and holds the GIL - Worker thread stops it monopolizing the loop, not using it - gzip is the part that truly parallelizes, since zlib drops the GIL - Coalescing only merges scrapes that overlap in time - Cardinality itself is unchanged, only scrape cost is - Thread offload uses the default asyncio executor ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/675dfbfab55e44f093c0d5fb93a9b0fc Requested by: @yassin-berriai

signals.title: fix(ptu): refuse an incomplete config.yaml reservation the way the endpoints do
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - config.yaml never ran the PTU cross-field checks the endpoints run - A reservation missing `team_id` loaded, served, and accrued nothing - Nothing was logged, so it looked exactly like the original bug How it solves it: - The rule moves into `litellm_core_utils.ptu_pricing`, stated once - Registration refuses such a deployment and names it - Only while PTU cost attribution is enabled ## User Flow Before: an operator fixes their PTU config, redeploys, and sees nothing change 1. The admin declares a provisioned-throughput deployment in `config.yaml` with `ptu_count`, `cost_per_ptu_per_hour` and `ptu_effective_from`, but no `team_id`, and starts the proxy with `LITELLM_ENABLE_PTU_COST_ATTRIBUTION=True` 2. The proxy starts and the deployment serves traffic 3. https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs shows those requests charged at the provider's per-token rate, because a deployment with no reservation to bill is not zeroed 4. The nightly job runs at 00:15 UTC and writes nothing for it 5. https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=usage shows no reserved-capacity cost, with no error, no warning, and no log line naming the deployment, which is indistinguishable from the feature not working After: the same configuration is refused, in the same terms `POST /model/new` already uses 1. The admin starts the same proxy 2. Startup logs `PTU configuration on model '' is invalid: team_id is required when PTU fields are set (one model maps to one team)` 3. That deployment is not registered; every other entry in the file loads and serves normally 4. The admin adds `team_id` and restarts, and the deployment loads and accrues flat cost An admin who has not enabled PTU cost attribution sees none of this; the deployment loads exactly as it does today ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Refs LIT-5809 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Both paths driven on a live proxy against real Postgres, with the same incomplete configuration, so the parity is observed rather than argued. ### The endpoint, unchanged by this PR ```bash curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4816/model/new -H "Authorization: Bearer $MASTER_KEY" \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"model_name":"db-ptu-noteam","litellm_params":{"model":"gemini/gemini-2.5-flash","api_key":"x"}, "model_info":{"ptu_count":10,"cost_per_ptu_per_hour":0.5,"ptu_effective_from":"2026-08-17T00:00:00Z"}}' ``` ``` status=400 {"error": {"message": "team_id is required when PTU fields are set (one model maps to one team)", ...}} ``` ### config.yaml, before this PR The same `model_info`, declared in a file, loads and serves: ``` models loaded: ['my-ptu-model-noteam', 'plain-sibling'] refusal log lines: 0 ``` ### config.yaml, after this PR ``` models loaded: ['plain-sibling'] PTU configuration on model 'my-ptu-model-noteam' is invalid: team_id is required when PTU fields are set (one model maps to one team), ignoring and continuing with other deployments. ``` The sibling entry in the same file still serves: ``` sibling chat=200 ``` ### With the feature flag unset ``` models loaded: ['my-ptu-model-noteam', 'plain-sibling'] refusal log lines: 0 ``` ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Changes `_validate_ptu_model_info` held the cross-field invariant inside the model endpoints, so only `POST /model/new` and `PATCH /model/{model_id}/update` enforced it. `ptu_config_error` now holds it in `litellm_core_utils.ptu_pricing`, beside the pricing rules the two paths already share, and returns the reason as a value. The endpoint raises its existing `400` with that message, so its responses are unchanged, which the endpoint suite passing untouched is the evidence for. `Router._create_deployment` asks the same question for a deployment no database row owns and raises when it has an answer. The proxy builds its router with `ignore_invalid_deployments`, so the cost is that one entry rather than startup. The check is gated on `is_ptu_cost_attribution_enabled()`. A deployment that accrues nothing cannot be refused for accruing nothing incorrectly, and gating it keeps a proxy that never opted in exactly as it is. `_parse_ptu_datetime` and `_coerce_ptu_datetime` in the endpoints module are removed. They duplicated `_as_utc` in the core module, and nothing else referenced them. ## QA runbook ## Caveats (if any) - A previously serving deployment with broken PTU config now disappears - Enforced only while PTU cost attribution is enabled ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR --- --- > [!NOTE] > **Medium Risk** > Touches PTU cost attribution and router registration: a previously serving incomplete PTU model can disappear when the flag is on. Endpoint 400 behavior is unchanged. > > **Overview** > **config.yaml PTU deployments now fail the same cross-field checks as `POST /model/new`**, so an incomplete reservation (missing `team_id`, start time, or a mismatched count/rate) is no longer loaded, served, and billed per token with no flat cost. > > The invariant lives once in `ptu_config_error`. Model endpoints still return 400 with the same messages. Router registration raises `ValueError` for config-sourced deployments **only when PTU cost attribution is enabled**; with `ignore_invalid_deployments` the proxy drops that entry and keeps the rest. Duplicate datetime helpers in the endpoints module are removed. > > Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 3b30981321da72a32aa3c02e17da51957c3536db. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).
