signals.title: fix(a2a): accept the whole JSON-RPC id union the spec defines
signals.text:
## TLDR Problem this solves: - JSON-RPC allows `string | integer | null`; our A2A response model required `str` - An agent echoing an integer id got a 500, not the agent's reply - A null id, which the spec mandates for uncorrelatable errors, also 500'd - Five distinct failing cases across `message/send` and `tasks/get` How it solves it: - Widen the A2A response model's `id` to the full spec union - Keep the caller's id type when backfilling an id the agent omitted - Exclude `bool`, which subclasses `int`, so `true` never returns as `1` ## User Flow Before: a developer whose A2A client numbers its JSON-RPC requests (`"id": 42`) cannot call any agent through the proxy at all 1. They register an agent and send POST https://litellm-domain/a2a/my-agent with `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":42,"method":"message/send","params":{...}}` 2. They get back HTTP 500 and `{"error":{"code":-32603,"message":"Internal error: 1 validation error for LiteLLMSendMessageResponse
id
 Input should be a valid string ..."}}` 3. The agent itself ran fine and answered, so nothing in its access log explains the failure 4. They retry with `"id": "42"` and it returns HTTP 200 with the agent's reply 5. `tasks/get` with `"id": 42` fails the same way, as does `"id": 0` 6. Dropping the id entirely does not help either: the agent's reply comes back as the same HTTP 500 After: the same requests succeed, and the id comes back as the value and type they sent 1. They send the same POST https://litellm-domain/a2a/my-agent with `"id": 42` 2. They get HTTP 200 and the agent's reply, carrying `"id": 42` as a number 3. `tasks/get` with `"id": 42` and with `"id": 0` both return HTTP 200 with the id unchanged 4. Omitting the id returns the agent's reply instead of a 500 5. String ids keep working exactly as before 6. When an agent answers an error without echoing the id, the reply carries `42` rather than `"42"`, so the client can still match it to its request ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-2818 ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/<your_test_file>.py -v` - [x] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Live proxy against a stub upstream agent that echoes the caller's JSON-RPC id back verbatim and logs every inbound request. The two string-id cases are controls: they must return a real 200 with the agent's reply on both sides, or the failing cases mean nothing. Shared setup, identical for both runs: ```yaml # a2a_config.yaml general_settings: master_key: sk-a2aint-1234 agents: - agent_name: stub-echo-agent agent_card_params: protocolVersion: "0.3.0" name: stub-echo-agent url: "http://127.0.0.1:8137/" version: "1.0.0" capabilities: {streaming: false} defaultInputModes: ["text/plain"] defaultOutputModes: ["text/plain"] skills: [] ``` ```bash python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config a2a_config.yaml --port 4137 ``` Every case below is the same curl with only the `id` and `method` changing: ```bash curl -sS -w '
HTTP %{http_code}
' -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4137/a2a/stub-echo-agent \ -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-a2aint-1234' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '<the body shown under each case>' ``` ### Before (fc3b160fb5) Code under test, `litellm/types/agents.py:334`, is ` id: str` #### message/send, string id (control) 1. Body `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":"ctl-1","method":"message/send","params":{"message":{"role":"user","messageId":"m1","parts":[{"kind":"text","text":"hi"}]}}}` 2. Output ``` {"id":"ctl-1","jsonrpc":"2.0","result":{"kind":"message","messageId":"stub-msg-1","parts":[{"kind":"text","text":"echoed"}],"role":"agent"}} HTTP 200 ``` #### message/send, integer id 1. Body `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":42,"method":"message/send","params":{"message":{"role":"user","messageId":"m1","parts":[{"kind":"text","text":"hi"}]}}}` 2. Output ``` {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":42,"error":{"code":-32603,"message":"Internal error: 1 validation error for LiteLLMSendMessageResponse
id
 Input should be a valid string [type=string_type, input_value=42, input_type=int]
 For further information visit https://errors.pydantic.dev/2.13/v/string_type"}} HTTP 500 ``` #### tasks/get, string id (control) 1. Body `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":"ctl-2","method":"tasks/get","params":{"id":"stub-task-1"}}` 2. Output ``` {"id":"ctl-2","jsonrpc":"2.0","result":{"kind":"task","id":"stub-task-1","contextId":"stub-ctx-1","status":{"state":"completed"}}} HTTP 200 ``` #### tasks/get, integer id 1. Body `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":42,"method":"tasks/get","params":{"id":"stub-task-1"}}` 2. Output ``` {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":42,"error":{"code":-32603,"message":"Internal error: 1 validation error for LiteLLMSendMessageResponse
id
 Input should be a valid string [type=string_type, input_value=42, input_type=int]
 For further information visit https://errors.pydantic.dev/2.13/v/string_type"}} HTTP 500 ``` #### tasks/get, falsy integer id 1. Body `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":0,"method":"tasks/get","params":{"id":"stub-task-1"}}` 2. Output ``` {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":0,"error":{"code":-32603,"message":"Internal error: 1 validation error for LiteLLMSendMessageResponse
id
 Input should be a valid string [type=string_type, input_value=0, input_type=int]
 For further information visit https://errors.pydantic.dev/2.13/v/string_type"}} HTTP 500 ``` #### tasks/get, id omitted so the agent answers with a null id 1. Body `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"tasks/get","params":{"id":"stub-task-1"}}` 2. Output ``` {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":null,"error":{"code":-32603,"message":"Internal error: 1 validation error for LiteLLMSendMessageResponse
id
 Input should be a valid string [type=string_type, input_value=None, input_type=NoneType]
 For further information visit https://errors.pydantic.dev/2.13/v/string_type"}} HTTP 500 ``` #### tasks/get, boolean id (not a legal JSON-RPC id) 1. Body `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":true,"method":"tasks/get","params":{"id":"stub-task-1"}}` 2. Output ``` {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":true,"error":{"code":-32603,"message":"Internal error: 1 validation error for LiteLLMSendMessageResponse
id
 Input should be a valid string [type=string_type, input_value=True, input_type=bool]
 For further information visit https://errors.pydantic.dev/2.13/v/string_type"}} HTTP 500 ``` #### upstream access log for the run 1. The stub logged every inbound request, so the agent was reached and answered on all seven legs; the failures are entirely proxy-side ``` UPSTREAM GET /.well-known/agent-card.json UPSTREAM POST / method='message/send' id='ce6ece59-3927-4aeb-b25b-2e8f99c6c35a' id_type=str UPSTREAM GET /.well-known/agent-card.json UPSTREAM POST / method='message/send' id='2d49544e-0f82-46bc-b233-6a50a7d17acd' id_type=str UPSTREAM POST / method='tasks/get' id='ctl-2' id_type=str UPSTREAM POST / method='tasks/get' id=42 id_type=int UPSTREAM POST / method='tasks/get' id=0 id_type=int UPSTREAM POST / method='tasks/get' id=None id_type=NoneType UPSTREAM POST / method='tasks/get' id=True id_type=bool ``` ### After (4affda47b1) Code under test, `litellm/types/agents.py:347`, is ` id: str | StrictInt | None = None` #### message/send, string id (control) 1. Body `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":"ctl-1","method":"message/send","params":{"message":{"role":"user","messageId":"m1","parts":[{"kind":"text","text":"hi"}]}}}` 2. Output ``` {"id":"ctl-1","jsonrpc":"2.0","result":{"kind":"message","messageId":"stub-msg-1","parts":[{"kind":"text","text":"echoed"}],"role":"agent"}} HTTP 200 ``` #### message/send, integer id 1. Body `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":42,"method":"message/send","params":{"message":{"role":"user","messageId":"m1","parts":[{"kind":"text","text":"hi"}]}}}` 2. Output, id returned as a number ``` {"id":42,"jsonrpc":"2.0","result":{"kind":"message","messageId":"stub-msg-1","parts":[{"kind":"text","text":"echoed"}],"role":"agent"}} HTTP 200 ``` #### tasks/get, string id (control) 1. Body `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":"ctl-2","method":"tasks/get","params":{"id":"stub-task-1"}}` 2. Output ``` {"id":"ctl-2","jsonrpc":"2.0","result":{"kind":"task","id":"stub-task-1","contextId":"stub-ctx-1","status":{"state":"completed"}}} HTTP 200 ``` #### tasks/get, integer id 1. Body `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":42,"method":"tasks/get","params":{"id":"stub-task-1"}}` 2. Output, id returned as a number ``` {"id":42,"jsonrpc":"2.0","result":{"kind":"task","id":"stub-task-1","contextId":"stub-ctx-1","status":{"state":"completed"}}} HTTP 200 ``` #### tasks/get, falsy integer id 1. Body `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":0,"method":"tasks/get","params":{"id":"stub-task-1"}}` 2. Output, `0` is preserved rather than read as absent ``` {"id":0,"jsonrpc":"2.0","result":{"kind":"task","id":"stub-task-1","contextId":"stub-ctx-1","status":{"state":"completed"}}} HTTP 200 ``` #### tasks/get, id omitted so the agent answers with a null id 1. Body `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"tasks/get","params":{"id":"stub-task-1"}}` 2. Output, the agent's reply is relayed ``` {"jsonrpc":"2.0","result":{"kind":"task","id":"stub-task-1","contextId":"stub-ctx-1","status":{"state":"completed"}}} HTTP 200 ``` #### tasks/get, boolean id (not a legal JSON-RPC id) 1. Body `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":true,"method":"tasks/get","params":{"id":"stub-task-1"}}` 2. Output, stringified rather than relayed as `1`, which would collide with a real integer id ``` {"id":"True","jsonrpc":"2.0","result":{"kind":"task","id":"stub-task-1","contextId":"stub-ctx-1","status":{"state":"completed"}}} HTTP 200 ``` #### upstream access log for the run 1. Same shape as the Before run, confirming the only variable was the response model ``` UPSTREAM GET /.well-known/agent-card.json UPSTREAM POST / method='message/send' id='33acb5d6-e696-43d0-822f-cbd4feafe8f1' id_type=str UPSTREAM GET /.well-known/agent-card.json UPSTREAM POST / method='message/send' id='565fbe21-b50c-4a8a-b0dc-4009bb0095c1' id_type=str UPSTREAM POST / method='tasks/get' id='ctl-2' id_type=str UPSTREAM POST / method='tasks/get' id=42 id_type=int UPSTREAM POST / method='tasks/get' id=0 id_type=int UPSTREAM POST / method='tasks/get' id=None id_type=NoneType UPSTREAM POST / method='tasks/get' id=True id_type=bool ``` ## Review notes Greptile filed the boolean trap twice and was right both times, including against my own reply. `bool` subclasses `int`, so widening to accept integers made pydantic coerce a boolean id to `1` or `0`, which is worse than the 500 it replaced because `1` collides with a real integer id another in-flight request may be using. My first correction guarded only `_normalize_a2a_jsonrpc_response`, and I said in a review reply that the annotation was guarded too. That was wrong: direct construction bypasses normalization, and the follow-up P1 saying so is accurate. The field is now `str | StrictInt | None`, which accepts exactly `string | integer | null` and rejects `bool`, `float`, `list` and `dict` on every path including direct construction. Only the integer half needs strictness, since `bool` subclasses `int` and not `str`. Getting there without raising a type ceiling took some measuring, which is worth recording. The ceilings in `basedpyright-code-budget.json` are ratcheted to the exact current count, so any `+1` reds `lint`. `StrictStr | StrictInt` costs two `reportUnknownVariableType` (basedpyright cannot resolve either pydantic symbol here) and a `field_validator` costs one of those plus a `reportUntypedFunctionDecorator` against a ceiling of 27. `str | StrictInt` costs exactly one, paid for by giving `response_dict` in `from_a2a_response` a real binding instead of an untyped rebind. Net per-rule delta against the merge base is zero on every rule. Rebased onto `fc3b160fb5` to pick up #37671, which added the `ruff check --config ruff-tests.toml tests` step. That job checks out the PR head rather than the merge ref, so the step ran against a tree predating the config file it names, and no rerun could clear it. Both proof legs above were re-captured after the rebase. This supersedes #29196, which proposed the same `str | int | None` widening for LIT-2818 in May. That branch targets `litellm_oss_agent_shin_daily_branch`, predates `_normalize_a2a_jsonrpc_response`, and would conflict. ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats - A null id is omitted from the response, not emitted as `"id": null` - That follows the endpoint's existing `exclude_none` dump, unchanged here - Bridge-backed agents still stringify the id; separate, larger change - That path narrows `request_id: str` across six provider packages ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signals.title: fix(reset_budget_job): reconnect and retry on transient DB transport errors
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Reset job skipped a whole tick on transient DB errors - Nothing reconnected, so due resets waited 10 minutes - Failures were untagged, so nobody could see which phase died How it solves it: - Reads, writes, raw queries route through the reconnect helper - One reconnect-and-retry per operation, tagged per sub-job - Writes only replay a ConnectError, where the statements provably never landed - Non-transport errors (unique violations, data errors) still surface ## User Flow Before: an admin whose keys carry a monthly budget sees spend stay above the cap for an extra reset cycle whenever the gateway's database transport blips 1. They create a key with a budget window: POST https://litellm-domain/key/generate with `{"max_budget": 10, "budget_duration": "30d"}` 2. Their team burns through the budget, so requests to POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions come back 400 with "Budget has been exceeded" 3. The budget window comes due while the database transport is briefly unreachable 4. GET https://litellm-domain/key/info?key=sk-... still reports the old `spend` and the old reset timestamp, and calls keep getting refused 5. The proxy logs "Failed to reset budget for keys" with a connection error and nothing else, so nothing is retried until the next cycle, up to ten minutes later After: the same blip costs one retry instead of a whole cycle, so the key is spendable again on time 1. They create the same key: POST https://litellm-domain/key/generate with `{"max_budget": 10, "budget_duration": "30d"}` 2. Their team burns through the budget, so requests come back 400 with "Budget has been exceeded" 3. The budget window comes due while the database transport is briefly unreachable 4. The gateway reconnects and repeats that one read or write on the spot 5. GET https://litellm-domain/key/info?key=sk-... reports `spend` back at 0 and a fresh reset timestamp, and POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions succeeds again on the cycle it was due ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5372 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/<your_test_file>.py -v` - [x] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Shared setup, identical for both runs: a proxy on localhost:4000 against a local Postgres, with the reset scheduler pinned to 10s so ticks are observable (`proxy_budget_rescheduler_min_time: 10`, `proxy_budget_rescheduler_max_time: 10`), one real Anthropic deployment (`anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5`), and `PRISMA_HEALTH_WATCHDOG_ENABLED=False` so the only thing that can recover a broken transport is the job itself. ```bash # 3 keys that come due on every tick for i in 1 2 3; do curl -s -X POST http://localhost:4000/key/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"max_budget": 10, "budget_duration": "10s", "models": ["anthropic-haiku-4-5"]}' > /dev/null done # break the database transport for 2 minutes: reject every 8th packet to the query engine PORT=$(ss -tnlp | grep -a query-engine | head -1 | awk '{print $4}' | cut -d: -f2) sudo iptables -I OUTPUT -p tcp -d 127.0.0.1 --dport $PORT \ -m statistic --mode nth --every 8 --packet 0 -j REJECT --reject-with tcp-reset sleep 120 sudo iptables -D OUTPUT -p tcp -d 127.0.0.1 --dport $PORT \ -m statistic --mode nth --every 8 --packet 0 -j REJECT --reject-with tcp-reset ``` ### Before (4af59d7c6e) #### A real chat completion is billed to a budgeted key 1. `curl -s -X POST http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"anthropic-haiku-4-5","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"say hi"}]}'` ``` {"id":"chatcmpl-...","model":"anthropic-haiku-4-5","choices":[{"finish_reason":"stop","index":0,"message":{"content":"Hi! How can I help you today?","role":"assistant"}}],"usage":{"completion_tokens":16,"prompt_tokens":9,"total_tokens":25}} ``` 2. Spend lands on the key, so the reset job has real work to do: `curl -s "http://localhost:4000/key/info?key=$KEY" -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" | python3 -c "import sys,json;print(json.load(sys.stdin)['info']['spend'])"` ``` 8.900000000000001e-05 ``` #### The transport is flaky for 2 minutes 1. Counted from the proxy log over the 120s window: ``` reset job ticks: 12 reconnect-and-retry tagged reset_budget: 0 phases that gave up (Failed to reset): 19 ``` 2. Every transport error is a dead end, and the log never names which read or write died: ``` 20:23:02 - LiteLLM Proxy:ERROR: reset_budget_job.py:671 - Failed to reset budget for keys: 20:23:12 - LiteLLM Proxy:ERROR: reset_budget_job.py:671 - Failed to reset budget for keys: 20:23:13 - LiteLLM Proxy:ERROR: reset_budget_job.py:965 - Failed to reset budget windows for keys: 20:23:22 - LiteLLM Proxy:ERROR: reset_budget_job.py:671 - Failed to reset budget for keys: 20:23:23 - LiteLLM Proxy:ERROR: reset_budget_job.py:965 - Failed to reset budget windows for keys: ... httpcore.ReadError httpx.ReadError ``` ### After (2415792316) #### A real chat completion is billed to a budgeted key 1. `curl -s -X POST http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"anthropic-haiku-4-5","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"say hi"}]}'` ``` {"id":"chatcmpl-...","model":"anthropic-haiku-4-5","choices":[{"finish_reason":"stop","index":0,"message":{"content":"Hi! How's it going?","role":"assistant"}}],"usage":{"completion_tokens":13,"prompt_tokens":9,"total_tokens":22}} ``` 2. With every 12th packet to the query engine rejected, the key's spend is still zeroed 5s into the flaky window, on the tick it was due ``` 22:14:01 key spend recorded in db: 7.900000000000001e-05 22:14:01 dropping every 12th packet to the db transport (engine port 48449) 22:14:02 (+1s) key spend in db: 7.900000000000001e-05 22:14:05 (+4s) key spend in db: 7.900000000000001e-05 22:14:06 (+5s) key spend in db: 0 RESULT: spend reset 5s into the flaky transport window ``` #### The transport is flaky for 2 minutes 1. Same command, same window length, same 12 ticks: ``` reset job ticks: 12 reconnect-and-retry tagged reset_budget: 3 phases that gave up (Failed to reset): 4 key batches actually written: 12 ``` 2. Each failure now names its sub-job and gets a reconnect, and the retry finishes the work on the tick it was due: ``` 22:11:36 - LiteLLM Proxy:WARNING: exception_handler.py:423 - DB transport error on read; attempting reconnect-and-retry. reason=reset_budget_read_key_windows_failure 22:11:36 - LiteLLM Proxy:INFO: utils.py:5243 - Prisma DB reconnect succeeded. reason=reset_budget_read_key_windows_failure 22:11:36 - LiteLLM Proxy:WARNING: exception_handler.py:423 - DB transport error on read; attempting reconnect-and-retry. reason=reset_budget_read_team_windows_failure 22:11:46 - LiteLLM Proxy:WARNING: exception_handler.py:423 - DB transport error on read; attempting reconnect-and-retry. reason=reset_budget_read_key_windows_failure ``` 3. The remaining give-ups are the two safety rails working as intended: a write that failed with `ReadError` after the statements were sent is not replayed, and back-to-back reconnects are throttled by the existing cooldown while 1-in-8 packet loss is held for two minutes. A single blip, which is what the ticket describes, resolves on the first retry ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - Retry is one attempt, throttled by the existing reconnect cooldown - A post-send error on a write is ambiguous, so it is not replayed and that phase still waits for the next tick - A sustained outage still skips the tick, by design - The ticket's watchdog question stays open, nothing here changes it ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/ce60e0aa6d3f44d4b13089aedca19838 Requested by: @yassin-berriai

signals.title: fix: map Anthropic API usage-limit errors to RateLimitError (429) not BadRequest (400)
signals.text: ## TLDR **Problem:** Anthropic returns spend/usage-limit exhaustion typed as an `invalid_request_error` (HTTP 400), e.g. *"You have reached your specified API usage limits. You will regain access on … UTC."* LiteLLM faithfully maps that to `BadRequestError` (400), but per the [exception-mapping docs](https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/exception_mapping) a usage/rate limit should surface as `RateLimitError` (429). The wrong class breaks callers' retry / fallback handling. **Fix:** Add one phrase branch to the shared `ExceptionCheckers.is_error_str_rate_limit()` helper — the same mechanism already used for Mistral's *"service tier capacity exceeded"* right above it — so an error string containing `"api usage limit"` is detected as a rate limit and mapped to 429. The phrase branches are intentionally ungated by status code, so a limit reported under a 400 is still classified correctly. Fixes #37599 ## Changes - `litellm/litellm_core_utils/exception_mapping_utils.py` - `is_error_str_rate_limit()` now treats Anthropic's `"api usage limit"` phrasing as a rate limit. ## Testing Added `test_anthropic_usage_limit_is_treated_as_rate_limit` in `tests/test_litellm/litellm_core_utils/test_exception_mapping_utils.py`, using the exact Anthropic payload from the issue and asserting it is detected as a rate limit even under `status_code=400`. ``` tests/test_litellm/litellm_core_utils/test_exception_mapping_utils.py ... 21 passed ```

signals.title: fix(proxy): capture requester IP in 401 and auth-time 429 failure logs
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - 401 and budget 429 failure logs carry no caller IP - those failures usually have no key or user identity either - operators cannot see or block repeated bad-key traffic How it solves it: - stamp the caller IP into the failure log for auth rejections - honors `use_x_forwarded_for` and keeps any IP already recorded ## User Flow Before: an operator watching a burst of rejected requests cannot tell who is sending them 1. A caller sends POST http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions with `Authorization: Bearer sk-bad-key` and gets back 401 with "Invalid proxy server token passed" 2. The operator opens http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=logs, filters to failures, and opens that 401 row 3. The row shows no user and no key owner, and its IP field is empty, so there is nothing to rate limit or block on 4. Same for a key that blew its budget: the caller gets 429 "Budget has been exceeded!" and the log row again shows no IP After: the same rejected requests are attributable to an IP 1. A caller sends the same POST http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions with `Authorization: Bearer sk-bad-key` and gets back the same 401 2. The operator opens http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=logs, filters to failures, and opens that 401 row 3. The row now shows the caller IP, so the operator can spot the source of repeated 401s and block it upstream 4. Same for the budget 429: its log row also shows the caller IP ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-4839 ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/<your_test_file>.py -v` - [x] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Shared setup, run against a live proxy hitting real OpenAI (`gpt-4o-mini`, real spend). Port 4707 instead of 4000 because another proxy already held 4000 on this box: ```bash docker run -d --name lit4839-pg -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=litellm -e POSTGRES_USER=litellm -e POSTGRES_DB=litellm -p 6407:5432 postgres:16 export DATABASE_URL=postgresql://litellm:litellm@127.0.0.1:6407/litellm .venv/bin/prisma db push --schema=./litellm/proxy/schema.prisma --accept-data-loss --skip-generate DISABLE_SCHEMA_UPDATE=True python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config litellm/proxy/dev_config.yaml --port 4707 READ_LOGS() { curl -s -G "http://localhost:4707/spend/logs/ui" -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" \ --data-urlencode "start_date=2026-08-20 00:00:00" --data-urlencode "end_date=2026-08-22 00:00:00" \ --data-urlencode "status_filter=failure" --data-urlencode "page_size=3" \ | python3 -c " import sys,json for r in json.load(sys.stdin)['data']: print(r['metadata']['error_information']['error_code'], r.get('requester_ip_address'))" } ``` `/spend/logs/ui` is what http://localhost:4707/ui/?page=logs reads, so the IP column an operator sees is exactly this field. Each leg ran on its own empty database, and `/health/liveliness` returned 200 immediately before and after every case ### Before (4af59d7c6e) #### 401, unknown key 1. `curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" -X POST http://localhost:4707/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-bad-key-lit4839" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"gpt-4o-mini","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]}'` prints `401` with `Authentication Error, Invalid proxy server token passed. Received API Key = sk-...4839` 2. `READ_LOGS` shows that row as `401 None`, so the rejected caller is unattributable #### 429, key over budget 1. A key from `curl -s -X POST http://localhost:4707/key/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"models":["gpt-4o-mini"],"max_budget":0.0000001}'` spends `6.599999999999999e-06` on one real `gpt-4o-mini` call, then the next identical call returns `429` with `Budget has been exceeded! Key=key (sk-...Skcg) Current cost: 6.599999999999406e-06, Max budget: 1e-07` 2. `READ_LOGS` shows that row as `429 None` ### After (5115e91b55) #### 401, unknown key 1. The same `curl` prints `401` with the same `Authentication Error, Invalid proxy server token passed. Received API Key = sk-...4839` 2. `READ_LOGS` shows that row as `401 127.0.0.1` #### 429, key over budget 1. A key from the same `/key/generate` call spends `6.599999999999999e-06` on one real `gpt-4o-mini` call, then the next identical call returns `429` with `Budget has been exceeded! Key=key (sk-...LmAA) Current cost: 6.599999999999406e-06, Max budget: 1e-07` 2. `READ_LOGS` shows that row as `429 127.0.0.1` ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - only covers rejections raised at the auth gate - rate limit 429s past auth already logged the IP ## Review notes On the bare `dict` annotation: `request_data` is the parsed request body, which spans every proxy route, so there is no single Pydantic model to validate it against. It is now `dict[str, object]` on the helper and on `_handle_authentication_error`, which is the honest shape and, unlike `dict[str, Any]`, forces narrowing at every read. The two reads narrow explicitly, the metadata bucket with `isinstance(metadata, Mapping)` and the budget model with `isinstance(budget_model, str)`, and the parameterized test's case arguments are typed too That stays inside the lint ceilings. basedpyright on `auth_exception_handler.py` goes from 23 diagnostics to 8, and the one rule that moves the wrong way anywhere is `reportUnknownArgumentType`, +2 at the two `user_api_key_auth.py` call sites that still hand over a bare `dict`, paid for by -2 in this file plus dropping the redundant `False` default on the `use_x_forwarded_for` lookup that `_get_request_ip_address` already compares with `is True` On where the IP comes from: `_get_request_ip_address` is pre-existing and gated on `general_settings.use_x_forwarded_for`, the same helper and the same operator switch the IP allowlist gate uses and the same rule `add_litellm_data_to_request` applies on the success path. With the switch off only the socket peer is used, so `X-Forwarded-For` cannot forge the logged IP. With it on, the deployment is asserting it sits behind a trusted load balancer, exactly as it already does for every successful request. Tightening the header chain further, the way the MCP surface does with `trusted_proxy_ranges`, would be a change to that shared helper rather than to this fix On redaction: the IP lands in the same `metadata` or `litellm_metadata` bucket the success path writes, so it reaches loggers through the standard payload and answers to the same switches, with no new bypass. Neither `turn_off_message_logging` nor `redact_user_api_key_info` has ever masked `requester_ip_address` on either path ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/b7d4e62082704377a178e62387d4e60d Requested by: @yassin-berriai

signals.title: fix(team): allow no-reset default budgets for team members
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Team member default budgets could not be set to never reset - Team Member Settings only offered Daily, Weekly, Monthly - An explicit null duration was ignored when a budget was sent - The old reset period and reset time stayed on the row How it solves it: - Team Member Settings now uses the shared budget duration dropdown - "Never resets" sends an explicit null duration - An explicitly null duration clears duration and reset time - A null duration no longer inherits the team's own duration - Omitted duration keeps inheriting the team duration as before ## User Flow Before: an admin who wants each team member capped at $100 with no periodic reset cannot express that, and any duration already set is permanent 1. They open https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=teams, pick a team, click Edit, open Team Member Settings 2. They set Default Budget (USD) to 100 3. They open Default Budget Duration and see only Daily, Weekly and Monthly, with no way to clear it 4. Going around the UI, they send POST https://litellm-domain/team/update with `{"team_id": ..., "team_member_budget": 100, "team_member_budget_duration": null}` and get 200 5. GET https://litellm-domain/team/info?team_id=... still shows the member budget resetting every `7d` with a `budget_reset_at` date 6. Creating a fresh team with `"team_member_budget_duration": null` instead copies the team's own `30d` reset period onto the member budget After: the same admin sets a $100 member budget that never resets, from the UI or the API 1. They open https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=teams, pick a team, click Edit, open Team Member Settings 2. They set Default Budget (USD) to 100 3. They open Default Budget Duration and pick "Never resets" alongside hourly, daily, weekly and monthly, then Save 4. Equivalently, POST https://litellm-domain/team/update with `{"team_id": ..., "team_member_budget": 100, "team_member_budget_duration": null}` returns 200 5. GET https://litellm-domain/team/info?team_id=... shows the member budget at $100 with `budget_duration` and `budget_reset_at` both null, so spend never rolls over 6. Creating a fresh team with `"team_member_budget_duration": null` leaves the member budget with no reset period, even when the team itself resets every `30d` ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5897 ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/<your_test_file>.py -v` - [x] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Shared setup: proxy on the dev config with `master_key: sk-1234` and a Postgres database ### Before (e07a7129c56c3ad54be965e63dc5b8688cc07a22) #### Keeping a member budget while clearing its reset period 1. `curl -X POST localhost:4000/team/new -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -d '{"team_alias":"qa-no-reset","budget_duration":"30d","team_member_budget":100,"team_member_budget_duration":"7d"}'` returns a team id 2. `curl -X POST localhost:4000/team/update -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -d '{"team_id":"<id>","team_member_budget":100,"team_member_budget_duration":null}'` returns 200 3. `curl "localhost:4000/team/info?team_id=<id>"` shows the member budget unchanged: `{"max_budget": 100.0, "budget_duration": "7d", "budget_reset_at": "2026-08-24T00:00:00Z"}` #### Creating a team whose member budget should never reset 1. `curl -X POST localhost:4000/team/new -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -d '{"team_alias":"qa-inherit","budget_duration":"30d","team_member_budget":100,"team_member_budget_duration":null}'` returns a team id 2. `curl "localhost:4000/team/info?team_id=<id>"` shows the team's own period copied onto the member budget: `{"max_budget": 100.0, "budget_duration": "30d", "budget_reset_at": "2026-09-01T00:00:00Z"}` ### After (2f420ba52381cba41fe747575f85a6c97839ce76) #### Keeping a member budget while clearing its reset period 1. `curl -X POST localhost:4100/team/new ... '{"team_alias":"qa-no-reset-after","budget_duration":"30d","team_member_budget":100,"team_member_budget_duration":"7d"}'` returns a team id 2. `curl -X POST localhost:4100/team/update ... '{"team_id":"<id>","team_member_budget":100,"team_member_budget_duration":null}'` returns 200 3. `curl "localhost:4100/team/info?team_id=<id>"` shows the reset period gone and the budget intact: `{"max_budget": 100.0, "budget_duration": null, "budget_reset_at": null}` #### Creating a team whose member budget should never reset 1. `curl -X POST localhost:4100/team/new ... '{"team_alias":"qa-inherit","budget_duration":"30d","team_member_budget":100,"team_member_budget_duration":null}'` returns a team id 2. `curl "localhost:4100/team/info?team_id=<id>"` shows no reset period inherited: `{"max_budget": 100.0, "budget_duration": null, "budget_reset_at": null}` UI before/after screenshots of Default Budget Duration under Team Member Settings are attached on LIT-5897 ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - Removed the unused duration selector that lacked a no-reset option - This field now also offers hourly, matching every other duration field - Option labels are lowercase here now, like the rest of the UI Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/042ece9260e54da0bd79fb98d375a164

signals.title: test: add six ruff rules that catch tests which cannot fail
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - `assert False` in a `try:` is caught by its own `except` - Bare `a == b` statements evaluate and throw the result away - 50 such sites in `tests/`, several unable to ever fail How it solves it: - Selects 6 more ruff rules in `ruff-tests.toml`, already wired to CI - Rewrites every `assert False` as `pytest.fail`, which escapes `except Exception` - Restores the missing `assert` on 9 dead comparisons - One test asserted `True == True`; now it tests its module ## User Flow Before: a proxy admin scopes MCP servers to a team, the gateway stops honoring that scope, and no test objects 1. They POST /team/new, then attach two MCP servers to the team through the Admin UI 2. A member of that team lists tools and sees zero servers instead of the two granted 3. A separate developer disables OpenAI container file errors so a missing file quietly returns nothing 4. Their app calls the container file content route for a deleted file, gets an empty body back instead of a 404, and writes it to disk as if it were real content 5. Both regressions land green, because the tests covering them either compare `True == True` or hide their failure inside their own `except Exception` After: both regressions are caught before merge 1. The same two changes are made 2. CI runs the same test files and both go red, naming the team whose servers vanished and the container file that should have errored 3. Any new test written with either shape is rejected at lint time, so the next one cannot reach the proxy either ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally - [x] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix This PR changes lint config and tests, so there is no proxy route to curl. The proof is four mutations: break a behavior a test exists to police, and show the old test does not notice while the new one does. Every command is identical on both sides; only the `tests/` tree differs. The four mutations, applied one at a time and reverted after each run: ``` mcp_team_servers litellm/proxy/_experimental/mcp_server/db.py `return mcp_servers or []` -> `return []` custom_llm_api_key litellm/images/main.py custom_handler.aimage_generation(api_key=api_key) -> (api_key=None) pattern_wildcard litellm/router_utils/pattern_match_deployments.py `if "*" not in litellm_deployment_litellm_model:` -> `if True:` container_file_content litellm/containers/endpoint_factory.py retrieve_container_file_content returns None instead of raising ``` `container_file_content` hits the real OpenAI containers API with a live key: it creates a container, asks for a file that does not exist, and deletes the container. ### Before (4af59d7c6e) #### Team MCP server grants stop working, test still green 1. Apply `mcp_team_servers`, then run ``` pytest tests/test_litellm/proxy/db/mcp_server/test_db.py -q ``` 2. Output: ``` 1 passed, 2 warnings in 1.64s ``` #### Custom provider stops receiving the caller's api_key, test still green 1. Apply `custom_llm_api_key`, then run ``` pytest tests/local_testing/test_custom_llm.py::test_image_generation_async_additional_params -q ``` 2. Output: ``` 1 passed, 3 warnings in 0.04s ``` #### Wildcard routing stops substituting the model, test still green 1. Apply `pattern_wildcard`, then run ``` pytest tests/local_testing/test_router_pattern_matching.py::test_router_pattern_match_e2e -q ``` 2. Output: ``` 1 passed, 1 warning in 0.08s ``` #### Container file errors get swallowed, test still green 1. Apply `container_file_content`, then run against the live OpenAI API ``` pytest tests/llm_translation/test_containers_api.py::test_container_files_api -q ``` 2. Output: ``` 1 passed, 1 warning in 1.53s ``` ### After (634131b34f) #### Team MCP server grants stop working, test now fails 1. Apply `mcp_team_servers` and run the same command: ``` pytest tests/test_litellm/proxy/db/mcp_server/test_db.py -q ``` 2. Output: ``` ____________ test_fetch_mcp_servers_by_team[team_record4-expected4] ____________ 1 failed, 4 passed, 2 warnings in 1.96s ``` #### Custom provider stops receiving the caller's api_key, test now fails 1. Apply `custom_llm_api_key` and run the same command: ``` pytest tests/local_testing/test_custom_llm.py::test_image_generation_async_additional_params -q ``` 2. Output: ``` > assert mock_client.call_args.kwargs["api_key"] == "my-api-key" E AssertionError: assert None == 'my-api-key' 1 failed, 3 warnings in 0.10s ``` #### Wildcard routing stops substituting the model, test now fails 1. Apply `pattern_wildcard` and run the same command: ``` pytest tests/local_testing/test_router_pattern_matching.py::test_router_pattern_match_e2e -q ``` 2. Output: ``` > assert request_body["model"] == "my-custom-model" E AssertionError: assert '*' == 'my-custom-model' 1 failed, 1 warning in 0.24s ``` #### Container file errors get swallowed, test now fails 1. Apply `container_file_content` and run the same command against the live OpenAI API: ``` pytest tests/llm_translation/test_containers_api.py::test_container_files_api -q ``` 2. Output: ``` 3. signals.title: fix(responses_bridge): map incomplete responses to finish_reason length instead of 500
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Chat completions through the Responses bridge return 500 when reasoning consumes the whole token budget - Truncated bridge streams ended with finish_reason "stop" and no usage How it solves it: - An incomplete response with no message now yields one empty assistant message - finish_reason maps from the incomplete reason: "length", or "content_filter" for filtered - Truncated partial text keeps its content and gets finish_reason "length" - Streaming handles the response.incomplete terminal event like response.completed, with the mapped finish_reason and usage ## User Flow Before: a developer whose app calls a bridged reasoning model with a small completion budget gets a 500 whenever reasoning uses up the whole budget 1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with `"model": "bridge/gpt-5.6-sol"` (a `openai/responses/...` deployment), `"reasoning_effort": "high"`, `"max_completion_tokens": 16` 2. The response is HTTP 500 with `"litellm.APIConnectionError: ... gpt-5.6-sol unable to complete request: max_output_tokens"`, so their app surfaces a gateway error to the end user 3. The same request with `"stream": true` returns 200, but the only meaningful chunk carries `"finish_reason": "stop"` and no usage, so the app believes the model finished normally and records zero spend 4. POST https://litellm-domain/v1/responses with the same model and `"max_output_tokens": 16` returns 200 with `"status": "incomplete"`, so only the chat completions surface is broken After: the same request behaves like OpenAI's native chat completions on truncation 1. They send the same POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with `"reasoning_effort": "high"`, `"max_completion_tokens": 16` 2. The response is HTTP 200 with one choice: an assistant message with `"content": ""`, `"finish_reason": "length"`, and usage showing prompt 37 / completion 16 / reasoning 16 tokens 3. The same request with `"stream": true` returns a terminal chunk with `"finish_reason": "length"`, and with `"stream_options": {"include_usage": true}` the final chunk carries the real usage 4. When the truncation reason is a content filter, the choice comes back with `"finish_reason": "content_filter"` instead ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5886 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more - [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Two proxies, same config, same prompt, real OpenAI calls with no mocks. Before is the merge base cb4eb82249, after is 5c89490124 on this branch. All four cases were re-run at the current tip 16bba15434 and came back identical, so the proof stands at the head, not just at the commit it was first captured on Shared config: ```yaml model_list: - model_name: bridge/gpt-5.6-sol litellm_params: model: openai/responses/gpt-5.6-sol api_key: os.environ/OPENAI_API_KEY general_settings: master_key: sk-1234 ``` Prompt used in every case: "Determine the last ten decimal digits of 7 raised to the power 123456789. Think through modular arithmetic carefully, then return only those ten digits." Every request caps output at 16 tokens, which is what makes the upstream response come back incomplete ### Before (cb4eb82249, port 52361) #### Non-streaming /v1/chat/completions 1. `curl -sS -i http://localhost:52361/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"bridge/gpt-5.6-sol","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"<prompt>"}],"reasoning_effort":"high","max_completion_tokens":16}'` 2. Observed `HTTP/1.1 500 Internal Server Error` with body `{"error":{"message":"litellm.APIConnectionError: APIConnectionError: OpenAIException - gpt-5.6-sol unable to complete request: max_output_tokens. ...","code":"500"}}`, no usage anywhere, and `x-litellm-response-cost: 0` 3. The proxy log carries `ValueError: gpt-5.6-sol unable to complete request: max_output_tokens`, raised at transformation.py:768 #### Streaming /v1/chat/completions 1. Same request with `"stream": true` and `"stream_options":{"include_usage":true}` 2. Observed HTTP 200 whose whole stream is `{"choices":[{"index":0,"delta":{},"finish_reason":"stop"}]}`, then a second empty-delta chunk, then `[DONE]` 3. No usage chunk arrives even though the request asked for one, and every cost header reads 0.0 #### Non-streaming /v1/messages 1. `curl -sS -i http://localhost:52361/v1/messages -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"bridge/gpt-5.6-sol","max_tokens":16,"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"<prompt>"}]}'` 2. Observed HTTP 200 with `"content":[],"stop_reason":"max_tokens"` and `"usage":{"input_tokens":37,"output_tokens":16}`, billed at `x-litellm-response-cost: 0.000665` #### Streaming /v1/messages 1. Same request with `"stream": true` 2. Observed `message_start`, then `message_delta` carrying `{"stop_reason": "max_tokens"}` with usage 37 in / 16 out, then `message_stop` ### After (5c89490124, port 35416) #### Non-streaming /v1/chat/completions 1. Same curl, against the fixed proxy 2. Observed `HTTP/1.1 200 OK` with `"choices":[{"finish_reason":"length","index":0,"message":{"content":"","role":"assistant","reasoning_items":[{"type":"reasoning","id":"rs_0785b87a...","encrypted_content":"gAAAAABqh4bd...","summary":[]}]}}]` and `"usage":{"completion_tokens":16,"prompt_tokens":37,"total_tokens":53,"completion_tokens_details":{"reasoning_tokens":16},...}` 3. The call is billed at `x-litellm-response-cost: 0.000665`, where the 500 billed nothing #### Streaming /v1/chat/completions 1. Same request with `"stream": true` and `"stream_options":{"include_usage":true}` 2. Observed the terminal choice chunk `{"choices":[{"index":0,"delta":{},"finish_reason":"length"}]}` 3. The final chunk carries the real usage `{"completion_tokens":16,"prompt_tokens":37,"total_tokens":53,"completion_tokens_details":{"reasoning_tokens":16},...}`, then `[DONE]` #### Non-streaming /v1/messages 1. Same curl as the before leg 2. Observed HTTP 200 with `"content":[],"stop_reason":"max_tokens"`, usage 37 in / 16 out, cost 0.000665, unchanged from before #### Streaming /v1/messages 1. Same request with `"stream": true` 2. Observed the same `message_start` / `message_delta` with `"stop_reason": "max_tokens"` and usage 37 / 16 / `message_stop`, unchanged The Anthropic shape already reported the truncation honestly at the merge base, so the fix lands only on the OpenAI chat completions shape and /v1/messages stays where it was ### Re-run at the tip (16bba15434, port 55643) The same four cases, driven again against a proxy booted from the current head with `PYTHONPATH` pinned to that worktree and the loaded `litellm.__file__` asserted to sit inside it: 1. Non-streaming /v1/chat/completions: `HTTP/1.1 200 OK`, `"finish_reason":"length"`, `reasoning_items` present, `"usage":{"completion_tokens":16,"prompt_tokens":37,"total_tokens":53,"completion_tokens_details":{"reasoning_tokens":16}}`, billed `x-litellm-response-cost: 0.000665` 2. Streaming /v1/chat/completions: terminal chunk `{"choices":[{"index":0,"delta":{},"finish_reason":"length"}]}` followed by the real usage chunk and `[DONE]` 3. Non-streaming /v1/messages: HTTP 200 with `"content":[],"stop_reason":"max_tokens"`, usage 37 in / 16 out, cost 0.000665 4. Streaming /v1/messages: `message_start`, `message_delta` carrying `{"stop_reason": "max_tokens"}` with usage 37 / 16, `message_stop` ### Surprises - Truncated calls now bill; the 500 billed nothing (causes) - Streamed chunks omit the reasoning items non-streaming returns (leaves alone) - Cost headers read zero on every streamed call (leaves alone) - /v1/messages already reported max_tokens before the fix (leaves alone) - message_start echoes responses/gpt-5.6-sol, not the alias (leaves alone) ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR <!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY --> --- > [!NOTE] > **Medium Risk** > Changes how truncated/incomplete Responses API results are mapped into chat completions, including finish_reason and usage/billing. Wrong mapping would mis-signal truncation or still 500, but the change is isolated to the bridge transformer. > > **Overview** > Chat completions through the Responses bridge no longer 500 when a reasoning model burns the whole token budget. Incomplete Responses API results now look like native OpenAI truncation: HTTP 200, `finish_reason` `length` (or `content_filter`), and real usage. > > If there is no message (reasoning-only output), the bridge emits one empty assistant choice and still round-trips `reasoning_items`. Partial text is kept and only the finish reason is overridden. Streaming treats `response.incomplete` like `response.completed`, so the terminal chunk carries the mapped finish reason and usage instead of `stop` with no spend. Unknown empty completed responses still raise. > > <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 16bba154347de9793cce83f94c13caa85e7492e6. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. signals.title: fix: don't retire a completed batch from cost recovery while output_file_id is lagging
signals.text: ## TLDR **Problem:** In `openai_files_endpoints/common_utils.py`, when a batch's `db_status` becomes `"complete"`, `update_data["batch_processed"] = True` was set **unconditionally**. `batch_processed=True` is the sole re-pickup gate for `CheckBatchCost`'s cost-recovery poller (`_find_jobs` selects on `batch_processed=False`). But a batch can legitimately reach `status="completed"` while `output_file_id` is still `None` — the provider response briefly lags before the output id populates. Retiring the batch in that window permanently removes it from every future cost-recovery pass, silently losing the spend record with no retry. **Fix:** Only retire a completed batch once it is provably safe — the output file has actually arrived (`output_file_id` is set), or the provider reports no successful request lines (`request_counts.completed == 0`, i.e. nothing to recover). When counts are unknown, stay eligible so the next poller pass revisits it. Fixes #37713 ## Changes - `litellm/proxy/openai_files_endpoints/common_utils.py` - Add `_completed_batch_safe_to_retire(response)`. - Gate the `batch_processed = True` assignment on it. ## Testing Added `TestCompletedBatchSafeToRetire` in `tests/test_litellm/proxy/openai_files_endpoint/test_files_common_utils.py`: - output file present → safe to retire - no output + `completed == 0` (all lines errored) → safe to retire - **no output + `completed > 0` (lagging output) → NOT retired** (the bug) - no output + unknown counts → NOT retired ``` tests/.../test_files_common_utils.py::TestCompletedBatchSafeToRetire ... 4 passed ```

signals.title: fix(proxy): rewrap chained batch output file IDs
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Completed chained batches expose upstream file IDs - The front proxy cannot fetch those results How it solves it: - Registers unknown upstream managed IDs under the front deployment - Preserves IDs already registered by the front proxy ## User Flow Before: a developer can create and complete a batch through the front proxy, but cannot download its results there 1. They POST https://front-proxy/v1/files with a batch JSONL file 2. They POST https://front-proxy/v1/batches with that returned input file ID 3. GET https://front-proxy/v1/batches/{batch_id} returns `completed` and an output file ID 4. GET https://front-proxy/v1/files/{output_file_id}/content returns a routing error After: the same completed batch result is fetched through the front proxy 1. They POST https://front-proxy/v1/files with the same batch JSONL file 2. They POST https://front-proxy/v1/batches with that returned input file ID 3. GET https://front-proxy/v1/batches/{batch_id} returns `completed` and a front proxy output file ID 4. GET https://front-proxy/v1/files/{output_file_id}/content returns the JSONL result ## Relevant issues Fixes #37352 ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] Focused regression tests pass locally - [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile Confidence Score of at least 4/5 before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Live two-proxy verification needs credentials and a runnable Postgres-backed proxy environment, which are unavailable in this workspace. The focused provider-free regression tests verify that an unknown upstream managed output ID is rewrapped and a front-proxy-registered ID is unchanged ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - Draft pending live two-proxy curl verification and CI ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests cover chained output rewrapping and registered-ID preservation

signals.title: feat(integrations): add Openlayer as an OTEL logging callback
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Openlayer had no named callback in LiteLLM - Routing traces there meant hand-writing OTLP env vars - One of those header values contains a colon - The endpoint is easy to get wrong and 404s How it solves it: - Adds an `openlayer` callback for SDK and proxy - Reads two env vars, plus one optional override - Builds the endpoint and headers for the user - Works on both the v1 and v2 OTel paths ## User Flow Before: an engineer who wants their gateway traffic in Openlayer sets `callbacks: ["openlayer"]`, and the gateway will not start 1. They put `callbacks: ["openlayer"]` under `litellm_settings` in `config.yaml` 2. They start the gateway and it exits during startup with `ValueError: Empty module name` 3. `POST http://0.0.0.0:4000/v1/chat/completions` returns nothing: `curl: (7) Failed to connect to 0.0.0.0 port 4000` 4. To get traces flowing they instead hand-write `OTEL_ENDPOINT` and a two-part `OTEL_HEADERS` string, and a wrong endpoint path silently 404s every export After: the same config starts, and their requests show up in Openlayer with model, tokens and cost 1. They set `OPENLAYER_API_KEY` and `OPENLAYER_INFERENCE_PIPELINE_ID`, keep `callbacks: ["openlayer"]`, and start the gateway 2. The gateway starts and answers `GET http://0.0.0.0:4000/health/liveliness` 3. They send `POST http://0.0.0.0:4000/v1/chat/completions` with `gpt-4o-mini` and get `HTTP 200` with a completion and a usage object 4. They open the Data view of their inference pipeline and see that request as a row carrying provider `OpenAI`, model `gpt-4o-mini`, prompt and completion token counts, cost and latency ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more - [x] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Shared setup for every case below. `config.yaml`: ```yaml model_list: - model_name: gpt-4o-mini litellm_params: model: openai/gpt-4o-mini api_key: os.environ/OPENAI_API_KEY litellm_settings: callbacks: ["openlayer"] ``` Environment, with a real OpenAI key and a real Openlayer workspace key and pipeline: ```shell export OPENAI_API_KEY="sk-proj-..." export OPENLAYER_API_KEY="sk-ol-..." export OPENLAYER_INFERENCE_PIPELINE_ID="cb47e4f7-15a0-4e70-bd6e-7b1b4b54e434" export LITELLM_MASTER_KEY=sk-1234 export OTEL_INSTRUMENTATION_GENAI_CAPTURE_MESSAGE_CONTENT=span_and_event ``` Start command, and the request every case sends: ```shell python -m litellm.proxy.proxy_cli --config config.yaml --port 4000 curl -sS -w 'HTTP %{http_code}\n' -L -X POST 'http://0.0.0.0:4000/v1/chat/completions' \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-1234' \ -d '{"model": "gpt-4o-mini", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Reply with one word: proxy-qa"}], "max_tokens": 16}' ``` These are real OpenAI calls billed to a real key, and the rows below are real rows read back from the Openlayer API ### Before (abdde94ad5) 1. Start the gateway with the config above: ``` File "litellm/proxy/common_utils/callback_utils.py", line 375, in initialize_callbacks_on_proxy File "litellm/proxy/types_utils/utils.py", line 65, in get_instance_fn ValueError: Empty module name ``` 2. The process exits during startup, so the request never reaches a provider: ``` curl: (7) Failed to connect to 0.0.0.0 port 4000 after 0 ms: Could not connect to server HTTP 000 ``` 3. Nothing arrives in the Openlayer pipeline, because nothing was ever sent ### After (4eb7bfdf8e) #### Default, no `LITELLM_OTEL_V2` 1. Start the gateway with the same config. It starts, and `GET /health/liveliness` answers 2. Send the request: ``` HTTP 200 id : chatcmpl-EF692thMQe6ejk1fIb2CPiSbq2xee content: 'Understood.' usage : {'completion_tokens': 3, 'prompt_tokens': 18, 'total_tokens': 21} ``` 3. Read the row back from the pipeline. The trace arrives with the gateway request at the root and the model call nested under it: ``` root: Received Proxy Server Request latency=3068ms status=success - auth - proxy_pre_call - litellm_request provider=OpenAI model=gpt-4o-mini - raw_gen_ai_request - router ``` #### `LITELLM_OTEL_V2=true` 1. Start the gateway with `LITELLM_OTEL_V2=true` and the same config 2. Send the request: ``` HTTP 200 id : chatcmpl-EF6DRPVVK9JhQ6e3CafJUBq6k4ywr content: 'Understood.' usage : {'completion_tokens': 3, 'prompt_tokens': 19, 'total_tokens': 22} ``` 3. Read the row back from the pipeline. Provider, model, token counts and cost are all populated, and the model call is typed as a chat completion: ``` inference_id: fSxA3MFZj7OHT15to7+Gmg== provider = OpenAI model = gpt-4o-mini openlayer_cost = 4.649999e-06 promptTokens = 19 completionTokens = 3 openlayer_latency = 137.311 status = success - chat gpt-4o-mini type=chat_completion provider=OpenAI model=gpt-4o-mini cost=4.649999e-06 ``` ## Type 🆕 New Feature ## Caveats (if any) - Cost lands on the v2 path, not the default path - Response text needs an Openlayer-side ingest fix, in flight - No per-request team or key credentials yet - v2 needs `opentelemetry-api` 1.40 or older ## Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signals.title: fix(model-costs): correct gpt-5.6 max input tokens to 922k
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - gpt-5.6 registry entries reported the context window as the input cap - We advertised 1,050,000 max input tokens instead of 922,000 How it solves it: - Set `max_input_tokens` to 922000 for all gpt-5.6 entries - Covers openai plus azure global, us, eu variants - Pins the corrected value in the existing cost-map tests ## User Flow Before: a developer sizing prompts from the gateway's model metadata trusts a cap that OpenAI and Azure will reject 1. They send GET https://litellm-domain/public/litellm_model_cost_map 2. `gpt-5.6-sol` comes back with `"max_input_tokens": 1050000`, matching the 1,050,000 context window rather than the published 922,000 input cap 3. They build a 1,000,000 token prompt against that number and the upstream provider rejects the request After: the same lookup reports the cap the provider actually enforces 1. They send GET https://litellm-domain/public/litellm_model_cost_map 2. `gpt-5.6-sol` comes back with `"max_input_tokens": 922000`, matching what OpenAI and Azure publish 3. They size prompts to 922,000 tokens and the request goes through ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more - [x] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Shared setup, proxy serving the registry from the working tree: ```bash sudo service postgresql start LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True uv run --no-sync litellm --config litellm/proxy/dev_config.yaml --port 4000 ``` ### Before (996693f1eb) 1. Query the registry the gateway serves ```bash curl -sS "http://localhost:4000/public/litellm_model_cost_map" | jq '{sol: .["gpt-5.6-sol"].max_input_tokens, azure_luna: .["azure/gpt-5.6-luna"].max_input_tokens, gpt55: .["gpt-5.5"].max_input_tokens, bedrock_mantle_sol: .["bedrock_mantle/openai.gpt-5.6-sol"].max_input_tokens}' ``` ```json { "sol": 1050000, "azure_luna": 1050000, "gpt55": 1050000, "bedrock_mantle_sol": 1000000 } ``` 2. Compare against what the providers publish: OpenAI's [gpt-5.6-sol page](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-5.6-sol.md) lists a 1,050,000 context window with "Maximum input tokens: 922,000", and Microsoft's [Azure model table](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/ai-foundry/openai/concepts/models) lists the same 1,050,000 / Input: 922,000 / Output: 128,000 for gpt-5.6-sol, -terra and -luna, so the 1,050,000 we served was the context window ### After (6bb677d30f) 1. Query the registry the gateway serves ```bash curl -sS "http://localhost:4000/public/litellm_model_cost_map" | jq '{sol: .["gpt-5.6-sol"].max_input_tokens, azure_luna: .["azure/gpt-5.6-luna"].max_input_tokens, gpt55: .["gpt-5.5"].max_input_tokens, bedrock_mantle_sol: .["bedrock_mantle/openai.gpt-5.6-sol"].max_input_tokens}' ``` ```json { "sol": 922000, "azure_luna": 922000, "gpt55": 1050000, "bedrock_mantle_sol": 1000000 } ``` 2. gpt-5.6 now matches the published 922,000 input cap, and the deliberately untouched entries (gpt-5.5 and the Bedrock Mantle ones) are unchanged ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - gpt-5.5 untouched: OpenAI publishes no separate input cap - Bedrock Mantle gpt-5.6 left at 1,000,000, AWS-specific and unverified Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/c63cc0412baf427d829e85bb79a7426f Requested by: @mateo-berri <!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY --> --- > [!NOTE] > **Low Risk** > Pricing JSON metadata only; no runtime logic, auth, or billing formula changes. Clients that sized prompts to 1.05M may now see a lower advertised cap. > > **Overview** > Corrects `max_input_tokens` for gpt-5.6 from **1,050,000** (the full context window) to **922,000**, matching the published OpenAI/Azure input cap. > > Applies to OpenAI `gpt-5.6` / `sol` / `terra` / `luna` and Azure global, US, and EU variants. Cost-map tests now pin `922000`. gpt-5.5 and Bedrock Mantle entries are unchanged. > > <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 6bb677d30f672c1e498b8eacbbf28d1ab42d3f6e. signals.title: fix: map Gemini ON_DEMAND_FLEX traffic type to flex service tier
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Vertex AI flex-tier requests are silently billed at standard rate. How it solves it: - Map the `ON_DEMAND_FLEX` traffic type to the `flex` service tier. ## User Flow Before: a developer runs Gemini/Vertex AI requests that opt into flex/shared capacity, and their spend dashboard bills those requests at the standard rate. 1. They send a Vertex AI `generateContent` request that opts into flex capacity. 2. The response comes back served at flex tier (its usage metadata reports the flex traffic type). 3. Their LiteLLM spend for that request is computed at the standard input/output price, with no signal that flex was actually applied. After: the same request is billed at the flex-tier price it was actually served at. 1. They send the same Vertex AI `generateContent` request that opts into flex capacity. 2. The response comes back served at flex tier. 3. LiteLLM now bills that request at the flex-tier price. ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix ![before: 2 failed on ON_DEMAND_FLEX / after: 8 passed](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9830893b-a43e-45fd-9efc-6da6e0bfe016) This is an internal cost-attribution mapping. `_map_traffic_type_to_service_tier` converts the provider-reported traffic type into the service tier that selects the `_flex` / `_priority` cost keys. Before this change the `ON_DEMAND_FLEX` value that Vertex AI reports for flex traffic was absent from the map, so it fell through to `None` (standard pricing). Setup (both sides), in a venv with litellm installed: ``` python -m pytest tests/test_litellm/llms/gemini/test_cost_calculator.py::test_map_traffic_type_to_service_tier -q ``` ### Before (007bd43) Direct call against the unpatched mapping: 1. `_map_traffic_type_to_service_tier("ON_DEMAND_FLEX")` returns `None` (billed as standard). 2. `_map_traffic_type_to_service_tier("FLEX")` returns `"flex"` (only the non-Vertex spelling was mapped). 3. The added regression test fails on the flex cases: ``` E AssertionError: assert None == 'flex' E + where None = _map_traffic_type_to_service_tier('on_demand_flex') FAILED ...::test_map_traffic_type_to_service_tier[ON_DEMAND_FLEX-flex] FAILED ...::test_map_traffic_type_to_service_tier[on_demand_flex-flex] 2 failed, 6 passed in 1.24s ``` ### After (c4383b3) Same call against the patched mapping: 1. `_map_traffic_type_to_service_tier("ON_DEMAND_FLEX")` returns `"flex"` (billed at flex tier). 2. `_map_traffic_type_to_service_tier("FLEX")` / `"BATCH"` still return `"flex"`; `"ON_DEMAND"` still returns `None`. 3. The full test passes: ``` 8 passed, 2 warnings in 0.29s ``` ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ✅ Test ## Caveats (if any) - A fully live Vertex AI flex-capacity request needs Vertex credentials and a flex-priced model; verified at the mapping and unit-test layer. ## QA runbook - tests/test_litellm/llms/gemini/test_cost_calculator.py::test_map_traffic_type_to_service_tier - the Gemini/Vertex traffic type maps to the service tier that selects flex/priority cost keys, and `ON_DEMAND_FLEX` maps to `flex`. - [ ] In a venv with litellm installed, run `python -m pytest tests/test_litellm/llms/gemini/test_cost_calculator.py::test_map_traffic_type_to_service_tier -q` - [ ] Expect 8 passed, including the `ON_DEMAND_FLEX` and `on_demand_flex` cases mapping to `flex` - [ ] Sanity check: this test asserts the exact tier string per traffic type (not just non-None), so an unmapped flex value fails it ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR Fixes #37647
