signal.title: fix(auth): return 403 for admin-only route denials
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Admin-only route denials return 401 instead of 403 - Prometheus records them as `exception_status="None"` - Those denials look identical to infrastructure failures How it solves it: - Raise `HTTPException` 403 instead of a bare `Exception` - The status code then reaches both the client and the metric ## User Flow Before: a developer holding a valid non-admin key is told their credentials are invalid, so they re-authenticate and nothing changes 1. An admin issues them a key with the `internal_user` role 2. They send `GET https://litellm-domain/policies/list` with that key 3. It comes back `401 Unauthorized`, and the message opens with "Authentication Error, Only proxy admin can be used to generate, delete, update info for new keys/users/teams" 4. Reading 401 as a credential problem, their client drops the key, signs in again, retries, and gets the same 401 5. Their operator opens the proxy metrics and finds the refusal recorded with `exception_class="Exception"` and `exception_status="None"` on `route="/policies/list"`, the same label pair an unreachable database produces, so it cannot be alerted on separately 6. A non-admin still cannot reach the route, and an admin still can After: the same request is refused as forbidden, so the client keeps its key and the metric names the status 1. An admin issues them a key with the `internal_user` role 2. They send `GET https://litellm-domain/policies/list` with that key 3. It comes back `403 Forbidden` with the same explanation and no "Authentication Error" prefix 4. Their client keeps the key and stops re-authenticating, because 403 says the credential is fine and the permission is not 5. Their operator finds the refusal recorded with `exception_class="HTTPException"` and `exception_status="403"`, now distinguishable from an infrastructure failure 6. A non-admin still cannot reach the route, and an admin still can. Who may call what is unchanged, only how the refusal is reported ## Relevant issues Fixes #37108 ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Shared setup, run once against a local proxy on `localhost:4000` backed by a scratch Postgres, with `callbacks: ["prometheus"]` enabled: ```bash export MASTER=sk-1234 USERKEY=$(curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4000/user/new \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $MASTER" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"user_email":"nonadmin@example.com","user_role":"internal_user"}' \ | python -c "import sys,json; print(json.load(sys.stdin)['key'])") ``` ### Before (973329e9864154d429a7d739fb6a552fe03a9b3e) 1. Call two admin-only routes with the valid non-admin key ```bash for r in /policies/list /prompts/list; do printf "GET %-16s -> " "$r" curl -s -o /tmp/b.json -w "%{http_code}" "http://127.0.0.1:4000$r" -H "Authorization: Bearer $USERKEY" echo " $(head -c 120 /tmp/b.json)" done ``` ``` GET /policies/list -> 401 {"error":{"message":"Authentication Error, Only proxy admin can be used to generate, delete, update GET /prompts/list -> 401 {"error":{"message":"Authentication Error, Only proxy admin can be used to generate, delete, update ``` 2. Read the failure metric for those two routes ```bash curl -sL http://127.0.0.1:4000/metrics -H "Authorization: Bearer $MASTER" \ | grep -oE 'exception_class="[^"]*",exception_status="[^"]*"[^}]*route="/(policies|prompts)/list"' ``` ``` exception_class="Exception",exception_status="None",...,route="/policies/list" exception_class="Exception",exception_status="None",...,route="/prompts/list" ``` ### After (2a0f2b6171) 1. Same two calls, same key ```bash for r in /policies/list /prompts/list; do printf "GET %-16s -> " "$r" curl -s -o /tmp/b.json -w "%{http_code}" "http://127.0.0.1:4000$r" -H "Authorization: Bearer $USERKEY" echo " $(head -c 120 /tmp/b.json)" done ``` ``` GET /policies/list -> 403 {"error":{"message":"Only proxy admin can be used to generate, delete, update info for new keys/us GET /prompts/list -> 403 {"error":{"message":"Only proxy admin can be used to generate, delete, update info for new keys/us ``` 2. Same metric read ```bash curl -sL http://127.0.0.1:4000/metrics -H "Authorization: Bearer $MASTER" \ | grep -oE 'exception_class="[^"]*",exception_status="[^"]*"[^}]*route="/(policies|prompts)/list"' ``` ``` exception_class="HTTPException",exception_status="403",...,route="/policies/list" exception_class="HTTPException",exception_status="403",...,route="/prompts/list" ``` ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - Clients treating 401 as "retry auth" see a status change - Master-key-only routes still raise a bare `Exception`, left out of scope - `/organization/list` and `/team/list` from the issue are already allowed for `internal_user` ## Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signal.title: feat(together_ai): capability baseline, reasoning controls, and a current model map
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Unmapped Together models silently lost tool calling - Structured outputs dropped alongside them - Reasoning controls never reached any Together model - Mapped per-model rates were shadowed by parameter-count buckets - Cache hits with no published discount billed as free - Calls went to the legacy api.together.xyz host - Model map missed most of today's serverless catalog How it solves it: - Provider-level capability baseline - Reasoning, logprobs and max_tokens mapped to Together's shapes - Size buckets now price only what the map does not - A cache hit falls back to the standard input rate - Catalog refreshed, with cached-input rates - Default base URL is now the documented api.together.ai ## User Flow Before: a developer building an agent on a model Together launched this week gets no tool calls back, cannot turn thinking off, and sees the wrong spend 1. They add `together_ai/moonshotai/Kimi-K3` to their proxy config and restart 2. They send POST http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions with that model, a `tools` array holding one `get_weather` function, and "What is the weather in Paris? Use the tool." 3. The reply is prose, "I don't have access to a weather tool or any real-time data sources", with no `tool_calls` array, so their agent loop has nothing to execute 4. On a proxy without `drop_params` the same request fails outright with 500 `together_ai does not support parameters: ['tools']` 5. They switch to `together_ai/Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B` and send `"reasoning_effort": "none"` to skip thinking on a simple question; the answer still arrives behind 1093 characters of chain of thought, and they pay for those tokens 6. They send a 4.7k-token prompt to Kimi K3 twice and read the `x-litellm-response-cost` response header: it is empty, so the call lands in their dashboard at zero spend 7. They repeat the same prompt against `together_ai/meta-llama/Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct-Turbo` and the header reads `0.0042876` every time, which is $0.90 per 1M tokens rather than the $1.04 Together publishes, and the response `usage` carries no cached-token count for their cache-hit dashboard After: the same requests return tool calls, thinking is controllable, and the spend numbers match Together's published rates 1. They add `together_ai/moonshotai/Kimi-K3` to their proxy config and restart 2. They send POST http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions with that model, a `tools` array holding one `get_weather` function, and "What is the weather in Paris? Use the tool." 3. The reply comes back with `finish_reason: "tool_calls"` and a `tool_calls` array naming `get_weather` with `{"location": "Paris"}`, so the agent loop runs 4. `"response_format": {"type": "json_schema", ...}` on the same model returns schema-shaped JSON instead of a 500 5. On `together_ai/Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B`, `"reasoning_effort": "none"` returns the answer with no chain of thought at all, and the same request without it still thinks 6. They send a 4.7k-token prompt to Kimi K3 twice: the first call's `x-litellm-response-cost` reads `0.0141018` and the second, hitting Together's warm prefix, reads `0.0015441`, a 9x drop that shows up in their dashboard 7. The same prompt against Llama 3.3 70B Instruct Turbo reads `0.00495456`, matching Together's published $1.04 per 1M, and the response `usage` now reports `prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens` so their cache-hit dashboard is no longer stuck at zero ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more - [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Both sides ran against the same live Together AI account, one proxy per side, with `LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True` so the bundled map is the one under test. `qa_config.yaml`: ```yaml model_list: - model_name: kimi-k3 litellm_params: model: together_ai/moonshotai/Kimi-K3 api_key: os.environ/TOGETHER_API_KEY - model_name: llama-3.3-70b litellm_params: model: together_ai/meta-llama/Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct-Turbo api_key: os.environ/TOGETHER_API_KEY - model_name: qwen3.5-9b litellm_params: model: together_ai/Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B api_key: os.environ/TOGETHER_API_KEY litellm_settings: drop_params: True telemetry: False general_settings: master_key: sk-1234 ``` ```bash LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config qa_config.yaml --port 4010 ``` Cases 3 and 4 send a 4.7k-token prefix twice so Together's automatic prefix cache is cold on the first call and warm on the second. Cache hits are best-effort, so the warm call does not always land. ### Before (66a89f5a6e) #### Tool calling on a model the cost map does not know 1. `curl -sS localhost:4010/v1/chat/completions -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-1234' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d @case1_tools.json | jq -c '{finish_reason: .choices[0].finish_reason, tool_calls: .choices[0].message.tool_calls, content_head: (.choices[0].message.content // "" | .[0:80])}'` 2. `{"finish_reason":"stop","tool_calls":null,"content_head":"I don't have access to a weather tool or any real-time data sources. The only to"}` #### Turning thinking off on a hybrid model 1. `curl -sS localhost:4010/v1/chat/completions -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-1234' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"model":"qwen3.5-9b","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Is 9.11 bigger than 9.9? Answer in one short sentence."}],"reasoning_effort":"none","max_tokens":600}' | jq -c '{reasoning_chars: (.choices[0].message.reasoning_content // "" | length), content_head: (.choices[0].message.content // "" | .[0:60])}'` 2. `{"reasoning_chars":1093,"content_head":"No, 9.9 is bigger than 9.11."}` #### Cost and cached input on Kimi K3 1. `for i in 1 2; do curl -sS -D h.txt localhost:4010/v1/chat/completions -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-1234' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d @case3_cache.json | jq -c .usage; grep -i '^x-litellm-response-cost:' h.txt; done` 2. call 1: `x-litellm-response-cost:` (empty) with `{"completion_tokens":8,"prompt_tokens":4747,"total_tokens":4755,"prompt_tokens_details":{"cached_tokens":64}}` 3. call 2: `x-litellm-response-cost:` (empty) with `{"completion_tokens":8,"prompt_tokens":4747,"total_tokens":4755,"prompt_tokens_details":{"cached_tokens":64}}` #### Published rate and flat cached tokens on Llama 3.3 70B 1. `for i in 1 2; do curl -sS -D h.txt localhost:4010/v1/chat/completions -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-1234' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d @case4_flat.json | jq -c '{usage, cached_via_details: .usage.prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens}'; grep -i '^x-litellm-response-cost:' h.txt; done` 2. call 1: `x-litellm-response-cost: 0.0042876` with `{"usage":{"completion_tokens":2,"prompt_tokens":4762,"total_tokens":4764,"cached_tokens":0},"cached_via_details":null}` 3. call 2: `x-litellm-response-cost: 0.0042876` with `{"usage":{"completion_tokens":2,"prompt_tokens":4762,"total_tokens":4764,"cached_tokens":4608},"cached_via_details":null}` ### After (0106e21b61) #### Tool calling on a model the cost map does not know 1. `curl -sS localhost:4010/v1/chat/completions -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-1234' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d @case1_tools.json | jq -c '{finish_reason: .choices[0].finish_reason, tool_calls: .choices[0].message.tool_calls, content_head: (.choices[0].message.content // "" | .[0:80])}'` 2. `{"finish_reason":"tool_calls","tool_calls":[{"function":{"arguments":"{\"location\":\"Paris\"}","name":"get_weather"},"id":"get_weather_0","type":"function"}],"content_head":"I'll check the current weather in Paris for you."}` #### Turning thinking off on a hybrid model 1. `curl -sS localhost:4010/v1/chat/completions -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-1234' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"model":"qwen3.5-9b","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Is 9.11 bigger than 9.9? Answer in one short sentence."}],"reasoning_effort":"none","max_tokens":600}' | jq -c '{reasoning_chars: (.choices[0].message.reasoning_content // "" | length), content_head: (.choices[0].message.content // "" | .[0:60])}'` 2. `{"reasoning_chars":0,"content_head":"No, 9.11 is smaller than 9.9."}` #### Cost and cached input on Kimi K3 1. `for i in 1 2; do curl -sS -D h.txt localhost:4010/v1/chat/completions -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-1234' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d @case3_cache.json | jq -c .usage; grep -i '^x-litellm-response-cost:' h.txt; done` 2. call 1 (cold): `x-litellm-response-cost: 0.014101800000000001` with `{"completion_tokens":8,"prompt_tokens":4747,"total_tokens":4755,"prompt_tokens_details":{"cached_tokens":96}}` 3. call 2 (warm): `x-litellm-response-cost: 0.0015441` with `{"completion_tokens":8,"prompt_tokens":4747,"total_tokens":4755,"prompt_tokens_details":{"cached_tokens":4747}}` #### Published rate and flat cached tokens on Llama 3.3 70B 1. `for i in 1 2; do curl -sS -D h.txt localhost:4010/v1/chat/completions -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-1234' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d @case4_flat.json | jq -c '{usage, cached_via_details: .usage.prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens}'; grep -i '^x-litellm-response-cost:' h.txt; done` 2. call 1 (cold): `x-litellm-response-cost: 0.004954559999999999` with `{"usage":{"completion_tokens":2,"prompt_tokens":4762,"total_tokens":4764,"prompt_tokens_details":{"cached_tokens":0},"cached_tokens":0},"cached_via_details":0}` 3. call 2 (warm): `x-litellm-response-cost: 0.00495456` with `{"usage":{"completion_tokens":2,"prompt_tokens":4762,"total_tokens":4764,"prompt_tokens_details":{"cached_tokens":4608},"cached_tokens":4608},"cached_via_details":4608}` Llama 3.3 70B publishes no cached-input discount, so its warm call costs the same as the cold one; what changes is the rate ($1.04 per 1M rather than the bucket's $0.90) and the cached count now reaching `prompt_tokens_details`. ## Type 🆕 New Feature 🐛 Bug Fix 🧹 Refactoring ## Caveats (if any) - basedpyright not run locally; left to CI - api.together.xyz still works; only the default moved - Llama 3.3 70B and Gemma 4 31B spend rises to published rates - Cache-rate fallback touches every provider, raising previously free hits - Rerank untouched, still ignores a custom api base - Retired catalog entries kept, so old spend still resolves - `max_output_tokens` omitted where Together publishes no cap ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signal.title: fix(logging): stop billing and logging response reads as LLM calls
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Reading a stored response bills its tokens again - Every read writes a second spend log row - Read/management calls log as normal chat calls - Their spans carry a fake `default-message-value` prompt How it solves it: - Read/management call types are priced at 0 - They report no usage, so no tokens are re-counted - No placeholder chat message is logged for them - Response reads get a `litellm.responses_management` operation name - Vector store and vector store file management call types are classified the same way ## User Flow Before: a developer polling a background response is charged again on every poll, so their spend for one generation keeps growing while they only read it 1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/responses with `{"model": "gpt-4o", "input": "hello"}` and get back `resp_...` plus an `x-litellm-response-cost: 0.03` header 2. They send GET https://litellm-domain/v1/responses/resp_... to check on it, and get 200 with the same stored output 3. They open https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs and see two rows for one generation: the create at 6000 tokens, and the read logged as another 6000 token call 4. Polling ten times leaves ten extra rows counting the same tokens, and each read shows up in the same charts as their real chat traffic 5. Deleting a vector store at DELETE https://litellm-domain/v1/vector_stores/vs_... also shows up as a call with a `default-message-value` prompt After: the same polling costs nothing and the read is visibly a management operation, not a generation 1. They send the same POST https://litellm-domain/v1/responses and get back `resp_...` plus `x-litellm-response-cost: 0.03` 2. They send the same GET https://litellm-domain/v1/responses/resp_... and get 200 with the same stored output, now with no cost header 3. https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs shows the create at 6000 tokens and $0.03, and the read at 0 tokens and $0 4. Polling ten times adds no tokens and no spend, and the reads carry a `litellm.responses_management` operation instead of landing in the chat series 5. The vector store delete is logged with no prompt at all instead of a made-up one ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5602 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Same commands run against a live proxy on localhost:4000 before the fix (at `0a25756e78`) and after it (at `6285192141`). The environment this was captured in cannot reach `api.openai.com`, so the OpenAI base URL pointed at a local server returning a real-shaped Responses object with 4000 input / 2000 output tokens: the double billing is entirely in how the gateway prices the object it reads back, so the numbers below are what a real key produces too. Worth re-running against real OpenAI before merge. ```bash # 1. create a response curl -s -i -X POST localhost:4000/v1/responses \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model":"gpt-4o","input":"hello"}' | grep -iE "^(HTTP|x-litellm-response-cost:)" # 2. read it back curl -s -i localhost:4000/v1/responses/$RID \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" | grep -iE "^(HTTP|x-litellm-response-cost:)" # 3. delete a vector store curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" -X DELETE localhost:4000/v1/vector_stores/vs_... \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" # 4. what got billed psql $DATABASE_URL -c 'select call_type, spend, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, total_tokens from "LiteLLM_SpendLogs" order by "startTime" desc limit 3;' ``` Before, at `0a25756e78`. The read is priced and counted like a generation: ``` POST /v1/responses -> HTTP/1.1 200 OK x-litellm-response-cost: 0.03 GET /v1/responses/{id} -> HTTP/1.1 200 OK x-litellm-response-cost: 0.03 DELETE /v1/vector_stores/{id} -> 200 call_type | spend | prompt_tokens | completion_tokens | total_tokens ----------------------+-------+---------------+-------------------+-------------- avector_store_delete | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 aget_responses | 0.03 | 4000 | 2000 | 6000 aresponses | 0.03 | 4000 | 2000 | 6000 ``` The same reading also shows the placeholder prompt: `grep -c default-message-value` over the proxy log for those three requests returns 4 before the fix and 0 after. After, at `6285192141`. The create is unchanged, the read costs nothing and counts nothing: ``` POST /v1/responses -> HTTP/1.1 200 OK x-litellm-response-cost: 0.03 GET /v1/responses/{id} -> HTTP/1.1 200 OK (no cost header) DELETE /v1/vector_stores/{id} -> 200 call_type | spend | prompt_tokens | completion_tokens | total_tokens ----------------------+-------+---------------+-------------------+-------------- avector_store_delete | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 aget_responses | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 aresponses | 0.03 | 4000 | 2000 | 6000 ``` The `litellm.responses_management` operation name applies to the newer otel payload builders, which this proxy run did not exercise, so that part is covered by unit tests on `resolve_operation` rather than by the log above. ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - Dashboards counting these reads as spend will now read 0 - Vector store management spans keep their existing operation name - Proof captured against a local provider, not real OpenAI Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/cc8575afe61740bfa53b4548be552350 <!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY --> --- > [!NOTE] > **High Risk** > Changes spend calculation and spend-log token counts for Responses and vector-store management. A wrong origin stamp would leave background jobs unbilled or keep double-charging user polls. > > **Overview** > Stops double-billing stored Responses (and other read/management routes) that replay the original call’s usage. User-facing get/delete/cancel/list and vector-store management now cost **$0**, report **0 tokens**, and no longer log a fake `default-message-value` prompt. > > Adds `NON_INFERENCE_CALL_TYPES` plus `is_unbilled_non_inference_call`, wired into cost calc, standard logging payloads, and spend logs. OTel maps those response routes to `litellm.responses_management` instead of chat. > > **Exception:** the background cost poller stamps `background_response_cost_poll` so its `aget_responses` still bills—queued jobs only expose usage on that poll. Create (`aresponses`) is unchanged. > > <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 120072c72a25ba4ee7c04c21fbf0d15fea972dd8. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup> <!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

signal.title: [Bug]: DeepSeek thinking-mode warnings scale with replayed history and obscure useful logs
signal.text: ### Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. ### What happened? When using the LiteLLM Python SDK with DeepSeek thinking mode and multi-turn tool calling, DeepSeek may return a successful assistant tool-call response containing: ```json { "role": "assistant", "content": "", "reasoning_content": "", "tool_calls": [...] } ``` This can be a real provider response rather than a client-side loss of reasoning content. In one recorded mini-swe-agent run, the preserved raw response objects contained `reasoning_content: ""`, while DeepSeek reported: ```json { "completion_tokens_details": { "reasoning_tokens": 0 } } ``` All six affected responses completed normally with `finish_reason: "tool_calls"` and valid tool calls. The DeepSeek Chat Completions API is stateless, so clients resend the conversation history on subsequent requests: [https://api-docs.deepseek.com/guides/multi_round_chat/](https://api-docs.deepseek.com/guides/multi_round_chat/) When LiteLLM receives an empty historical `reasoning_content`, it replaces `""` with a single-space placeholder so that DeepSeek accepts the request. It also emits this warning for every affected assistant message: ```text DeepSeek thinking mode: assistant message is missing `reasoning_content` and none was saved in `provider_specific_fields`. A single-space placeholder is being injected to satisfy API validation, but the model will receive a blank reasoning chain for this turn, which may silently degrade multi-turn response quality. Preserve `reasoning_content` from the original assistant response when building multi-turn conversation history. ``` The compatibility handling works, and warning that LiteLLM modified the request can be useful. The problem is the warning cardinality. LiteLLM transforms a request copy without modifying the caller-owned conversation history. The client therefore continues to store the original `reasoning_content: ""`. Every time the complete history is submitted again, the same historical message emits the same warning again. If multiple empty-reasoning assistant messages accumulate, LiteLLM emits one identical warning for each affected historical message on every subsequent request. During a long agent run, these warnings can dominate the console and make actual errors, tool output, evaluation results, and other actionable diagnostic information difficult to locate. In one successful mini-swe-agent run: ```text LiteLLM: 1.97.0 mini-swe-agent: 2.4.6 Model: deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash Logical model calls: 41 Final agent status: Submitted ``` Six provider responses contained an explicitly present empty `reasoning_content`. They occurred at assistant responses 3, 4, 10, 11, 16, and 22. Because every later request replayed the complete history, these six affected messages appeared: ```text (41 - 3) + (41 - 4) + (41 - 10) + (41 - 11) + (41 - 16) + (41 - 22) = 180 ``` times in aggregate across subsequent request histories. This is a count of affected-message replays derived from the trajectory, not a count extracted from the console. It demonstrates how a small number of provider-returned empty values can repeatedly enter the same warning path during one successful agent run. Expected behavior: 1. Continue replacing empty historical `reasoning_content` values with a DeepSeek-compatible placeholder. 2. Continue avoiding mutation of caller-owned history. 3. Emit at most one aggregated warning per request, including the number of affected messages, for example: ```text DeepSeek thinking mode: injected single-space reasoning_content placeholders into 6 assistant messages in this request. ``` No cross-request state or permanent suppression is required. Emitting one aggregated warning again on a later request would still be reasonable. A possible implementation direction would be to count affected messages during request transformation and emit one summary warning after processing the message list. Individual message indices could optionally be logged at debug level. This is related to, but distinct from, #28045 and #31439. Those issues concern missing `reasoning_content` causing request failures. Here, the compatibility handling succeeds; the reported problem is the amplification of identical warnings during normal history replay. #### Related issues This issue is a follow-up to #28045, not a duplicate of it. #28045 reported that missing reasoning_content in DeepSeek thinking-mode history caused HTTP 400 responses. The completed fix added the current compatibility behavior for the Chat Completions path: recover saved reasoning when possible, or inject a single-space placeholder and emit a warning. That compatibility behavior is working in this report—the provider requests succeed. This issue concerns a downstream logging consequence of the fix: the warning is emitted separately for every affected historical assistant message whenever a stateless client resubmits the full conversation history. #31439 reports the corresponding missing-reasoning failure on the separate DeepSeek Anthropic-compatible /v1/messages path. This report does not cover that endpoint; it concerns repeated warnings on the LiteLLM SDK Chat Completions path. ### User Flow #### Before a hypothetical fix The SDK requests succeed, but identical per-message warnings accumulate and obscure the developer's useful terminal output. 1. The developer stores `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` in `.env` and runs `LITELLM_LOG=INFO uv run --env-file .env python -u repro.py`; the script submits a real `POST https://api.deepseek.com/beta/chat/completions` request containing two historical assistant tool-call messages whose `reasoning_content` values are `""`. 2. The developer observes that the first SDK call returns normally and prints `call 1 succeeded`, but the terminal prints the same placeholder-injection warning twice—once for each affected historical assistant message. 3. The script submits a second real `POST https://api.deepseek.com/beta/chat/completions` request with the same history, and the developer observes that it prints `call 2 succeeded`. 4. The developer observes that the same two warnings are printed again before the second result; in a longer agent conversation, these repeated warnings increasingly obscure later tool and diagnostic output. #### After a hypothetical fix The same SDK requests succeed while the developer receives one concise summary warning per request. 1. The developer stores `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` in `.env` and runs `LITELLM_LOG=INFO uv run --env-file .env python -u repro.py`; the script submits a real `POST https://api.deepseek.com/beta/chat/completions` request containing two historical assistant tool-call messages whose `reasoning_content` values are `""`. 2. The developer observes that the first SDK call returns normally and prints `call 1 succeeded`, while the terminal prints one warning stating that two assistant messages required placeholders. 3. The script submits a second real `POST https://api.deepseek.com/beta/chat/completions` request with the same history, and the developer observes that it prints `call 2 succeeded`. 4. The developer observes one summary warning before the second result; other tool and diagnostic output remains easy to locate. ### Proof the bug occurs The following reproduction uses the LiteLLM Python SDK and sends real requests to the official DeepSeek API. It does not use mocks. #### SDK setup ```text OS: Ubuntu 22.04 under WSL2 Python: 3.11 LiteLLM: 1.97.0 Provider: DeepSeek official API Model: deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash Endpoint used by LiteLLM 1.97.0: POST https://api.deepseek.com/beta/chat/completions ``` A valid DeepSeek API key was provided through the following environment variable: ```text DEEPSEEK_API_KEY=<REDACTED> ``` The actual credential is intentionally omitted. Create `repro.py`: ```python from importlib.metadata import version from litellm import completion TOOLS = [ { "type": "function", "function": { "name": "bash", "description": "Execute a bash command", "parameters": { "type": "object", "properties": { "command": {"type": "string"}, }, "required": ["command"], }, }, } ] MESSAGES = [ { "role": "user", "content": "Use bash to inspect the working directory.", }, { "role": "assistant", "content": "", "reasoning_content": "", "tool_calls": [ { "id": "call_repro_1", "type": "function", "function": { "name": "bash", "arguments": "{\"command\":\"pwd\"}", }, } ], }, { "role": "tool", "tool_call_id": "call_repro_1", "content": "/tmp", }, { "role": "assistant", "content": "", "reasoning_content": "", "tool_calls": [ { "id": "call_repro_2", "type": "function", "function": { "name": "bash", "arguments": "{\"command\":\"printf done\"}", }, } ], }, { "role": "tool", "tool_call_id": "call_repro_2", "content": "done", }, { "role": "user", "content": "Reply only with OK.", }, ] def main() -> None: print("litellm:", version("litellm")) for call_number in range(1, 3): response = completion( model="deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash", messages=MESSAGES, tools=TOOLS, reasoning_effort="medium", max_tokens=32, ) reasoning_values = [ message["reasoning_content"] for message in MESSAGES if message.get("role") == "assistant" ] print( f"call {call_number} succeeded; " f"response={response.choices[0].message.content!r}; " f"caller reasoning values={reasoning_values!r}" ) if __name__ == "__main__": main() ``` Run: ```bash LITELLM_LOG=INFO uv run --env-file .env python -u repro.py 2>&1 | tee repro.log ``` Full output: ```text litellm: 1.97.0 19:35:06 - LiteLLM:WARNING: transformation.py:87 - DeepSeek thinking mode: assistant message is missing `reasoning_content` and none was saved in `provider_specific_fields`. A single-space placeholder is being injected to satisfy API validation, but the model will receive a blank reasoning chain for this turn, which may silently degrade multi-turn response quality. Preserve `reasoning_content` from the original assistant response when building multi-turn conversation history. 19:35:06 - LiteLLM:WARNING: transformation.py:87 - DeepSeek thinking mode: assistant message is missing `reasoning_content` and none was saved in `provider_specific_fields`. A single-space placeholder is being injected to satisfy API validation, but the model will receive a blank reasoning chain for this turn, which may silently degrade multi-turn response quality. Preserve `reasoning_content` from the original assistant response when building multi-turn conversation history. call 1 succeeded; response=''; caller reasoning values=['', ''] 19:35:08 - LiteLLM:WARNING: transformation.py:87 - DeepSeek thinking mode: assistant message is missing `reasoning_content` and none was saved in `provider_specific_fields`. A single-space placeholder is being injected to satisfy API validation, but the model will receive a blank reasoning chain for this turn, which may silently degrade multi-turn response quality. signal.title: fix(fal_ai): price gpt-image-2 per size and quality from request params
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - fal bills gpt-image-2 per size and quality, litellm charged flat $0.145 - a $0.006 low-quality image was logged as $0.145, 24x over - a $0.211 high-quality 1024x1024 image was logged 31% under - the edit endpoint was priced at the generation rate How it solves it: - adds fal's published price table as keyed cost-map entries - cost calculator picks the entry from the request's size and quality - unlisted sizes and missing params fall back to the flat entry ## User Flow Before: a developer generating a high-quality 1024x1024 image with fal gpt-image-2 sees $0.145 in spend logs while fal bills them $0.211 1. They send POST http://litellm-domain/v1/images/generations with `{"model": "fal_ai/openai/gpt-image-2", "prompt": "a red bicycle", "size": "1024x1024", "quality": "hd"}` 2. The image comes back 200, and the `x-litellm-response-cost` header reads `0.145` 3. They open http://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs and the request shows $0.145 spend, though fal's dashboard bills the same call at $0.211 After: the same request is logged at fal's actual $0.211 price 1. They send POST http://litellm-domain/v1/images/generations with `{"model": "fal_ai/openai/gpt-image-2", "prompt": "a red bicycle", "size": "1024x1024", "quality": "hd"}` 2. The image comes back 200, and the `x-litellm-response-cost` header reads `0.211` 3. They open http://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs and the request shows $0.211 spend, matching fal's bill ## Relevant issues Follow-up to #37729, which added fal gpt-image-2 support with a single flat price ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/<your_test_file>.py -v`. If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Both legs boot a real DB-backed proxy from the exact commit under test (own Postgres, random free ports, `LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True`) and hit the real fal API with the same two requests, differing only in the commit the proxy was booted from ### Before (987478abe48ecec29d32c8f60ebbe49acfb83c80) Tree proof ``` /private/tmp/falqa37751-before 987478abe48ecec29d32c8f60ebbe49acfb83c80 /private/tmp/falqa37751-before/litellm/__init__.py ``` 1. hd 1024x1024 ``` curl -sS -m 180 -X POST http://127.0.0.1:41983/v1/images/generations \ -H sk-falqa-after2" ``` ```json {"request_id": "476058c0-b355-41ba-8de3-41f99114a9fc", "call_type": "aimage_generation", "spend": 0.006, "model": "fal_ai/openai/gpt-image-2", "custom_llm_provider": signal.title: feat(ui): edit the auto-router tier set with custom classifier-defined tiers
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - The auto-router form is fixed at four complexity tiers - The merged backend tier_definitions support has no UI - Operators must hand-write raw config to add a tier How it solves it: - An Edit tiers button on the existing tier list - Remove any built-in tier, restore it, or add custom tiers - New tiers take a name, a definition, and models on the same rows - Escalation, adaptive, session pinning, and display names disable with a hint - Both forms dry-run the backend validator before every save - An untouched form still submits a byte-identical payload ## User Flow Before: an operator who wants a SECURITY_REVIEW tier cannot express it in the form 1. They open http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=models-and-endpoints, Add Model, Auto Router tab, expand Detailed Configuration 2. The Complexity Tier Configuration section shows exactly four tiers with no way to add or remove one 3. Their only options are renaming a tier or hand-writing tier_definitions in raw config and restarting the proxy After: the same tier list edits in place 1. They open the same section and click Edit tiers under the tier list 2. Each tier row gains a Remove button; Add tier appends a row asking for a name, a definition, and models 3. They name it SECURITY_REVIEW, write the definition the classifier routes on, pick its models, and pick a Fallback Tier 4. Classification Method locks to LLM Classifier, and escalation, adaptive, session pinning, and display names grey out with a one-line reason each 5. Submitting creates the router; the same editor appears in the Edit Auto Router modal and round-trips a stored custom config without losing keys ## Relevant issues Builds on #37226 and #37409 (both merged). Supersedes #37246: same feature rebuilt at less than half the diff by rendering built-in and custom tiers through one row renderer and letting the merged dry-run endpoint replace hand-mirrored validation ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5214 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more - [x] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix UI screenshots to be posted from the steps in the User Flow against `npm run dev` on port 3000. The wire behavior below ran against a live proxy on port 4471 from this branch, hitting real provider APIs ### Before (2dcd453860, staging) #### Create a custom-tier router 1. The form cannot express tier_definitions; the only path is hand-written raw config ### After (f13a7bcdeb) #### Create a custom-tier router with the exact payload the form builds 1. POST http://127.0.0.1:4471/model/new with complexity_router_config carrying tiers {CASUAL, SECURITY_REVIEW}, tier_definitions for both, fallback_tier CASUAL, plan_mode_min_tier SECURITY_REVIEW, classifier_type llm 2. Returns the created router; two live /v1/chat/completions calls through it return 200 #### The classifier routes on the custom definitions, both classes 1. POST /auto_router/test_routing with a security-audit prompt returns tier SECURITY_REVIEW, routed_model tier-security, cause llm_classifier 2. The same call with "what is the capital of France?" returns tier CASUAL, routed_model tier-simple #### The form's pre-save dry-run shows the backend verdict 1. POST /auto_router/validate_complexity_router_config with session_affinity beside a one-entry tier_definitions returns valid false naming both conflicts ## Type 🆕 New Feature ## Caveats (if any) - The Usage tab tier chart and log cards still label only built-in tiers - Presets remain built-in-only; a preset prefill then Edit tiers works like any other edit <!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY --> --- > [!NOTE] > **Medium Risk** > Touches create/edit serialization of complexity-router config (routing destinations, classifier type, and dropped incompatible keys). Untouched built-in routers still emit the same payload; saves dry-run the backend validator first. > > **Overview** > Operators can now **edit the complexity-router tier set in place** instead of being stuck with the four built-in rungs. **Edit tiers** adds/removes rows (2–8), each with a name, classifier definition, and models, plus a required **Fallback Tier**. Restoring the original four names/definitions clears `custom_tier_set` so an undone edit leaves nothing on the wire. > > An edited set **forces the LLM classifier** (heuristic is disabled; rubric/custom prompt are unused because the prompt is built from the definitions). Escalation, adaptive routing, session pinning, and display names are turned off with inline reasons. Keyword rules and plan-mode still work, keyed by custom names / stable row ids. > > Create and edit serialize through a shared `customTierSetWireFields` path (`tiers`, `tier_definitions`, `fallback_tier`, slim LLM config) and **drop keys the backend rejects** beside custom tiers. Both forms **dry-run** `/auto_router/validate_complexity_router_config` before write. Hydration round-trips stored custom configs; an untouched built-in form still submits a byte-identical payload. > > <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit aa1de1a55aee8ec345ed73529925932819dca730. signal.title: fix(caching): bound the semantic cache embedding lookup so a dead embedding endpoint can't block requests
signal.text: ## TLDR The semantic cache embedding lookup runs inline before the LLM call and had no deadline of its own, so it inherited the 6000s request timeout and the router's retries. When the configured embedding endpoint stops answering, every chat request parks in that lookup for minutes and the client often times out first. The failure is also silent: the only outward signs are the latency and `x-litellm-semantic-similarity: 0.0` This gives the lookup its own 5s deadline, and a single attempt on the routed path, so an unreachable embedding endpoint costs a few seconds and a cache miss instead of the whole request. Redis, Valkey and qdrant semantic caches all get the bound, and it is tunable per cache config or with `SEMANTIC_CACHE_EMBEDDING_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` Measured on a live proxy against a real Anthropic model: 685.7s before, 7.4s after, same config. ## User Flow ### Before Every chat completion through the gateway hangs for minutes, and most clients time out before an answer arrives 1. The operator boots the proxy with semantic caching on and checks it is up: `GET http://litellm-domain/health/liveliness` returns `"I'm alive!"` 2. They confirm the cache is wired: `GET http://litellm-domain/cache/ping` returns `{"status": "healthy", "cache_type": "redis-semantic"}` 3. The embedding endpoint named by `redis_semantic_cache_embedding_model` stops answering. Nothing in the proxy says so, and `GET /cache/ping` still answers `"status": "healthy"` because for a semantic cache it does not test the embedding endpoint at all 4. A user sends an ordinary request: `POST http://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions` with `{"model": "claude", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "What is the capital of France? Answer in one word."}]}`. Nothing comes back 5. The response lands 685 seconds later, carrying `x-litellm-response-duration-ms: 685519.593`, `x-litellm-overhead-duration-ms: 683421.74` and `x-litellm-semantic-similarity: 0.0`. The answer itself is a normal "Paris", so the 11 minutes bought nothing 6. When the embedding endpoint accepts connections and then goes quiet instead of refusing them, no response arrives at all. curl gives up with `curl: (28) Operation timed out after 700002 milliseconds with 0 bytes received` 7. The only way out is editing config.yaml to remove the `cache` block and restarting the proxy. The same request then returns in 5.2 seconds ### After The same request comes back in about seven seconds, with the cache skipped instead of waited on 1. Same boot, same `GET http://litellm-domain/health/liveliness` returning `"I'm alive!"` 2. Same `GET http://litellm-domain/cache/ping` returning `{"status": "healthy", "cache_type": "redis-semantic"}` 3. The embedding endpoint stops answering exactly as before 4. The user sends the identical `POST http://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions` 5. The response lands in 7.4 seconds with `x-litellm-response-duration-ms: 7204.558`, `x-litellm-overhead-duration-ms: 5021.482` and `x-litellm-semantic-similarity: 0.0`. The five seconds of overhead is the cache giving up, and the similarity of 0.0 is how the caller can tell the cache was skipped 6. The endpoint that goes quiet rather than refusing behaves the same way now. The wait is the same five seconds, and the completion arrives 7. No config edit and no restart. If the embedding endpoint is legitimately slower than five seconds, the operator raises `semantic_cache_embedding_timeout` under `cache_params` or sets `SEMANTIC_CACHE_EMBEDDING_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5879 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more - [x] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Both runs use the same config file, the same redis, the same real Anthropic model, and the same prompt. The only difference is the commit the proxy runs from. Shared setup, run once: ```bash docker run -d --name lit5879-redis -p 16279:6379 redis/redis-stack-server:latest cat > cache.yaml <<'YAML' model_list: - model_name: claude litellm_params: model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-5 api_key: os.environ/ANTHROPIC_API_KEY - model_name: cache-embedding litellm_params: model: openai/text-embedding-3-small api_base: "http://10.255.255.1:9/v1" api_key: dead-key litellm_settings: cache: true cache_params: type: redis-semantic similarity_threshold: 0.8 redis_semantic_cache_embedding_model: cache-embedding redis_url: "redis://127.0.0.1:16279" general_settings: master_key: sk-lit5879-repro YAML ``` `10.255.255.1:9` is an unroutable address, so every connection to the embedding endpoint blackholes. The request below is the same one in both runs: ```bash curl -sS -m 700 -w '\nWALL_SECONDS=%{time_total}\n' -D headers.txt -o body.json \ http://127.0.0.1:$PORT/v1/chat/completions \ -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-lit5879-repro' \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"model":"claude","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"What is the capital of France? Answer in one word."}],"max_tokens":64}' ``` ### Before (e07a7129c5) 1. Boot the proxy on the base commit and send the request. It returns, eventually: ``` WALL_SECONDS=685.7 HTTP/1.1 200 OK x-litellm-response-duration-ms: 685519.593 x-litellm-overhead-duration-ms: 683421.74 x-litellm-semantic-similarity: 0.0 x-litellm-attempted-retries: 0 {"choices":[{"message":{"content":"**Paris**", ...}}], ...} ``` 2. Subtracting the two duration headers puts the model at 2097.9ms, so 683.4 of the 685.7 seconds were spent inside the proxy before it ever dispatched. A direct Anthropic call with no proxy answers the same prompt in 2.52s 3. The proxy debug log shows why: `litellm.aembedding(... api_base='http://10.255.255.1:9/v1', ... timeout=6000.0)` and `Router._aembedding ..., num_retries - 2`. The lookup inherits the request timeout and gets retried 4. With an embedding endpoint that accepts connections and never answers rather than blackholing them, nothing times out at all. The same request produced `curl: (28)` at a 700s cap with no response at all, and the proxy log had zero hits for `api.anthropic.com` ### After (7d23d41cc4) 1. Boot the proxy on this branch with the identical cache.yaml and send the identical request, twice: ``` WALL_SECONDS=7.4 HTTP/1.1 200 OK x-litellm-response-duration-ms: 7204.558 x-litellm-overhead-duration-ms: 5021.482 x-litellm-semantic-similarity: 0.0 x-litellm-attempted-retries: 0 {"choices":[{"message":{"content":"**Paris**", ...}}], ...} ``` ``` WALL_SECONDS=8.0 x-litellm-response-duration-ms: 7433.985 x-litellm-overhead-duration-ms: 5041.333 x-litellm-semantic-similarity: 0.0 ``` 2. Both overheads land within 42ms of the 5000ms deadline, so the deadline is what ends the wait. Model time works out to 2183.1ms and 2392.7ms, matching the control 3. The debug log now shows the embedding call carrying `'semantic-cache-embedding': True, timeout=5.0` and `Router._aembedding ..., num_retries - 0`, where the run above logged `timeout=6000.0` and `num_retries - 2` 4. `grep -c 'api.anthropic.com'` over the proxy log returns 2, one dispatch per request, against 0 for the hanging-endpoint case before the fix Overhead drops from 683421.74ms to 5021.482ms, a factor of 136, and the response is byte-identical apart from ids and timing. ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) The default deadline is 5s. Raise it with `semantic_cache_embedding_timeout` under `cache_params`, or with the `SEMANTIC_CACHE_EMBEDDING_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` env var, if your embedding endpoint is legitimately slower than that. An embedding endpoint that answers slowly but correctly will now miss the cache instead of making the caller wait for it. When the embedding model is not a Router deployment, the lookup goes straight through `litellm.embedding`, where the provider client still applies its own retries. A dead endpoint costs about 16s on that path rather than 5s. Each attempt is still bounded by the deadline, and forcing zero retries there would change retry behavior for every embedding call, not just cache lookups ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR <!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY --> --- > [!NOTE] > **Medium Risk** > Changes the hot path in front of LLM calls: embedding timeouts and retries now fail open to a cache miss. Slow-but-valid embed endpoints will miss cache unless the new timeout is raised. > > **Overview** > Semantic-cache lookups no longer inherit the long request timeout and router retries. A hung embedding endpoint now fails the cache lookup quickly (default **5s**, one attempt) and the request continues to the LLM as a miss. > > `semantic_cache_embedding_timeout` (or `SEMANTIC_CACHE_EMBEDDING_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`) is applied on Redis, Valkey, and Qdrant backends. Embedding calls pass `timeout` and `num_retries=0`; async lookups are also wrapped in `asyncio.wait_for`. Tests cover the bound, hang fail-open, and config forwarding. > > <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit d57715bf46d1eac54e2b95dddea0ca9916a66440. signal.title: fix(otel): emit LLM Call spans for speech, image, moderation, ocr and transcription
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - V2 OTEL traces have no LLM Call span for speech - Same for image generation and moderations - OCR, speech and transcription spans were named `chat <model>` How it solves it: - Speech, async image and moderation now open their span - Those five routes map to standard GenAI operations, with modality on `gen_ai.output.type` - Caller image headers go to the upstream call only, never into the logged body ## User Flow Before: someone watching their traces sees text-to-speech, image and moderation requests arrive with the surrounding HTTP span only, so there is nothing recording which model was called or how long the provider took 1. They enable OTEL V2 tracing on the gateway and send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/audio/speech with `{"model": "tts-1", "input": "hi", "voice": "alloy"}` 2. Audio comes back 200, but the trace for that request holds only `POST /v1/audio/speech`, with no LLM Call child naming `tts-1` 3. The same happens for POST https://litellm-domain/v1/images/generations and POST https://litellm-domain/v1/moderations, success and failure alike 4. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/ocr and POST https://litellm-domain/v1/audio/transcriptions, and those requests do get an LLM Call span, but it is labelled `chat <model>`, so OCR and transcription latency lands in whatever their dashboard reads as chat After: every one of those requests carries its own LLM Call span, named for what the route actually did 1. They enable OTEL V2 tracing on the gateway and send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/audio/speech with `{"model": "tts-1", "input": "hi", "voice": "alloy"}` 2. Audio comes back 200 and the trace now holds an LLM Call child named `generate_content tts-1`, carrying `gen_ai.output.type=speech` plus the provider and model attributes 3. POST https://litellm-domain/v1/images/generations gets `generate_content <model>` with `gen_ai.output.type=image`, POST https://litellm-domain/v1/moderations gets `litellm.moderation <model>`, and on a provider error each span is recorded with error status 4. POST https://litellm-domain/v1/ocr and POST https://litellm-domain/v1/audio/transcriptions now report `generate_content <model>` with `gen_ai.output.type=text` instead of `chat <model>` Operation naming follows the current OTEL GenAI semantic conventions: the four content-producing routes use the registry's `generate_content` operation and distinguish themselves by `gen_ai.output.type`, span names follow `{gen_ai.operation.name} {gen_ai.request.model}`, and `litellm.call_type` keeps the exact route recoverable. Moderation is the one route the registry has no operation for, so it keeps a vendor-scoped `litellm.moderation` ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5601 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/<your_test_file>.py -v` - [x] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Shared setup, proxy run with `LITELLM_OTEL_V2=true OTEL_EXPORTER=console OTEL_SEMCONV_STABILITY_OPT_IN=gen_ai_latest_experimental`, `callbacks: ["otel"]`, one deployment per route, then the same eight requests replayed against each commit and the span names read off the console exporter ```bash AUTH='authorization: Bearer sk-1234'; CT='content-type: application/json' curl -H "$CT" -H "$AUTH" -X POST localhost:4000/v1/audio/speech -d '{"model":"tts-1","input":"hi","voice":"alloy"}' curl -H "$CT" -H "$AUTH" -X POST localhost:4000/v1/images/generations -d '{"model":"dall-e-3","prompt":"a cat"}' curl -H "$CT" -H "$AUTH" -X POST localhost:4000/v1/moderations -d '{"model":"omni-moderation-latest","input":"hi"}' curl -H "$CT" -H "$AUTH" -X POST localhost:4000/v1/ocr -d '{"model":"mistral-ocr-latest","document":{"type":"document_url","document_url":"https://example.com/a.pdf"}}' curl -H "$AUTH" -X POST localhost:4000/v1/audio/transcriptions -F model=whisper-1 -F file=@/tmp/audio.mp3 ``` ### Before (cc812cdfc7) #### /v1/audio/speech, /v1/images/generations, /v1/moderations 1. Ran the three curls above, each returned its normal 200 payload 2. Spans emitted per request: `auth <route>`, `POST <route>`, `batch_write_to_db _PROXY_track_cost_callback`. No LLM Call span at all, and the same on the error variants #### /v1/ocr, /v1/audio/transcriptions 1. Ran the OCR and transcription curls, both 200 2. An LLM Call span was emitted, but named `chat mistral-ocr-latest` and `chat whisper-1` ### After (76a5fb175f) #### /v1/audio/speech, /v1/images/generations, /v1/moderations 1. Ran the same three curls, same 200 payloads 2. Spans per request now include the LLM Call child: `generate_content tts-1` with `gen_ai.output.type=speech`, `generate_content dall-e-3` with `gen_ai.output.type=image`, and `litellm.moderation omni-moderation-latest`, all with `gen_ai.provider.name` and the request/response model set 3. Repeated each with a payload the provider rejects: the same three spans are emitted with error status and `error.type` set, alongside the 4xx returned to the caller #### /v1/ocr, /v1/audio/transcriptions 1. Ran the same two curls, both 200 2. The LLM Call spans are now named `generate_content mistral-ocr-latest` and `generate_content whisper-1`, both with `gen_ai.output.type=text`, and `gen_ai.provider.name` reads `mistral_ai` on the OCR one Caveat on this run: the network policy on the machine I ran it from only allows GitHub, so the deployments pointed at a local OpenAI-shaped upstream instead of the real provider APIs. The proxy, callback and span pipeline are the real ones, but the provider responses are not, so it is worth replaying these curls against real keys before merge. ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - Speech handlers take a required logging object now - Sync moderation still has no span, no logging object there ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/f3c57cda4d7642ff9c88e3d61c7f2086

signal.title: fix: add moonshot/kimi-k3 to the cost map on main
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - `moonshot/kimi-k3` is missing from `main`'s cost map, so models.litellm.ai doesn't list it - The entry is in review for `litellm_internal_staging` in #37552, but the hosted map reads `main` How it solves it: - Cherry-picks the #37552 cost map entry onto a `litellm_hotfix_*` branch targeting `main` - Data-only: `model_prices_and_context_window.json` plus the backup copy, nothing else ## User Flow Before: a developer looking up Kimi K3 on the hosted model catalog finds nothing 1. They open https://models.litellm.ai and search "kimi-k3" 2. The only match is the Azure Foundry variant `azure_ai/FW-Kimi-K3`; the native `moonshot/kimi-k3` is absent 3. They open https://models.litellm.ai/model/moonshot/kimi-k3 and get no pricing or context data After: the same search shows the native Moonshot entry with real pricing 1. They open https://models.litellm.ai and search "kimi-k3" 2. `moonshot/kimi-k3` appears with $3.00/M input, $0.30/M cache read, $15.00/M output, 1,048,576-token context 3. The model page shows reasoning, vision, video input, and tool calling support ## Relevant issues Data-only hotfix that copies the cost map entry from #37552, which is in review for `litellm_internal_staging`. models.litellm.ai and released litellm versions fetch `model_prices_and_context_window.json` from the `main` branch at runtime, so the hosted map won't show Kimi K3 until the entry reaches `main`. Same pattern as #30076. Pricing matches Moonshot's own published rates ([platform.kimi.ai](https://platform.kimi.ai/docs/pricing/chat-k3)): $3.00/M cache-miss input, $0.30/M cache hit, $15.00/M output, over a 1,048,576-token context. Those are the direct-API rates the `moonshot/` prefix bills against, so resellers like OpenRouter quote different numbers and aren't the reference here. The `fireworks_ai/*` and `azure_ai/*` kimi-k3 serverless variants are separate work that landed on `litellm_internal_staging` via #37658, which superseded #37512; this PR only adds the native `moonshot/kimi-k3` key, which that changeset doesn't touch ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5226 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [ ] I have added meaningful tests (n/a: data-only cherry-pick of the #37552 entry) - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/<your_test_file>.py -v`. If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix models.litellm.ai renders whatever `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/main/model_prices_and_context_window.json` serves, so the proof below curls the same file the site fetches, at the merge base and at the PR tip ### Before (007bd43cfb6eeeabe94d6aa77bd05dd3aa6aa1bf) 1. `curl -s https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/007bd43cfb6eeeabe94d6aa77bd05dd3aa6aa1bf/model_prices_and_context_window.json | jq '."moonshot/kimi-k3"'` ``` null ``` ### After (ef1cde433ea7c6dd1515de06c6d0d748fae4a197) 1. `curl -s https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/ef1cde433ea7c6dd1515de06c6d0d748fae4a197/model_prices_and_context_window.json | jq '."moonshot/kimi-k3" | {input_cost_per_token, cache_read_input_token_cost, output_cost_per_token, max_input_tokens}'` ``` { "input_cost_per_token": 0.000003, "cache_read_input_token_cost": 3E-7, "output_cost_per_token": 0.000015, "max_input_tokens": 1048576 } ``` 2. signal.title: feat(router): per-group supported reasoning efforts via model-map intersection
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Effort dropdown offers levels many models reject upstream - GPT, Claude, and Kimi accept different reasoning_effort sets - No per-group capability data reaches the dashboard How it solves it: - Model groups report supported_reasoning_efforts, intersected across deployments - Per-level polarity resolved in one backend function - Dropdown offers only what every deployment accepts ## User Flow Follows #37673 (merged), which added the per-model reasoning effort dropdown this PR filters Before: an operator configuring a tier picks an effort the model rejects at request time 1. They open http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=models-and-endpoints, Add Model, Auto Router, and select gpt-5-mini for the Medium tier 2. The Reasoning effort dropdown offers none through xhigh for every reasoning model alike 3. They pick xhigh for gpt-5-mini; the save succeeds because nothing validates levels 4. Requests classified Medium now fail: the provider rejects xhigh for that model, and the operator only finds out from error logs After: the dropdown only offers what the whole model group accepts 1. Same page, same Add Model flow, same tier picker 2. gpt-5-mini's dropdown offers Default, minimal, low, medium, high; a claude-opus group offers everything up to xhigh and max; a model absent from the model map keeps the full list since nothing is known about it 3. xhigh cannot be picked for gpt-5-mini, so the failing configuration can no longer be created 4. A hand-authored config carrying an out-of-set level still renders it and lets them clear it ## Relevant issues The intersection semantics are deliberate: a group mixing deployments offers only levels every deployment accepts, so routing can never hand an effort to a deployment that rejects it. Per-level polarity mirrors the provider gates: medium/high unconditional, none/minimal/low opt-out, xhigh/max opt-in ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Live rig: proxy from this branch on localhost:4381, dedicated Postgres, model_list carrying anthropic/claude-opus-5 as opus-5 and openai/gpt-5-mini ### Before (merge base cb4eb82249, where #37673 merged) GET /model_group/info carries no per-effort capability, and the dropdown offers the same six levels for every reasoning model ### After (PR tip 54b7b69ab0) ``` $ curl http://localhost:4381/model_group/info -H "Authorization: Bearer $MASTER_KEY" | jq '.data[] | {model_group, supported_reasoning_efforts}' {"model_group": "opus-5", "supported_reasoning_efforts": ["none","minimal","low","medium","high","xhigh","max"]} {"model_group": "gpt-5-mini", "supported_reasoning_efforts": ["minimal","low","medium","high"]} ``` Matches the model map exactly: claude-opus-5 sets xhigh and max true, gpt-5-mini sets none and xhigh false. A kimi-style entry with supports_reasoning true and no effort flags resolves to none/minimal/low/medium/high, and a deployment missing from the map contributes nothing to the intersection instead of zeroing it UI steps to screenshot on this branch: 1) /ui/?page=models-and-endpoints, Add Model, Auto Router, add gpt-5-mini to a tier and open its Reasoning effort dropdown: only Default, minimal, low, medium, high, 2) add opus-5 to a tier and open its dropdown: all seven levels including max, 3) save, reopen the edit modal, and confirm the same filtered options <!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY --> --- > [!NOTE] > **Medium Risk** > Touches router model-group capability aggregation and dashboard config for reasoning_effort, which can change what operators can select but does not alter auth or request execution. > > **Overview** > **Model groups now report `supported_reasoning_efforts`**, the intersection of levels every mapped deployment accepts, so the complexity-router effort dropdown no longer offers values a provider would reject. > > Backend resolution lives in `resolve_supported_reasoning_efforts`: medium/high are always on for reasoning models, none/minimal/low are opt-out, xhigh/max are opt-in. Deployments with no capability metadata do not shrink the group. `/model_group/info` (and the OpenAPI schema) expose the field. > > The dashboard joins team-allowed models with that group info, filters per-model dropdowns, and still shows a stored out-of-set value so it can be cleared. If the proxy omits the list, the UI falls back to the coarse `supports_reasoning` gate (without offering `max`). > > <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit a16312ae9289a9a0d3383e797e46ddfd266cc7a8. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup> <!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
