signal.title: feat(cognition): give Cognition its own provider identity
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - `model: cognition/swe-1.7` fails with "LLM Provider NOT provided" - The `openai/` workaround books Cognition traffic as OpenAI - OpenAI-specific cost discounts wrongly apply to that traffic - No built-in pricing for the SWE models How it solves it: - Adds a `cognition` entry to the JSON provider registry - Registers `LlmProviders.COGNITION` and both `constants.py` provider lists - Infers the provider from a known registry base URL - Adds cost map entries for `cognition/swe-1.6` and `cognition/swe-1.7` - Surfaces Cognition in provider endpoints support and the dashboard, covering chat completions, messages, and responses ## User Flow Before: a `cognition/` model entry fails outright, and the `openai/` workaround books the traffic as OpenAI 1. User adds `model: cognition/swe-1.7` to config.yaml and starts the proxy 2. User sends `POST /v1/chat/completions` with `"model": "swe-1.7"` 3. The request fails with 400: `LLM Provider NOT provided ... You passed model=cognition/swe-1.7` 4. User falls back to `model: openai/swe-1.7` plus an `api_base` override; requests succeed, but `/spend/logs` and provider-level spend reports attribute the traffic to `openai`, so OpenAI-specific discounts and reporting apply to it After: the same entry works and every report carries the `cognition` identity 1. User adds `model: cognition/swe-1.7` to config.yaml (key from `COGNITION_API_KEY` or `api_key`) and starts the proxy 2. User sends `POST /v1/chat/completions` with `"model": "swe-1.7"` 3. The response comes back normally from the OpenAI-compatible Cognition endpoint 4. `/spend/logs` rows carry `custom_llm_provider: cognition` and cost computed from the built-in SWE pricing, so provider-level reporting and discounts stay per-provider ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5348 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more - [x] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Cognition serves per-customer OpenAI-compatible endpoints, so the upstream stand-in here is a second LiteLLM proxy on 127.0.0.1:43117 serving model `swe-1.7` backed by a real `openai/gpt-4o-mini` key, with real round trips and real spend. That mirrors the load-bearing fact, which is that the endpoint is a plain `/v1/chat/completions` Stand-in upstream config: ```yaml model_list: - model_name: swe-1.7 litellm_params: model: openai/gpt-4o-mini api_key: os.environ/OPENAI_API_KEY general_settings: master_key: sk-inner-upstream-lit5348 ``` Config under test, carrying the new provider and the current workaround side by side: ```yaml model_list: - model_name: swe-1.7 litellm_params: model: cognition/swe-1.7 api_base: http://127.0.0.1:43117/v1 api_key: sk-inner-upstream-lit5348 - model_name: swe-workaround litellm_params: model: openai/swe-1.7 api_base: http://127.0.0.1:43117/v1 api_key: sk-inner-upstream-lit5348 general_settings: master_key: sk-repro-lit5348 ``` ### Before (9432f401452836f366ec3bece81be8043733a011) #### The `cognition/swe-1.7` deployment 1. Start the proxy on the config above; the router drops the deployment at startup ``` router.py:7779 - Error creating deployment: litellm.BadRequestError: LLM Provider NOT provided. Pass in the LLM provider you are trying to call. You passed model=cognition/swe-1.7 ... ignoring and continuing with other deployments. ``` 2. `curl -s http://127.0.0.1:52941/v1/models -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-repro-lit5348"` lists only the workaround ``` ['swe-workaround'] ``` 3. Call it anyway ``` $ curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:52941/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-repro-lit5348" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"model":"swe-1.7","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"say hi in three words"}]}' {"error":{"message":"litellm.BadRequestError: You passed in model=swe-1.7. There are no healthy deployments for this model. Received Model Group=swe-1.7 Available Model Group Fallbacks=None","type":null,"param":null,"code":"400"}} HTTP_STATUS=400 ``` #### Provider attribution 1. The same upstream through `openai/swe-1.7` answers, so the endpoint itself is fine ``` $ curl -s -D - -X POST http://127.0.0.1:52941/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-repro-lit5348" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"model":"swe-workaround","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"say hi in three words"}]}' HTTP/1.1 200 OK x-litellm-model-name: openai/swe-1.7 x-litellm-model-api-base: http://127.0.0.1:43117/v1 ... "content":"Hello, how are you?" ``` 2. `curl -s http://127.0.0.1:52941/model/info -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-repro-lit5348"` attributes it to OpenAI ``` swe-workaround -> openai/swe-1.7 | provider: openai ``` #### Built-in pricing for the SWE models 1. Look the models up in the cost map ``` $ python -c "from litellm import get_model_info; get_model_info(model='cognition/swe-1.7')" Exception: This model isn't mapped yet. model=cognition/swe-1.7 ``` 2. A warning at startup says the same, so cost fields fall back to zero ``` utils.py:2907 - register_model: model=cognition/swe-1.7 not in built-in cost map and no prefix/region variant matched; cache cost fields will default to 0 ``` ### After (6742637c955a9aa3d816a20ddc5d8163b437ffa8) #### The `cognition/swe-1.7` deployment 1. Start the proxy on the same config; no deployment error at startup, and `/v1/models` now lists both entries ``` $ curl -s http://127.0.0.1:59649/v1/models -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-repro-lit5348" ['swe-1.7', 'swe-workaround'] ``` 2. Call it ``` $ curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:59649/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-repro-lit5348" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"model":"swe-1.7","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"say hi in three words"}]}' {"id":"chatcmpl-EF81kbd7oBF7U4eLUhGXd9rijhtTb","model":"swe-1.7","object":"chat.completion", "choices":[{"finish_reason":"stop","index":0,"message":{"content":"Hello there, friend!", "role":"assistant"}}],"usage":{"completion_tokens":5,"prompt_tokens":12,"total_tokens":17}} HTTP_STATUS=200 ``` #### Provider attribution 1. The new entry answers under its own provider identity ``` $ curl -s -D - -X POST http://127.0.0.1:59649/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-repro-lit5348" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"model":"swe-1.7","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"say hi in three words"}]}' HTTP/1.1 200 OK x-litellm-model-name: cognition/swe-1.7 x-litellm-model-api-base: http://127.0.0.1:43117/v1 ``` 2. `curl -s http://127.0.0.1:59649/model/info -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-repro-lit5348"` separates the two ``` swe-1.7 -> cognition/swe-1.7 | provider: cognition swe-workaround -> openai/swe-1.7 | provider: openai ``` #### Built-in pricing for the SWE models 1. Both models resolve from the cost map ``` $ python -c "from litellm import get_model_info; print(get_model_info(model='cognition/swe-1.7'))" cognition/swe-1.7 provider: cognition in: 2.5e-06 out: 1.25e-05 cognition/swe-1.6 provider: cognition in: 5e-07 out: 2.5e-06 ``` 2. Cost computes off those rates ``` $ python -c "from litellm.cost_calculator import cost_per_token; print(sum(cost_per_token(model='swe-1.7', custom_llm_provider='cognition', prompt_tokens=12, completion_tokens=5)))" 9.25e-05 ``` ### Endpoint coverage behind the support matrix The provider entry declares `/messages` and `/responses` alongside `/chat/completions`, both served through the bridge rather than a native Cognition endpoint. Checked at the same commit so the matrix isn't claiming something the proxy won't do. There's no Before pair here because the deployment doesn't exist before the fix, which the first case already shows ``` $ curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:59649/v1/responses \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-repro-lit5348" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"model":"swe-1.7","input":"say hi in three words"}' HTTP_STATUS=200 {"id":"resp_ULDMbm2upSXUxPa9V7Zlrpc3zFTT-0atS79DLNpNVjxRnatxKdqCFI0HFwtqDWY9UNdwjHrp47FhMV... $ curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:59649/v1/messages \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-repro-lit5348" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"model":"swe-1.7","max_tokens":32,"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"say hi in three words"}]}' HTTP_STATUS=200 {"id":"chatcmpl-EF81oODR5HNkjrUOT8pZgjGO8bqw4","type":"message","role":"assistant","model":"swe-1.7", "usage":{"input_tokens":12,"output_tokens":5},"content":[{"type":"text","text":"Hello there, friend!"}], "stop_reason":"end_turn"} ``` ## Type 🆕 New Feature ## Caveats (if any) - No shareable Cognition endpoint or key, so QA ran against a stand-in upstream serving the same plain `/v1/chat/completions` - `x-litellm-response-cost` in QA reflects the stand-in proxy's own cost header, not the new rates - `swe-1.7` is mapped at the Lightning rates. The standard tier is 5x cheaper and the published table doesn't say which one the API serves, so it's worth confirming against a real contract before anyone leans on the cost numbers - Published pricing lists no context window, so both entries omit `max_input_tokens` and `max_output_tokens` - `responses: true` reflects the chat-completions bridge, verified live against the stand-in, not a native Cognition responses endpoint - Docs page ships separately in litellm-docs #822 ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR <!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY --> --- > [!NOTE] > **Medium Risk** > Touches provider resolution and spend attribution so Cognition traffic is no longer billed or reported as OpenAI. Routing is JSON-config based with tests, but cost numbers and endpoint coverage still depend on published rates and the chat-completions bridge. > > **Overview** > Gives Cognition a real provider identity so `cognition/swe-1.7` works without the `openai/` workaround that mis-attributed spend. > > Registers `cognition` in the JSON OpenAI-like registry (`COGNITION_API_KEY` / `https://api.cognition.ai/v1`) and infers it from a known base URL via `JSONProviderRegistry.get_by_base_url`. Adds cost map entries for `cognition/swe-1.6` and `cognition/swe-1.7` (function calling + prompt caching) so spend logs use Cognition pricing, not OpenAI discounts. > > Surfaces Cognition in the dashboard Add Model flow and endpoint matrix for chat, messages, and responses. > > <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 6742637c955a9aa3d816a20ddc5d8163b437ffa8. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup> <!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

signal.title: fix(proxy): restore model pricing in /v2/model/info after a request
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Calling a model blanks its price on the Model Management page - Only the models you actually use lose their pricing - The price never returns without a manual cost-map reload How it solves it: - A served deployment stores its cost keys as explicit null - Backfill skipped those, filling only fully absent keys - Treat null the same as absent when backfilling ## User Flow Before: an admin watching the Model Management page sees pricing disappear from exactly the models their team is using, which reads as though the busy models are the misconfigured ones 1. They open https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=models and see a price in the Costs column for every model 2. Their team sends a normal request to one of those models through POST https://litellm-domain/chat/completions, which succeeds and is billed correctly 3. They reload https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=models and the Costs column for that one model is now blank, while every model nobody called still shows its price 4. The blank never fills back in on its own, and the more models the team uses, the more of the page goes blank After: the Costs column keeps showing prices for models that are in use 1. They open https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=models and see a price in the Costs column for every model 2. Their team sends the same request to the same model, which succeeds and is billed the same 3. They reload https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=models and that model still shows its price 4. Continued traffic does not blank the column, so the page reflects configuration rather than usage ## Relevant issues Fixes #37637 ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix `Deployment` normalises `model_info` through the `ModelInfo` model, which materialises every unset cost field as `None`, so a deployment that has served a request holds `input_cost_per_token: None` rather than no key at all. The enrichment pass filled only keys that were absent, so those nulls stayed forever. Exercising the enrichment directly at 1132329245, once with the keys absent (a freshly reloaded deployment) and once with them null (a deployment that has served a request): Before: ``` ABSENT keys -> input_cost_per_token = 1e-06 None keys -> input_cost_per_token = None <- blank in the UI, permanently ``` After: ``` ABSENT keys -> input_cost_per_token = 1e-06 None keys -> input_cost_per_token = 1e-06 ``` For a live check, start the proxy with two models, GET /v2/model/info and note both prices, send one POST /chat/completions to just one of them, then GET /v2/model/info again. On current staging the called model reports null prices while the untouched one keeps its own. With this change both keep their prices, and http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=models shows a populated Costs column for both ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - Reporting only, cost tracking was always correct - `_get_proxy_model_info` has the same backfill shape, but its only caller passes `exclude_none=True`, so it cannot hit this today and is left alone to keep this change isolated

signal.title: fix(proxy): paginate legacy spend logs
signal.text: ## TLDR Legacy `GET /spend/logs` could materialize an unbounded `LiteLLM_SpendLogs` result set and exhaust proxy memory. This PR makes every legacy individual-log path database-bounded while preserving the endpoint's list-shaped JSON response. ## What changed - Adds `page` (default `1`) and `page_size` (default `50`, maximum `1000`). - Rejects invalid pagination and offsets above `10,000` with HTTP `422`. - Pushes `LIMIT` and `OFFSET` into the database for unfiltered, `api_key`, `user_id`, and date-range requests with `summarize=false`. - Uses deterministic ordering: `startTime DESC, request_id DESC`. - Excludes large payload columns from paginated list queries and hydrates the legacy JSON fields returned by the endpoint. - Keeps `request_id` lookup precise with a bounded ORM query and the complete matching record. - Performs `summarize=true` aggregation in the database instead of materializing raw logs. - Adds deprecation and pagination guidance headers without changing `/spend/logs/v2` or `/spend/logs/ui`. ## Compatibility - The response body remains a JSON list; this does not introduce the v2 pagination envelope. - Calls without pagination parameters now return the first bounded page of up to 50 logs. Clients that need more records must request subsequent pages. - Existing `request_id` and `summarize=true` response semantics are preserved. ## Validation - Spend management endpoint tests: `196 passed`. - V2/UI and query-optimization contract tests: `10 passed`. - Focused PostgreSQL probes covered stable ordering, deep offsets, UTC daily aggregation, and nullable users. - Ruff lint, Ruff format, type-discipline, basedpyright, import-safety, schema-sync, and all required GitHub checks pass. - Tests verify that no individual-log branch can reach `find_all` or an unbounded `find_many`. ## Relevant issue Fixes #37007 ## Type Bug Fix ## Caveats - There is intentionally no unbounded compatibility fallback because it would reintroduce the production OOM risk. - Offset pagination is deterministic, but concurrent inserts or deletes may move records between pages; this PR does not add snapshot pagination. ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests. - [x] All required CI checks pass. - [x] The scope is limited to legacy spend-log pagination and compatibility. - [x] Greptile reported a confidence score of 4/5 before maintainer review. ### Final Attestation - [x] Focused tests cover the bounded-query, pagination, filtering, compatibility, and failure paths described above.

signal.title: [Bug]: OAuth2 client_credentials MCP servers never receive client_id/client_secret at runtime — token endpoint always rejects with 400
signal.text: ### What happened? Registering an MCP server with `auth_type: oauth2` / `oauth2_flow: client_credentials` results in `tools/list` failing 100% of the time with: ``` misconfigured: OAuth2 client_credentials grant rejected: token endpoint returned HTTP 400 ``` This happens **regardless of how the server is configured** — via the REST API (`POST /v1/mcp/server` with a nested `credentials: {client_id, client_secret}` object) or via `config.yaml`'s `mcp_servers:` block (with either `os.environ/VAR` or literal values). In every case the token endpoint (a real, independently-verified-working Keycloak `client_credentials` grant) rejects the request, which points to litellm sending an empty or malformed `client_id`/`client_secret`. ### Root cause (traced in source, not guessed) 1. **`LiteLLM_MCPServerTable` (`schema.prisma`) has no `client_id` / `client_secret` columns** — only an encrypted `credentials Json?` blob: ```prisma model LiteLLM_MCPServerTable { server_id String @id @default(uuid()) ... credentials Json? @default("{}") ... } ``` 2. The runtime OAuth2 resolver builds its config from **flat fields on the `MCPServer` Pydantic model**: `litellm/proxy/_experimental/mcp_server/outbound_credentials/adapter.py`: ```python config=ClientCredentialsConfig( client_id=server.client_id, client_secret=SecretStr(server.client_secret) if server.client_secret else None, token_url=server.token_url, ... ) ``` 3. **Nothing in the codebase ever copies the decrypted `credentials` blob into `server.client_id` / `server.client_secret`.** Searched the whole `mcp_server` package for any `client_id=<decrypted value>` assignment feeding into an `MCPServer(...)` construction used by the OAuth2 resolver — there is none. `decrypt_credentials()` is only used for master-key rotation (`rotate_mcp_server_credentials_master_key`) and DCR client storage, never to populate the resolver's config. Result: for any server persisted through the database (which is every server registered via the REST API, and — because `general_settings.store_model_in_db: true` is a very common production setting — effectively every `config.yaml`-defined server too), `server.client_id` / `server.client_secret` are **always `None`** at the point the token request is built. Keycloak (or any spec-compliant IdP) correctly returns `400 invalid_request`/`invalid_client` for a `client_credentials` grant with an empty `client_id`. 4. Separately, **`config.yaml`'s `mcp_servers:` loader does not resolve `os.environ/VAR`** for `client_id`/`client_secret`, unlike `model_list.litellm_params`: `litellm/proxy/_experimental/mcp_server/mcp_server_manager.py`: ```python client_id=server_config.get("client_id", None), client_secret=server_config.get("client_secret", None), ``` This is a plain dict `.get()` — no `get_secret()` / env-var indirection. The [MCP OAuth docs](https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/mcp_oauth) show `client_id: os.environ/MCP_CLIENT_ID` as the documented pattern, but it is silently taken as a literal string, so the literal text `os.environ/MCP_CLIENT_ID` gets sent to the token endpoint instead of the resolved secret. ### Steps to Reproduce 1. Register (via REST API or `config.yaml`) an MCP server: ```yaml mcp_servers: my_server: url: "https://my-mcp-server.example.com/mcp" transport: http auth_type: oauth2 oauth2_flow: client_credentials client_id: "<a real, working client_id>" client_secret: "<its real secret>" token_url: "https://idp.example.com/protocol/openid-connect/token" ``` 2. Independently confirm the same `client_id`/`client_secret`/`token_url` succeed with a plain `curl -d grant_type=client_credentials&client_id=...&client_secret=...` — they do (200, valid token). 3. Call `tools/list` against the proxy's `/mcp/` endpoint for this server. 4. Observe `"status": "internal", "http_status": 500"` in `_meta.litellm.ai/server_outcomes`, and in the proxy logs: ``` Failed to get tools from server my_server: 500: misconfigured: OAuth2 client_credentials grant rejected: token endpoint returned HTTP 400 ``` 5. Confirm the grant mechanics themselves are fine by calling litellm's own `_prepare_grant` / `post_client_credentials_grant` directly with the identical config object (bypassing the server-record load path) — this **succeeds** and returns a valid access token. The bug is specifically in how the persisted/config-loaded `MCPServer` record's credentials reach that function, not in the grant logic itself. ### Expected behavior `client_id`/`client_secret` provided at registration time (via API `credentials` object or `config.yaml`, with or without `os.environ/` indirection) should reach the actual token request unchanged. ### Suggested fix - Add `client_id`/`client_secret` columns to `LiteLLM_MCPServerTable` (or decrypt+unpack the `credentials` blob into the `MCPServer.client_id`/`client_secret` fields at every read path that feeds `_client_credentials_spec`), and/or - Apply the same `get_secret()`/`os.environ/` resolution used for `model_list` to the `mcp_servers:` config.yaml loader for `client_id`, `client_secret`, and any other credential-shaped field. ### Environment - **LiteLLM version**: `ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:main-stable`, image pulled/deployed 2026-08-10 (prod) — well after the March 2026 fix for #24522, so this is not that issue. - **What part of LiteLLM is this about?**: MCP Gateway / OAuth2 `client_credentials` - Reproduced independently on two separate deployments (Azure Container Apps and an OpenShift-hosted instance with `store_model_in_db: true`), both via REST API registration and via `config.yaml`. ### Related issues Not a duplicate of #24522 (concurrent stateless teardown — different traceback, different mechanism). Possibly related in spirit to #22755 ("Unable to list MCP tools with OAuth through the UI Dashboard", closed `not_planned`) and #15957, which describe the same outward symptom (OAuth-protected MCP tool listing fails) without this root cause having been identified. --- ## Bug 2: `true_passthrough`/`oauth_delegate` MCP sessions time out despite the upstream call itself completing in milliseconds ### What happened? As an alternative to `client_credentials` (see Bug 1), we tested `auth_type: oauth_delegate` (`true_passthrough`), where litellm is supposed to forward the caller's own bearer token verbatim (via the `x-mcp-{alias}-authorization` header) instead of minting its own. `tools/list` against this server times out inside litellm. ### Root cause (traced in source) - `litellm/proxy/_experimental/mcp_server/outbound_credentials/resolver.py`, `_passthrough(self, subject)` (~line 163) forwards `subject.inbound_token` verbatim to the upstream MCP server — this part is correct and matches the caller-supplied-credential design we wanted. - `litellm/proxy/_experimental/mcp_server/mcp_server_manager.py` (~line 4200) wraps the actual `client.list_tools()` call in `anyio.fail_after(MCP_TOOL_LISTING_TIMEOUT)`. In our reproduction, this consistently fires before the upstream ever responds. - We isolated the upstream call from litellm's session/connection handling entirely: a standalone script (`debug_passthrough.py`), running inside the same cluster network as litellm and using the same caller token forwarded the same way, hit the internal MCP URL directly and got back **`HTTP 200` in `0.04s`**. The upstream server, network path, and token are all fine — the timeout is happening somewhere in litellm's own MCP client/session plumbing between accepting the passthrough token and actually completing the `list_tools()` round trip. ### Expected behavior `tools/list` over a `true_passthrough`/`oauth_delegate` MCP server should complete in roughly the same time as a direct call to the upstream (tens of milliseconds in our environment), not hit `MCP_TOOL_LISTING_TIMEOUT`. ### Environment Same as Bug 1 (OpenShift-hosted litellm instance, `store_model_in_db: true`). ### Status This is reported with less certainty than Bug 1 — we have not yet traced the exact point inside litellm's session/connection setup where the delay is introduced (as opposed to Bug 1, which we traced to an exact missing assignment). Flagging it here because it blocks the architecturally-preferred alternative to Bug 1. --- ## Bug 3: `client_credentials` grant requests every scope advertised by the realm's discovery document, instead of only the client's assigned scopes ### What happened? With Bug 1's root cause fixed locally (server record correctly populated with a real, independently-verified-working `client_id`/`client_secret`), the *live* litellm instance's `client_credentials` requests to our IdP (Keycloak) still fail — but with a different, more specific error surfaced in the IdP's own audit log (not visible from litellm's side, only from the token endpoint's server-side logs): ``` error="invalid_request", reason="Invalid scopes: basic uma_protection Custom_Scope a2a-chat-ia-mcp-audience roles phone microprofile-jwt openid web-origins offline_access acr email service_account profile address", grant_type="client_credentials", client_auth_method="client-secret", username="service-account-<client>" ``` Client authentication itself **succeeds** here (Keycloak resolves the service-account user, confirming the secret is valid) — the request fails only because of the `scope` parameter litellm sends. The requested scope list is unusually large and includes scopes that are not, and could never sensibly be, assigned to this specific client (`microprofile-jwt`, `web-origins`, `acr`, several other realm-wide default/optional scopes). This looks like litellm is requesting the full `scopes_supported` list from the IdP's OIDC discovery document (`/.well-known/openid-configuration`) rather than a scope the operator configured (or no `scope` parameter at all, which is valid per RFC 6749 §4.4.2 and lets the IdP apply the client's default scopes). ### Expected behavior The `client_credentials` grant should either omit `scope` entirely (letting the IdP apply the client's configured default scopes, which is spec-compliant and what a plain `curl` grant with no `scope` param does successfully against the same client/IdP), or send only an operator-configured scope list — never every scope advertised by discovery metadata. ### Environment Same as Bug 1/2. ### Related issues Not yet searched for a matching open issue — flagging here since it was discovered as a direct consequence of investigating Bug 1. **Update: Bug 3 also breaks the interactive `authorization_code` flow, not just `client_credentials`** Confirmed this is not specific to `client_credentials`. Registering a second server with `oauth2_flow: authorization_code` (same `client_id`, plus an `issuer` so LiteLLM does RFC 8414 discovery instead of using manually-set `authorization_url`/`token_url`) and hitting LiteLLM's own `/{server_name}/authorize` endpoint produces a `307` redirect to the IdP's `/auth` endpoint whose `scope` query param is the **exact same** full discovery scope list: ``` Invalid scopes: basic uma_protection Custom_Scope a2a-chat-ia-mcp-audience roles phone microprofile-jwt openid web-origins offline_access acr email service_account profile address ``` i.e. once `issuer` is set for discovery, LiteLLM builds this over-broad `scope` value for **every** OAuth2 flow it drives (both the M2M token request and the interactive `/authorize` redirect), not just `client_credentials`. Same root cause, hits both the token-request call site and the `/authorize` redirect builder. This was confirmed via a real interactive login attempt — the actual Keycloak login page itself surfaces `Invalid scopes` (same string as the token-endpoint audit log entry seen with `client_credentials`), which rules out this being a `client_credentials`-only or backend-log-only artifact. Cópialo desde el primer ```markdown hasta el cierre y pégalo directo en el comentario de GitHub — al pegarlo ahí se va a renderizar bien.

signal.title: fix(guardrails): run policy pipelines when the caller sends its own metadata (/v1/messages, Claude Code)
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Claude Code requests skipped every policy pipeline guardrail - Any caller sending its own `metadata` bypassed pipeline policies - Only `/v1/messages`, `/responses`, `batches`, `files`, `bedrock` affected How it solves it: - Read pipelines from whichever bucket the policy engine wrote them to - Same for the pipeline-managed skip list in the callback loop - Regression test covers a caller-supplied bucket on both route shapes ## User Flow Before: an admin attaches a moderation policy to every request, but a developer using Claude Code sends prompts that are never screened 1. The admin attaches a policy with a `pre_call` pipeline whose step blocks disallowed content, scoped to `*` 2. From a REST client, the developer sends POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages with disallowed content and gets back 400 with the guardrail's block message 3. The same user runs Claude Code against the same key, model and team, so every request carries `User-Agent: claude-cli` and a top-level `"metadata": {"user_id": "..."}` 4. POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages with the same disallowed content returns 200 with a normal model completion 5. https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs shows that request with an empty `applied_guardrails`, so the audit trail says nothing ran 6. Anyone on that key could route unscreened prompts through the gateway just by sending Anthropic's own `metadata` field After: the same policy blocks the Claude Code request too, and the log records the guardrail 1. The admin attaches the same policy 2. From a REST client, POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages with disallowed content returns 400 with the guardrail's block message 3. The same user runs Claude Code, so requests carry `User-Agent: claude-cli` and a top-level `"metadata": {"user_id": "..."}` 4. POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages with the same disallowed content now returns 400 with the same block message 5. https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs shows the guardrail recorded against the request 6. Sending Anthropic's `metadata` field no longer buys a caller an unscreened request ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5600 ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Shared setup: two live proxies against real Anthropic (`anthropic/*` wildcard, `claude-haiku-4-5`), same config, a global policy whose `pre_call` pipeline blocks on a guardrail failure, and `BLOCKME` as the disallowed content. Pre-fix runs on port 4000, fixed on port 4001. The Claude Code CLI is 2.1.238, pointed at each proxy with `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` and `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN=sk-1234` ### Before (`6704a105ee`) #### /v1/messages without provider metadata 1. Run ```bash curl -s -o /tmp/c1 -w 'HTTP %{http_code}\n' -X POST http://localhost:4000/v1/messages \ -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-1234' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"model":"claude-haiku-4-5","max_tokens":16,"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"BLOCKME"}]}' head -c 220 /tmp/c1 ``` 2. Blocked, as expected ``` HTTP 400 {"error":{"message":"400: {'error': 'blocked by marker-gr', 'guardrail_name': 'marker-gr', 'guardrail_mode': 'pre_call'}","type":"None","param":"None","code":"400"}} ``` #### /v1/messages with the Claude Code shape 1. Run ```bash curl -s -o /tmp/c2 -w 'HTTP %{http_code}\n' -X POST 'http://localhost:4000/v1/messages?beta=true' \ -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-1234' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -H 'User-Agent: claude-cli/2.1.238 (external, local-agent, agent-sdk/0.3.238)' \ -d '{"model":"claude-haiku-4-5","max_tokens":16,"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"BLOCKME"}],"metadata":{"user_id":"user_abc"}}' head -c 220 /tmp/c2 ``` 2. Served by the model, never screened ``` HTTP 200 {"model":"claude-haiku-4-5","id":"msg_011CeF4j6zPaP5Z8HWYhDTzX","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"I'm here to help! If you're looking to block something, I can"}],"stop_reason":"max_to ``` #### Real Claude Code CLI 1. Point the CLI at the pre-fix proxy and prompt it ```bash export ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://localhost:4000 ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN=sk-1234 ANTHROPIC_API_KEY= claude -p "say BLOCKME" ``` 2. The model answers, so the policy never ran ``` BLOCKME ``` ### After (`4fd0cbffb5`) #### /v1/messages without provider metadata 1. Run the case 1 curl against port 4001 2. Still blocked ``` HTTP 400 {"error":{"message":"400: {'error': 'blocked by marker-gr', 'guardrail_name': 'marker-gr', 'guardrail_mode': 'pre_call'}","type":"None","param":"None","code":"400"}} ``` #### /v1/messages with the Claude Code shape 1. Run the case 2 curl against port 4001 2. Now blocked by the same policy ``` HTTP 400 {"error":{"message":"400: {'error': 'blocked by marker-gr', 'guardrail_name': 'marker-gr', 'guardrail_mode': 'pre_call'}","type":"None","param":"None","code":"400"}} ``` #### Real Claude Code CLI 1. Point the CLI at the fixed proxy and prompt it ```bash export ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://localhost:4001 ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN=sk-1234 ANTHROPIC_API_KEY= claude -p "say BLOCKME" ``` 2. The CLI surfaces the guardrail block ``` API Error: 400 400: {'error': 'blocked by marker-gr', 'guardrail_name': 'marker-gr', 'guardrail_mode': 'pre_call'} ``` 3. A benign prompt on the same proxy still works, so ordinary Claude Code traffic is unaffected ``` $ claude -p "reply with the single word ok" ok ``` A video of the Claude Code runs on both proxies, including the benign control, is posted in the [Slack thread](https://berriaillm.slack.com/archives/C0BE49SAUE6/p1786683665130109?thread_ts=1786683665.130109&cid=C0BE49SAUE6) ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - Independently attached guardrails were already unaffected - Only pipeline-backed policies could be bypassed this way - The pipeline slots are stripped from caller-supplied metadata before the policy engine runs, so a forged bucket cannot win the lookup ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/adb590da643643b68f37fbec96628341

signal.title: [Bug]: Background health-check DB persistence is not leader-gated and LiteLLM_HealthCheckTable grows unbounded — causes DB storms at scale
signal.text: ## What happened? Two independent defects in the background health-check loop combine to storm the database every cycle (default 15 min) when running `use_shared_health_check: true` with multiple workers: **Bug 1 — DB persistence is not leader-gated:** `SharedHealthCheckManager` correctly gates the **probing** step (only the lock-holder sends health-check requests to LLM providers). But after probing, `_run_background_health_check()` unconditionally calls `_schedule_background_health_check_db_save()` on **every worker** (line ~3499 of `proxy_server.py`). Each worker runs `get_all_latest_health_checks()` — a `SELECT DISTINCT ON` full-table scan — plus per-model INSERTs. With N workers this multiplies DB load by N every cycle. **Bug 2 — HealthCheckTable is append-only with no retention:** `save_health_check_result()` in `PrismaClient` uses `.create()` (INSERT). There is no upsert and no pruning. The table grows unbounded. Because `get_all_latest_health_checks()` uses `DISTINCT ON (model_id, model_name)` ordered by `checked_at DESC`, Postgres must scan **all rows** to find the latest per model — there is no loose index-scan optimization for `DISTINCT ON`. **Combined impact at scale:** In our production environment (360 models, ~10 workers, 15-min cycle), the table grew to **3.9 million rows** in 64 days. `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` of `get_all_latest_health_checks()` shows: - **4.18 seconds** execution time - **~31 GB** buffer traffic (index + heap) - Scans all 3.9M rows to return 360 When ~10 workers run this simultaneously against a near-idle database (we use Aurora Serverless v2 with auto-scaling), it triggers a cold scale-up to max capacity, which causes connection churn, severs query-engine connections across all tasks, health saves fail, deployments get marked unavailable, and the proxy returns `No deployments available` 500s. We observed a **20.6% 5xx rate** during a 25-minute incident window. ## Steps to Reproduce 1. Configure LiteLLM proxy with: ```yaml general_settings: use_shared_health_check: true background_health_checks: true health_check_interval: 900 # 15 min ``` 2. Deploy with multiple workers (e.g. 4+ Gunicorn workers or multiple pods behind a load balancer) and 100+ models in config. 3. Let the proxy run for several weeks. 4. Observe `LiteLLM_HealthCheckTable` row count growing linearly (models × cycles × workers per cycle): ```sql SELECT count(*) FROM "LiteLLM_HealthCheckTable"; -- After 64 days with 360 models, 10 workers: ~3.9M rows ``` 5. Observe that **every worker** calls `get_all_latest_health_checks()` each cycle, not just the leader: ```sql -- Proof of leaderless fan-out: distinct checked_by values within a single cycle SELECT checked_at, checked_by, count(*) FROM "LiteLLM_HealthCheckTable" WHERE checked_at > now() - interval '20 minutes' GROUP BY checked_at, checked_by ORDER BY checked_at DESC; -- Returns rows for EACH pod writing the same models <60s apart ``` 6. At sufficient table size, the `DISTINCT ON` read becomes multi-second, and concurrent execution from N workers causes DB saturation / connection exhaustion. ## Relevant log output ``` # EXPLAIN ANALYZE on the DISTINCT ON read (3.9M rows, 360 models): Unique (cost=0.56..2847163.44 rows=360 width=1389) (actual time=0.194..4183.021 rows=360 loops=1) -> Index Scan using ... on "LiteLLM_HealthCheckTable" (actual time=0.193..3922.574 rows=3900000 loops=1) Planning Time: 0.422 ms Execution Time: 4183.541 ms Buffers: shared hit=31457280 ``` ## Root Cause in Code **`proxy_server.py` ~L3498-3505** — `_schedule_background_health_check_db_save()` is called unconditionally regardless of whether this worker was the health-check leader: ```python # Save background health checks to database (non-blocking) _schedule_background_health_check_db_save( prisma_client, shared_health_manager, _llm_model_list, healthy_endpoints, unhealthy_endpoints, ) ``` **`utils.py` ~L5138** — `save_health_check_result()` uses `.create()` (INSERT), never upserts or prunes: ```python return await HealthCheckRepository(self).table.create(data=health_check_data) ``` **`utils.py` ~L5180-5187** — `get_all_latest_health_checks()` does `DISTINCT ON` over the full table: ```python return await HealthCheckRepository(self).table.find_many( distinct=["model_id", "model_name"], order=[ {"model_id": "asc"}, {"model_name": "asc"}, {"checked_at": "desc"}, ], ) ``` ## Suggested Fix **Short-term (two changes):** 1. **Leader-gate the DB persistence:** `SharedHealthCheckManager` already elects a leader for probing. Expose an `is_current_pod_leader` flag (set True when the pod acquires the lock or falls back to local probe; reset to False on cache hit). Gate `_schedule_background_health_check_db_save()` on it so exactly one pod does the read + write per cycle. When `shared_health_manager is None`, preserve the existing per-pod behavior. 2. **Add retention pruning:** After a successful save, the leader prunes rows older than a retention window (e.g. 7 days) via a batched, bounded DELETE. This caps the `DISTINCT ON` scan cost at O(recent rows) instead of O(all history). Batching (e.g. 10k rows per pass, max 50 passes) avoids long locks on the first run against a large backlog. **Long-term (architectural):** Replace the append-only `LiteLLM_HealthCheckTable` with a **one-row-per-model upsert** design (a `LiteLLM_HealthCheckLatest` table with `model_id` as primary key, upserted each cycle). This makes the "latest per model" read O(N models) — a simple `SELECT *` — instead of `DISTINCT ON` over unbounded history. History can be kept in the existing table with retention, or dropped entirely. ## What part of LiteLLM is this about? Proxy ## What LiteLLM version are you on? v1.94.3

signal.title: [Bug] Anthropic protocol GLM-5.2 429 ratelimit response missing `anthropic-ratelimit-unified-status` and `retry-after` headers, causing ClaudeCode infinite retry
signal.text: ## Title [Bug] Anthropic protocol GLM-5.2 429 ratelimit response missing `anthropic-ratelimit-unified-status` and `retry-after` headers, causing ClaudeCode infinite retry ## Summary When using LiteLLM (v1.96.2) as gateway with **anthropic protocol backend for GLM-5.2**, after hitting model rate limit (429 Too Many Requests), LiteLLM does not forward / inject required response headers: `anthropic-ratelimit-unified-status: rejected` and `retry-after: <seconds>`. Direct calling GLM native anthropic endpoint with the same `anthropic-beta` headers returns these two headers correctly, ClaudeCode will fail fast instead of retrying. Missing headers behind LiteLLM gateway leads to infinite retry loop in ClaudeCode client. > > Important note: GLM only returns these two special rate-limit headers when the full `anthropic-beta` header for ClaudeCode is carried in the request. ## Environment - LiteLLM Version: `1.96.2` - Backend Model: `glm-5.2` (BigModel Open API, Anthropic compatible protocol) - Client: ClaudeCode - Gateway Front: APISIX/3.14.1 - Required request header: ``` anthropic-beta: claude-code-20250219,interleaved-thinking-2025-05-14,context-management-2025-06-27,prompt-caching-scope-2026-01-05,effort-2025-11-24 ``` ## Reproduction Steps 1. Configure LiteLLM model entry using anthropic compatible endpoint for glm-5.2 2. Send `/v1/messages` POST request with full `anthropic-beta` header as used by ClaudeCode 3. Trigger GLM rate limit error (error code `1310`, `rate_limit_error`) 4. Compare response headers between calling LiteLLM gateway vs direct GLM native endpoint ### Case 1: Request via LiteLLM Gateway ``` curl -i -sSL -X POST 'https://aigateway.sunacwy.com.cn/v1/messages' \ --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \ --header 'Authorization: Bearer sk-YzV42gfDGZqcj-Fhf6_pag' \ --header 'x-litellm-customer-id: customer888' \ --header 'anthropic-beta: claude-code-20250219,interleaved-thinking-2025-05-14,context-management-2025-06-27,prompt-caching-scope-2026-01-05,effort-2025-11-24' \ --data '{ "model": "glm", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "What is the capital of France?"}], "max_tokens": 9999 }' ``` **Actual LiteLLM 429 Response (missing target headers):** ``` HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 10:39:34 GMT Content-Type: application/json Content-Length: 405 Connection: keep-alive x-litellm-call-id: 1089e8ba-956c-4f75-8b2a-9c02ca3b3ed9 x-litellm-model-id: d17b5081-38a0-4692-a69b-c1c004d7b448 x-litellm-version: 1.96.2 x-litellm-response-cost: 0 x-litellm-key-spend: 12.212863420000009 x-litellm-timeout: 600.0 x-frame-options: DENY content-security-policy: frame-ancestors 'none' x-content-type-options: nosniff Server: APISIX/3.14.1 {"error":{"message":"{\"type\":\"error\",\"error\":{\"type\":\"rate_limit_error\",\"code\":\"1310\",\"message\":\"[1310][您已达到每周/每月使用上限，您的限额将在 2026-08-24 17:08:52 重置。][202608201839315ab4d26ea9144756]\"},\"request_id\":\"202608201839315ab4d26ea9144756\"}. Received Model Group=glm\nAvailable Model Fallbacks=None","type":"None","param":"None","code":"429"}} ``` ✅ Observation: No `anthropic-ratelimit-unified-status` and no `retry-after` header. ### Case 2: Direct Request to GLM Native Anthropic Endpoint (Reference Working Example) ``` curl -i -sSL -X POST 'https://open.bigmodel.cn/api/anthropic/v1/messages?beta=true' \ --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \ --header 'Authorization: Bearer sk-e3e124be03be4414a73690d1bca048af.1MDJ7mDqbRtyAUK2' \ --header 'anthropic-beta: claude-code-20250219,interleaved-thinking-2025-05-14,context-management-2025-06-27,prompt-caching-scope-2026-01-05,effort-2025-11-24' \ --data '{ "model": "glm-5.2", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "What is the capital of France?"}] }' ``` **Direct GLM 429 Response (contains required headers):** ``` HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 01:18:10 GMT Content-Type: application/json Content-Length: 253 Connection: keep-alive Set-Cookie: acw_tc=276077f617872750905264565ec54374ef8055c7578f6c92c1b1672ccc8a34;path=/;HttpOnly;Max-Age=1800 Vary: Origin Vary: Access-Control-Request-Method Vary: Access-Control-Request-Headers X-LOG-ID: 20260821091810b67f7ae6443d450c vary: Origin, Access-Control-Request-Method, Access-Control-Request-Headers anthropic-ratelimit-unified-status: rejected retry-after: 287441 request-id: 20260821091810b67f7ae6443d450c x-process-time: 0.153954 Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains {"type":"error","error":{"type":"rate_limit_error","code":"1310","message":"[1310][您已达到每周/每月使用上限，您的限额将在 2026-08-24 17:08:52 重置。][20260821091810b67f7ae6443d450c]"},"request_id":"20260821091810b67f7ae6443d450c"} ``` ✅ Observation: `anthropic-ratelimit-unified-status: rejected` and `retry-after: 287441` exist, ClaudeCode fails fast without retry. ## Expected Behavior When upstream GLM returns valid `anthropic-ratelimit-unified-status` and `retry-after` headers (triggered only when full anthropic-beta header is passed), LiteLLM should: 1. Preserve / forward these two response headers to downstream client on 429 2. Avoid stripping anthropic protocol specific headers when wrapping upstream error response 3. Let ClaudeCode recognize `rejected` status and stop automatic retry ## Root Cause Hypothesis 1. LiteLLM Anthropic protocol adapter strips upstream custom `anthropic-*` response headers while wrapping 429 error payload 2. Passthrough logic is missing for `retry-after` and `anthropic-ratelimit-unified-status` for third-party Anthropic-compatible backends like GLM 3. GLM only emits those two rate-limit headers when full ClaudeCode `anthropic-beta` list is forwarded to upstream; LiteLLM may alter beta headers before calling upstream or discard response headers after receiving reply ## Suggested Fix 1. For Anthropic compatible backends, forward all upstream `anthropic-*` custom response headers on 429 2. Explicitly passthrough `retry-after` header in Anthropic protocol path 3. Avoid wrapping and rewriting original upstream Anthropic native error response which removes protocol required headers ## Additional Context - GLM error code: `1310` (weekly/month quota exhausted) - Client retry behavior difference purely depends on presence of these two HTTP headers - Without headers: ClaudeCode treats generic 429 as temporary throttle and keeps retrying infinitely

signal.title: fix(responses_bridge): map incomplete responses to finish_reason length instead of 500
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Chat completions through the Responses bridge return 500 when reasoning consumes the whole token budget - Truncated bridge streams ended with finish_reason "stop" and no usage How it solves it: - An incomplete response with no message now yields one empty assistant message - finish_reason maps from the incomplete reason: "length", or "content_filter" for filtered - Truncated partial text keeps its content and gets finish_reason "length" - Streaming handles the response.incomplete terminal event like response.completed, with the mapped finish_reason and usage ## User Flow Before: a developer whose app calls a bridged reasoning model with a small completion budget gets a 500 whenever reasoning uses up the whole budget 1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with `"model": "bridge/gpt-5.6-sol"` (a `openai/responses/...` deployment), `"reasoning_effort": "high"`, `"max_completion_tokens": 16` 2. The response is HTTP 500 with `"litellm.APIConnectionError: ... gpt-5.6-sol unable to complete request: max_output_tokens"`, so their app surfaces a gateway error to the end user 3. The same request with `"stream": true` returns 200, but the only meaningful chunk carries `"finish_reason": "stop"` and no usage, so the app believes the model finished normally and records zero spend 4. POST https://litellm-domain/v1/responses with the same model and `"max_output_tokens": 16` returns 200 with `"status": "incomplete"`, so only the chat completions surface is broken After: the same request behaves like OpenAI's native chat completions on truncation 1. They send the same POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with `"reasoning_effort": "high"`, `"max_completion_tokens": 16` 2. The response is HTTP 200 with one choice: an assistant message with `"content": ""`, `"finish_reason": "length"`, and usage showing prompt 37 / completion 16 / reasoning 16 tokens 3. The same request with `"stream": true` returns a terminal chunk with `"finish_reason": "length"`, and with `"stream_options": {"include_usage": true}` the final chunk carries the real usage 4. When the truncation reason is a content filter, the choice comes back with `"finish_reason": "content_filter"` instead ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5886 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more - [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Two proxies, same config, same prompt, real OpenAI calls with no mocks. Before is the merge base cb4eb82249, after is 5c89490124 on this branch. All four cases were re-run at the current tip 16bba15434 and came back identical, so the proof stands at the head, not just at the commit it was first captured on Shared config: ```yaml model_list: - model_name: bridge/gpt-5.6-sol litellm_params: model: openai/responses/gpt-5.6-sol api_key: os.environ/OPENAI_API_KEY general_settings: master_key: sk-1234 ``` Prompt used in every case: "Determine the last ten decimal digits of 7 raised to the power 123456789. Think through modular arithmetic carefully, then return only those ten digits." Every request caps output at 16 tokens, which is what makes the upstream response come back incomplete ### Before (cb4eb82249, port 52361) #### Non-streaming /v1/chat/completions 1. `curl -sS -i http://localhost:52361/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"bridge/gpt-5.6-sol","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"<prompt>"}],"reasoning_effort":"high","max_completion_tokens":16}'` 2. Observed `HTTP/1.1 500 Internal Server Error` with body `{"error":{"message":"litellm.APIConnectionError: APIConnectionError: OpenAIException - gpt-5.6-sol unable to complete request: max_output_tokens. ...","code":"500"}}`, no usage anywhere, and `x-litellm-response-cost: 0` 3. Observed HTTP 200 whose whole stream is `{"choices":[{"index":0,"delta":{},"finish_reason":"stop"}]}`, then a second empty-delta chunk, then `[DONE]` 3. No usage chunk arrives even though the request asked for one, and every cost header reads 0.0 #### Non-streaming /v1/messages 1. `curl -sS -i http://localhost:52361/v1/messages -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"bridge/gpt-5.6-sol","max_tokens":16,"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"<prompt>"}]}'` 2. Observed HTTP 200 with `"content":[],"stop_reason":"max_tokens"` and `"usage":{"input_tokens":37,"output_tokens":16}`, billed at `x-litellm-response-cost: 0.000665` #### Streaming /v1/messages 1. The call is billed at `x-litellm-response-cost: 0.000665`, where the 500 billed nothing #### Streaming /v1/chat/completions 1. Same request with `"stream": true` and `"stream_options":{"include_usage":true}` 2. Observed the terminal choice chunk `{"choices":[{"index":0,"delta":{},"finish_reason":"length"}]}` 3. The final chunk carries the real usage `{"completion_tokens":16,"prompt_tokens":37,"total_tokens":53,"completion_tokens_details":{"reasoning_tokens":16},...}`, then `[DONE]` #### Non-streaming /v1/messages 1. Same curl as the before leg 2. Observed HTTP 200 with `"content":[],"stop_reason":"max_tokens"`, usage 37 in / 16 out, cost 0.000665, unchanged from before #### Streaming /v1/messages 1. Same request with `"stream": true` 2. Observed the same `message_start` / `message_delta` with `"stop_reason": "max_tokens"` and usage 37 / 16 / `message_stop`, unchanged The Anthropic shape already reported the truncation honestly at the merge base, so the fix lands only on the OpenAI chat completions shape and /v1/messages stays where it was ### Re-run at the tip (16bba15434, port 55643) The same four cases, driven again against a proxy booted from the current head with `PYTHONPATH` pinned to that worktree and the loaded `litellm.__file__` asserted to sit inside it: 1. Non-streaming /v1/messages: HTTP 200 with `"content":[],"stop_reason":"max_tokens"`, usage 37 in / 16 out, cost 0.000665 4. Streaming /v1/messages: `message_start`, `message_delta` carrying `{"stop_reason": "max_tokens"}` with usage 37 / 16, `message_stop` ### Surprises - Truncated calls now bill; the 500 billed nothing (causes) - Streamed chunks omit the reasoning items non-streaming returns (leaves alone) - Cost headers read zero on every streamed call (leaves alone) - /v1/messages already reported max_tokens before the fix (leaves alone) - message_start echoes responses/gpt-5.6-sol, not the alias (leaves alone) ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR <!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY --> --- > [!NOTE] > **Medium Risk** > Changes how truncated/incomplete Responses API results are mapped into chat completions, including finish_reason and usage/billing. signal.title: test(lint): ban blind pytest.raises(Exception) with ruff B017
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - `pytest.raises(Exception)` passes on any crash, not the rejection - A refactor's `TypeError` satisfies it as well as the real error - 111 such sites in `tests/`, several never reaching the code they name How it solves it: - Selects ruff `B017` in `ruff-tests.toml`, already wired to CI - Narrows every site to the type a runtime probe saw it catch - Adds `match=` where the code genuinely raises a bare `Exception` - Two sites turned out to be failing on setup, never on the behavior ## User Flow Before: a developer cancels a response id the gateway never issued, and nothing checks what comes back 1. They POST https://litellm-domain/v1/responses and get an id back 2. They POST https://litellm-domain/v1/responses/resp_never_issued/cancel with an id that was never issued 3. The gateway answers 404 naming the unknown response id 4. A later change makes that route answer 500 on every cancel, valid id or not 5. CI stays green: the test covering the invalid-id cancel accepts any exception at all, and it had never been reaching a provider in the first place, failing earlier on a missing provider argument After: the same change turns CI red before a developer ever sees it 1. The same change is made 2. CI runs the same test file and it fails, naming the provider error it expected and the crash it got instead 3. Any new test written to accept any exception is rejected at lint time, so the next one cannot reach the proxy either ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally - [x] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix This PR changes lint config and tests, so there is no proxy route to curl. The proof is three mutations: break a behavior a test exists to police, and show the old test does not notice while the new one does. Every command is identical on both sides; only the `tests/` tree differs. The three mutations, applied one at a time and reverted after each run: ``` validator_wrong_error litellm/proxy/_types.py UpdateKeyRequest's validator raises AttributeError instead of ValueError, so pydantic stops turning it into a 422 team_guard_dropped litellm/proxy/proxy_server.py the "team_id missing from team" guard is deleted, so a malformed default_team_settings entry crashes on the lookup instead breaker_rewraps litellm/caching/redis_cache.py the Redis circuit breaker re-raises Exception(str(e)), hiding which failure the caller actually saw ``` ### Before (21e9632713) #### A key-update validator starts failing with the wrong error class 1. Apply `validator_wrong_error`, then run ``` pytest tests/proxy_unit_tests/test_proxy_utils.py::test_update_key_request_validation -q ``` 2. Output: ``` 1 passed, 1 warning in 0.06s ``` #### A malformed team entry crashes instead of being rejected 1. Apply `team_guard_dropped`, then run ``` pytest tests/test_litellm/proxy/proxy_server/test_proxy_config.py::test_ProxyConfig__get_team_config_missing_team_id_raises -q ``` 2. Output: ``` 1 passed, 2 warnings in 2.45s ``` #### The Redis breaker hides which failure the caller saw 1. Apply `breaker_rewraps`, then run ``` pytest "tests/test_litellm/caching/test_redis_cache.py::test_only_connectivity_failures_open_the_breaker" -q ``` 2. Output: ``` 5 passed, 1 warning in 0.15s ``` ### After (ef07d8c63c) #### A key-update validator starts failing with the wrong error class 1. Apply `validator_wrong_error`, then run ``` pytest tests/proxy_unit_tests/test_proxy_utils.py::test_update_key_request_validation -q ``` 2. Output: ``` FAILED tests/proxy_unit_tests/test_proxy_utils.py::test_update_key_request_validation 1 failed, 1 warning in 0.15s ``` #### A malformed team entry crashes instead of being rejected 1. Apply `team_guard_dropped`, then run ``` pytest tests/test_litellm/proxy/proxy_server/test_proxy_config.py::test_ProxyConfig__get_team_config_missing_team_id_raises -q ``` 2. Output: ``` FAILED tests/test_litellm/proxy/proxy_server/test_proxy_config.py::test_ProxyConfig__get_team_config_missing_team_id_raises 1 failed, 2 warnings in 1.73s ``` #### The Redis breaker hides which failure the caller saw 1. Apply `breaker_rewraps`, then run ``` pytest "tests/test_litellm/caching/test_redis_cache.py::test_only_connectivity_failures_open_the_breaker" -q ``` 2. Output: ``` FAILED ...test_only_connectivity_failures_open_the_breaker[timeout_is_unhealthy] FAILED ...test_only_connectivity_failures_open_the_breaker[wrong_type_command_is_not] 5 failed, 1 warning in 0.26s ``` ### Rule and regression numbers `ruff check --config ruff-tests.toml tests` went from 111 `B017` findings to zero. Ruff has no autofix for this rule, so every site was edited by hand or by a script driven off the probe. The 55 touched test files were run in full at both hashes. 34 tests fail identically on each side, all of them live-provider tests with no Gemini, Bedrock, Azure or Databricks credentials on this machine. Exactly one test differs: ``` NEW at ef07d8c63c: tests/guardrails_tests/test_bedrock_guardrails.py::test_bedrock_guardrails_with_streaming ``` That is the finding, not a regression. 14 of the 15 tests in that file already fail here without AWS credentials; this one passed only because the `NoCredentialsError` boto3 raised, long before the guardrail ran, satisfied `pytest.raises(Exception)`. With credentials present it exercises the guardrail block it was written for. ## Type 🧹 Refactoring 🚄 Infrastructure ✅ Test ## Caveats (if any) - One site keeps `Exception` under a `noqa`: the code raises `Exception()` with no message - Nine live-API sites were narrowed by reading the code, not by probing - Two spend-flush tests raise `TypeError` from their mocks, never the DB error they name - The shared responses-API cancel test never reaches a provider; follow-up, not fixed here - Sites whose type depends on a provider key are pinned at the SDK base error ### Final Attestation - [ ] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signal.title: feat(ui): add per-key Savings tab to key detail page
signal.text: ## What Adds a "Savings" tab to the key detail view, showing the same four savings drivers (compression, prompt caching, auto-router, cache hit rate) and time-series chart as the proxy-wide Cost Optimization view, but filtered to one API key. For org admins, the tab shows the key's full savings across all requests. Non-admins see only their own requests on that key, with a scope note explaining the limitation. ## Root cause `userDailyActivityCall` and `userDailyActivityAggregatedCall` never forwarded an `api_key` query parameter to the backend, even though both handlers already accept and filter by it. ## Implementation **Unbundled scoping:** Extracted `useScopedDailyActivityRange(accessToken, scope: {userId, apiKey?})` so role resolution lives only in the org-wide entry point (`useDailyActivityRange`), not in a per-key caller. Reuse-by-parameter pattern scales to N callers without duplication. **Shared helpers:** Extracted `compressionOf`, `cachingOf`, `autorouterOf`, `savedTokensOf`, `cacheHitRatio` into utils so both UsageTab and KeySavingsTab use identical formulas and cannot diverge. **Shared component:** Extracted `SummaryCard` to avoid CSS/layout divergence. Both tabs render the same four-tile presenter. ## Files - `components/networking.tsx` — Add optional `apiKey` param to both daily-activity call wrappers - `costOptimizationUtils.ts` — Extract shared metrics helpers - `useDailyActivityRange.ts` — Refactor: `useScopedDailyActivityRange` + wrapper. Update test expectations for 6-arg tuple. - `UsageTab.tsx` — Import extracted helpers and `SummaryCard` component - `key_info_view.tsx` — Add "Savings" tab trigger + wiring; lazy-mounted (no keepMounted) - **NEW:** `components/shared/SummaryCard.tsx` — Shared four-tile presenter - **NEW:** `components/templates/KeySavingsTab.tsx` — Per-key view with admin/non-admin scoping - **NEW:** `components/templates/KeySavingsTab.test.tsx` — 7 tests ## Tests - 6121 component tests pass (1 pre-existing failure unrelated to this change) - Build succeeds with no new type errors - KeySavingsTab tests cover mount, loading, empty state, scoping, scope-note visibility ## Prior art / collision notes - PR #37570 (budgets tab) lands in same TabsList hunks as "Savings" tab, but different names → trivial conflict if both merge - PR #37659 (my own) adds fields to DailyActivityRange on different branch → no conflict with this PR's stable interface <!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY --> --- > [!NOTE] > **Medium Risk** > Touches spend-data scoping (who can see proxy-wide vs own-user activity) and forwards `api_key` on daily-activity fetches. Wrong role mapping would under- or over-show savings, though backend still enforces admin view. > > **Overview** > Adds a **Savings** tab on the key detail page with the same compression, prompt-caching, auto-router, and cache-hit figures as Cost Optimization, filtered to one key. > > Daily-activity clients now pass an optional `api_key`. Fetching is split into `useScopedDailyActivityRange` so callers choose `{userId, apiKey}` without the hook re-scoping. Proxy admins query the whole key (`userId: null`); everyone else, including **org admins**, is scoped to their own user id, with a note that shared-key spend from others is omitted. The tab is not `keepMounted`, so the rollup only loads when opened. > > Shared `SummaryCard`, savings metric helpers, and `cacheHitRatio` keep the two surfaces on the same formulas. `spendScopeUserId` / `hasProxyWideSpendView` replace `all_admin_roles` for this endpoint so org admin is not treated as proxy-wide. > > <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 3b592c0ad28453119b6c8806d15be9626cd6e20e. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup> <!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

signal.title: fix(vertex_ai): only fall back to a placeholder thought signature on the first parallel function call
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Gemini signs only the first parallel function call - LiteLLM fabricates a skip-validation placeholder on every sibling call - Replayed history no longer matches what Gemini emitted Google [documents both halves of this](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/models/thinking/thought-signatures#parallel_function_calling_example). On the expected shape: "In cases of parallel function calls in a single response, only the first functionCall part will contain the thought_signature." On the placeholder: "You can set thought_signature to skip_thought_signature_validator, but, this should be a last resort as it will negatively impact model performance." Fabricating one per sibling call is the opposite of a last resort, and it costs quality on every parallel tool-calling turn That cost is measurable, not theoretical. Internal testing at Google found that setting `skip_thought_signature_validator` on parallel function calls causes gemini-3.5 to return empty text responses. Following the documented shape, one real signature on the first call and nothing on the siblings, reduced the error rate How it solves it: - Placeholder fallback now applies to the first function call only - Unsigned sibling calls are replayed with no signature - Real signatures on any call are still preserved ## User Flow Before: a developer using parallel tool calling against a Gemini 3 model gets their conversation replayed with signatures the model never produced 1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with a `get_weather` tool and ask for Paris, London and Tokyo in parallel 2. Three tool calls come back; only the first id carries a `__thought__` suffix, the other two are bare 3. They append the assistant turn plus three tool results and send the same POST again 4. The turn is replayed upstream with the real signature on Paris and a `skip_thought_signature_validator` placeholder attached to London and Tokyo, so two of the three calls claim a signature the model never returned After: the same replay carries exactly the signatures the model produced 1. They send the same POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with the same tool and prompt 2. Three tool calls come back; only the first id carries a `__thought__` suffix, the other two are bare 3. They append the assistant turn plus three tool results and send the same POST again 4. The turn is replayed upstream with the real signature on Paris and nothing on London or Tokyo, matching the original response, and the answer comes back covering all three cities ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5888 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix E2e against real Vertex AI (`gemini-3.7-flash`, `vertex_location: global`). The observable that matters here is the exact payload Vertex receives on the replay turn, so the deployment's `api_base` points at a local recording relay that logs every request body and forwards it unchanged to the real `https://aiplatform.googleapis.com`. Proxy config: ```yaml model_list: - model_name: vertex_ai/gemini-3.7-flash litellm_params: model: vertex_ai/gemini-3.7-flash vertex_project: <project> vertex_location: global api_base: http://127.0.0.1:<relay port> general_settings: master_key: sk-1234 ``` Both legs run the same two turns against their own proxy, booted from the commit under test: ``` # Turn 1: three cities, one get_weather tool, parallel calls requested curl -sS "http://127.0.0.1:<proxy port>/v1/chat/completions" \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-1234' \ -d '{"model":"vertex_ai/gemini-3.7-flash","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"What is the weather in Paris, London and Tokyo? Call the get_weather tool once per city, all three in parallel."}],"tools":[{"type":"function","function":{"name":"get_weather","description":"get weather for a city","parameters":{"type":"object","properties":{"city":{"type":"string"}},"required":["city"]}}}]}' # Turn 2: turn 1's user message + the assistant tool_calls message + three {"role":"tool","tool_call_id":...,"content":"20C"} results curl -sS "http://127.0.0.1:<proxy port>/v1/chat/completions" \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-1234' \ -d @turn2_payload.json ``` ### Before (da7a10ebbdb16b34413566b0c980dac27af1de5b, the merge base) Turn 1 returns three parallel tool calls, a signature only on the first id: ``` {"city": "Paris"} id=call_2117163__thought__AY89a18pdiowbEw4FF1FoNDFGqoXixvwugvVO... {"city": "London"} id=call_2117164 {"city": "Tokyo"} id=call_2117165 ``` Turn 2 answers normally (200, `finish_reason: stop`): "The current weather in Paris, London, and Tokyo is: Paris 20°C, London 20°C, Tokyo 20°C". The model parts of that request as the relay recorded them on their way to Vertex: ``` get_weather({"city":"Paris"}) thoughtSignature=AY89a18pdiowbEw4FF1FoNDFGqoXixvwugvVOvu4gYXn... (the model's real signature, 468 chars) get_weather({"city":"London"}) thoughtSignature=c2tpcF90aG91Z2h0X3NpZ25hdHVyZV92YWxpZGF0b3I= (fabricated placeholder) get_weather({"city":"Tokyo"}) thoughtSignature=c2tpcF90aG91Z2h0X3NpZ25hdHVyZV92YWxpZGF0b3I= (fabricated placeholder) ``` `c2tpcF90aG91Z2h0X3NpZ25hdHVyZV92YWxpZGF0b3I=` is base64 for `skip_thought_signature_validator`: London and Tokyo were sent claiming a signature the model never produced ### After (a5ad22b8a3f734b09ce5e05a68dab5c5205907a4, the PR tip) Turn 1 returns three parallel tool calls, same shape as before, a signature only on the first id: ``` {"city": "Paris"} id=call_2351596__thought__AY89a1/YoawiNHzbcgAo4j41xnvh25ItNyHlm... {"city": "London"} id=call_2351597 {"city": "Tokyo"} id=call_2351598 ``` Turn 2 answers normally (200, `finish_reason: stop`): ``` The weather in Paris, London, and Tokyo is currently: * **Paris:** 20°C * **London:** 20°C * **Tokyo:** 20°C ``` The model parts of that request as the relay recorded them on their way to Vertex: ``` get_weather({"city":"Paris"}) thoughtSignature=AY89a1/YoawiNHzbcgAo4j41xnvh25ItNyHlmafAJ8Ln... (the model's real signature, 452 chars) get_weather({"city":"London"}) no thoughtSignature field get_weather({"city":"Tokyo"}) no thoughtSignature field ``` Paris keeps its real signature and the two unsigned siblings are replayed bare, matching what Gemini returned. No placeholder anywhere in the request Notes from the runs, both pre-existing behavior this PR leaves alone: - Real signature also rides inside the first tool_call id - Model parts serialize snake_case (`function_call`); Vertex accepts them ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - Placeholder still applies when the whole turn is unsigned, since Vertex returns a 400 on a turn with no signature anywhere. That keeps history migrated off pre-gemini-3 models working - The gemini-3 gate on the placeholder is pre-existing behavior from #16812 and is unchanged here, only narrowed to the first call - Through the proxy, a signature replayed inside a tool call id does not reach this code, so `provider_specific_fields.thought_signature` is the carrier that works there. Pre-existing and unchanged by this PR: the first call still gets a placeholder and the siblings go bare, which Vertex accepts ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR - [x] a5ad22b8a3f734b09ce5e05a68dab5c5205907a4 passes /live-pr-risk

signal.title: feat(ui): edit project input and output TPM limits from the Projects modal
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Project ITPM/OTPM quotas were API-only, unreachable from the UI - Admins had to hand-edit raw project metadata to set them - A limit removed in the modal stayed enforced by the proxy How it solves it: - Model-Specific Limits rows now take Input TPM and Output TPM - Update sends every limit map, empty ones included - An emptied map is what /project/update reads as "clear this" ## User Flow Before: an admin capping input and output tokens separately for an application cannot do it from the Projects page, and cannot take a cap back off once it exists 1. They open http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=projects and click Edit on a project 2. Under Advanced Settings, Model-Specific Limits offers only a TPM Limit and an RPM Limit per model, so input and output share one bucket 3. To get separate caps they instead add raw metadata pairs named `model_itpm_limit` and `model_otpm_limit`, which only accept a single string value, not a per-model map 4. Reopening the modal shows those two keys sitting in the Metadata editor as stringified objects, and any save writes the stringified value back 5. Deleting the row that holds a cap and saving reports success, yet requests for that model keep getting 429s against the cap the admin just removed After: the same admin sets and later removes independent input and output caps per model straight from the modal 1. They open http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=projects and click Edit on a project 2. Under Advanced Settings, each Model-Specific Limits row now offers Model, TPM Limit, RPM Limit, Input TPM Limit and Output TPM Limit 3. They enter a model name with, say, 10000 Input TPM and 2000 Output TPM, and save 4. Reopening the modal shows the row prefilled with both values, and the Metadata editor no longer lists the limit keys 5. Traffic for that project is then capped independently: exceeding the input budget returns 429 while output budget still has room, and vice versa 6. They reopen the modal, clear the Input TPM Limit field or remove the whole row, and save 7. Reopening shows the cap gone, and traffic that the cap used to reject now goes through ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-4693 ## Review notes The Projects modal talks to `/project/update`, where an omitted key means "leave the stored value alone". The form used to omit any limit map that came out empty, so removing a quota in the UI sent nothing about it and the proxy kept enforcing the quota the admin believed was gone. Empty metadata behaved the same way. The fix splits the payload builder in two. Create still leaves blanks out, since a new project has nothing to clear. Update sends every map the form knows about, empty included, and an empty map is what makes the stored quota disappear. The absent case is still reachable: the Edit modal submits nothing about guardrails, limits or metadata unless Advanced Settings was opened, so an untouched save is byte for byte what it was before. Both halves are covered. On the frontend, the modal test removes the row and asserts the payload carries `model_itpm_limit: {}`; restoring the omit-when-empty behaviour fails it. On the backend, `/project/update` is exercised with an empty map and asserted to write metadata that no longer carries the quota, alongside the counterpart test pinning that an update which says nothing about limits does not touch metadata at all. ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more - [x] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge?
