The call is sent to fal's generic endpoint with OpenAI's own field names, so it comes back as a 4xx from fal rather than an image URL 4. They open https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs and, for anything that did get through, see the request at $0 spend After: the same request returns a hosted image and shows real spend 1. They add the same deployment and restart the proxy 2. They send the same POST https://litellm-domain/v1/images/generations 3. They get back 200 with a `data` array holding a fal-hosted image URL at 1024x1536 4. https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs shows that request at non-zero spend ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5910 ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Runbook for whoever has one, with `FAL_AI_API_KEY` exported and this deployment in the config: ```yaml model_list: - model_name: fal-gpt-image-2 litellm_params: model: fal_ai/openai/gpt-image-2 ``` 1. `python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config <config>.yaml --detailed_debug 2>&1 | tee litellm.log` 2. `curl -s http://localhost:4000/v1/images/generations -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model": "fal-gpt-image-2", "prompt": "a red bicycle in the rain", "size": "1024x1536", "quality": "high", "n": 1}'` 3. signal.title: fix(redis): apply Azure AD and GCP IAM auth to every async client path
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Async Redis clients from `REDIS_URL` never authenticated at all - Their connection pools failed the exact same way - So did async Sentinel clients - Azure AD and GCP IAM Redis caching was silently dead How it solves it: - Build the credential provider once, before any branch - URL, pool, sentinel, and cluster paths all inherit it - Let `credential_provider` through the cluster kwargs filter - Leave a coroutine connect func for redis-py to await - Drop it where the async cluster client cannot accept it - Keep the data node's token off the Sentinel monitors - Regression tests cover every one of those paths ## User Flow Before: an admin running two proxy replicas that cache into a managed Redis with Microsoft Entra ID gets no shared cache at all, so every replica pays the provider separately 1. They set `REDIS_URL=rediss://<their-cache>.<region>.redis.azure.net:10000`, `REDIS_USERNAME=<the identity's object id>`, and `REDIS_AZURE_AD_TOKEN=true`, turn on `cache: true` with `cache_params.type: redis`, and start two replicas 2. They call `GET /cache/ping` on replica A and get `503 Service Unavailable` with `{"message": "Service Unhealthy"}` 3. They send `POST /v1/chat/completions` to replica A and are billed for it, `x-litellm-response-cost: 0.000645` 4. They send the identical `POST /v1/chat/completions` to replica B and are billed a second time, `x-litellm-response-cost: 0.000675`, coming back with a different response id and no `x-litellm-cache-key` header 5. Their proxy logs fill with `AuthenticationError: Azure AD authentication failed for Redis`, followed by `Redis circuit breaker is open` 6. They connect to the cache themselves and find it empty, so nothing either replica did ever reached it After: the same setup authenticates, so the second replica serves the answer out of Redis instead of buying it again 1. They set the same three environment variables, turn on the same cache config, and start two replicas 2. They call `GET /cache/ping` on replica A and get `200 OK` with `{"status":"healthy","cache_type":"redis","ping_response":true,"set_cache_response":"success"}` 3. They send `POST /v1/chat/completions` to replica A and are billed for it, `x-litellm-response-cost: 0.00035` 4. They send the identical `POST /v1/chat/completions` to replica B and get back the same response id as replica A carrying `x-litellm-cache-key: 6c2debe1...`, so no second call to the provider happens 5. Their proxy logs carry no Redis authentication errors at all 6. They connect to the cache themselves and find the cache key sitting there next to the proxy's own config keys ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Related to LIT-5889 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more - [x] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Everything below ran against a real Azure Managed Redis (Balanced_B0, TLS, access keys **Disabled**, so Microsoft Entra ID is the only way in) and the real OpenAI API. No mocks, real spend. Before is the merge base `cb4eb82249` on ports 47311 and 47313, After is the PR tip `c09643ac4c` on ports 56981 and 56249 Shared setup, identical on both sides. Two proxy replicas point at that one cache, which is what an HA deployment looks like and what makes a shared cache observable at all: a single replica hides the whole bug behind its own in-memory layer, still answering "Cache Hit!" while Redis is unreachable ```bash export REDIS_URL='rediss://litellm-lit5889-redis.eastus2.redis.azure.net:10000' export REDIS_USERNAME='<object id of the Entra identity>' export REDIS_AZURE_AD_TOKEN='true' $ cat config.yaml model_list: - model_name: gpt-5.6 litellm_params: model: openai/gpt-5.6 api_key: os.environ/OPENAI_API_KEY litellm_settings: cache: true cache_params: type: redis $ python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config config.yaml --port <replica A port> --detailed_debug $ python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config config.yaml --port <replica B port> --detailed_debug ``` Shared background, and the reason the fix takes the shape it does. Three redis-py legs against that same cache, driven by LiteLLM's own Azure AD helpers, showing that an async connection cannot authenticate through a `redis_connect_func` no matter which code path hands it one ``` redis-py 5.3.1, server rediss://litellm-lit5889-redis.eastus2.redis.azure.net:10000 1. sync client + redis_connect_func : PING -> True 2. async client + redis_connect_func : AuthenticationError: Azure AD authentication failed for Redis 3. async client + credential_provider : PING -> True ``` Leg 2 fails because that connect function runs the AUTH exchange with the blocking client API, so on an async connection `send_command` and `read_response` hand back coroutines nobody awaits. Python says so itself in the same run ``` litellm/_redis.py:314: RuntimeWarning: coroutine 'AbstractConnection.send_command' was never awaited self.send_command("AUTH", *auth_args, check_health=False) ``` ### Before (cb4eb82249) #### Cache health on replica A 1. `curl -s -i http://127.0.0.1:47311/cache/ping -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234"` ``` HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable {"error":{"message":"{\"message\": \"Service Unhealthy\", ... ``` #### The same completion on two replicas sharing one cache 1. `curl -s -i http://127.0.0.1:47311/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"model":"gpt-5.6","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Reply with exactly: lit5889 before probe"}]}'` ``` HTTP/1.1 200 OK x-litellm-response-cost: 0.000645 x-litellm-cache-key: <absent> body id: chatcmpl-EF5z2Zc8Riy9I3MYoCYnVwce8q8Bp body content: lit5889 before probe ``` 2. The identical request against replica B on port 47313, billed all over again and answering with a different id ``` HTTP/1.1 200 OK x-litellm-response-cost: 0.000675 x-litellm-cache-key: <absent> body id: chatcmpl-EF5z4zm1mztUElYsqVpNgiz2Gi7JD body content: lit5889 before probe ``` #### What actually reached the Redis server 1. Connecting to the cache directly and listing its keys ``` keys matching '*': 0 ``` 2. Replica A's log over that run ``` 14 Azure AD authentication failed for Redis 4 circuit breaker is open — skipping async_get_cache 17 circuit breaker is open — skipping async_set_cache ``` ### After (c09643ac4c) #### Cache health on replica A 1. `curl -s -i http://127.0.0.1:56981/cache/ping -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234"` ``` HTTP/1.1 200 OK {"status":"healthy","cache_type":"redis","ping_response":true,"set_cache_response":"success", ... ``` #### The same completion on two replicas sharing one cache 1. `curl -s -i http://127.0.0.1:56981/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"model":"gpt-5.6","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Reply with exactly: lit5889 after6 probe"}]}'` ``` HTTP/1.1 200 OK x-litellm-response-cost: 0.00035 x-litellm-cache-key: <absent> body id: chatcmpl-EF6tzdlwAN7DkG6m0QfIAFyBSBL7L body content: lit5889 after6 probe ``` 2. The identical request against replica B on port 56249, which now serves replica A's own answer with a cache key instead of calling the provider a second time ``` HTTP/1.1 200 OK x-litellm-cache-key: bf79f7bcbbf817e07c2fceace95d8060e92b97c746bbc90eb234ab50fe3d31b9 body id: chatcmpl-EF6tzdlwAN7DkG6m0QfIAFyBSBL7L body content: lit5889 after6 probe ``` #### What actually reached the Redis server 1. Connecting to the cache directly and listing its keys, which is where replica A's write landed and where replica B's read found it ``` keys matching '*': 14 86d4ac816220d30f86882fe349625d1b1a9a2b7b4821e2ae1c9e5ee050c5896a bf79f7bcbbf817e07c2fceace95d8060e92b97c746bbc90eb234ab50fe3d31b9 litellm_config:param:anthropic_beta_headers_reload_config litellm_config:param:environment_variables litellm_config:param:general_settings ``` 2. Replica A's log over that run, with no Redis authentication errors and no circuit breaker trips at all ``` (no matches) ``` ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - Managed Redis wants `REDIS_USERNAME` set to the identity's object id - A blocking custom `redis_connect_func` still cannot run on async - The cluster and Sentinel paths are proven by construction, not live ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR - [x] c09643ac4c0053c4d5514ecf199041c6013070b5 passes /live-pr-risk

The same three calls with `"model": "fireworks_ai/accounts/fireworks/models/deepseek-v4-flash-0731"` bill at $0.14/1M input and $0.28/1M output, so downstream spend reports carry the real numbers ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5852 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [ ] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Live A/B through a real proxy against the real Fireworks API, no mocks. Both legs run the same wildcard config and the same venv, and the tree under test is asserted from `litellm.__file__`, so the runs differ only in the commit the proxy serves: ```yaml model_list: - model_name: "fireworks_ai/*" litellm_params: model: "fireworks_ai/*" api_key: os.environ/FIREWORKS_AI_API_KEY general_settings: master_key: sk-1234 ``` ```bash LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True .venv/bin/litellm --config fw_wildcard.yaml --port <free port> ``` ### Before (merge base f6eaca9069) ```bash curl -sS -D - http://localhost:46910/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model": "fireworks_ai/accounts/fireworks/models/kimi-k3", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Say hi"}], "max_tokens": 16}' ``` ``` HTTP/1.1 200 OK x-litellm-response-cost-original: 0.0 x-litellm-response-cost-input: 0.0 x-litellm-response-cost-output: 0.0 x-litellm-key-spend: 0.0 ``` The bare `x-litellm-response-cost` header is absent on every 200, and the sub-headers all read 0.0 ### After (PR tip c15e4602e8) Same curl, same prompt, same port-free proxy on the PR commit: ``` HTTP/1.1 200 OK x-litellm-response-cost: 0.00051 x-litellm-response-cost-original: 0.00051 x-litellm-response-cost-input: 0.00027 x-litellm-response-cost-output: 0.00024 x-litellm-key-spend: 0.00051 ``` That lines up with the published rates exactly. Usage came back as 90 prompt and 16 completion tokens, so 90 at $3/M is $0.00027 in and 16 at $15/M is $0.00024 out ### Both legs, every call | Call | Endpoint | Model | Before | After | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 1 | /v1/chat/completions | kimi-k3 | 200, cost 0.0 | 200, cost 0.00051 | | 2 | /v1/responses | kimi-k3 | 200, cost 0.0 | 200, cost 0.00051 | | 3 | /v1/messages | kimi-k3 | 200, cost 0.0 | 200, cost 0.00051 | | 4 | /v1/chat/completions | deepseek-v4-flash | 200, cost 0.0 | 200, cost 5.32e-06 | | 5 | /v1/responses | deepseek-v4-flash | 200, cost 0.0 | 200, cost 5.32e-06 | | 6 | /v1/messages | deepseek-v4-flash | 200, cost 0.0 | 200, cost 5.32e-06 | | 7 | /v1/chat/completions | kimi-k3 short slug | 200, cost 0.0 | 200, cost 0.00051 | | 8 | GET /v1/models | both | absent, 294 ids | present, 314 ids | | 9 | chat + tool_choice required | kimi-k3 | 400 | 200, tool_calls | Call 8: the twenty added keys are exactly the twenty new ids in the wildcard expansion, 294 to 314 Call 9 before, the capability gate rejected the request before it ever reached Fireworks: ``` litellm.UnsupportedParamsError: fireworks_ai does not support parameters: ['tool_choice'], for model=accounts/fireworks/models/kimi-k3 ``` Call 9 after, the same request is forwarded and comes back with a real tool call: ```json {"finish_reason": "tool_calls", "tool_calls": [{"index": 0, "function": {"arguments": "{}", "name": "say_hi"}, "id": "say_hi_0", "type": "function"}]} ``` So the entry does not just fix billing, it also unblocks tool calling that the gate was refusing. That one call runs with `max_tokens` 400 rather than 16, because kimi-k3 spends its budget on reasoning before emitting a tool call and 16 truncates first. The before-leg rejection comes from the param gate ahead of the provider, so the token budget has no bearing on it ### Pricing sources Every cost value comes from the [Fireworks serverless pricing table](https://docs.fireworks.ai/serverless/pricing), re-checked row by row for all ten models. Context windows were verified against the live models API rather than the docs page: kimi-k3, kimi-k3-fast and deepseek-v4-flash-0731 each report `context_length` 1048576, which is what this PR sets ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - Data-only change; no test file maps to the cost map JSON - `qwen3p8-max` carries `max_output_tokens: 65536` from the upstream Qwen spec, but Fireworks enforces no output cap of its own, `max_tokens` of 65537 and 999999 both come back 200. It only has an effect under `modify_params: true`, which is off by default, where a larger `max_tokens` gets clamped down to 65536 - fast/us variants keyed under accounts/fireworks/routers/, matching the existing glm-5p1-fast pattern - deepseek-v4-flash-0731 kept alongside the older deepseek-v4-flash slug ### Final Attestation - [ ] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR <!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY --> --- > [!NOTE] > **Low Risk** > Data-only cost-map updates; incorrect prices could mis-bill spend reports but there is no runtime or auth logic change. > > **Overview** > Stops Fireworks serverless models from reporting **$0 cost** by adding them to the cost map (and backup) with published rates, context windows, and capability flags. > > New aliases cover `kimi-k3` (plus fast/us), `deepseek-v4-flash-0731`, `glm-5p2-fast` (plus us), `qwen3p8-max`, `muse-glimmer-30b`, and Nemotron variants, under both short `fireworks_ai/` names and full `accounts/fireworks/models` or `routers` paths. > > <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit c15e4602e83d047dade394097f5247929d49f09e. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup> <!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY --> - [x] c15e4602e8 passes /live-pr-risk

signal.title: fix(model_prices): consolidate eleven open registry audits into one changeset
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Eleven open PRs all edit the same cost map - Each one conflicts with the others on merge - Older branches revert fields the base gained since - Two of them carry deprecation dates the docs contradict How it solves it: - One branch carrying all eleven PRs' registry data - Merged per model entry, per field, onto current staging - Contradicted Gemini / text-embedding-004 dates dropped - Fresh 2026-08-20 audit adds Gemini, Voyage, Perplexity entries - Same tests as the source PRs, all passing This replaces #35911, #36017, #36080, #36113, #36188, #36444, #37029, #37252, #37632, #37512 and #37536. Those can be closed once this lands; nothing in this branch is new registry research beyond re-verifying what they claimed, plus the audit findings below ### What was merged, per source PR | Source PR | Entries carried in | Notes | | --- | --- | --- | | #35911 | 4 | Vertex AI MaaS per-token rates | | #36017 | 3 | `bedrock_mantle/openai.gpt-5.6-{sol,terra,luna}` 1M context | | #36080 | 66 | provider `deprecation_date` backfill (minus `text-embedding-004`, see below) | | #36113 | 3 | `gemini-3.1-flash-lite-image` pricing + capability fields, plus its test | | #36188 | 86 | OpenAI/Anthropic `deprecation_date` refresh (minus 4 Gemini rows, see below) | | #36444 | 3 | `gpt-5.6-cyber`, `daybreak-red-latest`, `daybreak-blue-latest`, plus its test | | #37029 | 16 | missing OpenAI models, stale limits | | #37252 | 3 | `openrouter/claude-opus-5`, `deepseek-v4-pro` | | #37632 | 17 | Mistral `*-latest` refresh, Z.ai GLM 5.2, Mistral OCR 4.1, xAI + Cohere deprecation dates | | #37512 | 20 | Fireworks serverless models, re-verified row by row (see below) | | #37536 | 15 | Bedrock batch rates for Claude 4.5 and Qwen, plus its test | Five conflicts arose where two PRs edited the same field; in every case the newer PR's value is a strict superset and won: ``` gpt-5.6-cyber / daybreak-red-latest / daybreak-blue-latest #36444: mode=responses, supported_endpoints=[/v1/responses] #37029: mode=chat, supported_endpoints=[/v1/chat/completions, /v1/responses] + supports_computer_use (cyber and red only), supports_parallel_function_calling, source <-- kept xai/grok-code-fast-1, xai/grok-code-fast-1-0825 #36080 and #37632 set deprecation_date=2026-05-15 identically ``` The merge is field-level, not entry-level, on purpose. #36017 was opened before staging gained tiered `*_above_272k_tokens` pricing for the same three `bedrock_mantle` models; replacing its entries wholesale would have silently deleted those four fields per model. Only the fields each PR actually changed relative to its own merge base are applied After merging current `litellm_internal_staging` back in, `mistral/zai-glm-5-2` (which landed on staging via #37110 with `max_input_tokens` 1048576 and `supports_reasoning: true`, plus a `mistral/glm-5-2` alias) was dropped from this branch so staging's version and its pinning test stand, which also removes the duplicate JSON key the merge produced. A field-level audit of the final delta then caught the one place the consolidation itself deleted a field: refreshing `mistral/mistral-small-latest` to Small 4.0 copied the `mistral/mistral-small-2603` entry shape and dropped `supports_vision: true`, even though the Small 4 model card states "Accepts both text and image input". Restored on `-latest`, added on `-2603` which had the same gap, and pinned by `tests/test_litellm/test_mistral_small_4_0_model_metadata.py`. Test-quality gate fixes on the two carried-in test files: dropped the `sys.path.insert` no-op in the Gemini image pricing test, and switched the GPT-5.6 Cyber cost test to `monkeypatch.setenv` / `monkeypatch.setattr` so it no longer leaks `LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP` and `litellm.model_cost` into later tests A second capability gap turned up in the same sweep, this time carried in from the source PR rather than created by the merge: #37029 sets `supports_computer_use` on `gpt-5.6-cyber` and `daybreak-red-latest` but not on `daybreak-blue-latest`, even though OpenAI lists `computer_use` among the supported tools for Daybreak Blue and for `gpt-5.6-sol`, the snapshot the blue alias resolves to. Both entries now carry the flag, which stops `/model/info` and the capability gates from reporting blue as unable to use computer tools while its siblings can. `gpt-5.6-sol` was already in the registry and untouched by any of the eleven PRs, so fixing only the alias would have left the alias and its own snapshot disagreeing. `tests/test_litellm/test_daybreak_model_metadata.py` pins the family's capability contract and that agreement ### New registry research (2026-08-20 audit run) #### Gemini / Vertex (https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/pricing, https://cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/pricing) - Added `gemini/gemini-3.5-live-translate-preview` (`gemini-3.5-live-translate-preview` on the AI Studio pricing page and in the Gemini 3 model list): audio in $3.50/1M, audio out $21.00/1M, `/v1/realtime`, audio-only in and out. Google publishes no input/output token limits for this model, so `max_input_tokens` / `max_output_tokens` are deliberately omitted rather than guessed. - Fixed a wrong audio rate on Gemini 3.5 Flash (`gemini/gemini-3.5-flash`, `gemini-3.5-flash`, `vertex_ai/gemini-3.5-flash`): the registry had `input_cost_per_audio_token` $1.00/1M and `input_cost_per_audio_token_priority` $1.80/1M. Both pages price 3.5 Flash audio at the *same* rate as text (AI Studio shows a single "Input price $1.50", Vertex shows "Input (text, image, video, audio) Global $1.50" and Priority "$2.70"), so these become $1.50/1M and $2.70/1M. - Added the batch and flex tiers for the same three entries, which were missing entirely: batch input $0.75/1M, batch output $4.50/1M, flex input $0.75/1M, flex output $4.50/1M. Flex context caching is $0.08/1M on the AI Studio page and $0.075/1M on the Vertex page, so `cache_read_input_token_cost_flex` follows whichever page the entry's `source` points at. #### Voyage (https://docs.voyageai.com/docs/pricing, plus the model tables on the embeddings / contextualized-chunk / multimodal doc pages for context length) Six missing models, all `mode: embedding`: | Entry | input $/1M | context | dim | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `voyage/voyage-4-large` | 0.12 | 32,000 | 1024 | | `voyage/voyage-4` | 0.06 | 32,000 | 1024 | | `voyage/voyage-4-lite` | 0.02 | 32,000 | 1024 | | `voyage/voyage-code-4` | 0.12 | 32,000 | 1024 | | `voyage/voyage-context-4` | 0.12 | 120,000 | 1024 | | `voyage/voyage-multimodal-3.5` | 0.12 | 32,000 | 1024 | `voyage-4-nano` is listed in the docs as an open-weight Hugging Face model with no row on the pricing page, so it is not added. `voyage-multimodal-3.5` also has a per-pixel price ($0.60/1B pixels) with no registry field for it, so only the per-token rate is recorded #### Perplexity (https://docs.perplexity.ai/getting-started/pricing, https://docs.perplexity.ai/api-reference/contextualized-embeddings-post) Two missing contextualized-embedding models, which have their own `/v1/contextualizedembeddings` endpoint and their own prices: - `perplexity/pplx-embed-context-v1-0.6b`: $0.008/1M, 32K tokens per document, 1024 dims - `perplexity/pplx-embed-context-v1-4b`: $0.05/1M, 32K tokens per document, 2560 dims #### Absorbed: #37512 (Fireworks serverless models) Registry-data-only PR. All 20 entries carried in. Prices re-verified row by row against https://docs.fireworks.ai/serverless/pricing (input / cache-read / output per 1M): Kimi K3 3.00/0.30/15.00, Kimi K3 Fast 4.50/0.45/22.50, Kimi K3 US 3.30/0.33/16.50, DeepSeek V4 Flash (0731) 0.14/0.028/0.28, GLM 5.2 Fast and GLM 5.2 Fast US 2.10/0.21/6.60, Qwen 3.8 Max 2.00/0.25/6.00, Muse Glimmer 30B 0.35/0.04/1.50, Nemotron 3.5 Lightning 30B A3B 0.05/0.01/0.20, Nemotron 3 Ultra 0.60/0.12/2.40. All match Context lengths and the vision / tool flags were re-checked against each model's own page on https://app.fireworks.ai/models/fireworks/<model>, which publishes `contextLength`, `supportsImageInput` and `supportsTools`: kimi-k3 1,048,576 + image true, deepseek-v4-flash-0731 1,048,576 + image false, glm-5p2 1,048,576 + image false, muse-glimmer-30b 131,072 + image true, nemotron-lightning-3p5-30b-a3b and nemotron-3-ultra-nvfp4 262,144 + image false. The `-fast` / `-us` SKUs are routers with no model page; they inherit the base model's verified context length One deviation from #37512: its 65,536 output cap for `qwen3p8-max` is confirmed by no official Fireworks source (the models API reports `contextLength: 0`, and a live completion accepts an arbitrary `max_tokens` with no validation error), so `max_output_tokens` / `max_tokens` stay off that entry. The input side is published: the model page (fireworks.ai/models/fireworks/qwen3p8-max) states a 262k context length, so both `qwen3p8-max` entries carry `max_input_tokens: 262144`. Its price and its vision / tool flags are confirmed and are carried in. `max_output_tokens` is not published anywhere by Fireworks for any of these models; the values carried in match what the registry already uses for the same base models #### Absorbed: #37536 (Bedrock batch rates for Claude 4.5 and Qwen) Registry-data-only PR, plus its `tests/test_litellm/test_bedrock_batch_pricing.py`. 15 entries gain `input_cost_per_token_batches` / `output_cost_per_token_batches`. Every added value is exactly 50% of that same entry's on-demand rate, which is what AWS documents: https://aws.amazon.com/bedrock/pricing/ states batch inference for select FMs is "at a 50% lower price compared to on-demand inference pricing", and https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/batch-inference-supported.html lists `anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0`, `anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929-v1:0` and `qwen.qwen3-235b-a22b-2507-v1:0` as batch-supported ### Deprecation dates that were dropped as unverifiable Cross-checking every `deprecation_date` in this branch against the raw provider tables found five values that the official docs contradict, all of them from the two deprecation-focused PRs: | Entry | PR claimed | https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/deprecations says | This PR | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `gemini/gemini-embedding-001` | 2026-07-14 (#36188) | shutdown May 14, 2028 | keeps 2028-05-14 | | `gemini/gemini-2.5-pro` | 2026-10-16 (#36188) | "No shutdown date announced" | no date | | `gemini/gemini-2.5-flash` | 2026-10-16 (#36188) | "No shutdown date announced" | no date | | `gemini/gemini-2.5-flash-lite` | 2026-10-16 (#36188) | "No shutdown date announced" | no date | | `text-embedding-004` | 2027-04-01 (#36080) | shutdown January 14, 2026 | keeps 2026-01-14 | The 2026-07-14 and 2026-10-16 values look like the *deprecation announcement* column, not the shutdown column, so #36188 should not be merged as-is even if this consolidation is rejected `gpt-audio-mini-2025-12-15` and `gpt-realtime-mini-2025-12-15` keep the 2027-01-20 date from #36188 on the strength of the family-level statement on https://platform.openai.com/docs/deprecations ("legacy audio, realtime, and transcription model families and snapshots ... removal from the API on January 20, 2027"); the individual snapshots are not listed as rows there, only the `gpt-audio-mini` / `gpt-realtime-mini` families and the `-2025-10-06` snapshots. Say the word and I'll drop those two too ### Checked, nothing changed - **Cohere**: https://docs.cohere.com/docs/models lists `command-a-plus-05-2026`, `command-a-reasoning-08-2025`, `command-a-translate-08-2025`, `command-a-vision-07-2025`, `rerank-v4.0-fast` and `rerank-v4.0-pro`, none of which are in the registry, but https://cohere.com/pricing renders its price table client-side and the per-model doc pages carry no per-token rates, so nothing could be added without guessing. Left out on purpose. - **Anthropic** (https://docs.claude.com/en/docs/about-claude/pricing), **OpenAI** (https://platform.openai.com/docs/pricing), **DeepSeek** (https://api-docs.deepseek.com/quick_start/pricing), **Groq** (https://console.groq.com/docs/models): current model lists and the newest entries' rates and limits match the registry already. - Open registry PRs left alone as not registry-data changes or not Devin-owned rolling scope: #28170 (Telnyx provider, new provider code), #36233 (Vertex Chirp 3 gRPC/WebSocket transport), #29898 (bedrock-invoke output_format behavior), #30383 (router cost backfill logic). ### Sources Every value in this branch comes from a source PR that cited it; the pages re-checked while consolidating and auditing are: - https://platform.openai.com/docs/deprecations - https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/deprecations - https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/pricing - https://cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/pricing - https://docs.claude.com/en/docs/about-claude/model-deprecations - https://docs.x.ai/developers/migration/may-15-retirement - https://docs.cohere.com/docs/deprecations - https://docs.mistral.ai/getting-started/models/models_overview/ - https://docs.voyageai.com/docs/pricing - https://docs.perplexity.ai/getting-started/pricing - https://docs.fireworks.ai/serverless/pricing - https://aws.amazon.com/bedrock/pricing/ ## User Flow Before: a proxy admin cannot tell which of eleven open cost-map PRs to merge, and merging more than one of them by hand conflicts 1. They open https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pulls and see eleven open PRs all editing `model_prices_and_context_window.json`. 2. They merge one; the next one now conflicts on the same JSON and has to be rebased by hand. 3. If they merge #36017 after staging gained tiered `bedrock_mantle` pricing, `GET https://litellm-domain/model/info` stops reporting the above-272k rates for `bedrock_mantle/openai.gpt-5.6-sol` and long-context spend is undercharged. 4. If they merge #36188, `GET https://litellm-domain/model/info` reports `gemini-2.5-pro` as retiring on 2026-10-16 and `gemini-embedding-001` on 2026-07-14, and neither matches Google's docs. 5. If they merge #37029, `GET https://litellm-domain/model/info` comes back with `supports_computer_use: true` on `gpt-5.6-cyber` and `daybreak-red-latest` but no such field on `daybreak-blue-latest`, so a client that picks models off that field sends computer-use work to red and skips blue even though OpenAI ships the tool on both. 6. They send a 200k-token prompt to `mistral/codestral-2508`, it goes out over the wire, and Mistral answers with a context-length error. After: one PR carries all of it, and the numbers match the provider docs 1. They merge this PR alone and close the other eleven. 2. `GET https://litellm-domain/model/info` reports the refreshed entries, including `bedrock_mantle/openai.gpt-5.6-sol` with both its 1M context window and its above-272k rates. 3. `gemini-2.5-pro` and `gemini-2.5-flash` come back with no deprecation date, `gemini-embedding-001` with 2028-05-14, matching https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/deprecations. 4. `daybreak-blue-latest` comes back with `supports_computer_use: true` alongside `gpt-5.6-cyber` and `daybreak-red-latest`, and so does `gpt-5.6-sol`, the snapshot the blue alias resolves to, so the same client now sends computer-use work to blue as well. 5. That same 200k-token prompt to `mistral/codestral-2508` is turned away by the gateway before it leaves, once `enable_pre_call_checks` is on, rather than travelling to Mistral to be refused there. 6. `xai/grok-4`, `command-r`, `rerank-english-v2.0` and the other newly annotated entries carry the `deprecation_date` that `GET https://litellm-domain/model/deprecations` (#26900) surfaces. 7. Requests to `voyage/voyage-4`, the new Fireworks serverless models, and Bedrock batch jobs on Claude 4.5 are priced from the new entries instead of logging $0 spend at https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs. ## Relevant issues Supports #26900. Supersedes #35911, #36017, #36080, #36113, #36188, #36444, #37029, #37252, #37632, #37512, #37536 ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5896 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more - [x] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (5/5 on this PR) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix A proxy booted at the tip `5c9ed89301` from a clean worktree, with `LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True` and a config-only model list, no database attached. Provider calls below are real billed requests against real provider APIs, not fixtures. Merge-base values come from `git show 2f23cf5701:model_prices_and_context_window.json`, and where behavior is at stake the diff itself is cited rather than a second run. ### Registry integrity at the tip 1. `git diff --name-only 2f23cf5701..5c9ed89301` lists the two registry JSON files and five test files, and nothing else. No production code is touched, so every behavior change below is driven by the data alone. 2. `python3 ci_cd/check_files_match.py` prints `Passed! Files model_prices_and_context_window.json and litellm/model_prices_and_context_window_backup.json match.` 3. `uv run --no-sync python ci_cd/generate_model_prices_schema.py` regenerates the schema and `git status` reports no change to it, so the merged data introduces no new field shape. 4. Entry-level delta against the merge base: 40 added, 0 removed, 45 changed, and no field is dropped from any changed entry. ### Prices reach the API surface `GET /v1/model/info` against the tip proxy, with the merge-base value from `git show 2f23cf5701:model_prices_and_context_window.json` alongside: | Entry and field | Base `2f23cf5701` | Tip `5c9ed89301`, served live | |---|---|---| | `fireworks_ai/deepseek-v4-flash-0731` input | not in registry | 1.4e-07 | | `fireworks_ai/deepseek-v4-flash-0731` output | not in registry | 2.8e-07 | | `voyage/voyage-4` input | not in registry | 6e-08 | | `fireworks_ai/qwen3p8-max` max_input_tokens | not in registry | 262144 | | `gemini-3.5-flash` audio input | 1e-06 | 1.5e-06 | | `mistral/mistral-small-latest` input | 6e-08 | 1.5e-07 | ### Billing matches the merged rates, on real calls **Fireworks `deepseek-v4-flash-0731`,** an entry this PR adds. Usage came back 11 prompt / 5 completion. A live call with `"service_tier":"priority"` at the tip, with the body confirming `service_tier: "priority"` came back honored, billed 13 audio + 8 text prompt tokens at `4.11e-05`. signal.title: fix(proxy): route blocked models through healthy fallbacks
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Fully blocked primary deployments reject requests before configured fallbacks run. - Healthy fallback deployments therefore cannot recover availability. How it solves it: - Preserve the blocked-model error when no fallback deployment is available. - Let the Router fallback chain run when a fallback remains unblocked. - Add mocked regression coverage for recovery and rejection behavior. ## User Flow Before: a client receives `Model is blocked` even though its configured fallback is healthy. 1. The operator blocks every deployment behind the alias's primary model group. 2. The client sends `POST https://<proxy-host>/v1/chat/completions` with `model: "DeepSeek-Flash"`. 3. The gateway immediately returns a `Model is blocked` permission error. 4. The client receives no completion because the configured fallback is never attempted. After: the same client request uses the healthy configured fallback. 1. The operator blocks every deployment behind the alias's primary model group. 2. The client sends `POST https://<proxy-host>/v1/chat/completions` with `model: "DeepSeek-Flash"`. 3. The gateway sees that a configured fallback still has an unblocked deployment. 4. The client receives the completion from that fallback; fully blocked models without a usable fallback still return `Model is blocked`. ## Relevant issues Fixes #36665 ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [ ] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix No live provider proof was captured in this environment. The regression tests use mocked deployments, as required for tests under `tests/test_litellm/`; a maintainer should run the live proxy scenario before merging. ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - Live provider end-to-end verification requires a configured proxy and provider credentials. ## Final Attestation - [ ] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signal.title: perf(reset_budget_job): elect one sweeper per tick and bound the window scan
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Every pod runs the budget reset job, so a fleet multiplies one sweep - Daily budgets all come due at once, so the sweep lands on every pod together - Postgres, auth latency and in-flight requests spike at the reset boundary - The per-window scan reads every row carrying budget limits, unbounded - Found and updated rows are serialized on the event loop for nobody How it solves it: - One pod takes a Redis lease per tick, the rest skip - No Redis, or unreachable Redis, keeps sweeping rather than stranding budgets - The window scan is keyset-paginated, so memory no longer tracks key count - Service hooks carry counts, and debug payloads serialize only when logged ## User Flow Before: a developer whose classification service calls the proxy sees requests stall past their deadline every day just after the daily budget boundary 1. Their service sends POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions on a key belonging to a team with a 24h budget 2. Through the day the call returns 200 in tens of milliseconds 3. At the budget boundary every replica starts the same reset sweep against the same database 4. The same POST now takes tens of seconds, past the 15s deadline the caller allows, and the caller records a timeout 5. Their load balancer returns 503 while replicas are unavailable, and the retries that follow extend the window After: the same request keeps returning in tens of milliseconds across the boundary, because one replica does the reset and the others carry on serving 1. The proxy admin runs the fleet with Redis configured, as before, and changes no settings 2. Their service sends the same POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions on the same key 3. At the budget boundary one replica takes the reset and the rest skip it 4. The same POST returns 200 in tens of milliseconds, and the caller records no timeout 5. Budgets are reset exactly as before, so a key over its cap is still refused and a key under it still serves ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-4793 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [ ] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Four proxy processes sharing one Postgres and one Redis, mirroring a fleet pointed at a single database. Flipping `budget_reset_at` into the past is exactly what the daily boundary does to a 24h budget, so the run below makes 40,000 keys come due at one instant and counts the reset writes the fleet actually issues. The minimum possible is one write per due key; anything above that is a second pod redoing work the first already did. Before captured at `05943b47a3`, the base commit, and after at `eecee2073f`. Round two then removed the per-run cap from the windowed scan, so the after leg was re-run on `e90f3f95b2`, and that run, reported at the end of this section, is where the AFTER v2 numbers come from. Head is now `661d853da5`, which is `f3115e2f51` merged with staging. Nothing in this section has been re-measured since `e90f3f95b2`, which was still the capped, cursor-carrying build of the windowed scan. That change does not reach these counters. Keys still due and total spend read `budget_reset_at` and `spend`, and the windowed scan writes neither: it rewrites only the `budget_limits` JSON. The write count is the one it could touch, since a window write lands on the same table the count greps, but the cap it lost reached `RESET_BUDGET_JOB_BATCH_SIZE * RESET_BUDGET_JOB_MAX_CHUNKS_PER_RUN`, 50,000 rows at the defaults this rig ran, against the 40,000 seeded here, so it never bit and the capped and uncapped walks issue the same writes. `budget_limits` is nullable with no default besides, so rows the seed leaves it unset on never enter that scan Rig: ```bash docker run -d --name litfix-4793-pg -p 6226:5432 \ -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=litellm -e POSTGRES_USER=litellm -e POSTGRES_DB=litellm \ postgres:16 -c log_statement=all docker run -d --name litfix-4793-redis -p 7172:6379 redis:7 # four pods against the same DB and Redis, ports 4793-4796 for p in 4793 4794 4795 4796; do DATABASE_URL="postgresql://litellm:litellm@127.0.0.1:6226/litellm" \ PYTHONPATH="$PWD" python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config config.yaml --port $p & done ``` `config.yaml` carries `store_model_in_db: true`, a Redis cache block, and `proxy_budget_rescheduler_min_time: 15` to compress the ten-minute production cycle. Make 40,000 keys due at once, then count reset writes over the next 150s: ```bash psql -c "INSERT INTO \"LiteLLM_VerificationToken\" (token, key_name, spend, max_budget, budget_duration, budget_reset_at, ...) SELECT 'midnight-' || g, 'sk-' || g, 9.99, 100, '24h', NOW() - INTERVAL '1 minute', ... FROM generate_series(1, 40000) AS g;" docker logs --since 150s litfix-4793-pg | grep -c 'UPDATE \"public\".\"LiteLLM_VerificationToken\"' ``` Before, at `05943b47a3`: ``` === BEFORE (no leader election, 4 pods, 40000 keys due at once) === pod :4793 health=200 pod :4794 health=200 pod :4795 health=200 pod :4796 health=200 keys made due at once : 40000 reset UPDATE statements : 102500 keys still due after : 0 (0 means the reset completed) total spend after reset : 0 (0 means every key was zeroed) redundant writes : 62500 (2.56x the minimum of 40000) redis lock key : (nil) ``` After, at `eecee2073f`: ``` === AFTER (leader election, 4 pods, 40000 keys due at once) === pod :4793 health=200 pod :4794 health=200 pod :4795 health=200 pod :4796 health=200 keys made due at once : 40000 reset UPDATE statements : 40000 keys still due after : 0 (0 means the reset completed) total spend after reset : 0 (0 means every key was zeroed) redundant writes : 0 (1.00x the minimum of 40000) redis lock key : (nil) ``` Both runs finish the reset: no key is left due and every key is zeroed, so the fix removes duplicate work without dropping any. The 2.56x figure is what four pods produce; it grows with replica count and with how long a sweep takes, which is why a 40-pod fleet on a large due population melts rather than merely spiking. The pods that skipped a tick say so, and the lease is handed back after each sweep rather than held for its TTL: ``` Pod 4c68ac20-2d59-433e-b3cc-0066a4c48f2c successfully acquired Redis lock for cronjob_id=reset_budget_job Pod 4c68ac20-2d59-433e-b3cc-0066a4c48f2c successfully released Redis lock for cronjob_id=reset_budget_job ... pod 9a1f could not acquire lock for cronjob_id=reset_budget_job, held by pod 4c68ac20 ``` Counted across the burst, the three non-leader pods yielded 4 times between them, which is the contention the lease converts into a skip instead of a duplicate sweep. The event-loop cost the hooks used to pay, measured on the same 500-row chunk the job reads: ``` batch size : 500 one json.dumps : 4.0 ms, 530 KiB calls per key chunk : 5 blocking per chunk : 20 ms ``` Re-run of the after leg on `e90f3f95b2`. This one counts row updates from `pg_stat_user_tables` rather than the statement log, because the log had grown large enough across runs that reading it returned an empty window; the previous script refused to compare that run rather than reporting a zero: ``` === AFTER v2 (leader election + resumable scan, 4 pods, 40000 keys) === keys seeded due at once : 40000 row updates on the table : 39000 redundant writes : -1000 (0.97x the minimum of 40000) keys still due after : 0 (0 means the reset completed) total spend after reset : 0 (0 means every key was zeroed) ``` `pg_stat` counters are sampled rather than exact, which is why this reads slightly under one write per key; the statement-log count above is the precise one. What matters is that it is nowhere near the 2.56x the unfixed build produces, and the reset still completes. ## Review notes Three review rounds, and the last two each shrank the diff. Round one: capping the window scan without remembering where it stopped meant every tick restarted at the first row, so a deployment with more windowed rows than one run's cap would never reach the rest, leaving them pinned at their cap indefinitely. The unbounded original could not starve, so the cap created that. First fix carried the position across ticks in the job instance. Round two: that was still wrong, because the lease is released after every sweep, so consecutive ticks routinely run on different pods and a fresh pod's position is unset. It would restart at the first row and the tail would starve anyway. Rather than move the position into Redis, the per-run cap is gone: paging is what bounds the memory, and the cursor strictly advances so the walk terminates without a bound. That removes the cursor state, the resume logic, the wrap logic and the truncation warning, and with them the whole starvation question. Against the previous unbounded single-statement read this is strictly better on memory and identical on coverage. Coverage for it: one test walks a table needing far more pages than a per-run cap would allow and asserts the last row is reached, and one runs two independent job instances, standing in for two pods, and requires each to cover the table end to end. Both were mutation-checked against reintroducing the cap, and both initially SURVIVED that mutant because the fixture tables were smaller than the default cap, so the tests now force the cap low to make it bite. Round three: rebased onto current staging after the PR went conflicting, and deleted the review comments rather than defending them. Staging had independently added the same `db_spend_update_writer` mock line to `tests/test_litellm/proxy/test_proxy_server.py`, so that file drops out of the diff entirely, and the only comment left to remove was the one on the lock wiring in `proxy_server.py`. `_acquire_lease` already carries that rationale in its docstring, so the comment was restating it in a second place The pod-local cursor finding is already resolved at this head, and was resolved before it was filed: it is anchored to `e90f3f95b2`, the commit round two replaced. `_reset_windows_for` starts every walk at an empty cursor and loops until a page comes back short, with no per-run cap and no position on the instance, so which pod won the lease cannot change what gets swept. `test_every_tick_sweeps_the_whole_window_table_whichever_pod_won` runs two separate job objects over one table and requires each to reach the last row, and reintroducing the cap fails it along with `test_reset_budget_windows_pages_to_the_end_of_a_large_table` ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - Redis absent or unreachable sweeps unguarded, matching sibling jobs - A sweep outliving its 900s lease can overlap one other pod - Duplicate sweeps were already harmless, so this removes cost only - Service hooks no longer carry full row payloads, only counts - The window scan walks the whole table each sweep, on the leader only ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/4f559acee90644a1bca9ad024785fb53 Requested by: @yassin-berriai

signal.title: fix(db): apply the configured connection params to the read replica URL
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Read replica ignored the configured DB pool cap - Reader pool fell back to Prisma's CPU-based default - Only writer and direct URLs got connection params How it solves it: - Reader URL now inherits the writer's pool params - One allowlist keeps schema-affecting params on the writer - Params pinned on the replica URL still win ## User Flow Before: an operator caps DB connections to protect their database, but the read replica opens as many connections as it likes 1. They set `general_settings.database_connection_pool_limit: 3` and `database_connection_pool_timeout: 20`, point `DATABASE_URL_READ_REPLICA` at their reader, and start the proxy 2. They send a few hundred concurrent `GET http://localhost:4592/key/list` with the master key, all returning 200 3. They count live connections on the database and see the reader holding 11 of them, Prisma's `num_physical_cpus * 2 + 1` default, far more than the 3 they configured 4. The database hits its own connection ceiling under load even though the cap they configured says it should not After: the same cap applies to the reader, so the total stays where the operator put it 1. They set the same two settings, point `DATABASE_URL_READ_REPLICA` at their reader, and start the proxy 2. They send the same concurrent `GET http://localhost:4592/key/list`, all returning 200 3. They count live connections and see the reader holding exactly 3, matching the configured cap 4. If they had pinned `?connection_limit=50` on the replica URL themselves, that value is still what gets used 5. A `search_path` they set on the writer, whether on `DATABASE_URL` or through `database_extra_connection_params`, still does not reach the reader, so replica queries keep resolving against the reader's own schema ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5692 ## Review notes Inheritance is an allowlist of pool and timeout params (`connection_limit`, `pool_timeout`, `connect_timeout`, `socket_timeout`, `pgbouncer`), deliberately not a denylist. A denylist over Postgres' open-ended parameter space cannot be completed, and the one you forget is the one that hurts: `options` carries `search_path`, so copying it wholesale would silently repoint every replica query at the writer's schema. An allowlist fails closed, and a parameter nobody has vetted for the reader stays on the writer by default. There is a test pinning exactly that, so flipping this back to a denylist breaks the build rather than quietly widening what the reader inherits. Both startup paths share the one allowlist. That matters for the CLI in particular, because `database_extra_connection_params` is an untyped passthrough whose keys override everything else, so without the filter an operator could route a writer `search_path` to the reader through config rather than through the URL. The CLI does still set `options` on the reader, but it builds that value from the reader's own `options` plus the configured statement and lock timeouts, never from the writer's. History note: this branch carries a staging merge, `0bf8fe09ba`, that was authored by someone other than the PR author, resolving conflicts against the Azure Entra ID token-auth work. The resolution was reviewed independently before being adopted: the `db_url_settings.py` import block is the union of both sides rather than a pick, which matters because taking either side alone yields a module that imports cleanly and fails at runtime, and the reader-parameter allowlist, its two helpers, the CLI call site, and all four regression tests are present and unchanged. ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Start the proxy with the Case 3 config, confirm liveliness returns 200 2. Run `count_conns` 3. The writer picks up the marker, the reader stays `(unset)`, and the reader holds 13 connections rather than the configured 3 ```text litellm_writer | 1 psql | 1 (unset) | 13 litellm_writer | 1 psql | 1 (unset) | 13 litellm_writer | 1 psql | 1 (unset) | 13 litellm_writer | 1 psql | 1 (unset) | 13 litellm_writer | 1 psql | 1 (unset) | 13 litellm_writer | 1 psql | 1 (unset) | 13 ``` ### After (0bf8fe09ba) #### Case 1: reader pool size against a configured cap of 3 1. Start the proxy with the Case 2 URLs, confirm liveliness returns 200 2. Run `count_conns` 3. signal.title: fix(model-costs): correct gpt-5.6 max input tokens to 922k
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - gpt-5.6 registry entries reported the context window as the input cap - We advertised 1,050,000 max input tokens instead of 922,000 How it solves it: - Set `max_input_tokens` to 922000 for all gpt-5.6 entries - Covers openai plus azure global, us, eu variants - Pins the corrected value in the existing cost-map tests ## User Flow Before: a developer sizing prompts from the gateway's model metadata trusts a cap that OpenAI and Azure will reject 1. They send GET https://litellm-domain/public/litellm_model_cost_map 2. `gpt-5.6-sol` comes back with `"max_input_tokens": 1050000`, matching the 1,050,000 context window rather than the published 922,000 input cap 3. They build a 1,000,000 token prompt against that number and the upstream provider rejects the request After: the same lookup reports the cap the provider actually enforces 1. They send GET https://litellm-domain/public/litellm_model_cost_map 2. `gpt-5.6-sol` comes back with `"max_input_tokens": 922000`, matching what OpenAI and Azure publish 3. They size prompts to 922,000 tokens and the request goes through ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more - [x] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Shared setup, proxy serving the registry from the working tree: ```bash sudo service postgresql start LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True uv run --no-sync litellm --config litellm/proxy/dev_config.yaml --port 4000 ``` ### Before (996693f1eb) 1. Query the registry the gateway serves ```bash curl -sS "http://localhost:4000/public/litellm_model_cost_map" | jq '{sol: .["gpt-5.6-sol"].max_input_tokens, azure_luna: .["azure/gpt-5.6-luna"].max_input_tokens, gpt55: .["gpt-5.5"].max_input_tokens, bedrock_mantle_sol: .["bedrock_mantle/openai.gpt-5.6-sol"].max_input_tokens}' ``` ```json { "sol": 1050000, "azure_luna": 1050000, "gpt55": 1050000, "bedrock_mantle_sol": 1000000 } ``` 2. Compare against what the providers publish: OpenAI's [gpt-5.6-sol page](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-5.6-sol.md) lists a 1,050,000 context window with "Maximum input tokens: 922,000", and Microsoft's [Azure model table](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/ai-foundry/openai/concepts/models) lists the same 1,050,000 / Input: 922,000 / Output: 128,000 for gpt-5.6-sol, -terra and -luna, so the 1,050,000 we served was the context window ### After (6bb677d30f) 1. Query the registry the gateway serves ```bash curl -sS "http://localhost:4000/public/litellm_model_cost_map" | jq '{sol: .["gpt-5.6-sol"].max_input_tokens, azure_luna: .["azure/gpt-5.6-luna"].max_input_tokens, gpt55: .["gpt-5.5"].max_input_tokens, bedrock_mantle_sol: .["bedrock_mantle/openai.gpt-5.6-sol"].max_input_tokens}' ``` ```json { "sol": 922000, "azure_luna": 922000, "gpt55": 1050000, "bedrock_mantle_sol": 1000000 } ``` 2. gpt-5.6 now matches the published 922,000 input cap, and the deliberately untouched entries (gpt-5.5 and the Bedrock Mantle ones) are unchanged ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - gpt-5.5 untouched: OpenAI publishes no separate input cap - Bedrock Mantle gpt-5.6 left at 1,000,000, AWS-specific and unverified Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/c63cc0412baf427d829e85bb79a7426f Requested by: @mateo-berri <!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY --> --- > [!NOTE] > **Low Risk** > Pricing JSON metadata only; no runtime logic, auth, or billing formula changes. signal.title: [Feature]: Pass immutable safety identifiers (user_ids) by default
signal.text: ### The Feature Problem: • Teams can override or omit user_id fields in API calls. • This creates gaps in safety tracking and attribution. • Security/compliance frameworks often require immutable attribution of requests. Proposed Solution: • LITELLM_ENFORCE_SAFETY_IDENTIFIER = TRUE should automatically attach a safety_identifier (user_id) to every request. • This value should be sourced from a trusted context (e.g., LiteLLM’s internal auth/session/user object). • Teams/users should not be able to override or modify this value in their request payloads. • Identifier should be passed downstream to providers in the most appropriate param (e.g., safety_identifier, user_id, metadata, or x-litellm-user-id header). ### Motivation, pitch Description: Currently, LiteLLM allows teams/users to configure and send request parameters, including a safety_identifier to some providers, but there’s no mechanism to guarantee that a safety identifier (e.g., user_id) is always attached to requests and cannot be altered by teams or end-users. This is important for auditing, abuse detection, and regulatory compliance. ### LiteLLM is hiring a founding backend engineer, are you interested in joining us and shipping to all our users? signal.title: fix(ollama): track tool_calls state across streaming chunks for correct finish_reason
signal.text: ## Summary Fixes the streaming case for Ollama tool calling that was missed in #18924. ### The Problem Ollama sends `tool_calls` in one chunk and `done: true` in a **separate** chunk. The existing fix from #18924 only checked for `tool_calls` in the current chunk when setting `finish_reason`, causing streaming to incorrectly return `finish_reason: "stop"` instead of `finish_reason: "tool_calls"`. This breaks agentic workflows (like Claude Code, OpenCode, etc.) where clients use `finish_reason` to determine whether to process tool calls and continue the agent loop. ### The Fix Add a `seen_tool_calls` state variable to `OllamaChatCompletionResponseIterator` that tracks whether tool_calls were seen in **any** chunk during streaming: \`\`\`python class OllamaChatCompletionResponseIterator(BaseModelResponseIterator): started_reasoning_content: bool = False finished_reasoning_content: bool = False seen_tool_calls: bool = False # NEW: Track if tool_calls were seen in any chunk \`\`\` When processing chunks: - Set `seen_tool_calls = True` when tool_calls are found in any chunk - When `done: true` arrives, check both current chunk AND historical state ### Tests Added Added 2 new tests in `tests/test_litellm/llms/ollama/test_ollama_chat_transformation.py`: - `test_streaming_finish_reason_tool_calls_across_chunks` - verifies the fix - `test_streaming_finish_reason_stop_when_no_tool_calls` - verifies no regression All existing Ollama tests continue to pass. ### Related - Original issue: #18922 - Previous fix (non-streaming): #18924 Fixes: #18922 (streaming case)

signal.title: fix(caching): sort embedding results by index to prevent cache misalignment
signal.text: ## Summary Fixes #20456 When providers like vLLM return embedding results out of order (i.e. `result.data[0].index != 0`), the async batch embedding + Redis cache flow produces index misalignment, duplication, and missing entries in the final response. This is a regression of the same class of bug fixed in #2990. ### Root Cause (3 interrelated bugs) 1. **Cache store bug** (`caching.py`): `async_add_cache_pipeline` uses positional access (`result.data[idx]`) to match input items with embeddings when storing to cache. If the provider returns results out of order, the wrong embedding gets stored under the wrong cache key. 2. **Combine bug** (`caching_handler.py`): `_combine_cached_embedding_response_with_api_result` fills `None` (uncached) slots using a sequential counter into the unsorted API response. If the API response items are not sorted by `index`, wrong embeddings land at wrong positions. 3. **Index field bug** (`caching_handler.py`): After combining cached and API results, the `index` field on API result items retains the provider-relative value (0, 1, 2, ...) instead of the correct final merged position. This causes `[data.index for data in result.data]` to show duplicates/gaps instead of `[0, 1, 2, ..., N-1]`. ### Fixes - **`litellm/caching/caching.py`**: Sort `result.data` by the `index` field in `async_add_cache_pipeline` before storing, so positional access correctly maps `input[i]` to the embedding for `input[i]` - **`litellm/caching/caching_handler.py`**: Sort `embedding_response.data` by `index` before the sequential fill loop; after merging, correct the `index` field on every item to match its final position - **`litellm/proxy/policy_engine/policy_resolve_endpoints.py`**: Fix pre-existing unused import lint error (F401) - **`tests/`**: 9 new regression tests covering out-of-order API responses, index correction after merging, large batches with scattered cache hits, and the sorting logic ### Before / After ```python # Before (with cache hits at positions 0, 3 and vLLM returning shuffled): [data.index for data in result.data] # [0, 2, 0, 3, 1] — WRONG # After: [data.index for data in result.data] # [0, 1, 2, 3, 4] — CORRECT ``` ### Test plan - [x] `pytest tests/test_litellm/test_embedding_cache_index_alignment.py` — 5/5 pass - [x] `pytest tests/local_testing/test_caching_handler.py` (4 embedding combine tests) — all pass - [x] `ruff check` passes on all modified files - [x] Existing combine tests still pass (backward compatible)

signal.title: fix(guardrails): skip INPUT validation when no user messages with experimental_use_latest_role_message_only
signal.text: Fixes #23476 ## Relevant issues Fixes #23476 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have Added testing in the [`tests/test_litellm/`](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/tree/main/tests/test_litellm) directory, **Adding at least 1 test is a hard requirement** - [see details](https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/extras/contributing_code) - [x] My PR passes all unit tests on [`make test-unit`](https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/extras/contributing_code) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible, it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have requested a Greptile review by commenting `@greptileai` and received a **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## CI (LiteLLM team) > **CI status guideline:** > > - 50-55 passing tests: main is stable with minor issues. > - 45-49 passing tests: acceptable but needs attention > - <= 40 passing tests: unstable; be careful with your merges and assess the risk. - [ ] **Branch creation CI run** Link: - [ ] **CI run for the last commit** Link: - [ ] **Merge / cherry-pick CI run** Links: ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Changes When `experimental_use_latest_role_message_only` is enabled and no user-role messages exist in the conversation, the post-call hooks (`async_post_call_success_hook`, `async_post_call_streaming_iterator_hook`) and `apply_guardrail` fall back to sending ALL messages — including `tool` and `assistant` role content — to the Bedrock guardrail API. This happens because `_prepare_guardrail_messages_for_role` returns `None` for `payload_messages`, and the `or` fallback (`payload_messages or all_messages`) evaluates to the full unfiltered list. **Fix**: Replace the `or` fallback in 3 locations with explicit logic that skips INPUT validation entirely when no user messages are found (runs OUTPUT validation only). Added a defense-in-depth role guard in `_create_bedrock_input_content_request` that filters out non-user messages when the flag is enabled. **Tests**: 4 new unit tests in `tests/test_litellm/proxy/guardrails/guardrail_hooks/test_bedrock_guardrails.py`: - Role guard filters non-user messages when flag enabled - Role guard includes all messages when flag disabled - `_prepare_guardrail_messages_for_role` returns None when no user messages - `async_post_call_success_hook` skips INPUT and only runs OUTPUT when no user messages

signal.title: [WIP] test: regression test for completion_tokens_details on Responses API usage (#15377)
signal.text: ## Summary Fixes #15377 Issue #15377 reported that Azure OpenAI Responses API calls produced `Usage` objects with `completion_tokens_details=None` in `async_log_success_event`, even though the raw Azure response includes `output_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens`. The underlying fix (map `output_tokens_details` -> `CompletionTokensDetailsWrapper`) is already present in the shared OpenAI Responses transformation used by Azure (`litellm/responses/utils.py::ResponseAPILoggingUtils._transform_response_api_usage_to_chat_usage`). Since Azure inherits this behaviour, the bug is already resolved on `main`. This PR adds a focused regression test that explicitly locks in the behaviour from issue #15377: - Feeds the transformer a raw Azure Responses API usage dict with `output_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens = 64`. - Asserts the returned `Usage.completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens == 64` (and that `completion_tokens_details` is not `None`). This prevents future regressions that could reintroduce the `completion_tokens_details=None` symptom reporters saw in v1.77.7. ## Changes - `tests/test_litellm/responses/test_responses_utils.py`: add `test_transform_response_api_usage_populates_reasoning_tokens_regression_15377`. ## Notes - No production code changes required — the mapping is already in the shared OpenAI Responses base path (`litellm/responses/utils.py`), which Azure reuses since `AzureOpenAIResponsesAPIConfig` does not override usage transformation. - The existing test file has 3 pre-existing ruff warnings (unused imports) that I intentionally left untouched to keep the diff surgical. ## Test Plan ``` uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/responses/test_responses_utils.py -xvs ``` All 20 tests pass (19 existing + 1 new).

signal.title: [Feature]: Custom Transport support for acompletion calls
signal.text: ### Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. ### The Feature Allow customizing transport layer (HTTP) by passing a custom `httpx` client as a "client" argument. The customization will provide a simplified path to resolve simple tasks as an alternative to a more complex setup of litellm proxy. ### Motivation, pitch Today in order to make many atomic manipulations such as: * Refresh bearer token * Inject an observability or analytic action before and after inference call * Dynamically change headers a developer has to configure and deploy a proxy. While the proxy does this work, it is extra burden which rarely justifies the additional complexity and inherited costs. To be able to do these tasks in-process by implementing a standardized middleware using `httpx` package is a common way to solve these problems. This FR proposes to add it *only* to `acompletion()` calls to narrow the scope of the change. However, if proved useful, it can be extended to other execution paths as well. ### What part of LiteLLM is this about? SDK (litellm Python package) ### LiteLLM is hiring a founding backend engineer, are you interested in joining us and shipping to all our users? signal.title: Responses API streaming bridge: multi-step Anthropic tool calls emit text-delta with unregistered chatcmpl- ID
signal.text: ## Description When using LiteLLM's Responses API (`/v1/responses`) to proxy Anthropic models, multi-step tool call flows produce: ``` text part chatcmpl-<id> not found ``` The AI SDK tracks text parts via `text-start` → `text-delta` → `text-end` by ID. During step 2+ (text after tool use), the `text-delta` event arrives with a `chatcmpl-` response-level ID that was never registered via `text-start`, causing the AI SDK to drop the text. Single-step text-only responses work fine. Only multi-step tool call sequences break. **The Bug** In _transform_chat_completion_chunk_to_response_api_chunk: ``` if self._cached_item_id is None and chunk.id: self._cached_item_id = chunk.id # ← sets cache to "chatcmpl-aaa" on first chunk item_id = self._cached_item_id or chunk.id # ← uses cached value for all events ``` Step 1 (tool call): First chunk arrives, _cached_item_id is None, so it caches chunk.id = "chatcmpl-aaa". The _ensure_output_item_for_chunk method then overwrites it to "msg_{uuid}" for the output item. Text events use "msg_{uuid}" — consistent. ✅ Step 2 (text after tool result): LiteLLM internally makes a new Chat Completion call, which returns chunks with a new chunk.id = "chatcmpl-bbb". But _cached_item_id is already set from step 1 (either "chatcmpl-aaa" or "msg_{uuid}"), so the if self._cached_item_id is None check never fires. The problem is that sent_output_item_added_event and sent_content_part_added_event are not reset between steps. So step 2 skips _ensure_output_item_for_chunk (which would emit a new text-start with OutputItemAddedEvent + ContentPartAddedEvent), and jumps straight to emitting text-delta with the stale item_id. ## Related Issues - #14962 / PR #14965 — Fixed per-chunk ID inconsistency in Chat Completions streaming - #19125 / PR #19390 — Fixed `text-start`/`text-delta` ID mismatch in Responses API streaming (single-step). Added ID caching at stream start. - #26529 — Same symptom on the Chat Completions path (`/v1/chat/completions`), still open This issue covers the **Responses API path** (`/v1/responses`), which was refactored into a shared format mapping in 1.83.14. ## Environment - LiteLLM version: 1.83.14-stable - Model: `claude-haiku-4-5` (Anthropic, via Responses API bridge) - Client: `@ai-sdk/openai` (uses Responses API by default) - AI SDK: 5.x / 6.x ## Steps to Reproduce 1. Point `@ai-sdk/openai` at LiteLLM proxy's `/v1` endpoint 2. Send a prompt to an Anthropic model that triggers tool use followed by a text response (multi-step) 3. Step 1 (tool call) streams correctly 4. Step 2 (text after tool result) emits `text-delta` with `chatcmpl-<id>` that has no matching `text-start` ## Root Cause PR #19390 added ID caching at stream start to ensure consistency within a single step. However, in multi-step tool call flows, each step creates a new internal completion with a new `chatcmpl-` ID. The cache doesn't reset cleanly between steps, so the new `chatcmpl-` ID leaks into `text-delta` events without a corresponding `text-start` registration. ``` Step 1 (tool call): cached ID → text-start(id="0") → text-delta(id="0") ✅ ↓ new internal completion, new chatcmpl-bbb generated Step 2 (text): text-start(id="0") but text-delta(id="chatcmpl-bbb") 💥 ``` ## Evidence from Production Logs ```json {"level":"error","event":"bridge.session_error","error_msg":"\"text part chatcmpl-3b58c921-4f8f-4f85-90c2-e53c9f79750c not found\""} {"level":"info","event":"prompt.run","model":"claude-haiku-4-5","reasoning_effort":"max","outcome":"error","duration_ms":21914} ``` Same session, later prompt (text-only, no tool calls): ```json {"level":"info","event":"prompt.run","model":"claude-haiku-4-5","reasoning_effort":"max","outcome":"success","duration_ms":8176} ``` ## Expected Behavior All `text-start`, `text-delta`, and `text-end` events within a step should share the same part ID, including across step boundaries in multi-step tool call flows.
