signal.title: fix(logging): bound the shared logging executor backlog
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Proxy memory on ECS climbs for days until the task restarts - Sync logging callbacks queue on an unbounded shared executor - Each queued task pins its request/response payload in memory How it solves it: - Caps the shared logging executor at 10,000 queued-plus-running tasks - Past the cap, new logging tasks are dropped with a rate-limited warning - Cap is tunable via `LOGGING_EXECUTOR_MAX_PENDING_TASKS` ## User Flow Before: an operator running the proxy on ECS watches per-task memory climb until the task restarts 1. They deploy the proxy with logging callbacks enabled and see task memory start at 30-40% 2. Under steady traffic, CloudWatch memory utilization climbs over days to 55-60% and never plateaus 3. At about 60% the task restarts on its own, memory drops back to baseline, and the sawtooth repeats After: the same deployment levels off instead of climbing without bound 1. They deploy the proxy with logging callbacks enabled and see task memory start at 30-40% 2. Under steady traffic, memory utilization levels off at a stable ceiling 3. If log delivery ever falls so far behind that entries must be skipped, the task log shows a warning naming `LOGGING_EXECUTOR_MAX_PENDING_TASKS` so they can raise the cap ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5386 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more - [x] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Shared setup: `flood.py` floods the shared logging executor the same way request logging does, with one slow sync callback and 200k submissions, then prints the backlog size and peak RSS ```python import resource import sys import time from litellm.litellm_core_utils.thread_pool_executor import executor def slow_callback(payload: str) -> None: time.sleep(120) for _ in range(200_000): executor.submit(slow_callback, "x" * 10_000) peak_rss_mb = resource.getrusage(resource.RUSAGE_SELF).ru_maxrss / (1024 * 1024 if sys.platform == "darwin" else 1024) print("queued tasks:", executor._work_queue.qsize()) print("peak rss mb:", round(peak_rss_mb)) ``` ### Before (cde134488c) 1. `LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True python flood.py` 2. Observed output: the backlog holds every submission and memory grows with it ``` queued tasks: 199900 peak rss mb: 2720 ``` ### After (29c77e81f8) 1. `LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True python flood.py` 2. Observed output: the backlog stops at the cap, memory stays flat, and a warning names the knob ``` 15:01:37 - LiteLLM:WARNING: thread_pool_executor.py:71 - litellm logging executor backlog is full (max_pending_tasks=10000); dropped 1 logging task(s) since the last warning. Set LOGGING_EXECUTOR_MAX_PENDING_TASKS to raise the cap. queued tasks: 9900 peak rss mb: 329 ``` ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - Past the cap, sync logging callbacks are shed, not backpressured - Proxy spend tracking is async and never rides this executor - The sync SDK passthrough flush shares the same cap - A shed submission logs a count, not a per-call-site failure line - Async callbacks already have their own bounded queue and are unaffected ## Review notes Shedding is only safe if nothing waits on what the executor hands back, so every caller of the shared executor was audited: `litellm/utils.py`, `litellm/litellm_core_utils/litellm_logging.py` (both dispatch paths and the async success hook), `litellm/litellm_core_utils/streaming_handler.py`, `litellm/interactions/streaming_iterator.py`, `litellm/responses/streaming_iterator.py`, `litellm/passthrough/main.py`, `litellm/proxy/guardrails/guardrail_endpoints.py`, and the AssemblyAI passthrough handler. All of them submit and move on. The call sites that do read a future (`batch_completion`, `asyncify`, `dual_cache`, presidio, the batches handlers, and the guardrail test-run endpoint) each build their own private `ThreadPoolExecutor` and never touch this one, so the cap cannot strand a caller The drop warning is emitted through a logger injected into the executor rather than an in-function import of `verbose_logger`, which also lets the rate-limiting test capture real log records instead of patching the module What rides this executor is worth being precise about, since shedding cost data would be a very different tradeoff from shedding log lines. On the proxy, passthrough streaming always takes the async route (`common_request_processing.py` passes `route_type="allm_passthrough_route"`, and `passthrough/main.py:191` gates on that flag), so its spend flush goes through `asyncio.create_task` at `passthrough/main.py:454` and never touches this executor. Spend rows reach the database through `_ProxyDBLogger`, which implements `async_log_success_event` and no sync counterpart, so the shed path cannot drop a billing record. The one spend-adjacent submission that does ride it is `passthrough/main.py:405`, reachable only from the sync SDK, and even there `success_handler` already skips `CustomLogger` callbacks when the call type is pass-through and defers them to the async handler The pre-fix behavior was not "this work always ran" either. An unbounded queue only runs its backlog if the process lives long enough, and the repro above shows 199,900 tasks pinning 2.7 GB right before the ECS task hits its memory limit and restarts, discarding all of them. Shedding a bounded few is strictly less loss than losing the whole backlog to a restart Every test here was mutation checked. Removing admission control, dropping the slot release, disabling the interval check, forgetting to reset the drop counter, returning an uncancelled future, and defaulting to the wrong logger each turn at least one test red ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/5e39dc1f0a084d5ead9ef6fe376e843b Requested by: @yassin-berriai

signal.title: fix(router): isolate deployment model info from cached backend metadata
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Deployment lookups mutated litellm's cached backend model info - Nested metadata leaked from one deployment to its siblings - A `base_model` deployment overwrote that base model's cached info How it solves it: - Deployment lookups now merge into deep copies of cached info - Nothing returned shares objects with `model_cost` or the lookup cache ## User Flow Before: an admin runs two deployments of the same backend model, one with its own metadata, and the other one silently starts reporting the first one's values 1. They configure `claude-a` with `search_context_cost_per_query: {search_context_size_low: 0.999}` and `claude-b` with no custom metadata, both on `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929` 2. They GET https://litellm-domain/model_group/info and both deployments read as configured, `claude-b` at the built-in `0.01` 3. Traffic flows, or they read the metadata again 4. `claude-b` now reports `0.999`, the value only `claude-a` was ever configured with, and so does anything else on that backend model After: the same setup keeps each deployment's metadata to itself 1. They configure the same two deployments 2. They GET https://litellm-domain/model_group/info and both read as configured 3. Traffic flows, or they read the metadata again 4. `claude-a` still reports `0.999` and `claude-b` still reports the built-in `0.01` ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5471 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/<your_test_file>.py -v`. signal.title: fix(datadog): normalize alias-derived tag values so metrics match what was sent
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Team and key aliases look wrong in Datadog metrics - `P&T` loses everything after the `&` - Aliases show up lowercased, unlike in logs How it solves it: - Normalize alias-derived tag values before sending them - Datadog does the same transform, so nothing is silently dropped ## User Flow Before: an admin who names a team `P&T CTO-B2B` cannot line up their Datadog metrics with the same requests in Datadog logs 1. They create the team at POST https://litellm-domain/team/new with `{"team_alias": "P&T CTO-B2B"}`, mint a key for it, and send traffic to https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions 2. In Datadog Logs the request shows `@metadata.user_api_key_team_alias:P&T CTO-B2B`, exactly the alias they typed 3. In Datadog Metrics the same traffic is tagged `team:p`, with everything from the `&` onward gone, so filtering by the alias they know returns nothing 4. They cannot tell whether the gateway sent the wrong value or the metric backend changed it After: the same traffic carries a metric tag the admin can predict and filter on 1. They create the same team, mint a key, and send the same request 2. Datadog Logs still shows the raw alias `P&T CTO-B2B` 3. Datadog Metrics now shows `team:p_t_cto-b2b`, keeping the whole alias with the disallowed characters folded into underscores 4. Filtering metrics on `team:p_t_cto-b2b` returns the team's traffic, and the value matches character for character what the gateway sent ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-3706 ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more - [x] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Root cause The gateway was never mangling anything. `_sanitize_prometheus_label_value` keeps `&` and case intact, and the log payload carries the alias verbatim, which is why the log side always looked right. Datadog normalizes metric and span *tags* on ingest (lowercase, anything outside Unicode letters, digits, `_`, `-`, `:`, `.`, `/` becomes `_`, runs of `_` collapse, leading and trailing `_` are stripped) while log *attributes* stay raw and case sensitive, so an alias with `&` or uppercase reads differently depending on which of the two you are looking at, and the transform happens invisibly server side after we hand over the raw string The gateway cannot make a Datadog tag case sensitive, so this normalizes the alias-derived values itself: what we send is now exactly what Datadog stores, which is stable, greppable, and never drops characters ``` normalize_datadog_tag_value("P&T CTO-B2B") -> "p_t_cto-b2b" normalize_datadog_tag_value("regression-team") -> "regression-team" # unchanged normalize_datadog_tag_value(12345) -> "12345" ``` Applied to the values users name themselves: the `team:` tag and each `request_tag:` value in `get_datadog_tags`, the `team:` tag in the Datadog metrics logger, and `user` / `team` / allowlisted custom tag values in the Datadog cost management logger. Infra tags (`env`, `service`, `version`, `HOSTNAME`, `POD_NAME`) and core payload fields (`provider`, `model`, `model_group`, `status_code`) are left alone. Since Datadog applies the identical transform on ingest, stored tag values and existing dashboards do not change ## Review notes Request tags and team ids are not guaranteed to be strings at runtime: `metadata.tags` is caller-supplied JSON, so a client can send `"tags": [12345]`. The helper takes `object` and coerces with `str()` rather than skipping non-string elements, which keeps the previous f-string behaviour intact for those values and keeps the tag visible. Skipping was the alternative, but the Datadog callbacks swallow their own exceptions, so anything that raises inside tag construction silently drops the whole event for that request rather than surfacing an error, and quietly losing telemetry is the worse failure here Swept the rest of the Datadog package for the same shape of unguarded string call before calling this done: `rt.partition(":")` in the cost management logger is already behind an `isinstance(rt, str)` check, `str(_code).strip()` in the logs handler coerces first, and the `.replace("Z", "+00:00")` in the LLM Observability logger sits inside an `isinstance(..., str)` branch. The helper is the single normalization point, so coercing there covers every call site at once ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Shared setup for both sides: a live proxy on localhost:4682 with `datadog` and `datadog_metrics` as callbacks, `DD_SITE` and `DD_BASE_URL` pointed at a local HTTPS listener that records the raw `/api/v2/logs` and `/api/v2/series` batches Datadog would have received, a team created with `team_alias` `P&T CTO-B2B`, and real Anthropic traffic through `claude-opus-5` costing real $$$ Both sides run the same two commands after minting a key on the team: ```bash TEAM_ID=$(curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4682/team/new -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-1234' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"team_alias":"P&T CTO-B2B","models":["claude-opus-5"]}' | jq -r .team_id) KEY=$(curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4682/key/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-1234' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d "{\"team_id\":\"$TEAM_ID\",\"models\":[\"claude-opus-5\"]}" | jq -r .key) ``` ### Before (4af66657f996d91a6467329798d1ea9d70e66a02) #### Team alias with `&` and uppercase, real chat completion 1. Send the request: ```bash curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4682/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"model":"claude-opus-5","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Reply with exactly OK."}],"max_tokens":16,"thinking":{"type":"disabled"}}' ``` The completion comes back with `"content":"OK"` 2. Read what the Datadog intake received. The raw alias goes over the wire, so Datadog is the one that lowercases it and drops everything after the `&`: ``` LOG ddtags=env:qa,service:litellm-e2e,version:qa-run,HOSTNAME:qa-host,POD_NAME:qa-pod,request_tag:User-Agent: curl,request_tag:User-Agent: curl/8.7.1,team:P&T CTO-B2B SERIES {"metric": "litellm.llm_api.request_count", "tags": ["env:qa", "service:litellm-e2e", "version:qa-run", "HOSTNAME:qa-host", "POD_NAME:qa-pod", "provider:anthropic", "model_name:anthropic/claude-opus-5", "model_group:claude-opus-5", "status_code:200", "team:P&T CTO-B2B"]} ``` #### Numeric request tag, real chat completion 1. Send the same request with a non-string tag: ```bash curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4682/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"model":"claude-opus-5","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Reply with exactly OK."}],"max_tokens":16,"thinking":{"type":"disabled"},"metadata":{"tags":[12345]}}' ``` The completion comes back with `"content":"OK"` 2. Read what the Datadog intake received. The numeric tag rides along, and the team tag is still raw: ``` LOG ddtags=env:qa,service:litellm-e2e,version:qa-run,HOSTNAME:qa-host,POD_NAME:qa-pod,request_tag:12345,request_tag:User-Agent: curl,request_tag:User-Agent: curl/8.7.1,team:P&T CTO-B2B SERIES {"metric": "litellm.llm_api.request_count", "tags": ["env:qa", "service:litellm-e2e", "version:qa-run", "HOSTNAME:qa-host", "POD_NAME:qa-pod", "provider:anthropic", "model_name:anthropic/claude-opus-5", "model_group:claude-opus-5", "status_code:200", "team:P&T CTO-B2B"]} ``` ### After (ab788c5e74e9ca4ad25ad2392ccada5cfda68d54) #### Team alias with `&` and uppercase, real chat completion 1. Send the same request: ```bash curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4682/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"model":"claude-opus-5","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Reply with exactly OK."}],"max_tokens":16,"thinking":{"type":"disabled"}}' ``` The completion comes back with `"content":"OK"` again, so the tag values are the only thing that differs 2. Read what the Datadog intake received. The whole alias survives, in exactly the form Datadog stores it, on both the log and the metric: ``` LOG ddtags=env:qa,service:litellm-e2e,version:qa-run,HOSTNAME:qa-host,POD_NAME:qa-pod,request_tag:user-agent:_curl,request_tag:user-agent:_curl/8.7.1,team:p_t_cto-b2b SERIES {"metric": "litellm.llm_api.request_count", "tags": ["env:qa", "service:litellm-e2e", "version:qa-run", "HOSTNAME:qa-host", "POD_NAME:qa-pod", "provider:anthropic", "model_name:anthropic/claude-opus-5", "model_group:claude-opus-5", "status_code:200", "team:p_t_cto-b2b"]} ``` #### Numeric request tag, real chat completion 1. Send the same request with a non-string tag: ```bash curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4682/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"model":"claude-opus-5","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Reply with exactly OK."}],"max_tokens":16,"thinking":{"type":"disabled"},"metadata":{"tags":[12345]}}' ``` The completion comes back with `"content":"OK"` 2. Read what the Datadog intake received. The event still arrives, the numeric tag is still there, and the alias is normalized: ``` LOG ddtags=env:qa,service:litellm-e2e,version:qa-run,HOSTNAME:qa-host,POD_NAME:qa-pod,request_tag:12345,request_tag:user-agent:_curl,request_tag:user-agent:_curl/8.7.1,team:p_t_cto-b2b SERIES {"metric": "litellm.llm_api.request_count", "tags": ["env:qa", "service:litellm-e2e", "version:qa-run", "HOSTNAME:qa-host", "POD_NAME:qa-pod", "provider:anthropic", "model_name:anthropic/claude-opus-5", "model_group:claude-opus-5", "status_code:200", "team:p_t_cto-b2b"]} ``` ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - Datadog tags stay lowercase, that is a backend rule - Prometheus labels unchanged, they already carry raw aliases - Non-string tag values are coerced with `str()`, never dropped - 200 character tag truncation is left to Datadog ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/6bcc9502b2274c15a065b1fb0cc3a227 Requested by: @yassin-berriai

signal.title: feat(helm): compose DATABASE_URL_READ_REPLICA from a reader host secret key
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - No way to compose DATABASE_URL_READ_REPLICA from separate secret keys - envFrom vars don't resolve in $(VAR) env interpolation - Secret stores often hold a bare reader hostname, not a full URL How it solves it: - New db.secret.readReplicaEndpointKey injects DATABASE_READER_HOST into the env array - db.readReplicaUrl can then reference $(DATABASE_READER_HOST), same pattern as the writer URL ## User Flow Before: an operator whose secret store holds the reader hostname as its own secret key cannot enable read-replica routing 1. They store username, password, writer host, and reader host as separate keys in one Kubernetes secret synced from their secret store 2. They set db.readReplicaUrl to `postgresql://$(DATABASE_USERNAME):$(DATABASE_PASSWORD)@$(DATABASE_READER_HOST):5432/$(DATABASE_NAME)?sslmode=require` and mount the secret via environmentSecrets 3. The pod starts with DATABASE_URL_READ_REPLICA containing the literal text `$(DATABASE_READER_HOST)` because Kubernetes only interpolates vars defined in the env array, not envFrom 4. The proxy fails to reach the reader and read-replica routing never activates After: the same operator enables read-replica routing with the same secret layout 1. They store the same keys in the same Kubernetes secret 2. They set db.secret.readReplicaEndpointKey to the reader host key and keep the same db.readReplicaUrl 3. The pod starts with DATABASE_READER_HOST sourced from the secret and placed before DATABASE_URL_READ_REPLICA, so the URL interpolates fully 4. The proxy connects to the reader and routes read-only queries there ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5653 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Shared setup: values file used for both renders ```yaml db: deployStandalone: false useExisting: true database: litellm url: postgresql://$(DATABASE_USERNAME):$(DATABASE_PASSWORD)@$(DATABASE_HOST):5432/$(DATABASE_NAME)?sslmode=require secret: name: pg-creds usernameKey: username passwordKey: password endpointKey: writer-host readReplicaEndpointKey: reader-host readReplicaUrl: postgresql://$(DATABASE_USERNAME):$(DATABASE_PASSWORD)@$(DATABASE_READER_HOST):5432/$(DATABASE_NAME)?sslmode=require ``` ### Before (973329e986) 1. `helm template litellm helm/litellm-helm -f reader-values.yaml -s templates/deployment.yaml` 2. Rendered env has DATABASE_URL_READ_REPLICA referencing `$(DATABASE_READER_HOST)` but no DATABASE_READER_HOST entry anywhere in the env array, so Kubernetes leaves the reference as literal text at runtime ```yaml - name: DATABASE_URL value: "postgresql://$(DATABASE_USERNAME):$(DATABASE_PASSWORD)@$(DATABASE_HOST):5432/$(DATABASE_NAME)?sslmode=require" - name: DATABASE_URL_READ_REPLICA value: "postgresql://$(DATABASE_USERNAME):$(DATABASE_PASSWORD)@$(DATABASE_READER_HOST):5432/$(DATABASE_NAME)?sslmode=require" ``` ### After (0dd9870fe4) 1. Same `helm template` command 2. DATABASE_READER_HOST is now sourced from the secret and rendered immediately before DATABASE_URL_READ_REPLICA, so the $(VAR) reference resolves ```yaml - name: DATABASE_URL value: "postgresql://$(DATABASE_USERNAME):$(DATABASE_PASSWORD)@$(DATABASE_HOST):5432/$(DATABASE_NAME)?sslmode=require" - name: DATABASE_READER_HOST valueFrom: secretKeyRef: name: pg-creds key: reader-host - name: DATABASE_URL_READ_REPLICA value: "postgresql://$(DATABASE_USERNAME):$(DATABASE_PASSWORD)@$(DATABASE_READER_HOST):5432/$(DATABASE_NAME)?sslmode=require" ``` 3. Adding `readReplicaUrlKey: reader-url` to the same values file suppresses the reader-host secret ref entirely and sources DATABASE_URL_READ_REPLICA from that key; likewise no reader-host ref is emitted when readReplicaUrl is unset, so an unused key can't block pod creation 4. `helm unittest -f 'tests/*.yaml' helm/litellm-helm` passes: 14 suites, 97 tests ## Type 🆕 New Feature ## Caveats (if any) - readReplicaUrlKey wins when both keys are set; the reader-host ref is then omitted Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/4977773ef12040748630173bf865083a

signal.title: fix(reset_budget_job): reconnect and retry on transient DB transport errors
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Reset job skipped a whole tick on transient DB errors - Nothing reconnected, so due resets waited 10 minutes - Failures were untagged, so nobody could see which phase died How it solves it: - Reads, writes, raw queries route through the reconnect helper - One reconnect-and-retry per operation, tagged per sub-job - Writes only replay a ConnectError, where the statements provably never landed - Non-transport errors (unique violations, data errors) still surface ## User Flow Before: an admin whose keys carry a monthly budget sees spend stay above the cap for an extra reset cycle whenever the gateway's database transport blips 1. They create a key with a budget window: POST https://litellm-domain/key/generate with `{"max_budget": 10, "budget_duration": "30d"}` 2. Their team burns through the budget, so requests to POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions come back 400 with "Budget has been exceeded" 3. The budget window comes due while the database transport is briefly unreachable 4. GET https://litellm-domain/key/info?key=sk-... still reports the old `spend` and the old reset timestamp, and calls keep getting refused 5. The proxy logs "Failed to reset budget for keys" with a connection error and nothing else, so nothing is retried until the next cycle, up to ten minutes later After: the same blip costs one retry instead of a whole cycle, so the key is spendable again on time 1. They create the same key: POST https://litellm-domain/key/generate with `{"max_budget": 10, "budget_duration": "30d"}` 2. Their team burns through the budget, so requests come back 400 with "Budget has been exceeded" 3. The budget window comes due while the database transport is briefly unreachable 4. The gateway reconnects and repeats that one read or write on the spot 5. GET https://litellm-domain/key/info?key=sk-... reports `spend` back at 0 and a fresh reset timestamp, and POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions succeeds again on the cycle it was due ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5372 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/<your_test_file>.py -v` - [x] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Shared setup, identical for both runs: a proxy on localhost:4000 against a local Postgres, with the reset scheduler pinned to 10s so ticks are observable (`proxy_budget_rescheduler_min_time: 10`, `proxy_budget_rescheduler_max_time: 10`), one real Anthropic deployment (`anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5`), and `PRISMA_HEALTH_WATCHDOG_ENABLED=False` so the only thing that can recover a broken transport is the job itself. ```bash # 3 keys that come due on every tick for i in 1 2 3; do curl -s -X POST http://localhost:4000/key/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"max_budget": 10, "budget_duration": "10s", "models": ["anthropic-haiku-4-5"]}' > /dev/null done # break the database transport for 2 minutes: reject every 8th packet to the query engine PORT=$(ss -tnlp | grep -a query-engine | head -1 | awk '{print $4}' | cut -d: -f2) sudo iptables -I OUTPUT -p tcp -d 127.0.0.1 --dport $PORT \ -m statistic --mode nth --every 8 --packet 0 -j REJECT --reject-with tcp-reset sleep 120 sudo iptables -D OUTPUT -p tcp -d 127.0.0.1 --dport $PORT \ -m statistic --mode nth --every 8 --packet 0 -j REJECT --reject-with tcp-reset ``` ### Before (4af59d7c6e) #### A real chat completion is billed to a budgeted key 1. `curl -s -X POST http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"anthropic-haiku-4-5","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"say hi"}]}'` ``` {"id":"chatcmpl-...","model":"anthropic-haiku-4-5","choices":[{"finish_reason":"stop","index":0,"message":{"content":"Hi! How can I help you today?","role":"assistant"}}],"usage":{"completion_tokens":16,"prompt_tokens":9,"total_tokens":25}} ``` 2. Spend lands on the key, so the reset job has real work to do: `curl -s "http://localhost:4000/key/info?key=$KEY" -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" | python3 -c "import sys,json;print(json.load(sys.stdin)['info']['spend'])"` ``` 8.900000000000001e-05 ``` #### The transport is flaky for 2 minutes 1. Counted from the proxy log over the 120s window: ``` reset job ticks: 12 reconnect-and-retry tagged reset_budget: 0 phases that gave up (Failed to reset): 19 ``` 2. Every transport error is a dead end, and the log never names which read or write died: ``` 20:23:02 - LiteLLM Proxy:ERROR: reset_budget_job.py:671 - Failed to reset budget for keys: 20:23:12 - LiteLLM Proxy:ERROR: reset_budget_job.py:671 - Failed to reset budget for keys: 20:23:13 - LiteLLM Proxy:ERROR: reset_budget_job.py:965 - Failed to reset budget windows for keys: 20:23:22 - LiteLLM Proxy:ERROR: reset_budget_job.py:671 - Failed to reset budget for keys: 20:23:23 - LiteLLM Proxy:ERROR: reset_budget_job.py:965 - Failed to reset budget windows for keys: ... httpcore.ReadError httpx.ReadError ``` ### After (2415792316) #### A real chat completion is billed to a budgeted key 1. `curl -s -X POST http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"anthropic-haiku-4-5","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"say hi"}]}'` ``` {"id":"chatcmpl-...","model":"anthropic-haiku-4-5","choices":[{"finish_reason":"stop","index":0,"message":{"content":"Hi! How's it going?","role":"assistant"}}],"usage":{"completion_tokens":13,"prompt_tokens":9,"total_tokens":22}} ``` 2. With every 12th packet to the query engine rejected, the key's spend is still zeroed 5s into the flaky window, on the tick it was due ``` 22:14:01 key spend recorded in db: 7.900000000000001e-05 22:14:01 dropping every 12th packet to the db transport (engine port 48449) 22:14:02 (+1s) key spend in db: 7.900000000000001e-05 22:14:05 (+4s) key spend in db: 7.900000000000001e-05 22:14:06 (+5s) key spend in db: 0 RESULT: spend reset 5s into the flaky transport window ``` #### The transport is flaky for 2 minutes 1. Same command, same window length, same 12 ticks: ``` reset job ticks: 12 reconnect-and-retry tagged reset_budget: 3 phases that gave up (Failed to reset): 4 key batches actually written: 12 ``` 2. Each failure now names its sub-job and gets a reconnect, and the retry finishes the work on the tick it was due: ``` 22:11:36 - LiteLLM Proxy:WARNING: exception_handler.py:423 - DB transport error on read; attempting reconnect-and-retry. reason=reset_budget_read_key_windows_failure 22:11:36 - LiteLLM Proxy:INFO: utils.py:5243 - Prisma DB reconnect succeeded. reason=reset_budget_read_key_windows_failure 22:11:36 - LiteLLM Proxy:WARNING: exception_handler.py:423 - DB transport error on read; attempting reconnect-and-retry. reason=reset_budget_read_team_windows_failure 22:11:46 - LiteLLM Proxy:WARNING: exception_handler.py:423 - DB transport error on read; attempting reconnect-and-retry. reason=reset_budget_read_key_windows_failure ``` 3. The remaining give-ups are the two safety rails working as intended: a write that failed with `ReadError` after the statements were sent is not replayed, and back-to-back reconnects are throttled by the existing cooldown while 1-in-8 packet loss is held for two minutes. A single blip, which is what the ticket describes, resolves on the first retry ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - Retry is one attempt, throttled by the existing reconnect cooldown - A post-send error on a write is ambiguous, so it is not replayed and that phase still waits for the next tick - A sustained outage still skips the tick, by design - The ticket's watchdog question stays open, nothing here changes it ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/ce60e0aa6d3f44d4b13089aedca19838 Requested by: @yassin-berriai

signal.title: [Feature]: size and quality keyed cost tracking for fal_ai gpt-image-2
signal.text: ### Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. ### The Feature Price fal_ai image generation by the size and quality actually requested instead of one flat `output_cost_per_image`. fal bills `openai/gpt-image-2` per image at rates that vary with both dimensions (pricing table on https://fal.ai/models/openai/gpt-image-2), from roughly $0.04 to $0.36 per image. PR #37729 adds the model with a single flat rate of $0.145 and documents the variance only in `metadata.notes` inside `model_prices_and_context_window.json`, so every non-default request records spend that differs from the fal invoice, silently and in either direction. A quality `hd` 1024x1024 image bills $0.211 on fal but logs $0.145, a 31% under-count that compounds across requests and makes budget and rate limit enforcement drift. The unprefixed alias `fal_ai/gpt-image-2` (accepted since the config auto-prefixes it) has no cost map entry at all and logs $0. Requested: keyed per-image pricing (size x quality) for fal image models, applied from the request parameters at spend-logging time, plus a cost map entry for the unprefixed alias ### User Flow Before this feature (today): a proxy admin routing image generation to fal gets $0.145 logged for every image no matter what size or quality was requested, so LiteLLM budgets stop matching the fal invoice 1. POST http://localhost:4000/v1/images/generations with `{"model": "gpt-image-2-fal", "prompt": "...", "quality": "hd", "size": "1024x1024"}` and a virtual key, response is 200 with a fal.media PNG url 2. Open the Logs page on http://localhost:4000/ui and find the request, the row shows $0.145 spend 3. Compare with the fal dashboard usage page for the same call, fal billed $0.211, and the gap repeats on every non-default request 4. POST the same body with `"model": "gpt-image-2-fal-shortname"` (an alias for `fal_ai/gpt-image-2`), response is 200 with a real image but the Logs row shows $0.00 After this feature (ideal user flow): the same admin sees LiteLLM spend match the fal invoice for every size and quality combination 1. POST http://localhost:4000/v1/images/generations with the same `quality: "hd"`, `size: "1024x1024"` body, response is unchanged 2. The Logs page row for that request shows $0.211 3. The fal dashboard usage page and LiteLLM spend agree within rounding for the whole billing period 4. The unprefixed `fal_ai/gpt-image-2` alias logs the same keyed price instead of $0.00 ### How far you got Config / setup the proxy ran with (env: `FAL_AI_API_KEY` and `DATABASE_URL` set, values redacted): ```yaml model_list: - model_name: gpt-image-2-fal litellm_params: model: fal_ai/openai/gpt-image-2 api_key: os.environ/FAL_AI_API_KEY - model_name: gpt-image-2-fal-shortname litellm_params: model: fal_ai/gpt-image-2 api_key: os.environ/FAL_AI_API_KEY general_settings: master_key: sk-REDACTED ``` Version or commit: PR #37729 head `f3896c0527b62f896f519be72a25f028856a9806` (the model only exists there, current main 500s on it) Commands and their full output, up to the step that dead-ends: ``` $ curl -s http://127.0.0.1:16259/v1/images/generations -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model": "gpt-image-2-fal", "prompt": "a lighthouse at dusk", "quality": "hd", "size": "1024x1024"}' {"created": 1787266032, "data": [{"b64_json": null, "revised_prompt": null, "url": "https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0aa726c0/FETroCyUVg5qIY6tnMDCi_SeslVLNw.png"}], ...} $ psql -c 'SELECT "model", "call_type", "spend", "status" FROM "LiteLLM_SpendLogs" ORDER BY "startTime";' fal_ai/openai/gpt-image-2 | aimage_generation | 0.145 | success <-- the hd 1024x1024 call above fal_ai/gpt-image-2 | aimage_generation | 0 | success <-- the shortname alias call ``` What stopped me there: the request succeeds and returns a real image, but there is no way to make the logged spend follow the requested size and quality. The cost map only holds one scalar `output_cost_per_image` per model, so $0.145 is recorded for a call fal bills at $0.211, and the fal pricing page (https://fal.ai/models/openai/gpt-image-2) shows a different price per size/quality tier. signal.title: fix(auth): cache team member default budget as a typed model (LIT-5311)
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Team member default budget never lands in Redis - Redis write fails on raw datetime columns - Error line repeats in logs, every pod re-queries DB How it solves it: - Cache a validated `LiteLLM_BudgetTable`, not the raw row - Pass `model_type` on both read and write ## User Flow Before: a team admin with Redis-backed auth caching sees a recurring cache error, and every pod keeps hitting the database for the team's per-member budget 1. The admin runs the proxy with `enable_redis_auth_cache: true` and a Redis cache backend 2. They send POST http://localhost:4000/team/new with `"team_member_budget": 25`, which comes back with a team id 3. They mint a key for a member of that team via POST http://localhost:4000/key/generate and send a POST http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions with it 4. The call succeeds, but the proxy logs `LiteLLM Redis Caching: async set() - Got exception from REDIS Object of type datetime is not JSON serializable` 5. Nothing is stored in Redis for that budget, so each pod repeats the database lookup once per cache window and logs the error again After: the same flow is quiet, and the budget is shared across pods through Redis 1. Same setup, same team, same key 2. They send the same POST http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions 3. The call succeeds and no Redis serialization error appears in the logs 4. Redis now holds the budget as JSON, so other pods read it from the shared cache instead of the database ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5311 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/<your_test_file>.py -v`. If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Shared setup, identical on both sides: local Redis on 6379, `litellm/proxy/dev_config.yaml` plus ```yaml litellm_settings: enable_redis_auth_cache: true cache: true cache_params: type: redis host: 127.0.0.1 port: 6379 ``` Team and key created once against the same database, with a real Anthropic call: ```bash curl -s -X POST http://localhost:4000/team/new -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"team_alias":"lit5311-team","team_member_budget":25,"models":["anthropic-haiku-4-5"]}' # -> team_id 0e225030-..., metadata {"team_member_budget_id": "team-lit5311-team-budget-0cfdc66a..."} ``` ### Before (3a31331435) 1. Mint a key for a team member and make a live call ```bash K=$(curl -s -X POST http://localhost:4000/key/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"team_id":"0e225030-ccf2-4701-bbf1-db05763bc2e1","user_id":"lit5311-user2"}' | jq -r .key) curl -s -X POST http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer $K" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model":"anthropic-haiku-4-5","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"say hi in 3 words"}]}' ``` ``` {"id":"chatcmpl-08d600fc-90da-4a41-b7fe-7b6678c15287","model":"anthropic-haiku-4-5",...} ``` 2. The proxy log carries the reported failure ``` 20:16:02 - LiteLLM:ERROR: redis_cache.py:762 - LiteLLM Redis Caching: async set() - Got exception from REDIS Object of type datetime is not JSON serializable, Writing value={'budget_id': 'team-lit5311-team-budget-0cfdc66ac73c44dd80df22ea170a65c0', 'max_budget': 25.0, ..., 'created_at': datetime.datetime(2026, 8, 20, 20, 15, 37, 289000, tzinfo=TzInfo(0)), ...} ``` 3. Redis holds nothing for that budget ```bash redis-cli keys 'team_member_default_budget*' ``` ``` (empty) ``` ### After (b85546fdf3) 1. Same key mint and live call ```bash K=$(curl -s -X POST http://localhost:4000/key/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"team_id":"0e225030-ccf2-4701-bbf1-db05763bc2e1","user_id":"lit5311-user3"}' | jq -r .key) curl -s -X POST http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer $K" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model":"anthropic-haiku-4-5","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"say hi in 3 words"}]}' ``` ``` Hey there friend. ``` 2. No serialization error in the log ```bash grep -c "Object of type datetime is not JSON serializable" litellm.log ``` ``` 0 ``` 3. Redis now carries the budget as JSON ```bash redis-cli keys 'team_member_default_budget*' redis-cli get team_member_default_budget:team-lit5311-team-budget-0cfdc66ac73c44dd80df22ea170a65c0 ``` ``` team_member_default_budget:team-lit5311-team-budget-0cfdc66ac73c44dd80df22ea170a65c0 {"budget_id": "team-lit5311-team-budget-0cfdc66ac73c44dd80df22ea170a65c0", "soft_budget": null, "max_budget": 25.0, "max_parallel_requests": null, "tpm_limit": null, "rpm_limit": null, "model_max_budget": null, "budget_duration": null, "allowed_models": []} ``` ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - Redis entries now carry only user-facing budget fields ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/225c12d857dd4668b01f73235a1705c1 Requested by: @yassin-berriai

signal.title: fix(scim): fail group sync when a member add or user creation fails (LIT-5105)
signal.text:
## TLDR Problem this solves: - SCIM group sync reported success while some members never landed on the team - Larger groups (10+, often 50+) ended up with users missing from teams - A member whose user row failed to create was silently dropped How it solves it: - Group membership adds and removes now propagate genuine failures to the IdP - A member whose user can neither be found nor created fails the request with 500 - Idempotent no-ops (already in team, already absent) are still swallowed - Repeated member ids in one request are created once instead of twice ## User Flow Before: an admin provisions a 50-member group from their identity provider and the IdP reports success, but the team is missing users 1. The admin assigns a 50-member group to the SCIM app and triggers provisioning 2. The IdP sends PUT https://litellm-domain/scim/v2/Groups/{group_id} with all 50 members and gets 200 back 3. The IdP marks every member as provisioned 4. The admin opens https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=teams and the team shows fewer than 50 members 5. The admin has to add the missing users to the team by hand After: the same sync either lands every member or surfaces an error the IdP retries 1. The admin assigns a 50-member group to the SCIM app and triggers provisioning 2. The IdP sends PUT https://litellm-domain/scim/v2/Groups/{group_id} with all 50 members 3. If every member lands, the IdP gets 200 and https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=teams shows all 50 members 4. If any member fails to enroll, the IdP gets a 5xx naming the failed user and retries that sync instead of recording a false success ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5105 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more - [x] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Captured against a live proxy on 127.0.0.1:4171 backed by its own Postgres. The proxy ran from a directory outside every checkout so it could not pick up a repo `.env`, with `PYTHONPATH` pointed at the branch worktree, so the two legs really do serve different code. No LLM provider is involved: SCIM provisioning is a management-plane path, so the whole capture is `/scim/v2/*` plus `/team/info` Every case pushes a 24-member group, comfortably past the size the ticket describes. In cases 2 and 3, 8 of those 24 already have a LiteLLM user row that the pushed member id does not resolve to. Four were onboarded by SSO, so their row is keyed by the identity provider's object id while the group lists them by email, and four arrived through `POST /scim/v2/Users` in lowercase while the group lists them with the casing the directory displays. LiteLLM itself emits group members by email on `GET /scim/v2/Groups/{id}`, so a directory that reads a group back and re-pushes it sends exactly these values The two legs use disjoint user and team ids (`...before...` / `...after...`) so neither leg can inherit rows the other created Shared setup, run identically inside each leg: ```bash API=http://127.0.0.1:4171 V=before # "after" on the second leg # 4 people already onboarded by SSO: their row is keyed by the IdP object id for i in 1 2 3 4; do curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}
" -X POST $API/user/new \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $SCIM_TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d "{"user_id":"c9p37688-$V-oid-$i","user_email":"c9p37688.$V.sso$i@example.com","user_role":"internal_user"}" done # 4 people already provisioned through SCIM, userName in lowercase for i in 1 2 3 4; do curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}
" -X POST $API/scim/v2/Users \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $SCIM_TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/scim+json' \ -d "{"schemas":["urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:core:2.0:User"],"userName":"c9p37688.$V.case$i@example.com","active":true,"emails":[{"value":"c9p37688.$V.case$i@example.com","primary":true}]}" done ``` Both legs printed `200 200 200 200` then `201 201 201 201`, and `select count(*) from "LiteLLM_UserTable" where user_id like 'c9p37688-$V-%' or user_id like 'c9p37688.$V.%'` returned `8` Group pushes are built from a `for` loop over the member list: ```bash members() { local out=""; for v in "$@"; do out="$out{"value":"$v"},"; done; echo "[${out%,}]"; } PAYLOAD=$(printf '{"schemas":["urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:core:2.0:Group"],"id":"%s","displayName":"%s","members":%s}' "$TEAM" "$NAME" "$(members "${MEMBERS[@]}")") ``` Each leg re-printed the identity of the code it was actually serving, so every number below carries proof of which tree produced it: ``` Before After $ grep -c _ensure_group_member_user .../scim/scim_v2.py 0 2 $ grep -c 'raise_on_error=True' .../scim/scim_v2.py 1 3 $ shasum -a 256 .../scim/scim_v2.py 67f9d761 2b566279 $ python -c 'import litellm, os; print(bool(os.environ.get("OPENAI_API_KEY")))' False False $ curl -s $API/scim/v2/ServiceProviderConfig -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' 200 200 ``` ### Before (3a31331435) #### Case 1: a 24-member group where nobody exists yet 1. `curl -s -w '
HTTP %{http_code}' -X POST $API/scim/v2/Groups -H "Authorization: Bearer $SCIM_TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/scim+json' -d "$PAYLOAD"` ``` HTTP 201 {"id":"c9p37688-before-clean","displayName":"C9 Clean Team (before)","members_written":24} ``` 2. `curl -s $API/scim/v2/Groups/c9p37688-before-clean -H "Authorization: Bearer $SCIM_TOKEN" | jq '{id, members_on_team: (.members|length)}'` ``` {"id":"c9p37688-before-clean","members_on_team":24} ``` 3. `curl -s "$API/team/info?team_id=c9p37688-before-clean" -H "Authorization: Bearer $SCIM_TOKEN" | jq '.team_info.members_with_roles | length'` ``` 24 ``` #### Case 2: a 24-member group where 8 members already have a user row under another id 1. `curl -s -w '
HTTP %{http_code}' -X POST $API/scim/v2/Groups -H "Authorization: Bearer $SCIM_TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/scim+json' -d "$PAYLOAD"` ``` HTTP 201 {"id":"c9p37688-before-mixed","displayName":"C9 Mixed Team (before)","members_written":16} ``` The push is reported as a success and the group comes back with 16 of the 24 members that were sent 2. `curl -s $API/scim/v2/Groups/c9p37688-before-mixed -H "Authorization: Bearer $SCIM_TOKEN" | jq '{id, members_on_team: (.members|length)}'` ``` {"id":"c9p37688-before-mixed","members_on_team":16} ``` 3. `curl -s "$API/team/info?team_id=c9p37688-before-mixed" -H "Authorization: Bearer $SCIM_TOKEN" | jq -r '.team_info.members_with_roles[].user_id' | sort` ``` c9p37688.before.new01@example.com ... 16 lines, new01 through new16 ... c9p37688.before.new16@example.com ``` All 8 people who already existed are missing from the team, and nothing in the response says so 4. `grep -c "Failed to create user" proxy-before.log` ``` 8 ``` ``` ERROR: scim_v2.py:884 - Failed to create user c9p37688.before.sso1@example.com: {'error': 'User with email c9p37688.before.sso1@example.com already exists'} ERROR: scim_v2.py:884 - Failed to create user C9P37688.before.Case1@example.com: {'error': 'User with email c9p37688.before.case1@example.com already exists'} ... 8 lines total ... ``` The proxy knew about all 8 failures and still answered 201 #### Case 3: the same 24-member set pushed with PUT onto an existing group 1. Seed the group with one member: `POST $API/scim/v2/Groups` returns `HTTP 201` 2. `curl -s -w '
HTTP %{http_code}' -X PUT $API/scim/v2/Groups/c9p37688-before-put -H "Authorization: Bearer $SCIM_TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/scim+json' -d "$PAYLOAD"` ``` HTTP 200 ``` 3. `curl -s "$API/team/info?team_id=c9p37688-before-put" -H "Authorization: Bearer $SCIM_TOKEN" | jq '.team_info.members_with_roles | length'` ``` 16 ``` Same silent loss on the route an identity provider uses for every re-sync #### Case 4: the same 24 people, addressed by ids that already resolve 1. `curl -s -w '
HTTP %{http_code}' -X POST $API/scim/v2/Groups -H "Authorization: Bearer $SCIM_TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/scim+json' -d "$PAYLOAD"` ``` HTTP 201 {"id":"c9p37688-before-ctl","displayName":"C9 Control Team (before)","members_written":24} ``` 2. `curl -s "$API/team/info?team_id=c9p37688-before-ctl" -H "Authorization: Bearer $SCIM_TOKEN" | jq '.team_info.members_with_roles | length'` ``` 24 ``` The 8 people dropped in case 2 are real, enrollable users, so the loss there is a loss of people and not a rejected payload ### After (74a409bf2b) #### Case 1: a 24-member group where nobody exists yet 1. `curl -s -w '
HTTP %{http_code}' -X POST $API/scim/v2/Groups -H "Authorization: Bearer $SCIM_TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/scim+json' -d "$PAYLOAD"` ``` HTTP 201 {"id":"c9p37688-after-clean","displayName":"C9 Clean Team (after)","members_written":24} ``` 2. `curl -s $API/scim/v2/Groups/c9p37688-after-clean -H "Authorization: Bearer $SCIM_TOKEN" | jq '{id, members_on_team: (.members|length)}'` ``` {"id":"c9p37688-after-clean","members_on_team":24} ``` 3. `curl -s "$API/team/info?team_id=c9p37688-after-clean" -H "Authorization: Bearer $SCIM_TOKEN" | jq '.team_info.members_with_roles | length'` ``` 24 ``` #### Case 2: a 24-member group where 8 members already have a user row under another id 1. `curl -s -w '
HTTP %{http_code}' -X POST $API/scim/v2/Groups -H "Authorization: Bearer $SCIM_TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/scim+json' -d "$PAYLOAD"` ``` HTTP 500 {"error":{"message":"{'error': "Failed to create user 'c9p37688.after.sso1@example.com' while provisioning group membership."}","type":"internal_server_error","param":"None","code":"500"}} ``` The failure now reaches the caller and names the member it could not provision, so the identity provider retries instead of recording 24 people as synced 2. `curl -s -w '
HTTP %{http_code}' $API/scim/v2/Groups/c9p37688-after-mixed -H "Authorization: Bearer $SCIM_TOKEN"` ``` HTTP 404 {"error":{"message":"{'error': 'Group not found with ID: c9p37688-after-mixed'}",...,"code":"404"}} ``` 3. `curl -s "$API/team/info?team_id=c9p37688-after-mixed" -H "Authorization: Bearer $SCIM_TOKEN" | jq '.team_info.members_with_roles | length'` ``` 0 ``` No half-populated team is left behind claiming to be the group #### Case 3: the same 24-member set pushed with PUT onto an existing group 1. Seed the group with one member: `POST $API/scim/v2/Groups` returns `HTTP 201` 2. `curl -s -w '
HTTP %{http_code}' -X PUT $API/scim/v2/Groups/c9p37688-after-put -H "Authorization: Bearer $SCIM_TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/scim+json' -d "$PAYLOAD"` ``` HTTP 500 {"error":{"message":"{'error': "Failed to create user 'c9p37688.after.sso1@example.com' while provisioning group membership."}",...,"code":"500"}} ``` 3. `curl -s "$API/team/info?team_id=c9p37688-after-put" -H "Authorization: Bearer $SCIM_TOKEN" | jq '.team_info.members_with_roles | length'` ``` 1 ``` The group keeps the member it already had rather than being rewritten to a roster that silently lost 8 people #### Case 4: the same 24 people, addressed by ids that already resolve 1. `curl -s -w '
HTTP %{http_code}' -X POST $API/scim/v2/Groups -H "Authorization: Bearer $SCIM_TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/scim+json' -d "$PAYLOAD"` ``` HTTP 201 {"id":"c9p37688-after-ctl","displayName":"C9 Control Team (after)","members_written":24} ``` 2. `curl -s "$API/team/info?team_id=c9p37688-after-ctl" -H "Authorization: Bearer $SCIM_TOKEN" | jq '.team_info.members_with_roles | length'` ``` 24 ``` A 24-member sync that can land still lands in full, so the strict path costs nothing when the ids resolve Both legs answered `/health/liveliness` with 200 immediately before and immediately after every case, so no result straddles a restarted proxy ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - A failing member now fails the whole group sync; IdPs retry these - test_update_group_metadata_serialization_issue now mocks membership writes, since its unmocked DB call was previously swallowed by the bug this PR removes Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/79e76557aa114b229b47fd35e18bf1f2 Requested by: @yassin-berriai

signal.title: fix(scim): keep the matched user_id on POST /Users email match
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - SCIM POST /Users renamed a matched user's user_id - Keys, rosters, memberships and spend kept the old id - Later SCIM calls for that user failed with 409 How it solves it: - Keep the matched row's user_id, only update its fields - Team roster sync now runs against that stable id - SCIM response returns the stable id to the IdP ## User Flow Before: an admin whose users signed in through OIDC SSO first, then turned on SCIM user provisioning, loses those users along with their keys and team history as soon as the IdP sends a userName that differs from the OIDC sub 1. The admin creates a team with POST http://localhost:4000/team/new for `team_id: team-x` 2. A user already exists from SSO: POST http://localhost:4000/user/new with `user_id: oidc-sub-x` and `user_email: user@example.com`, added to `team-x`, holding a virtual key from POST http://localhost:4000/key/generate 3. The IdP starts provisioning: POST http://localhost:4000/scim/v2/Users with that same email but `userName: scim-username-x`, which comes back `200` with `"id": "scim-username-x"` 4. GET http://localhost:4000/user/info?user_id=oidc-sub-x now returns `404 User oidc-sub-x not found`, so the admin cannot find the user they had 5. GET http://localhost:4000/key/list?user_id=oidc-sub-x still lists the virtual key under the id that no longer exists, and GET http://localhost:4000/team/info?team_id=team-x still shows `oidc-sub-x` on the roster 6. When the IdP sends the next update for that user, POST http://localhost:4000/scim/v2/Users returns `409 User already exists with username: scim-username-x`, so group changes from the IdP stop landing and the stale roster entry stays After: the same flow links the SSO user to SCIM without moving them, so their keys, roster entry and spend stay attached and later IdP updates apply 1. Same team creation with POST http://localhost:4000/team/new for `team_id: team-x` 2. Same pre-existing SSO user `oidc-sub-x` with `user@example.com`, on `team-x`, holding a virtual key 3. The IdP starts provisioning: POST http://localhost:4000/scim/v2/Users with that same email and `userName: scim-username-x`, which comes back `200` with `"id": "oidc-sub-x"`, the id the admin already knows 4. GET http://localhost:4000/user/info?user_id=oidc-sub-x returns `200` with the user, their team and their key 5. GET http://localhost:4000/key/list?user_id=oidc-sub-x lists the key under a user that still exists, and the key keeps working on POST http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions 6. When the IdP later drops the user from the group, POST http://localhost:4000/scim/v2/Users with `"groups": []` returns `200` and GET http://localhost:4000/team/info?team_id=team-x no longer lists them ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5382 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/<your_test_file>.py -v`. signal.title: fix(deepseek): aggregate reasoning_content placeholder warning to one per request
signal.text: ## What DeepSeek thinking mode emits one identical `reasoning_content` placeholder warning **per historical assistant message** on **every** request. Because clients replay the full conversation, six affected messages produce dozens of warnings on a single run and bury the useful logs. This aggregates them into a single warning per request. Fixes #37629. ## Why `DeepSeekChatConfig._transform_messages_helper` logs the warning inside the per-message loop, in the `else` branch that injects the placeholder (`litellm/llms/deepseek/chat/transformation.py`). The count of warnings is therefore exactly the number of replayed empty-`reasoning_content` messages, repeated every request. The reporter diagnosed this precisely in the issue, down to the aggregation approach and the warning text. ## What changed - Count placeholder injections in the loop; emit a single aggregated warning **after** the loop when any occurred. - No change to the placeholder injection itself, to `provider_specific_fields` recovery, or to the guarantee that the caller's history is never mutated. ## Test - `test_deepseek_chat_transformation.py`: a regression that replays multiple empty-`reasoning_content` assistant messages and asserts exactly one warning. Red before the fix (`assert 6 == 1`), green after. ## Note to the reporter @Lucius646 — you outlined this exact fix in the issue. Full credit for the diagnosis and the aggregation design is yours.

signal.title: feat(proxy): Azure Entra ID auth for the proxy database
signal.text: ## Summary Adds keyless **Microsoft Entra ID** authentication for the proxy's PostgreSQL database (Azure Database for PostgreSQL), mirroring the existing AWS RDS `IAM_TOKEN_DB_AUTH` mechanism. Today the proxy can already reach **upstream** Azure OpenAI keyless, but its **own** database still required a static password — this closes that gap. Implements the request in #29661. ## How it works When `IAM_TOKEN_DB_AUTH=true`, the provider is **auto-detected from `DATABASE_HOST`**: an Azure Database for PostgreSQL endpoint (`*.postgres.database.azure.com`) uses the new Azure path; anything else (e.g. AWS RDS/Aurora) uses the existing AWS RDS IAM provider. **No new env vars are introduced.** On the Azure path the proxy mints a short-lived Entra access token (scope `https://ossrdbms-aad.database.windows.net/.default`) via `azure-identity`'s `DefaultAzureCredential`, presents it as the Postgres password, and the existing `PrismaWrapper` background-refresh machinery rotates it. This works keyless on AKS Microsoft Entra Workload Identity, managed identity, and the Azure CLI. - Refresh is scheduled from the Entra token's JWT `exp` claim; the existing AWS presigned-token parsing is retained (both shapes handled). - A single `build_postgres_url()` helper assembles the IAM `DATABASE_URL` for all sites (CLI startup, the componentized `DatabaseURLSettings` writer/reader, and the `PrismaWrapper` refresh), so writer and reader can't drift. It URL-encodes the principal, db name, and schema (Azure Entra user principals are UPNs containing `@`). ## Config ```bash IAM_TOKEN_DB_AUTH=true DATABASE_HOST=<server>.postgres.database.azure.com # Azure host -> Entra auth auto-selected DATABASE_PORT=5432 DATABASE_USER=<managed-identity-or-principal-name> DATABASE_NAME=litellm # no DATABASE_PASSWORD ``` For AWS RDS the existing `IAM_TOKEN_DB_AUTH` behavior is unchanged — a non-Azure host selects the RDS IAM provider. ## Backwards compatibility AWS RDS / Aurora IAM is the default for any non-Azure host and is behavior-preserving: principal/db-name encoding is a no-op for conventional RDS identifiers, and there are **no new environment variables**. `PrismaWrapper.get_rds_iam_token` keeps its name (now provider-agnostic) to avoid churning existing references/tests. ## Tests Adds unit tests for host-based provider detection, the Azure token mint (mocked credential — `azure-identity` not required to run the tests), the credential cache, JWT `exp` parsing, principal/db-name/schema URL-encoding, and writer/reader parity. Existing AWS RDS IAM tests pass unchanged.

signal.title: feat(proxy): authenticate to Azure Postgres with Microsoft Entra ID tokens
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Entra-only Azure Postgres cannot back the proxy at all - Its passwords are access tokens that expire every hour - `IAM_TOKEN_DB_AUTH` mints AWS SigV4 tokens Azure denies How it solves it: - New `AZURE_POSTGRESQL_AUTH=true` and `--azure_postgresql_auth` opt-in - Proxy mints an Entra token as the Postgres password - A background task refreshes it before the token expires - Reader replicas get their own freshly minted token - Setting both token auth toggles now fails fast - A misspelled toggle value fails startup instead of reading as off - AKS workload identity exchanges its federated token instead of calling IMDS ## User Flow Before: an operator whose only Postgres is an Entra-only Azure Flexible Server cannot keep the proxy connected to it 1. They set `DATABASE_HOST=litellm-qa.postgres.database.azure.com`, `DATABASE_USER`, and `DATABASE_NAME` with no password, then start the proxy 2. Startup aborts with `"Authentication failed against database server ... the provided database credentials for (not available) are not valid"`, `error_code` `P1000`, and `GET http://localhost:4000/health/readiness` never answers because the process exited 3. They try `IAM_TOKEN_DB_AUTH=true`, the only token-based option on offer, and startup aborts again with `"User was denied access on the database litellm.public"`, `error_code` `P1010` 4. They fall back to pasting the output of `az account get-access-token --resource-type oss-rdbms` into `DATABASE_URL` by hand; the proxy starts and `GET http://localhost:4000/health/readiness` returns `{"status":"healthy","db":"connected"}` 5. About an hour later that token expires, every new connection fails with `P1000` again, and the only way back is restarting the proxy with a token pasted in by hand After: the same operator sets one flag and the proxy mints and refreshes the Entra token on its own 1. They set `AZURE_POSTGRESQL_AUTH=true` next to `DATABASE_HOST=litellm-qa.postgres.database.azure.com`, `DATABASE_USER`, and `DATABASE_NAME`, with no password anywhere, then start the proxy 2. Startup completes and `GET http://localhost:4000/health/readiness` returns `{"status":"healthy","db":"connected"}` 3. `POST http://localhost:4000/key/generate` returns a `sk-...` key that survives a restart, and `POST http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions` with that key returns a completion 4. Hours later, well past the one-hour token lifetime, the same `GET http://localhost:4000/health/readiness` still returns `{"status":"healthy","db":"connected"}` and `http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=logs` still lists new requests 5. If they set `IAM_TOKEN_DB_AUTH=true` as well, the proxy refuses to start and names both variables, rather than quietly picking one ## Relevant issues Fixes #29661 ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5889 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more - [x] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix All of this ran against a real Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible server (`litellm-lit5889-qa.postgres.database.azure.com`, Entra-only auth, no password ever set) and the real Anthropic API, with no mocks and real spend. Everything below is at the PR tip `affe2b4529`, and the before leg is at `487356733c`, the branch point it was taken from **Before the change, at `487356733c`.** Discrete host/user/name with no password gets you nowhere, and the only token toggle that existed was the AWS one 1. `DATABASE_HOST=... DATABASE_USER=mateo@berri.ai DATABASE_NAME=litellm python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config config.yaml --port 41873 --detailed_debug` ``` {"is_panic":false,"message":"Authentication failed against database server at `litellm-lit5889-qa.postgres.database.azure.com`, the provided database credentials for `(not available)` are not valid.", ... "error_code":"P1000"} ``` 2. Same command plus `IAM_TOKEN_DB_AUTH=True`, which mints an AWS RDS IAM token and sends it to Azure: ``` {"is_panic":false,"message":"User `mateo@berri.ai` was denied access on the database `litellm.public`", ... "error_code":"P1010"} ``` **After, at `affe2b4529`.** One new toggle, no password anywhere 3. Boot: ``` AZURE_POSTGRESQL_AUTH=true \ DATABASE_HOST=litellm-lit5889-qa.postgres.database.azure.com \ DATABASE_USER=mateo@berri.ai \ DATABASE_NAME=litellm \ python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config config.yaml --port 48227 --detailed_debug ``` ``` LiteLLM Proxy:INFO: prisma_client.py:656 - Started Azure Entra token proactive refresh background task LiteLLM Proxy:INFO: prisma_client.py:691 - Azure Entra token refresh loop started. Tokens will be refreshed 180s before expiration. LiteLLM Proxy:INFO: prisma_client.py:704 - Azure Entra token refresh scheduled in 2506 seconds (41.8 minutes) INFO: Uvicorn running on http://0.0.0.0:48227 ``` 4. `curl -s http://127.0.0.1:48227/health/readiness` -> `{"status":"healthy","db":"connected", ...}` 5. Generate a key and spend real money through it: ``` curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:48227/key/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $LITELLM_MASTER_KEY" \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"models":["claude-fable-5"]}' curl -s -D - -X POST http://127.0.0.1:48227/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"model":"claude-fable-5","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Reply with exactly: ENTRA AUTH OK"}],"max_tokens":512}' ``` ``` x-litellm-response-cost: 0.002 {"id":"chatcmpl-b16ea2ee-7f05-4136-aa84-63f8f2dbb19a","model":"claude-fable-5", ... "content":"ENTRA AUTH OK"} ``` 6. `curl -s "http://127.0.0.1:48227/spend/logs?request_id=chatcmpl-b16ea2ee-..." -H "Authorization: Bearer $LITELLM_MASTER_KEY"` shows the row landed in Postgres, proving the token-minted connection actually writes: ``` chatcmpl-b16ea2ee-7f05-4136-aa84-63f8f2dbb19a spend=0.002 model=anthropic/claude-fable-5 ``` 7. Kill the proxy, boot it again with the same env, and the key and its spend row are still there. A second completion on the same key returns `chatcmpl-1e449822-...` with content `SURVIVED RESTART` 8. The proactive refresh, observed live rather than simulated. The scheduler re-armed itself at 30 seconds because the az CLI's cached token was nearly out of runway, then: ``` 14:36:50 - LiteLLM Proxy:INFO: prisma_client.py:704 - Azure Entra token refresh scheduled in 30 seconds (0.5 minutes) 14:37:20 - LiteLLM Proxy:INFO: prisma_client.py:711 - Proactively refreshing Azure Entra token... 14:37:22 - LiteLLM Proxy:INFO: prisma_client.py:772 - Azure Entra token refreshed successfully. 14:37:22 - LiteLLM Proxy:INFO: prisma_client.py:704 - Azure Entra token refresh scheduled in 4319 seconds (72.0 minutes) ``` A real completion right after the refresh still works, so the reconnect is genuine and not just a log line: `chatcmpl-7b7da3f8-...` returns `POST REFRESH OK` with `x-litellm-response-cost: 0.00173` 9. Both toggles at once fails loudly at boot instead of silently picking one: ``` RuntimeError: IAM_TOKEN_DB_AUTH and AZURE_POSTGRESQL_AUTH are both enabled, but the database password can only come from one token source. Keep IAM_TOKEN_DB_AUTH for AWS RDS IAM auth, or AZURE_POSTGRESQL_AUTH for Azure Database for PostgreSQL with Microsoft Entra ID, and unset the other one. ``` 10. A typo in either toggle fails loudly too, rather than being read as off: ``` ValueError: AZURE_POSTGRESQL_AUTH='enabled' is not a recognized boolean. Set it to one of 1, on, t, true, y, yes to turn token auth on, or to one of 0, f, false, n, no, off to turn it off. ValueError: IAM_TOKEN_DB_AUTH='enabled' is not a recognized boolean. ... ``` while `AZURE_POSTGRESQL_AUTH=false` is accepted as a legitimate off value and the proxy boots normally 11. `DATABASE_USER=mateo%40berri.ai`, already percent-encoded, boots and connects exactly like the raw `mateo@berri.ai` form, so the quoting is not applied twice **Workload identity, the case bugbot caught.** AKS injects `AZURE_CLIENT_ID`, `AZURE_TENANT_ID`, and `AZURE_FEDERATED_TOKEN_FILE` into the pod, and the shared credential helper used to read a bare `AZURE_CLIENT_ID` as managed identity. Same env, same boot command, with and without the two-line inference change: 12. Before the fix (`4eb7bf32c0`), the mint goes to IMDS, which does not exist outside a VM: ``` ImdsCredential.get_token_info failed: ManagedIdentityCredential authentication unavailable, no response from the IMDS endpoint. azure.core.exceptions.ServiceRequestError: HTTPConnection(host='169.254.169.254', port=80): Failed to establish a new connection: [Errno 64] Host is down ``` 13. After the fix (`affe2b4529`), the same env reaches the federated-token leg instead: ``` azure.core.exceptions.ClientAuthenticationError: DefaultAzureCredential failed to retrieve a token from the included credentials. Attempted credentials: EnvironmentCredential: EnvironmentCredential authentication unavailable. Environment variables are not fully configured. WorkloadIdentityCredential: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: '/var/run/secrets/azure/tokens/azure-identity-token' ``` Both runs fail on a laptop, which is the honest result: there is no AKS-projected token file here and no IMDS. What changed is which credential is tried, and that is the whole fix. On a real AKS pod that file exists and the workload-identity leg succeeds ## Type 🆕 New Feature ## Caveats (if any) - Needs a credential the proxy can use: managed identity, workload identity, service principal, or `az login` - The Entra principal still needs its Postgres role created server-side - With `AZURE_FEDERATED_TOKEN_FILE` present, credential selection goes through `DefaultAzureCredential`, which falls through to any other ambient credential when the federated token cannot be used ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR - [x] affe2b4529ff84fc8d52a606dd80fc457f02cdae passes /live-pr-risk <!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY --> --- > [!NOTE] > **High Risk** > Changes how the proxy authenticates to Postgres (token minting, URL assembly, and Prisma reconnect on refresh), which is a security- and availability-critical path. A bug here can drop DB connectivity or send the wrong credential type. > > **Overview** > Lets the proxy connect to Azure Database for PostgreSQL using a Microsoft Entra ID access token as the password, with the same mint-and-refresh loop already used for AWS RDS IAM. > > Operators opt in with `AZURE_POSTGRESQL_AUTH=true` or `--azure_postgresql_auth` (Helm: `database.writer.useAzureEntraAuth`). The proxy mints a token for the OSS RDBMS scope, embeds it in `DATABASE_URL`, and refreshes it ~3 minutes before JWT `exp`. Read replicas get a pre-minted token too. IAM and Entra toggles are mutually exclusive and fail at startup; unreadable toggle values also fail instead of silently falling back to password auth. > > Token minting, expiry parsing, and URL assembly move into `token_auth.py`. User/name/schema are encoded without double-escaping so Entra UPNs (`user@tenant`) and pre-encoded RDS users both survive. Refresh sleep is floored at 30s so a cached Entra token whose `exp` does not advance cannot spin the query-engine recreate loop. > > AKS workload identity (`AZURE_FEDERATED_TOKEN_FILE`) now selects `DefaultAzureCredential` instead of managed identity, so the federated token is exchanged rather than IMDS being called. > > <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit affe2b4529ff84fc8d52a606dd80fc457f02cdae. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup> <!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

signal.title: [Feature]: Azure Entra ID (managed identity) auth for the proxy database
signal.text: ### Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. ### The Feature Add keyless **Microsoft Entra ID / Azure Workload Identity** authentication for the proxy's PostgreSQL database, mirroring the existing AWS `IAM_TOKEN_DB_AUTH` path. The proxy would mint a short-lived Entra access token (scope `https://ossrdbms-aad.database.windows.net/.default`) via `azure-identity`'s `DefaultAzureCredential`, use it as the DB password, and let the **existing `PrismaWrapper` background-refresh / reconnect machinery** handle rotation — so no static DB password is needed on Azure. Proposed, intentionally small and symmetric with the AWS path: - New `litellm/proxy/auth/azure_entra_db_token.py` with `generate_azure_entra_db_token(db_host, db_user)`, mirroring `litellm/proxy/auth/rds_iam_token.py::generate_iam_auth_token`. - Select the token source in `PrismaWrapper.get_rds_iam_token()` / `litellm/proxy/db/db_url_settings.py` based on a provider — e.g. reuse the `IAM_TOKEN_DB_AUTH` activation plus a new `IAM_DB_AUTH_PROVIDER=aws|azure` (default `aws`, fully backward compatible). - Reuse the entire existing refresh/reconnect/lock wrapper unchanged. Azure tokens are JWTs with an `exp` claim, so the proactive refresh can parse expiry directly; otherwise the existing fallback interval already keeps connections alive. This complements the recently merged Azure-token support for Redis (#27556). Together they make a **fully keyless LiteLLM on Azure AKS (Workload Identity)** possible: no provider API keys, no DB password, no Redis access key. **One question for maintainers on the preferred seam:** generalize the existing `iam_token_db_auth` flag to a provider enum (`aws|azure`), or add a parallel `AZURE_ENTRA_DB_AUTH` flag? Happy to send the PR either way — it's a small, symmetric diff with unit tests + docs. ### Motivation, pitch We run LiteLLM on Azure AKS with Microsoft Entra **Workload Identity**, where our PostgreSQL Flexible Server and Redis have password/access-key auth disabled (Entra-only) by org policy. Today LiteLLM can already reach **upstream Azure OpenAI** keyless (`enable_azure_ad_token_refresh`) and, since **#27556**, **Azure Redis** keyless — but the proxy's **own Postgres** still requires a static password in `DATABASE_URL`, which Prisma can't refresh and which breaks a passwordless posture. The AWS side already solved this exact problem with `IAM_TOKEN_DB_AUTH` + the `PrismaWrapper` token-refresh machinery; this asks for the **symmetric Azure path** so Entra-only / Workload-Identity environments can run the proxy with **zero standing secrets**. This is a common requirement for regulated Azure tenants. Prior art / precedent: #27556 (Azure Redis token auth), the existing RDS IAM design (`IAM_TOKEN_DB_AUTH`, #5893), and #9078 (closed *not planned* as stale — but that predates the RDS IAM wrapper and #27556; this issue is narrower and PR-ready). ### What part of LiteLLM is this about? Proxy ### LiteLLM is hiring a founding backend engineer, are you interested in joining us and shipping to all our users? No ### Twitter / LinkedIn details _No response_
