signal.title: [Bug]: /v1/responses batches reconcile to 0 tokens and $0.00 spend, silently
signal.text: ### Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. ### What happened? A completed managed batch created with `endpoint="/v1/responses"` reconciles to **0 prompt tokens, 0 completion tokens, and $0.00 spend** — even though the batch's output file reports real usage. There is no error and no warning. The consequence is that batch spend for Responses workloads is invisible: it does not reach `LiteLLM_SpendLogs` with a real value, so per-key and per-team `max_budget` is not enforced for them, and the spend does not appear on any dashboard. For a 3-line batch whose output file reported 33 input / 57 output tokens: ``` call_type | model | prompt_tokens | completion_tokens | spend aretrieve_batch | openai/gpt-5.2 | 0 | 0 | 0 ``` The same batch content submitted as `/v1/chat/completions` records its usage correctly, which is what pointed us at the Responses path specifically. A Responses API output line reports usage as `input_tokens` / `output_tokens`, whereas a chat line reports `prompt_tokens` / `completion_tokens`. Constructing the usage object from the Responses-shaped keys does not raise on the unrecognized names — it yields zeros: ```python from litellm.types.utils import Usage print(Usage(**{"input_tokens": 100, "output_tokens": 50})) # prompt_tokens=0 completion_tokens=0 print(Usage(**{"prompt_tokens": 100, "completion_tokens": 50})) # prompt_tokens=100 completion_tokens=50 ``` **Expected:** a `/v1/responses` batch records the provider's token counts and a non-zero cost, the same as an equivalent chat batch. Worth covering in a fix: a **mixed** output file, with some Responses-shaped lines and some chat-shaped, should sum correctly across both. A fix keyed off the batch's `endpoint` rather than each line's shape would pass the single-shape case and fail this one. ### Second, smaller issue: endpoint literals reject `/v1/responses` `CreateBatchRequest.endpoint` and the `create_batch` / `acreate_batch` annotations allow only `/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/embeddings`, and `/v1/completions`. A type-checked caller therefore cannot pass `/v1/responses`, even though it is forwarded correctly at runtime — the value is not validated against those literals. Filing it here rather than separately since it is the same feature, but it is an independent one-line change. ### Possibly related #27944 reports batch costs always 0 for Anthropic, with fix PR #27998. We have not verified whether the underlying cause is the same, but the symptom matches closely enough to be worth checking. Neither that PR's changes nor an equivalent appear to be present in v1.89.1. ### Steps to Reproduce 1. Run a DB-backed proxy with managed files/batches enabled (`/v1/files` and `/v1/batches` returning `litellm_proxy;...` unified IDs) and `CheckBatchCost` enabled: ```yaml model_list: - model_name: my-gpt litellm_params: model: openai/gpt-4o-mini api_key: os.environ/OPENAI_API_KEY model_info: id: my-gpt_unified-1 general_settings: database_url: os.environ/DATABASE_URL litellm_settings: enable_preview_features: true ``` 2. Reproduce the usage-shape half directly, with no provider call needed: ```python from litellm.types.utils import Usage print(Usage(**{"input_tokens": 100, "output_tokens": 50})) # prompt=0 completion=0 print(Usage(**{"prompt_tokens": 100, "completion_tokens": 50})) # prompt=100 completion=50 ``` 3. For the end-to-end case, create `responses_batch.jsonl` with Responses-shaped lines: ```jsonl {"custom_id":"1","method":"POST","url":"/v1/responses","body":{"model":"my-gpt","input":"hello"}} {"custom_id":"2","method":"POST","url":"/v1/responses","body":{"model":"my-gpt","input":"how are you"}} ``` 4. Upload it and create the batch: ```python from openai import OpenAI client = OpenAI(base_url=PROXY_URL, api_key=KEY) f = client.files.create( file=open("responses_batch.jsonl", "rb"), purpose="batch", extra_body={"target_model_names": "my-gpt"}, ) b = client.batches.create( input_file_id=f.id, endpoint="/v1/responses", completion_window="24h", ) ``` 5. Wait for completion, then download the output file and note the usage it reports — the keys will be `input_tokens` / `output_tokens`: ```python print(client.files.content(client.batches.retrieve(b.id).output_file_id).text) ``` 6. After a `CheckBatchCost` cycle, compare against the recorded spend: ```sql SELECT call_type, model, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, spend FROM "LiteLLM_SpendLogs" WHERE call_type = 'aretrieve_batch'; ``` Expected: the token counts from step 5, and a non-zero spend. Observed: `0 | 0 | 0`. 7. For comparison, repeat steps 3–6 with `/v1/chat/completions` lines and `endpoint="/v1/chat/completions"`. That batch records its usage correctly. 8. For the type-level half, run a type checker (e.g. mypy) over: ```python import litellm litellm.create_batch( completion_window="24h", endpoint="/v1/responses", input_file_id="file-abc", custom_llm_provider="openai", ) ``` Expected: clean. Observed: the `endpoint` literal is rejected. ### Relevant log output ```shell # No error is emitted. The cost event is dispatched with zeroed usage: CheckBatchCost: processing job litellm_proxy;model_id:my-gpt_unified-1;llm_batch_id:batch_abc... CheckBatchCost: marked job batch_abc... processed # Resulting spend row: # aretrieve_batch | openai/gpt-5.2 | 0 | 0 | 0 ``` ### What part of LiteLLM is this about? Proxy ### What LiteLLM version are you on ? v1.89.1 ### Twitter / LinkedIn details _No response_

signal.title: [Bug]: Streamed /openai_passthrough/v1/responses is cost-logged as $0 with 0 tokens (url_route ignored in the passthrough streaming logging handler)
signal.text: ### Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. ### What happened? `POST /openai_passthrough/v1/responses` with `"stream": true` writes a `LiteLLM_SpendLogs` row that is present but empty of cost: 0 prompt tokens, 0 completion tokens, `spend = 0.0`, and no pricing lookup attempted. No exception is raised and the client receives a correct, complete 200 stream The identical request **without** `stream: true` is recorded correctly and exactly. Reproduced 4× Expected: a streamed passthrough Responses call should log the same tokens, the same `spend`, and a `resp_…` `request_id` as the equivalent buffered call, exactly as passthrough *chat completions* streaming already does #### Buffered vs streamed, same request body | Field | buffered (correct) | streamed (broken) | |---|---|---| | `request_id` | `resp_0c72ddebf05f8751…` | `chatcmpl-dcbe4214-f51f-4f97…` (random uuid4) | | `call_type` | `pass_through_endpoint` | `pass_through_endpoint` | | `model` | `gpt-4o-mini` | `gpt-4o-mini` (correct) | | `prompt_tokens` / `completion_tokens` | 14 / 2 | **0 / 0** | | `spend` | `3.3e-06` (exact: `14×1.5e-07 + 2×6e-07`) | **`0.0`** | | `metadata.model_map_information.model_map_key` | `gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18` | **`''`** (no pricing lookup ran) | | assembled `response.object` | `response` | **`chat.completion`** (wrong type) | OpenAI puts full `input_tokens: 14 / output_tokens: 2 / total_tokens: 16` on the wire in the terminal `response.completed` SSE event, so the data is present and simply never read The tell is `model` correct while `model_map_key` is empty. Those come from different sources: `model` from the raw request body, `model_map_key` from the assembled response object, which is the fingerprint of assembly having failed while request metadata survived. The `usage_object` on the row is chat-completion-shaped (`prompt_tokens_details`, `completion_tokens_details`) with every field null or zero, confirming which assembler ran #### Root cause Line numbers below are from `main` at HEAD `6a919aec6` (2026-08-08), file `litellm/proxy/pass_through_endpoints/llm_provider_handlers/openai_passthrough_logging_handler.py` (616 lines) The same structure holds at the **v1.94.0 tag** (621 lines), independently verified 2026-08-11 by grepping the released file, so a reader on the affected release sees the same thing: ``` $ curl -sS https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/v1.94.0/litellm/proxy/pass_through_endpoints/llm_provider_handlers/openai_passthrough_logging_handler.py \ | grep -n "is_openai_responses_route\|call_type" 137: def is_openai_responses_route(url_route: str) -> bool: # definition 256: call_type="responses", # ONLY occurrence in the file 280: is_responses = ...is_openai_responses_route(url_route) # ONLY call site (non-streaming) def _build_responses_api_response_and_cost( -> line 225 (non-streaming helper) def openai_passthrough_handler( -> line 261 (non-streaming dispatcher) def _build_complete_streaming_response( -> line 470 (chat-only assembler) def _handle_logging_openai_collected_chunks( -> line 527 (streaming dispatcher, no route check) ``` The passthrough logger first classifies the upstream by **hostname only**, discarding the path (`pass_through_endpoints.py`), so `/v1/responses` and `/v1/chat/completions` both collapse to `EndpointType.OPENAI`: ```python elif ( parsed_url.hostname == "api.openai.com" or parsed_url.hostname == "openai.azure.com" or (parsed_url.hostname and "openai.com" in parsed_url.hostname) ): return EndpointType.OPENAI ``` The path is meant to be recovered downstream via `url_route`. The **non-streaming** handler does exactly that: ``` 265: url_route: str, # openai_passthrough_handler 280: is_responses: Final = OpenAIPassthroughLoggingHandler.is_openai_responses_route(url_route) 391: ) = OpenAIPassthroughLoggingHandler._build_responses_api_response_and_cost( ``` and that helper (225–258) is the only place `call_type` is set: ``` 252: response_cost: Final = litellm.completion_cost( 256: call_type="responses", ``` The **streaming** handler `_handle_logging_openai_collected_chunks` (522–616) receives the same argument and never reads it. `grep -n url_route` over the whole file shows **line 525 is the last occurrence in the file**, with the parameter declared and never used: ``` 522: def _handle_logging_openai_collected_chunks( 525: url_route: str, # <- declared here; last url_route in the file 537: model: Final = request_body.get("model", "gpt-4o") 542: complete_response: Final = handler._build_complete_streaming_response( 557: response_cost: Final = litellm.completion_cost( 558: completion_response=complete_response, 559: model=model, 560: custom_llm_provider=custom_llm_provider, 561: ) # <- note: no call_type argument ``` Relatedly, `is_openai_responses_route` occurs exactly twice in the file: the definition at 137 and the single call site at 280. The streaming path never consults it `_build_complete_streaming_response` (465–519) is hardcoded to the chat path with no alternative branch: ``` 480: from litellm.llms.openai.openai import OpenAIChatCompletionResponseIterator 482: openai_iterator: Final = OpenAIChatCompletionResponseIterator( 500: transformed_chunk = openai_iterator.chunk_parser(chunk=stripped_json_chunk) 513: complete_streaming_response: Final = litellm.stream_chunk_builder(chunks=all_openai_chunks) ``` The caller *does* supply the argument, per `pass_through_endpoints/streaming_handler.py` 224–229: ```python elif endpoint_type == EndpointType.OPENAI: OpenAIPassthroughLoggingHandler._handle_logging_openai_collected_chunks( ... url_route=url_route, ) ``` So the routing information reaches the function and is discarded. Dispatch one level up branches only on `EndpointType` (`ANTHROPIC` / `VERTEX_AI` / `OPENAI`), never on the OpenAI sub-route #### Relationship to PR #29728: this is the streaming half of an already-merged fix PR #29728 ("fix(proxy): use Responses-API transformer in pass-through cost tracking", merged 2026-06-10) describes this symptom in its own words: the chat transformer raised `KeyError: 'choices'` on a Responses payload, *"swallowed by the surrounding `except Exception` in the handler, and the SpendLogs row was written by the fallback path with zeroed-out tokens, spend, and model."* That PR fixed the non-streaming branch only. Its changed-file list does not include `streaming_handler.py`, and its handler hunks (`@@ -188,6 +190,42 @@`, `@@ -253,7 +291,12 @@`, `@@ -336,29 +379,18 @@`) all sit in the non-streaming path. It also added `is_openai_responses_route` to `_is_supported_openai_endpoint` in `success_handler.py`, opening the outer gate so Responses traffic reaches the handler, while wiring up only the buffered branch The docstring it left behind at `success_handler.py::_is_supported_openai_endpoint` states the consequence directly: > "Without including it here, the outer dispatch filters Responses calls out before reaching the > handler — the inner branch is then unreachable and Responses calls land in `LiteLLM_SpendLogs` > with zero tokens / zero spend." So this is an unfinished migration rather than a regression: the problem was diagnosed, the branch was written, the outer dispatch was wired, and none of it was mirrored into `_handle_logging_openai_collected_chunks` #### Why that yields these four specific symptoms A Responses SSE event nests everything under `response`. The chat parser wants `id`, `model`, `choices[].delta.content` and `usage.prompt_tokens` at the **top level**. All four are absent, so defaults fill in: | Symptom | Mechanism | |---|---| | `chatcmpl-<uuid4>` id | no top-level `id` -> `ModelResponseStream.__init__` mints one per chunk via `_generate_id()` = `"chatcmpl-" + uuid4()`; `_get_chunk_id` returns the first chunk's synthetic id (`types/utils.py`, `streaming_chunk_builder_utils.py`) | | `object: chat.completion` | `ModelResponse.__init__` hardcodes the literal, discarding the argument (`types/utils.py`) | | 0 tokens | usage is nested at `response.usage` as `input_tokens`; all three probes in `_extract_usage_chunk` miss, and the `token_counter` fallback receives `messages=None` and empty text (`streaming_chunk_builder_utils.py`) | | `model_map_key: ''` | assembled `model` is `None` -> `_select_model_name_for_cost_calc` returns `None` -> **no pricing lookup runs at all** (`litellm_logging.py`, `cost_calculator.py`) | Zero tokens × any price = $0. The cost engine is not wrong; it is asked to price an empty response All four rows are now **directly observed**, not inferred: the credential-free repro under "Proof the bug occurs" prints `response.object`, `response.id`, `response.model` and both token counts straight off the assembled object. In particular `response.model : None` on the bug path (vs `'gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18'` on the control) is the observed cause of the empty `model_map_key` #### Blast radius is narrow Only passthrough **+** Responses **+** streaming fails. All four rows below were located and read: | Path | `request_id` | tokens | spend | `model_map_key` | Verdict | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | passthrough **chat**, streamed, `include_usage` | real SSE chunk id | 14 / 1 | `2.7e-06` | `gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18` | exact | | **translated** `/v1/responses`, streamed | `resp_…` (base64) | 14 / 2 | `3.3e-06` | `openai/gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18` | exact | | passthrough **chat**, streamed, no `include_usage` | real SSE chunk id | **0** / 1 | `6e-07` | `gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18` | input unbilled (separate issue) | | **passthrough Responses, streamed** | `chatcmpl-<uuid4>` | **0 / 0** | **0.0** | `''` | broken | The chat rows survive the shared assembler because chat SSE chunks *do* carry a top-level `id`, precisely the field Responses events lack #### Secondary consequence: the row cannot be correlated to the request `request_id` is a fresh random uuid4 (version nibble `4`, variant nibble `a`) bearing no relation to either id the client holds. Measured side by side for one call: | Source | Value | |---|---| | `x-litellm-call-id` header | `323dfe4f-2741-4473-b6e2…` | | `resp_` id from terminal SSE event | `resp_06295c6e23348c50…` | | spend row `request_id` | `chatcmpl-a5ec9096-274b…` | Longest common substring is 3 characters against the header and 2 against the `resp_` id: chance. We explicitly tested and disproved the plausible hypothesis that the row id is `"chatcmpl-" + x-litellm-call-id`. So even once cost is fixed, the id should come from `response.id`, or per-request attribution remains impossible. (#28562 and #28568 cover the equivalent correlation problem on the Anthropic passthrough handler, which *does* assign the provider id onto the model response, so the OpenAI streaming path is the outlier) #### Test coverage gap On `main`, `tests/test_litellm/proxy/pass_through_endpoints/llm_provider_handlers/test_openai_passthrough_logging_handler.py`: - `test_build_complete_streaming_response` covers chat completions only - `test_responses_api_cost_tracking` exercises the **non-streaming** `openai_passthrough_handler` and asserts `call_args[1]["call_type"] == "responses"` Nothing invokes `_handle_logging_openai_collected_chunks` with a Responses `url_route`, which is how this survived #29728 #### Note on the docs listing Cost Tracking as unsupported The [OpenAI Passthrough docs](https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/pass_through/openai_passthrough) list Cost Tracking as unsupported and Streaming as supported, so this could be read as "not supported yet". I'd argue it is a genuine defect rather than a feature request: - the **buffered** passthrough Responses path already tracks cost, and does so *exactly* - `_build_responses_api_response_and_cost` exists specifically for it, and its docstring names the shape mismatch: *"The Responses API has a different on-the-wire shape from chat completions (`output: [...]` instead of `choices: [...]`), so the chat-completions `transform_response` raises KeyError 'choices' on a Responses payload."* - PR #29728 was accepted and merged for the identical symptom on the sibling branch #### Possibly related, not proven With one API key, a stored **streamed** passthrough response returns **403** (`Access denied to passthrough {resource_type} resource`, from `litellm_enterprise/proxy/hooks/passthrough_permissions_base.py`) on both `GET` and `DELETE /v1/responses/{id}` **by the key that created it**, while a buffered one returns 200 for both. The master key deletes the streamed resource successfully, so the resource exists upstream and this is an ownership-registry miss, not a missing resource I have **not** verified in source that the ownership registry keys off the same post-call id as cost tracking: this is inferred from the coincidence of symptoms. If it does, it is one root cause with two faces, and streamed stored passthrough responses are only reapable by an admin. Flagging in case it helps triage; happy to split it into its own issue ### User Flow Before a (hypothetical) fix: a developer streaming Responses API calls through the proxy's OpenAI passthrough route gets every streamed call logged at $0 with 0 tokens, so streamed usage is neither billed nor attributable 1. They send `POST https://litellm-domain/openai_passthrough/v1/responses` with their key and body `{"model": "gpt-4o-mini", "input": "Say hi in one word.", "max_output_tokens": 16, "stream": true}` 2. The 200 SSE stream completes normally and its terminal `response.completed` event carries `"id": "resp_06295c6e…"` and `"usage": {"input_tokens": 14, "output_tokens": 2, "total_tokens": 16}` 3. They open `https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs` after the spend flush and that request's row reads 0 prompt tokens, 0 completion tokens, spend $0.00 4. The row's request id is `chatcmpl-<random uuid>`, matching neither the `resp_…` id from step 2 nor the `x-litellm-call-id` response header, so the call cannot be reconciled against their own records or OpenAI's billing 5. They resend the identical body without `"stream": true` and that call's row is exact: 14 prompt tokens, 2 completion tokens, spend 3.3e-06, request id equal to the `resp_…` id from the response body After a (hypothetical) fix: the same streamed call books the same tokens, spend, and `resp_…` request id as its buffered twin 1. They send `POST https://litellm-domain/openai_passthrough/v1/responses` with their key and body `{"model": "gpt-4o-mini", "input": "Say hi in one word.", "max_output_tokens": 16, "stream": true}` 2. The 200 SSE stream completes normally and its terminal `response.completed` event carries `"id": "resp_06295c6e…"` and `"usage": {"input_tokens": 14, "output_tokens": 2, "total_tokens": 16}` 3. They open `https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs` and that request's row reads 14 prompt tokens, 2 completion tokens, spend 3.3e-06, the same as a buffered call 4. The row's request id is the `resp_…` id from step 2, so the call reconciles against both their own records and OpenAI's billing ### Proof the bug occurs #### End-to-end through the proxy (OpenAI key + Postgres) Config / setup the proxy ran with (a database is required so `LiteLLM_SpendLogs` rows are written): ```yaml model_list: - model_name: gpt-4o-mini litellm_params: model: openai/gpt-4o-mini api_key: os.environ/OPENAI_API_KEY general_settings: database_url: os.environ/DATABASE_URL ``` ```bash export OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-... export DATABASE_URL=postgresql://... litellm --config config.yaml ``` Version or commit: v1.94.0. Use v1.94.0 or later: on v1.89.1 and earlier both branches fail (for different reasons), so the contrast below will not be visible. Line numbers in the root cause section are from `main` at `6a919aec6`, and the symptom was re-reproduced 2026-08-11 at `litellm_internal_staging` head `422d925334` Commands and their full output: 1. **Control (buffered).** This one is correct; run it first so the contrast is visible: ```bash curl -sS http://0.0.0.0:4000/openai_passthrough/v1/responses \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model": "gpt-4o-mini", "input": "Say hi in one word.", "max_output_tokens": 16}' ``` Note the `id` (`resp_…`) and the `usage` block from the response body 2. **The bug: same body plus `stream: true`:** ```bash curl -sS -N http://0.0.0.0:4000/openai_passthrough/v1/responses \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model": "gpt-4o-mini", "input": "Say hi in one word.", "max_output_tokens": 16, "stream": true}' ``` Note the `resp_…` id and `usage` (`input_tokens` / `output_tokens`) in the terminal `response.completed` event: the tokens **are** on the wire 3. Wait for the async spend flush (`proxy_batch_write_at`; ~15s sufficed for us), then read both rows: ```sql SELECT request_id, call_type, model, spend, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, metadata->'model_map_information'->>'model_map_key' AS model_map_key FROM "LiteLLM_SpendLogs" WHERE api_base LIKE '%/v1/responses%' ORDER BY "startTime" DESC LIMIT 5; ``` Important: `request_id` holds the **response body's** `id`, not the `x-litellm-call-id` response header. Searching by the header returns zero rows and looks identical to missing cost tracking 4. Observe: the buffered row has correct tokens and `spend`, keyed by its `resp_…` id. The streamed row has `prompt_tokens = 0`, `completion_tokens = 0`, `spend = 0.0`, an empty `model_map_key`, and a `request_id` of `chatcmpl-<random uuid4>` matching neither the `resp_…` id nor the `x-litellm-call-id` header. No exception appears in the proxy logs 5. *(Optional, for the possibly-related 403)* Repeat steps 1 and 2 with `"store": true`, then `GET /openai_passthrough/v1/responses/{resp_id}` using the same key that created each. Buffered -> 200, streamed -> 403 The rows and on-wire data those commands captured: ```shell === Spend log row: BUFFERED /openai_passthrough/v1/responses (correct) === request_id = resp_0c72ddebf05f8751… call_type = pass_through_endpoint model = gpt-4o-mini spend = 3.3e-06 prompt_tokens = 14 completion_tokens = 2 api_base = https://api.openai.com/v1/responses model_map_key = gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18 response.object = response cost check: 14 x 1.5e-07 + 2 x 6e-07 = 3.3e-06 -> exact match S3 archive carries the same figure: response_cost = 3.2999999999999997e-06 === Spend log row: SAME REQUEST + "stream": true (broken) === request_id = chatcmpl-dcbe4214-f51f-4f97-b946-… <- random uuid4, not resp_ call_type = pass_through_endpoint model = gpt-4o-mini <- correct (from request body) spend = 0.0 <- BUG prompt_tokens = 0 completion_tokens = 0 <- BUG api_base = https://api.openai.com/v1/responses <- so it IS the responses route model_map_key = '' <- no pricing lookup ran response.object = chat.completion <- assembled as the WRONG type No exception in the proxy logs. Client received a complete 200 stream. usage_object on the row is chat-completion-shaped (prompt_tokens_details, completion_tokens_details) with every field null or zero, confirming which assembler ran. === What OpenAI actually sent on that same stream === event: response.completed data: {"type":"response.completed","response":{"id":"resp_06295c6e23348c50…", "model":"gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18", "usage":{"input_tokens":14,"output_tokens":2,"total_tokens":16}}} === Reproduced 4x (2026-08-10, dev then on v1.94.0) === chatcmpl-dcbe4214-… 0/0 spend 0.0 chatcmpl-667ff0c8-… 0/0 spend 0.0 chatcmpl-a5ec9096-… 0/0 spend 0.0 (one further streamed call: no row found under either client-visible id within 120s; that row is only locatable by sweeping on api-key hash + api_base, per the correlation problem above) === Re-reproduced 2026-08-11 on a freshly restored v1.94.x dev, same request body === buffered : request_id resp_044fa62e4937c871… 14/2 spend 3.3e-06 model_map_key gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18 streamed : request_id chatcmpl-70c1fc4f-ee41-4c40-a4ec-… 0/0 spend 0.0 model_map_key '' The streamed row's StandardLoggingPayload carries "stream": true, so the proxy knows it was a stream; it simply reassembles it down the chat path. Correlatability, tested: searched the ENTIRE streamed spend row (all columns) and the ENTIRE archived S3 payload for the regex resp_[A-Za-z0-9]+ -> NO MATCH. The only ids present are the synthetic chatcmpl-<uuid4>, litellm_call_id 9ea21e3f-a9da-4a5c-b060-…, and trace_id 6f2e69d0-0a42-4d8b-a433-…, none of which correspond to anything OpenAI issued. The call cannot be reconciled against the provider's own billing records by any stored identifier. === Re-reproduced 2026-08-11 at litellm_internal_staging head 422d925334, same request body === buffered : request_id resp_0d1add55… 13/3 spend 3.75e-06 (exact) model_map_key gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18 streamed : request_id chatcmpl-19f71043-ea9a-44af-9f54-… 0/0 spend 0.0 model_map_key '' (the streamed 200 SSE completed normally and its terminal response.completed event carried usage input_tokens 13 / output_tokens 3; zero tracebacks in the --detailed_debug log) === Credential-free reproduction (no proxy, no key) === See the credential-free reproduction below. Calling _build_complete_streaming_response directly on litellm 1.94.0 with Responses-shaped SSE prints: response.object : 'chat.completion' response.model : None prompt_tokens : 0 completion_cost: 0.0 SENTINEL PRESENT: False and the one-variable control (chat-shaped SSE, same content) prints: response.model : 'gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18' prompt_tokens : 14 completion_cost: 3.2999999999999997e-06 SENTINEL PRESENT: True Note the control's cost is bit-identical to the buffered production row above. === url_route declared and never read (main @ 6a919aec6, file is 616 lines) === litellm/proxy/pass_through_endpoints/llm_provider_handlers/openai_passthrough_logging_handler.py $ grep -n "url_route" openai_passthrough_logging_handler.py | tail -8 265: url_route: str, # non-streaming handler 277: is_chat_completions: Final = ...is_openai_chat_completions_route(url_route) 278: is_image_generation: Final = ...is_openai_image_generation_route(url_route) 279: is_image_editing: Final = ...is_openai_image_editing_route(url_route) 280: is_responses: Final = ...is_openai_responses_route(url_route) 298: url_route=url_route, 456: url_route=url_route, 525: url_route: str, # streaming handler -> line 525 is the LAST occurrence of url_route in the file. _handle_logging_openai_collected_chunks spans 522-616, so the parameter is declared at 525 and never read in the 535-616 body. $ grep -n "is_openai_responses_route" openai_passthrough_logging_handler.py 137: def is_openai_responses_route(url_route: str) -> bool: # definition 280: is_responses: Final = ...is_openai_responses_route(url_route) # only call site The assembler the streaming path calls instead, hardcoded with no branch: 465: def _build_complete_streaming_response( 480: from litellm.llms.openai.openai import OpenAIChatCompletionResponseIterator 482: openai_iterator: Final = OpenAIChatCompletionResponseIterator( 500: transformed_chunk = openai_iterator.chunk_parser(...) 513: complete_streaming_response: Final = litellm.stream_chunk_builder(chunks=all_openai_chunks) Cost then computed without call_type: 557: response_cost: Final = litellm.completion_cost( 558: completion_response=complete_response, 559: model=model, 560: custom_llm_provider=custom_llm_provider, 561: ) Contrast the non-streaming path, which does branch and does set call_type: 225: def _build_responses_api_response_and_cost( 252: response_cost: Final = litellm.completion_cost( 256: call_type="responses", 391: ) = ..._build_responses_api_response_and_cost( The caller supplies the argument that is then discarded: litellm/proxy/pass_through_endpoints/streaming_handler.py 224: elif endpoint_type == EndpointType.OPENAI: 226: OpenAIPassthroughLoggingHandler._handle_logging_openai_collected_chunks( 229: url_route=url_route, And the id source: litellm/types/utils.py:86-87 def _generate_id(): return "chatcmpl-" + str(uuid.uuid4()) ``` #### Credential-free reproduction (no key, no proxy, no database, no network) This calls the affected function directly, so reproduction costs nothing and takes ~10 seconds **1. Install the affected version** ```bash pip install litellm==1.94.0 fastapi ``` (`fastapi` is only needed because importing anything under `litellm.proxy` pulls it in) **2. Run this script** ```python """Streamed OpenAI-passthrough Responses SSE is reassembled as a ChatCompletion, losing the resp_ id, the model, and the token counts.""" import importlib.metadata import json import litellm from litellm.proxy.pass_through_endpoints.llm_provider_handlers.openai_passthrough_logging_handler import ( # noqa: E501 OpenAIPassthroughLoggingHandler, ) ID_SENTINEL = "resp_PROOFSENTINEL0123456789abcdef" CTRL_ID_SENTINEL = "chatcmpl-CONTROLSENTINEL0123456789" IN_TOK, OUT_TOK = 14, 2 USAGE_RESPONSES_SHAPE = { "input_tokens": IN_TOK, "input_tokens_details": {"cached_tokens": 0}, "output_tokens": OUT_TOK, "output_tokens_details": {"reasoning_tokens": 0}, "total_tokens": IN_TOK + OUT_TOK, } # What /v1/responses actually streams. Usage arrives ONLY on the terminal # response.completed event, nested under "response". No event has a top-level id or usage. RESPONSES_CHUNKS = [ {"type": "response.created", "sequence_number": 0, "response": {"id": ID_SENTINEL, "object": "response", "status": "in_progress", "model": "gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18", "usage": None}}, {"type": "response.output_text.delta", "sequence_number": 3, "item_id": "msg_abc", "output_index": 0, "content_index": 0, "delta": "OK"}, {"type": "response.completed", "sequence_number": 8, "response": {"id": ID_SENTINEL, "object": "response", "status": "completed", "model": "gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18", "output": [{"id": "msg_abc", "type": "message", "status": "completed", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"type": "output_text", "text": "OK"}]}], "usage": USAGE_RESPONSES_SHAPE}}, ] # CONTROL: identical content, chat-completions shape -- top-level id, top-level usage. CHAT_CHUNKS = [ {"id": CTRL_ID_SENTINEL, "object": "chat.completion.chunk", "created": 1786374786, "model": "gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18", "choices": [{"index": 0, "delta": {"role": "assistant", "content": "OK"}, "finish_reason": None}]}, {"id": CTRL_ID_SENTINEL, "object": "chat.completion.chunk", "created": 1786374786, "model": "gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18", "choices": [{"index": 0, "delta": {}, "finish_reason": "stop"}], "usage": {"prompt_tokens": IN_TOK, "completion_tokens": OUT_TOK, "total_tokens": IN_TOK + OUT_TOK}}, ] def as_sse(events: list) -> list: return [f"data: {json.dumps(e)}" for e in events] + ["data: [DONE]"] def run(label: str, events: list, sentinel: str) -> None: assembled = OpenAIPassthroughLoggingHandler()._build_complete_streaming_response( all_chunks=as_sse(events), litellm_logging_obj=None, model="gpt-4o-mini", ) print(f"=== {label} ===") if assembled is None: print(" assembled = None (handler gave up)\n SENTINEL PRESENT: False\n") return usage = getattr(assembled, "usage", None) print(f" assembled type : {type(assembled).__name__}") print(f" response.object : {getattr(assembled, 'object', None)!r}") print(f" response.id : {getattr(assembled, 'id', None)!r}") print(f" response.model : {getattr(assembled, 'model', None)!r}") print(f" prompt_tokens : {getattr(usage, 'prompt_tokens', None)}") print(f" completion_tokens: {getattr(usage, 'completion_tokens', None)}") try: print(f" completion_cost : {litellm.completion_cost(completion_response=assembled, model='gpt-4o-mini', custom_llm_provider='openai')}") except Exception as exc: # noqa: BLE001 print(f" completion_cost : raised {type(exc).__name__}: {exc}") print(f" SENTINEL PRESENT: {sentinel in json.dumps(assembled.model_dump(), default=str)}\n") print(f"litellm version: {importlib.metadata.version('litellm')}\n") print(f"input carries id={ID_SENTINEL} usage={IN_TOK} in / {OUT_TOK} out\n") run("BUG: Responses-API SSE (what /v1/responses streams)", RESPONSES_CHUNKS, ID_SENTINEL) run("CONTROL: chat-completions SSE (one variable changed)", CHAT_CHUNKS, CTRL_ID_SENTINEL) print(f"cost that should be booked for {IN_TOK} in / {OUT_TOK} out: {IN_TOK * 1.5e-07 + OUT_TOK * 6.0e-07}") ``` **3. Observe: verbatim stdout on v1.94.0** ``` litellm version: 1.94.0 input carries id=resp_PROOFSENTINEL0123456789abcdef usage=14 in / 2 out === BUG: Responses-API SSE (what /v1/responses streams) === assembled type : ModelResponse response.object : 'chat.completion' response.id : 'chatcmpl-0884643f-99bc-4099-83a8-982304d30a29' response.model : None prompt_tokens : 0 completion_tokens: 0 completion_cost : 0.0 SENTINEL PRESENT: False === CONTROL: chat-completions SSE (one variable changed) === assembled type : ModelResponse response.object : 'chat.completion' response.id : 'chatcmpl-CONTROLSENTINEL0123456789' response.model : 'gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18' prompt_tokens : 14 completion_tokens: 2 completion_cost : 3.2999999999999997e-06 SENTINEL PRESENT: True cost that should be booked for 14 in / 2 out: 3.2999999999999997e-06 ``` - **Expected:** the Responses stream assembles with `id = resp_PROOFSENTINEL…`, `prompt_tokens = 14`, `completion_tokens = 2`, and `completion_cost = 3.3e-06` - **Observed:** `SENTINEL PRESENT: False`. The `resp_` id is gone, replaced by a random uuid4. `response.model` is `None`, both token counts are `0`, and cost is `0.0` **4. The control isolates it.** The only variable changed between the two halves is the *shape* of the SSE events: same content, same token counts, same model string. The chat-shaped stream round-trips perfectly and prices to `3.2999999999999997e-06`, which is **bit-identical** to the figure the buffered passthrough path records in production (see the S3 archive line in the captured rows above). So the assembler and the cost engine are both fine; only the Responses shape fails **5. Note on `response.model : None`.** This is the mechanical cause of the empty `model_map_key` in the spend row: with no model name on the assembled object, `_select_model_name_for_cost_calc` returns `None` and no pricing lookup is attempted at all. Re-running the script yields a different uuid4 each time, confirming the id is freshly minted rather than derived from anything on the wire ### What a fix PR should look like Mirror what PR #29728 did for the buffered branch into the streaming branch. In `litellm/proxy/pass_through_endpoints/llm_provider_handlers/openai_passthrough_logging_handler.py`, `_handle_logging_openai_collected_chunks` should consult `is_openai_responses_route(url_route)` (it already receives `url_route` and ignores it) and, on a Responses route, assemble the collected SSE events into a Responses API response instead of running the chat-completions chunk parser. The terminal `response.completed` event already carries the full `id`, `model`, `output`, and `usage`, so assembly can read that event directly. Cost should then be computed with `call_type="responses"` exactly as `_build_responses_api_response_and_cost` does for the buffered branch, and the assembled object should keep `response.id` so the spend row's `request_id` becomes the `resp_…` id and the row is correlatable For tests, extend `tests/test_litellm/proxy/pass_through_endpoints/llm_provider_handlers/test_openai_passthrough_logging_handler.py`, which today covers chat-only streaming and buffered Responses, with a case that feeds Responses-shaped SSE chunks and a `/v1/responses` `url_route` through `_handle_logging_openai_collected_chunks` and asserts nonzero tokens, pricing computed as a Responses call, and the `resp_…` request id QA is the two curls and the spend-log query from the proof section against a live proxy, before and after the change: before shows the 0/0 `chatcmpl-` row at spend 0.0, after shows real tokens, exact spend, and the `resp_…` request id ### What part of LiteLLM is this about? Proxy ### What LiteLLM version are you on ? v1.94.0 ### Twitter / LinkedIn details _No response_

signal.title: Completing a batch with output_file_id=None sets batch_processed=True unconditionally, permanently losing spend recovery
signal.text: ### What happened? In litellm/proxy/openai_files_endpoints/common_utils.py, when a batch's `db_status` transitions to `"complete"`, `update_data["batch_processed"] = True` is set unconditionally. `batch_processed=True` is the sole re-pickup gate for CheckBatchCost's cost-recovery poller (`_find_jobs` selects on `batch_processed=False`). A batch can legitimately reach `status="completed"` with `output_file_id` still `None` — either the provider response is briefly lagging before the output id populates, or every request line errored. Setting the flag unconditionally in the lagging case permanently retires the batch from any future cost-recovery pass, silently losing the spend record with no retry. ### Steps to Reproduce 1. Create a batch whose provider marks it `completed` before `output_file_id` is populated in the same response (a real, observed timing window). 2. The retrieve-success path sets `batch_processed=True` on that response. 3. Expected: the batch is only retired once the provider proves there were no successful lines (or its output file has actually arrived); otherwise it stays eligible for the next `CheckBatchCost` pass. 4. Actual: `batch_processed=True` is set immediately regardless, and the batch is never revisited even after its output file id later populates. ### What part of LiteLLM is this about? Proxy ### What LiteLLM version are you on? v1.94.3
signal.author: jimmychen-p72

signal.title: is_thinking_enabled crashes with AttributeError when thinking is passed as a bare bool (follow-up to #25792)
signal.text: ### What happened? `BaseConfig.is_thinking_enabled` (litellm/llms/base_llm/chat/transformation.py) does `(non_default_params.get("thinking") or {}).get("type") == "enabled"`. When `thinking` is a bare bool (`true`/`false`, per Claude Code's shorthand for the enabled flag, as opposed to the dict shape `{"type": "enabled"}`), `True or {}` evaluates to `True`, and `.get("type")` is then called on a bool — raising `AttributeError: 'bool' object has no attribute 'get'`. This is the same root-cause class as #25792 (a `None` thinking value from `_map_reasoning_effort("none", ...)` hits the same `.get()` chain) — any non-dict truthy `thinking` value breaks it, not just `None`. ### Steps to Reproduce ```python from litellm.llms.base_llm.chat.transformation import BaseConfig BaseConfig().is_thinking_enabled({"thinking": True}) ``` Expected: returns `True`. Actual: `AttributeError: 'bool' object has no attribute 'get'`. ### What part of LiteLLM is this about? Completions ### What LiteLLM version are you on? v1.94.3

signal.title: `split_concatenated_json_objects` raises `JSONDecodeError` on a malformed remainder, aborting the whole multi-tool-call turn
signal.text: ### What happened? `split_concatenated_json_objects` (litellm/litellm_core_utils/prompt_templates/common_utils.py) parses a raw string containing concatenated JSON objects (tool-call `arguments` from parallel tool calls). When one object in the sequence is truncated or otherwise malformed, `decoder.raw_decode(raw, idx)` raises `json.JSONDecodeError` uncaught, propagating out of the function and aborting the caller's (`parse_tool_call_arguments`) entire multi-tool-call turn — not just the one malformed call. ### Steps to Reproduce ```python from litellm.litellm_core_utils.prompt_templates.common_utils import ( split_concatenated_json_objects, ) split_concatenated_json_objects('{"a": 1}{"b": ') ``` Expected: returns `[{"a": 1}]` — the complete objects already decoded — so the caller can fall back to `{}` for the one unparseable tool call. Actual: raises `json.JSONDecodeError`. ### What part of LiteLLM is this about? Completions ### What LiteLLM version are you on? v1.94.3
signal.author: jimmychen-p72

signal.title: [Bug]: Function tools fail with reasoning_effort error for OpenAI gpt-5.6 family models (gpt-5.6-sol/luna/terra) on /chat/completions
signal.text: ### Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. ### What happened? Calling /chat/completions on a self-hosted LiteLLM proxy with function tools set for any model in the OpenAI gpt-5.6 family (gpt-5.6-sol, gpt-5.6-luna, gpt-5.6-terra) fails with a 400 BadRequestError, even without explicitly setting reasoning_effort in the request body. ### Steps to Reproduce 1. Request (via curl): ``` curl --location 'http://localhost:4000/chat/completions' \ --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \ --header 'Authorization: Bearer 1234' \ --data '{ "model": "openai/gpt-5.6-sol", "stream": false, "messages": [ { "role": "user", "content": "What'\''s the weather like in Boston today? in celsius" } ], "tools": [ { "type": "function", "function": { "name": "get_current_weather", "description": "Get the current weather in a given location", "parameters": { "type": "object", "properties": { "location": { "type": "string", "description": "The city and state, e.g. San Francisco, CA" }, "unit": { "type": "string", "enum": ["celsius", "fahrenheit"] } }, "required": ["location"] } } } ] }' ``` 2. Response: ``` { "error": { "message": "litellm.BadRequestError: OpenAIException - Function tools with reasoning_effort are not supported for gpt-5.6-sol in /v1/chat/completions. To use function tools, use /v1/responses or set reasoning_effort to 'none'....", "type": "invalid_request_error", "param": "reasoning_effort", "code": "400" } } ``` Same behavior reproduced with openai/gpt-5.6-luna and openai/gpt-5.6-terra. This looks related to #23156, which reports the same underlying restriction for gpt-5.4 via the openai-agents SDK. This report is filed separately because it reproduces directly against /chat/completions on the proxy (no SDK involved) and affects the newer gpt-5.6 family, so LiteLLM's model-family detection (e.g. is_model_gpt_5_4_plus_model referenced in #28782) may need to be extended to recognize gpt-5.6* models as well. ### Expected behavior LiteLLM should either automatically route gpt-5.6* + function tools requests to /v1/responses, or default/force reasoning_effort to 'none' for /v1/chat/completions when function tools are present, or surface a clearer, actionable error before hitting the OpenAI API (ideally at request-validation time) explaining that /v1/responses is required for tool calls on this model family. ### Relevant log output ```shell litellm.BadRequestError: OpenAIException - Function tools with reasoning_effort are not supported for gpt-5.6-sol in /v1/chat/completions. To use function tools, use /v1/responses or set reasoning_effort to 'none'.... ``` ### What part of LiteLLM is this about? Proxy ### What LiteLLM version are you on ? v1.92.0 ### Twitter / LinkedIn details _No response_

signal.title: [Bug]: tagged auto-router captures untagged requests to a shared model name, skipping tag matching
signal.text: ## What happened? With `enable_tag_filtering: true`, a `model_name` served by both an untagged plain deployment and an `auto_router/` marker carrying `tags: ["route"]` is meant to split traffic: requests tagged `route` go through the semantic router, untagged requests fall through to the plain deployment. Instead every request to the name goes through the semantic router, tags or not. When exactly one pre-routing strategy is registered under a model name it is returned unconditionally, before any tag matching, so the plain deployment is unreachable and untagged requests are semantically routed to tiers the caller never opted into The caller's request is then answered by a model they did not select and billed against the tier deployment, and combined with the alias param-forwarding bug #36619 it becomes a hard failure: the hijacked untagged request goes out to the Gemini tier at the OpenAI `api_base` and 404s Found while reproducing a customer report (ticket #7159) ## User Flow Before a (hypothetical) fix: an untagged request meant for the plain OpenAI deployment 404s, or is silently answered by a different provider 1. They send POST http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions with `{"model": "gpt4o", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "What is the capital of France?"}]}` and no tags 2. The response is HTTP 404: `{"error":{"message":"litellm.NotFoundError: GeminiException - . Received Model Group=gpt4o\nAvailable Model Group Fallbacks=None","code":"404"}}` even though the plain gpt-4o deployment is configured and healthy 3. With the marker listed first in config.yaml instead, the same request returns 200, but http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=logs shows it was served by `gemini/gemini-3.6-flash`, not `openai/gpt-4o` After a (hypothetical) fix: the untagged request is served by the plain deployment and only tagged requests are semantically routed 1. The same untagged POST returns 200 and http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=logs shows `openai/gpt-4o` served it 2. A POST with `"tags": ["route"]` added goes through the semantic router to the Gemini tier ## Proof the bug occurs Config the proxy ran with (env vars: OPENAI_API_KEY, GEMINI_API_KEY): ```yaml model_list: - model_name: gpt4o litellm_params: model: openai/gpt-4o api_key: os.environ/OPENAI_API_KEY api_base: https://api.openai.com/v1 - model_name: gpt4o litellm_params: model: auto_router/gpt4o-router auto_router_config: '{"routes": [{"name": "gemini-flash", "utterances": ["What is the capital of France?", "capital city questions", "geography questions"], "score_threshold": 0.3}]}' auto_router_default_model: gemini-flash auto_router_embedding_model: text-embedding tags: ["route"] - model_name: gemini-flash litellm_params: model: gemini/gemini-3.6-flash api_key: os.environ/GEMINI_API_KEY - model_name: text-embedding litellm_params: model: openai/text-embedding-3-small api_key: os.environ/OPENAI_API_KEY router_settings: enable_tag_filtering: true general_settings: master_key: sk-repro-1234 ``` Version: litellm_internal_staging at commit 7a55ca811b, proxy booted with `python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config repro_config.yaml --port 47613 --detailed_debug` (needs `pip install "semantic-router>=0.1.15"`) Untagged request: ``` curl -sS -i -X POST http://localhost:47613/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-repro-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model": "gpt4o", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "What is the capital of France?"}]}' HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found {"error":{"message":"litellm.NotFoundError: GeminiException - . Received Model Group=gpt4o\nAvailable Model Group Fallbacks=None","type":null,"param":null,"code":"404"}} ``` Proxy debug log for that request, showing the semantic router captured it despite the request carrying no tags: ``` route_choice: name='gemini-flash' ... similarity_score=0.4733... POST Request Sent from LiteLLM: curl -X POST \ https://api.openai.com/v1/models/gemini-3.6-flash:generateContent \ ``` Same config with the two `gpt4o` entries swapped (marker first), same untagged curl: 200, but the debug log shows `https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1alpha/models/gemini-3.6-flash:generateContent`, so the answer came from the Gemini tier either way; the plain OpenAI deployment is never used ## What a fix PR should look like In `litellm/router.py`, `_select_pre_routing_strategy` short-circuits `len(candidates) == 1` before reading the request's tags. The single-candidate path must still respect tags when tag filtering is enabled: if the sole strategy carries real tags, the request matches none of them, and the alias name also has non-marker deployments, return None so ordinary deployment selection, which already understands tags, serves the request from the plain entries. Keep returning the sole strategy when it is untagged or default-tagged, when tag filtering is disabled, or when the marker is the only entry under the name, so existing single-router setups keep working Regression test: in the test file mapped to `litellm/router.py` under `tests/test_litellm/`, a Router with a tagged auto-router marker plus an untagged plain deployment under one name must leave an untagged request alone (hook returns None) and still rewrite a request tagged to match the marker QA: config above on a live proxy; the untagged curl must be answered by `openai/gpt-4o` (visible on the logs page), and the tagged curl must be routed by the semantic router
signal.author: mateo-berri

signal.title: [Bug]: Managed batch retrieve/cancel returns 403 team_model_access_denied because the deployment model_id hash is checked against team model access
signal.text: ## What happened Retrieving or cancelling a LiteLLM-managed batch through the proxy returns 403 `team_model_access_denied`, and the model the check reports as denied is a 64 character sha256 hash rather than a model name: ``` Error code: 403 - {'error': {'message': "team not allowed to access model. This team can only access models=['group-a', 'group-b']. Tried to access 8d0eaa7e6c6f54a425dfd0062cb6b0dc38093f36f0d15994e6ae491ccfc53ac4", 'type': 'team_model_access_denied', 'param': 'model', 'code': '403'}} ``` The virtual key's team is allowed to access the batch model's access group, and a normal `/v1/chat/completions` call to the same model group succeeds. Batch create also succeeds. Only retrieve and cancel fail, and the "Tried to access" value is the deployment model_id hash, never a model group name ## How to reproduce Config for a batch-capable deployment whose access group the calling key's team is allowed to use ```yaml - model_name: 'bedrock-batch-model' model_info: access_groups: ['group-a'] mode: 'batch' litellm_params: model: 'bedrock/global.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0' aws_region_name: 'us-east-1' aws_batch_role_arn: '...' s3_bucket_name: '...' s3_region_name: 'us-east-1' ``` Then, with a virtual key whose team may access `group-a` ```python client = OpenAI(base_url=PROXY_URL, api_key=VIRTUAL_KEY) f = client.files.create(file=open("batch.jsonl","rb"), purpose="batch", extra_body={"target_model_names": "bedrock-batch-model"}) b = client.batches.create(input_file_id=f.id, endpoint="/v1/chat/completions", completion_window="24h") client.batches.retrieve(b.id) # 403 team_model_access_denied, "Tried to access <sha256 hash>" ``` The failure is in the authorization layer and happens before any provider call, so it does not depend on the batch provider or on the batch having completed. The returned batch id base64 decodes to ``` litellm_proxy;model_id:<sha256-deployment-hash>;llm_batch_id:<provider-batch-id> ``` so the same 403 can be reproduced directly by calling `GET /v1/batches/<that id>` or `POST /v1/batches/<that id>/cancel`. This is provider agnostic; it was hit with a Bedrock batch model but the id encoding is shared by all managed batches ## Root cause On retrieve and cancel the path param `batch_id` is copied into the request body by `populate_request_with_path_params`, then `common_checks` resolves the model to authorize with `get_model_from_request` and calls `can_team_access_model` `get_model_from_request` -> `_extract_model_candidates_from_request` matches the `/batches` route and, for the `batch_id` field, calls `_extract_models_from_managed_resource_id`. Inside that function (`litellm/proxy/auth/auth_utils.py:1306`), the file/batch branch appends the raw deployment `model_id` with no resolution: ```python # litellm/proxy/auth/auth_utils.py:1331-1334 _append_model_candidates( candidates=candidates, value=get_model_id_from_unified_batch_id(unified_file_id), ) # and litellm/proxy/auth/auth_utils.py:1343 _append_model_candidates(candidates=candidates, value=parsed_id.get("model_id")) ``` `get_model_id_from_unified_batch_id` is literally `file_id.split("model_id:")[1].split(";")[0]` (`litellm/proxy/openai_files_endpoints/common_utils.py:66`), so it returns the deployment model_id, which is `hashlib.sha256(model_group + litellm_params).hexdigest()` (`litellm/router.py`). That hash becomes the model handed to `can_team_access_model`, which compares it against the team's allowed access groups and model group names and raises at `litellm/proxy/auth/auth_checks.py:3820` because a raw deployment hash is never in that list The video/character branch a few lines below does the right thing and resolves the model_id through the router before appending it: ```python # litellm/proxy/auth/auth_utils.py:1355-1366 model_id = decode_video_id_with_provider(resource_id).get("model_id") _append_model_candidates( candidates=candidates, value=_resolve_model_id_with_router(model_id, llm_router), ) ``` The file/batch branch is missing this resolution step Create is not affected because the authorized resource there is the `input_file_id`, which decodes to `litellm_proxy:...;target_model_names,<model group names>;...;llm_output_file_model_id,<hash>`. `get_models_from_unified_file_id` returns the model group names (which the team is granted), and the boundary anchored `model_id` parse does not pick up `llm_output_file_model_id`, so create authorizes against the group name and passes ## Suggested fix In `_extract_models_from_managed_resource_id`, resolve the values coming from `get_model_id_from_unified_batch_id` (`auth_utils.py:1331-1334`) and `parse_unified_id(...).get("model_id")` (`auth_utils.py:1343`) to the deployment's public model_name before appending, the same way the video/character branch resolves its model_id. One caveat for whoever implements it: `Router.resolve_model_name_from_model_id` returns the id unchanged when it is a known deployment id, so it will not map a batch model_id hash on its own; the deployment hash to model_name mapping is `Router.get_deployment(model_id=<hash>).model_name` (or `Router.get_model_info(id=<hash>)["model_name"]`), with a fallback to the raw value only if resolution fails ## Impact Managed batch status polling and cancellation are unusable for any team key scoped to specific model access groups. Admin role does not help on its own; a proxy admin key whose team is scoped to access groups is still denied, because the check is on the team's model access. This also overlaps the background batch cost poller path in #30635 ## Related #30635 (background batch cost poller denied on managed batch retrieve), #29236 (proxy alias validation for managed batch input files), #31432 (Bedrock batch create alias and credential handling), #25104 (Bedrock batch broken via proxy) ## Environment litellm 1.91.0, proxy. Reproduced live against a running gateway

signal.title: fix(mcp): allow oauth token to target a custom upstream header
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Minted MCP OAuth token always lands on `Authorization` - Upstreams needing a second static credential lose one of them - Tools list comes back empty because upstream rejects the call How it solves it: - New per-server `oauth_token_header` (defaults to `Authorization`) - Minted token owns that header, static `Authorization` rides alongside - Applies to the legacy client and to every v2 resolver grant that mints an upstream token (client credentials, authorization code, token exchange, ID-JAG) ## User Flow Before: an admin whose MCP gateway wants a long-lived platform token on `Authorization` plus an hourly OAuth token on `esb-oauth` cannot get both onto one request, so every tool call fails 1. They add an MCP server with `auth_type: oauth2`, client id/secret, and `static_headers` carrying `Authorization: Bearer <platform token>` and `envlbl: eng` 2. They POST http://litellm-domain/v1/Test_MCP/MCP with `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"tools/list","id":1}` 3. The gateway sees the minted OAuth token on `Authorization` and no platform token, so it answers 401 and the response carries no tools 4. Flipping it around, putting a placeholder on `esb-oauth` instead, the placeholder is sent verbatim because nothing ever writes the minted token there 5. The same failure shows up through POST http://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions and http://litellm-domain/v1/responses when the model tries to call one of that server's tools After: the admin points the minted token at `esb-oauth` and both credentials arrive on the same request 1. They add the same MCP server, this time also setting `oauth_token_header: esb-oauth` 2. They POST http://litellm-domain/v1/Test_MCP/MCP with `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"tools/list","id":1}` 3. The gateway receives `Authorization: Bearer <platform token>`, `esb-oauth: Bearer <minted token>`, and `envlbl: eng`, and answers 200 with the real tool list 4. An hour later the minted token expires, the gateway 401s once, and LiteLLM refetches and retries on `esb-oauth` while `Authorization` stays untouched 5. POST http://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions and http://litellm-domain/v1/responses now execute that server's tools normally ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-3735 ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/<your_test_file>.py -v` - [x] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Shared setup: a live proxy on port 4000 with master key `sk-1234`, plus two stubs standing in for the customer's estate, since no reachable gateway here demands two credentials. One is a fake OAuth token endpoint on :8901 that mints a fresh incrementing `minted-token-N` on every call, so a refetch is objectively visible. The other is a real streamable-HTTP MCP upstream on :8902 (`mcp.server.fastmcp`, tools `echo` and `ping`) wrapped in middleware that records inbound headers and can be armed to answer one 401. Every case drives a real JSON-RPC `initialize` plus `tools/list` through `POST /{alias}/mcp`. ```yaml mcp_servers: esb_custom: # after case url: http://localhost:8902/mcp transport: http auth_type: oauth2 oauth2_flow: client_credentials client_id: litellm-cid client_secret: litellm-secret token_url: http://localhost:8901/token oauth_token_header: esb-oauth static_headers: Authorization: Bearer static-platform-token envlbl: eng esb_baseline: # same thing without oauth_token_header ... # identical, oauth_token_header omitted ``` ```bash litellm --config config.yaml --detailed_debug --port 4000 curl -sX POST http://localhost:4000/esb_custom/mcp \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -H 'Accept: application/json, text/event-stream' \ -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"tools/list","id":1}' ``` ### Before (d2d158f271) #### Two credentials on one request 1. Point the same curl at `esb_baseline`, which is the merge base's only option since `oauth_token_header` does not exist there 2. Headers recorded by the upstream, platform credential gone and nothing on the custom header: ```json {"envlbl": "eng", "authorization": "Bearer minted-token-14"} ``` #### Refetch after a 401 1. Not reachable at the merge base: the minted token can only occupy `Authorization`, so there is no static credential left for a refetch to preserve ### After (9cd4a7bb99) #### Two credentials on one request 1. Run the curl above against `esb_custom` 2. `tools/list` answers with `esb_custom-echo` and `esb_custom-ping`, and the upstream records both credentials: ```json {"authorization": "Bearer static-platform-token", "envlbl": "eng", "esb-oauth": "Bearer minted-token-2"} ``` 3. Same config with `oauth_token_header` omitted still sends the minted token on `authorization` (`Bearer minted-token-3`) and nothing on `esb-oauth`, so the default is unchanged 4. `oauth_token_header: ESB-OAuth` with `static_headers` also claiming `esb-oauth: Bearer static-should-lose` yields `esb-oauth: Bearer minted-token-5`, so the minted token wins its own header with no duplicate 5. `oauth_token_header: " "` falls back to `authorization: Bearer minted-token-6` #### Refetch after a 401 1. Arm the upstream to answer one 401, then run the same curl against `esb_custom` 2. Requests recorded in order, refreshed token staying on the custom header while the platform credential is untouched: ``` 0 {"authorization": "Bearer static-platform-token", "envlbl": "eng", "esb-oauth": "Bearer minted-token-2"} <- 401 1 {"authorization": "Bearer static-platform-token", "envlbl": "eng", "esb-oauth": "Bearer minted-token-7"} 2 {"authorization": "Bearer static-platform-token", "envlbl": "eng", "esb-oauth": "Bearer minted-token-7"} 3 {"authorization": "Bearer static-platform-token", "envlbl": "eng", "esb-oauth": "Bearer minted-token-7"} ``` 3. `tools/list` still returns both tools ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - Not yet exposed as a field in the Admin UI form - Custom header keeps `Bearer` prefix, no prefix knob - Config path verified live, DB-stored value only unit-tested Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/da674df654414dabbc98754a496487d2

signal.title: feat(newrelic): per-team New Relic trace routing via team callbacks
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Each team needs its LLM call traces in its own New Relic account - The existing New Relic integration is one global agent, no per-team routing - Team callback config rejected New Relic credentials outright How it solves it: - Team callback `newrelic` now carries `newrelic_api_key` and `newrelic_region` - Traces export over OTLP to that team's account and region - Requests without team credentials export nowhere, no cross-tenant leakage ## User Flow Before: a platform admin cannot route a team's traces to that team's New Relic account 1. Admin sends POST https://litellm-domain/team/{team_id}/callback with `{"callback_name": "newrelic", "callback_vars": {"newrelic_api_key": "...", "newrelic_region": "us"}}` 2. The proxy replies 422 `Invalid callback variable: newrelic_api_key` 3. Configuring `newrelic` with no vars returns 200 but sends the team nothing; the team's New Relic account stays empty After: the same call configures per-team routing, and traces land in the team's own account 1. Admin sends the same POST https://litellm-domain/team/{team_id}/callback body 2. The proxy replies 200; a GET of the same route shows `newrelic_api_key` as `***REDACTED***` 3. A developer on that team sends POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with the team's key 4. Within about a minute the span appears in that team's New Relic account: `FROM Span SELECT name, litellm.team.alias, litellm.cost.total` shows the call with its team alias, model, tokens, and cost 5. A request from any other team leaves nothing in that account, and a caller who puts `newrelic_api_key` in a request body gets a 401 naming the rejected field ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5094 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more - [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.) - [ ] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Shared setup: proxy with one Gemini model, `LITELLM_OTEL_V2=true`, fresh Postgres, two teams (tenant-a with a real New Relic ingest key for account 8412808 via the team callback, tenant-b with no New Relic callback). All completions hit the real Gemini API. ### Before (5290150a05) #### Per-team New Relic callback is rejected 1. `curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:14195/team/$TEAM/callback -H "Authorization: Bearer $MASTER" -d '{"callback_name": "newrelic", "callback_type": "success", "callback_vars": {"newrelic_api_key": "NRAL-x", "newrelic_region": "us"}}'` 2. `422` with `Invalid callback variable: newrelic_api_key. Must be one of {...}` #### Bare newrelic callback silently binds nothing 1. Same POST with `"callback_vars": {}` 2. `200`, but requests export nothing to any New Relic account (the global agent path needs env keys) ### After (1ae5b27b82) #### Team A's real trace lands in its own account 1. `curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:14194/team/$TEAM_A/callback ... '{"callback_name": "newrelic", "callback_type": "success", "callback_vars": {"newrelic_api_key": "", "newrelic_region": "us"}}'` -> `200` 2. `curl http://127.0.0.1:14194/team/$TEAM_A/callback ...` -> `"newrelic_api_key": "***REDACTED***"`, `"newrelic_region": "us"` 3. `curl http://127.0.0.1:14194/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY_A" -d '{"model": "gemini-flash", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Reply with exactly: lit5094-final-1787211946"}]}'` -> `200`, content `lit5094-final-1787211946` 4. NRQL against account 8412808 about a minute later: `FROM Span SELECT name, litellm.team.id, litellm.team.alias, gen_ai.usage.output_tokens, litellm.cost.total SINCE 6 minutes ago` returns exactly one row: `chat gemini-flash`, `litellm.team.alias: tenant-a`, `litellm.cost.total: 0.00045225` #### Team B's request leaves nothing in team A's account 1. `curl http://127.0.0.1:14194/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY_B" -d '{"model": "gemini-flash", ...}'` -> `200` in the same window 2. The NRQL above still returns only the tenant-a row #### Caller-supplied credentials are rejected 1. `curl http://127.0.0.1:14194/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY_B" -d '{"model": "gemini-flash", "messages": [...], "newrelic_api_key": "NRAL-attacker"}'` 2. `401` `Rejected Request: newrelic_api_key is not allowed in request body` #### Provider failures reach the team as ERROR spans, gate rejections do not 1. `curl ... -d '{"model": "gemini-flash", "messages": [...], "temperature": 99}'` -> `400` from Gemini 2. NRQL shows the span with `otel.status_code: ERROR` and the provider's message 3. `curl ... -d '{"model": "gemini/does-not-exist", ...}'` -> `400`, and no span appears (the call never reached a provider) #### Misconfiguration is rejected at save time 1. `curl -X POST .../team/$TEAM_B/callback ... '{"callback_vars": {"newrelic_api_key": "k", "newrelic_region": "mars"}}'` -> `400` `Unknown newrelic_region 'mars'. Supported regions: eu, us.` 2. `curl -X POST .../team/$TEAM_B/callback ... '{"callback_vars": {"newrelic_region": "eu"}}'` -> `400` `newrelic_region requires newrelic_api_key` #### Admin UI (screenshots to be added after merge-base run) 1. Open http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=teams with `LITELLM_OTEL_V2=true`, pick a team, Settings, Add Integration under Logging Integrations 2. Integration Type lists New Relic; the New Relic Api Key field carries the Sensitive badge, New Relic Region takes us or eu 3. Save Changes, reopen: the key reads back masked ## Type 🆕 New Feature ## Caveats (if any) - Requires `LITELLM_OTEL_V2=true`; flag off keeps the legacy agent path untouched - With the flag on, `newrelic` upgrades from the agent to OTLP export (same shape as `langfuse_otel`) - Region is a fixed `us`/`eu` table, never a caller-supplied URL - `newrelic_api_key`/`newrelic_region` are now rejected in request bodies (matches `dd_*`) - Global exporters still receive team spans (LIT-4764, pre-existing, unchanged here) - Masked `***REDACTED***` write-back on team callbacks is pre-existing family behavior - Disable-by-header/team for v2 logger instances misses the registry (pre-existing, same as arize) ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR --- --- > [!NOTE] > **High Risk** > Touches tenant telemetry credentials, OTLP exporter routing, and request-body credential blocking. Misrouting could leak traces across New Relic accounts. > > **Overview** > Enables **per-team New Relic tracing**: a `newrelic` team/key callback with `newrelic_api_key` and `newrelic_region` (`us`/`eu` only) exports that team's LLM spans over OTLP to that account. Requires `LITELLM_OTEL_V2=true`; otherwise the legacy agent path is unchanged. > > Tenant routing stamps the team's ingest key and a **fixed-table** region endpoint onto the New Relic exporter only. Request-body credentials are blocked; proxy-stamped trusted vars drive routing. Keyless exporters are skipped so unauthenticated traffic is not sent. > > Team-scoped loggers (success/failure only) now emit a deferred LLM span when a real upstream call happened, without fabricating spans for gate rejections. Duplicate success/failure closes are deduped. > > Save-time validation on team callbacks and key metadata rejects unknown regions, region-without-key, and per-team New Relic config when OTel v2 is off. Dashboard callback config now exposes New Relic key/region fields. > > Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 64885771d98531a5240d47293e815a32d5399a53. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).

signal.title: [Bug]: Streamed /v1/messages to an openai/ backend never emits a logging callback (AnthropicStreamWrapper / AnthropicResponsesStreamWrapper never thread litellm_logging_obj)
signal.text: ### Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. ### What happened? Streaming `POST /v1/messages` (Anthropic-format endpoint) routed to an `openai/`-provider backend returns HTTP 200 successfully and streams a correct Anthropic-shape SSE body to the client — but **no logging callback (`StandardLoggingPayload`) is ever emitted** for the request. The request is billed by the provider but recorded with 0 tokens / $0 cost, so it's invisible to any success-logging integration (spend tracking, S3/Datadog callbacks, etc). No exception is raised anywhere — this is a silent gap, not a crash. This affects **both** of the custom Anthropic-messages streaming adapters: | Adapter | Backend models | Streaming wrapper | |---|---|---| | `litellm/llms/anthropic/experimental_pass_through/adapters/` | chat-completions-API models (e.g. `gpt-4o-mini`) | `AnthropicStreamWrapper` | | `litellm/llms/anthropic/experimental_pass_through/responses_adapters/` | Responses-API models | `AnthropicResponsesStreamWrapper` | ### Root cause Both `AnthropicStreamWrapper` and `AnthropicResponsesStreamWrapper` drain the inner provider SSE stream and translate/yield Anthropic-shape SSE bytes back to the client — but neither ever receives the `litellm_logging_obj`, and neither invokes the success-logging handler once the stream is fully consumed. This is different from how litellm's other streaming paths behave: - The standard `CustomStreamWrapper` (chat/responses) fires the success handler on stream completion. - The Bedrock/Azure `BaseAnthropicMessagesStreamingIterator` (used for the *other* `/v1/messages` backends) also correctly fires logging on stream end. Only the `openai/`-backend `/v1/messages` streaming path is missing this plumbing entirely — for both of its adapter variants. ### Reproduction ```bash curl -sS -X POST -H 'content-type: application/json' \ -H "Authorization: Bearer <LITELLM_KEY>" \ "http://127.0.0.1:4000/v1/messages?beta=true" \ -d '{"model":"<openai-backed-model>","stream":true,"max_tokens":100, "messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]}' ``` The client receives a normal streamed Anthropic-shape response. No `LiteLLM_SpendLogs` row is written and no logging callback (e.g. a custom success-logging callback registered via `litellm.callbacks`) fires for the request — non-streaming `/v1/messages` to the same backend logs fine, and streaming `/v1/messages` to Bedrock/Azure backends also logs fine. ### Expected behavior `litellm_logging_obj` should be threaded into both `AnthropicStreamWrapper` and `AnthropicResponsesStreamWrapper`, and the success-logging handler should fire once the SSE stream is fully consumed — mirroring `CustomStreamWrapper` / `BaseAnthropicMessagesStreamingIterator`. ### Related issues For context, these are *different* failure mechanisms and not duplicates of this report: - #28595 (closed, fixed by #28985) — a Pydantic `ValidationError` crash in the Responses-bridge success handler. - #32487 — a crash (`'dict' object has no attribute 'usage'`) on **direct** `/v1/responses` streaming, not `/v1/messages`. Both of those are exception-based failures on adjacent paths. This report is about a silent gap with no exception at all — the success handler is simply never invoked for either `/v1/messages` streaming adapter above. ### Relevant log output _No exception is raised — that is the bug. Nothing appears in logs indicating the request was processed for logging purposes._ ### Are you a ML Ops Team? No ### What LiteLLM version are you on? v1.89.1

signal.title: fix(chatgpt): forward prompt cache key
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - ChatGPT Responses requests silently drop `prompt_cache_key` - Session-scoped prompt caching cannot reach ChatGPT Codex How it solves it: - Forward `prompt_cache_key` through the ChatGPT provider allowlist - Retain filtering of unsupported `context_management` ## User Flow Before: a developer sends a ChatGPT Responses request with a cache key, but the backend never receives it 1. They send POST `https://litellm-domain/v1/responses` with model `chatgpt/gpt-5.6-sol` and `"prompt_cache_key": "session_123"` 2. LiteLLM forwards a ChatGPT Codex request without `prompt_cache_key` 3. The request cannot use the caller's intended prompt-cache scope After: the same request forwards the caller's cache key 1. They send the same POST `https://litellm-domain/v1/responses` with `"prompt_cache_key": "session_123"` 2. LiteLLM forwards the ChatGPT Codex request with `prompt_cache_key` unchanged 3. The backend receives the caller's intended prompt-cache scope ## Relevant issues - Related to #21193 and #21209 - Restores the field previously included by unmerged #24983 - Complements #35720 and #37623 - Does not forward `context_management`; live subscription proof was unavailable ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally - [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile Confidence Score of at least 4/5 before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix ### Before (6d47468daeac7ce630c7185f5fed59d02578562e) 1. Run `uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/llms/chatgpt/responses/test_chatgpt_responses_transformation.py::TestChatGPTResponsesAPITransformation::test_chatgpt_drops_unsupported_responses_params -q -o 'addopts='` after asserting `prompt_cache_key` is preserved. 2. Result: 2 failures, both `KeyError: 'prompt_cache_key'`. ### After (025438cffdabf00c67eb2f5b8d94bda3629ca378) 1. Run `uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/llms/chatgpt/responses/test_chatgpt_responses_transformation.py -q -o 'addopts='`. 2. Result: 19 passed, 1 existing dependency warning. 3. Run `uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/llms/openai/responses/test_openai_responses_transformation.py -q -o 'addopts='`. 4. Result: 63 passed, 2 existing warnings. ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - GPT-5.6 Sol/Luna/Terra context-management probes received identical 401 responses - The stored ChatGPT subscription tokens were expired and refresh was unauthorized - Keep `context_management` filtered pending authenticated backend acceptance proof - Codex's documented `/responses/compact` path remains the likely compaction integration ### Final Attestation - [x] The test covers allowlist preservation while retaining existing unsupported-field filtering
