signal.title: perf(ci): measure unit-shard coverage with the sys.monitoring core
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Coverage costs more than the tests on most shards - Shards run Python 3.12, where sysmon is not the default - So they pay for the slow tracer on every run How it solves it: - Ask for the sys.monitoring core explicitly on the shared base - One env var, same lines measured, same tests passing - Cuts the pytest step 47% to 89%, measured on four shards - Records why this and `branch = true` cannot both be on ## User Flow Before: a contributor waits on a required check that is spending much of its time in coverage bookkeeping 1. They push a backend change and watch the checks on their pull request 2. The slowest unit shard, `proxy-infra / Run tests`, takes about 15 minutes 3. The same directory under the legacy no-coverage workflow finished in roughly 5, so a large share of that wall clock is the tracer, not the tests 4. Nothing about the coverage number they get back is different for the wait After: the same check measures the same lines through the cheapest core coverage.py ships 1. They push the same change 2. The shards run with `COVERAGE_CORE=sysmon`, so coverage.py drives PEP 669 `sys.monitoring` instead of the settrace tracer 3. Codecov receives the same line coverage from the same `--cov=./litellm` invocation 4. This pull request's own run against #37586, which is the same code on the same day without the change, is the measurement; the numbers are in Proof of Fix below ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/<your_test_file>.py -v` - [x] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Two things need proving: that asking for sysmon is not a no-op at this Python, and that it cannot be combined with branch coverage. Both are shown against the exact versions CI pins, Python 3.12 and coverage 7.14.0. The wall-clock effect is measured by this pull request's own shard run, since a laptop under other load cannot produce a number worth quoting. Shared setup: ``` uv venv --python 3.12 .venv312 uv pip install --python .venv312/bin/python coverage==7.14.0 .venv312/bin/python -V ``` ``` Python 3.12.13 ``` ### Before (5290150a05) #### coverage does not choose sysmon on its own at 3.12 1. Command: ``` .venv312/bin/python -c "from coverage import env; print('SYSMON_DEFAULT =', env.SYSMON_DEFAULT)" ``` 2. Output, so without the env var the shards get the slow core: ``` SYSMON_DEFAULT = False ``` ### After (e4ffd6535c) #### Asking for sysmon works, and is silent 1. Command: ``` COVERAGE_CORE=sysmon .venv312/bin/python -m coverage run --source=. run.py ``` 2. Output, no warning, so the core was accepted: ``` pos nonpos ``` #### Asking for sysmon together with branch coverage is refused 1. Command: ``` COVERAGE_CORE=sysmon .venv312/bin/python -m coverage run --branch --source=. run.py ``` 2. Output: ``` coverage/core.py:94: CoverageWarning: Can't use core=sysmon: sys.monitoring can't measure branches in this version, using default core (no-sysmon); see https://coverage.readthedocs.io/en/7.14.0/messages.html#warning-no-sysmon warn(f"Can't use core=sysmon: {reason_no_sysmon}, using default core", slug="no-sysmon") pos nonpos ``` This is the open question answered: the two are mutually exclusive until the runners move to Python 3.14. Nothing in this change turns branch coverage on. #### Wall clock, this run against #37586 #37586 is the same tree on the same day with no coverage-core change, so its shards are the baseline. Comparing whole-job durations would be misleading, since a job also pays for checkout, dependency install and Prisma generation, so the numbers below are pytest's own reported wall time from each job's log, and each row states the test counts on both sides to show the same work was done. 1. Command, per shard and per pull request: ``` jobid=$(gh pr checks <pr> | grep -F "<shard> / Run tests" | awk -F'\t' '{print $4}' | sed 's#.*/job/##') gh api "repos/BerriAI/litellm/actions/jobs/$jobid/logs" | grep -E "=+ .*(passed|failed).* =+" | tail -1 ``` 2. Output: ``` budgets before 38 passed, 8 warnings in 432.37s (0:07:12) after 38 passed, 8 warnings in 47.68s proxy-utils before 200 passed, 6 warnings in 429.17s (0:07:09) after 200 passed, 6 warnings in 48.73s core-utils before 1692 passed, 1 skipped, 35 warnings in 209.43s (0:03:29) after 1692 passed, 1 skipped, 35 warnings in 88.58s (0:01:28) All Other Providers before 7742 passed, 80 skipped, 162 warnings in 464.28s (0:07:44) after 7742 passed, 80 skipped, 163 warnings in 245.20s (0:04:05) ``` Same counts on both sides of every row, so this is the same work measured twice. 3. Step-level confirmation that the gain is in the tests and not in setup, for the `budgets` shard: ``` gh api "repos/BerriAI/litellm/actions/jobs/$jobid" --jq '.steps[] | "\(.name)\t\(.started_at)\t\(.completed_at)"' ``` ``` before after 150s Install dependencies 168s Install dependencies 27s Generate Prisma client 11s Generate Prisma client 659s Run tests 74s Run tests 860s TOTAL 281s TOTAL ``` Setup did not get faster, it got slightly slower. The whole difference is the test step. The size of the gain tracks how much work each test does rather than how many tests there are: `budgets` runs 38 tests in what was seven minutes, and it drops about 89%, while `All Other Providers` runs 7,742 fast tests and drops about 47%. Shards dominated by heavy execution under the tracer are the ones that were paying most for it. ## Type 🚄 Infrastructure ## Caveats - Measured 47% to 89% off the pytest step, four shards - Blocks `branch = true` on 3.12; that trade is now documented - Same lines measured, so the coverage number should not move - Test counts identical on both sides, so it is like for like ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signal.title: fix(team): allow no-reset default budgets for team members
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Team member default budgets could not be set to never reset - Team Member Settings only offered Daily, Weekly, Monthly - An explicit null duration was ignored when a budget was sent - The old reset period and reset time stayed on the row How it solves it: - Team Member Settings now uses the shared budget duration dropdown - "Never resets" sends an explicit null duration - An explicitly null duration clears duration and reset time - A null duration no longer inherits the team's own duration - Omitted duration keeps inheriting the team duration as before ## User Flow Before: an admin who wants each team member capped at $100 with no periodic reset cannot express that, and any duration already set is permanent 1. They open https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=teams, pick a team, click Edit, open Team Member Settings 2. They set Default Budget (USD) to 100 3. They open Default Budget Duration and see only Daily, Weekly and Monthly, with no way to clear it 4. Going around the UI, they send POST https://litellm-domain/team/update with `{"team_id": ..., "team_member_budget": 100, "team_member_budget_duration": null}` and get 200 5. GET https://litellm-domain/team/info?team_id=... still shows the member budget resetting every `7d` with a `budget_reset_at` date 6. Creating a fresh team with `"team_member_budget_duration": null` instead copies the team's own `30d` reset period onto the member budget After: the same admin sets a $100 member budget that never resets, from the UI or the API 1. They open https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=teams, pick a team, click Edit, open Team Member Settings 2. They set Default Budget (USD) to 100 3. They open Default Budget Duration and pick "Never resets" alongside hourly, daily, weekly and monthly, then Save 4. Equivalently, POST https://litellm-domain/team/update with `{"team_id": ..., "team_member_budget": 100, "team_member_budget_duration": null}` returns 200 5. GET https://litellm-domain/team/info?team_id=... shows the member budget at $100 with `budget_duration` and `budget_reset_at` both null, so spend never rolls over 6. signal.title: test: add six ruff rules that catch tests which cannot fail
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - `assert False` in a `try:` is caught by its own `except` - Bare `a == b` statements evaluate and throw the result away - 50 such sites in `tests/`, several unable to ever fail How it solves it: - Selects 6 more ruff rules in `ruff-tests.toml`, already wired to CI - Rewrites every `assert False` as `pytest.fail`, which escapes `except Exception` - Restores the missing `assert` on 9 dead comparisons - One test asserted `True == True`; now it tests its module ## User Flow Before: a proxy admin scopes MCP servers to a team, the gateway stops honoring that scope, and no test objects 1. They POST /team/new, then attach two MCP servers to the team through the Admin UI 2. A member of that team lists tools and sees zero servers instead of the two granted 3. A separate developer disables OpenAI container file errors so a missing file quietly returns nothing 4. Their app calls the container file content route for a deleted file, gets an empty body back instead of a 404, and writes it to disk as if it were real content 5. Both regressions land green, because the tests covering them either compare `True == True` or hide their failure inside their own `except Exception` After: both regressions are caught before merge 1. The same two changes are made 2. CI runs the same test files and both go red, naming the team whose servers vanished and the container file that should have errored 3. Any new test written with either shape is rejected at lint time, so the next one cannot reach the proxy either ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally - [x] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix This PR changes lint config and tests, so there is no proxy route to curl. The proof is four mutations: break a behavior a test exists to police, and show the old test does not notice while the new one does. Every command is identical on both sides; only the `tests/` tree differs. The four mutations, applied one at a time and reverted after each run: ``` mcp_team_servers litellm/proxy/_experimental/mcp_server/db.py `return mcp_servers or []` -> `return []` custom_llm_api_key litellm/images/main.py custom_handler.aimage_generation(api_key=api_key) -> (api_key=None) pattern_wildcard litellm/router_utils/pattern_match_deployments.py `if "*" not in litellm_deployment_litellm_model:` -> `if True:` container_file_content litellm/containers/endpoint_factory.py retrieve_container_file_content returns None instead of raising ``` `container_file_content` hits the real OpenAI containers API with a live key: it creates a container, asks for a file that does not exist, and deletes the container. ### Before (4af59d7c6e) #### Team MCP server grants stop working, test still green 1. Apply `mcp_team_servers`, then run ``` pytest tests/test_litellm/proxy/db/mcp_server/test_db.py -q ``` 2. Output: ``` 1 passed, 2 warnings in 1.64s ``` #### Custom provider stops receiving the caller's api_key, test still green 1. Apply `custom_llm_api_key`, then run ``` pytest tests/local_testing/test_custom_llm.py::test_image_generation_async_additional_params -q ``` 2. Output: ``` 1 passed, 3 warnings in 0.04s ``` #### Wildcard routing stops substituting the model, test still green 1. Apply `pattern_wildcard`, then run ``` pytest tests/local_testing/test_router_pattern_matching.py::test_router_pattern_match_e2e -q ``` 2. Output: ``` 1 passed, 1 warning in 0.08s ``` #### Container file errors get swallowed, test still green 1. Apply `container_file_content`, then run against the live OpenAI API ``` pytest tests/llm_translation/test_containers_api.py::test_container_files_api -q ``` 2. Output: ``` 1 passed, 1 warning in 1.53s ``` ### After (634131b34f) #### Team MCP server grants stop working, test now fails 1. Apply `mcp_team_servers` and run the same command: ``` pytest tests/test_litellm/proxy/db/mcp_server/test_db.py -q ``` 2. Output: ``` ____________ test_fetch_mcp_servers_by_team[team_record4-expected4] ____________ 1 failed, 4 passed, 2 warnings in 1.96s ``` #### Custom provider stops receiving the caller's api_key, test now fails 1. Apply `custom_llm_api_key` and run the same command: ``` pytest tests/local_testing/test_custom_llm.py::test_image_generation_async_additional_params -q ``` 2. Output: ``` > assert mock_client.call_args.kwargs["api_key"] == "my-api-key" E AssertionError: assert None == 'my-api-key' 1 failed, 3 warnings in 0.10s ``` #### Wildcard routing stops substituting the model, test now fails 1. Apply `pattern_wildcard` and run the same command: ``` pytest tests/local_testing/test_router_pattern_matching.py::test_router_pattern_match_e2e -q ``` 2. Output: ``` > assert request_body["model"] == "my-custom-model" E AssertionError: assert '*' == 'my-custom-model' 1 failed, 1 warning in 0.24s ``` #### Container file errors get swallowed, test now fails 1. Apply `container_file_content` and run the same command against the live OpenAI API: ``` pytest tests/llm_translation/test_containers_api.py::test_container_files_api -q ``` 2. Output: ``` 3. Testing retrieve_container_file (expect error)... Got expected error ✓ 3b. Testing retrieve_container_file_content (expect error)... > pytest.fail("Should have raised error for non-existent file content") E Failed: Should have raised error for non-existent file content 1 failed, 1 warning in 2.42s ``` #### The gate is clean and would catch the next one 1. Run the CI step's exact command: ``` ruff check --config ruff-tests.toml tests All checks passed! ``` 2. Same rules on the merge base, for the count this PR started from: ``` ruff check --isolated --select B011,B015,B018,PT015,PLR0133,PLW0127 tests --statistics 27 B011 assert-false 27 PT015 pytest-assert-always-false 9 B015 useless-comparison 5 PLW0127 self-assigning-variable 3 B018 useless-expression 1 PLR0133 comparison-of-constant Found 72 errors. ``` #### Touched files are unchanged in pass/fail 1. Run all 23 edited test files on this branch and on the merge base: ``` pytest $(cat touched.txt) -q 66 failed, 1551 passed, 14 skipped, 22 rerun in 296.25s ``` 2. The same 66 node ids fail identically on `4af59d7c6e`, on absent Gemini, Bedrock, Azure and Databricks credentials. `comm` over the two FAILED lists reports no id that fails only after this PR. ## Type 🧹 Refactoring 🚄 Infrastructure ✅ Test ## Caveats (if any) - Follows #37671, which added `ruff-tests.toml` and F821 - No safe ruff autofix for these six, so all 50 by hand - `test_router_pattern_match_e2e` compared against a model it never routes to - Raises discipline (B017, PT011, PT012) is the next PR ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signal.title: [Bug]: /v1/messages drops the vendor half of `perplexity/perplexity/*` model ids — Agent API models 400, `sonar` silently answers off the chat endpoint
signal.text: ### Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. ### What happened? Perplexity's Agent API names its third-party models `<vendor>/<model>`, so a litellm deployment for one of them reads `model: perplexity/perplexity/kimi-k3`. That deployment answers on `/v1/responses` but returns 400 on `/v1/messages`, with Perplexity rejecting `Invalid model 'kimi-k3'`. The vendor half of the id is dropped somewhere on the Anthropic Messages path, so what reaches Perplexity is a name it has never heard of The same drop happens quietly for `perplexity/perplexity/sonar`, which is already in the shipped cost map. There the shortened name `sonar` happens to be a real Perplexity chat model, so `/v1/messages` returns 200, but it answers off the chat endpoint rather than the Agent API the deployment asked for, and the spend recorded is litellm's own per-token math instead of the amount Perplexity metered I expected `/v1/messages` to reach the same model `/v1/responses` reaches, since both point at one deployment ### User Flow Before a (hypothetical) fix: a developer running an Anthropic-SDK app against a Perplexity Agent API model gets a 400 naming a model they never asked for 1. Their proxy admin adds a deployment named `kimi-k3` pointing at `perplexity/perplexity/kimi-k3` and restarts the proxy 2. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/responses with `"model": "kimi-k3"` and get a 200 whose output text reads `pong` 3. They point their Anthropic SDK at the proxy and send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages with the same `"model": "kimi-k3"` 4. They get a 400 reading `Invalid model 'kimi-k3'. Permitted models can be found in the documentation at https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/getting-started/models.`, naming a model id neither they nor their admin ever wrote 5. Swapping in the shipped `perplexity/perplexity/sonar` deployment hides the failure instead of fixing it: POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages returns 200, but the answer comes back without the Agent API's search results, and https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs records a different dollar amount than Perplexity's own dashboard bills for that call After a (hypothetical) fix: the same request answers on `/v1/messages` exactly as it does on `/v1/responses` 1. Their proxy admin adds the same deployment and restarts the proxy 2. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/responses with `"model": "kimi-k3"` and get a 200 whose output text reads `pong` 3. They point their Anthropic SDK at the proxy and send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages with the same `"model": "kimi-k3"` 4. They get a 200 whose content text reads `pong` 5. The shipped `perplexity/perplexity/sonar` deployment answers off the Agent API on `/v1/messages` too, and https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs shows the amount Perplexity metered for the call ### Proof the bug occurs Config the proxy ran with (`pplx_config.yaml`): ```yaml model_list: - model_name: kimi-k3 litellm_params: model: perplexity/perplexity/kimi-k3 api_key: os.environ/PERPLEXITY_API_KEY general_settings: master_key: sk-1234 ``` Env vars: `PERPLEXITY_API_KEY=<redacted>`, nothing else set Commit: `edbb3429a3` on `litellm_internal_staging` (v1.99.0), started with `python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config pplx_config.yaml --port 43821 --detailed_debug` Commands and their full output: 1. The model answers on `/v1/responses` ``` $ curl -s -D - http://localhost:43821/v1/responses \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model":"kimi-k3","input":"Reply with exactly: pong","max_output_tokens":2048}' HTTP/1.1 200 OK {"model": "kimi-k3", "status": "completed", "output": [{"type": "message", "content": [{"type": "output_text", "text": "pong"}]}]} ``` 2. The same model, same proxy, on `/v1/messages` ``` $ curl -s -D - http://localhost:43821/v1/messages \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model":"kimi-k3","max_tokens":2048,"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Reply with exactly: pong"}]}' HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request {"error":{"message":"litellm.BadRequestError: PerplexityException - Invalid model 'kimi-k3'. Permitted models can be found in the documentation at https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/getting-started/models.. Received Model Group=kimi-k3\nAvailable Model Group Fallbacks=None","type":null,"param":null,"code":"400"}} ``` 3. The shipped `perplexity/perplexity/sonar` deployment (`model_name: agent-sonar`) on the same proxy returns 200 on `/v1/messages`, but off the chat endpoint ``` $ curl -s -D - http://localhost:43821/v1/messages \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model":"agent-sonar","max_tokens":256,"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Reply with exactly: pong"}]}' HTTP/1.1 200 OK x-litellm-response-cost: 5.999999999999999e-06 {"id":"0122f771-c977-4952-b4e3-e217031c637a","type":"message","role":"assistant","model":"agent-sonar","stop_sequence":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":5,"output_tokens":1},"content":[{"type":"text","text":"pong"}],"stop_reason":"end_turn"} ``` The 5 input and 1 output tokens priced at 6e-06 are litellm's own per-token math for Perplexity's `sonar` chat model, not what the Agent API metered ### What part of LiteLLM is this about? Proxy ### What LiteLLM version are you on ? v1.99.0 ### Twitter / LinkedIn details _No response_

signal.title: fix(mcp): let a salt-key-orphaned OAuth credential be replaced by re-authorization
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - A salt-key change leaves MCP OAuth users permanently unable to reconnect - Re-authorizing succeeds upstream, then the proxy refuses to save the token - An undecryptable credential looks exactly like "never connected" in the logs How it solves it: - Refuse the overwrite only when the stored value is genuinely readable - Replace an undecryptable row with the newly authorized token, and log it - Warn on both read paths, naming the user and server, never the value ## User Flow Before: after the proxy admin changes `LITELLM_SALT_KEY`, a developer whose MCP server was already connected can never reconnect it 1. They call `GET https://litellm-domain/v1/mcp/tools` with their key and get `{"tools":[]}` where that server's tools used to be 2. They re-run the connect flow for the server, which completes at the identity provider and hands back a fresh token 3. They send `POST https://litellm-domain/v1/mcp/server/<server_id>/oauth-user-credential` with that token 4. The proxy answers `500 {"error":{"message":"Internal server error","type":"internal_server_error"}}`, with nothing in the response saying why 5. `GET /v1/mcp/tools` still returns `{"tools":[]}`, and repeating steps 2 to 4 changes nothing, indefinitely 6. A colleague who had never connected that server completes the identical flow and gets `200`, which makes the failure look specific to the first developer rather than systemic After: the same reconnect succeeds and the server's tools come back 1. They call `GET https://litellm-domain/v1/mcp/tools` with their key and get `{"tools":[]}` where that server's tools used to be 2. They re-run the connect flow for the server, which completes at the identity provider and hands back a fresh token 3. They send `POST https://litellm-domain/v1/mcp/server/<server_id>/oauth-user-credential` with that token 4. The proxy answers `200` with `has_credential: true` and a fresh `expires_at` 5. `GET /v1/mcp/tools` lists that server's tools again, and calls to them reach the server carrying the new token 6. A developer who has their own API key saved for a bring-your-own-key server still cannot have it replaced by connecting that server over OAuth, so no live secret becomes overwritable ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5892 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more - [x] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Live proxy on Postgres 16, one OAuth2 MCP server and one bring-your-own-key MCP server, both pointed at a stub upstream that records the `Authorization` header of every request it receives, so each leg shows the credential LiteLLM actually sent rather than just the status code the caller saw. Shared setup, run once against the unfixed tree: ``` $ LITELLM_SALT_KEY=OLD-SALT-KEY-lit5892-aaaa # the proxy the user originally connected against $ curl -X POST /v1/mcp/server/$OAUTH_SID/oauth-user-credential -H "Authorization: Bearer $UK" \ -d '{"access_token":"token-minted-under-OLD-salt-key","refresh_token":"refresh-old","expires_in":86400}' {"server_id":"dfc832f4-...","has_credential":true,"expires_at":"2026-08-21T19:51:35Z","is_expired":false} HTTP 200 $ curl /v1/mcp/tools -H "Authorization: Bearer $UK" HTTP 200 upstream MCP server received: tools/list Bearer token-minted-under-OLD-salt-key stored row: KM9BVLt_iwQLuV_9Bn_YrE... ``` Then the salt key is changed to `NEW-SALT-KEY-lit5892-bbbb` and the proxy restarted. The stored row is untouched, so it is now ciphertext under a key the proxy no longer holds. Each leg starts from that state: the setup above is replayed on the unfixed tree before the After leg, so both legs face a row holding the same token written under the same old key. The ciphertext differs between the two prefixes below only because each write draws a fresh nonce. ### Before (d542c82f0e) #### The wedged user re-authorizes 1. Egress for the wedged user, and what the upstream server actually received ``` $ curl /v1/mcp/tools -H "Authorization: Bearer $UK" {"tools":[]} HTTP 200 upstream MCP server received: <the proxy never reached it> ``` 2. The user re-runs the OAuth flow and presents the newly issued token ``` $ curl -X POST /v1/mcp/server/$OAUTH_SID/oauth-user-credential -H "Authorization: Bearer $UK" \ -d '{"access_token":"token-minted-AFTER-salt-key-change","refresh_token":"refresh-new","expires_in":86400}' {"error":{"message":"Internal server error","type":"internal_server_error"}} HTTP 500 stored row now: KM9BVLt_iwQLuV_9Bn_YrE... ``` 3. Egress after the re-authorization attempt, unchanged ``` $ curl /v1/mcp/tools -H "Authorization: Bearer $UK" HTTP 200 upstream MCP server received: <the proxy never reached it> ``` 4. The only trace anywhere, and it names nothing the operator can act on ``` ValueError: Existing credential for user wedged-user and server dfc832f4-... could not be verified as an OAuth2 token. Refusing to overwrite. ``` #### A live bring-your-own-key secret is not overwritten 1. Save a BYOK secret under the current salt key, then try to clobber it by connecting OAuth ``` $ curl -X POST /v1/mcp/server/$BYOK_SID/user-credential -H "Authorization: Bearer $BK" \ -d '{"credential":"sk-live-byok-secret","save":true}' {"server_id":"165c4f40-...","has_credential":true} HTTP 200 $ curl -X POST /v1/mcp/server/$BYOK_SID/oauth-user-credential -H "Authorization: Bearer $BK" \ -d '{"access_token":"attacker-token","expires_in":86400}' {"error":{"message":"Internal server error","type":"internal_server_error"}} HTTP 500 BYOK row before: MdUI-JgO1PDJcBZZ6FHi6Q... BYOK row after: MdUI-JgO1PDJcBZZ6FHi6Q... => BYOK secret preserved ``` ### After (645103d5e4) #### The wedged user re-authorizes 1. Egress for the wedged user, and what the upstream server actually received ``` $ curl /v1/mcp/tools -H "Authorization: Bearer $UK" {"tools":[]} HTTP 200 upstream MCP server received: <the proxy never reached it> ``` 2. The user re-runs the OAuth flow and presents the newly issued token ``` $ curl -X POST /v1/mcp/server/$OAUTH_SID/oauth-user-credential -H "Authorization: Bearer $UK" \ -d '{"access_token":"token-minted-AFTER-salt-key-change","refresh_token":"refresh-new","expires_in":86400}' {"server_id":"dfc832f4-...","has_credential":true,"expires_at":"2026-08-21T19:52:08Z","is_expired":false} HTTP 200 stored row now: C09E9xOSRXbS3HGpMO-tHI... ``` 3. Egress after the re-authorization, now carrying the token that was just issued ``` $ curl /v1/mcp/tools -H "Authorization: Bearer $UK" HTTP 200 upstream MCP server received: tools/list Bearer token-minted-AFTER-salt-key-change ``` 4. The proxy log now says what happened, on the read path and on the write path ``` LiteLLM Proxy:WARNING: MCP user credential for user=wedged-user server=dfc832f4-... could not be decrypted (likely written under a previous LITELLM_SALT_KEY); the user is treated as not connected and must re-authorize. LiteLLM Proxy:WARNING: store_user_oauth_credential: existing credential for user=wedged-user server=dfc832f4-... could not be decrypted (likely written under a previous LITELLM_SALT_KEY); replacing it with the newly authorized OAuth2 token. ``` #### A live bring-your-own-key secret is not overwritten 1. Save a BYOK secret under the current salt key, then try to clobber it by connecting OAuth ``` $ curl -X POST /v1/mcp/server/$BYOK_SID/user-credential -H "Authorization: Bearer $BK" \ -d '{"credential":"sk-live-byok-secret","save":true}' {"server_id":"165c4f40-...","has_credential":true} HTTP 200 $ curl -X POST /v1/mcp/server/$BYOK_SID/oauth-user-credential -H "Authorization: Bearer $BK" \ -d '{"access_token":"attacker-token","expires_in":86400}' {"error":{"message":"Internal server error","type":"internal_server_error"}} HTTP 500 BYOK row before: 8m-wtNbO3hlmJ_ngMZd83x... BYOK row after: 8m-wtNbO3hlmJ_ngMZd83x... => BYOK secret preserved ``` ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Review notes The discriminator this turns on is that `_decode_user_credential` returns a string for anything readable and `None` only when a value can be neither decrypted nor base64-decoded. Driving it over 300 rows per encryption algorithm, written under a previous salt key and read back under the current one, classified 0 of 600 as readable, under both the legacy XSalsa20-Poly1305 format and the versioned `v2:gcm:` AES-256-GCM one, with same-key OAuth rows, same-key BYOK rows and legacy plain-base64 BYOK rows as positive controls Eleven mutants, one per behaviour, all die on the tests added here: restoring the old unconditional refusal, dropping the guard entirely, silencing either read path, warning on every non-OAuth row, attributing a bulk-path warning to a constant server or to the batch's first row, swapping the two identifiers, inspecting the payload about to be written instead of the row already stored, refusing a blank row, and ignoring the caller's `skip_byok_guard` opt-out A blank `credential_b64` decodes to an empty string rather than to `None`, because `base64.urlsafe_b64decode` discards non-alphabet characters and the decrypt helper short-circuits on an empty buffer. The guard therefore tests the decoded value for content rather than for `None`: a row holding nothing is not a secret worth protecting. No in-app writer can produce one, since every write goes through `encrypt_value_helper`, so this only reaches a row edited or restored outside LiteLLM Switching `encryption_algorithm` between `xsalsa20-poly1305` and `aes-256-gcm` never manufactures a false orphan. Decryption detects the format from the `v2:gcm:` prefix before any base64 work, and all four write-algorithm by read-algorithm combinations read back cleanly The sibling `LiteLLM_MCPUserEnvVars.values_b64` column already takes exactly this position: `_decode_user_env_vars` warns and returns empty on a decrypt failure, and `merge_user_env_vars` then overwrites the undecryptable blob. This brings `credential_b64` in line with it Greptile flagged that the read path decoded a failed credential twice. That was correct, so `_decode_oauth_payload` is now split into a decode and a parse: each read decodes once and the warning condition reads directly off that single result, which also let the separate predicate helper go away Greptile also suggested throttling the read-path warning. I kept it per-read deliberately. A process-global once-only flag is the wrong shape here, because the condition is per user and per server and it clears the moment that user re-authorizes: the reported incident had two affected users, and a once-only warning would have named one of them and gone quiet forever. The sibling `values_b64` column takes the same per-read position today. The volume is bounded by wedged users only, and it is the signal whose absence made this take 35 minutes to diagnose `rotate_mcp_user_credentials_master_key` is unchanged. It is the planned-rotation path and correctly skips what it cannot read; this is the unplanned case, where it was never run ## Caveats (if any) - Encrypted BYOK secrets are also unreadable post-rotation, so OAuth can now replace them - Not data loss: that value was already unrecoverable with the key the proxy holds - A pod that boots without the salt key reads every encrypted row as orphaned - Re-authorizing on that pod replaces a secret a correctly-keyed pod could still read - Legacy plain-base64 rows stay readable throughout, so they stay protected - Deleting an undecryptable credential is still a no-op, left as follow-up - `purge_user_oauth_credentials_for_server` still treats such a row as non-OAuth - The dashboard still shows an undecryptable credential as connected, per the ticket ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signal.title: fix: map Anthropic API usage-limit errors to RateLimitError (429) not BadRequest (400)
signal.text: ## TLDR **Problem:** Anthropic returns spend/usage-limit exhaustion typed as an `invalid_request_error` (HTTP 400), e.g. *"You have reached your specified API usage limits. You will regain access on … UTC."* LiteLLM faithfully maps that to `BadRequestError` (400), but per the [exception-mapping docs](https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/exception_mapping) a usage/rate limit should surface as `RateLimitError` (429). The wrong class breaks callers' retry / fallback handling. **Fix:** Add one phrase branch to the shared `ExceptionCheckers.is_error_str_rate_limit()` helper — the same mechanism already used for Mistral's *"service tier capacity exceeded"* right above it — so an error string containing `"api usage limit"` is detected as a rate limit and mapped to 429. The phrase branches are intentionally ungated by status code, so a limit reported under a 400 is still classified correctly. Fixes #37599 ## Changes - `litellm/litellm_core_utils/exception_mapping_utils.py` - `is_error_str_rate_limit()` now treats Anthropic's `"api usage limit"` phrasing as a rate limit. ## Testing Added `test_anthropic_usage_limit_is_treated_as_rate_limit` in `tests/test_litellm/litellm_core_utils/test_exception_mapping_utils.py`, using the exact Anthropic payload from the issue and asserting it is detected as a rate limit even under `status_code=400`. ``` tests/test_litellm/litellm_core_utils/test_exception_mapping_utils.py ... 21 passed ```

signal.title: [Bug]: `content: null` is stripped from assistant messages with `tool_calls` before the provider call
signal.text: ### Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. ### What happened? # What happened For an assistant message carrying `tool_calls` and `content: null` — the shape the OpenAI spec prescribes for a tool-call-only turn — litellm removes the `content` key entirely before handing the request to the provider SDK. Providers that require the key to be present then reject the request. This is in the library, not the proxy: it reproduces with a plain `litellm.completion()` call. # Reproduction (no proxy, no provider, no API key) ```python import json, litellm from openai.resources.chat.completions import Completions captured = {} def spy(self, *a, **kw): captured["messages"] = kw.get("messages") raise RuntimeError("stop") Completions.create = spy # intercept at the litellm -> openai-SDK boundary msgs = [ {"role": "user", "content": "hi"}, {"role": "assistant", "content": None, "tool_calls": [{"id": "call_1", "type": "function", "function": {"name": "f", "arguments": "{}"}}]}, {"role": "tool", "tool_call_id": "call_1", "content": "ok"}, ] try: litellm.completion(model="openai/some-model", messages=msgs, max_tokens=1, api_base="http://127.0.0.1:1/v1", api_key="x", timeout=3) except Exception: pass print(json.dumps(captured["messages"][1])) print("content key present:", "content" in captured["messages"][1]) ``` Actual output: ``` {"role": "assistant", "tool_calls": [{"id": "call_1", "type": "function", "function": {"name": "f", "arguments": "{}"}}]} content key present: False ``` Expected: the message reaches the SDK as `{"role": "assistant", "content": null, "tool_calls": [...]}`. # Where it is *not* happening Called in isolation, these both preserve `content: null`: - `OpenAIGPTConfig.transform_request(...)` - `openai` SDK 2.33.0 — `maybe_transform(...)` and `client._build_request(...)` (inspected the final httpx body) `grep -rn "exclude_none=True"` over the installed package only matches under `llms/openai/responses/`. So the key is dropped earlier in the pre-processing path. # Real-world impact Against a provider whose deserialiser requires the key: ``` litellm.BadRequestError: OpenAIException - Failed to deserialize the JSON body into the target type: messages[1]: missing field `content` at line 1 column 165. ``` The identical body sent **directly** to the same provider returns `200`, as does one with `content: ""`. Only the key-absent form fails — which is what litellm produces. Confirmed against the proxy's own `POST Request Sent from LiteLLM` debug line: `content: null` goes in, no `content` key goes out. Any agent framework on the OpenAI SDK emits `content: null` for tool-call-only turns, so every multi-turn tool-calling conversation breaks against such providers. In our deployment this caused 28 failed agent runs over 8 days and looked like a provider fault, since the error text names the upstream. # Expected Forward `content: null` verbatim. If normalisation is intended, `""` is a safe substitute — dropping the key is not, since the two are not equivalent for strict deserialisers. # Ruled out - `drop_params: true` vs. removed — identical - 1.95.0 → 1.97.0 — no change - `modify_params` / message sanitization — only runs in the Anthropic transformation path - `custom_llm_provider: hosted_vllm` instead of `openai` — identical - `custom_llm_provider: openai_like` — not routable via the proxy (`Unmapped LLM provider for this endpoint`) # Environment - litellm `v1.97.0` (Docker `ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.97.0`), Python 3.13, `openai` SDK 2.33.0 - `custom_llm_provider: openai`, `drop_params: true` - Client in production: Cline 3.0.55 ### User Flow The application is an unattended documentation agent: a scheduled job wakes a Cline agent (v3.0.55) in a container, hands it a ticket, and the agent reads the repository, writes a wiki page or an ADR, and opens a PR. All of its model traffic goes to our self-hosted LiteLLM gateway at `https://ai-gateway.int.ai-in-action.de/v1`, model group `inceptron/GLM-5.2`. Multi-turn tool calling is the whole job — the agent reads files, runs commands, and writes files, one tool call at a time. ### Before a (hypothetical) fix The run dies on the second round trip, the moment the agent sends back a turn in which it only called a tool and wrote no prose. 1. The job starts the agent on ticket `CICD-338`. The agent sends `POST https://ai-gateway.int.ai-in-action.de/v1/chat/completions` with a system prompt, the ticket text, and its four tools (`read_files`, `run_commands`, `editor`, `submit_and_exit`). Returns `200`, body carries an id like `chatcmpl-948cc3d44e4d5cf95cf2dca81de44e8d` and an assistant message with `"content": null` and one `tool_calls` entry for `read_files`. 2. The agent reads the requested file locally and appends two messages to its history: the assistant turn it just received, verbatim (so `"content": null` plus `tool_calls`), and the tool result. 3. The agent sends the grown history to `POST https://ai-gateway.int.ai-in-action.de/v1/chat/completions`. Returns **`422`**: `litellm.BadRequestError: OpenAIException - Failed to deserialize the JSON body into the target type: messages[3]: missing field 'content' at line 1 column 20417. Received Model Group=inceptron/GLM-5.2`. No id, no assistant turn, nothing to continue from. 4. The agent retries the same history twice more. Same `422` each time, only the index in the message differs — observed at `messages[3]`, `[5]`, `[34]`, `[44]`, depending on where in the conversation the first prose-less turn sits. 5. The run ends after ~90 seconds with no wiki page, no ADR, no PR, and no output file. The operator sees only a failed run whose error text names the model provider, so the provider looks at fault. 6. After three such rounds the job stops picking up that ticket at all. It stays parked until someone clears the state by hand. Over 8 days this happened 28 times. 7. Sanity check the operator runs by hand: the exact same conversation sent directly to the provider at `POST https://api.inceptron.io/v1/chat/completions` returns `200` with an id like `chatcmpl-948cc3d4…`. The same conversation through the gateway returns `422`. No security or authorization consequence: no data is exposed, and no user gains access they shouldn't have. The damage is availability — long tool-calling runs cannot complete. ### After a (hypothetical) fix The same run continues past the second round trip and finishes the documentation task. 1. The job starts the agent on ticket `CICD-338`. The agent sends `POST https://ai-gateway.int.ai-in-action.de/v1/chat/completions` with a system prompt, the ticket text, and its four tools. Returns `200`, body carries an id like `chatcmpl-948cc3d44e4d5cf95cf2dca81de44e8d` and an assistant message with `"content": null` and one `tool_calls` entry for `read_files`. 2. The agent reads the requested file locally and appends two messages to its history: the assistant turn it just received, verbatim (so `"content": null` plus `tool_calls`), and the tool result. 3. The agent sends the grown history to `POST https://ai-gateway.int.ai-in-action.de/v1/chat/completions`. Returns **`200`**, with a fresh `chatcmpl-…` id and the next assistant turn — again `"content": null` plus a `tool_calls` entry, this time for `editor`. 4. Steps 2 and 3 repeat for roughly 40 further round trips, each returning `200`. The agent reads, edits, and commits. 5. The run ends after ~10 minutes with a wiki page written, a PR opened on branch `docs/CICD-338-doku`, and a result file the job can read. 6. The ticket moves on by itself. Nothing is parked, and nothing has to be cleared by hand. 7. Sanity check: the same conversation returns `200` both directly at `POST https://api.inceptron.io/v1/chat/completions` and through the gateway — the two agree. ### Proof the bug occurs See "what happened" ### What part of LiteLLM is this about? Proxy ### What LiteLLM version are you on ? v1.97.0 ### Twitter / LinkedIn details _No response_

signal.title: feat(e2e): move record/replay to the provider edge (LIT-5745)
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - e2e replay stubbed the whole proxy, not just the providers - a replay pass proved nothing about auth, routing, cost, or spend - replay even passed with the proxy process fully stopped How it solves it: - record/replay now scopes to the proxy's provider-bound traffic only - an in-process provider edge server fronts the real providers - edge-wired tests register deployments whose api_base points at the edge - record forwards to the real provider and stores each exchange - replay answers provider calls from the bundle, zero provider spend - proxy and database stay live, so proxy regressions turn replay red - drift fails loudly with HTTP 599 instead of silently going live ## User Flow Before: a contributor replays an e2e suite and gets a green run that never touched the proxy, so it certifies nothing the proxy does 1. They start the proxy and confirm GET http://localhost:4000/health/liveliness returns "I'm alive!" 2. They record a spend test with `E2E_FIXTURE_MODE=record uv run pytest tests/e2e/quota_management/spend_tracking/ -v`; it passes against the real provider and writes a fixture bundle 3. They rerun it with `E2E_FIXTURE_MODE=replay`; it passes, but the proxy saw zero requests during the run: every response, key mint included, came from the bundle 4. They stop the proxy entirely and replay again; still green, so a replay pass says nothing about key auth, routing, cost calculation, or spend-log writes After: the same replay drives the live proxy end to end and only the provider is answered from the recording 1. They start the proxy and confirm GET http://localhost:4000/health/liveliness returns "I'm alive!" 2. They record with `E2E_FIXTURE_MODE=record uv run pytest tests/e2e/quota_management/spend_tracking/test_provider_edge_spend_e2e.py -v`; the test registers its model via POST http://localhost:4000/model/new with an api_base pointing at a local edge address, and the real provider's answer lands in the bundle 3. They replay with `OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-fake` on both the proxy and the run; POST http://localhost:4000/key/generate mints a real key, POST http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions returns the recorded completion, GET http://localhost:4000/spend/logs shows a non-zero spend row, and the run passes with zero provider calls 4. They stop the proxy and replay again; the run now goes red at setup with "No live proxy", because replay needs the proxy 5. They break the proxy instead (disable spend logging, or corrupt key generation); replay goes red with "no SpendLogs row" or a 401, catching the regression ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5745 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more - [x] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Shared setup: a scratch database `lit5745_qa`, and this proxy config ```yaml model_list: - model_name: bootstrap-noop litellm_params: model: openai/gpt-5.5 api_key: os.environ/OPENAI_API_KEY general_settings: master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY store_model_in_db: true proxy_batch_write_at: 5 ``` Proxy boot (per checkout, port checked free first with `lsof -nP -iTCP:<port> -sTCP:LISTEN`): ```bash set -a && source .env && set +a export DATABASE_URL="postgresql://...:.../lit5745_qa" uv run python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config lit5745_qa_config.yaml --port <port> --use_v2_migration_resolver curl -fs http://localhost:<port>/health/liveliness # "I'm alive!" ``` ### Before (629d7683f2) #### record 1. Boot the merge-base proxy on port 28353 and record one spend test against the real provider: ```bash E2E_FIXTURE_MODE=record E2E_RESET_SPEND_LOGS=1 LITELLM_PROXY_URL=http://localhost:28353 \ uv run pytest "tests/e2e/quota_management/spend_tracking/test_spend_tracking_e2e.py::test_chat_completion_writes_nonzero_spend_row" -v ``` ``` tests/e2e/quota_management/spend_tracking/test_spend_tracking_e2e.py::test_chat_completion_writes_nonzero_spend_row PASSED [100%] ========================= 1 passed in 66.49s (0:01:06) ========================= ``` #### replay with zero provider calls 1. Stop the proxy and confirm nothing listens: ```bash kill <proxy pid>; lsof -nP -iTCP:28353 -sTCP:LISTEN # proxy DOWN ``` 2. Replay the same test with the proxy down and a fake provider key: ```bash E2E_FIXTURE_MODE=replay LITELLM_PROXY_URL=http://localhost:28353 OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-fake \ uv run pytest "tests/e2e/quota_management/spend_tracking/test_spend_tracking_e2e.py::test_chat_completion_writes_nonzero_spend_row" -v ``` ``` tests/e2e/quota_management/spend_tracking/test_spend_tracking_e2e.py::test_chat_completion_writes_nonzero_spend_row PASSED [100%] ========================= 1 passed in 65.06s (0:01:05) ========================= ``` Green with no proxy process running at all: the run certified key auth, cost calculation, and spend writes that never executed #### replay against a broken proxy 1. No separate run can go red: the replay above already passed with the proxy stopped, the most broken proxy possible, so no proxy regression can ever turn a Before replay red ### After (ef6af5c615) #### record 1. Boot the PR-tip proxy on port 29417 with real keys and record the edge-wired spend test (one real OpenAI call): ```bash E2E_FIXTURE_MODE=record E2E_RESET_SPEND_LOGS=1 LITELLM_PROXY_URL=http://localhost:29417 \ uv run pytest tests/e2e/quota_management/spend_tracking/test_provider_edge_spend_e2e.py -v ``` ``` tests/e2e/quota_management/spend_tracking/test_provider_edge_spend_e2e.py::test_edge_wired_chat_writes_nonzero_spend_row PASSED [100%] ========================= 1 passed in 82.35s (0:01:22) ========================= ``` #### replay with zero provider calls 1. Reboot the proxy with `OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-fake ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-fake` in its env, then replay with the same fake keys on the pytest side: ```bash E2E_FIXTURE_MODE=replay E2E_RESET_SPEND_LOGS=1 LITELLM_PROXY_URL=http://localhost:29417 \ OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-fake ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-fake \ uv run pytest tests/e2e/quota_management/spend_tracking/test_provider_edge_spend_e2e.py -v ``` ``` tests/e2e/quota_management/spend_tracking/test_provider_edge_spend_e2e.py::test_edge_wired_chat_writes_nonzero_spend_row PASSED [100%] ========================= 1 passed in 81.84s (0:01:21) ========================= ``` Neither side holds a real provider key, so a single leaked provider call would 401 and fail the run; the key mint, chat routing, cost calculation, and the non-zero spend row all executed against the live proxy and database #### replay against a broken proxy 1. Break spend writes: add `disable_spend_logs: true` to the config, reboot, replay again: ``` > assert matching, f"no SpendLogs row for request_id {chat.id}; saw {len(rows)} row(s)" E AssertionError: no SpendLogs row for request_id chatcmpl-EEtAp3sE7wu3V9mbDhyhyYFyiydMH; saw 0 row(s) ======================== 1 failed in 195.96s (0:03:15) ========================= ``` 2. Revert that, then break key generation with a temporary one-line patch that persists the hash of a corrupted token (`{**key_data, "token": f"{key_data['token']}-broken"}` at the DB insert), reboot, replay again: ``` E AssertionError: kind='unauthorized' body='{"error":{"message":"Authentication Error, Invalid proxy server token passed. Received API Key = sk-...knNQ, Key Hash (Token) =f5a6af59475670cee7b767db3d6ba86405a11852184867faebf65a14a6cbf66b. Unable to find token in cache or `LiteLLM_VerificationTokenTable`","type":"token_not_found_in_db","param":"key","code":"401"}}' ======================== 1 failed in 75.87s (0:01:15) ========================= ``` 3. Revert the patch (`git checkout -- litellm/`), reboot clean, and replay goes green again: ``` tests/e2e/quota_management/spend_tracking/test_provider_edge_spend_e2e.py::test_edge_wired_chat_writes_nonzero_spend_row PASSED [100%] ========================= 1 passed in 80.69s (0:01:20) ========================= ``` ## Type 🧹 Refactoring ✅ Test ## Caveats (if any) - streaming records as one buffered body for now (LIT-5742) - CI wiring for record/replay is LIT-5748 - Bedrock cannot be edge-mounted: SigV4 signs the Host header - multipart bodies miss on replay: per-run random boundaries - only `/model/new` deployments can be edge-wired, not config-baked ones - replaying over a record run's DB rows dedupes spend writes (same response id is the SpendLogs primary key); run both modes with `E2E_RESET_SPEND_LOGS=1` or replay against a fresh DB ## QA runbook - tests/e2e/quota_management/spend_tracking/test_provider_edge_spend_e2e.py::test_edge_wired_chat_writes_nonzero_spend_row - an edge-wired chat billed through the live proxy writes a non-zero spend row, in live, record, and replay modes alike (needs `OPENAI_API_KEY` for live/record, `store_model_in_db: true`, and `DATABASE_URL` plus `E2E_RESET_SPEND_LOGS=1` in the pytest env so consecutive record/replay sessions do not dedupe each other's spend rows) - [ ] Run it once with `E2E_FIXTURE_MODE=record`; it registers a model via POST /model/new whose api_base points at the local provider edge, sends one real chat, and writes `tests/e2e/.fixtures` - [ ] Restart the proxy with `OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-fake` and rerun with `E2E_FIXTURE_MODE=replay`; expect green with zero provider calls - [ ] To reproduce by hand against the same proxy: POST /key/generate with the master key, POST /v1/chat/completions with that key and the registered model, then GET /spend/logs?api_key=<hashed key> and expect a row whose request_id matches the completion id with spend > 0 - [ ] Sanity check: this test makes sense to add and is not hand-wavey (e.g., assert actual expected spend instead of just spend > 0) or potentially flaky CI note, so the red gate is not mistaken for this diff: the assertion this PR fixes, `llm_translation/test_audio_transcriptions_e2e.py::TestAudioTranscriptions::test_missing_model_returns_error`, passed in every e2e run at this tip, and so did the provider-edge spend test the PR adds. The runs that came back red fell over on one of two things this branch does not touch: `quota_management/spend_tracking/test_spend_tracking_e2e.py::test_streaming_chat_completion_tracks_spend`, which intermittently finds no spend row for a streamed call after its 120s poll, and the shared Jaeger at `jaeger.monitoring.svc.cluster.local:16686` refusing connections, which reddens all of `logging/test_otel_trace_e2e.py` for that run. Separately, `buildkite/e2e-tests` is not one of `litellm_internal_staging`'s required checks, so the red X does not block merging ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR CHECKED: live-pr-risk at ef6af5c615. Harness-only change: no references to the reworked modules outside tests/e2e (repo and docs greps), full e2e suite collects clean on the head, basedpyright over tests/e2e reports 0 errors, and record/replay plus three broken-proxy red runs were driven live on a real proxy, database, and provider. The only branch commit since the previous pass at 367dd537b9 loosens one assertion inside a single test file and exports nothing, so it adds no dependents of its own - [x] ef6af5c615 passes flake test (ran 6 times). Two builds came back fully green, two hit the pre-existing streaming-spend flake, and two hit the shared Jaeger being down. The assertion this PR fixes and the provider-edge spend test it adds passed in all six <!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY --> --- > [!NOTE] > **Medium Risk** > Harness-only change (no product code), but it rewrites the record/replay contract: replay now depends on a live proxy/DB, a new HTTP edge, and a v2 bundle format. Mis-wiring or leftover spend rows can silently fail spend assertions. > > **Overview** > Moves e2e record/replay off the test-to-proxy `Transport` and onto a local **provider edge**, so replay still drives a live proxy and database. Only the proxy→provider hop is recorded or served from the bundle; key auth, routing, cost, and spend-log writes execute for real. > > `fixture_transport.py` is gone. Mode parsing lives in `fixture_mode.py`. `provider_edge.py` boots an in-process HTTP server that mounts OpenAI/Anthropic, forwards in record, and answers from the bundle in replay. Tests opt in by registering `/model/new` with `provider_edge_base(...)`. Replay misses return HTTP 599 (never fall through live). Bundle format is now raw HTTP (v2): no request headers on disk, responses as status + filtered headers + base64 body. > > Replay always requires a live proxy. Documented caveats: spend-log PK reuse (use `E2E_RESET_SPEND_LOGS=1` or a fresh DB), no Bedrock/SigV4, no multipart, streaming still buffered (LIT-5742). Reference test: `test_provider_edge_spend_e2e.py`. Also loosens the missing-model transcription 400 assertion. > > <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit ef6af5c615815592da85e26315b6212046ba82ba. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup> <!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY --> - [x] 367dd537b9 passes /live-pr-risk

signal.title: fix(guardrails): honour mode=block on all LLM passthrough providers, not just bedrock
signal.text: Fixes #37638. When a guardrail was configured with `additional_provider_specific_params.secrets.config.mode: block`, it correctly blocked on `/chat/completions` but silently downgraded to `redact` on provider-native passthrough routes (e.g. Gemini `generateContent`, Vertex AI) because `LlmPassthroughRouteHandler` returned early without invoking the guardrail at all. ## Root cause `_get_provider_handlers()` only contained an entry for `"bedrock"`. For every other provider, both `process_input_messages` and `process_output_response` returned the original data unchanged — the guardrail never ran, so `resolve_check_mode()` fell back to the guardrail's built-in default (`redact`). ## Fix Added `_generic_passthrough_handler()` which returns a `PassThroughEndpointHandler` instance — the same generic fallback `BedrockPassthroughGuardrailHandler` already uses for its own non-Converse (invoke) routes. Unknown providers now delegate to it instead of returning early. This fixes the issue for Gemini, Vertex AI, and all future passthrough providers automatically, with no new provider-specific code needed. ## Tests 9 new unit tests in `tests/test_litellm/llms/pass_through/guardrail_translation/test_llm_passthrough_route_handler.py`: - Gemini input blocking (`mode=block` raises) - Vertex AI input blocking raises - Gemini output blocking raises - Unknown provider falls back to generic handler (not skipped) - Bedrock still routes to its dedicated handler (regression guard) - Non-dict responses pass through unchanged ## Checklist - [x] Tests added and all 9 pass - [x] No existing behaviour changed (bedrock still uses its dedicated handler) - [x] Inline comments explain the two-tier dispatch architecture

signal.title: fix(bedrock): forward provider response headers on chat completions
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Bedrock responses dropped `x-amzn-requestid` on `/chat/completions` - Broke request correlation with AWS when debugging - Affected converse (both modes) and invoke streaming How it solves it: - Converse non-streaming now surfaces the provider's headers - Converse and invoke streaming carry them to the caller - Generic HTTP streaming path forwards them too ## User Flow Before: a developer debugging a slow Bedrock deployment can't get the AWS request id back out of the gateway, so AWS support has nothing to look up 1. The proxy admin sets `return_response_headers: true` and points a model at `bedrock/converse/us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0` 2. The developer sends POST http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions with that model and reads the response headers 3. The response is 200 with a normal completion, but carries no `llm_provider-*` headers at all, so there is no AWS request id to hand to support 4. Same thing with `"stream": true`, and same thing again for a `bedrock/invoke/...` model with `"stream": true` After: the same requests come back with the AWS request id in the response headers 1. The proxy admin sets `return_response_headers: true` and points a model at `bedrock/converse/us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0` 2. The developer sends POST http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions with that model and reads the response headers 3. The response now includes `llm_provider-x-amzn-requestid: 836b894b-b89a-40e2-8522-532c4e71f882`, which they can quote verbatim to AWS support 4. Same for `"stream": true`, and for `bedrock/invoke/...` in both streaming and non-streaming, which also exposes the `x-amzn-bedrock-*` token and latency headers ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5145 ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Live proxy against real bedrock-runtime us-east-1 and real Anthropic (claude-haiku-4-5, real spend), `litellm_settings: return_response_headers: true` ```bash # for each of: bedrock-converse-haiku-4-5 (bedrock/converse/us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0), # bedrock-invoke-haiku-4-5 (bedrock/invoke/us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0), # anthropic-haiku-4-5 (anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5-20251001) # and for each of stream=false, stream=true: curl -s -D /tmp/h.txt -o /tmp/b.txt -X POST localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model":"MODEL","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"say hi"}],"max_tokens":16,"stream":STREAM}' grep -i "^llm_provider" /tmp/h.txt || echo " (NONE)" ``` Before, at `1a183efaa1` (base): ```text == BEDROCK CONVERSE non-streaming (NONE) == BEDROCK CONVERSE streaming (NONE) == BEDROCK INVOKE non-streaming llm_provider-x-amzn-requestid: 198e5fda-7d53-45f8-ac22-88e42d9f4a5c == BEDROCK INVOKE streaming (NONE) == ANTHROPIC baseline non-stream llm_provider-request-id: req_011Ce3m... == ANTHROPIC baseline streaming llm_provider-request-id: req_011Ce3m... ``` After, at `9c922f4aa4`: ```text == BEDROCK CONVERSE non-streaming llm_provider-date: Sat, 15 Aug 2026 02:48:57 GMT llm_provider-content-type: application/json llm_provider-x-amzn-requestid: 836b894b-b89a-40e2-8522-532c4e71f882 == BEDROCK CONVERSE streaming llm_provider-content-type: application/vnd.amazon.eventstream llm_provider-x-amzn-requestid: 73fcf3fe-13d0-41cf-9368-e120c4d741a4 == BEDROCK INVOKE non-streaming llm_provider-x-amzn-requestid: f2d37bbb-7413-4927-9105-86eef40587e5 llm_provider-x-amzn-bedrock-invocation-latency: 717 llm_provider-x-amzn-bedrock-output-token-count: 16 llm_provider-x-amzn-bedrock-input-token-count: 9 == BEDROCK INVOKE streaming llm_provider-content-type: application/vnd.amazon.eventstream llm_provider-x-amzn-requestid: d424e810-9c73-4f22-b2df-4d4306694eda llm_provider-x-amzn-bedrock-content-type: application/json == ANTHROPIC baseline non-stream llm_provider-request-id: req_011Ce3mkgiRLu5WtvZdoM3PM llm_provider-anthropic-ratelimit-requests-remaining: 9999 == ANTHROPIC baseline streaming llm_provider-request-id: req_011Ce3mkjmiskvQcvh2fUmYa llm_provider-anthropic-ratelimit-requests-remaining: 9999 ``` Regression tests kill the mutation: reverting only the `litellm/` changes fails all three new tests, and they pass with the fix ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - Invoke streaming now builds its stream eagerly, not lazily ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge signal.title: feat(ui): add and delete auto-router tiers with classifier definitions
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - The tier list in the auto-router forms is fixed at four - The backend's tier_definitions (stacked PR below) has no UI - Custom tiers need a definition the classifier can use How it solves it: - An Edit tiers button after the Reasoning tier - Remove any built-in tier, restore it, or add custom tiers - Every new tier requires a name, a definition, and models - The definition becomes that tier's bullet in the classifier rubric - Going custom forces the LLM classifier and shows a Fallback Tier select - Escalation, adaptive, session pinning, and display names disable with a hint - An untouched tier set submits a payload identical to today's ## User Flow Before: an operator wants a SECURITY_REVIEW tier and the form cannot express it 1. They open http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=models-and-endpoints, Add Model, Auto Router tab, and expand Detailed Configuration 2. The Complexity Tier Configuration section shows exactly four tiers with no way to add or remove one 3. Their only options are renaming a tier or hand-writing tier_definitions in raw config and restarting the proxy After: the same form edits the tier set directly 1. They open the same tab and click Edit tiers after the Reasoning tier 2. They click Add tier, name it SECURITY_REVIEW, write the definition the classifier should route on, and pick its model(s) 3. They optionally remove Medium, pick a Fallback Tier, and see the classifier method locked to LLM with escalation and session pinning disabled 4. Submitting creates the router; the same edits work in the Edit Auto Router modal and round-trip a stored custom config without losing keys ## Relevant issues Builds on #37226 (merged), which added the backend tier_definitions/fallback_tier fields this form writes ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5214 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix UI change; screenshots to be posted from the steps below. Run the proxy from this branch and open the dev dashboard (`npm run dev` in ui/litellm-dashboard, port 3000): ### Before (e2d8fc919f, staging after #37226) 1. Go to Models and Endpoints, Add Model, Auto Router tab, expand Detailed Configuration 2. Observe the fixed four-tier list with no Edit tiers control ### After (687f2ad26d) #### Create a custom tier 1. Same page; click Edit tiers after the Reasoning tier, then Add tier 2. Name it SECURITY_REVIEW, write a definition, select a model, pick a Fallback Tier 3. Observe Classification Method locked to LLM Classifier and the escalation, adaptive, and session pinning controls disabled with hints 4. Submit and confirm the created router's complexity_router_config carries tier_definitions, fallback_tier, and the SECURITY_REVIEW tiers key #### Remove a built-in tier and undo 1. In Edit tiers, remove Medium; a Restore MEDIUM chip appears and the ordinal reads Tier 1 of 3 2. Restore it and add no custom tiers; the submitted payload is byte-identical to a form that never entered Edit tiers (pinned by unit test) #### Edit an existing custom router 1. Open the router's Edit Auto Router modal; the stored tier set hydrates with its definitions and fallback tier 2. Save without changes and confirm the stored config round-trips, including keys the modal does not manage ## Type 🆕 New Feature #### Backend validation dry-run 1. The form calls POST /auto_router/validate_complexity_router_config (merged in #37409) before every save, so the backend's own validator verdict shows inline instead of a raw 400 ## Caveats (if any) - The Usage tab tier chart still lists only built-in tiers - Rebased over the plan-mode override and form-migration merges; the plan-mode tier picker and its guard are custom-tier aware, and the floor tracks the tier row id (like fallback_tier_id) and serializes through the shared custom-tier wire owner, so renames follow and edit saves round-trip it - Consumes #37409's validate endpoint (team-scoped when the router is team-scoped), so form validation can never drift from the backend - Rebased over #37216 (heuristic scorer UI): scorer knobs are dropped on a custom tier set, same rationale as its default-model fallback rule - Rebased over the second form-migration wave: the tier editor is re-expressed with the shadcn primitives - Now UI-only: the backend endpoint landed via #37409 and the keyword hydration fix via #37413 <!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY --> --- > [!NOTE] > **Medium Risk** > Changes how complexity-router configs are built, hydrated, and saved (including a pre-save backend validate call). Mistakes could write invalid routing payloads, but this is dashboard config UI rather than auth or request-path code. > > **Overview** > Lets operators **edit the auto-router tier set** instead of being stuck with the four built-in tiers. They can add custom tiers (name, classifier definition, models), remove/restore built-ins, and pick a **Fallback Tier**. An untouched set still serializes like today. > > A custom set **pins classification to LLM** (derived, not written into form state so undoing the edit fully reverts). Heuristic scoring, rubric/prompt editors, adaptive routing, session pinning, escalation keywords, and display names are disabled or stripped on the wire. Keyword rules and plan-mode floors target row ids/names so renames follow. > > Create and edit both serialize `tier_definitions` / `fallback_tier`, hydrate stored custom configs, and **dry-run** `POST /auto_router/validate_complexity_router_config` before save so backend rejections show inline. Connection tests include custom-tier models. > > <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 687f2ad26dd73807dfbb667458b922a37296d6ae. signal.title: fix(auth): hydrate team model_aliases on the direct JWT auth path
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - JWT team aliases were ignored under JWT-only login - The alias lookup crashed prisma, breaking JWT auth How it solves it: - Carries #37645's alias hydration for direct JWT auth - Sends a plain dict as prisma's where clause - Evicts the alias cache even when one delete fails - Caches the empty result for teams without aliases - Adds regression tests for all three ## User Flow Before: a developer on OIDC JWT-only login cannot use any model alias their team admin configured 1. The proxy admin gives the team the alias `claude-opus-4-8` pointing at `anthropic-haiku-4-5` 2. The developer sends POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with their OIDC JWT and `"model": "claude-opus-4-8"` 3. A team restricted to `anthropic-haiku-4-5` gets 403 "team not allowed to access model", and a team on `all-proxy-models` gets 400 "Invalid model name passed in model=claude-opus-4-8", while the very same alias works with a virtual key of that team After: the same request resolves the alias and reaches the aliased model 1. The proxy admin gives the team the alias `claude-opus-4-8` pointing at `anthropic-haiku-4-5` 2. The developer sends POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with their OIDC JWT and `"model": "claude-opus-4-8"` 3. The request returns 200 with `x-litellm-model-name: anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5`, for both the restricted team and the `all-proxy-models` team ## Relevant issues Supersedes #37645, whose commits this branch carries ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5858 ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more - [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Shared setup, used identically for both runs: a local RSA JWKS on :8099, `enable_jwt_auth` with `team_id_jwt_field: team_id`, one real deployment `anthropic-haiku-4-5` mapped to `anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5`, and two teams whose `model_aliases` is `{"claude-opus-4-8": "anthropic-haiku-4-5"}`, one restricted to `["anthropic-haiku-4-5"]` (JWT in `jwt.txt`) and one on `["all-proxy-models"]` (JWT in `jwt2.txt`) ```bash for f in jwt.txt jwt2.txt; do curl -s -i -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4000/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $(cat $f)" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model":"claude-opus-4-8","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"say hi"}],"max_tokens":10}' done ``` ### Before (9bd43ca125) #### Restricted team, direct JWT 1. Run the loop above for `jwt.txt` 2. `HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized` with `{"error":{"message":"Authentication Error, Type <class 'mappingproxy'> not serializable","type":"auth_error","code":"401"}}`, and the proxy log ends in prisma's json serializer with `TypeError: Type <class 'mappingproxy'> not serializable` #### all-proxy-models team, direct JWT 1. Run the loop above for `jwt2.txt` 2. Same `HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized` and the same `mappingproxy` error, so no JWT request authenticates at all ### After (3954d0d8ab) #### Restricted team, direct JWT 1. Run the loop above for `jwt.txt` 2. `HTTP/1.1 200 OK` with `x-litellm-model-name: anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5` and a real Anthropic completion, `"content":"Hi! 👋 How's it going"`, and the same on an immediate second call, which now reads the alias from cache #### all-proxy-models team, direct JWT 1. Run the loop above for `jwt2.txt` 2. `HTTP/1.1 200 OK` with `x-litellm-model-name: anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5` and a real Anthropic completion, `"content":"Hi! 👋 How's it going"`, likewise stable on a repeat call The original ticket reproduction, captured on `litellm_internal_staging` at 487356733c, returned 403 "team not allowed to access model. This team can only access models=['anthropic-haiku-4-5']. Tried to access claude-opus-4-8" for the restricted team and 400 "Invalid model name passed in model=claude-opus-4-8" for the `all-proxy-models` team, while a virtual key of the same team returned 200 ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - The proxy-admin JWT branch still omits team aliases - JWT proxy admins cannot reach /chat/completions today ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/ecd61fb981eb415e8c64f7da5f5f9813
