signal.title: feat(complexity_router): add business classification rubric preset
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Built-in rubrics only cover chat and agentic coding traffic - Business/sales prompts over-route with engineering-flavored tier criteria How it solves it: - Adds a `business` classification rubric preset to the dropdown - The preset swaps in business tier definitions and business calibration examples - Keeps the same four tiers, so escalation and tier renames still work ## User Flow Before: an admin routing sales and support traffic has no business preset, so routine drafting over-routes to expensive tiers 1. They open http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=llm-playground, Add Model, Auto Router tab, and expand Complexity Router settings 2. The Classification Rubric dropdown offers only Legacy, Chat, and Agentic 3. They pick Chat, save, and send POST http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions with "draft a cold outreach email for a VP of Engineering at a fintech" 4. The classifier routes it to the COMPLEX tier model, and http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=logs shows the expensive deployment served it After: the same admin picks the Business preset and routine business drafting stays on the mid tier 1. They open the same Auto Router form and expand Complexity Router settings 2. The Classification Rubric dropdown now also offers Business, described as suited to sales, support, and go-to-market traffic 3. They pick Business, save, and send the same POST http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions with the same outreach-email prompt 4. The classifier routes it to the MEDIUM tier model, and http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=logs shows the cheaper deployment served it ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [ ] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix QA steps against a live proxy (`python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config litellm/proxy/dev_config.yaml --detailed_debug --reload --use_v2_migration_resolver` plus `npm run dev` in `ui/litellm-dashboard`): 1. Open http://localhost:3000, Add Model, Auto Router tab, pick Complexity Router and the LLM classifier 2. Confirm the Classification Rubric dropdown shows Business with the business/sales description, and that the info tooltip says Business also rewrites the tier definitions 3. Select Business and save; confirm the stored router shows `classification_rubric: "business"` in its config 4. POST http://localhost:4000/auto_router/test_routing with "draft a cold outreach email for a VP of Engineering at a fintech" and expect the MEDIUM tier; repeat with "do we discount to close this quarter or hold price and risk slipping? commit to a recommendation" and expect REASONING Offline evidence: on a 136-case hand-labeled business corpus (2 runs, claude-haiku-4-5 classifier, anchor-lookalike cases excluded), this preset scores 87.3% accuracy with 9.4% over-routing versus 81.6% and 13.1% for legacy, and 77.0%/73.4% accuracy for chat/agentic on the same corpus ## Type 🆕 New Feature ## Caveats (if any) - Corpus labels are hand-authored; shadow eval recommended before defaulting anyone to it - Business is the only preset that swaps tier criteria; legacy, chat, and agentic prompts are byte-identical to before ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/c9cfad97660c420a8f7090a7685fac0f <!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY --> --- > [!NOTE] > <sup>[Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) is generating a summary for commit 7c6dc20021e7806796d89de6c1410639eba9dba6. signal.title: feat(ui): serve a dark-mode variant of the LiteLLM logo
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Dark mode shows the sidebar logo inside a white slab - The bundled logo is a JPEG, so it carries no transparency - Its near-black wordmark would vanish if simply made transparent How it solves it: - Ships a transparent dark logo with a light wordmark - `/get_image?theme=dark` serves it, default response untouched - The sidebar renders both and swaps on the `dark` class ## User Flow Before: someone viewing the Admin UI with dark styling on sees the logo boxed in bright white, so the sidebar header looks broken 1. They open http://localhost:4000/ui/ with dark styling applied 2. The sidebar header shows the LiteLLM logo sitting inside a bright white rectangle against the dark sidebar 3. They ask the proxy for a dark logo at http://localhost:4000/get_image?theme=dark and get the same white-background JPEG back After: the logo sits directly on the dark sidebar with no box, and light mode is untouched 1. They open http://localhost:4000/ui/ with dark styling applied 2. The sidebar header shows the mark and a light "LiteLLM" wordmark straight on the dark sidebar, no white rectangle 3. http://localhost:4000/get_image?theme=dark now returns a transparent PNG 4. They turn dark styling off and the original logo comes back exactly as it was 5. An admin who set their own logo through `UI_LOGO_PATH` keeps seeing that logo in both modes ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more - [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Shared setup: a proxy booted from the checkout at each commit, no config changes, listening on `http://localhost:4001` ### Before (d2d158f271) #### Asking the proxy for a dark logo 1. `curl -s -D - -o /tmp/dark.out "http://localhost:4001/get_image?theme=dark"` ``` HTTP/1.1 200 OK content-type: image/jpeg content-length: 24694 ``` 2. `file /tmp/dark.out` ``` /tmp/dark.out: JPEG image data, JFIF standard 1.01, ... 1000x257, components 3 ``` Three components means R, G and B with no alpha, so the white background is baked into every pixel and there is nothing a dark sidebar can show through #### Admin UI sidebar 1. Screenshot pending ### After (f3885f6296) #### Asking the proxy for a dark logo 1. `curl -s -D - -o /tmp/dark.out "http://localhost:4001/get_image?theme=dark"` ``` HTTP/1.1 200 OK content-type: image/png content-length: 35771 ``` 2. `file /tmp/dark.out` ``` /tmp/dark.out: PNG image data, 1000 x 257, 8-bit/color RGBA, non-interlaced ``` RGBA, and the same 1000x257 as the light logo, so swapping between them cannot shift the sidebar header 3. The default response is unchanged: `curl -s -D - -o /tmp/light.out "http://localhost:4001/get_image"` ``` HTTP/1.1 200 OK content-type: image/jpeg content-length: 24694 ``` 4. `cmp /tmp/dark_before.out /tmp/light.out` exits silently, so what this build serves by default is byte for byte what the base served #### Admin UI sidebar 1. Screenshot pending ## Type 🆕 New Feature ## Caveats (if any) - No dark mode toggle ships yet, so this lands ahead of it - A custom `UI_LOGO_PATH` has no dark variant, follow-up PR - Dark asset derived from the JPEG, no vector source available - `?theme=` rejects anything but `light` and `dark` with 422 ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signal.title: feat(cli): store the lite login credential in the OS keychain
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - `lite login` writes the proxy credential to a cleartext file - Any process running as the user can read it - `~/.litellm` was created traversable by other accounts How it solves it: - The credential now lives in the OS keychain - The token file keeps only non-secret metadata - Headless boxes fall back to a private file - Credentials from an older `lite` keep working - A `--pkce` refresh token is not moved yet, see Caveats ## User Flow Before: a developer signs in to their company gateway, and the credential that grants their whole role sits in a cleartext file, so any program running as them can lift it and spend against their account 1. The developer runs `lite --base-url https://litellm-domain login`, finishes SSO in the browser, and sees `Login successful!` 2. They run `lite models list` and get their model list back 3. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions through the CLI and get a 200 with a completion 4. They check the directory holding the credential with `ls -ld ~/.litellm` and see `drwxr-xr-x`, traversable by other accounts on the box 5. They run `cat ~/.litellm/token.json` and read the credential itself in the clear, in a `key` field next to their gateway URL and user id 6. The developer runs `lite --base-url https://litellm-domain login`, finishes SSO in the browser, and sees `Login successful!` followed by `Credential stored in your OS keychain.` 2. They run `lite models list` and get their model list back 3. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions through the CLI and get a 200 with a completion 4. They check the directory with `ls -ld ~/.litellm` and see `drwx------`, reachable only by them 5. They run `cat ~/.litellm/token.json` and see only their gateway URL, user id, role, and sign-in time; there is no credential in the file 6. A build script or editor extension reading `~/.litellm/token.json` finds no credential, and the request it sends without one comes back 401 7. They run `security find-generic-password -s litellm-cli -a credential -w` on macOS, or open Credential Manager on Windows, and the credential is there, held by the OS keychain 8. On a headless Linux box with no keychain available, the same login prints that it stored the credential in the file instead, and everything keeps working, with the file readable only by the developer 9. A developer whose last sign-in was on an older `lite` is not asked to sign in again: their existing credential still authenticates on the next command, moves into the keychain, and is wiped from the file 10. `lite logout` clears the keychain entry as well as the file, and warns rather than reporting success if the keychain refuses to release it 11. On a box where `~/.litellm` will accept no new file, `lite logout` still prints `Logged out successfully`, and `cat ~/.litellm/token.json` shows the credential gone, instead of handing the developer instructions to delete the file themselves 12. When the keychain holds the credential but will not release it, `lite whoami` opens with `Signed in, but the credential cannot be read` rather than `Authenticated`, so the developer knows why their next request fails 13. Setting `LITELLM_PROXY_API_KEY` or passing `--api-key` still wins over the stored credential, unchanged 14. On a box where `~/.litellm/token.json` cannot be replaced, a fresh `lite login` still takes effect: the CLI says the file could not be replaced, and the next command authenticates with the credential just minted rather than the superseded one the file still names, and that still holds when the machine's clock has moved backwards since the previous sign-in 15. A developer who signs in with `lite login --pkce` instead gets the same result: `Credential stored in your OS keychain.`, and no key in `~/.litellm/token.json` 16. A day later their key has expired, and the next `lite` command renews it without asking; the renewed key goes into the keychain too, so `cat ~/.litellm/token.json` still shows no key 17. `lite logout` on that credential sends POST https://litellm-domain/revoke first, so the refresh token stops working on the server as well as disappearing from the machine 18. Unlock your keychain and run 'lite logout' again to clear it. --- the entry the keychain would not give up is still there --- keys still held: ['credential-preflight', 'credential'] $ ls -A $HOME/.litellm (the file half was still cleared) ########## E5. whoami WHEN THE KEYCHAIN HOLDS THE CREDENTIAL BUT WILL NOT READ IT ########## signed in; the credential is in the stub keychain, token.json has no key: base_url: 'http://localhost:9714' user_id: 'qa5855_run8_user' user_email: 'unknown' user_role: 'cli' auth_header_name: 'Authorization' jwt_token: '' timestamp: 1787249850.129784 now the same keychain refuses every read $ lite whoami Signed in, but the credential cannot be read User Email: unknown User ID: qa5855_run8_user User Role: cli Token age: 0.0 hours Your credential is in your OS keychain, which could not be read. Unlock it, or run 'lite login' to start over. $ lite auth print-token Your credential is in your OS keychain, which could not be read. Unlock it, or run 'lite login' to start over. ########## E6. THE SLOT IS ONE PER OS USER, NOT ONE PER $HOME ########## slot after clean: security: SecKeychainSearchCopyNext: The specified item could not be found in the keychain. signed in under $HOME=.../home_E6a keychain blob key: LX4_4ZY4YRjO...REDACTED... now a second $HOME with no token.json of its own $ ls -A $HOME/.litellm ls: $QA/home_E6b/.litellm: No such file or directory (no ~/.litellm at all) $ lite whoami Not authenticated. Run 'lite login' to authenticate. and a logout from this second $HOME clears the first one's credential $ lite logout Logged out successfully. Authentication token cleared. slot: security: SecKeychainSearchCopyNext: The specified item could not be found in the keychain. $ lite whoami (back in the first $HOME) Not authenticated. Run 'lite login' to authenticate. EDGES DONE ``` </details> Reading those in order: - **E1**, the kill switch. `LITELLM_CLI_DISABLE_KEYRING=1` keeps the credential in the owner-only file and never touches the machine keychain, and login says so by name. Logout blanks the secret out of the file but leaves the metadata behind and warns, because with the keychain switched off it cannot confirm that an earlier login left nothing there - **E2**, a backend that accepts writes and keeps nothing. Login reads the value back, finds it gone, falls back to the file, and names the fix. `whoami` and a real request both work - **E3**, migration. A `token.json` carrying a key in the clear, the shape an older `lite` wrote, is picked up by the next ordinary command: the key moves to the keychain and comes out of the file, with nothing printed about it - **E4**, a keychain that will not release the entry. Logout says the credential is still there rather than reporting success, and the file half is cleared anyway - **E5**, a keychain that holds the credential and refuses every read. `whoami` opens with `Signed in, but the credential cannot be read` instead of `Authenticated`, and `print-token` says the same rather than printing nothing - **E6**, the machine-wide slot. A second `$HOME` does not inherit the first one's session, because the metadata it needs is in the first one's `token.json`. What it does share is the slot itself, so a `lite logout` from the second `$HOME` clears the credential the first one was using, and the first one then reads as not authenticated ### What surprised me - `security find-generic-password -w` hangs on an approval dialog. PR leaves alone. - The 5-second keychain pre-flight is paid per process. PR causes it. - Login still echoes the credential's first 20 characters. PR leaves alone. - A directory at token.json breaks auth despite a good keychain. PR leaves alone. - A logout that cannot remove the file still exits 0. PR leaves alone. - One keychain entry per Mac user, every `$HOME` shares. PR causes it. - A hand-stamped future login makes whoami print negative age. PR leaves alone. - A full keychain volume reads fine and refuses writes. PR handles it. - The `lite` REPL never re-runs its group callback per command. PR leaves alone. - A `--pkce` refresh token sits in the token file in the clear. PR leaves alone. ## Type 🆕 New Feature ## Caveats (if any) - Revoking a live CLI session ships separately in #36846 - `keyring` installs with the `cli` extra - On Linux that extra now also pulls `cryptography` - Headless boxes keep today's file-based exposure - One keychain entry per OS user, not per `$HOME` - A sign-in inherits a stored stamp that sits in the future - A keychain that takes reads but refuses writes costs 5s a command - The SDK getter needs the `cli` extra to reach a keychain credential - A backend that discards writes reads back as not authenticated - A `--pkce` refresh token stays in `token.json` in the clear The keychain entry is one per operating-system user, so two `$HOME`s on the same account pointed at the same gateway now share one slot where they used to keep a token file each. A second `$HOME` does not silently inherit the first one's session, because the metadata naming the gateway and the user is still in the first one's `token.json`, so it reads as not authenticated. What they do share is the slot: the last login wins it, and a `lite logout` from either `$HOME` clears the credential the other was using. Keying the entry per `$HOME` would restore the split, and it would also mint entries that a logout from any other `$HOME` can never find or clear, which is the stranded-credential failure the logout logic exists to prevent. `$HOME` was never a trust boundary inside one OS account either, since that user could already read every other `$HOME`'s token file, so the split was not buying isolation. It stays one entry per user A sign-in is stamped past the latest stamp either store already holds, which is what keeps the ordering of the two independent of the clock, and it costs `lite login` one keychain read before the write it was going to make anyway. A store left carrying a stamp in the future therefore hands that stamp to the next login as well, where before this PR a fresh login would have reset it to the current time. The one thing that reads it is the local expiry shortcut behind `lite auth print-token` and `lite up`, so the cost is that they stop failing fast and let the gateway reject the call instead; the gateway is what enforces expiry either way. Giving the arbitration a counter of its own would separate the two, and it would add a second stored field and a migration for it to close a gap that costs a round trip, so the stamp stays shared A machine whose keychain answers reads but refuses writes pays the five-second write pre-flight on every command that still finds a secret in `token.json`, because the migration that would take the secret out of the file is the thing that cannot finish. The file keeps its copy, so the next command tries again and pays it again. Containers, CI images, `sudo -H`, and service accounts are where this lands, and `lite auth print-token` is what Claude Code calls as its `apiKeyHelper`, so the cost is per request rather than per session. Measured on one such box, `print-token` went from 1.30s and 1.13s before this PR to 6.15s and 6.27s after. Setting `LITELLM_CLI_DISABLE_KEYRING=1` skips the keychain and returns those boxes to the file-only path they were already on. Remembering the refusal across processes would fix it properly, and it needs somewhere to write that verdict down, which is its own change `litellm.get_litellm_gateway_api_key()` reads the keychain now, and `keyring` ships only with the `cli` extra, so an install without that extra cannot see a credential `lite login` put in the keychain and returns `None` without saying why. An install that never had `keyring` is unaffected, because its own login fell back to the token file and the getter still reads it there. The gap is the mixed case, one environment signing in with the extra and another reading without it, and installing `litellm[cli]` on the reading side closes it A `lite login --pkce` credential comes in two pieces, and this PR only moves one of them. The key goes to the keychain, and every silent renewal puts the new key there too, but the refresh token that mints those keys stays in `~/.litellm/token.json` in the clear. A second process running as the user cannot read a bearer token out of that file any more, and it does not need one: it can post the refresh token to the proxy's `/token` endpoint and be handed a key that works, which is the leg above. So `token.json` is still worth protecting on a `--pkce` login, and the exposure this PR closes is narrower there than it is for `lite login`. Moving the refresh token into the keychain blob alongside the key is the rest of LIT-5855 and is tracked as a follow-up; it was not folded in here because the PKCE flow arrived from the base branch mid-review and widening the scope during a merge resolution is how merges go wrong A keyring backend that accepts writes and keeps nothing reads back as `SecretMissing`, which is the same answer a machine that never signed in gives, so `lite whoami` says not authenticated rather than naming the backend. The write path catches this by reading the value back and says so plainly; the read path has nothing to compare against, since telling the two apart needs a write. `lite login` names it at the moment it happens, which is the point where the user can act on it ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR - [x] `5f7c0e1e49c70b030aad11d38dcf82b1f0149a0c` passes /live-pr-risk, with its findings recorded under Caveats

signal.title: fix(otel): route Phoenix traces to per-key/team projects under otel v2
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - otel v2 sends every Phoenix trace to one env-configured project - v1's per-key/team `phoenix_project_name` routing silently stopped working - clients sending `phoenix_project_name` in request metadata got a 400 How it solves it: - key/team metadata project rides Phoenix's `x-project-name` OTLP header - routed spans root their own trace so Phoenix can route them - client request metadata still cannot choose the destination project - evicted routed providers drain in-flight spans before shutting down - route selection and the provider hold are one atomic, locked step - deferred pre_call skips tenant routing until the span actually opens ## User Flow Before: an admin who sets a Phoenix project on a team's key still finds every trace in the default project 1. The admin creates a key: POST http://localhost:4000/key/generate with `{"metadata": {"phoenix_project_name": "otel-v2-routing-demo"}}` and gets back an `sk-` key 2. A developer sends POST http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions with that key and gets a normal 200 completion 3. The admin opens Phoenix and no project named `otel-v2-routing-demo` exists; GET `<phoenix>/v1/projects/otel-v2-routing-demo/spans/otlpv1` returns 404 Not Found 4. The request's chat span sits in the `default` project instead 5. A caller who adds `"metadata": {"phoenix_project_name": "attacker-project"}` to their request body gets a 400 "Rejected Request" even though the value was never honored After: the same key now sends its LLM spans to the named project 1. The admin creates a key: POST http://localhost:4000/key/generate with `{"metadata": {"phoenix_project_name": "otel-v2-routing-demo"}}` and gets back an `sk-` key 2. A developer sends POST http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions with that key and gets a normal 200 completion 3. Phoenix now shows a project named `otel-v2-routing-demo` containing that request's chat span; the same works for /v1/messages and /v1/responses 4. Requests on keys without a project name keep landing in the `default` project, controlled by `PHOENIX_PROJECT_NAME` 5. A caller who adds `"metadata": {"phoenix_project_name": "attacker-project"}` to their request body gets a normal 200, the value is ignored, and no `attacker-project` ever appears in Phoenix ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix All runs against a live proxy (`LITELLM_OTEL_V2=true`, callbacks `["arize_phoenix"]`, Phoenix Cloud via `PHOENIX_COLLECTOR_HTTP_ENDPOINT`/`PHOENIX_API_KEY`, `PHOENIX_PROJECT_NAME=default`), hitting the real Gemini API with `gemini/gemini-3.6-flash` Before, captured at 32535987e8 (the base commit): ``` $ curl -s -X POST http://localhost:4000/key/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" \ -d '{"metadata": {"phoenix_project_name": "otel-v2-routing-demo"}}' key created: sk-jj7ZYd3Mj... metadata: {'phoenix_project_name': 'otel-v2-routing-demo'} $ curl -s -X POST http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \ -d '{"model": "gemini-3.6-flash", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Say BEFORE-PROOF-32535987e8 and nothing else"}]}' "content": "BEFORE-PROOF-32535987e8" $ curl -s -w "HTTP %{http_code}" -H "Authorization: Bearer $PHOENIX_API_KEY" \ "$PHOENIX/v1/projects/otel-v2-routing-demo/spans/otlpv1?limit=5" HTTP 404 $ curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $PHOENIX_API_KEY" "$PHOENIX/v1/projects/default/spans/otlpv1?limit=5" chat gemini-3.6-flash dc2ac271218a <- the routed key's span, stuck in default POST /v1/chat/completions dc2ac271218a auth /v1/chat/completions dc2ac271218a ``` After, captured at 3bbbe893a2, same key metadata, all three LLM endpoints: ``` $ curl -s -X POST http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \ -d '{"model": "gemini-3.6-flash", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Say FINAL-PROOF-3bbbe893a2 and nothing else"}]}' FINAL-PROOF-3bbbe893a2 $ curl -s -X POST http://localhost:4000/v1/messages -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \ -d '{"model": "gemini-3.6-flash", "max_tokens": 50, "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Say MESSAGES-PROOF-3bbbe893a2 and nothing else"}]}' 200 OK $ curl -s -X POST http://localhost:4000/v1/responses -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \ -d '{"model": "gemini-3.6-flash", "input": "Say RESPONSES-PROOF-3bbbe893a2 and nothing else"}' RESPONSES-PROOF-3bbbe893a2 $ curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $PHOENIX_API_KEY" "$PHOENIX/v1/projects/otel-v2-routing-demo/spans/otlpv1?limit=8" chat gemini-3.6-flash | trace 82ff1a87aec5 <- /v1/responses chat gemini-3.6-flash | trace 1f5ee0f9b9ac <- /v1/messages chat gemini-3.6-flash | trace cb0549d6b0c1 <- /v1/chat/completions ``` A plain key still lands in the default project, and a client-supplied project in request metadata is accepted but ignored: ``` $ curl -s -X POST http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer $PLAIN_KEY" \ -d '{"model": "gemini-3.6-flash", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Say FINAL-ATTACK-3bbbe893a2 and nothing else"}], "metadata": {"phoenix_project_name": "attacker-project"}}' FINAL-ATTACK-3bbbe893a2 $ curl -s -w "HTTP %{http_code}" -H "Authorization: Bearer $PHOENIX_API_KEY" \ "$PHOENIX/v1/projects/attacker-project/spans/otlpv1?limit=5" HTTP 404 $ curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $PHOENIX_API_KEY" "$PHOENIX/v1/projects/default/spans/otlpv1?limit=8" chat gemini-3.6-flash | trace f6b304ab6025 <- plain key and attack calls stay in default POST /v1/chat/completions | trace f6b304ab6025 ``` ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - the request's root/auth/db spans stay in the default project - routed spans root a new trace, linked to the request trace - gRPC Phoenix exporters can't route; the header is HTTP-only - guardrail spans aren't project-routed (no auth metadata reaches them) - providers evicted while still draining open spans are capped at 64; past that the stalest one is shut down and whatever it was draining is dropped ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions signal.title: fix(ui): draw one Per Day savings bar per date on Cost Optimization
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Per Day savings chart split each day into per-page partial bars - Daily bars read near zero while Cumulative showed real savings - Wide ranges loaded page by page for minutes with shifting numbers How it solves it: - Cost Optimization now calls the single-shot aggregated endpoint first - Paginated fallback merges pages by date, so days never fragment - Aggregated endpoint gained include_current_utc_day, keeping today's spend visible ## User Flow Before: a user checking daily savings sees near-zero bars on every day while the running total shows real money 1. They open http://localhost:4000/ui/cost-optimization and pick a month-wide range 2. The page fires GET /user/daily/activity once per 1,000 raw rows, hundreds of requests on a busy deployment, and every card keeps shifting while pages stream in 3. They click Per day on the Savings chart 4. A day holding $5.00 of savings renders as three thin bars of $2.00, $2.00, and $1.00, all labeled with the same date, and no bar reaches the real total 5. They switch to Cumulative and watch the line jump by the full $5.83, contradicting the Per day view they just saw After: the same view loads in one request and draws one truthful bar per day 1. They open http://localhost:4000/ui/cost-optimization and pick the same range 2. The page fires one GET /user/daily/activity/aggregated request that returns each day already summed, and the cards land on their final values immediately 3. They click Per day on the Savings chart 4. The $5.00 day renders as a single $5.00 bar, and the daily bars visibly add up to the Cumulative total 5. Spend recorded today keeps appearing through the evening for callers west of UTC, matching what the paginated path already guaranteed ## Relevant issues - Fixes the Cost Optimization Per Day chart drawing one partial bar per API page instead of one bar per day (Pylon #7383) - Switches the page to the aggregated endpoint, one request instead of hundreds, and merges the paginated fallback by date - Adds include_current_utc_day to /user/daily/activity/aggregated so the switch cannot regress the stale-evening fix from #36051 ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5818 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more - [x] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Setup: seeded LiteLLM_DailyUserSpend with 2,500 rows on 2026-08-16 at $0.002 compression savings each ($5.00 total), 500 rows on 2026-08-15 at $0.001 each ($0.50), and one row in today's UTC bucket 2026-08-20 at $0.333, then ran a live proxy on localhost:4000 backed by real Postgres ### Before (fad8116cdc) #### Per Day chart splits a day into per-page partial bars 1. Page the endpoint the way the UI does: `for p in 1 2 3; do curl -s "http://localhost:4000/user/daily/activity?start_date=2026-08-10&end_date=2026-08-17&page=$p&page_size=1000&timezone=420&include_current_utc_day=true" -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234"; done` 2. Observed: page 1 returns date 2026-08-16 with compression_savings_spend 2.0, page 2 returns 2026-08-16 again with 2.0, page 3 returns 2026-08-16 with 1.0 plus 2026-08-15 with 0.5, so the same date arrives three times with partial sums 3. Open http://localhost:4000/ui/cost-optimization, click Per day on the Savings chart: the x axis reads Aug 15, Aug 15, Aug 16, Aug 16, Aug 16, Aug 20, the y axis caps at $2.20, no bar reaches the day's real $5.00, while Total saved reads $5.83 #### Aggregated endpoint ignores include_current_utc_day 1. `curl -s "http://localhost:4000/user/daily/activity/aggregated?start_date=2026-08-15&end_date=2026-08-19&timezone=1020&include_current_utc_day=true" -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234"` (capture ran after 12:00 UTC, so a synthetic offset larger than any real timezone forces the caller-local date behind UTC; real offsets are pinned by the unit tests) 2. Observed dates: 2026-08-16 and 2026-08-15 only, today's UTC bucket is missing even though the flag was sent ### After (27d6b0ddc0) #### Per Day chart splits a day into per-page partial bars 1. `curl -s "http://localhost:4000/user/daily/activity/aggregated?start_date=2026-08-10&end_date=2026-08-17&timezone=420&include_current_utc_day=true" -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234"` 2. Observed: one row per date in a single request, 2026-08-16 with compression_savings_spend 5.0 and 2026-08-15 with 0.5, the numbers the paginated path only reached after all pages 3. Open http://localhost:4000/ui/cost-optimization: the network tab shows exactly one request, GET /user/daily/activity/aggregated?start_date=...&timezone=420&include_current_utc_day=true returning 200, and zero page-by-page calls 4. Click Per day: one bar per day, Aug 15 at $0.50, Aug 16 at $5.00, Aug 20 at $0.33, and the bars sum to the Cumulative $5.83 #### Aggregated endpoint ignores include_current_utc_day 1. Same curl with the flag now returns 2026-08-20, 2026-08-16, and 2026-08-15 2. Dropping the flag from the same command returns 2026-08-16 and 2026-08-15, so historical ranges stay untouched ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - Overlaps open PR #36022, which also merges pages by date inside the same hook - userDailyActivityAggregatedCall takes its two optional trailing args as a named rest tuple: the pagination hook spreads one positional args array into both fetch functions, and this keeps the declared parameter count at four without touching the eslint suppression baseline ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR <!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY --> --- > [!NOTE] > **Medium Risk** > Changes spend-analytics date bounds and how daily metrics are merged for charts. Wrong date extension or merge logic could under- or over-count spend, but auth and write paths are untouched. > > **Overview** > Cost Optimization now loads daily activity from the single-shot aggregated endpoint so Per Day savings charts show one bar per date instead of one partial bar per API page. > > `useDailyActivityRange` prefers `userDailyActivityAggregatedCall`. If pagination still runs, `mergeDailyResults` collapses the same date across pages (metrics and nested breakdowns) so days never fragment. > > `/user/daily/activity/aggregated` now honors `include_current_utc_day` (same live-end UTC-bucket extension as the paginated path) so today’s spend stays visible west of UTC. Historical ranges are unchanged. > > <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit bfe9a693ead9e2a979557e18a65106c7559b8b05. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup> <!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

signal.title: fix(cost): stop double-billing the Azure AI Model Router flat fee
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Azure AI Foundry Model Router requests are billed the flat routing fee twice - logged spend for those requests is ~2x the real cost How it solves it: - when the token-cost path already folded the flat fee into prompt cost, skip adding it again via additional_costs ## User Flow Before: a developer routing through Azure AI Foundry Model Router sees double the expected spend 1. They send a completion whose model resolves to the Azure Model Router (e.g. `azure-model-router`) 2. `cost_per_token` folds the flat $0.14 per million input-token fee into prompt cost, and `completion_cost` then adds the same fee again through its additional_costs hook 3. Their logged spend is twice the flat fee After: the same request is billed the flat fee once 1. They send the same completion 2. The flat fee is billed a single time through the token-cost path 3. Logged spend matches the real charge ## Relevant issues ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Changes `completion_cost` computes token cost via `azure_ai` `cost_per_token`, which already folds the Model Router flat fee into prompt cost whenever it detects the router from the response `model` or the `request_model` (`is_router_request`). Right after, for `custom_llm_provider == "azure_ai"`, `completion_cost` separately computed the same flat fee through `_get_additional_costs` and summed it into the total, so any request where the token path detected the router was charged the fee twice. This guards the additional_costs branch: when `_is_azure_model_router(model)` or `_is_azure_model_router(request_model_for_cost)` is true, the token path already billed the fee, so additional_costs is left unset. The hidden-params-only path (response carries the underlying model, router known only from `_hidden_params`) is unchanged and still bills the fee once through additional_costs. ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix For a pure `azure-model-router` response with 5000 prompt tokens, `completion_cost` now returns a single flat fee (5000 * rate / 1e6) instead of twice that. Regression test `tests/test_litellm/llms/azure_ai/test_azure_ai_cost_calculator.py::TestAzureModelRouterCostBreakdown::test_additional_costs_in_cost_breakdown` asserts the single-fee total; it fails on the pre-fix code (double) and passes after. All 32 tests in that file pass. ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signal.title: fix(streaming): keep reasoning_items when reassembling a streamed response
signal.text: ## Title fix(streaming): keep reasoning_items when reassembling a streamed response ## Relevant issues None open. Searched issues and PRs (open and closed) for `reasoning_items`, `stream_chunk_builder reasoning` and `encrypted_content`: the only `reasoning_items` PRs are #24690 (merged, the feature that added the field) and its closed predecessor #24557, plus #29761, #33931, #35289, #24803, #30216, #21322, #21313, none of which adds a `reasoning_items` branch to `stream_chunk_builder`. #27765 and #28052 are about a raw `reasoning` delta key from Scaleway, a different field. ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added testing in the `tests/` directory: `tests/test_litellm/test_stream_chunk_builder_reasoning_items.py` - [x] I have added a screenshot of my new test passing locally (output pasted below) - [x] My PR passes all unit tests - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Changes `stream_chunk_builder` dropped `delta.reasoning_items` on both of its paths, so the encrypted reasoning state a provider streams back never reached the assembled assistant message. Two independent reasons, both of which had to be fixed: 1. The simple-text fast path (`litellm/main.py`, the `is_simple_text_stream` scan) checks for `tool_calls`, `function_call`, `reasoning_content`, `thinking_blocks`, `annotations`, `audio`, `images` and `provider_specific_fields`, but not `reasoning_items`. A stream carrying only text plus reasoning items is therefore classified as simple text and returns before any aggregation runs. 2. The full path has an aggregation block for each of those fields but none for `reasoning_items`. The assembled message is not throwaway. `_assemble_complete_response_from_streaming_chunks` caches exactly this response (`litellm/caching/caching_handler.py`), and the Responses API bridge reads `msg["reasoning_items"]` off assistant messages through `_get_reasoning_items` to rebuild its input. A streamed reasoning turn therefore lost its reasoning state and could not be round-tripped, and a cached one replayed without it. The fix adds `reasoning_items` to the fast-path bail-out condition and adds a merge block that concatenates the items from every chunk, matching the existing `annotations` and `images` blocks (a provider may spread items across chunks). ## Reproduction, before the fix ```python import litellm from litellm.completion_extras.litellm_responses_transformation.transformation import ( OpenAiResponsesToChatCompletionStreamIterator as It, ) text_chunk = It.translate_responses_chunk_to_openai_stream( {"type": "response.output_text.delta", "delta": "Hello"} ) done_chunk = It.translate_responses_chunk_to_openai_stream( {"type": "response.completed", "response": {"output": [{"type": "reasoning", "id": "rs_abc123", "encrypted_content": "ENCRYPTED-REASONING-BLOB", "summary": [{"type": "summary_text", "text": "Thinking"}]}], "usage": {"input_tokens": 10, "output_tokens": 5, "total_tokens": 15}}} ) rebuilt = litellm.stream_chunk_builder([text_chunk, done_chunk], messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "hi"}]) print(done_chunk.choices[0].delta.reasoning_items) # the item is streamed print(getattr(rebuilt.choices[0].message, "reasoning_items", None)) # ... and then lost ``` Before: ``` [{'id': 'rs_abc123', 'type': 'reasoning', 'encrypted_content': 'ENCRYPTED-REASONING-BLOB', 'summary': [...]}] None ``` After: both lines print the item. ## Testing New test file, run against the branch: ``` $ pytest tests/test_litellm/test_stream_chunk_builder_reasoning_items.py -q ... [100%] 3 passed in 0.53s ``` Same file run against unpatched `litellm/main.py`, to show it actually catches the bug: ``` FAILED tests/test_litellm/test_stream_chunk_builder_reasoning_items.py::test_reasoning_items_are_merged_across_chunks FAILED tests/test_litellm/test_stream_chunk_builder_reasoning_items.py::test_reasoning_items_survive_a_text_only_stream 2 failed, 1 passed in 0.54s ``` The one test that passes both ways is deliberate: it asserts a stream with no reasoning items does not grow a `reasoning_items` field. Regression control, the surrounding suites, run on the branch and on a pristine tree: ``` $ pytest tests/test_litellm/litellm_core_utils/ tests/test_litellm/test_stream_chunk_builder_annotations.py -q branch: 3 failed, 1641 passed, 1 skipped in 44.05s pristine: 3 failed, 1641 passed, 1 skipped in 37.00s ``` Identical, and the 3 failures are pre-existing on the base branch (`test_bedrock_converse_messages_pt_document_various_formats`, `TestIsBlockedIp::test_blocks_ietf_protocol_assignments_old_oracle_metadata`, `test_logfire_logger_accepts_env_vars_for_base_url`), unrelated to this change. `ruff check litellm/main.py` reports the same 76 pre-existing findings before and after, none of them in the changed lines; `ruff format --check` reports both files already formatted. To be explicit about what I did not do: I validated this at the chunk-reassembly level and with the test suite, not against a live proxy making paid reasoning-model calls, so the end-to-end provider path is not something I can claim to have exercised.

signal.title: chore(lint): ban the object.__setattr__ frozen-instance bypass
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - `object.__setattr__` bypasses frozen dataclasses unchecked - TID251 cannot see the bare `object` builtin How it solves it: - New LIT013 flags `object.__setattr__` / `__delattr__` calls - TID251 bans the qualified `builtins.` form too - `# setattr-ok: <reason>` is the escape hatch ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Worth reading first: adding `"object.__setattr__"` to the TID251 banned-api table alone would have done nothing. ruff's banned-api resolves *imported* qualified names through the semantic model, so it matches `builtins.object.__setattr__` but never the bare `object` builtin, which is the only form anyone actually writes (all 5 sites in the tree use it). Verified on ruff 0.15.3 with a config containing both keys; only the `builtins.` line is flagged. So the TID251 entry is here for the qualified form and completeness, and the bare form is enforced by LIT013 in `scripts/check_type_discipline.py`, which is exactly what that checker exists for ("the rules ruff can't enforce") The demo file, a frozen row being mutated after construction: ```python # /tmp/bypass_demo.py from dataclasses import dataclass @dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True) class Row: spend: float def bump(row: Row) -> None: object.__setattr__(row, "spend", 999.0) ``` Before, at `c40828509b` (base). Both gates are silent: ``` $ uv run --no-sync ruff check /tmp/bypass_demo.py --config ruff-strict.toml --select TID251 All checks passed! $ python3 scripts/check_type_discipline.py /tmp/bypass_demo.py; echo "exit=$?" exit=0 ``` After, at `3e48ec5ffe` (this branch): ``` $ python3 scripts/check_type_discipline.py /tmp/bypass_demo.py; echo "exit=$?" /tmp/bypass_demo.py:10: LIT013 `object.__setattr__` writes through a frozen dataclass' guard, so the immutability the type promises is not real; build the final value and construct once, or dataclasses.replace() (suppress: `# setattr-ok: <reason>`) 1 violation(s). exit=1 ``` The qualified form, now caught by TID251 at the same commit: ``` $ uv run --no-sync ruff check /tmp/bypass_qualified.py --config ruff-strict.toml --select TID251 TID251 `builtins.object.__setattr__` is banned: Writes through a frozen dataclass' guard. Build the final value and construct once, or dataclasses.replace(). --> /tmp/bypass_qualified.py:11:5 | 10 | def bump(row: Row) -> None: 11 | builtins.object.__setattr__(row, "spend", 999.0) | ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ | Found 1 error. ``` And the budget gate stays green, since LIT013's ceiling is pinned to the 5 that exist today (4 in `litellm/types/integrations/prometheus.py`, 1 in `litellm/types/utils.py`; both files sit in the `litellm/types/*` path ruff excludes, so nothing there is newly gated by ruff): ``` $ uv run --no-sync python scripts/type_discipline_gate.py OK: every LIT rule is within its codebase ceiling (base origin/litellm_internal_staging) ``` ## Type 🚄 Infrastructure ## Changes `ruff-strict.toml` gains `builtins.object.__setattr__` and `builtins.object.__delattr__` under `[lint.flake8-tidy-imports.banned-api]`, with a note on why the bare builtin can't live there `scripts/check_type_discipline.py` gains LIT013, which walks calls and flags an `__setattr__`/`__delattr__` attribute call whose receiver is `object` (or `builtins.object`). Matching on the receiver rather than the attribute name keeps a class' own `super().__setattr__(...)` or `self.__setattr__(...)` clean; those are cooperative writes through the owner's own guard, not a way around it. Suppression is `# setattr-ok: <reason>`, wired into `OK_SUPPRESSIONS` so a reasonless suppression is an LIT005 as well `type-discipline-budget.json` pins LIT013 at 5, its current count, so the existing sites are grandfathered and any net-new bypass fails the gate; `make lint-budget-update` ratchets it down as they get rewritten Tests cover both dunders, the qualified `builtins.` spelling, the cooperative `super()`/`self` calls staying clean, the suppression working, and a reasonless suppression tripping LIT005 alongside LIT013 Numbered LIT013 rather than LIT010, since staging took LIT010 (Final declarations), LIT011 (argument mutation), and LIT012 (writable TypedDict fields) while this branch was open Worth flagging for a follow-up rather than doing here: ruff's own `PLC2801` (unnecessary-dunder-call, preview) also catches this, and it exempts the one legitimate use, `object.__setattr__` inside `__post_init__`. It reports 21 violations tree-wide today though, most of them unrelated dunders (`__anext__`, `__aenter__`), so turning it on is a bigger call than this PR ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/5b544a28902e4699826c7819dc74d07f

signal.title: perf(caching): skip cache bookkeeping when caching is disabled
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Every sync completion does cache bookkeeping even when caching is off - `convert_args_to_kwargs` calls `inspect.signature` on every single call How it solves it: - Return from `sync_set_cache` before building `new_kwargs` - Memoize the parameter-name lookup, keeping `inspect.signature` semantics ## Relevant issues None filed; this came out of profiling the request path ## Linear ticket ## Changes `LLMCachingHandler.sync_set_cache` builds `new_kwargs`, which is a `kwargs.copy()` plus a `convert_args_to_kwargs` call, and only then checks `if litellm.cache is None: return`. The other three call sites in this file test `litellm.cache` first, and `_sync_get_cache` carries the comment "Check if caching should be performed BEFORE doing expensive kwargs copy". This one site has the order reversed, so a deployment with caching disabled, which is the default, pays the full cost on every completion and then throws the result away `convert_args_to_kwargs` calls `inspect.signature(original_function)` and uses only `parameters.keys()`. A given function's signature does not change between calls, so it can be computed once per function and reused. The rewrite also returns early when `args` is empty, which the old version could not do because it computed the signature before testing `args` ## Measurements Python 3.13, one pinned core, `mock_response` so no network or provider call sits inside the timed region. CPU time via `time.process_time`, reported per `litellm.completion()` call `convert_args_to_kwargs` costs 45.0 us per call. It costs the same 45.0 us whether `args` is empty or not, because the signature is computed before the `if args` test, so a call with no positional args burns 45.0 us to return `{}` With caching disabled, removing the wasted work from `sync_set_cache` takes a completion from 0.8834 ms to 0.8046 ms. That is 0.0787 ms per call, or 8.91%. The two arms did not overlap across two separate measurement blocks: unpatched ranged 0.865 to 0.960, patched 0.799 to 0.819 On a mixed workload, half the calls with caching disabled and half with an in-memory cache enabled, both changes together move per-call CPU cost from 0.93027 ms to 0.82402 ms, a reduction of 11.4%. Run-to-run spread of that measurement is 0.65%, so the effect is about 18 times the noise What this is and is not: these are CPU-time figures for the Python request path, not an end-to-end proxy latency claim. Under real provider latency this is a fixed per-request CPU saving, so it shows up as throughput headroom per worker rather than as latency any single user would notice. I am not claiming a wall-clock proxy improvement ## A note on the earlier attempt PR #14343 proposed the same signature optimization and was closed by the stale bot in December after seven months without review. It targeted `main` rather than `litellm_internal_staging` I would not recommend reviving it as written. It replaced `inspect.signature(fn)` with `fn.__code__.co_varnames[:co_argcount]`. litellm's public entry points are wrapped by the `client` decorator, whose wrapper is `def wrapper(*args, **kwargs)`, so `co_argcount` is 0 and that expression returns an empty tuple. `inspect.signature` follows `__wrapped__` and returns the real 43-parameter signature; reading `__code__` does not. Verified on current staging: ``` litellm.completion has __wrapped__: True, co_name: wrapper, co_argcount: 0 co_varnames[:co_argcount] -> () inspect.signature -> ('model', 'messages', 'timeout', 'temperature', ...) 43 params ``` So `convert_args_to_kwargs(litellm.completion, ("gpt-4o", messages))` would return `{}` rather than `{"model": ..., "messages": ...}`. Positionally-passed `model` and `messages` would drop out of the cache key, and distinct requests would then collide on one key. It fails quietly rather than raising. This PR keeps `inspect.signature` and memoizes its result, which preserves the `__wrapped__` handling ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix This changes CPU cost on the Python request path with no user-visible behaviour change, so a curl against a live proxy would show identical output before and after. The honest proof here is a reproduction anyone can run, plus a regression test that fails on the bug Reproduction, run at commit `23de7a1` before and after: ```bash python - <<'EOF' import time, litellm litellm.suppress_debug_info = True msgs = [{"role": "user", "content": "hi"}] def call(): return litellm.completion(model="gpt-4o", messages=msgs, temperature=0.3, max_tokens=32, mock_response="ok") for _ in range(200): call() t0 = time.process_time() for _ in range(2000): call() print("ms/call:", (time.process_time() - t0) / 2000 * 1000) EOF ``` ``` before (23de7a1) ms/call: 0.8834 after (this branch) ms/call: 0.8046 ``` The two added tests pin the property PR #14343 broke. Applying that PR's `__code__.co_varnames` approach to this branch makes `test_convert_args_to_kwargs_maps_positional_args_on_decorated_functions` fail, and the fix makes it pass: ``` $ pytest tests/test_litellm/caching/test_caching_handler.py \ tests/test_litellm/caching/test_llm_caching_handler.py -q 24 passed, 9 warnings in 0.70s # same tests, with PR #14343's approach substituted in: FAILED tests/test_litellm/caching/test_caching_handler.py::test_convert_args_to_kwargs_maps_positional_args_on_decorated_functions 1 failed, 1 passed ``` If you would rather see this measured through a live proxy against a real provider, tell me which config you want and I will run it and post the output ## Type Infrastructure

signal.title: fix(ui): make hardcoded palette surfaces theme-aware
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Raw palette fills had no dark counterpart - Dark mode rendered them as near-white islands - Dark text on those islands was unreadable How it solves it: - Fills with a matching token move onto that token - Purple, violet and indigo take the dark palette step - Gradient stops get a dark step too - Foregrounds on those new fills take the matching light step ## User Flow Before: an operator running the dashboard in dark mode hits patches of blinding white with dark text they cannot read 1. They open http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=teams and switch the theme to dark 2. The Resources column on every team row shows a bright white chip with dark violet text on it 3. They move to http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=access-groups and the Agents chip does the same 4. Same on http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=users (the key-count badge), http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=skills (purple category badges) and http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=logs (the violet type badge) 5. Opening a guardrail policy at http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=policies and clicking Suggest with AI shows the high-complexity chip as another white island 6. The API Reference page at http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=api-reference draws every doc link on a translucent white pill After: the same operator sees every one of those surfaces sitting in the dark palette, legible at a glance 1. They open http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=teams in dark mode 2. The Resources chips render as deep violet, blue and green fills with light text 3. http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=access-groups, ?page=users, ?page=skills and ?page=logs all render their badges the same way 4. The AI suggestion chips on ?page=policies read as deep purple with light text 5. Doc links on ?page=api-reference sit on the card colour instead of white 6. Light mode looks the way it did before, except four surfaces that moved onto a token and stayed in the same colour family ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more - [x] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) No tests here on purpose. Every line in this diff is a Tailwind class string, and asserting on class strings in jsdom pins the implementation without proving anything a reader can see. The check that matters is looking at the pages in both themes, which the User Flow above walks through ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix ### Before (d7e4b1bdd0) ### After (2f29e63032) ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - Purple, violet and indigo still have no token - The #1e1e1e code slabs stay dark in both themes deliberately - Raw ring colours on already-migrated chips left alone ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signal.title: test: run the 30 test files stranded in the second mirror
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - `tests/litellm/` sat beside `tests/test_litellm/` and ran nowhere - The allowlist assumed a duplicate mirror and left it unresolved - 30 of its 34 files have no counterpart, so they are simply unrun - Not running is why three of their assertions had drifted off the code How it solves it: - Moves 29 into the real mirror and 1 beside the repo-wide checks - Corrects the three assertions the code had moved past - Leaves four files whose twins hold disjoint tests, and says so ## User Flow Before: a test is written, reviewed, merged, and never runs again 1. Someone adds a Vertex text-to-speech test under `tests/litellm/llms/vertex_ai/text_to_speech/`, matching what they see in that tree 2. It passes locally and is merged. No CI job collects `tests/litellm/`, so it never runs again 3. The handler later moves from `data=` to `json=`. Nothing fails, because nothing runs 4. The next reader sees a test asserting the old wire shape and cannot tell whether it is a stale test or a real regression After: the same test runs on every PR 1. The file now lives at `tests/test_litellm/llms/vertex_ai/text_to_speech/test_transformation.py`, inside the `llms` shard 2. It is claimed by a shard's `test-path`, not by an allowlist entry, so `assert-ci-coverage` counts it as run 3. Its assertion reads the body off the `json` kwarg, which is what the handler sends today 4. The next handler change that alters the request shape fails this test in CI ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/<your_test_file>.py -v` - [x] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix The claim is "these files were not running, and now they are." The first two commands establish it, the rest show the moved tests actually pass. ### Before (`litellm_internal_staging`) #### 30 of the 34 files have no counterpart, so nothing else covers them 1. Command: ``` find tests/litellm -name "test_*.py" | while read f; do rel=${f#tests/litellm/}; [ -f "tests/test_litellm/$rel" ] && echo "TWIN $rel" || echo "ORPHAN $rel"; done | cut -d' ' -f1 | sort | uniq -c ``` 2. Output: ``` 4 TWIN 30 ORPHAN ``` #### No job collects them 1. Command, asking the census which job token claims each file: ``` python3 .github/scripts/assert_ci_coverage.py ``` 2. Output, they pass only because the allowlist exempts the directory: ``` OK: 2422 test files and 10 Dockerfiles are each invoked by at least one job or carry an explicit allowlist entry. ``` ### After (b7d3746d59) #### Every moved file is now claimed by a real job, not by the allowlist 1. Command: ``` python3 - <<'PY' import importlib.util, sys spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("acc", ".github/scripts/assert_ci_coverage.py") m = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec); sys.modules["acc"] = m; spec.loader.exec_module(m) tokens = m._invoked_test_tokens(m._all_scalars()) paths = [l.strip() for l in open("moved.txt") if l.strip()] unrun = [p for p in paths if not any(m._token_covers(t, p) for t in tokens)] print(f"moved files: {len(paths)}; covered by a real job token: {len(paths)-len(unrun)}") PY ``` 2. Output: ``` moved files: 30; covered by a real job token: 30 ``` #### And they pass 1. Command: ``` uv run pytest $(cat moved.txt | tr '\n' ' ') -q -n 2 ``` 2. Output: ``` 216 passed, 147 warnings in 103.24s (0:01:43) ``` Before the three drift fixes the same command reported `29 failed, 241 passed, 2 errors`, with 25 of those failures inside one of the four files that stay behind. #### The shards they joined still collect Several of the moved files are named `test_transformation.py`, which pytest cannot import twice from non-package directories in one session, so this is the check that matters. 1. Command: ``` uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/llms --collect-only -q | tail -1 uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/integrations --collect-only -q | tail -1 uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/proxy/management_endpoints --collect-only -q | tail -1 uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/test_*.py --collect-only -q | tail -1 ``` 2. Output: ``` 9240 tests collected in 1.49s 2683 tests collected in 65.10s (0:01:05) 2797 tests collected in 3.53s 2654 tests collected in 65.04s (0:01:05) ``` Without the added `__init__.py`, the first of those reports `9229 tests collected, 1 error`. #### The secret scan still runs, from its new path `test_no_hardcoded_secrets.py` is the one file that did not go to the mirror. Its job runs pytest under `uv run --no-project`, an environment holding pytest and nothing else, and the mirror's conftest imports litellm on collection. It went to `tests/code_coverage_tests/` with the other repo-wide checks, which has no conftest. Verified with the job's exact command: 1. Command: ``` uv run --no-project --with 'pytest==9.0.2' pytest tests/code_coverage_tests/test_no_hardcoded_secrets.py -q ``` 2. Output: ``` 1 passed in 0.47s ``` #### The census is still green 1. Command: ``` python3 .github/scripts/assert_ci_coverage.py ``` 2. Output: ``` OK: 2422 test files and 10 Dockerfiles are each invoked by at least one job or carry an explicit allowlist entry. ``` ## Type 🧹 Refactoring ✅ Test ## Caveats - Moves are byte-identical, so `git diff --find-renames` shows every one at R100 - The three edited assertions are the only test semantics touched - The four files left behind need their bodies merged into their twins, not moved - The secret scan went to `tests/code_coverage_tests/`, not the mirror, since its job has no litellm deps - The allowlist now names those four and the test counts each would bring ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signal.title: feat(ci): catch files a -k expression deselects from every job
signal.text: > #37593 has merged, so this now stands alone against staging and holds only its own four files. ## TLDR Problem this solves: - The census asks whether a job names a file, and stops there - It cannot see the `-k` that job then applies - `tests/local_testing` is globbed by five jobs, all of which drop the caching files - 118 tests run nowhere today while counting as covered How it solves it: - Reads the same jobs and asks whether each globbed file survives its `-k` - Stays quiet on any expression it cannot model, so it never guesses - Records the eight files already in the hole, so the count can only fall ## User Flow Before: a suite stops running and every signal says it is fine 1. Someone adds `not cache` to the `local_testing_part1` and `part2` selectors, to move caching tests to a dedicated job 2. The dedicated job ends up naming three files by hand, and the rest are never wired up 3. `assert-ci-coverage` stays green, because the globs still list `tests/local_testing/**/test_*.py` 4. `test_caching.py` and seven others stop running. Nothing says so, and two years of edits land on tests that never execute After: the same change fails the check that day 1. The selector edit lands in a PR 2. `assert-ci-coverage` runs the new step and fails with each file the change orphaned, by name 3. The author either gives them a job whose `-k` keeps them, or writes down in the allowlist why they may stay unrun 4. The existing eight are already written down, so the list can only get shorter ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/<your_test_file>.py -v` - [x] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix The check decides statically what pytest decides by collecting, so the first thing to show is that the two agree. ### The gap, measured by pytest itself `tests/local_testing` is globbed by `local_testing_part1`, `local_testing_part2`, `langfuse_logging_unit_tests`, `litellm_router_testing` and `litellm_assistants_api_testing`. Running the directory under each job's own selector: 1. signal.title: feat(ci): ratchet tests that skip themselves when a credential is absent
signal.text: > Stacked on #37588, which adds the TQ rules and the ratchet this extends. Review that one first. ## TLDR Problem this solves: - 34 tests skip themselves when a provider credential is missing - On a runner without that key they report green having run nothing - Nothing in CI distinguishes that from coverage that exists - 13 of the 34 sit in `tests/test_litellm`, which runs mock-only How it solves it: - New TQ006 flags a `pytest.skip` reached only when a credential env var is absent - Follows the `key = os.getenv(...)` then `if not key: skip` shape, which is most of them - Seeds the budget at today's 34, so the count can only fall ## User Flow Before: a provider's tests are added, and never run 1. Someone adds a suite for a new provider that calls the live API and skips when its key is unset 2. CI has no key for that provider, so every test in the file skips 3. The run is green, the file counts toward the suite, and the summary shows skips nobody reads 4. Months later the provider's transformation breaks and no test notices After: the same suite has to say what it is 1. The suite lands in a PR 2. `test-quality-gate` fails, naming each skip and the credential it waits on 3. The author fakes the provider at the HTTP boundary, so the tests run everywhere 4. Or keeps the live call and suppresses with a reason, which puts the choice on the record instead of in a skip message ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/<your_test_file>.py -v` - [x] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix ### Before (9dbd5cffc5) 1. Command: ``` python3 scripts/check_test_quality.py tests/ | grep -c TQ006 ``` 2. Output, the rule does not exist yet: ``` 0 ``` ### After (b4b5611c19) #### What the rule finds, and where 1. Command: ``` python3 scripts/check_test_quality.py tests/ | grep TQ006 | cut -d/ -f1-2 | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn ``` 2. Output: ``` 13 tests/test_litellm 6 tests/llm_translation 4 tests/litellm_utils_tests 3 tests/vector_store_tests 3 tests/mcp_tests 2 tests/llm_responses_api_testing 1 tests/proxy_unit_tests 1 tests/ocr_tests 1 tests/batches_tests ``` #### One of them, in full 1. Command: ``` python3 scripts/check_test_quality.py tests/test_litellm/llms/ovhcloud/ | grep TQ006 | head -1 sed -n '185,189p' tests/test_litellm/llms/ovhcloud/test_ovhcloud_chat_transformation.py ``` 2. Output: ``` tests/test_litellm/llms/ovhcloud/test_ovhcloud_chat_transformation.py:188: TQ006 this test skips itself when OVHCLOUD_API_KEY is absent, so a run without that credential reports green having executed nothing; fake the provider at the HTTP boundary, or fail loudly so the missing credential is visible (suppress: `# test-quality-ok: <reason>`) api_key = os.getenv("OVHCLOUD_API_KEY") if not api_key: pytest.skip("OVHCLOUD_API_KEY not set, skipping test") ``` #### The gate is green at the seeded ceiling 1. Command: ``` python3 scripts/test_quality_gate.py ``` 2. Output: ``` OK: every TQ rule is within its test-suite ceiling (base origin/litellm_internal_staging) ``` #### Unit tests 1. Command: ``` uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/test_check_test_quality.py tests/test_litellm/test_test_quality_gate.py -q ``` 2. Output: ``` 61 passed, 1 warning in 1.77s ``` 3. Command, the new ones against the checker without this change, to show they fail first: ``` git checkout 9dbd5cffc5 -- scripts/check_test_quality.py uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/test_check_test_quality.py -q -k "credential or gate or gated" ``` 4. Output: ``` 3 failed, 5 passed, 37 deselected, 1 warning in 0.22s ``` ## Type 🆕 New Feature ✅ Test ## Caveats - The rule is repo-wide, not scoped to the mock-only tree - 21 of the 34 sit in suites that are meant to call live providers - For those the expected resolution is a suppression with a reason, not a rewrite - Scoping it to `tests/test_litellm` instead would seed at 13; say the word and I will - Only a credential-shaped name gates: `_API_KEY`, `_KEY`, `TOKEN`, `SECRET`, `PASSWORD`, `CREDENTIAL`, `DATABASE_URL`, `ACCESS_KEY_ID` - The gate follows one binding, so a credential reached through a helper call is not seen - The condition must test for absence: `not`, `is None`, `not in os.environ` ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

Step labels and body text read light on dark 4. The guardrail, pass, fail and API-failure icons keep their meaning in the dashboard's info, success, destructive and warning colours 5. POST http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions and http://localhost:4000/v1/messages with the same model also return grounded answers, served through the gateway's responses bridge 4. POST http://localhost:4000/v1/search/parallel-search with `"after_date": "2025-01-01"` now applies the date filter, and the response carries `search_id`, `parallel_usage`, and each result's raw `excerpts` array alongside the unified fields ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [ ] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix All captured at commit 7f73ef13 against a live proxy (`--config` wiring `parallel_ai/parallel` and a `parallel-search` search tool), hitting the real Parallel API with a real key ```bash curl -sS -D - http://localhost:4000/v1/responses \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model": "parallel-research", "input": "What company acquired Windsurf in 2025?
