signal.title: test: retire tests/old_proxy_tests, which holds no tests
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - `tests/old_proxy_tests/` holds 20 files named `test_*.py` - pytest collects zero tests from all 20 of them - 16 cannot even be imported in this environment - They occupy 20 of the 88 paths on the coverage allowlist How it solves it: - Deletes the directory and its allowlist entry together - No job loses anything, because no job ran anything there - Git keeps them if a snippet turns out to be someone's habit ## User Flow Before: a directory that looks like a test suite and is not one 1. Someone auditing coverage opens `.github/ci-coverage-allowlist.yml` and reads "Legacy proxy suite superseded by the proxy shards ... whether it still describes supported behaviour is unresolved" 2. They open `tests/old_proxy_tests/tests/test_openai_request.py` to check, and find a module-level snippet calling a proxy at `0.0.0.0:8000` with no test function and no assertion 3. To learn whether it "still describes supported behaviour" they would have to run 20 snippets by hand against a live proxy 4. The entry survives another audit, and the number on the "dead-file allowlist entries" metric stays where it is After: the question does not exist 1. The directory is gone, and so are its 20 allowlist paths 2. The allowlist drops from 88 paths to 68 3. `assert-ci-coverage` reports 2402 test files instead of 2422, and stays green, because the 20 were never invoked by a job 4. Anyone who wants a snippet back takes it out of git history ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/<your_test_file>.py -v` - [x] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Deleting something named `test_*.py` is only safe if it holds no tests, so that is the thing to show. ### Before #### pytest collects nothing from any of the 20 files 1. Command: ``` uv run pytest tests/old_proxy_tests --collect-only -q | tail -2 ``` 2. Output: ``` !!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! Interrupted: 16 errors during collection !!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! no tests collected, 16 errors in 114.17s (0:01:54) ``` The 16 errors are import failures wanting `langchain`, `llama_index` and `google.api_core`, none of which this environment installs. #### Not one of them defines a test 1. Command: ``` for f in $(find tests/old_proxy_tests -name "test_*.py" | sort); do echo "$(grep -cE '^def test_|^async def test_|^class Test' $f) $(basename $f)" done | awk '{s+=$1} END {print "test functions and classes across all files:", s}' ``` 2. Output: ``` test functions and classes across all files: 0 ``` #### What they actually are `tests/old_proxy_tests/tests/test_openai_request.py`, in full at the top: ``` import openai client = openai.OpenAI(api_key="hi", base_url="http://0.0.0.0:8000") response = client.chat.completions.create( model="azure/gpt-4.1-mini", messages=[ {"role": "user", "content": "this is a test request, write a short poem"} ], ... ) ``` Ten of the twenty still address `0.0.0.0:8000`; `--port` has defaulted to 4000 in `proxy_cli.py` for a long while. #### Nothing outside the directory refers to it 1. Command: ``` grep -rn "old_proxy_tests" --exclude-dir=.git . | grep -v "^./tests/old_proxy_tests/" | grep -v ci-coverage-allowlist ``` 2. Output: ``` (no matches) ``` ### After 1. Command: ``` python3 -c "import yaml; d=yaml.safe_load(open('.github/ci-coverage-allowlist.yml')); print('entries:', len(d['test_paths']), '| paths:', sum(len(e['paths']) for e in d['test_paths']))" python3 .github/scripts/assert_ci_coverage.py ``` 2. Output: ``` entries: 9 | paths: 68 OK: 2402 test files and 10 Dockerfiles are each invoked by at least one job or carry an explicit allowlist entry. ``` ## Type 🧹 Refactoring ✅ Test ## Caveats - The directory's other contents go too: five `load_test_*.py`, a bursty variant, two committed log files, an essay fixture and a `.js` snippet - If any of these is someone's manual habit, say so and it comes back out of history - This is deletion only; nothing is rewritten or moved ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signal.title: chore(ci): close the test-census blind spots and move scripts out of workflows/
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Two test files ran nowhere and the census could not see it - A `grep -v` hid them from `assert_ci_coverage.py` - `tests/scim_tests/` held a fixture and no tests - Two plain scripts were sitting in `.github/workflows/` - The agent-shin rollout heads-up one-shot is long spent How it solves it: - CircleCI glob excludes the local-only dir structurally - Those files get an allowlist entry with a dated rationale - Scripts move to `.github/scripts/`, callers updated - Spent heads-up workflow, script and tests deleted ## User Flow Before: a maintainer auditing which tests actually run gets a clean bill of health that is wrong 1. They run `python .github/scripts/assert_ci_coverage.py` and read `OK: 2422 test files ... are each invoked by at least one job` 2. They believe every test file has a runner 3. In fact `tests/agent_tests/local_only_agent_tests/test_a2a.py` and `test_a2a_completion_bridge.py` execute in no job at all, because the CircleCI agent job pipes its glob through `grep -v "^tests/agent_tests/local_only_agent_tests/"` and the census reads only the glob 4. Nothing anywhere records that those two files are deliberately out of scope After: the same audit reports the same clean bill of health, and this time it is true 1. They run `python .github/scripts/assert_ci_coverage.py` and read `OK: 2421 test files ... are each invoked by at least one job or carry an explicit allowlist entry` 2. They open `.github/ci-coverage-allowlist.yml` and find `tests/agent_tests/local_only_agent_tests` listed with the reason it cannot run in a pull request job, the date the hidden filter was removed, and the condition for revisiting 3. If someone later drops a third test file into that directory, the census still passes, because the entry is the directory 4. If someone instead deletes the allowlist entry, the census fails and names both files ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/<your_test_file>.py -v` - [x] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix The change this PR makes to the census is mechanical, so the proof is the guard itself going from a false pass, to a true failure, to a true pass. All three runs are the same command on the same machine. ### Before (5290150a05) #### The census passes while two files run nowhere 1. Command: ``` python .github/scripts/assert_ci_coverage.py ``` 2. Output: ``` OK: 2422 test files and 10 Dockerfiles are each invoked by at least one job or carry an explicit allowlist entry. ``` 3. The two files it silently counted as covered: ``` $ sed -n '1028p' .circleci/config.yml TEST_FILES=$(circleci tests glob "tests/agent_tests/**/test_*.py" | grep -v "^tests/agent_tests/local_only_agent_tests/") ``` The glob matches them, the `grep -v` drops them before pytest ever sees them, and the census parses only the glob. ### After (03b74381b3) #### The census fails once the filter is structural, and names the files 1. With the glob narrowed to `tests/agent_tests/test_*.py` and no allowlist entry yet: ``` python .github/scripts/assert_ci_coverage.py ``` 2. Output: ``` ERROR: test files that no CI job invokes - tests/agent_tests/local_only_agent_tests: 2 test file(s) invoked by no job: test_a2a.py, test_a2a_completion_bridge.py Add each to a job's test path, or list it in .github/ci-coverage-allowlist.yml with a reason. ``` #### The census passes for the right reason once the entry lands 1. Command: ``` python .github/scripts/assert_ci_coverage.py ``` 2. Output: ``` OK: 2421 test files and 10 Dockerfiles are each invoked by at least one job or carry an explicit allowlist entry. ``` #### The sibling triage invariants still hold after the heads-up removal 1. Command: ``` uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/test_github_triage_workflows.py -q ``` 2. Output: ``` ........... [100%] 11 passed, 1 warning in 0.36s ``` #### Both moved scripts still resolve from their callers 1. Command: ``` python -m py_compile .github/scripts/run_llm_translation_tests.py .github/scripts/auto_update_price_and_context_window_file.py && echo "both compile OK" make -n test-llm-translation | tail -1 ``` 2. Output: ``` both compile OK python .github/scripts/run_llm_translation_tests.py ``` ## Type 🧹 Refactoring 🚄 Infrastructure ## Caveats - Collected agent test set is unchanged: one top-level file - The audit called the translation runner orphaned; Makefile still runs it - Heads-up removal also drops its two workflow-invariant tests - `.github/workflows/test-model-map.yaml` still uses `.yaml`, left alone ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signal.title: refactor(ci): fold the nine thin unit-shard callers into one matrix
signal.text:
## TLDR Problem this solves: - Nine workflow files each made one call to the same base - Adding a shard meant adding a file - Changing anything shared meant editing nine files How it solves it: - One `test-unit.yml` matrix caller replaces all nine - Shard names preserved, so every required check keeps its name - No ruleset edit needed, and none should be made - 382 lines of workflow deleted, 219 added ## User Flow Before: adding a unit shard means adding a workflow file, and the reviewer has to check it against eight siblings 1. A contributor splits a slow directory and needs a new shard 2. They copy one of the nine `test-unit-*.yml` files, edit `test-path` and `artifact-name`, and commit the new file 3. They ask an admin to add the new `<shard> / Run tests` context to the branch ruleset 4. Anyone later changing something shared, a Python version or a permission block, edits nine files and hopes they are consistent After: adding a shard is one matrix entry, and the reviewer sees the whole set on one screen 1. The contributor adds an entry to the `include:` list in `.github/workflows/test-unit.yml` with its `shard`, `test-path`, `artifact-name`, workers, reruns and timeouts 2. The shard reports as `<shard> / Run tests`, the same shape as the existing eleven 3. They still ask an admin to add that one new context to the ruleset, because it is genuinely a new check 4. Anyone changing something shared edits one file, and the eleven shards cannot drift apart Nothing changes for the existing eleven shards: same names, same paths, same workers, same reruns, same timeouts. ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/<your_test_file>.py -v` - [x] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix A consolidation is only safe if it is a rename-free identity: the same eleven shards, the same inputs, and the same required-check names. All three are checked mechanically rather than by eye, and the check names are compared against the live ruleset rather than against the audit doc. ### Before (5290150a05) #### Nine files, eleven jobs, one call each 1. Command: ``` grep -l "_test-unit-base.yml" .github/workflows/test-unit-*.yml | grep -v proxy-db | wc -l ``` 2. Output: ``` 9 ``` ### After (2cd6b25a3d) #### Every shard's resolved inputs are identical, field by field The script below resolves each old caller's `with:` block against the base workflow's declared defaults, resolves the new matrix the same way, and diffs them per shard and per field. 1. Command, run with the nine old callers still present so both sides are readable at once: ``` python - <<'EOF' import yaml, pathlib, re, sys BASE_DEFAULTS = {"workers": 2, "reruns": 2, "timeout-minutes": 20, "job-timeout-minutes": 55, "max-failures": 10, "dist": "loadscope"} norm = lambda v: re.sub(r"\s+", " ", v).strip() if isinstance(v, str) else v old = {} for p in sorted(pathlib.Path(".github/workflows").glob("test-unit-*.yml")): if p.name in ("test-unit-proxy-db.yml", "test-unit.yml"): continue for jid, job in yaml.safe_load(p.read_text())["jobs"].items(): if job.get("uses") != "./.github/workflows/_test-unit-base.yml": continue old[job.get("name") or jid] = {**BASE_DEFAULTS, **{k: norm(v) for k, v in (job.get("with") or {}).items()}} wf = yaml.safe_load(pathlib.Path(".github/workflows/test-unit.yml").read_text()) new = {e["shard"]: {**BASE_DEFAULTS, **{k: norm(v) for k, v in e.items() if k != "shard"}} for e in wf["jobs"]["unit"]["strategy"]["matrix"]["include"]} print(f"old shards: {len(old)} new shards: {len(new)}") print("missing from new:", sorted(set(old) - set(new)) or "none") print("extra in new:", sorted(set(new) - set(old)) or "none") bad = 0 for shard in sorted(old): for key in sorted(set(old[shard]) | set(new.get(shard, {}))): o, n = old[shard].get(key), new.get(shard, {}).get(key) if o != n: bad += 1 print(f" DIFF {shard!r} {key}:
 old={o!r}
 new={n!r}") print("
RESULT:", "IDENTICAL" if not bad and set(old) == set(new) else f"{bad} differences") EOF ``` 2. Output: ``` old shards: 11 new shards: 11 missing from new: none extra in new: none RESULT: IDENTICAL ``` #### Every produced check name is a context the ruleset already requires 1. Command: ``` gh api repos/BerriAI/litellm/rules/branches/litellm_internal_staging \ --jq '[.[] | select(.type=="required_status_checks") | .parameters.required_status_checks[].context] | sort | .[]' ``` 2. Output, intersected with the eleven names the new matrix reports: ``` shards this workflow will report: 11 required '/ Run tests' contexts the ruleset asks for: 23 covered by the new matrix: OK All Other Providers / Run tests OK Vertex AI / Run tests OK core-utils / Run tests OK enterprise-routing / Run tests OK integrations / Run tests OK misc / Run tests OK proxy-auth / Run tests OK proxy-endpoints / Run tests OK proxy-infra / Run tests OK proxy-server / Run tests OK responses-caching-types / Run tests required but NOT produced by the new matrix (must be proxy-db or another workflow): -- auth-checks / Run tests -- budgets / Run tests -- custom-logging / Run tests -- db-and-spend / Run tests -- endpoints-and-responses / Run tests -- guardrails-hooks / Run tests -- jwt-and-keys / Run tests -- key-generation / Run tests -- logging-misc / Run tests -- proxy-runtime / Run tests -- proxy-server-core / Run tests -- proxy-utils / Run tests ``` Eleven here plus twelve from `test-unit-proxy-db.yml` accounts for all twenty-three. Nothing is orphaned and nothing is renamed. #### No test file lost its runner 1. Command: ``` python .github/scripts/assert_ci_coverage.py ``` 2. Output: ``` OK: 2422 test files and 10 Dockerfiles are each invoked by at least one job or carry an explicit allowlist entry. ``` #### The real proof is this pull request's own check list The eleven shard checks appear on this PR under their existing names. If any name had drifted, the ruleset would report a missing required check instead. ## Type 🧹 Refactoring 🚄 Infrastructure ## Caveats - `test-unit-proxy-db.yml` deliberately not folded in yet - Its shard guard reads that filename, so it moves with the guard - `test-unit-documentation.yml` stays; it calls no base workflow - All shards now share one concurrency group, same net behaviour - Setup-tax work on the base workflow is separate and untouched ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signal.title: feat(anthropic): auto-inject context-1m beta header for [1m] model suffix
signal.text: ## Relevant issues None ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [ ] My PR passes all unit tests on `make test-unit` - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem ## CI (LiteLLM team) - [ ] **Branch creation CI run** Link: - [ ] **CI run for the last commit** Link: - [ ] **Merge / cherry-pick CI run** Links: ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix ## Type 🆕 New Feature ✅ Test ## Changes Auto-inject the anthropic-beta header `context-1m-2025-08-07` when the model name carries a trailing `[1m]` / `[1M]` suffix. The proxy strips the suffix before routing so standard model resolution works and preserves the original via `_original_model`. The Anthropic chat transformation and the experimental passthrough handler both read `_original_model` and add the beta header automatically, with no per-deployment config needed. ### Files - `litellm/llms/anthropic/chat/transformation.py` — inject context-1m in `update_headers_with_optional_anthropic_beta` - `litellm/llms/anthropic/common_utils.py` — add `context_1m_supported` param to `get_anthropic_headers`, auto-detect suffix in `_get_anthropic_headers` - `litellm/llms/anthropic/experimental_pass_through/messages/transformation.py` — same injection in `_update_headers_with_anthropic_beta` - `litellm/proxy/route_llm_request.py` — strip suffix and stash `_original_model` in the request data - `tests/test_litellm/test_utils.py` — 8 test cases (3 injection sites, positive + negative paths)

signal.title: [Bug]: native CLI login consent page lists teams in database order and preselects the first one
signal.text: ### Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. ### What happened? The consent page that `lite login --pkce` opens in the browser (added by #37626) asks a user who belongs to several teams which team their CLI requests should be attributed to. The dropdown lists the teams in whatever order the database returns them and the first entry is what the form submits when the user clicks Approve without touching it. On the same proxy, with the same user, that first entry was `forge-team-b-35551` while the alphabetical first is `forge-team-a-35551`, and during an earlier QA run the order changed between two logins. A user who takes the default can end up bound to a team they did not mean to pick, and their first chat call then fails with `403 team not allowed to access model` if that team's allowlist does not cover the model they asked for Expected: the teams come back in a stable, predictable order (alias, case-insensitively, then id as a tiebreaker), or the form does not preselect anything when there is more than one team and makes the user choose. The same team lookup backs the classic `lite login` flow's team choice, so sorting it there fixes both ### User Flow Before a (hypothetical) fix: a developer on several teams clicks Approve on the consent page, gets bound to whichever team the database listed first, and their first chat call is refused 1. The developer runs `lite login --pkce` against `https://litellm-domain`; the CLI opens `GET https://litellm-domain/authorize?response_type=code&client_id=...&code_challenge=...&resource=https://litellm-domain` in their browser 2. After signing in, the consent page shows an "Attribute requests to team" dropdown whose first entry is `forge-team-b-35551`, with `lit5874-cli-team` second and `forge-team-a-35551` sixth, in no recognizable order 3. They click Approve without touching the dropdown; the browser posts `POST https://litellm-domain/authorize/complete`, lands back on the CLI's loopback page, and the terminal prints `Login successful!` 4. They send `POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions` with `"model": "gpt-5.4-mini"` and get `403 {"error": {"message": "team not allowed to access model. This team can only access models=['gpt-4o-mini']. Tried to access gpt-5.4-mini", "type": "team_model_access_denied"}}` 5. They open `https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs` and see the failed request attributed to `forge-team-b-35551`, a team they never meant to use from the CLI After a (hypothetical) fix: the dropdown is sorted and the developer sees the team they expect before approving 1. The developer runs `lite login --pkce` against `https://litellm-domain`; the CLI opens the same `GET https://litellm-domain/authorize?...` URL in their browser 2. After signing in, the consent page lists the teams alphabetically (`forge-team-a-35551`, `forge-team-b-35551`, `lit5874-cli-team`, ...), so the entry at the top is the same on every login and on every replica 3. They pick `lit5874-cli-team`, click Approve, the browser posts `POST https://litellm-domain/authorize/complete`, and the terminal prints `Login successful!` 4. They send `POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions` with `"model": "gpt-5.4-mini"` and get `200` with a normal completion 5. `https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs` shows the request attributed to `lit5874-cli-team` ### Proof the bug occurs Config the proxy ran with (`litellm --config config.yaml --port 53218`, Postgres-backed so teams and memberships live in the DB; the env vars named are `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY`, and `DATABASE_URL`, values redacted): ```yaml model_list: - model_name: gpt-5.4-mini litellm_params: model: openai/gpt-5.4-mini api_key: os.environ/OPENAI_API_KEY - model_name: claude-haiku-4-5 litellm_params: model: anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5 api_key: os.environ/ANTHROPIC_API_KEY general_settings: master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY database_url: os.environ/DATABASE_URL store_model_in_db: true coordination_redis: host: 127.0.0.1 port: 53217 ``` Commit: `64e7ab1beb`, the tip of #37626 (branch `litellm_lit5874_native_cli_oauth_pkce`, based on `litellm_internal_staging` at `6fcdea03b0`) The signed-in user is `default_user_id`, a member of nine teams. The "browser" below is a script standing in for the system browser: it signs in at `POST /login`, fetches the consent page the CLI sent it to, prints the dropdown's `<option>` entries in page order, and then submits the form. Two logins in a row: ``` $ lite --base-url http://127.0.0.1:53218 login --pkce (run 1) Login successful! browser side: POST /login -> 303 GET /authorize -> 200 team <select> options, in page order: forge-team-b-35551 (f7f1356b...) lit5874-cli-team (e34bc8db...) qa-team-a-35551 (4c2befa8...) qa-team-b-35551 (dd13137d...) qa-team-a-35551 (57d853bc...) forge-team-a-35551 (94554a34...) qa-team-b-35551 (57f324f9...) risk37518-team-1787186008 (a0a759e9...) testteam (ae98be70...) same labels sorted, for comparison: forge-team-a-35551 (94554a34...) forge-team-b-35551 (f7f1356b...) lit5874-cli-team (e34bc8db...) qa-team-a-35551 (4c2befa8...) qa-team-a-35551 (57d853bc...) qa-team-b-35551 (57f324f9...) qa-team-b-35551 (dd13137d...) risk37518-team-1787186008 (a0a759e9...) testteam (ae98be70...) preselected (first option, what Approve submits untouched): forge-team-b-35551 POST /authorize/complete (team_id=lit5874-cli-team) -> 200 $ lite --base-url http://127.0.0.1:53218 logout Logged out successfully. Authentication token cleared. $ lite --base-url http://127.0.0.1:53218 login --pkce (run 2) Login successful! browser side: POST /login -> 303 GET /authorize -> 200 team <select> options, in page order: forge-team-b-35551 (f7f1356b...) lit5874-cli-team (e34bc8db...) qa-team-a-35551 (4c2befa8...) qa-team-b-35551 (dd13137d...) qa-team-a-35551 (57d853bc...) forge-team-a-35551 (94554a34...) qa-team-b-35551 (57f324f9...) risk37518-team-1787186008 (a0a759e9...) testteam (ae98be70...) preselected (first option, what Approve submits untouched): forge-team-b-35551 POST /authorize/complete (team_id=lit5874-cli-team) -> 200 ``` The order is neither alphabetical nor the order the user joined the teams in (`lit5874-cli-team` was the most recent membership). What happens to a user who clicks Approve without touching the dropdown, same proxy, same user: ``` $ lite --base-url http://127.0.0.1:53218 login --pkce (browser clicks Approve without touching the team dropdown) Login successful! browser side: GET /authorize -> 200 preselected (first option, what Approve submits untouched): forge-team-b-35551 POST /authorize/complete (team_id left at the preselected first option) -> 200 stored team_id: f7f1356b-a734-41f0-9120-6f01756f9853 $ curl http://127.0.0.1:53218/v1/chat/completions -H 'Authorization: Bearer <stored key>' -d '{"model":"gpt-5.4-mini","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]}' {"error":{"message":"team not allowed to access model. This team can only access models=['gpt-4o-mini']. Tried to access gpt-5.4-mini","type":"team_model_access_denied","param":"model","code":"403"}} HTTP 403 $ lite --base-url http://127.0.0.1:53218 logout Logged out successfully. Authentication token cleared. ``` ### Fix sketch The order comes from `fetch_cli_sso_team_details` in `litellm/proxy/management_endpoints/ui_sso.py`, which runs `find_many(where={"team_id": {"in": teams}})` with no `order`, and `lookup_consent_teams` in `litellm/proxy/_experimental/mcp_server/proxy_api_credentials.py` hands those rows to `_team_field` in `litellm/proxy/common_utils/html_forms/native_client_consent.py` as is. Sort once at the source: have `fetch_cli_sso_team_details` return the details ordered by `(team_alias or team_id).casefold()` and then `team_id`, so the consent page, the classic `lite login` team choice, and anything else reading that helper agree. If the product call is that a multi-team user must choose explicitly, `_team_field` can additionally render a disabled, selected placeholder option (`Choose a team`) and mark the select `required` when there is more than one team, so Approve without a choice is refused by the browser Tests: extend `tests/test_litellm/proxy/management_endpoints/test_ui_sso.py` with a `find_many` stub that returns rows out of order and assert the helper's output is sorted by alias then id (including two teams that share an alias), extend `tests/test_litellm/proxy/_experimental/mcp_server/test_proxy_api_credentials.py` so `lookup_consent_teams` keeps that order, and, if the placeholder is added, extend `tests/test_litellm/proxy/common_utils/html_forms/test_native_client_consent.py` to assert the first option is the disabled placeholder whenever two or more teams are passed QA: on a Postgres-backed proxy, add one user to three teams whose aliases sort differently from their creation order, run `lite login --pkce`, and check that the consent page at `/authorize` lists them alphabetically on two consecutive logins (and on each replica when running more than one); then click Approve untouched and confirm the stored `team_id` in `~/.litellm/token.json` is the alphabetical first, or that the browser refuses to submit without a choice if the placeholder route is taken ### What part of LiteLLM is this about? Proxy ### What LiteLLM version are you on ? commit 64e7ab1beb (PR #37626 branch, based on litellm_internal_staging at 6fcdea03b0) ### Twitter / LinkedIn details _No response_

signal.title: perf(streaming): add shared JSONFragmentAccumulator for Vertex and Anthropic
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Vertex and Anthropic each copy the whole SSE-fragment buffer on every chunk, O(n^2) in payload size - Anthropic also has no parse-deferral heuristic and can wedge forever on two concatenated JSON envelopes How it solves it: - Add a shared JSONFragmentAccumulator in litellm_core_utils/, an O(1)-append buffer with a peel-one-value primitive - Migrate both providers' ModelResponseIterator onto it instead of fixing Vertex alone ## User Flow Before: a developer streaming a large tool-call response from Gemini sees latency that grows with the size of the response 1. They send a streaming chat completion to a Gemini model with a tool whose output is a large (multi-KB to multi-MB) JSON payload 2. The response streams back correctly, but time-to-completion grows faster than the payload size does, and profiling the proxy process shows most of the time inside the JSON-reassembly step of the SSE parser After: the same request streams back in time proportional to the payload size, not proportional to its square 1. They send the same streaming chat completion 2. The response streams back with latency that scales linearly with payload size 3. The same fix applies to Anthropic tool-call and structured-output streaming, which had the identical buffer-copy cost plus no parse-deferral at all ## Relevant issues Fixes #31861 ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [ ] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Live proxy verification against real Vertex/Gemini and Anthropic traffic was not run in this session (no provider credentials available in this environment). The commands below reproduce the fix end to end against a local proxy; posting as a follow-up PR comment once run. Vertex/Gemini: ```bash curl -N -s -X POST http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model": "gemini-flash", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Return a JSON array of 20 country names, one per line."}], "stream": true}' | cat ``` Anthropic (a tool-call large enough to fragment across multiple SSE chunks): ```bash curl -N -s -X POST http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model": "claude-anthropic", "stream": true, "tools": [{"type": "function", "function": {"name": "emit_report", "description": "Emit a structured report", "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {"summary": {"type": "string"}, "findings": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}}}}}}], "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Call emit_report with a summary of at least 2000 characters and 20 findings."}]}' | cat ``` Expect no `JSONDecodeError` in the proxy logs and the full response to stream through in both cases. signal.title: [Bug]: search router silently drops provider-specific litellm_params from yaml search_tools entries
signal.text: ### Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. ### What happened? When a `search_tools` entry in the proxy config carries provider-specific keys in its `litellm_params` (for example `tool_name` for the agentcore provider, or `aws_access_key_id` / `aws_secret_access_key` overrides), those keys are silently dropped. The search router forwards only `search_provider`, `api_key`, and `api_base` from the tool's `litellm_params` to the underlying search call (`SearchAPIRouter.async_search_with_fallbacks_helper` in `litellm/router_utils/search_api_router.py`), so every other key is ignored with no warning, no boot error, and no request-time error Expected: either every `litellm_params` key is forwarded to the provider (the way `model_list` entries forward their `litellm_params` to completion calls), or the proxy rejects unknown keys loudly at boot so an admin finds out their knob is dead The same keys do work when passed per request in the body or set via provider env vars (for agentcore, `AGENTCORE_SEARCH_TOOL_NAME`), which is how the guard behind `tool_name` stays reachable. Only the yaml path is dead. The agentcore example config was corrected in #36331 to stop advertising the yaml knobs; this issue tracks fixing the plumbing itself, which affects all search providers ### User Flow Before a (hypothetical) fix: a proxy admin whose AgentCore gateway target has a custom name configures it in yaml and every search silently uses the wrong tool name 1. They add a `search_tools` entry with `search_provider: agentcore`, their gateway `api_base`, and `tool_name: MyTarget___WebSearch` in `litellm_params`, then start the proxy; boot succeeds with no warning 2. They send POST http://litellm-domain/v1/search/agentcore-search with `{"query": "latest AI developments", "max_results": 5}` 3. The request goes out with the default `web-search-tool___WebSearch` instead of their configured name; on a gateway whose target really has a custom name this comes back as an MCP tool-not-found error, and on a gateway that also has a default-named target it silently searches through the wrong one 4. Nothing in the response or the logs says their yaml `tool_name` was ignored After a (hypothetical) fix: the same config works, or fails loudly 1. They add the same `search_tools` entry and start the proxy 2. They send the same POST http://litellm-domain/v1/search/agentcore-search request 3. The request goes out with `MyTarget___WebSearch` and returns results from their target, or, if the key is deliberately unsupported, the proxy refuses to boot naming the unsupported key ### Proof the bug occurs Config the proxy ran with (proxy booted from PR #36331 at commit `70a4f9a73aabd327b9c06e52bf5d47b437b76430`; the router file involved is untouched by that PR and identical on `litellm_internal_staging`): ```yaml search_tools: - search_tool_name: agentcore-badtool litellm_params: search_provider: agentcore api_base: https://litellm-qa-agentcore-tez4ymmxfc.gateway.bedrock-agentcore.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/mcp tool_name: my-target___ListFiles ``` The agentcore provider rejects any `tool_name` not ending in `___WebSearch`, so this request must fail. Instead it returns HTTP 200 with real web results, against a real AgentCore gateway: ``` curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:26793/v1/search/agentcore-badtool \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED' \ -d '{"query": "anything", "max_results": 2}' -w '\nHTTP %{http_code}\n' {"results":[{"title":"Anything","url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anything", ...}],"object":"search"} HTTP 200 ``` The proxy debug log shows the outgoing JSON-RPC call used the default tool name, not the configured one, proving the yaml value never reached the provider: ``` -d '{'jsonrpc': '2.0', 'id': 1, 'method': 'tools/call', 'params': {'name': 'web-search-tool___WebSearch', 'arguments': {'query': 'anything', 'maxResults': 2}}}' ``` Control showing the guard itself works when the value arrives via env var: rebooting the same proxy with `AGENTCORE_SEARCH_TOOL_NAME=my-target___ListFiles` exported makes the same request refuse with ``` Invalid AgentCore search tool_name 'my-target___ListFiles': must end with '___WebSearch' (a web-search connector tool). Other gateway tools cannot be invoked through this provider. ``` Fix sketch: forward the tool's full `litellm_params` (minus `search_provider`, which becomes the positional provider) as kwargs from `SearchAPIRouter.async_search_with_fallbacks_helper` into the search call, mirroring how `model_list` `litellm_params` flow into completion calls, with request-body params winning over yaml on key collisions. Needs a check across all search providers that previously-ignored yaml keys don't change behavior for existing configs ### What part of LiteLLM is this about? Proxy ### What LiteLLM version are you on ? litellm_internal_staging at 2059033352de (also present at PR #36331 tip 70a4f9a7) ### Twitter / LinkedIn details _No response_

signal.title: fix(responses bridge): map incomplete responses to finish_reason length instead of 500
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Reasoning models can spend every output token on reasoning - The Responses bridge then returned 500 on /v1/chat/completions - A user token-limit condition was counted as a system error How it solves it: - Map `incomplete_details.reason` to a chat `finish_reason` - `max_output_tokens` becomes `length`, `content_filter` becomes `content_filter` - Return an empty assistant message instead of raising - Streaming handles `response.incomplete` the same way ## User Flow Before: a developer with a small `max_completion_tokens` gets a 500 when the model spends all tokens on reasoning 1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with `"max_completion_tokens": 16` and `"reasoning_effort": "high"` to a model served through the Responses bridge 2. The model uses all 16 tokens on reasoning and produces no message 3. The gateway returns HTTP 500 with `"gpt-5.6-sol unable to complete request: max_output_tokens"`, which their monitoring counts as a gateway outage After: the same request comes back as a normal truncated completion 1. They send the same POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with `"max_completion_tokens": 16` and `"reasoning_effort": "high"` 2. The model uses all 16 tokens on reasoning and produces no message 3. The gateway returns HTTP 200 with an empty assistant message, `"finish_reason": "length"`, and real usage, matching what POST https://litellm-domain/v1/responses already reported for the same call ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Think through modular arithmetic carefully, then return only those ten digits."}], "reasoning_effort": "high", "max_completion_tokens": 16 } ``` ### Before (6d47468dae) #### Non-streaming request 1. `curl -sS -i http://localhost:4010/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d "$REQ"` 2. Observed output ```text HTTP/1.1 500 Internal Server Error {"error":{"message":"litellm.APIConnectionError: APIConnectionError: OpenAIException - gpt-5.6-sol unable to complete request: max_output_tokens. Received Model Group=bridge/gpt-5.6-sol\nAvailable Model Group Fallbacks=None","type":null,"param":null,"code":"500"}} ``` #### Streaming request 1. The admin configures `model_name: smart-router` twice: a plain `openai/gpt-5.6` default and an `auto_router/smart-router` entry tagged `auto_route` that carries `aws_region_name: eu-west-3`, plus the routed tier `bedrock-tier` = `bedrock/us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5` with its own `aws_region_name: us-east-1`, turns on `router_settings.enable_tag_filtering`, and starts the proxy 2. signal.text: ## Relevant issues Fixes #31872 ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have requested a Greptile review by commenting `@greptileai` and received a **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Type Bug Fix ## Changes `CerebrasConfig.get_supported_openai_params()` overrides the parent `OpenAIGPTConfig` with a hand-crafted list that was missing `max_retries` and `extra_headers`. Since `map_openai_params` only passes through params in this list, both were silently discarded — `max_retries` always fell back to the hardcoded default of 2 in `openai.py:653`, and custom `extra_headers` were dropped before reaching the HTTP handler. Added both params to the supported list and added regression tests (including the `max_retries=0` falsy-value edge case) verifying `map_openai_params` passes them through unchanged. ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Verified against a local proxy with a real Cerebras API key: ```bash curl -X POST http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-local-dev-master-key" \ -d '{"model":"llama-cerebras","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"say hi"}],"max_retries":0,"extra_headers":{"X-Verify":"patch-05"}}' # -> {"choices":[{"message":{"content":"Hi! How can I assist you today?"}}]} ``` Log evidence: `max_retries` now appears in `optional_params` (previously silently dropped), and `extra_headers` was forwarded in the outbound HTTP request. All requests are signed in-process with HMAC-SHA1; no extra Python dependency and no sidecar is required. New files under `litellm/proxy/guardrails/guardrail_hooks/aliyun/`: - `aliyun_ai_guardrail.py` — the `AliyunAIGuardrail` hook (inherits `AliyunGuardrailBase` + `CustomGuardrail`): request signing, region→endpoint routing, long-text chunking, concurrent chunk verification (semaphore-limited), risk-level → protection-level blocking logic, and all event hooks. - `base.py` — `AliyunGuardrailBase` helpers to extract the last consecutive user-message block (`get_user_prompt`) and its public http(s) image URLs (`get_image_urls`). - `__init__.py` — `initialize_guardrail` loader plus initializer/class registries; manually resolves `os.environ/` references for the custom `access_key_id` / `access_key_secret` fields. - `README.md` — configuration, usage examples, region table, protection levels, and detection types. Supporting changes: - `litellm/types/proxy/guardrails/guardrail_hooks/aliyun/aliyun_ai_guardrail.py` — typed request/response models, `AliyunAIGuardrailOptionalParams`, and `AliyunAIGuardrailConfigModel` (with `ui_friendly_name`). - `litellm/types/guardrails.py` — registers the `ALIYUN_AI_GUARDRAIL = "aliyun_ai_guardrail"` enum entry and wires the config model in. - `tests/test_litellm/proxy/guardrails/guardrail_hooks/aliyun/test_aliyun_ai_guardrail.py` — unit tests. Key behaviors: - **pre_call** scans text and public image URLs from the last consecutive user messages; blocks with HTTP 400 on violation. - **post_call (non-streaming)** scans the full response and blocks with HTTP 400 on violation. - **post_call (streaming)** uses a buffer-and-release sliding window (`stream_window_size` / `stream_slide_step`, with an earlier `stream_first_check_step` first check to reduce first-token latency); on violation it emits an SSE error event rather than raising. - **pre_mcp_call / post_mcp_call** inspect MCP tool name + arguments and tool execution results. - Four protection levels (`low` / `medium` / `high` ), mapping detected risk levels (`none/low/medium/high` and sensitive-data `S0–S4`) against a configurable threshold. - Long text is split preferentially at punctuation boundaries; chunks are checked concurrently (max 5 in flight; MultiModalGuard limit is 20). - Per-region endpoint routing across 7 regions; configurable service codes for input / output / MCP detection. Matched content is only surfaced as detection metadata (type, risk level, per-type details) in the 400 body; raw credentials are read via `os.environ/` and never echoed. ## QA runbook <!-- Only needed when your PR edits tests/e2e; delete this section otherwise For each e2e test you added or changed, list the manual steps a reviewer can follow to reproduce it by hand against a live proxy, mapping 1:1 to what the test asserts: one top-level bullet per test giving its pytest node id followed by what it proves in plain words, then a nested "- [ ]" checklist where each item is a concrete action (route, request body, expected response) and the final item is the sanity-check step shown in the examples. signal.title: feat(guardrails): add Needlepath context selection guardrail
signal.text: > **This PR is intentionally a draft.** We are keeping it in draft pending our own upstream validation against a live engine, and will mark it ready for review shortly. Review comments are very welcome in the meantime. ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Tool outputs push whole documents into every agent turn - Operators have no in-gateway way to send only the relevant spans How it solves it: - Adds a `needlepath` pre_call guardrail that selects spans per message - Selection is conditioned on the tool call's own intent - Any failure or stand-down forwards the original messages unchanged ## User Flow Before: a developer running a filings agent sends a 40k token tool result on every turn, and pays for all of it. 1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with a `user` question, an `assistant` turn carrying a `tool_calls` entry, and a `tool` message holding the full filing text 2. The whole filing is forwarded upstream, and the response usage shows prompt tokens covering all of it 3. They open https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs and see the request logged at the full input cost After: the same request forwards only the part of the filing that answers the question. 1. The proxy admin adds a `needlepath-selection` guardrail to `config.yaml` and restarts the proxy 2. The developer sends the same POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions, adding `"guardrails": ["needlepath-selection"]` 3. The reply carries `x-litellm-applied-guardrails: needlepath-selection`, and the response usage shows fewer prompt tokens 4. https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs shows the request with `messages_selected`, `chars_before`, and `chars_after` under guardrail information 5. If the selection service is unreachable, the same request still succeeds and forwards the full filing, with no visible difference other than the header being absent ## What this adds A first-party `needlepath` guardrail. During `pre_call` it takes each eligible message, sends its text plus a query to `POST {api_base}/v1/context/select`, and replaces that message's content with the returned `rendered_context`. Selection is extractive: the returned block is made of spans of the submitted text. The query for a `tool` or `function` result is the intent of the call that produced it, found by `tool_call_id` and rendered as `name: arguments`. Everything else uses the last user message. Each message is selected independently and concurrently, so one message's outcome never affects another's and the added latency is roughly one round trip rather than one per message. Config, conservative by default: ```yaml guardrails: - guardrail_name: needlepath-selection litellm_params: guardrail: needlepath mode: pre_call api_key: os.environ/NEEDLEPATH_API_KEY optional_params: select_tool_outputs: true # default true select_history: false # default false select_system: false # default false min_chars_to_select: 500 # skip small payloads entirely max_context_tokens: 4000 operating_point: np-2026-07-r2 # pinned, not inherited ``` `operating_point` is an immutable engine label. It is pinned here rather than inheriting the service's current default, so the behaviour of a given proxy build does not change underneath a deployment. ## Fail-open, and why This guardrail is unconditionally fail-open. It returns the caller's messages byte-identical whenever any of the following holds: - the service is unreachable, times out, or answers a non-2xx status, including 402, 403, and 429 - the body is not JSON, or is JSON of an unexpected shape - the gate reports a stand-down (any `gate.reason` prefixed `standdown:`), which is the service saying the full content is what the caller should send - `records_selected` is 0, `tokens_after` is 0, or `rendered_context` is missing or blank - the returned block is not shorter than the text it would replace The reasoning is that a proxy which silently blanks a tool output is far worse than a proxy that does nothing. Selection sits on the request path of every call behind the gateway, so its worst case has to be a no-op. That is why there is no `unreachable_fallback` knob here: `fail_closed` would turn a selection hiccup into a failed LLM request for everyone behind the proxy, and we do not think that trade is ever right for this guardrail. When nothing is applied, the exact `inputs` object is returned rather than a rebuilt one, so the handlers' identity check sees no edit and an untouched request is not written back. ## Registration points touched - `litellm/proxy/guardrails/guardrail_hooks/needlepath/` (new package; exposes `guardrail_initializer_registry` and `guardrail_class_registry` for auto-discovery) - `litellm/types/proxy/guardrails/guardrail_hooks/needlepath.py` (new config model) - `litellm/types/guardrails.py`: the config model import, `SupportedGuardrailIntegrations.NEEDLEPATH`, and the `LitellmParams` base list ## Relevant issues <!-- none --> ## Linear ticket <!-- external contributor --> ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [ ] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Not yet attached, which is the reason this is a draft. Live end-to-end proof against a running proxy is in progress on our side and will be added before this is marked ready for review. What is done today, at commit `845ee4b`: - 32 unit tests in `tests/test_litellm/proxy/guardrails/guardrail_hooks/test_needlepath.py`, all mocked, no network - one test per fail-open condition above, each asserting the messages come back byte-identical - mutation checks: removing the stand-down guard turns 5 tests red, removing the empty-selection guard turns 2 red, and removing the blank-`rendered_context` guard rewrites a tool message to `' '`, which is exactly the failure the guard exists to prevent - `ruff format --check` clean on all added files ## Type 🆕 New Feature ## Caveats (if any) - `/v1/responses` passes through unchanged; no `texts` write-back yet - Messages whose content mixes text and non-text parts are skipped ## CI note The `documentation` check reads env-var docs from a checkout of `BerriAI/litellm-docs`@main, so it stays red until the companion docs PR — [BerriAI/litellm-docs#858](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm-docs/pull/858) — merges (it documents `NEEDLEPATH_API_KEY` / `NEEDLEPATH_API_BASE` on the guardrail page). `code-quality`, `lint`, and the strict-rule budget are addressed in-branch.

signal.title: fix: let s3_bucket_name reach litellm_params
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - `s3_bucket_name` in a model's `litellm_params` is silently dropped - Bedrock batch output cannot be downloaded without an env var - `gcs_bucket_name` works, so Vertex users never hit this How it solves it: - Adds `s3_bucket_name` to `OPTIONAL_KWARGS_KEYS` - One-line change, plus a regression test ## User Flow Before: someone running Claude batch jobs on Bedrock configures the bucket on the model, submits a job that completes, and then cannot fetch the results 1. They set `s3_bucket_name` on their Bedrock deployment in `config.yaml` and start the proxy with no `AWS_S3_BUCKET_NAME` in the environment 2. They `POST /v1/files` with `purpose=batch` and a JSONL of requests, and get a file ID back 3. They `POST /v1/batches` with that file ID, and get a batch ID back 4. They poll `GET /v1/batches/{id}` until it reports `completed`, with an empty failure message and no error file 5. They `GET /v1/files/{output_file_id}/content` and get `500 {"error":{"message":"S3 bucket_name is required. Set 's3_bucket_name' in proxy config or AWS_S3_BUCKET_NAME for Bedrock file content retrieval."}}` 6. The results are unreachable through the gateway even though the job succeeded and was billed, and the only way out is to restart the proxy with the environment variable set After: the same configuration works, and the results come back 1. They set `s3_bucket_name` on their Bedrock deployment in `config.yaml` and start the proxy with no `AWS_S3_BUCKET_NAME` in the environment 2. They `POST /v1/files` with `purpose=batch` and a JSONL of requests, and get a file ID back 3. They `POST /v1/batches` with that file ID, and get a batch ID back 4. They poll `GET /v1/batches/{id}` until it reports `completed`, with an empty failure message and no error file 5. They `GET /v1/files/{output_file_id}/content` and get `200` with one JSONL line per record 6. They read the results, matching each line back to their input by ID ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [ ] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Captured against a deployed proxy on `v1.91.3`, which carries the same allowlist as the merge base, rather than against the two commit hashes. The reproduction is a real Bedrock batch job in `eu-west-1` billed to a real account, and the download is the exact call an end user makes. A run at the merge base and at the PR tip is still worth doing before merge; I could not stand up managed files locally because that path needs a database and the migration step did not complete under emulation on my machine. Shared setup: one Bedrock deployment whose `litellm_params` carry `model`, `aws_access_key_id`, `aws_secret_access_key`, `aws_region_name` and `s3_bucket_name`, with `AWS_S3_BUCKET_NAME` absent from the process environment. Input is a 100 record JSONL, which is Bedrock's minimum. ### Before (allowlist without `s3_bucket_name`) 1. Upload the input ``` POST /v1/files purpose=batch, target_model_names=bedrock/global.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0 200 status=uploaded ``` 2. Create the batch ``` POST /v1/batches 200 status=validating ``` 3. Poll until terminal ``` GET /v1/batches/{id} 200 status=completed failure_message '' error_file_id null job: arn:aws:bedrock:eu-west-1:...:model-invocation-job/kpiid5uv6b9l ``` 4. Download the output, which is where it breaks ``` GET /v1/files/{output_file_id}/content 500 {"error":{"message":"S3 bucket_name is required. Set 's3_bucket_name' in proxy config or AWS_S3_BUCKET_NAME for Bedrock file content retrieval.","code":"500"}} ``` 5. Repeat step 4 passing the model explicitly, since a caller would try that next, and get the same result ``` GET /v1/files/{output_file_id}/content?model=bedrock/global.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0 500 same error GET /v1/files/{output_file_id}/content with header x-litellm-model 500 same error ``` ### After (`070320e94c`, and equivalently with the env var set) 1. Upload the input ``` POST /v1/files 200 status=uploaded ``` 2. Create the batch ``` POST /v1/batches 200 status=validating ``` 3. Poll until terminal ``` GET /v1/batches/{id} 200 status=completed failure_message '' error_file_id null ``` 4. Download the output ``` GET /v1/files/{output_file_id}/content 200 59400 bytes, 100 JSONL records ``` 5. Confirm every submitted record came back, keyed by ID ``` matched 100/100 ticket-0000 -> DELIVERY ticket-0001 -> BILLING ticket-0002 -> PROMO ``` ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - `s3_region_name` is likely dropped the same way, untested - Proof captured on `v1.91.3`, not at the two hashes

signal.title: [BUG] Virtual key BudgetExceededError uses stale spend while /key/info shows spend below max_budget
signal.text: ## What happened? We saw failed proxy requests for a team-scoped virtual key where LiteLLM rejected the request with `BudgetExceededError`, but the current key/team spend reported by management APIs was still below the configured budget. This looks related to #27639, but this case is for a **virtual key max_budget** check rather than an end-user budget. ## Relevant LiteLLM version `1.84.0` From `/health/readiness`: ```json { "status": "healthy", "db": "connected", "cache": "redis", "litellm_version": "1.84.0", "use_aiohttp_transport": true, "log_level": "WARNING" } ``` Runtime from traceback: Python `3.13` in `/app/.venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/litellm/...`. ## Setup LiteLLM proxy with: - Postgres DB connected - Redis cache connected - Team-scoped virtual keys - `budget_duration: 30d` - OpenRouter model group Example sanitized virtual key config: ```json { "key_alias": "<service>-Dev", "team_id": "<team-id>", "models": [ "openrouter/qwen/qwen3.5-27b", "openrouter/qwen/qwen3.6-flash" ], "max_budget": 10.0, "budget_duration": "30d", "budget_reset_at": "2026-06-01T00:00:00Z", "blocked": null, "soft_budget_cooldown": false } ``` The team budget was much higher: ```json { "team_alias": "<team>", "spend": 3.546499379999998, "max_budget": 100.0, "budget_duration": "30d" } ``` ## Actual behavior `/spend/logs/v2` showed `15` failures for the virtual key in one day. `13/15` failures were `BudgetExceededError` before the LLM call was made. All failures had: ```json { "status": "failure", "model": "openrouter/qwen/qwen3.5-27b", "spend": 0.0, "total_tokens": 0, "request_duration_ms": 0, "api_base": "", "model_id": "" } ``` The actual error was only visible under `metadata.error_information`: ```json { "metadata": { "error_information": { "error_code": "429", "error_class": "BudgetExceededError", "llm_provider": "", "error_message": "Budget has been exceeded! Current cost: 10.607015384999993, Max budget: 10.0" }, "user_api_key_alias": "<service>-Dev", "user_api_key_team_alias": "<team>", "user_api_key_team_id": "<team-id>" } } ``` A few minutes/hours later, management APIs showed the same key was not over budget: ```json { "key_alias": "<service>-Dev", "spend": 3.536490479999998, "max_budget": 10.0, "budget_duration": "30d", "budget_reset_at": "2026-06-01T00:00:00+00:00", "blocked": null, "soft_budget_cooldown": false } ``` So the failed request saw `Current cost: 10.48-10.60`, while `/key/info` and `/key/list` later showed spend around `3.536 / 10`. ## Expected behavior The virtual key budget check should be consistent with the spend shown by `/key/info` / `/key/list`, or the API should expose which Redis/reservation counter is being used for the budget decision. If a stale Redis reservation/counter can trigger the check, it should be finalized/decremented reliably so a virtual key is not blocked while its DB/current spend is below budget. ## Additional logging/API issue For these failed logs, `/spend/logs/v2` returns top-level error fields as null: ```json { "error_code": null, "error_message": null, "error_class": null } ``` But the real error exists at: ```text metadata.error_information.error_code metadata.error_information.error_class metadata.error_information.error_message ``` This makes it hard for the UI/API consumers to filter or summarize failures unless they know to inspect nested metadata. Expected: top-level `error_code`, `error_class`, and `error_message` should be populated from `metadata.error_information` for failed proxy requests, or the docs/API response schema should make this nesting explicit. ## Failure summary For the affected key on one day: ```json { "total_failures": 15, "by_error_class": [ {"error_class": "APIError", "count": 2}, {"error_class": "BudgetExceededError", "count": 13} ], "by_model": [ {"model": "openrouter/qwen/qwen3.5-27b", "count": 15} ] } ``` The two `APIError` entries were unrelated OpenRouter parse errors. The recurring issue is the 13 virtual-key `BudgetExceededError` failures. ## Impact Production requests from the dev virtual key were rejected with HTTP 429 despite current key/team spend being below budget, causing intermittent service failures and confusing failure logs.

signal.title: fix(router): honor weights when first deployment has none in simple-shuffle
signal.text: ## Relevant issues Fixes #33329 ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix The bug is a pure routing decision inside simple_shuffle, so the proof runs the exact offline reproduction script from the issue body, which patches only the two random pick functions so the chosen routing path is observable and deterministic. Both runs use the identical script saved as repro_33329.py; the only variable is the checked out commit Before, at base commit 10d5804b3ef4ead5abb77c3f5fafdd0c0159de0f (litellm_oss_daily_2026_07_14): ```shell $ PYTHONPATH=. uv run --no-sync python repro_33329.py openai/first uniform calls: 1 weighted calls: 0 ``` After, at fix commit ebb0c0de9dc27528210dc033fc1453f258b56119: ```shell $ PYTHONPATH=. uv run --no-sync python repro_33329.py openai/second uniform calls: 0 weighted calls: 1 ``` The deployment that has the configured weight is now selected through the weighted pick path, and reversing the deployment list no longer changes the routing mode; the regression test asserts both orders ## Type Bug Fix ## Changes simple_shuffle decided whether to use a weighted pick by reading the metric (weight, rpm, tpm) from healthy_deployments[0] only. When the first healthy deployment did not set the metric but a later one did, the function fell through to uniform random.choice, so whether configured weights were honored depended on list order, which shifts with cooldowns, filtering, and attempted-deployment exclusion The fix enables a metric when any healthy deployment has a non-null value for it. The weight vector is still built with m["litellm_params"].get(weight_by, 0), so deployments without the metric keep contributing weight 0 and the existing zero-total fallthrough to the next metric is unchanged Added tests/test_litellm/router_strategy/test_simple_shuffle.py with a regression test parametrized over weight, rpm, and tpm that puts the metric only on the second deployment, asserts the weighted path is used with the normalized weight vector, and repeats the assertion with the deployment list reversed

signal.title: fix(router): apply model_info nested under litellm_params instead of dropping it
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Custom pricing nested one level deeper is silently dropped - Those deployments then log $0.00 spend forever - A common config mistake fails without any warning - Budgets keyed on that spend never fire How it solves it: - Detect model info nested under the params block - Promote it to where it is read, and warn once - Correctly-placed config keeps working unchanged ## User Flow Before: an admin puts a deployment's pricing one level deeper than expected, the proxy starts cleanly, and every request on that deployment records $0.00. 1. The admin adds a deployment to `config.yaml` where `model_info` (carrying `input_cost_per_token` / `output_cost_per_token`) is nested **inside** the params block rather than beside it, then starts the proxy 2. The proxy starts with no error or warning about the placement 3. A developer sends POST `https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions` against that deployment and gets a normal completion 4. `https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs` shows the request at **$0.00**, and the custom rates the admin set are nowhere in effect 5. A monthly budget on that key never triggers, because recorded spend stays at zero After: the misplacement is tolerated and announced. 1. The admin adds the same deployment with the same nesting, and starts the proxy 2. The proxy logs a warning naming that deployment and saying its model info was found in the wrong place 3. The developer sends the same POST `https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions` and gets the same completion 4. `https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs` shows the request priced at the admin's configured rates 5. The budget enforces correctly, and the admin can move the block to silence the warning ## Relevant issues Fixes #35691 ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Captured at commit `09889e1986` (`litellm_internal_staging`). Deployment registration and cost lookup both run before any provider call, so the proof drives the real Router startup path directly. Worth recording how this diagnosis was reached: my first explanation of #35691 was wrong, and three independent verification passes refuted it. Reading the reporter's actual config showed the real cause — the pricing was nested a level deeper than the code reads it, so it was never seen at all. The wrong fix was discarded rather than shipped. **Before:** a deployment whose `model_info` sits inside the params block registers with no custom pricing, and cost for its requests resolves to `0.0` with no warning emitted. **After:** the same config emits a warning naming the deployment, the pricing is promoted to where it is read, and cost resolves at the configured rates. A correctly-placed `model_info` takes exactly the same path as before — 6/6 tests cover both placements plus the warning. ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats - Warns rather than erroring, so existing misconfigured deployments keep serving ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signal.title: fix(vertex_ai): stop dropping conversation history on agent engine
signal.text:
## TLDR Problem this solves: - Only the last message ever reaches the agent - Every turn starts with no conversation context How it solves it: - Flatten the whole message list when there is no session - Send only the new message when the caller supplies one ## User Flow Before: a developer chatting with a Vertex AI Agent Engine deployment finds the agent remembers nothing they said 1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with `model: vertex_ai/agent_engine/<id>` and one user message naming their internal project, and get an acknowledgement back 2. They send the same POST again with all three messages, the two above plus "What is my internal project called?" 3. The reply does not name the project, because the two earlier messages were dropped and only the last question was forwarded After: the same conversation carries its own context 1. They send the same first POST and get the same acknowledgement 2. They send the same three-message POST 3. The reply names the project, because the earlier turns now travel with the request ## Relevant issues None open for this specific behaviour. Related report against the same provider: #19121 ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally - [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix A note on the setup, so it is not overstated. The provider needs a real reasoning engine on Vertex AI, which I have access to, and a proxy instance a reviewer could reach, which I do not. So each commit builds the request body it would send, and both bodies then go to a deployed Agent Engine agent in `europe-west1` as real unmocked calls. What differs between the two runs is only the body the provider produced. Shared setup, the same three-message conversation on both sides: ```python messages = [ {"role": "user", "content": "My internal project is called QUARTZ-BADGER-7731."}, {"role": "assistant", "content": "Understood."}, {"role": "user", "content": "What is my internal project called?"}, ] ``` The token is deliberately one the model cannot produce on its own, so an answer naming it can only have come from the conversation ### Before (5290150a05) 1. The merge base builds this body: ```json {"class_method": "stream_query", "input": {"message": "What is my internal project called?", "user_id": "pf-user"}} ``` 2. Send it to the deployment: ``` $ curl -sN -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ ".../reasoningEngines/<id>:streamQuery?alt=sse" -d @before.json HTTP 200 Here is a proposed research plan to identify your internal project name: * [RESEARCH] Investigate contextual workspace metadata, configuration files, and repository manifests to detect explicit internal project identifiers or codenames. * [RESEARCH] Analyze version control history, branch names, and commit messages for references to project aliases or development tags. ... ``` 3. The agent cannot name the project. The first two messages never left the gateway ### After (4b8c94a0eb) 1. The PR tip builds this body: ```json {"class_method": "stream_query", "input": {"message": "user: My internal project is called QUARTZ-BADGER-7731.

assistant: Understood.

user: What is my internal project called?", "user_id": "pf-user"}} ``` 2. Send it to the same deployment: ``` $ curl -sN -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ ".../reasoningEngines/<id>:streamQuery?alt=sse" -d @after.json HTTP 200 Your internal project is called **QUARTZ-BADGER-7731**. Would you like to initiate a new research plan or explore a specific topic related to this project? ``` 3. A caller who passes an explicit `session_id` still gets one message per turn, since the deployment holds that history itself ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - Flattening uses a plain `role: content` layout - Tool calls and image parts flatten to their text, as before - The proxy's own session id is deliberately not reused here - A per-request user id would make such a session unfindable anyway ### Final Attestation - [ ] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signal.title: [Bug]: provider_budget_config reports budget_reset_at ~57 years in the future without Redis
signal.text: ### What happened? With `provider_budget_config` and **no Redis configured**, `GET /provider/budgets` reports a `budget_reset_at` roughly 57 years in the future, so a monthly budget effectively never resets. Config: ```yaml router_settings: provider_budget_config: openrouter: budget_limit: 5 time_period: 30d ``` Response: ```json {"providers":{"openrouter":{"budget_limit":5.0,"time_period":"30d", "spend":4.8888e-06,"budget_reset_at":"2083-05-04T16:04:00.635943+00:00"}}} ``` Same result with `time_period: 1mo` (`2083-05-05T15:39:32`), so it is not specific to the period format. Today's date when this was captured: 2026-08-18. ### Root cause `async_get_ttl` means different things in the two cache backends, and `_get_current_provider_budget_reset_at` assumes the Redis meaning: - `RedisCache.async_get_ttl()` returns **remaining seconds** (Redis `TTL`). - `InMemoryCache.async_get_ttl()` returns `self.ttl_dict.get(key)` — and `ttl_dict` stores an **absolute expiry timestamp**: `self.ttl_dict[key] = time.time() + float(kwargs["ttl"])` (`litellm/caching/in_memory_cache.py`). `litellm/router_strategy/budget_limiter.py`: ```python if self.dual_cache.redis_cache: ttl_seconds = await self.dual_cache.redis_cache.async_get_ttl(spend_key) else: ttl_seconds = await self.dual_cache.async_get_ttl(spend_key) if ttl_seconds is None: return None return (datetime.now(timezone.utc) + timedelta(seconds=ttl_seconds)).isoformat() ``` Without Redis, `ttl_seconds` is an absolute unix timestamp (~1.79e9), so the result is `now + ~56.7 years` — which matches the observed 2083. The budget limit itself works; only the reported reset time (and therefore the reset window for in-memory deployments) is wrong. ### Suggested fix Either make `InMemoryCache.async_get_ttl` return remaining seconds like the Redis backend does, or convert at the call site: ```python ttl_seconds = await self.dual_cache.async_get_ttl(spend_key) ttl_seconds = ttl_seconds - time.time() # in-memory stores absolute expiry ``` The first option is preferable — `async_get_ttl` returning different units per backend is a trap for any other caller. ### Relevant log output ``` LiteLLM.LoggingError: [Non-Blocking] Exception occurred while success logging File ".../litellm/router_strategy/budget_limiter.py", line 412, in async_log_success_event raise ValueError("custom_llm_provider is required") ValueError: custom_llm_provider is required ``` Separate but related observation while testing the same feature: every request through a `pass_through_endpoints` route raises the above in `budget_limiter.async_log_success_event`, so pass-through traffic is not counted toward provider budgets at all. Happy to file that separately if useful. ### Are you a ML Ops Team? No ### What LiteLLM version are you on? v1.97.0 ### Twitter / LinkedIn details _No response_

signal.title: [Bug]: GET /health returns extra_headers and aws_session_token in plaintext
signal.text: ### Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. Related, not a duplicate: #18818 fixed masking of `extra_headers` on `/model/info`. `GET /health` is a different sanitizer. It still returns those values in full. `api_key` is stripped (CVE-2025-11203 class). `extra_headers` and `aws_session_token` were never added to that strip list. ### What happened? LiteLLM 1.96.2. No master key. A deployment in `config.yaml` has `extra_headers` (Azure `api-key`, Google `x-goog-api-key`, a Bearer token) and `aws_session_token`. `GET /health` returns those values in plaintext on the healthy (or unhealthy) row. `api_key` is absent. `api_base` is absent for a non-admin caller. The extra headers stay. This was reproduced with fake `CANARY_*` strings, not real provider keys. A live proxy with a normal `api_key: os.environ/...` and no `extra_headers` does not echo the resolved key on `/model/info` (`api_key` is popped). The hole is specifically fields that are not `api_key`. Expected: `/health` should omit or mask `extra_headers`, `headers`, and `aws_session_token` the same way it already omits `api_key`. ### User Flow Before a (hypothetical) fix: a tenant who can call `/health` can read the admin's upstream credentials out of the JSON. 1. The proxy admin puts provider auth in `litellm_params.extra_headers` (and optionally `aws_session_token`) in `config.yaml`, then starts the proxy on `http://127.0.0.1:4000`. 2. Any caller sends `GET http://127.0.0.1:4000/health` with no `Authorization` header (default install, no master key). 3. HTTP 200. The `healthy_endpoints` (or `unhealthy_endpoints`) row contains `extra_headers.Authorization`, `extra_headers.x-goog-api-key`, `extra_headers.api-key`, and `aws_session_token` in full. 4. That caller can take those values and call the provider directly, bypassing the proxy. After a (hypothetical) fix: the same `/health` call still reports healthy/unhealthy, but those secret fields are gone or masked. 1. The proxy admin uses the same `config.yaml` and starts the same proxy. 2. The same caller sends `GET http://127.0.0.1:4000/health`. 3. HTTP 200. The row still has `model` and health status. It does not contain the `extra_headers` values or `aws_session_token`. 4. That caller cannot recover the admin's upstream credentials from `/health`. ### Proof the bug occurs Config / setup the proxy ran with: ```yaml model_list: - model_name: mock litellm_params: model: openai/mockmodel api_base: http://127.0.0.1:9996/v1 api_key: sk-x-CANARY_DEPLOYMENT_API_KEY extra_headers: Authorization: Bearer CANARY_EXTRA_HEADERS_AUTHORIZATION x-goog-api-key: CANARY_X_GOOG_API_KEY_VALUE api-key: CANARY_AZURE_STYLE_API_KEY aws_session_token: CANARY_AWS_SESSION_TOKEN_VALUE ``` The backend at `127.0.0.1:9996` is a local OpenAI-compatible stub that returns HTTP 200 so the row lands in `healthy_endpoints`. The leak is the proxy copying `litellm_params` into the `/health` body. It does not depend on a real provider key. You can drop the stub: point `api_base` at `http://127.0.0.1:1`. The health check fails, and the same fields still appear under `unhealthy_endpoints`. No API key required. Version or commit: LiteLLM **1.96.2** Commands and their full output: ``` curl -s http://127.0.0.1:4000/health ``` ```json { "healthy_endpoints": [ { "model": "openai/mockmodel", "extra_headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer CANARY_EXTRA_HEADERS_AUTHORIZATION", "x-goog-api-key": "CANARY_X_GOOG_API_KEY_VALUE", "api-key": "CANARY_AZURE_STYLE_API_KEY" }, "aws_session_token": "CANARY_AWS_SESSION_TOKEN_VALUE" } ], "unhealthy_endpoints": [], "healthy_count": 1, "unhealthy_count": 0 } ``` `api_key` is not in that object. `GET /v1/models` and `GET /health/liveliness` do not contain the canaries. Copy-paste repro, no keys, no stub: ```yaml # leak.yaml model_list: - model_name: demo litellm_params: model: openai/gpt-4o-mini api_base: http://127.0.0.1:1 api_key: sk-not-a-real-key extra_headers: x-goog-api-key: CANARY_X_GOOG_API_KEY_VALUE api-key: CANARY_AZURE_STYLE_API_KEY aws_session_token: CANARY_AWS_SESSION_TOKEN_VALUE ``` ``` litellm --config leak.yaml --port 4000 --host 127.0.0.1 curl -s http://127.0.0.1:4000/health ``` The canaries show up on the unhealthy row. ### What part of LiteLLM is this about? Proxy ### What LiteLLM version are you on ? v1.96.2
