AZURE_CLIENT_ID=... AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET=... unset AZURE_AI_API_KEY OPENAI_API_KEY cat > /tmp/azure_ai_entra.yaml <<'YAML' model_list: - model_name: azure-embed litellm_params: model: azure_ai/cohere-embed-v3-english api_base: os.environ/AZURE_AI_API_BASE tenant_id: os.environ/AZURE_TENANT_ID client_id: os.environ/AZURE_CLIENT_ID client_secret: os.environ/AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET - model_name: azure-rerank litellm_params: model: azure_ai/cohere-rerank-v3-english api_base: os.environ/AZURE_AI_API_BASE tenant_id: os.environ/AZURE_TENANT_ID client_id: os.environ/AZURE_CLIENT_ID client_secret: os.environ/AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET YAML python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config /tmp/azure_ai_entra.yaml --detailed_debug 2>&1 | tee litellm.log curl -sS http://localhost:4000/v1/embeddings -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-1234' \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"model": "azure-embed", "input": ["good morning from litellm"]}' curl -sS http://localhost:4000/v1/rerank -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-1234' \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"model": "azure-rerank", "query": "what is litellm", "documents": ["litellm is an llm gateway", "the weather is nice"]}' ``` Before this change both calls fail during validation with a missing-API-key error even though the service principal is configured; after it they return a real embedding and a real rerank result billed to the Foundry project ## Type 🆕 New Feature 🐛 Bug Fix ## Changes `get_azure_ai_auth_headers(api_key, litellm_params, api_key_header, api_key_env_var)` in `litellm/llms/azure_ai/common_utils.py` is the single auth entry point for Foundry routes. It keeps whatever header a route already used for API keys (`api-key`, `Api-Key`, `Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key`, or a bearer `Authorization`), and when no key is configured it resolves a token through the provider's existing `get_azure_ad_token`, which already understands service principals, `azure_ad_token`, OIDC federated tokens, username/password, managed identity and `DefaultAzureCredential`, plus `azure_scope`: ```python if api_key: return {api_key_header: f"Bearer {api_key}" if api_key_header == "Authorization" else api_key} azure_ad_token = get_azure_ai_entra_token(litellm_params=litellm_params) if azure_ad_token: return {"Authorization": f"Bearer {azure_ad_token}"} raise ValueError("Missing Azure AI credentials - ...") ``` Callers: embeddings (`litellm/main.py`), image generation (`litellm/images/main.py`, which still leaves a caller-supplied `api-key` / `Authorization` header untouched), rerank, Azure AI OCR, Document Intelligence OCR, and the FLUX / FLUX 2 / MAI image edit configs Rerank needed plumbing: `BaseRerankConfig.validate_environment` now takes `litellm_params`, `BaseLLMHTTPHandler` passes it, and the other rerank configs accept the new keyword `get_azure_ad_token_from_entra_id` now goes through an `lru_cache`d factory keyed on tenant, client, secret and scope, so one `ClientSecretCredential` is built per credential set instead of one per request; the credential's own token cache then keeps AAD round trips to one per token lifetime Docs live in the docs repo: BerriAI/litellm-docs#728 ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/5df71ea3473e41b8913326682dab9d56 Requested by: @mateo-berri

signal.title: fix(vertex_ai): assemble agent engine responses from every event
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - A tool call ends the stream before the answer - Only one step's text survives a multi-step run - Reported token counts are replaced by a wrong estimate - Internal agent state can be returned as the answer How it solves it: - Only a text-bearing event may finish the stream - Keep every text part of every finalised event - Sum the counts Agent Engine actually returns - Drop the model's own reasoning parts from the answer ## User Flow Before: a developer calling a Vertex AI Agent Engine deployment that uses any tool gets an empty answer back 1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with `model: vertex_ai/agent_engine/<id>`, `"stream": true`, and one question 2. The agent calls one of its own tools, which arrives as an event carrying no text 3. The stream closes on that event, so the response is an empty message with `finish_reason: stop` 4. They repeat the request without `"stream": true` and get text back, but the `usage` block reports a few hundred tokens where the deployment charged several thousand 5. They open https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs and see that request logged at a fraction of its real spend After: the same requests return the answer and the spend the deployment reported 1. They send the same POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with `"stream": true` 2. The tool call arrives and the stream stays open 3. The answer streams in when the agent produces it, and `finish_reason: stop` arrives with it 4. The non-streaming repeat returns the same text with a `usage` block matching what the deployment charged 5. https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs shows that request at its real spend ## Relevant issues #19121 reported the stream ending early on Agent Engine deployments with MCP tools and proposed a fix in the thread. It was closed as stale without review, and the behaviour is unchanged on current main. This PR shares that diagnosis but deliberately does not surface the agent's `function_call` parts as OpenAI `tool_calls`. Agent Engine executes those server side, so a client that received them would be told to run functions it cannot run, and to reply with results the deployment is not waiting for ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally - [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix A note on the setup, so it is not overstated. The provider needs a real reasoning engine on Vertex AI, which I have access to, and a proxy instance a reviewer could reach, which I do not. So the live half is a real unmocked `:streamQuery` call against a deployed Agent Engine agent in `europe-west1`, and the two commits are then exercised by feeding that captured response through the provider on each one. The event shapes below are the API's, not mine. The same capture is committed, redacted, as the test fixture. Shared setup, one question to a deployment whose agent calls a single tool before answering: ``` $ curl -sN -X POST \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ "https://europe-west1-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/<project>/locations/europe-west1/reasoningEngines/<id>:streamQuery?alt=sse" \ -d '{"class_method":"stream_query","input":{"user_id":"pf-user","message":"What is my internal project called?"}}' [0] partial=None finish_reason=None parts=[] [1] partial=False finish_reason=STOP parts=[function_call, thought_signature] usage: p=907 c=129 t=1036 [2] partial=None finish_reason=None parts=[function_response] [3] partial=False finish_reason=STOP parts=[text(1162 chars)] usage: p=1120 c=225 t=1345 [4] partial=None finish_reason=None parts=[] ``` Event 1 is the tool call. It reports `finish_reason: STOP` and carries no text. The answer is in event 3, and the run was billed for two model calls totalling 2381 tokens ### Before (5290150a05) 1. Feed the captured response to the streaming iterator and the non-streaming transform on the merge base: ``` STREAMING stopped at event: 1 of 4 STREAMING client received : '' NON-STREAMING usage : prompt=8 completion=226 total=234 ``` 2. The stream closes on the tool call, so a streaming caller receives an empty message. The non-streaming path discards the 2381 tokens the deployment reported and substitutes a 234 token estimate produced by a gpt-3.5 tokenizer ### After (1969770c4b) 1. Feed the same captured response through the same two paths at the PR tip: ``` STREAMING stopped at event: 3 of 4 STREAMING client received : 'Here is a proposed research plan to identify your internal p' NON-STREAMING usage : prompt=2027 completion=354 total=2381 ``` 2. The tool call passes through, the answer reaches the caller, and usage is the sum of what both model calls reported ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - This capture had one text event; concatenation is covered by tests - Partial events are skipped so finalised text and counts are not doubled - The capture emitted `partial: false` only; incremental deltas are unverified - Streaming still forwards partials as deltas, which streaming callers want - Usage summing is non-streaming only; the wrapper aggregates streaming itself ### Final Attestation - [ ] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signal.title: [Bug]: Serving a request permanently clears that model's pricing from /v2/model/info (Model Management Costs column goes blank)
signal.text: ### What happened? Serving a single completion for a model permanently clears that model's `input_cost_per_token` / `output_cost_per_token` from `/v2/model/info`, so the **Costs** column on the Model Management page goes blank for that model. The price never comes back on its own. The net effect is that the models you actually use show no pricing in the UI, while the models you have never called still show theirs — which is a confusing signal, because it looks like the *used* models are the misconfigured ones. The pricing data itself is fine the whole time: `litellm.model_cost` still holds the correct entry, and cost tracking keeps working (the `x-litellm-response-cost` header stays exact). This is a reporting bug in `/v2/model/info` only. ### Config (nothing custom — no pricing overrides anywhere) ```yaml model_list: - model_name: claude-fable-5 # control: never called litellm_params: model: anthropic/claude-fable-5 api_key: os.environ/ANTHROPIC_API_KEY - model_name: claude-haiku-4-5 # the one we call litellm_params: model: anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 api_key: os.environ/ANTHROPIC_API_KEY general_settings: master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY store_model_in_db: true ``` ### Steps to reproduce 1. `POST /reload/model_cost_map` (to start from a known-good state — every model reports its price) 2. `GET /v2/model/info` — both models report prices 3. `POST /chat/completions` with `{"model": "claude-haiku-4-5", ...}` — one request, succeeds normally 4. `GET /v2/model/info` again ``` reload Price data reloaded successfully! 3054 models updated. BEFORE claude-fable-5 input_cost_per_token=1e-05 output_cost_per_token=5e-05 BEFORE claude-haiku-4-5 input_cost_per_token=1e-06 output_cost_per_token=5e-06 BEFORE cost map claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 input=1e-06 output=5e-06 --- one request to claude-haiku-4-5; response cost header = 3.3e-05 --- AFTER claude-fable-5 input_cost_per_token=1e-05 output_cost_per_token=5e-05 AFTER claude-haiku-4-5 input_cost_per_token=None output_cost_per_token=None AFTER cost map claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 input=1e-06 output=5e-06 ``` Only the model that was called loses its pricing. The untouched control model keeps its. `litellm.model_cost` (via `/public/litellm_model_cost_map`) is unchanged and still correct, and the request billed correctly (`3.3e-05` = 8 in × $1/M + 5 out × $5/M). Leaving the proxy idle does **not** cause the drop — only traffic to that specific model does. I verified this by reloading, waiting 20s with no traffic (prices stayed), then calling one model (only that one dropped). ### What I think is going on Two things combine: 1. After a request, that deployment's `model_info` contains the cost keys as explicit `None` rather than being absent. `Deployment.__init__` (`litellm/types/router.py`, ~L442-457) normalises a `model_info` dict through the `ModelInfo` pydantic model, which materialises every unset cost field as `None`; the router passes the deployment's `model_info` into per-request kwargs at `litellm/router.py:3170`. 2. `_enrich_model_info_with_litellm_data` (`litellm/proxy/proxy_server.py`, ~L11761) then backfills from the cost map with: ```python for k, v in litellm_model_info.items(): if k not in model_info: model_info[k] = v ``` That fills keys that are **absent**, but never keys that are present-and-`None`. So once step 1 has written a `None`, the cost map can no longer heal it, and the value stays blank for the life of the process. A merge that treated `None` as "not set" (`if model_info.get(k) is None`) would fix the symptom; not clobbering the deployment's `model_info` with a null-filled dump in the first place would fix the cause. ### Workaround `POST /reload/model_cost_map` (or the reload button in the UI) rebuilds the deployments and restores every price — but only until each model is called again. ### Relevant log output No errors are logged; requests succeed normally and are billed correctly. ### Are you a ML Ops Team? Yes ### What LiteLLM version are you on? litellm 1.97.0 (`ghcr.io/berriai/litellm-database:main-stable`), litellm-proxy-extras 0.4.84, litellm-enterprise 0.1.54, Python 3.13.15, Postgres-backed with `store_model_in_db: true`.

signal.title: [Bug]: DeepSeek thinking-by-default models + tools: _fill_reasoning_content guard never fires without explicit reasoning params, upstream 400
signal.text: ## What happened? DeepSeek V4 models (`deepseek-v4-pro`, `deepseek-v4-flash`) run **thinking mode by default server-side**. In a multi-turn tool-calling loop, DeepSeek's API requires `reasoning_content` to be passed back on assistant messages, otherwise it returns: ``` 400 {"error":{"message":"The `reasoning_content` in the thinking mode must be passed back to the API.", "type":"invalid_request_error"}} ``` LiteLLM already handles this: `DeepSeekChatConfig._fill_reasoning_content` (added for #28045) promotes `provider_specific_fields.reasoning_content` or injects a minimal placeholder. However, the gate that decides whether to run it assumes thinking is **opt-in**: ```python # litellm/llms/deepseek/chat/transformation.py def _thinking_mode_active(self, model: str, optional_params: dict) -> bool: return ( supports_reasoning(model=model, custom_llm_provider="deepseek") and (optional_params.get("thinking") or {}).get("type") == "enabled" ) ``` When the request carries **no** `thinking`/`reasoning_effort` at all — the common case for a router/proxy deployment that doesn't inject reasoning params — the guard is `False`, `_fill_reasoning_content` never runs, and the DeepSeek API rejects every second call of a tool loop with the 400 above. The model was in thinking mode the whole time; the request just never said so. The guard's opt-in assumption is documented in its own comment ("preventing spurious injection on models like deepseek-v3.2 that support thinking as opt-in but not always-on") — correct for opt-in models, wrong for thinking-by-default models. ## Reproduction (litellm proxy v1.96.2 or SDK) ```python import litellm TOOLS = [{"type": "function", "function": {"name": "get_time", "description": "Get current time", "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {}}}}] MSGS = [ {"role": "user", "content": "What time is it? Use the tool."}, {"role": "assistant", "content": "", "tool_calls": [{"id": "call_1", "type": "function", "function": {"name": "get_time", "arguments": "{}"}}]}, {"role": "tool", "tool_call_id": "call_1", "content": "14:32 UTC"}, ] # FAILS with the 400 above — no reasoning params, guard never fires: litellm.completion(model="deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro", messages=MSGS, tools=TOOLS) # WORKS — reasoning_effort maps to thinking:{"type":"enabled"}, guard fires, # _fill_reasoning_content runs: litellm.completion(model="deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro", messages=MSGS, tools=TOOLS, reasoning_effort="high") ``` Both verified against the live DeepSeek API through a litellm proxy v1.96.2. ## Expected behavior For models whose thinking mode is on by default, `_fill_reasoning_content` should run unless the request **explicitly disables** thinking (`thinking: {"type": "disabled"}` / `reasoning_effort: "none"` — explicit disable works today and needs no fill: verified that a disabled-thinking tool loop passes). ## Proposed fix Make the default-on property data-driven and extend the guard: 1. Add a capability flag in the model cost map for thinking-by-default models (e.g. `"thinking_by_default": true` on `deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro`, `deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash`, and other always-on reasoning models). 2. Change the guard to: ```python def _thinking_mode_active(self, model: str, optional_params: dict) -> bool: if not supports_reasoning(model=model, custom_llm_provider="deepseek"): return False thinking = (optional_params.get("thinking") or {}).get("type") if thinking == "enabled": return True if thinking == "disabled": return False return thinking_by_default(model) # <- new: no explicit choice on the wire ``` This keeps the #28045 behavior intact for opt-in models (deepseek-v3.2) and closes the hole for default-on models. ## Workaround we're using today Pin `reasoning_effort` on the proxy deployment so the guard fires (wire-neutral: every non-`"none"` value maps to plain `thinking: {"type": "enabled"}`, which is already the server default): ```yaml - model_name: deepseek-v4-pro litellm_params: model: deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro api_key: os.environ/DEEPSEEK_API_KEY reasoning_effort: "high" ``` ## Environment - litellm v1.96.2 (proxy, `ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.96.2`) - Models: `deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro`, `deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash` - Surfaced at scale behind a router where client requests carry no reasoning params (the deployment decides) — every tool-using turn 400s on its second call.

signal.title: feat(wavespeed): add WaveSpeed AI image and video generation
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - WaveSpeed image and video models need hand-rolled REST calls - No LiteLLM routing, fallbacks, or logging for them - #34620 covers only the chat half of #34618 How it solves it: - Adds `wavespeed` image generation with submit-then-poll - Adds `wavespeed` video generation on the OpenAI video contract - Registers the OpenAI-compatible chat endpoint as a JSON provider ## User Flow Before: a developer generating images through the gateway cannot route to WaveSpeed at all, so they call it out of band and lose gateway logging and fallbacks 1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/images/generations with `{"model": "wavespeed/bytedance/seedream-v5.0-pro", "prompt": "a red panda"}` 2. The gateway answers 400 saying the provider is not supported 3. They fall back to calling WaveSpeed themselves, submitting the task and polling for the result in their own code, and nothing about that spend or latency lands in https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs After: the same request works, and the gateway does the polling 1. The proxy admin sets `WAVESPEED_API_KEY` and adds `model: wavespeed/bytedance/seedream-v5.0-pro` 2. The developer sends the same POST https://litellm-domain/v1/images/generations 3. The response is a normal image payload whose `data[0].url` is a hosted WaveSpeed URL, returned once the task finished 4. For video they send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/videos with `{"model": "wavespeed/bytedance/seedance-2.5/text-to-video", "prompt": "..."}`, get back a video id with status `queued`, poll GET https://litellm-domain/v1/videos/{id} until `completed`, then download GET https://litellm-domain/v1/videos/{id}/content 5. Both requests appear in https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs ## Relevant issues Addresses the media generation half of #34618 Relationship to #34620: that PR, opened by a bot and currently blocked on an unsigned CLA, registers the same chat provider and adds 92 LLM cost map entries. This PR deliberately does not duplicate the cost map. It repeats only the small registration needed for `wavespeed` to exist as a provider at all, since the image and video surfaces depend on it. If #34620 lands first I will rebase and drop the overlapping registration hunks; if it does not, this PR still leaves chat working, minus per-model pricing. The chat registration here matches #34620's, including the base URL and the rule that only the leading `wavespeed/` prefix is stripped, and credit for working that out belongs to that PR Docs live in BerriAI/litellm-docs#962, which has to merge for `code-quality` and `documentation` to go green here: `test_env_keys.py` fails until `WAVESPEED_API_KEY` and `WAVESPEED_API_BASE` are in the environment variables reference ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/<your_test_file>.py -v` - [x] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Not captured. Every WaveSpeed media call is a billable generation and I did not want to bill a live account from an automated run, so the only runs here are the mocked tests. The commands a reviewer can use once `WAVESPEED_API_KEY` is set, against a proxy configured with `model: wavespeed/wavespeed-ai/z-image/turbo` and `model: wavespeed/bytedance/seedance-2.5/text-to-video`: ```bash curl http://localhost:4000/v1/images/generations -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model": "wavespeed/wavespeed-ai/z-image/turbo", "prompt": "a red panda skateboarding", "size": "1024x1024"}' curl http://localhost:4000/v1/videos -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model": "wavespeed/bytedance/seedance-2.5/text-to-video", "prompt": "a red panda skateboarding", "seconds": "5"}' ``` ## Type 🆕 New Feature ## Caveats (if any) - Chat cost map entries are left to #34620 - No cost tracking yet for image or video - Remix, list, delete, edit, extension are not supported - `response_format: b64_json` is rejected; WaveSpeed returns URLs - Needs BerriAI/litellm-docs#962 for the docs gates - Video content downloads go through the shared SSRF guard ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signal.title: [Bug]: azure/gpt-5.6* entries missing cache_creation_input_token_cost — cache writes billed at zero since v1.97.0
signal.text: ### Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. ### What happened? Every `azure/gpt-5.6*` entry in the price map lacks `cache_creation_input_token_cost`, while its non-Azure counterpart has it. Since v1.97.0 correctly classifies Azure's `cache_write_tokens` as cache-creation tokens, those tokens now resolve to no rate and are billed at **zero**. This is a regression in effect, though not in code. Before v1.97.0 the same tokens were folded into plain input and under-reported by ~20%; now they are dropped entirely and under-report by ~98%. The fix for #33772 corrected the code path and the OpenAI entries, but the Azure entries were not updated to match. All eight Azure entries are missing the key; all four non-Azure counterparts have it: | Model | input_cost_per_token | cache_creation_input_token_cost | |---|---|---| | `gpt-5.6` | 5e-06 | 6.25e-06 | | `azure/gpt-5.6` | 5e-06 | **missing** | | `azure/us/gpt-5.6` | 5.5e-06 | **missing** | | `gpt-5.6-sol` | 5e-06 | 6.25e-06 | | `azure/gpt-5.6-sol` | 5e-06 | **missing** | | `azure/us/gpt-5.6-sol` | 5.5e-06 | **missing** | | `gpt-5.6-luna` | 2e-07 | 2.5e-07 | | `azure/gpt-5.6-luna` | 2e-07 | **missing** | | `azure/us/gpt-5.6-luna` | 2.2e-07 | **missing** | | `gpt-5.6-terra` | 2e-06 | 2.5e-06 | | `azure/gpt-5.6-terra` | 2e-06 | **missing** | | `azure/us/gpt-5.6-terra` | 2.2e-06 | **missing** | Azure prices cache writes at 1.25× input, same as OpenAI, so the values should mirror the non-Azure entries (with the 10% uplift already present on `azure/us/*`). **Expected:** a request whose prompt tokens are mostly cache writes is billed at the cache-creation rate. **Actual:** those tokens cost nothing, so spend is under-reported by ~98%. Not a duplicate of #36094 — that one is about the per-token input/output prices for Luna being wrong by 5×. This one is about a missing key across the whole gpt-5.6 Azure family causing cache-write tokens to price at zero. Fixing either leaves the other in place. ### User Flow Before a (hypothetical) fix: a platform team charging back Azure OpenAI spend per team sees almost nothing billed for their RAG service, whose requests carry a large cached system prompt 1. Their RAG service sends POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with "model": "azure-gpt-5.6-sol" and a ~2,200-token system prompt 2. The response comes back 200 with "usage": {"prompt_tokens": 2219, "prompt_tokens_details": {"cache_write_tokens": 2217}} 3. They open https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs and the request shows $0.000225 spend 4. Their monthly Azure invoice for the same traffic is roughly 60× higher than the total the gateway reports, so per-team chargeback is unusable After a (hypothetical) fix: the same request is billed at the cache-write rate, and the gateway total lines up with the invoice 1. Their RAG service sends the same POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with "model": "azure-gpt-5.6-sol" and the same ~2,200-token system prompt 2. The response comes back 200 with the same usage object 3. https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs shows that request at $0.014015 spend 4. The monthly total tracks the Azure invoice, so chargeback per team is accurate ### Proof the bug occurs **Config / setup the proxy ran with:** ```yaml model_list: - model_name: azure-gpt-5.6-sol litellm_params: model: azure/gpt-5.6-sol api_base: os.environ/AZURE_OPENAI_ENDPOINT api_version: "2025-04-01-preview" general_settings: master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY database_url: os.environ/DATABASE_URL ``` Live Azure OpenAI deployment, `gpt-5.6-sol`, GlobalStandard. ' + ( 'The following is reference material about cloud architecture patterns. signal.title: fix(guardrails): take caller identity on /guardrails/apply_guardrail from auth, not the body
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Caller metadata decides identity on `/guardrails/apply_guardrail` - A caller can claim any alias or team id - Guardrails keyed on that metadata can be steered How it solves it: - Authenticated identity is layered over caller metadata - Uses the same sanitizer the in-line request path uses - Non-identity metadata still passes through untouched ## User Flow Before: a guardrail configured to treat one team differently can be talked into it by anyone 1. An admin runs a guardrail that behaves differently for a known key alias or team id, reading it from request metadata 2. A caller sends POST https://litellm-domain/guardrails/apply_guardrail with `"metadata": {"user_api_key_alias": "<the privileged alias>"}` and their own text 3. The response comes back as if the request came from that alias, so text the guardrail would otherwise act on is returned untouched After: the same request is judged on who the caller actually is 1. The caller sends the same POST with the same forged `metadata` 2. The proxy overwrites the identity fields with the ones authentication established for that key 3. The guardrail runs against the real identity, so the forged alias buys nothing, while any other metadata the caller sent still reaches the guardrail ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Live proxy on `localhost:4000` at commit `9ce19120fc`, postgres-backed, with a guardrail that skips work for one key alias and a guardrail endpoint that records every payload it receives. The route is admin-only, so the master key is used; its authenticated alias is empty, which is exactly what has to win over the alias the body claims. ``` $ # 1) forged identity in the body $ curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4000/guardrails/apply_guardrail \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"guardrail_name":"gg-skip-alias","text":"scan me","metadata":{"user_api_key_alias":"e2e-batch-worker"}}' 200 $ curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8787/_count # payloads the guardrail received {"records":1} $ # 2) the same call without the forged alias, for contrast 200 {"records":1} ``` Before this change the first call returned `{"records":0}`: the forged alias matched the exemption and the guardrail never ran. ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - `request_data` now always carries authenticated metadata - Callers relying on it being absent will see it ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR <!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY --> --- > [!NOTE] > <sup>[Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) is generating a summary for commit 2a7f02826f811a2bfa4e88201bea5de60d62431a. Anthropic returns 400: `messages.N.content.0.thinking: each thinking block must contain thinking` After: the same fallback request keeps history thinking blocks, so the fallback can actually run 1. Same fallback config with `additional_drop_params: ["thinking", ...]` 2. Same multi-turn request with thinking blocks in history 3. The primary model errors and the router falls back 4. The fallback request still has `messages[].content[].thinking` intact and is not rejected for an empty thinking block ## Relevant issues Fixes #37479 ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/<your_test_file>.py -v`. signal.title: v3 rate limiter double-counts team per-model limits (model_per_team) → effective RPM/TPM is half configured
signal.text: Repository owner assessment aside — filing precise repro + root cause. ### What happened Per-team per-model rate limits set via `POST /team/update {metadata: {model_rpm_limit: {...}}}` are enforced at **half** the configured value. A team-model limit of `N` starts returning 429 after ~`N/2` requests per window. ### Version `v1.83.14-stable` (also present on `main` as of filing — both code paths below still exist). ### Root cause In `litellm/proxy/hooks/parallel_request_limiter_v3.py`, `async_pre_call_hook` builds the descriptor list via **two** paths that each append the *same* `model_per_team` descriptor from the *same* `team_metadata["model_rpm_limit"]`: 1. `_create_rate_limit_descriptors()` → team block (~line 1011, via `get_team_model_rpm_limit()`), appends `RateLimitDescriptor(key="model_per_team", value=f"{team_id}:{model}")`. 2. `_add_team_model_rate_limit_descriptor_from_metadata()` (~line 1125, called from `async_pre_call_hook` ~line 1336), appends the **identical** descriptor. `should_rate_limit()` then puts that counter key into `keys_to_fetch` **twice** (no dedup), and `BATCH_RATE_LIMITER_SCRIPT` (`for i = 1, #KEYS, 2`) does `INCR` per pair → the counter is incremented **twice per request**. ### Evidence (self-hosted proxy, single instance) Team-model `model_rpm_limit = 20`, fired 30 requests through one pod: - Redis `{model_per_team:<team>:<model>}:requests` = **60** (2× the requests) - Redis `{model_per_key:<hash>:<model>}:requests` = **30** (1× — `model_per_key` is appended only once, so it is correct) Single-instance test rules out replica/counter-sharing effects — it is a per-request double-add. ### Expected Each request increments the `model_per_team` counter once; effective limit == configured limit. ### Suggested fix De-duplicate the team-model descriptor: keep exactly one of the two append sites (or dedupe descriptors by `(key, value)` before building `keys_to_fetch`). The `model_per_key` path (single append) is the correct reference.

They call `resources/list` and the upstream returns 401 After: the same OAuth session works for tools, prompts, and resources 1. They complete the same OAuth authorization code 2. `tools/list` and `tools/call` still succeed 3. `prompts/list` and `prompts/get` succeed with the same per-user credential 4. `resources/list`, `resources/read`, and `resources/templates/list` succeed as well Another user still cannot use this user's stored OAuth token, because the credential is resolved from the request's auth context rather than a process-wide default ## Relevant issues Fixes #37497 ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/<your_test_file>.py -v`. signal.title: fix(streaming): backfill response.completed output from output_item.done events
signal.text: ## Relevant issues Fixes #25429. Related to #26179. Supersedes #30934 ## Linear ticket N/A ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all unit tests on [`make test-unit`](https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/extras/contributing_code) (201 pre-existing failures in prisma/database, vertex AI, and MCP semantic filter tests; none in touched files — 324 tests across `tests/test_litellm/responses/` and `tests/test_litellm/llms/chatgpt/` pass cleanly) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have requested a Greptile review by commenting `@greptileai` and received a **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## CI (LiteLLM team) > **CI status guideline:** > > - 50-55 passing tests: main is stable with minor issues. > - 45-49 passing tests: acceptable but needs attention > - <= 40 passing tests: unstable; be careful with your merges and assess the risk. - [ ] **Branch creation CI run** Link: - [ ] **CI run for the last commit** Link: - [ ] **Merge / cherry-pick CI run** Links: ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix The `chatgpt/` provider routes through chatgpt.com's Codex backend, which sends `response.completed` with `output: []`. The actual assistant content arrives via preceding `response.output_item.done` SSE events. Without accumulation, the chat-completions bridge receives an empty output list and raises: ``` ChatgptException - Unknown items in responses API response: [] ``` The fix teaches `BaseResponsesAPIStreamingIterator._process_chunk` to accumulate `response.output_item.done` payloads as they stream in and backfill them into the `response.completed` chunk before it is stored as `completed_response`. Items are serialized to plain dicts via `model_dump()` so the downstream `_handle_raw_dict_response_item` callback in the transformation layer can process them. The existing `_recover_output_items_from_raw_sse` fallback in `LiteLLMResponsesTransformationHandler.transform_response` is preserved as a second layer if the streaming path is ever bypassed. **Before:** ``` $ curl -s http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-test" \ -d '{"model":"gpt-5.4","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Reply with exactly: hello"}],"stream":false}' {"error":{"message":"litellm.APIConnectionError: ChatgptException - Unknown items in responses API response: []. Received Model Group=gpt-5.4\nAvailable Model Group Fallbacks=None","type":null,"param":null,"code":"500"}} ``` **After:** ``` $ curl -s http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-test" \ -d '{"model":"gpt-5.4","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Reply with exactly: hello"}],"stream":false}' {"id":"chatcmpl-764df91c-940a-47ea-be8c-d2aff173b8f4","created":1782409329,"model":"gpt-5.4","object":"chat.completion","choices":[{"finish_reason":"stop","index":0,"message":{"content":"hello","role":"assistant"}}],"usage":{"completion_tokens":5,"prompt_tokens":1635,"total_tokens":1640,"completion_tokens_details":{"reasoning_tokens":0},"prompt_tokens_details":{"cached_tokens":0}}} ``` ## Type Bug Fix ## Changes `BaseResponsesAPIStreamingIterator` accumulates `response.output_item.done` items into `_streamed_output_items` during streaming. A secondary `_streamed_text_only_items` dict catches providers that emit `response.output_text.done` without a preceding `response.output_item.done`. At `response.completed` or `response.incomplete`, if `output` is empty and either dict is non-empty, the merged items are sorted by `output_index` and backfilled onto the response object. Items are serialized via `model_dump()` when they are Pydantic instances and passed through unchanged when they are already plain dicts; both the serialization and the assignment sit inside a `try/except` so any failure degrades to a logged warning rather than crashing the stream. `FallbackResponsesStreamWrapper` (router.py) and `MCPEnhancedStreamingIterator` (mcp_streaming_iterator.py) both bypass `super().__init__()` and are updated to mirror the two new instance attributes. Twelve regression tests are added to `tests/test_litellm/responses/test_streaming_iterator_output_recovery.py`, covering: the core backfill, multi-item index ordering, authoritative output preservation, `response.incomplete` backfill, `response.failed` no-backfill, `output_text.done` fallback, `output_item.done` precedence, replace-in-place content slots, gap padding, absent `output_index` sequential fallback, exception swallowing, and the dict-type contract required by the downstream transformation layer. The bulk of the line-count change in `streaming_iterator.py` is ruff reformatting of pre-existing code required to pass `ruff format`; the logical additions are confined to the accumulation block in `_process_chunk` and the two new instance attributes in `__init__`. <!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY --> --- > [!NOTE] > <sup>[Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) is generating a summary for commit 755a8b1e26224ae13cbf244bfe1b4b6077b98b61. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup> <!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

signal.title: [Bug]: Per-user authorization-code credentials are omitted from MCP prompt and resource operations
signal.text: ### Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. ### What happened? For an MCP server configured with per-user OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code credentials, LiteLLM applies the stored user credential to tool operations but not to prompt or resource operations. After the user completes OAuth, `tools/list` and `tools/call` work. The same upstream server returns 401 for `prompts/list` and `resources/list`, and LiteLLM turns those failures into empty lists. `prompts/get`, `resources/read`, and `resources/templates/list` use the same unauthenticated client-construction path and are affected as well. Expected behavior: every protected MCP operation should resolve and send the same stored per-user OAuth credential. Actual behavior: only the tool paths pass `user_api_key_auth` into `_create_mcp_client`, which is required by the Authorization Code credential resolver. The difference is visible in the v1.97.0 source: - Tool listing passes `user_api_key_auth`: https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/v1.97.0/litellm/proxy/_experimental/mcp_server/server.py#L1965-L2025 - Prompt and resource listing do not pass it to the manager: https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/v1.97.0/litellm/proxy/_experimental/mcp_server/server.py#L2130-L2305 - The manager constructs prompt and resource clients without `user_api_key_auth`: https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/v1.97.0/litellm/proxy/_experimental/mcp_server/mcp_server_manager.py#L3480-L3682 ### Steps to Reproduce 1. Configure an upstream Streamable HTTP MCP server that requires the same bearer token for tools, prompts, and resources. 2. Configure that server in LiteLLM with `auth_type: oauth2` and `oauth2_flow: authorization_code`. 3. Complete the per-user OAuth connection and verify that the credential status reports `has_credential: true`. 4. Connect an MCP client through LiteLLM and call `tools/list`. The protected upstream tools are returned. 5. Call `prompts/list` and `resources/list` through the same connection and user identity. 6. Observe upstream 401 responses in the LiteLLM logs and empty prompt and resource lists at the client. 7. Call a protected prompt or resource directly. These operations also create an MCP client without the per-user credential. ### Relevant log output ```text Failed to get prompts from server protected-mcp: Client error '401 Unauthorized' Failed to get resources from server protected-mcp: Client error '401 Unauthorized' ``` ### Suggested fix Pass `user_api_key_auth` through every prompt and resource manager method and into `_create_mcp_client`, using the same Authorization Code credential-resolution path as tool listing and tool calls. Please cover list, get, read, and resource-template operations with regression tests. ### What part of LiteLLM is this about? Proxy ### What LiteLLM version are you on? v1.97.0

signal.title: additional_drop_params strips fields from message content blocks, not just top-level request params
signal.text: # Bug: `additional_drop_params` strips fields from message content blocks, not just top-level request params ## Description `additional_drop_params` is intended to drop top-level request parameters (e.g., `thinking`, `temperature`) before they're sent to the provider. However, it also recursively strips fields with the same name from **inside message content blocks**, breaking valid conversation histories. ## Reproduction ### Config: ```yaml - model_name: "claude-opus-5" litellm_params: model: "anthropic/claude-opus-5" api_key: os.environ/ANTHROPIC_API_KEY additional_drop_params: ["thinking", "temperature", "top_p", "top_k"] ``` ### Request: ```python import litellm response = litellm.completion( model="claude-opus-5", messages=[ {"role": "user", "content": "What is 2+2?"}, {"role": "assistant", "content": [ {"type": "thinking", "thinking": "The user asks about 2+2. The answer is 4."}, {"type": "text", "text": "4"} ]}, {"role": "user", "content": "And 3+3?"} ], max_tokens=100 ) ``` ### Expected behavior: - The top-level `thinking` request parameter (if present) should be stripped. - The `thinking` **field inside message content blocks** (`messages[].content[].thinking`) should be left intact — it's part of the conversation history, not a request parameter. ### Actual behavior: The `thinking` field is stripped from inside the assistant message content block, turning: ```json {"type": "thinking", "thinking": "The user asks about 2+2. The answer is 4."} ``` into: ```json {"type": "thinking"} ``` Anthropic then rejects this with: ``` messages.X.content.0.thinking: each thinking block must contain thinking ``` ## Impact This breaks **fallback routing** in production. When a primary model fails and LiteLLM falls back to a model with `additional_drop_params: ["thinking"]`, the conversation history (which may contain thinking blocks from prior reasoning model responses) gets corrupted, causing the fallback to also fail. Error observed: ``` Error doing the fallback: {"type":"error","error":{"type":"invalid_request_error", "message":"messages.27.content.0.thinking: each thinking block must contain thinking"}} ``` ## Environment - LiteLLM version: v1.93.2 - Deployment: LiteLLM Proxy (Docker/K8s) - Provider: Anthropic (claude-opus-5) - Router with fallbacks enabled ## Suggested Fix `additional_drop_params` should only strip keys from the **top-level request body** (the kwargs dict passed to the completion call), not recurse into nested structures like `messages[].content[]`. The stripping logic should be scoped to: ```python # Only strip from top-level params for param in additional_drop_params: kwargs.pop(param, None) ``` And should NOT traverse into: - `messages[].content[]` (message content blocks) - `messages[].tool_calls[]` (tool call arguments) - Any other nested message payload structures ## Workaround Remove `"thinking"` from `additional_drop_params` on models that are used as fallback targets. This means clients sending the unsupported `thinking` parameter will get a raw provider error, but fallback routing won't break.

signal.title: fix: preserve prompt cache for mid-conversation system on unflagged Claude models
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Mid-conversation system reminders on pre-4.8 Claude get hoisted into `system` - The hoist rewrites the cached prefix, re-billing the whole conversation How it solves it: - Convert the reminder to a user turn in place instead - A system run caught between a tool call and its result moves to right after the result, so the pair stays adjacent - Leading system runs still hoist; flagged models are untouched ## User Flow Before: a Claude Code user routed to a Vertex Claude 4.6 deployment pays full cache-write pricing every turn a reminder appears 1. They run a long session against POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages with their proxy key, history carrying `cache_control` breakpoints 2. Claude Code inserts a `role: "system"` reminder mid-conversation 3. The response is 200, but `usage` shows `cache_creation_input_tokens` around 1746 with `cache_read_input_tokens` dropping to 5265: the whole prior history was re-billed at cache-write pricing (reporter's real Vertex numbers in #36559) 4. Every later reminder repeats the same full-prefix rebill After: the same session keeps its cache; only the new turn is fresh 1. They run a long session against POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages with their proxy key, history carrying `cache_control` breakpoints 2. Claude Code inserts a `role: "system"` reminder mid-conversation 3. The response is 200, and `usage` shows `cache_read_input_tokens` around 6973 with `cache_creation_input_tokens` around 60: the full prior history read back from cache 4. Follow-up turns keep reading the full cached prefix ## Relevant issues Fixes #36559 ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5872 https://linear.app/litellm-ai/issue/LIT-5872/hoisting-mid-conversation-system-reminders-on-pre-48-claude ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix The changed path runs only for the partner routes (Vertex, Bedrock Invoke, Azure Foundry) behind POST /v1/messages; the first-party Anthropic route and chat completions never call it. Both legs drive the real Claude Code CLI (2.1.237) through a local proxy, one session per provider, with the proxy booted from the merge base (Before) and from this PR (After) and nothing else different Shared setup. `config.yaml` (keys come from the environment): ```yaml model_list: - model_name: vertex-sonnet-4-6 litellm_params: model: vertex_ai/claude-sonnet-4-6 vertex_project: os.environ/VERTEXAI_PROJECT vertex_location: global - model_name: bedrock-haiku-4-5 litellm_params: model: bedrock/invoke/us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0 aws_region_name: us-east-1 - model_name: azure-foundry-opus-4-7 litellm_params: model: azure_ai/claude-opus-4-7 api_base: os.environ/AZURE_FOUNDRY_API_BASE api_key: os.environ/AZURE_FOUNDRY_API_KEY ``` The aliases are deliberately names Claude Code does not recognize: for those it sends its reminders as `role: "system"` turns after every prompt, which is the issue's setup. For a recognized name such as `claude-sonnet-4-6` it inlines them as `<system-reminder>` text instead, and that session read its cache fine on both legs. `big.txt` in the working directory is 400 lines of inventory text, about 45k tokens. Each session: ```bash python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config config.yaml --port $PORT export ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:$PORT ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN=$PROXY_KEY CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL=high claude --model <alias> --strict-mcp-config --mcp-config '{"mcpServers":{}}' ``` then the user types, in order, `Read big.txt in full, then reply with exactly one word: done`, `Reply with exactly one word: thanks`, `Reply with exactly one word: again`, and `/cost`. Every session answered `done`, `thanks`, `again` on both legs. Per-response usage below comes from the session transcript Claude Code writes for the user (`cache_read_input_tokens / cache_creation_input_tokens`, one line per response): ```bash jq -r 'select(.type=="assistant") | [.message.id, .message.usage.cache_read_input_tokens, .message.usage.cache_creation_input_tokens] | @tsv' ~/.claude/projects/<cwd>/<session>.jsonl | awk '!seen[$1]++' ``` ### Before (6fcdea03b0) #### Vertex (vertex-sonnet-4-6) 1. `claude --model vertex-sonnet-4-6 --strict-mcp-config --mcp-config '{"mcpServers":{}}'`, then the three prompts 2. Usage per response: `0 / 48827`, `0 / 64609`, `42868 / 22089`, `42868 / 22439`. The read never grows past the first breakpoint and about 22k tokens are written again on every turn 3. `/cost`: `vertex-sonnet-4-6: 10 input, 163 output, 85.7k cache read, 158.0k cache write ($1.03)` #### Bedrock (bedrock-haiku-4-5) 1. `claude --model bedrock-haiku-4-5 --strict-mcp-config --mcp-config '{"mcpServers":{}}'`, then the three prompts 2. Usage per response: `0 / 50156`, `44174 / 21062`, `44174 / 21275`, `44174 / 21625` 3. `/cost`: `bedrock-haiku-4-5: 862 input, 751 output, 132.5k cache read, 114.1k cache write ($0.80)` #### Azure Foundry (azure-foundry-opus-4-7) 1. `claude --model azure-foundry-opus-4-7 --strict-mcp-config --mcp-config '{"mcpServers":{}}'`, then the three prompts 2. Usage per response: `0 / 53972`, `45998 / 8302`, `45998 / 26473`, `45998 / 26969`, `45998 / 27471` 3. `/cost`: `azure-foundry-opus-4-7: 1.2k input, 385 output, 184.0k cache read, 143.2k cache write ($1.00)` ### After (155ef8cb11) e11399fc56 on top of it only touches `tests/e2e`, which cannot change proxy behavior #### Vertex (vertex-sonnet-4-6) 1. `claude --model vertex-sonnet-4-6 --strict-mcp-config --mcp-config '{"mcpServers":{}}'`, then the three prompts 2. Usage per response: `0 / 45456`, `36513 / 28111`, `64624 / 54`, `65041 / 10`. The read grows to the whole conversation and later turns write only the new turn 3. `/cost`: `vertex-sonnet-4-6: 4.9k input, 190 output, 295.9k cache read, 74.4k cache write ($0.64)` #### Bedrock (bedrock-haiku-4-5) 1. `claude --model bedrock-haiku-4-5 --strict-mcp-config --mcp-config '{"mcpServers":{}}'`, then the three prompts 2. Usage per response: `0 / 46785`, `46785 / 18319`, `65104 / 59`, `65526 / 10` 3. `/cost`: `bedrock-haiku-4-5: 5.7k input, 1.9k output, 308.1k cache read, 65.9k cache write ($0.64)` #### Azure Foundry (azure-foundry-opus-4-7) 1. `claude --model azure-foundry-opus-4-7 --strict-mcp-config --mcp-config '{"mcpServers":{}}'`, then the three prompts 2. Usage per response: `0 / 49570`, `49570 / 4738`, `54308 / 18211`, `72519 / 79`, `73115 / 15` 3. `/cost`: `azure-foundry-opus-4-7: 7.8k input, 411 output, 395.2k cache read, 73.6k cache write ($0.71)` Observations from the run: - Recognized model names never hit the symptom; PR leaves alone - Azure opus-4-7 sometimes calls the operator note injection; PR causes - Vertex global location can miss fresh cache writes; pre-existing - Trailing-system turn: Vertex/Azure 400 becomes 200; PR causes ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - A converted reminder loses true system-role priority; tradeoff discussed and accepted in #36559 - The operator-note prefix is part of the request bytes; changing it later invalidates caches again, so it is pinned by tests ## QA runbook The unflagged-model tests in both e2e files prime the prompt cache first and assert the reminder turn reads the whole primed prefix back, so the same steps prove both the completion and the cache. Priming waits until the first turn reads back on three sends in a row, because the Vertex global location serves the cache per region and a chunk written seconds earlier can still be missing from the region the next request lands on; the Vertex test also pins `us-east5`, a single cache store, for the same reason. The flagged-model cache tests stay skipped under LIT-4873 and are untouched - tests/e2e/llm_translation/test_messages_mid_conversation_system_e2e.py::TestBedrockInvokeMidConversationSystem::test_unflagged_model_converts_system_reminder_and_succeeds - an unflagged Bedrock Claude still answers when a reminder appears, and the reminder turn reads the full primed prefix from cache - [x] POST /model/new with the master key registering `bedrock/invoke/us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0` in us-east-1 (needs AWS credentials), then POST /key/generate for a key scoped to it - [x] Prime: POST /v1/messages with a system block unique to this run (300 short paragraphs, above Haiku's 2048-token cache minimum) carrying `cache_control`, plus one `cache_control` user turn of about 100 notes; repeat with a fresh user turn every 3s until one response shows both `cache_read_input_tokens > 0` and `cache_creation_input_tokens > 0`, note their sum, then re-send that exact turn until `cache_read_input_tokens` reaches that sum on three sends in a row - [x] POST /v1/messages with the same system block, that same first user turn, a `role: "system"` reminder, an assistant turn, and a fresh `cache_control` user turn - [x] Expect 200 with assistant text, no provider 400 about role "system", and `cache_read_input_tokens` at least the sum noted above - [x] Sanity check: this test makes sense and is not hand-wavey or potentially flaky - tests/e2e/llm_translation/test_messages_mid_conversation_system_native_providers_e2e.py::TestAzureFoundryMidConversationSystem::test_unflagged_model_converts_system_reminder_and_succeeds - same shape against Azure Foundry with `azure_ai/claude-opus-4-7` (needs AZURE_AI_API_BASE and AZURE_AI_API_KEY) - [x] Same four steps as above with the Azure Foundry deployment - [x] Sanity check: this test makes sense and is not hand-wavey or potentially flaky - tests/e2e/llm_translation/test_messages_mid_conversation_system_native_providers_e2e.py::TestVertexMidConversationSystem::test_unflagged_model_converts_system_reminder_and_succeeds - same shape against Vertex with `vertex_ai/claude-sonnet-4-6` in `us-east5` (needs VERTEXAI_PROJECT and Google credentials) - [x] Same four steps as above with the Vertex deployment - [x] Sanity check: this test makes sense and is not hand-wavey or potentially flaky ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR <!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY --> --- > [!NOTE] > **Medium Risk** > Changes request shaping on hot proxy paths (Bedrock/Vertex/Azure Messages) and alters how system reminders are interpreted for older Claude; leading-system hoist and flagged-model paths are unchanged but billing/cache behavior is sensitive. > > **Overview** > Fixes **prompt-cache invalidation** on Bedrock Invoke, Vertex, and Azure Foundry when Claude Code sends a mid-conversation `role: "system"` reminder on **pre-4.8** Claude models. > > **Before:** models without `supports_mid_conversation_system` had every in-thread system message **hoisted** into the top-level `system` field. That rewrote the cached prefix and forced full **cache-write** billing on later turns. > > **After:** `_normalize_system_role_messages` still **hoists only a leading run** of system messages (required by the API). Mid-conversation reminders on unflagged models are **rewritten in place** to `role: "user"` with a fixed operator-note prefix plus the original content, so bytes before the reminder stay unchanged. Flagged Claude 4.8+/5 behavior is unchanged (reminders stay as system in `messages`). > > Unit tests for Azure, Bedrock, and Vertex pin the new message shape; unflagged-model **e2e** flows now prime the cache and assert `cache_read_input_tokens` on the reminder turn. Vertex adds coverage that **leading** system runs are still hoisted on unsupported models. > > <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 1b5e50727c62cdec0c06ab7c1f54006ad8c8f8a9. signal.title: [Bug/Docs]: Snowflake (snowflake/) provider: streaming tool-calls dropped, misleading endpoint docs, and gaps using the OpenAI-/Anthropic-compatible Cortex endpoints
signal.text: ### Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. ### What happened? ### Summary Using litellm (SDK / Router) with Snowflake Cortex, I hit a cluster of related issues — some in the `snowflake/` provider code, some in the docs, and some when following the docs' suggestion to use the OpenAI-/Anthropic-compatible Cortex endpoints. Filing together for context; happy to split. Verification status tagged per item (source-checked on `main` 2026-06-18 unless noted). Background: Snowflake Cortex exposes three REST endpoints — `/api/v2/cortex/inference:complete` (native), `/api/v2/cortex/v1/chat/completions` (OpenAI-compatible), `/api/v2/cortex/v1/messages` (Anthropic-compatible). The litellm `snowflake/` provider only ever targets `inference:complete`. --- ### Issue 1 — `snowflake/` drops `tool_calls` when streaming [BUG, verified on main] `SnowflakeConfig.transform_response` converts Cortex `content_list`/`tool_use` → OpenAI `tool_calls`, but **only for non-streaming**. There is no `get_model_response_iterator` / `chunk_parser`, so streaming inherits the generic `OpenAIGPTConfig` SSE parser, which ignores Snowflake's `{"type":"tool_use",...}` deltas → tool calls silently dropped. Plain-text streaming works, so it's easy to miss. Repro: ```python import litellm tools=[{"type":"function","function":{"name":"get_weather", "parameters":{"type":"object","properties":{"location":{"type":"string"}}}}}] common=dict(model="snowflake/claude-3-5-sonnet", api_base="https://<ACCOUNT>.snowflakecomputing.com/api/v2", api_key="<SNOWFLAKE_JWT>", messages=[{"role":"user","content":"weather in Paris?"}], tools=tools, tool_choice={"type":"function","function":{"name":"get_weather"}}, max_tokens=100) print(litellm.completion(**common).choices[0].message.tool_calls) # populated ✅ print([c.choices[0].delta.tool_calls for c in litellm.completion(**common, stream=True)]) # all None ❌ ``` Fix: add a `SnowflakeStreamingHandler(BaseModelResponseIterator)` whose `chunk_parser` maps `tool_use`(id/name + streamed `input` fragments) → `delta.tool_calls`, `text` → `delta.content`, and sets `finish_reason="tool_calls"` on the terminal chunk. (Working ~70-line impl on hand; can PR.) Possibly related: `transform_request` does `stream = optional_params.pop("stream", None) or False` and returns `"stream": stream` — if `stream` isn't present in `optional_params` on streaming calls, the request body is sent with `stream:false`. Maintainers should confirm whether `stream` reaches `optional_params` here. --- ### Issue 2 — Docs misrepresent supported endpoints & never mention you must switch prefixes [DOCS, verified on main] `docs/providers/snowflake` presents `/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/messages` as endpoints and shows `api_base=https://<account>.snowflakecomputing.com/api/v2/cortex/v1`, implying the `snowflake/` provider uses them. In reality: - `SnowflakeConfig.get_complete_url()` hardcodes `f"{api_base}/cortex/inference:complete"` — it never calls `/v1/chat/completions` or `/v1/messages`. - `_get_api_base()` does `rstrip("/")` then `if not endswith("/api/v2"): += "/api/v2"`. So feeding the documented `.../api/v2/cortex/v1` to the `snowflake/` provider **double-appends** → `.../api/v2/cortex/v1/api/v2/cortex/inference:complete` (malformed). The docs never state that to actually use the OpenAI- or Anthropic-compatible Cortex endpoints you must use a **different prefix** — `openai/<model>` (+ `api_base=.../api/v2/cortex/v1`) for `/v1/chat/completions`, or `anthropic/<model>` (+ `api_base=.../api/v2/cortex`) for `/v1/messages` — not `snowflake/`. This is the only way to get working streaming tool calls (Cortex translates server-side). Please document this explicitly and fix the `api_base` examples. --- ### Issue 3 — Empty `finish_reason` from Cortex chat/completions → `Choices` ValidationError [BUG, verified on main] When using the `openai/` prefix against Cortex `/v1/chat/completions` for Claude, Cortex returns `finish_reason: ""` on non-streaming responses. In `convert_dict_to_response.convert_to_model_response_object`, litellm coerces `finish_reason is None → "stop"` but **not** `"" → "stop"`, so the strict `Choices` pydantic model raises: ``` litellm.InternalServerError: OpenAIException - Invalid response object ... pydantic ValidationError: finish_reason Input should be 'stop'|'tool_calls'|... [input_value=''] ``` The `is None` check is identical in 1.81.15, 1.88.0, and `main`. Suggest treating empty-string `finish_reason` like `None` (coerce to `"stop"`), consistent with the existing fallback. --- ### Issue 4 — `max_tokens` rejected by Cortex chat/completions; not auto-mapped [GOTCHA/DOCS] Cortex `/v1/chat/completions` follows the newer OpenAI spec and **rejects `max_tokens`**, requiring `max_completion_tokens` (even for Claude). litellm only renames `max_tokens → max_completion_tokens` for detected o-series/gpt-5 models (`o_series_transformation`/`gpt_5_transformation`); the base `OpenAIGPTConfig` forwards `max_tokens` as-is. So via the `openai/` prefix you get: ``` OpenAIException - max_tokens is deprecated in favor of max_completion_tokens ``` At minimum this should be documented for Cortex; ideally litellm offers a way to mark an OpenAI-compatible endpoint as "strict new spec." [Verified empirically.] --- ### Issue 5 — `cache_control` dropped from the converted `system` field [BUG, observed on 1.81.15 — please confirm on main] Passing Anthropic prompt-caching `cache_control` on a **system** message in OpenAI content-block form: ```python {"role":"system","content":[{"type":"text","text":"<large>","cache_control":{"type":"ephemeral"}}]} ``` the outgoing Anthropic request's `system` field comes through as `[{"type":"text","text":"<large>"}]` — **`cache_control` stripped** — so no cache is created. `cache_control` on a **user** message content block IS preserved. Affects `anthropic/` and `vertex_ai/*claude*` (and Snowflake via `anthropic/`), not just Snowflake. Observed on 1.81.15; please verify current. (Empirically: user-message breakpoint with a >threshold prompt caches correctly — `cache_creation_input_tokens` then `cache_read_input_tokens` — confirming the issue is specifically the system-field conversion.) --- ### Issue 6 — Auth header required for the compatible endpoints isn't documented [DOCS/GOTCHA] Cortex with key-pair JWT requires `Authorization: Bearer <JWT>` **and** `X-Snowflake-Authorization-Token-Type: KEYPAIR_JWT`. Via the `anthropic/` prefix, litellm's Anthropic handler puts the key in `x-api-key` by default → Cortex returns `390146 "Bearer token is missing in the HTTP request authorization header."`. Users must inject `Authorization`/token-type via `extra_headers`. Worth documenting for both the `openai/` and `anthropic/` Cortex routes. --- ### Environment litellm used as SDK (Router). Issues source-verified on `main` (2026-06-18) except Issue 5 (observed 1.81.15). Provider: Snowflake Cortex, Claude models. ### Steps to Reproduce ### Steps to Reproduce **Prerequisites:** A Snowflake account with Cortex enabled, a Claude model available (e.g. `claude-3-5-sonnet`), and key-pair (RSA) auth configured for a user. 1. Install litellm: ```bash pip install "litellm>=1.81.15" # also repro'd on 1.88.0 and main ``` 2. Generate a Snowflake key-pair JWT (or use your existing one): <details><summary>minimal JWT helper (PyJWT + cryptography)</summary> ```python import base64, hashlib, jwt from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone from cryptography.hazmat.primitives import serialization def snowflake_jwt(account: str, user: str, private_key_pem: str) -> str: account, user = account.upper(), user.upper() # no region/cloud suffix pk = serialization.load_pem_private_key(private_key_pem.encode(), password=None) der = pk.public_key().public_bytes( serialization.Encoding.DER, serialization.PublicFormat.SubjectPublicKeyInfo) fp = "SHA256:" + base64.b64encode(hashlib.sha256(der).digest()).decode() qn = f"{account}.{user}" now = datetime.now(timezone.utc) return jwt.encode( {"iss": f"{qn}.{fp}", "sub": qn, "iat": now, "exp": now + timedelta(hours=1)}, pk, algorithm="RS256") ``` </details> 3. Run the same tool-calling request twice — once non-streaming, once streaming: ```python import litellm JWT = "<SNOWFLAKE_KEYPAIR_JWT>" tools = [{ "type": "function", "function": { "name": "get_weather", "description": "Get the weather for a location", "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {"location": {"type": "string"}}}, }, }] common = dict( model="snowflake/claude-3-5-sonnet", api_base="https://<ACCOUNT>.snowflakecomputing.com/api/v2", # snowflake/ wants /api/v2 api_key=JWT, messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "What's the weather in Paris?"}], tools=tools, tool_choice={"type": "function", "function": {"name": "get_weather"}}, max_tokens=100, ) # (a) NON-streaming r = litellm.completion(**common) print("non-stream tool_calls:", r.choices[0].message.tool_calls) # (b) STREAMING stream_tool_calls = [ c.choices[0].delta.tool_calls for c in litellm.completion(**common, stream=True) if c.choices[0].delta.tool_calls ] print("stream tool_calls:", stream_tool_calls) ``` 4. Observe the difference: **Expected:** both print a `get_weather` tool call. **Actual:** ``` non-stream tool_calls: [ChatCompletionMessageToolCall(function=Function( name='get_weather', arguments='{"location":"Paris"}'), ...)] # ✅ stream tool_calls: [] # ❌ dropped ``` In streaming mode the `tool_use` deltas from Cortex's `inference:complete` are silently discarded (the `snowflake/` provider has no `chunk_parser`); only `delta.content` survives. **Reproducing the other issues:** switch the prefix/`api_base` to the OpenAI-/Anthropic-compatible Cortex endpoints (which the docs imply the provider uses): - **Issue 3 (empty finish_reason):** `model="openai/claude-3-5-sonnet"`, `api_base=".../api/v2/cortex/v1"`, `extra_headers={"X-Snowflake-Authorization-Token-Type":"KEYPAIR_JWT"}`, non-streaming → `InternalServerError: Invalid response object` (ValidationError, `finish_reason=''`). - **Issue 4 (max_tokens):** same call with `max_tokens=` → `OpenAIException - max_tokens is deprecated in favor of max_completion_tokens`. - **Issue 6 (auth):** `model="anthropic/claude-3-5-sonnet"`, `api_base=".../api/v2/cortex"`, passing the JWT as `api_key` → `390146 "Bearer token is missing..."` (litellm sends it as `x-api-key`; must inject `Authorization: Bearer` via `extra_headers`). ``` ### Relevant log output ```shell ``` ### What part of LiteLLM is this about? SDK (litellm Python package) ### What LiteLLM version are you on ? 1.81.15 ### Twitter / LinkedIn details @Bhogi-sai-sathwik

signal.title: Mid-conversation system-role hoist invalidates the entire prompt-cache prefix (AnthropicMessagesConfig)
signal.text: ## Summary `AnthropicMessagesConfig._normalize_system_role_messages` (introduced in #33807) hoists mid-conversation `role: "system"` messages into the top-level `system` field for Claude models without `supports_mid_conversation_system` (pre-4.8 generation). This avoids the 400 those models throw on partner endpoints (Vertex, Azure Foundry, Bedrock Invoke) — but the hoist itself invalidates the entire cached prompt prefix on every turn a reminder appears, which is exactly the cost [mid-conversation system messages](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/mid-conversation-system-messages) are designed to avoid. ## Why the hoist breaks caching Per Anthropic's docs, prompt caching hashes the request prefix in order `tools` → `system` → `messages`, and a cache hit requires everything up to the breakpoint to match byte-for-byte. The `system` field sits early in that order, so any change to it — including appending a hoisted message — invalidates the cache for the system prompt *and every cached message after it*, not just the new content. Current code (`litellm/llms/anthropic/experimental_pass_through/messages/transformation.py`, at `6a919aec6a` on `main`): ```python else: hoisted = [m for m in messages if self._is_system_role_message(m)] remaining = [m for m in messages if not self._is_system_role_message(m)] if hoisted: anthropic_messages_request["messages"] = remaining system_content: Final = [ block for source in ( anthropic_messages_request.get("system"), *(m.get("content") for m in hoisted), ) for block in self._as_system_content_blocks(source) ] ``` Every system-role message anywhere in `messages` gets pulled out and folded into `system` on every request (LiteLLM re-derives the downstream payload from the client's full history each call). The turn a *new* reminder first appears, `system`'s content changes for the first time since the last request — full cache miss on that call, reprocessing the entire prior conversation. ## Measured impact (real Vertex AI traffic, unflagged model) | | current (hoist) | proposed (convert-in-place, see below) | |---|---|---| | Reminder-turn `cache_read_input_tokens` | 5265 | 6973 (full prior history preserved) | | Reminder-turn `cache_creation_input_tokens` | 1746 | 60 | | Follow-up turn `cache_read_input_tokens` | 7011 | 7033 | Both variants return `200` — this isn't about the correctness fix from #33807, which works fine. It's specifically the caching side effect of *how* it avoids the 400. ## Proposed fix Since the model itself can't accept `role: "system"` in `messages` at all (that's the actual constraint being worked around), and the hoist target (`system`) sits earlier in the cache hash than `messages`, moving the offending message *anywhere* in `system` will always cost the full prefix. Instead: for unflagged models, mutate the message's `role` to `"user"` **in place** (same position in `messages`) rather than moving it to `system`. Nothing before that position changes, so an existing cache breakpoint still hits; only the new message needs fresh processing — the same cost as any ordinary new turn. I have this working as a local patch with the measurements above, happy to open a PR if that's useful. One tradeoff worth surfacing first: converting to `role: "user"` loses Claude's "system beats a conflicting user instruction" priority for that specific message, compared to a true system-role turn. For models that don't support the feature at all, there may not be a way to fully avoid that tradeoff — but it seemed worth confirming that's an acceptable direction before sending a PR, given it's a behavior change beyond just fixing the 400. ## Environment - litellm `main` @ `6a919aec6a2a0c54cc6a2e6f67ff7b236a3a2573` - Reproduced against real `vertex_ai/` Claude deployments (unflagged, pre-4.8 generation) with the Claude Agent SDK's `mid-conversation-system-2026-04-07` reminder shape - Related: #33807 (introduced the current model-aware hoist), #31452 (earlier draft of the same base-class idea, predates #33807, does not address caching)

signal.title: fix(ui): resolve Generic Guardrail API config fields not rendering
signal.text: ## Problem When adding a Generic Guardrail API guardrail via the Admin UI (Guardrails > Add New Guardrail > Add Provider Guardrail), selecting "Generic Guardrail API" as the provider renders "No configuration fields available for this provider." The expected API Base, API Key, and optional parameter fields never appear. Closes #34927 ## Root Cause In guardrail_provider_fields.tsx, the provider key is resolved via: const providerKey = guardrail_provider_map[selectedProvider]?.toLowerCase(); For dynamically-added providers (populated from the API response), guardrail_provider_map may not yet contain the mapping when the component renders. This happens because: 1. The Select dropdown uses camelCase keys (e.g. "GenericGuardrailApi") generated by populateGuardrailProviders 2. guardrail_provider_map is populated by populateGuardrailProviderMap inside a useEffect 3. When providerParams are passed via props (providerParamsProp), the effect returns early without calling populateGuardrailProviderMap 4. Result: guardrail_provider_map["GenericGuardrailApi"] is undefined, so providerKey is undefined, and providerParams[undefined] yields no fields ## Fix Add a camelCase-to-snake_case fallback when the map lookup fails: const providerKey = guardrail_provider_map[selectedProvider]?.toLowerCase() ?? selectedProvider.replace(/([A-Z])/g, "_").toLowerCase().replace(/^_/, ""); This converts "GenericGuardrailApi" to "generic_guardrail_api", which matches the API response key. The fallback is only used when the primary map lookup fails, so existing hardcoded providers are unaffected. ## Testing - Verified the regex conversion: "GenericGuardrailApi" -> "generic_guardrail_api" - Existing hardcoded providers (PresidioPII, Bedrock, etc.) still resolve via the primary map path - No changes to component behavior when guardrail_provider_map is fully populated

signal.title: fix(nebius): route requests to Token Factory
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Nebius requests target the retired AI Studio endpoint - Provider docs claim four unsupported API surfaces How it solves it: - Routes chat and embeddings to Token Factory - Tests routing, authentication, models, and overrides - Aligns branding and capability metadata with implementation ## User Flow Before: a developer using LiteLLM's Nebius provider sends requests to the former AI Studio host 1. They configure `NEBIUS_API_KEY` and call `completion(model="nebius/moonshotai/Kimi-K3", ...)` 2. LiteLLM sends POST https://api.studio.nebius.ai/v1/chat/completions 3. They must override `NEBIUS_API_BASE` to reach Token Factory After: the same configuration reaches Token Factory without an endpoint override 1. They configure `NEBIUS_API_KEY` and call `completion(model="nebius/moonshotai/Kimi-K3", ...)` 2. LiteLLM sends POST https://api.tokenfactory.nebius.com/v1/chat/completions 3. The response returns through the existing OpenAI-compatible chat transformation ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Live proof is not included because this environment has no `NEBIUS_API_KEY` At commit `8812573511`, focused mocked requests verify the full chat and embedding URLs, bearer authentication, provider-prefix stripping, request model IDs, response parsing, environment overrides, endpoint detection, and unsupported Responses config ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ✅ Test 📖 Documentation ## Caveats (if any) - Token Factory Responses support remains stateless and unimplemented here - Model catalog refresh is intentionally excluded from this repair ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signal.title: PATCH /update/mcp_semantic_filter_settings returns HTML 504 when enabling semantic filter
signal.text: ## Bug Description When calling `PATCH /update/mcp_semantic_filter_settings` with `enabled: true`, the server successfully saves the settings but returns an HTML 504 error page from the reverse proxy instead of a valid JSON response. ## Steps to Reproduce 1. Call `PATCH /update/mcp_semantic_filter_settings` with body `{"enabled": true, "embedding_model": "text-embedding-3-small", "top_k": 10, "similarity_threshold": 0.3}` 2. The settings are actually persisted (verified by `GET /get/mcp_semantic_filter_settings`) 3. But the PATCH response is an HTML 504 page, not JSON ## Expected Behavior Return a proper JSON response (e.g., `200 OK` with `{"status": "success"}` or `204 No Content`). ## Actual Behavior Returns HTML 504 Gateway Timeout from nginx/openresty, even though the update succeeded. ## Workaround Clients must make a subsequent GET request to verify if settings were actually applied. ## Environment - LiteLLM version: 1.86.2 - Reverse proxy: openresty/nginx
